title: Along the Aare between Bern and Münsingen
Out of the city under bridges
long_description: Beautiful and leisurely hike along the Aare. The tour starts at the Bärengraben bus stop and then leads immediately along the left side of the river to the Felsenau weir. Here you change to the right side. Continue downstream along the riverbank path towards Tiefenau. Pass the Reichenbach ferry and Bremgarten Castle. You then reach the Felsenaubrücke bridge, then the Seftausteg footbridge, where the water collected at the Felsenau weir is returned to the Aare. On soft ground you hike to Neubrügg, which is the oldest covered wooden bridge in Canton Bern. At Vorderdettige you briefly take the asphalt road. In Underdettige you follow the path along the river bank to the Stägmattsteg, which you cross. The last stretch goes through the forest to the Eymatt bus stop where the bus takes you back to the station. The entire route is characterised by imposing bridges.

title: Tomlishorn Flower Path
short_description: The Flower Trail is one of the most beautiful hiking trails in the Swiss Alps;
long_description: The path is well secured by a railing, so that you can walk with gym and leisure shoes. Steps have been cut into the rock in the steeper parts. Along the trail, flower signs provide information about the flora, including flower colour and time.

title: About the Mannenberg
short_description: The easy circular hike with great views takes you over the Emmental hills and along the Emme.
long_description: The hike starts at Hasle-Rüegsau railway station and begins with an easy but steady ascent üvia the Ötzenberg, Schallenberg, Mannenberg to the Rachisberg. From there it is practically all downhill via Busswil, Wirtenmoos and finally along the Emme back to the starting point. The route is varied and characterised by a sensational view.

title: Dorfwaldweg
long_description:
This very family-friendly, easy circular tour starts at the railway station in Randa. First you hike on the normal road to Ännerna. At the village stream, turn right onto the forest road. Looking towards the Klein Matterhorn, you hike through the forest and across lush meadows. At the chapel the trail rejoins the asphalt road and leads back to the starting point.

Note(s)
Suitable for children from 4 years.

title: Baker’s Pond Hiking Trail
short_description: The hiking trail leads to the pond that is the source of the headwaters of the Wolf River.  There is a graveled, stairway trail to the ridgetop overlooking Baker’s Pond.
long_description: Baker’s Pond Trail is a 1 mile lightly trafficked out and back trail located near Falkner, Mississippi that features a lake and is good for all skill levels. The trail is primarily used for hiking, nature trips, and birding and is accessible year-round. Dogs are also able to use this trail but must be kept on leash.

title: Schwalmquellen Tour - Ulrichstein-Helpershain
short_description:
This beginner's tour takes us to the source of the Schwalm between Köddingen, Meiches and Helpershain.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
The trail begins at the Grundmühle in Helpershain and leads up the Heckenweg, past the former rubble dump and then through mixed beech forest to Köddinger Straße. There it follows a stretch of the road towards Meiches before turning right again into the forest path that leads to the Schwalmquelle. There it follows a stretch of the road in the direction of Meiches, before turning right again into the forest path that leads to the Schwalmquelle spring. At the Schwalmquelle there used to be a pond that was used by the landgraves and great dukes as a foal pool. The forest aisle in which the spring lies is still known today as the foal pen. In earlier times it was also a place of worship.
The trail continues through the Hegwald, the Rhine Weser watershed, in a southerly direction, üe over the road, through the Lohwald to the edge of the forest. Then it goes über the Helges along the edge of the forest and through the hedges back to Helpershain.

title: Mirim Tijuca Peak Trail in Tijuca National Park
short_description: This beautiful and easy trail is ideal for those who want to know a little more of the natural wonders of the city of Rio de Janeiro. The trail is light and well signposted, and can be done even with children.
long_description:
The trail to Pico da Tijuca Mirim é easy and perfect to do with family. Located in the beautiful Tijuca Forest, the largest urban forest in the world, the peak is 917m high. From its top, it is possible to get a privileged view of the city of Rio de Janeiro. 
The Tijuca National Park is the most visited conservation unit in Brazil. Although it was created in 1961, the project of reforestation and protection of the region began in 1861, by order of D. Pedro II.
Today the Park has a green area of almost 40 km ², and among its beautiful forests é possible still recognize a little of the history of the place, through the ruins of the coffee farms é that were expropriated to allow the reforestation of the region

title: Poschiavo - San Romerio - Viano - Brusio
short_description: Varied hike to the Sanctuary of S. Romerio (12th century).
long_description:
Varied hike to the church of pilgrimage S. Romerio (12th century). This day-hike is called the «classic route» of Valposchiavo. From the church San Romerio you have a beautiful view of the lower valley.
From Poschiavo to the fork which is about 70 m above Cologna one can hike to Barghi. From this path one has a splendid view. Piz Lagalb and Corn da Campasc are prominent points in the north. The picture of the western valley's flank with Piz Cancian, Pizzo Scalino and Piz Varuna is broken up by numerous Alpine huts. High above the Lake of Poschiavo you can see Piz Mürasc, Corn dal Solcun and Giümelin. In the south you have a view of the Bergamasc Alps.
From San Romerio a partially steep and stony path leads to the Alpine hut Piaz and down to La Greda. Then a nice trail continues to Alp Predasc. On route 37 you hike across Viano to Brusio. The road between Viano and Brusio is asphalted.

title: Moraine Lake Trail
short_description: A short hike with a slight ascent leads to an indescribable view of the mesmerizing Lake Moraine. Stunning scenery and lots of nimble little squirrels await you within this short walk.
long_description:
The short hiking trail leads from Lake Moraine's parking to the most stunning view of the gorgeous lake and nature surrounding it. The walk is on paved and neat paths, which are slightly challenging but manageable even for less experienced hikers. The viewpoints are easily accessible from the paths.
There are viewpoints at the top, but the view from the lakefront is also amazing and you are closer to the shimmering blue water.

title: Big Trees Trail
short_description: Easy loop trail that runs through a forest of giant trees in Sequoia National Park.
long_description:
As the name suggests, this hike takes you past numerous giant trees. In the Sequoia National Park, you will find a large concentration of giant sequoias. Some of them are still growing. Some of them have been uprooted despite their enormous size and are now lying on the ground in their entire length.
As this is a relatively short route, it is advisable to combine this hike with the route that leads to the impressive Sunset Rock.
This hike is barrier-free and therefore accessible for wheelchair users and with a stroller.

title: Taft Point
short_description: A short-medium hiking route leading through a forest to a panoramic view point on the Yosemite Valley from where the point of view known as "Taft's Point" emerges
long_description:
This hiking route begins with a level walk in a wooded area, while further down the road there is a relatively short graded descent leading to a wide and panoramic view point overlooking the Yosemite Valley and the El Capitan mountain. The high point of the route is the spiky and high rock point that stands out towards the valley - the Taft point.
The first part of the route is accessible to strollers, but the following section with the descent towards the observation deck is not accessible. In general, it is not particularly recommended to take a walk with very young children to the viewpoints, as it is a wide unfenced area that descends steeply into the valley.
Since this is a one-way route, the estimated walking times as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only.

title: Sfazù - Sfazù
short_description: This classic hike from Puschlaver leads into the Val da Camp, which is listed in the Federal Inventory of Landscape and Cultural Monuments of National Importance. Pastures, plateaus and lakes characterise this unique hike.
long_description:
The classic hike at Valposchiavo goes to Val da Camp, a valley that is listed in the federal inventory of landscape and cultural monuments of national importance. Pastures, elevated plains and lakes characterize this unique hike.
In Sfazù the hike starts along the road that goes upwards. After the first ascent one comes to Buril. The path climbs gently up to the next settlements Salva, Mottacalva, Lungacqua and Camp. Here the trails branch off towards the lakes Lagh da Saoseo and Lagh da Val Viola. From here one has free sight to Val Mera on the opposite side.
The trail leads downhill across an impressive area of landslide to the enchanted, deep blue lake Saoseo, then it continues gently downhill. Through a mixed coniferous forest with exuberantly growing bilberry bushes and fern one reaches the place of Terzana.
On easy hiking trails along the pastures one comes to the branch to Sfazù and descends to Val da Camp, in order to cross it. On the other side of the river the path goes steep upwards and reaches quite soon the holiday camp of Buril. The last 10 minutes to Sfazù can be done along the street.

Lagh da Saoseo:
The beautiful lake Lagh da Saoseo is situated between hiking trails and forests which are surrounded by an intense scent of moss and resin. Its colours vary between blue, turquoise, dark green and violet. From Alp Campo the lake can be reached within a 10 minute walk.

Note(s)
Signage:
From Sfazù you follow the signs for «Camp». From Camp you follow the signs for «Lagh da Val Viola» until you come to the lake Val Viola. From there you follow the signs for «Lagh da Saoseo». Then you follow the signs for «Rifugio Saoseo SAC - Terzana/Sfazù-Terzana/Pozzulasc-Sfazù-Doss/Sfazù-Sfazù».

Bus:
If you prefer to walk less, you may take the small bus that starts at Sfazù and drives to Lungacqua or Camp (booking compulsory, at least one hour in advance: +41 (0) 81 844 10 42 / +41 (0) 79 599 96 76).

title: 01 - The path "of the viewpoints"
short_description: North of the Gulf of Salò is a route that offers several panoramic views through the forest and then, in an even more open manner, from the relief of the "cross of Salò."
long_description:
The climb to Croce di Salò requires some physical effort, but the effort is amply repaid by the beauty of the landscape and the tranquility of the trail. After leaving the historic center of Salò, the trail begins to climb gradually, passing through residential areas and small gardens. As you move away from the built-up area, the noise of traffic fades, giving way to the sounds of nature.
The first part of the climb features a paved road that winds through olive groves and vineyards. Here, it is possible to make short stops to admire the view of the lake that opens up more and more as you gain altitude. During spring, the fields are in bloom and the air is pervaded by the scent of wildflowers.
Continuing on, the paved road gives way to dirt paths that enter oak and chestnut forests. The terrain becomes more uneven and the gradient increases, making the trail more challenging. It is advisable to take regular breaks to catch your breath and hydrate. Along the trail, you may encounter small streams and natural fountains where you can refresh yourself.
The vegetation is lush and varied, with old trees providing shade and coolness during the summer months. It is possible to spot several species of birds, squirrels and, with a little luck, even some deer. For botany enthusiasts, the trail offers the opportunity to observe a wide variety of plants and flowers typical of the pre-Alpine area.
As you ascend, the trail offers numerous viewpoints from which to admire Lake Garda in all its expanse. These vantage points are ideal for taking photographs and enjoying the view. In some sections, the trail becomes narrower and steeper, requiring attention and surefootedness.
The last section of the climb is the most challenging, with a steep gradient and rocky terrain. However, fatigue is forgotten once you reach the top, where the Croce di Salò stands out against the sky. The view from here is simply spectacular, with the lake stretching as far as the eye can see and the mountains providing the backdrop.

title: Mono Mills & Mono Lake
short_description: A short, flat and easy route in the historic Mono Mills site from which you can have a great view of the beautiful Mono Lake
long_description:
A track is located in the Inyo National Forest in California and is a light and great stopping point for refreshment on the way to Yosemite Park or the ghost town of Bodie . Inside the wooden gazebo that is placed there you can read about the history of the site as well as watch in a unique and wonderful way over the wonderful Mono Lake. Lake Mono is an alkali salt (sodium) lake 21 kilometers long and 15 kilometers wide, its average depth is 17 meters and the deepest point is 48 meters. According to estimates, the lake was formed at least 760,000 years ago, inside the lake there are tuff rocks in varied and interesting shapes that you can observe.
You can have a picnic on the spot, and it is also in principle accessible for strollers.

title: A trip to Grosser Alpsee
short_description: An easy and relatively flat hiking trail next to the Grosser Alpsee in the Allegoi (Upper) region
long_description:
A leisurely hiking route next to the large Alfaza lake, which is considered one of the largest in the Oberallgäu. A host of attractions, activities, cafes, bathing beaches, playgrounds and more await you along the route. The route first circles the lake from south to north and then curves to the left and circles it across its width from east to west. Along the way and the gorgeous view of the Alps, the following attractions await you:
* An information center where you can gather information about the area, buy local delicacies, drink coffee and more.
* Mini golf complex.
* Small playgrounds, a pirate themed playground with a small trampoline, climbing rock, water games, a slide that goes down the hill and more.
* Adventure rope climbing park.
* Option to rent pedal boats.
* Cruising in a large sailboat.
* Vessel rental center and SAP.
* Cafes, ice cream parlors and restaurants.
* A bridge hanging over the water.
* A variety of free public bathing beaches, as well as a paid bathing beach that includes a playground and other facilities.
* Concerts of the local orchestra (on Fridays, during the summer season, free entry).
* Festivals (in summer)
* In winter you can walk on the frozen lake (in the permitted and safe places).
The track is accessible to strollers.
The walking time and distance shown are for one direction, but since most of the attractions are concentrated at the beginning of the route, it is possible to also do only part of the route and still enjoy most of the activities.

title: Sunset Rock
short_description: A relatively easy, short, flat trail leading to a panoramic view of one of the valleys of Sequoia National Park
long_description:
The trail passes through wooded terrain and leads to a huge and impressive rock that offers a wonderful view of one of the surrounding valleys. The path leading to the rock is beautiful and partly runs along a small stream. Arriving at the giant rock, it almost feels like you are on the moon.
This is an easy walk that is especially recommendable during the evening hours - as the name suggests, this is the ideal place to watch the sunset. This walk can be combined with the "Big Trees Trail" next door.
Due to the terrain's nature, this walk is not suitable for prams but suitable for families with older children. The trail is not accessible for wheelchairs.

title: Osterley Park
short_description: Osterley Park is home to one the few remaining Georgian country estates in London.  The spectactular grounds are operated by the National trust in which actvities such as Hiking, walking and cycling can be enjoyed.
long_description:
A short 15-30 minute circular walk covering one of the largest open green spaces in West London.  The walk will lead you through the beautiful parkland, followed by a trip along the Grand Union Canal and then The walk will take you through a mixture of parkland, industrial landscapes, a beautiful section of the Grand Union Canal and then back through residential streets to farmland which takes you up to the Historic attraction of Osterley House. 
The Park is situated in West London, Isleworth and is a short tube line away from central London.

title: A romantic trip to Point Bonita Lighthouse
short_description: A cable tour on a raised promontory in the natural municipal territory of the city of San Francisco leading to the lighthouse known as Point Bonita
long_description:
A great hiking trail surrounded by water on the right and left, with a great view of the Golden Gate Bridge. Through a tunnel cut in the rock you will reach a white bridge that will lead you to the charming Magdal (note that the road to the lighthouse is open to the general public only on Sundays and Mondays for three hours only). Along the road that starts downhill you can see a number of animals including seals resting on a large rock in the water, goats, fowls and birds of various species. A lovely hiking trail a short drive from the city center.
The route is paved and organized and therefore accessible for walking with strollers, but a slight climb on the way back should be taken into account.
Since it is a one-way route, the estimated walking time as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only.

title: Ospizio Bernina - Alp Grüm - Poschiavo
short_description: After Lago Bianco, the trail climbs to the fantastic vantage point of Sassal Mason with views of Piz Pal, the heart-shaped Lagh da Pal, Alp Grum and Valposchiavo. The Cavaglia high valley below invites you to linger.
long_description:
After Lago Bianco it goes up to the great viewpoint Sassal Mason with view of Piz Palü, of heart-shaped Lago di Palü, Alp Grüm and Valposchiavo. Below there is the high valley of Cavaglia that invites for a rest.
The trail offers fantastic views of mountains and glaciers, of the deep notch of Valposchiavo and of the Bergamasc Alps in Italy located behind. The railway makes lots of turns in order to conquer the difference in altitude: an impressive sight!
From the high valley of Cavaglia that was used as a real village with school, shop and restaurant for some decades due to the construction of the railway and of the power plant, the descent continues and passes by the numerous Alpine huts which are well kept and surrounded by forests and hedges. Finally you arrive to Poschiavo, the main place of the valley.
It is worthwhile visiting the glacier potholes of Cavaglia that are accessible for the public. The stones that rotated due to the strong currents of the prehistoric glacial water ground the potholes into the rock and formed them to sleek cavities and gaps.

title: Twin Peaks San Francisco
short_description: A short and easy hike to two twin hills located on a mountain overlooking the city of San Francisco
long_description:
This route will take you to several great and unique view points on the city of San Francisco. Near the hills there is a wide promenade from which you can also look out over the city and the famous Golden Gate Bridge. in a great way. A great itinerary for those who want to enjoy an ideal and panoramic view of the city.
The climb up the hills is organized and includes several steps and is therefore not accessible to strollers or wheelchairs, but from the adjacent boardwalk you can also enjoy the view of the city (just from a slightly different angle).

title: Hiking circuit: tour of the Gruissan lake
short_description: This thematic trail, which circles the lake, is divided into ten explanatory panels to make the public aware of the richness and fragility of the wetlands of the lake in Gruissan.
long_description:
<Depending on the season, you may see pink flamingos and/or cormorants. The tang, vineyards and Massif de la Clape make this place a magical ideal to recharge your batteries.
Easy thematic trail, allowing to cover all the diversity of the ecosystem living in symbiosis with this lagoon space. 10 information panels as well as remarkable viewpoints mark out the route.

title: Trip to Monument Geyser Basin
short_description: A one-way, relatively short hiking route, leading to the geyser known as "Monument" through a great view point on the valley
long_description:
This hiking route begins with a relatively level walk, and as you progress, the road becomes a little steeper until you reach the wonderful view of the valley and further on to the smoking geyser that comes out of the hillside in which it is located.
Due to its nature, the path is not accessible to strollers.
Since it is a one-way route, the distance and walking time shown on this page are for one direction only.

title: FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path (Tour 1)
short_description: A tour in Brandenburg specially adapted to the needs of cyclists and inline skaters. Good asphalt conditions, no cars and flexible division of the stages of varying degrees of difficulty make this tour suitable for families as well as for endurance athletes.
long_description: The FlaemingSkate cycle and skate route (Tour 1) is one of the sporting attractions in the region. The various entrances to the route are clearly recognisable and marked with "Flaemming Skate". Along the way you will find many places of interest, such as various BMX trails, castles, monuments and, of course, the idyllic forests of the region. At just under 100 km, the tour is the longest continuous route of its kind in Europe. There are plenty of accommodation options along the way to suit every budget.

title: Walking along the Amalfi coast: Amalfi - Lone (Il Duoglio Spiagia)
short_description: The towns on the Amalfi Coast are linked by a scenic road, but also by numerous side roads and paths with stairs that can be crossed on foot. This route links Amalfi to Il Duoglio Spiagia, often listed in the top 5 most beautiful beaches on the Amalfi Coast.
long_description:
This route is just one of the possibilities to cross from one resort to another, enjoying the fabulous scenery and (lots of) movement.
The journey starts in Amalfi, either in the bus stop or in the centre of the resort. Climb up to the Gran Hotel Convento di Amalfi, a former 13th-century monastery converted îinto a luxury hotel. Unfortunately, the location can not be visited by those not staying here, but it's worth climbing the stairs for the view.
You'll get off in front of a tunnel that has space for pedestrian crossings; there's also a crossing area on the left side of the tunnel, on the way in. After the tunnel, follow the road up on the right, not the main road. From here on, you can't get lost, even if there are no proper signposts. Just keep it straight.
Besides the wonderful sea views beyond the coastal road, you can admire the local houses, courtyards, and numerous narrow streets with stairs.
The descent to Il Duoglio Spiagia is done in two stages: first, you go down a street with stairs from the side path to the main coastal road. Then you will have to walk about 2-300 metres along the side of the houses until they end (around a bend). On the right, a panorama opens up. On the left, it's a long stretch. Here you should find an access gate - open - and you'll start to descend again, this time towards the beach.

title: On the Schwellbrunn - Schönengrund hill range
short_description: The tour starts in Schwellbrunn, the highest municipality in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden;
long_description: If you are not travelling by public transport, it is best to park your car in Herisau. After just a few minutes you arrive at «Högg» on the first hügelzug and enjoy the magnificent view of the Alpstein with the Säntis as a prominent elevation. The view from the seat with the well-known restaurant reaches as far as Central Switzerland if the view is good. The route follows the hilly terrain, so there are no major ascents or descents to contend with. Via Landscheidi and Arnig, the «Chäseren» again a popular excursion destination is reached. On the last section, the trail leads down to the village of Schönengrund, where the post bus takes you back to Herisau.

title: Olmsted Point
short_description: A short but special route that passes over a huge rock and includes several panoramic views of the split dome as well as Yosemite Valley from the rock as well as from Olmsted Point
long_description:
A hiking route starting near the famous Togga Pass road. This route has a special terrain character due to the fact that it passes almost entirely on top of a huge rock overlooking the Yosemite Valley. The walk on the route starts on a huge rock sitting diagonally on the ground on which you actually descend towards a viewpoint with another viewpoint on the Yosemite Valley known as "Olmsted Point" from which you can see the famous Half Dome Mountain as well as the Tenaya Canyon.
Due to the nature of the terrain, this route is not accessible to wheelchairs or strollers, but it is not too challenging for children.
Since this is a one-way route, the estimated walking time as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only.

title: Glacier Point
short_description: A well maintained, short and easy hiking trail that leads to one of the most famous viewpoints in Yosemite Park, known as "Glacier Point".
long_description:
Hiking trail with panoramic views of one of the most beautiful and special valleys in Yosemite Park. From an altitude of 2,200 meters, we enjoy great views of Half Dome, Yosemite Falls and other valley attractions. There are several viewpoints, wildlife and a souvenir shop with a kiosk.
This trail is asphalted and has only minimal inclines, making it suitable for walking with strollers and wheelchairs.

title: General Sherman Tree Trail
short_description: A relatively short hike in Sequoia National Park, leading through a wooded area to a Sequoia tree known as the "General Sherman Tree," considered the tree with the world's largest trunk volume.
long_description:
This trail takes us from the car park on easy terrain to the General Sherman Tree, a famous giant sequoia in Sequoia National Park. The estimated age of the tree is 1900 to 2500 years. In terms of trunk volume, the tree is considered the largest of its kind in the world. However, the tallest tree in the world still towers over it by more than 30 meters.
The tree was given its name in 1879 by a naturalist who served under General William Sherman in the American Army. Sherman is considered a national hero of the American Civil War.
In 2006, a large branch 30 m long and 2 m in diameter broke off the General Sherman Tree.
The route is easy to walk, but you have to consider the way back, which is uphill on the same route. For people with reduced mobility, there is a car park directly at the General Sherman Tree. Other car parks are a short walk away. The asphalted route is basically suitable for walking with prams, but here, too, the way back and the ascending meters in altitude should be taken into account.

title: Gibbon Falls
short_description: A short, flat and easy route on top of a boardwalk with panoramic views of the impressive Gibbon Falls located in the northern part of the Yellowstone Nature Reserve
long_description:
This hiking route passes on top of an asphalt boardwalk that overlooks in a wonderful and unique way the Gibbon Falls flowing from a height of 26 meters. From the boardwalk you can watch the falls from a side angle as well as from an almost frontal angle.
This hiking route is paved and relatively wide and is therefore largely accessible to wheelchairs as well as strollers.

title: Grand View Yellowstone
short_description: An easy and short hiking route that passes over a neat boardwalk known as "The Giant Lookout" and leads to some great viewpoints on the Grand Canyon of Yellowstone from the north
long_description:
A beautiful hiking route that passes on top of a neat boardwalk overlooking the Yellowstone Grand Canyon with its yellowish tint and the wonders of nature that part of it from the north. From this direction you can view the upper and lower Yellowstone Falls behind, as well as the Yellowstone River and more. From this route you can see one of the best views of the lower Yellowstone Falls in the back.
This hiking route is also well accessible for strollers.

title: Appenzell Alpine Path
long_description: The Alpstein is perhaps "the most beautiful mountain range in the world", as the famous geologist Albert Heim (1849-1937) put it. On this tour you will learn that the rather unknown alpine landscape in front of the Alpstein is just as attractive. The tour starts in Urnäsch, the "centre of Appenzell customs", and leads over the Hochalp to Schwägalp. In Urnäsch, a visit to the Appenzell customs museum right on the village square is recommended as a prelude to the hike. Once you arrive at Schwägalp, you have the option of visiting the Alpschau cheese dairy or taking the cable car up to the Säntis. The tour is specially signposted as an official Switzerland Mobil route. Return journey from Schwägalp possible by post bus.

short_description: מסלול טיול יחסית קצר וקליל. המסלול מתחיל בהליכה בדרך ישרה ומתחבר למסלול מעגלי. לאורך הדרך חולפים על פני מעיינות חמים צבעוניים בגדלים שונים וכן גייזרים קטנים
long_description:
מסלול הטיול ״דלי הצבע של האמן״ מכונה בשם זה בשל כך שהוא עובר לצד מספר בריכות/ מעיינות חמים בעלי גוונים שונים. רוב המסלול מסודר ועובר על גבי גשרי עץ המאפשרים הליכה וצפיה נוחה על בריכות המים המהפנטות והמיוחדות שבמקום. ישנם חלקים קצרים במסלול הכוללים הליכה על אדמה כמו כן גם מספר מדרגות ועליה קצרה בעלת שיפוע זניח.
חלקו התחתון של המסלול הינו נגיש לעגלות אך חלקו העליון הכולל מספר מעיינות נוספים וכן תצפית, כולל עליה במדרגות ועל כן אינו נגיש לעגלות אך ניתן בכל זאת לטייל וליהנות מחלקו התחתון של המסלול.

title: Hundwiler Height
short_description: The Hundwiler Höhe is a popular hiking destination. From the top of the pyramid-shaped elevation, the hiker enjoys a magnificent view from Alpstein to Lake Constance;
long_description:
Just as famous as the mountain is the summit restaurant where various specialities await the hungry hiker.
This tour starts right at the Zürchersmühle railway station, first crossing the Urnäsch and then following a smaller Bächlein in an eastern direction. A large part of the first ascent to the hamlet of Ramsten is in the forest, which is very pleasant, especially in summer. Now the trail follows the hillside to its top. Impressive nagelfluh walls and idyllic alpine pastures dominate the picture. The view across the hilly Appenzellerland is already far-reaching. From Hundwiler Hütte, you can also see the Alpstein with Kronberg and Suntis as prominent points. The descent takes you across open meadows to Gonten. The starting and end points can be reached with the Appenzell cable cars.

title: Fountain Paint Pots
short_description: A short and easy trip, but rich in a number of colorful hot mineral springs and pools, as well as a number of low but impressive geysers
long_description:
A great circular hiking route due to the thermal springs and the colorful and special thermal/mud pools in its territory as well as due to its active geysers. The most active geysers in this route do not spray to a great height, but they release a lot of smoke and emit water actively and in a form reminiscent of a water fountain, hence the name given to this route. Most of the walk is on the level, on wooden bridges, but there are also a few steps.
Due to the stairs in the place, the route is not fully accessible to strollers and wheelchairs, but the part up to the stairs can definitely be done on both sides. Children who are able to walk a distance of about a kilometer will be able to navigate the route relatively easily even without a stroller.
A great hiking route even for those who are not good at walking and still want to experience natural wonders.

title: Hüreli
long_description: From Davos Stilli you go up via the Steinschlagwald forest to Chaltboden. Continue climbing along the ridge to just below the Hüreli. With a left turn you reach the summit. Enjoy the unique view and continue hiking along the ridge to Pischa to the Mitteltälli station, where the cable car takes you to Davos Dörfji.

title: From the meadows of Seceda to Piz Duleda
short_description: Hike in the heart of the Dolomites from the Seceda meadows to the summit of Piz Duleda, with a small section of equipped trail.
long_description:
This route leads to the discovery of the true heart of the Dolomites, passing through some of the most iconic and well-known views but also discovering new and decidedly less frequented corners and viewpoints.
The landscape here is constantly changing. You start from the green meadows of Seceda at the top station of the Col Raiser gondola and here you begin to climb gently, enjoying the view of the Odle peaks in front and Sassolungo and Sassopiatto behind you. You then walk at the foot of iconic dolomite peaks such as Gran Fermeda, Gran Odla and Sass di Mesdì.
Entering Val dla Roa, the view changes and you ascend within a rock amphitheater to Furcela dla Roa; a short and easy equipped passage now begins (for the less experienced it is advisable to bring a via ferrata kit) that quickly gains altitude to the foot of Piz Duleda.
The climb to the summit is steep but the 360° view from the summit repays any effort. From up here the view sweeps almost infinitely, touching the most famous mountains of the Dolomite area such as Sassolungo and Sassopiatto, Cinque Torri, Sass de Putia, Lagazui, Marmolada and many others. A true spectacle.
The descent from the lace takes place along the same trail but then you choose another path going down some steps and, skirting Rio Cisles, reaching Rifugio Firenze for a refreshing drink.
From here it is a short walk to the Cabinovia.

You can comfortably drive to the mountain station at 1280 m.ü.m. with the Habergschwänd mountain restaurant. title: Between resorts on the Amalfi coast: Amalfi - Ravello
short_description: The resorts on the Amalfi coast can be reached not only by the main scenic road, but also by foot, on numerous side roads and paths with stairs. This route is one of the many possibilities to cross from one resort to another, enjoying the fabulous scenery and (lots of) movement.
long_description:
The route starts in Amalfi, right in the Museo della Carta. Many signposts and guidebooks recommend a foray into the Valle delle Ferriere; there are signposts for this, but we wanted to get to a nearby resort.
The route goes uphill for quite a while, up wide or narrow, gentle or steep stairs. For resting, there are stone benches. Just off the main road, the lemon groves of Valle delle Ferriere are almost always in sight. Behind, through the openings of the staircase, you can see the roofs of Amalfi and the Tyrrhenian Sea.
After a few hours, depending on your pace, you reach the quiet little town of Pontone, where you can see the terraced hills between Amalfi and Atrani, with their luxurious villas and panoramic balconies.
The route goes a little way along the road and then back up the stairs. Beautifully painted ceramic signposts guide you to Ravello. After about 30 minutes, you enter the resort, close to the centre. Visit everything you like, then allow yourself plenty of time to get out.
We descended in the evening, under the gardens of the Cimbrone villa, through a slightly wilder, unlit area. The last stretch were just very steep stairs.

title: Mattjisch Horn
short_description: Across snow-covered fields and mountains, the snowshoes take you leisurely to the summit of the Mattjisch Horn.
long_description:
Wonderful snowshoe tour in the midst of the snow-covered mountain world with a fantastic view. From the Fideriser Heubergen, we slowly climb up to the Arflinafurgga, where we reach the Mattjisch Horn via the ridge. Here a great panoramic view of some of the most famous Swiss peaks awaits. The descent is down to the Casanna ski house, from where you can follow the toboggan run to Langwies. Those who prefer to descend by toboggan can hire one from the ski house.

The beautiful nature of the Allgäu can be enjoyed to the full and discovered in a playful way. title: Winter ascent in Piatra Craiului to Ascuțit/ Carol Lehman refuge
short_description: A difficult route in winter conditions, with parts that pose an avalanche risk (a detail specified on the signposts), but with wonderful views if the ridge is clear.
long_description:
Start from Fântâna lui Botorog on the classic route that goes up to Curmătura Cabin. Depending on the number of hikers so far, on the know conditions, and on the temperature, the foliage can sometimes be mixed with ice, as has happened now.
Take a short break for hydration and possibly go to the toilet at Curmătura Cabin. However, a longer stop is not recommended because the route is still long.
The ascent to the ridge and to the Ascuțit Refuge begins as a constant ascent through the forest, crossing several valleys. In dry season, there is rubble on the valleys; in winter, everything is covered in snow.
The difficult ascent begins somewhere in the middle of this segment, when the climb gets very steep (about 38% degree of inclination). The winding path in the summer months becomes almost a straight ascent in the winter, depending on the traces previously made. In the absence of traces, the effort is doubled.
The short segment provided with chains I knew existed somewhere was now completely buried under the snow. Above the valley, we came out in an area of juniper, fir, and rock. Partly scattered snow hid deceptive chunks of ice.
The ridge (and the whole route, by the way) remained shrouded in fog while we rested in the shelter. Somewhere nearby, a few dozen yards away, the Ascuțit Peak was hiding in the clouds.
We descended on the same route, carefully, keeping as much as possible the traces already made and with a longer stop at Cabana Curmătura.

title: Santo Isidro Waterfall Trail
short_description: A hike to one of the main waterfalls in the highland region of the Serra da Bocaina National Park, in São José do Barreiro, SP.
long_description: This walk coincides with the initial stretch of the famous Trilha do Ouro (or Mambucaba Trail) and begins at the gateway of the Serra da Bocaina National Park. The Santo Izidro Waterfall is one of the highlights of the park and its fall is an impressive 70 meters high, forming a beautiful pool perfect for bathing. The waterfall is located only 1.5 km from the entrance and the trail is well signposted.

title: Bibbona - Tour of the Macchia della Magona Nature Reserve
short_description: The tour leads through the Macchia della Magona nature reserve. This area is known for its challenging mountain bike tours and its beautiful hiking trails.
long_description: It is pleasant to hike on the paths that have been laid out. The signposting is present in large parts of the nature reserve but should be used with caution. The information boards are unfortunately only written in Italian and some of the locations are incorrectly marked. The route leads on partly unpaved ground over the officially signposted hiking trails 5 and 9. It leads through the pine forests typical of the region above the vineyards with a great view all the way to the Mediterranean Sea.

title: Heerweg / Ox Trail through North Jutland - North Stage
short_description: In the original, the Heerweg / Ox Trail starts in Fredrikshavn, In this version, the first stage starts from the northernmost point of Denmark and goes to Hobro.
long_description:
The Heerweg is a historical route that has served a variety of purposes over the centuries. The military could move quickly from north to south on it, oxen were driven from Viborg to the ox market in Wedel near Hamburg and pilgrims used the route in a northerly direction on their way to Nidaros in Norway and in a southerly direction to Rome.
Today the Heerweg, Hærvejen is a well-developed long-distance cycle route and part of Eurovelo 3.
The first stage starts in Skagen, where the North Sea and Baltic Sea meet. This is the northernmost point in Denmark. To get used to it, you cycle the first 40 km to Fredrikshavn, where the Heerweg officially begins.
For 210 km, the Heerweg continues south past Aalborg, Denmark's fourth largest city, to Hobro at the end of the Mariagerfjord.
With arrival and departure and sights along the way, you can plan a good week for this first stage of the long-distance cycle route Heerweg.

title: A trip to Grawafall
short_description: A relatively short and easy hiking route with a great view in the Stubai Valley (South Tyrol) that reaches several viewpoints on the formidable Grawa Falls
long_description:
This itinerary is one-way and will lead you to a number of viewpoints on the Grawa waterfall, which is considered one of the largest and most impressive in the Tyrol region. It is a waterfall with a 85-meter-wide solid structure, due to its natural structure, the water flows from it in a way that resembles stairs, and this from a height of more than 120 meters!
There you can enjoy a number of observation points on the waterfall, so for example within a few minutes of walking you can reach the first observation point in the form of a wide balcony with luxurious reclining benches from which you can enjoy a special angle observation of the waterfall.
It is recommended to visit the place especially around the month of July, since during this period the flow of water in the waterfall is especially abundant and powerful due to the snow that melts and feeds it. An excursion route recommended for those who love water as well as for those who wish to enjoy a formidable view within a short walking distance.

title: Circular hike with magnificent panorama near Ofterschwang
short_description: A beautiful circular hike without any notable climbs via the small district of Wielenberg and the Wittelsbacher Höhe near Schweineberg with wonderful panoramic views of the Allgäu mountains.
long_description: The varied tour leads across meadows and through forests and always offers a magnificent view of the Allgäu mountains. It is definitely worth climbing the small hill and vantage point "Wittelsbacher Höhe". The family-friendly circular route can be extended as desired. There are also refreshment stops along the way.

images.caption: Hiking in the Allgäu: circular hike with a magnificent panorama near Ofterschwang

title: Landslide experience
short_description: On this hike with its great views, you will get a good overview of the departure of the great Flims landslide and of the landslide masses and their deposition area.
long_description:
The water systems are at least as exciting: Further down, the Segnesbach is called Flembach. It meanders through meadows and forests and through the Stennatobel. Below Flims village it has found a path between the rock of the Flimserstein and the landslide mass. At point 1245 a water conduit branches off, which once served to irrigate the meadows of Conn. Further down, the Drausbach is called Laaxerbach. It is used to generate electricity. The outflow is also collected from Lag Tiert, the headwaters of a wide karst lake. Lag Prau Pult is connected to Lag Tiert underground. In spring, when the water level of the karst lake is high enough, it is filled. Its outflow is as an overflow into the Pultébach and underground, to feed the Lag Prau Tuleritg and ultimately Lake Cauma.

The hike leads from Foppa through the Uaul Steina with Erika-Föhrenwald on landslide mass to the Segnesbach and to the Maiensäss Muletg. At Ault la Runca, a small sinkhole can be seen between the pioneer-like forest cover. Continue to Runcahöhe, where the bend in the path offers a fantastic view of the erosion forms of the Drausbach. Via Runca Sura we reach the Uaul Runca, the sedimentation area of the landslide with a coarse blocky surface. Lag Prau Pulté can be circumnavigated on a comfortable path. In winter, this lake is completely dry. In sections you meet the Pulté stream until you reach the cantonal road above the campsite. From there it is only a few minutes to the Flims Waldhaus post office.

title: Les Bois - La Ferrière
short_description: This hike offers a wonderful panorama of the Doubs valley.
long_description: It goes from Les Bois to Biaufond and through the gorge of Biaufond to La Ferrière.

title: About the Pont des Anabaptistes
short_description:
Auf dieser Wanderung können wir nicht nur die Weiten des Juras geniessen sondern uns auch bei den verschiedenen Berggasthäusern kulinarisch verwöhnen lassen.
Translate to English
long_description:
On this hike, we can not only enjoy the vastness of the Jura but also indulge in the culinary delights of the various mountain inns. From the Place centrale, we head straight for the Pont des Anabaptistes (Anabaptist Bridge) where various panels give us an insight into its history. Up to la Cuisinière we hike briefly through the forest and across a pasture. From here, follow the signs to Petite Douanne. A short stretch on hard surface follows. Then we walk uphill along a dirt road, over pastures and through forest past Le Pletz to Petite Douanne. We tackle another climb until we reach the Métairie du Milieu de Bienne. Downhill over pastures and through forest we reach Hacki. There is another short ascent to Clédar de Pierrefeu until we are back at the starting point.

Note(s)
Arrival: The best way is by car via Biel-Frinvillier-Les Prés-d'Orvin-Métairie de Prêles to the car park at the Place centrale (central square).

title: Panoramic circular hiking trail
short_description: Scenic hike starts at Courtételle railway station.
long_description: We walk through the forest of Combe-Aléry to the mountain restaurant Chez les Pic. We then follow the path along the edge of the pasture to the Pic forest, then up through some rocky areas to the ridge until we reach the Derrière le Château. We go up a little more until we reach the hut on the Haut du Droit. Now we tackle the descent, past the Futchies mountain restaurant. Through the gorge we return to the starting point.

title: 33.07 St.Moritz - Osp. Bernina, Via Albula/Bernina
long_description:
The hiking trail along the Rhaetian Railway's UNESCO World Heritage route runs as close as possible to the Albula and Bernina line and repeatedly offers enchanting views of a more than 100-year-old synthesis of the arts in a magnificent Alpine landscape.

Through moorland and alpine pastures to the Bernina Pass. Highlight follows highlight. Stazerwald, Pontresina, Morteratsch glacier world, Lago Bianco-Lej Nair watershed and the highest mountains in Graubünden.

Note(s)
Beware: snowfields are possible on high-altitude sections until the summer months.

title: 33.05 Preda - Spinas, Via Albula/Bernina
short_description: The hiking trail along the UNESCO World Heritage route of the Rhätische Bahn runs as close as possible to the Albula and Bernina line and offers enchanting views of a 100-year-old work of art in a magnificent Alpine landscape.

images.caption: Albula Railway Experience Trail © Rhätische Bahn

title: From Bellelay to Tramelan
short_description: Easy hike from Bellelay to Tramelan.
long_description: From Bellelay, a village on the edge of the Franches-Montagnes, you walk towards the moorland of La Sagne. On the other side, at the foot of the steep forest flank of Montbautier, you head towards Les Genevez. The path then climbs gently up to the Prés de la Montagne. We then reach Tramelan. On the entire tour, we hike along artistic dry stone walls several times.

images.caption: Maison de la Tête du Moine.

title: Tramelan - Cortébert
short_description: Hiking trail from Tamelan to Cortébert.
long_description: From Tramelan, the path goes straight uphill. We hike across fields and through dense forest parcels, gaining more and more altitude, until we reach the Bise de Cortébert farm. We then reach the highest point of the tour. A path leads us through the Côte du Droit forest flank down to Courtelary. We then hike along the Suze until we reach our destination, Cortébert.

images.caption: The Combe Grède from the Chasseral

title: Mettembert - Delémont
short_description: Through a wild forest gorge to La Haute de Borne.
long_description: We start in the smallest municipality in the canton of Jura, Mettembert. We first hike down to the stream. Then we follow the stream up into the Combe du Vivier, a rather wild forest gorge. The highest point of the tour is La Haute de Borne, where a long rest is recommended. Afterwards, we follow the path down to Delémont.

title: From Glovelier to St-Ursanne
short_description:
Die Wanderung führt von Govelier hinauf in die Combe du Bé und weiter durch eine wunderschöne Naturwelt.
Translate to English
long_description: From Govelier we hike up to the Combe du Bé where a beautiful natural world awaits us. We gain height on a pleasant incline and hike along the stream for a while. We leave the Combe and continue towards Le Bosnire. Through the forest, it's first a steep descent, then flatter again out onto the open pastureland. We pass the hamlets of Montmelon and continue our hike along the Doubs to St-Ursanne.

title: Bohusleden - Stage 12 - Kaserna to Svarteborg
short_description: The second stage of Bohusleden leads from Kaserna along the rivers Munkedalsälven and Örekilsälven to Svarteborg.
long_description: The landscape of southern Sweden is incredibly rich in rivers and lakes. On this stage we experience nature at its best. We walk along two rivers and small ponds that provide a habitat for many beavers and salmon. Then the trail leads through easy terrain in the Harska nature reserve, past prehistoric stone circles and burial sites.

images.caption: View over a southern Swedish lake

title: At the Etang de la Gruère
In the heart of the Franches-Montagnes
short_description: Leisurely circular hike on the Jurah henweg. Across meadows, fields and through forests on the Freiberg Plain;
long_description: Our hike begins in Le Noirmont. We go up through the village. Once at the top, you take the Jurassic path and pass the Saigne aux Femmes farm. Continue straight on into the area of Sous les Craux. The path continues through an unspoilt landscape - the home of the Freiberger horses. After an up and down, you reach the Chez Chailat farm. On a well-marked path, past the hamlet of Le Boéchet, across meadows and fields, you hike back to the starting point.

images.caption: Some cow pastures have to be crossed
Mostly the tour leads without big ups and downs over wide nature paths.
There are plenty of rest areas along the tour

title: Over Mont Soleil to Les Breuleux
short_description: Hike from St. Imier to Les Breuleux. Ascent in St. Imier by train.
long_description: We start our tour at St-Imier station and walk towards the valley station of the funicular railway. With the cable car we climb the first few metres up to Mont-Soleil. This is where our actual hike begins. Past the solar power station we hike uphill to the highest point of the tour. After that, it's all downhill across pastures and through forests to Les Breuleux.

title: Les Bois - Le Noirmont
short_description: Hike on the ridge from Les Bois to Le Noimont
long_description: This pleasant hike takes us from Le Bois towards Sur la Croix. We walk through woodland, along the edge of the forest and over open hills. At Les Barrières we walk along dry stone walls and enjoy the view again and again until we reach our destination Le Noirmont.

title: Rando de la pointe de Congrigoux à Saint Marc sur Mer
short_description:
Belle randonnée aller-retour sur le chemin côtier des douaniers, pour tous niveaux, avec une vue magnifique sur la mer, les pêcheries, les criques et les plages.
Translate to English
long_description:
Le parcours suit le tracé du GR34. Il se fait facilement en famille et permet d’avoir une belle vue sur la mer en longeant la côte. Ce chemin est beau en toute saison, offrant une variété de paysages et d’ambiances lumineuses sur la mer. Il ravira notamment les photographes. Les nombreuses plages et criques traversées invitent à faire de belles pauses pour une baignade ou un pique-nique.
Il y a de nombreuses possibilités de parking au départ à proximité de la Pointe de Congrigoux dont un parking avec bornes de recharge pour voiture électrique juste en face du bar La Caravelle situé au 21 Av. du Littoral à Pornichet.
À cet endroit, il y a aussi une petite boulangerie, une pharmacie et même une petite supérette “Le Relais des Mousquetaires” située au 24 Av. de Villes Babin, Pornichet. C’est très pratique si on veut y acheter de quoi faire un pique-nique.
L’arrivée se fait à la célèbre plage de M. Hulot à Saint Marc sur Mer où il y a de nombreuses possibilités de restauration.
Translate to English

title: From Delémont to the Col des Rangiers
short_description: A beautiful and technically easy but physically demanding tour in the hilly Jura mountains from Deléacute Mont to the Col des Rangiers in the tranquil town of St. Ursanne.
long_description: We start right away with the biggest part of the climb and hike from Delémont towards La Haute Borne. After that, it's practically straight ahead on mainly hard surface. We leave the road and hike first up, then down to the Col des Rangiers. Via La Caquerelle and Le Malrang we reach St-Ursanne.

title: Small round trip
short_description: A panoramic round trip from a moorland lake to a hamlet and over the Cerneux Belin ridge;
long_description: A pleasant little round trip with hardly noticeable ascents and descents. We start in Les Cerlatez and walk to the farm La Petite Theurre. Shortly along the moorland lake Etang de la Gruère, we reach the hamlet of La Theurre. Our walk continues to a slight ridge near Cerneux Belin where we can enjoy a beautiful view of the village of Les Cerlatez, which is also our destination.

title: Round trip over the Col des Rangiers

images.caption: Bahnlinie Chemin de fer du Jura.

title: Jura Trail: Delémont - Moutier
short_description: Hike from Delémont to Moutier.
long_description: For this hike you need a lot of stamina and endurance. A beautiful tour with great panoramas and a historic trail. It takes us from Delémont üvia Mont Raimeux to Moutier.

images.caption: View of the Alps from Raimeux de Grandval

title: Climbing Trail in the Chapada dos Veadeiros
short_description: The Saltos Trail is one of the most stunning routes in the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park.
long_description: This trail runs along the banks of Preto River and presents adventurers with impressive waterfalls of up to 120 meters high. The trail starts at the Tourist Service Centre, near the entrance to the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park, in Alto Paraíacute;so de Goiás, but precisely on the outskirts of the village of São Jorge. The trail is well signposted with yellow arrows and it is not necessary to hire a guide. The number of visitors on the Trail is restricted, so start early and avoid holidays and weekends. Remember to bring cash, as access to all of PARNA's trails costs R$ 18 per person.

title: Jura Trail: Sonceboz - Biel
short_description:
Eine schöne Tour entlang der Suze.
Translate to English

title: Hiking up to the Rumer Alm - Starting in the village of Rum
short_description: This relaxing Rout leads along beautiful forest paths to the Rumer Alm and offers a breathtaking view over the Intaal and the city of Innsbruck.
long_description:
The hike to the Rumer Alm is an absolutely recommended destination in snow-free months. In about an hour you have left the hustle and bustle of the city behind and can enjoy the view over the Intal and Innsbruck with delicious Tyrolean food.
Our tour starts in the village of Rum and leads at the beginning through a branched deciduous forest. After half an hour we reach the wide main forest path, which takes us to the Rumer Alm after another 30 minutes. Be sure to order one of the Tyrolean specialties here, such as Kaspress Knödel, and then enjoy the sun from the hill with a full belly!
On the way back you can walk on forest paths as well as on the main path back down to the parking lot.

images.caption: Wanderung zur Rumer Alm - Start in Rum

title: The Mont Girod
short_description: It is a varied round in the heart of the Faltenjura.
long_description: We start at the station in Moutier. Initially, the trail runs along the road, then branches off onto the hiking trail. We climb up to the farm of Petit Champoz. Then we follow the path up through the forest to the viewpoint «Point de vue» on Mont Girod. A fantastic view of Moutier awaits us. We descend to the Joux fork and follow the path westwards across pastures of the Pâturage de Mont Girod. Passing the Mont Girod farm, we reach Lac Vert via steps and pastures. Through the forest and up some steps, we follow a forest path that descends steeply until we reach the entrance of the gorge. The impressive gorge path through the Gorges de Court leads through a tunnel and over footbridges. Soon we are back at our destination in Moutier.

title: From Schwarzenburg via Guggershorn to Zollhaus
Eggelsberg glacier rim trail
short_description: A landscape formed by the glacier and stones that come from the Hohe Tauern. A voyage of discovery üover the national border around Eggelsberg.
long_description: It is hard to believe that the Salzach glacier almost filled the Salzburg basin to the summit of the Gaisberg and was a good two hundred metres thick at the height of the Bavarian border town of Tittmoning. The end moraines that characterise the landscape around Eggelsberg were also deposited by the Salzach glacier at the height of the last ice age. The hike along the Gletscherrandweg (Glacier Edge Trail) is a very special experience and describes a circuit through a landscape with a diverse wealth of forms and shows the traces left behind by the thrust of the outgoing glacier.

images.caption: Some erratic blocks were transported from the Hohe Tauern mountains to the Innviertel region

title: Along the Blackwater and the Sense
long_description:
From Schwarzenburg you first go down towards Grasburg. A stairway takes you up to the outer castle and on to the main castle. A metal ladder leads up about 700 m into the Hohenstaufen Imperial Castle and then down onto a path that is not marked on the map. Again you descend steeply via stairs. After the rock gate, take the better path southwards around the castle rock and up to the picnic area. It goes down on a narrow path to the Harrissteg. Cross the bridge and descend to the stony bank. Now you ford the Sense for about 1.5 km until you reach the bridge of Ruchmühle on the left bank. Cross the bridge and keep left. Now you "water-walk" again for about 2 km. On the right bank you meet a path that leads to the confluence with the Schwarzwasser, where you pass under the suspension bridge. You wade through the water for the last time to save yourself the long diversions to the bridge in the Schwarzwasser ditch. Then it's along the right bank of the Sense on the hiking trail past the buffalo rock to Thörishaus.

Note(s)
Recommended in summer and in good weather conditions as you wade through the river bed. There may be closures in the Sensegraben during the bird nesting season.

title: Choleren Gorge
long_description:
The starting and end points are Thun. First the trail leads along the Aare to Hünibach on Lake Thun. Then you leave the lakeshore and follow the Hünibach up through the picturesque Choleren Gorge with its waterfalls. The first destination is then the Rabenflue with its beautiful viewpoint. The trail now descends somewhat more steeply to Jakobshübeli and back to the destination of Thun.

Note(s)
Partially T2 spots

title: View of the Ravenna Bridge (Ravennabrücke)
short_description: A short and easy hiking route that leads within a few minutes' walk to an impressive view point on the Rowan railway bridge near the Rowan gorge in the Black Forest (High)
long_description:
This hiking route includes a short and relatively moderate ascent that leads to a panoramic view point on the Raven railway bridge as well as the valley and the surrounding mountains. The relatively short walk on this route will lead you to a high point and a good view of the area. It is possible to combine the walk on this route as an addition to the walk with Ravon Channel .
This route is not shaded and due to its nature it is not suitable for walking with strollers, but due to its length even young children can manage to walk it on foot.
** Due to the fact that the route is linear, the walking time as well as the distance shown are for one direction only.

images.caption: From here the ascent to the observation deck begins

title: In the Chasseral Nature Park
short_description: A popular hike in the Chasseral Nature Park.
long_description: From the Hotel Chasseral, we follow the ridge in a southerly direction. We hike gently up and down through rocky terrain, then descend somewhat more steeply down a pasture to the Métairie de l'Ile. From here we hike down the alpine path and then rejoin the Jura ridge path and follow it to the alpine farm of Chuffort. Then we leave the ridge path and hike in the direction of Clémensin. Pass the striking house with bell tower and turn right onto the field path. At the next fork, take the left-hand path and you will reach the entrance to Combe Biosse. There is a steep ascent through the stony gorge, then a moderate climb along the ditch through pastures back to the starting point.

title: Saignelégier
short_description:
Konditionell fordernde, aber aussichtsreiche Tour auf dem Jura-Höhenweg, mit Sicht auf die beschauliche Felskette Sommêtres. 
Translate to English
long_description:
In Saignelégier beginnt die Wanderung dem gelb-rot markierten Jura-Höhenweg entlang bis zum Bahnhof von Muriaux. Weiter geht es stetig hinauf bis zum Aussichtspunkt Rochers des Sommêtres. Danach verlässt man den Höhenweg und steigt steil hinab durch Wald parallel zum Grat von Sommêtres. Bis zur idyllisch gelegenen ehemaligen Mühle Le Theusseret, folgt nochmals ein kräftiger Steilabstieg. Auf einem flachen Weg immer dem Lauf des Wassers folgend, gelangt man nun nach Goumois. Hier steigt der Weg nochmals an, bis es dann über Weiden wieder zurück nach Saignelégier geht.

Translate to English

images.caption: Der Felskamm Les Sommêtres. Ein Paradies für Kletterer und eine Augenweide für jeden Wanderer
In Luftiger Höhe - Sicht auf den Doubs
Schöne Wasserläufe in der Nähe des Restaurants Le Theusseret
Wild und majestätisch. Der Fluss Doubs

title: Gorge of the Tabeillon
short_description: Hike through the romantic gorge of the Tabeillon
long_description: We start in Saulcy and follow the road briefly, but then take the footpath. Through fields and meadows we reach the Sur les Roches farm. Then we descend to La Combe. We continue along the railway tracks through the romantic gorge of the Tabeillon. Past the Etang de Bollement, we follow the path along the stream to Combe Tabeillon. Here we cross the stream and hike steeply uphill back to the starting point.

title: Between Switzerland and France
short_description:
Schöne abwechslungsreiche Rundwanderung am Grenzfluss Doubs entlang. Die Tour startet und endet in der Schweiz, in Biaufond. Die Wanderung verläuft aber grösstenteils in Frankreich.
Translate to English
long_description:
Beautiful, varied circular hike along the border river Doubs. The tour starts and ends in Switzerland, in Biaufond. However, most of the hike is in France. First we follow the narrow path along the river bank to the Barrage du Refrain dam. Passing the power station, we come to the start of the via ferrata and the so-called "death ladders". We quickly gain height on the zigzag path in the forest and then climb the steep cliffs of the Doubs via two long iron ladders. A dreamlike view awaits us. Behind the clearing of Les Côtes, we hike on a wide forest path to the high plateau. We reach the road that leads us to the car park of La Cendrée. We follow the unmarked tracks that lead us to the Belvédère Sur les Roches, a magnificent viewpoint. We then continue along the path to Fournet. There is a short stretch on the road to Blancheroche and then we take the hiking trail to La Rasse, down to the Doubs. Along the riverbank we'll return to Switzerland.

Note(s)
In wet conditions, the ladders can be slippery.
Take your identity card with you.

title: Round trip in the Ajoie region
short_description: Panoramic, leisurely circular tour along the Doubs. From the Goths of Réclère üover the border into France along the banks of the Doubs back into Switzerland.
long_description: We start at the caves of Réclère. Following the road, we cross the border and descend through the forest to the French town of Vaufrey on the banks of the Doubs. As far as the village of Glère, we hike along the marked east bank path. Then there is an ascent via the hamlets of Vernois and Le Fol. We return to Switzerland and reach the Faux d'Enson lookout tower. At the top, we enjoy a beautiful panorama. Through the forest we follow the path back to the caves of Réclère.

title: Golden Sands of Issyk Kul, Ferris Wheel 72 m - Bosteri
short_description: Sandy beaches, a rollercoaster, the country's tallest 72m high «Devil's Wheel» a boat station, camels, delicious traditional food – all this is about Bosteri, the village resort at Issyk Kul.

images.caption: Bosteri is the most popular beach in Issyk Kul
Lake Issyk Kul - the pearl of Kyrgyzstan
A traditional form of entertainment on the sands of Issyk Kul
Issyk-Kul beach against the background of the Kungei Alatau ridge

title: त्रिंगलवाड़ी किला ट्रैक
short_description: नाशिक ज़िले के इगत पुरी शहर से कुछ दूर स्थित त्रिंगलवा़ी किला 10वी शताब्दी का एक प्रा चीन किला है जो हाईकिंग और ट्रैकिंग के लिए बेहद लोकप्रिय है ।
long_description:
त्रिंगलवाड़ी किला नासिक जिले के इगतपुरी तालुक में त्रिंगलवाड़ी गांव से करीब तीन किलोमीटर दूर स्थित है। यह किला इस इलाके में मौजूद कई किलों में से एक है, जो थाल घाट से गुजरने वाले प्राचीन 'कोंकण-नासिक व्यापार मार्ग' की रक्षा के लिए बनाया गया था।
त्रिंगलवाड़ी किले की ट्रेल आसान और सरल है इसलिए यह ट्रैक सभी के लिए बढ़िया है। किले में जाने वाली सीढ़ियाँ थोड़ी खड़ी चढाई वाली हैं। ट्रेल से हर समय किला दिखाई देता है इसलिए रास्ते साइनपोस्ट की कोई ज़रूरत ही नहीं पड़ती है। ट्रेल पर एक छोटा तालाब भी है। किले से शानदार सहयाद्रि पर्वत श्रृंखला, इगतपुरी शहर, और भव्य कलसुबाई चोटी के पैनोरामिक दृश्य दिखाई देते है।
किले पर कैंपिंग, तम्बू लगाने और रात गुजरने की अनुमति है, हालांकि आसपास कोई रेस्तरां या दुकानें नहीं हैं, इसलिए सलाह दी जाती है कि अगर रात बिताने की योजना हो तो आते समय इगतपुरी से ही सारा जरूरी सामान ले कर आएं।

images.caption: त्रिंगालडी किले का पैनोरमिक दृश्य, इगतपुरी, नासिक जिला, महाराष्ट्र, भारत।
त्रिंगलवाड़ी किले की ट्रेल के करीब मौजूद एक खूबसूरत तालाब, इगतपुरी, नासिक जिला, महाराष्ट्र, भारत।
नासिक जिले के इगतपुरी शहर के त्रिंगलवाड़ी किले के रास्ते में जैन गुफाएँ, महाराष्ट्र, भारत।

title: From the Passion Play location Erl to the Kranzhorn
short_description: We enjoy a varied mountain tour to a magnificent panoramic peak. On the way, you can enjoy a leisurely stop at the Kranzhorn refuge. The view stretches from the Schliersee mountains over the Chimgau Alps and the Lower Inn Valley far into the Zillertal Alps.
long_description:
Passion plays have existed in Tyrol since the Middle Ages. In Erl they have been performed since 1613, today every 6 years. Between 1957 and 1959 a new Passion Playhouse was built because the old one had burnt down. Because of the good acoustics, the Tyrolean Festival has also been held there for some years.
  The Kranzhorn refuge is about 15 minutes' walk below the summit. Hikers are well and abundantly provided with food and drinks there. There is a small playground for children and rabbits can be seen in a cage. The mountain pasture also offers overnight accommodation. However, registration is required here.
The Buchenau is a romantic old mountain pasture that we pass on the way down. Here you could think that time has stood still. This mood is further enhanced by the stone enclosures of the willows.

title: A trip to the Ponte Tibetano Carasc
short_description: A pleasant one-way hiking route leading to a large and impressive suspension bridge in the province/canton of Ticino in Switzerland
long_description:
This hiking route passes through a wooded area and reaches its peak at a long suspension bridge which you can cross with fun and enjoy a gorgeous and panoramic view towards the wooded valley over which the bridge passes. Also, on both sides of the bridge there are historical points of interest that you can admire. On the other side of the bridge there is a fountain with water that can be filled in bottles.
The route itself offers relatively favorable terrain conditions, but nevertheless due to the nature of the route and its width, it is in principle not suitable for walking with strollers.
Walking on the bridge is free, that is, it does not involve any payment.

title: Hierapolis Ancient City Walking
short_description: Alternative walking route in the ancient city of Hierapolis, right next to Denizli's beautiful Pamukkale Travertines
long_description:
The ancient city of Hierapolis, along with Pamukkale Travertines of Denizli, is a historical location that is often wondered and visited a lot. Every year thousands of local and foreign tourists come here to discover the natural and historical beauty of the region.
This short walking route offers an alternative route within the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Hierapolis. Starting from the car park, the route first allows you to experience the magnificent view of the Hierapolis Theatre. Afterwards, you go up to the Agora and continue on the route from the side where the Hierapolis Museum is located. This route, which can be an alternative for those who want to visit the ancient city, ends at the car park again. 
This natural, historical and cultural böltürel bölge is one of the must-visit places in Denizli together with Pamukkale Travertines.

title: Royal Road
short_description: An excellent playground to prepare for races (10km, half and marathon)
long_description:
This course in the forest is mainly on road. Very popular at weekends with people from the Ile-de-France looking for greenery, it allows you to work on your splits with some nice straight lines that serve as a reference point. The course runs along the A13 motorway between Saint Nom la Bret and Feucherolles. Most of the course is flat. However, after passing under the motorway, you come across a section that offers a few levels that allow you to work on your heart rate.
Please note that the course is very easy to ride.
>
The entire course is closed to motorised vehicles. To enjoy the peace and quiet and to avoid the crowds, choose the morning between 7 and 9 am, especially on weekends.

title: Easy walk on Dealul Melcilor (Snails Hill) on an autumn day
short_description: Though many people avoid Dealul Melcilor (Snails Hill) in Brașov because of garbage heaps or dogs, with a little luck, the place offers beautiful panoramas, walking possibilities, and an MTB pump track.
long_description:
A walk on this hill and in the forest at the top is just the right stretching dose you might need on an afternoon. The ascent is easy, there are many paths, and the convenient location between the city center and the Răcădău neighborhood makes it accessible from several directions. In addition, Dealul Melcilor can be climbed by children and is perfect for a walk with the dog.
We started from the Răcădău neighborhood, at the foot of the hill, near one of the water tanks. After admiring the city center and the Tâmpa peak, we continued on the path that walks on the edge of the former stone quarry. The process of natural regeneration is very visible.
Another group of water tanks appeared in front of us, but we took a path to the left quickly arriving at the pump track on the plateau. Here, MTB enthusiasts sometimes come for training. Now, however, it seemed that the route has been abandoned. We descended easily right at the back of the Civic neighborhood, near some barbecue places frequented by noisy teenagers.
Considering the testimonies on the internet, I was probably lucky on this walk - instead of dogs and garbage, I came across lots of autumn flowers, romantic paths full of leaves, and a lot of tranquility. Dealul Melcilor can turn out as a pleasant surprise, despite its troubled history.

title: Loop to the Mazamet footbridge via Hautpoul and Labrespy
short_description: A lovely loop that follows forest paths through chestnut trees, over the factory road and the Arnette valley, before reaching the beautiful medieval village of Hautpoul and of course crossing the void on the now famous Mazamet footbridge.

short_description: Hike from the Pederühütte to the Seekofelhütte
long_description: Beautiful hike in the Fanes-Sennes-Prags Nature Park from the Pederühütte hut near San Vigilio di Marebbe to the Seekofelhütte hut.  The Seekofelhütte hut offers a fabulous view of the Fanes-Sennes-Prags area.

title: Circuit hike to Amfiteatrul Transilvania hotel& restaurant
short_description: The route follows one of the eco-tourist routes marked by an NGO in the Bran-Moieciu area and offers not only panoramic views but also a very human perspective of the places.
long_description:
The Bran-Moieciu area is recognized locally and widely promoted internationally as one of the most picturesque in Romania. In order to discover it in depth, you have to explore more than just the places close to the main road.
The route to the Amfiteatrul Transilvania (Transilvania Amphitheater) takes you to a local landmark for weekend tourism. Fortunately, you only reach it toward the end.  The rest of the route carries you through the truly idyllic landscape above the village of Moieciu, dominated by traditional households, haystacks, and summer cottages, and maybe even facilitates your meeting with a herd of sheep.
You cross Poiana Andolia, with large meadows that are very important for the area's ecosystem. At the end of a deciduous forest, the view opens towards the Piatra Craiului Mountains.
After a short descent into the Grădiștei Gorges, follows a sustained climb that takes you back to the peaceful landscape of the Transylvanian mountain villages.
Catch your breath and enjoy the view at the Transilvania Amphitheater, but keep in mind that reservations are required for the restaurant.

title: Nagatoro Iwadatami round-the-clock course
short_description: A hiking course to enjoy the gentle flow of Nagatoro, the surrounding nature, the rocky cliffs in the area, which is also known as the birthplace of Japanese geology, and the steam locomotives of the Chichibu Railway.
long_description:
The Nagatoro area is made up of crystalline schist, which was formed by volcanic ejecta, mud and sand deposited on the seabed and taken deep underground with the plate around 80 million years ago and subjected to enormous pressure. The rock terrace is 80 m wide from east to west and 500 m long from north to south, and is a fluvial terrace formed by the erosion of the Ara River, which eroded the rock crystal schist, which is easily peeled off like a thin pie crust. The rocks have been broken up by fault movement, leaving the bedrock bare. The rock wall on the opposite bank, which remained uneroded, has become red due to oxidation caused by the iron in the black schist seeping through, and is known as the Chichibu Red Wall, after the Red Wall carved by the Yangtze River in China.
The Nagatoro rock pavement spreads out immediately after Nagatoro Station. The course continues north from there along Kita Sakura Dori (North Cherry Blossom Street). This street becomes a tunnel of cherry blossoms in spring. The Kinseki Water Pipe Bridge next to the auto campsite offers a panoramic view of the Nagatoro river. After crossing the bridge, walk south along the river into Nagatoro Shizen no michi, a path lined with trees. Continue along the road and turn onto Shimotano-dori Street, where you will see the Nagatoro Line Rafting A course boat boarding area. Cross the bridge and enter the footpath over the rock pavement from Sakura-minami-dori. Nagatoro stream can be seen on the right and after passing through the Moonstone Maple Park, you will come out in front of Nagatoro Station.

When you continue the route you will pass a museum with information on local history. This used to be a place where thieves were hanged. title: Marins Peak Trail
short_description: As one of the most classic mountain trails in Brazil, the Pico dos Marins Trail offers an unforgettable adventure amidst the unique beauty of the Mantiqueira mountain range.
long_description:
As one of the classic routes in Brazilian mountaineering and a must for all who enjoy a good hike and adventure, the Marins Peak Trail is approximately six kilometres long and begins after 1,555 metres at base camp. Pico do Marins é the second highest peak in the state of São Paulo with 2422 meters of height and is á wedged in the Serra da Mantiqueira, right on the border between São Paulo and Minas Gerais, in the Paraíba Valley.
It is recommended that the adventure begins early in the morning with a 4-hour climb through the remnants of the high-altitude Atlantic Forest, passing by the Morro do Careca and the curious Pedra Equilibrada (Balanced Stone). During the climb, the landscape changes and the rocks become more and more visible. The walk é difficult, but  the resume of the summit  é a wonderful view of 360 degrees amid the clouds. The best time to climb é in autumn and winter, so we avoid the summer storms and the cooler air also helps during trekking.

title: Crossing Petrópolis - Teresópolis: Day 1
short_description: The crossing between the two mountain cities of Petrópolis and Teresópolis in Rio de Janeiro is one of the most famous in Brazil and is also considered one of the most beautiful;
long_description:
Included in the National Park of Serra dos Órgãos - PARNASO - the recommended duration of the Traverse é of 3 days, so that you can take greater advantage of its stunning landscapes. There is a total distance of 30 kilometres between the two sites, reaching an altitude of 2,275 metres.
The first day of the Traverse begins at the headquarters of the Park in Petrópolis and goes to the Açu Shelter, place for the first overnight stay. The walk is relatively short, approximately 8 kilometres, but due to the large altitude variation (1,145) it is the most difficult and demanding part of the walk.
