title: Alpine hike from Hirzer mountain station Klammeben to the peak Pfandlspitz
short_description: This tour leads from Hirzer mountain station Klammeben via the Hirzer hut to Pfandlspitz and on the way back via Mahdalm and Reseggeralm to the mountain station.
long_description:
The valley station of the Hirzer cable car is in Saltaus (490m) in the Passeier Valley. Take the cable car via the Prenn middle station (1,404 m) to the Klammeben mountain station (1,980 m). Here the tour begins!
From Klammeben you can reach the Hirzer hut via paths and gravel paths. From there it goes up to the Pfandlspitz (2538m), from where you have a great view of the Passeier Valley. The tour leads through alpine terrain and includes rocky sections and secured trails. On the way back you pass the Mahdalm and the Reseggeralm before you reach Klammeben.

title: High alp
long_description: This very popular tour is very busy at the weekend. The ascent from Schwägalp is therefore correspondingly more pleasant and interesting. The first part of the route is clearly marked as a snowshoe hiking trail. It leads over Chräzerenpass to the vantage point at Spicher. From here it goes along the steep flank to Älpli and further along the Ostrippe up to Hochalp. Along the winter hiking trail via Färenstetten, the route leads down to Urnäsch Schwantelen.

title: Sidelhorn
long_description: The tour starts in Oberwald and first follows the alpine road until you reach the forest road towards Grimsel. From here you climb up to the Nassbode, cutting the bends. You can also follow the tracked route. From Nassbode, the trail leads north-west through hollows and a small saddle, later over the SW ridge up to the Sidelhorn, where you have an overwhelming view.

title: Brudelhorn
long_description: This dream tour offers an overwhelming view and is therefore very popular with both snowshoe hikers and ski tourers. From the small bridge next to the railway station, cross the cross-country ski trail in the direction of Mossmattebächi. Now it is important not to cross too early to the left into the forest, so that you meet the path to Unner Flesche. From here the forest thins out and you take a large right-hand bend up to Altstafel. Over hollows and crests, the trail leads in open terrain via Brau over the ridge to the summit.

title: Hiking to the top of Gurghiu Mountains - Saca Mare (1776m)
short_description: The hike up to Saca Mare (1776m), the highest peak in the Gurghiu Mountains, starts near the Aluniș Ski Slope, just outside the Sovata resort. Ideally, you do this route by foot, but there are many who go up with off-road vehicles from Bucin Pass.
long_description:
The route described here is a circuit. It starts from the Sovata stone quarry, about 2 kilometers upstream from the barrier at Valea Sebeșului, which provides access to the quarry road.
The first part of the route is marked with a red dot, and crosses paths with a blue strip pathway about 15 minutes before reaching the peak; the second part descends on this blue stripe path.
The path marked with the red dot is less frequented, sometimes more difficult to guess, with less visible signs in some places, with a fresher and sometimes more surprising nature. Also, while on this section, there are higher chances of meeting a bear.
Shortly after entering the blue stripe route, you get to the Saca Refuge and to an observatory. 10 minutes later, you reach the peak. From the plateau where the Saca Mare peak is located, in clear conditions, you can spot not only the surrounding mountains (Giurgeu, Harghita, Hășmaș) but even Rodnei or Piatra Craiului Mountains. Perfect visibility is usually achieved in winter when there's no atmospheric pressure.
Descending on the blue stripe path, you have more chances to meet other hikers, and the path is broader and more visible. In fact, more than half of this route is on a forest road.

images.caption: Lots of junipers on the Saca Mare plateau

title: My King's Forest trail running circuit 1, Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk
short_description: If you're looking for trail running routes in the Bury St Edmunds area, the quiet surroundings of King's Forest provide plenty of solid options. This is my go-to one when I feel like stretching my legs.
long_description:
Like its larger neighbour (I'm looking at you, Thetford), the great thing about King's Forest is the extensive network of paths and trails that runs through it, which means that you can walk or jog distances that suit your personal fitness level and plans.  The woods are also very peaceful and the further you get from the car parking areas, the fewer people you're likely to encounter. 
As someone who prefers to run longer distances, the thing I like about this particular route is that it blends forest with stretches of open countryside and in doing so, creates a run that is quite actually varied and interesting (relatively speaking).
If you want to mix things up, the route is equally doable in reverse. It's also suitable throughout the year. You can even hike the route if you're not into running. 
Check out my other route nearby:  My King's Forest trail running circuit 2, Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk

title: An interesting walk around the Dubrovica estate
short_description: The charming Dubrovitsy estate to the south of Moscow and west of Podolsk has been boasting of its beauty and sophistication for centuries. But there is no museum in it, much less an entrance.
long_description:
The charming Dubrovitsy estate to the south of Moscow and west of Podolsk has been boasting of its beauty and delicacy for centuries. But it no longer has a museum and entry is forbidden.
Our walking route around the estate will at least give us some insight into the outside of the estate and its park area. There is a linden grove in the park, and rumour has it that Peter the Great planted the first linden trees. The 17th century manor house first belonged to Boyar Morozov. Then the Golitsyns took a liking to it, who never parted with the manor for centuries. However, Catherine II found out about some machinations of her Golitsyn and gave the manor to her new favourite - Potemkin. The tsarina knew a lot about gifts. After Potemkin the estate passed to Count Dmitriev-Morozov. During the Soviet times the estate finally began to serve the people and the land on which it is situated. The Institute of cattle breeding and civil registry office was established in the manor. The beautiful place is now set aside for weddings, and it lifts the spirits of newlyweds.
The main attraction in Dubrovica – is the Church of the Sign of the Blessed Virgin Mary. It was built in baroque style and at first it was so unusual that people resisted its consecration.
But our route awaits us in the parkland, which is free of charge.

title: Nature Experience Trail - Lautertal
short_description:
An interesting tour for children and adults alike.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
We start at the holiday home and walk towards the south until we reach the district road towards Eichelhain. After crossing the road, walk past the sports field to the next windbreak.
Follow this and you will come to a bench with a good view over the district of Engelrod. Continue on to the windbreak that separates the markings, with a wonderful distant view as far as the Rhön.
Downhill to Eichelhain and then steeply uphill again. A long, sloping straight road leads to the district road to Lanzenhain, which we follow for a few metres
and reach the „Karl-August-Vieregge-Anlage“ (named after a former district administrator of the old district of Lauterbach, a special supporter of nature conservation). The nature trail begins here. You can now walk along it or continue to Eichenrod to the children's playground with a rest area.
In Eichenrod you have the option of stopping at the Bloß inn. From there we walk to the Hopfmannsfeld gallows. Here a display board informs about its origin. In addition, there are bars and tables for a rest. From here we walk along paths without steep inclines, past the Engelröm cemetery and back to the holiday home.

title: Hike along the Achensee
short_description: This tour impresses with the scenic beauty around the elongated Achensee. For the way back we choose the ferry across the lake.
long_description:
With an area of approx. 6.8 square kilometres, Lake Achensee is the largest lake in Tyrol. Its main part forms the border between the Karwendel and Rofan mountains. Because of its elongated shape, it is often compared to a fjord. We hike along the lower flanks of the steep rock faces that tower up on its banks.
On the first section of the hike along the Achensee to the Gaisalm, we are offered many bathing opportunities. Up to the Alm, the path is very easy to walk. In the second part, the Gaisalmsteig, it becomes steeper and more exposed. Here, mountain pines alternate with bushes and pines, and in between we pass some scree fields.
At about the halfway point of the tour, we reach the Gaisalm, a managed hut. It is the only alpine pasture with a boat connection and can only be reached on foot or via the lake. Along the lake we experience the vegetation typical of the Karwendel: bushes, alpine meadows, extensive stands of mountain pines, pine forests and scree areas. On the north shore we finally come to the landing stage of the Achensee shipping company. We use a ferry for the way back and can thus admire the blue shining lake in all its beauty.

images.caption: Bay in front of the Gaisalm.
Behind the Gaisalm, the path becomes steeper and more exposed.

title: The Simmental House Trail
short_description: The Simmentaler Hausweg leads past beautiful old farmhouses through the strongly rural Simmental valley.
long_description: Through the village, the trail goes up to Tal and on to Oberberg. The hike continues gently up and down via the hamlets of Eschlen and Balzenberg to Nidflue. Past the former Weissenburgbad, which housed prominent guests for years, but finally burned down in 1974, the trail continues to Brüel to the beautifully renovated Vennerhaus. In the direction of Oberwil, you should let your gaze wander to the right in the direction of the striking rocks. Thousands of bones and stone tools have been found in the three caves there. These can be visited. Finally, in Adlemsried, you hike downhill to your destination Boltigen.

title: From the Rappensee Hut to the Hermann von Barth Hut
short_description: Alpine hike from the Rappenseehütte via the Heilbronner Weg and the Großer Krottenkopf (2656 m) and on to the Hermann-von-Barth Hütte.
long_description:
The alpine hike from the Rappenseehütte to the Hermann-von-Barth Hütte is a long and demanding tour. Between the two very cosy huts, the path is clearly the goal.
The first part takes us along the Heilbronner Weg. This is one of the oldest paths in the Alps and was established more than 100 years ago. Absolute surefootedness and a head for heights are required on this trail, as it runs directly along the ridge of the Allgäu main ridge in some places. Along the way, there are numerous panoramic views over the Allgäu and into the Lech valley with its mountains. In good weather, you can always make out the Zugspitze and the Wildspitze on the horizon. One of the highlights is the Heilbronner Thörle. This is a crevice in the rock, which is already very narrow with a large rucksack. A short time later there is a 5 m high airy ladder to climb and we reach the highest point of the Heilbronner Weg, the Steinschartenkopf. Directly afterwards, a small bridge has to be crossed on the ridge. In the further course, there are repeatedly passages secured with steel ropes, until we finally reach the end of the Heilbronner Weg after the Bockkarkopf at the Bockkarscharte.
We then cross the - still remaining - rest of the Schwarzmilz Ferner. Up to the turnoff to the Großer Krottenkopf at the Krottenkopfscharte, the trail leads without any major technical demands, at first in an up and down and later sharply uphill through a varied landscape. From the Scharte, the path up to the Großer Krottenkopf becomes more demanding again, so that absolute sure-footedness and a head for heights are again required here. On the summit of the Großer Krottenkopf, which is the highest peak in the Allgäu, we have a wonderful 360-degree view.
We leave the highest point of the tour and descend into Hermannskar to the ice-cold Hermannskarsee. The trail continues on mostly rocky terrain towards the Hermann-von-Barth Hut.

images.caption: Großer Krottenkopf (2656 m) - Normalweg zum Gipfel

title: Rundwanderweg durch den Dschungel Pozuzos inklusive Museumsbesuch Casa Palmatambo
short_description: Rundwanderweg der im Centrum von Pozuzo startet, durch den Primärwald führt und zum eikehren in der Casa Palmatambo (Museum) einlädt.
long_description: Start und Endpunkt der Wanderung ist der Plaza de Armas im Centrum von Pozuzo. Über die Brücke Puente Emperador Guillermo I von der aus man einen schönen Blick auf der Rio Huancabamba genießen kann führt der Wanderweg weiter durch einen tollen Primärwald und verläuft am Museum Casa Palmatambo vorbei. Dort kann man einen Einblick in das Leben der Auswanderer von 1859 bekommen. Kurz darauf erreicht man der höchsten Punkt der Wanderung bevor es wieder ins Tal zurück geht und man kurzzeitig parallel zum Fluss läuft. Wieder an der Brücke angekommen kann man anschließend im Zentrum von Pozuzo z.b. im Tipico Pozuzo einkehrern und einen leckeren Kartoffelsalat mit Schnitzel genießen.

title: From Saint-Raphaël to Arles
short_description: The third/last stage of Via Aurelia is for exploring natural sites and leads you to Arles, one of the oldest French cities.
long_description: With a total length of approx. 200 km, the last stage of Via Aurelia offers a lot of space for spontaneous stop-offs at the coast or in the French hinterland. Off the route you can find two particular geolocial sites, the plateau of “Balcons de la Mescla“ and the breathtaking canyon of Verdon. At the end of the tour, in the city of Arles you can enjoy one of the oldest cities of France with its well-preserved ancient buildings. Even passionate hikers will find a suitable tour at a nearby regional park.

title: A trip to the "Thieves' Path" through the Hausbach Gorge (Räuber-Kasimir-Weg)
short_description: Here is a hiking route with a magical view, which passes by many flowing waters and later enters a forest where there are several stations with fun and exciting activities for children
long_description:
It is a circular trip starting from the center of the town of Weiler in the Allgäu region of southern Germany. The beginning of the path is in a field, but very quickly the road becomes a promenade shaded by trees along the length of a stream called the Hausbach (German: Hausbachklamm). Along the way you will see wooden signs with the face of an elderly person with a finger pointing to the right direction of walking towards the forest where the road called "Thieves' Path" (in German: Räuber-Kasimir-Weg) passes. This is a themed road where there are several game stations for children, including ball tracks.
Beyond the fact that the itinerary is simply beautiful, it is also wonderful for families and will arouse the children's interest and enthusiasm for nature.

title: Stelvio Marathon
short_description: Every year in June, the so-called Stelvio Marathon takes place, leading passionate runners up one of the most beautiful mountain passes in the Alps.
long_description: The original route of the Stelvio Marathon has it all, but offers an unforgettable experience with the legendary Stilfserjoch pass road and the view of the imposing Ortler group. Those who want to spare themselves the initial kilometres around Prad choose the Classic route, which is signposted throughout its 26 kilometres.

title: Sunday tour Mariaberg via the Alpine Club Trail from Kempten West
short_description: Beautiful hike on Kempten's local mountain. Also suitable for families.
long_description: The route in Kempten West starts out on paved footpaths, later we find ourselves on a gravel path or forest trail. If you like, you can stop off at the innkeeper's on the Mariaberg, but we walk straight on to enjoy the magnificent all-round alpine view. On some days the Zugspitze looks close enough to touch. We continue and soon find ourselves on a tarred road again. We look for the way into the forest to enjoy the forest path (Alpenvereinsweg) running parallel to the ridge. Here we find oodles of interesting spots for the little hikers among us: steps, bumpy paths, large and small roots and a waterfall. After this little adventure, our path leads back to the city on gravel. There are many ways to get back to the starting point in the city. Have fun on the tour!

title: Trail running up and around the Piesenkopf (1,630 m) by Rohrmoos, Allgäu
short_description: A fun run in Rohrmoos' back of beyond that takes in the summit of the Piesenkopf (1,630 m) and some superb views over both the Nagelfluhkette and Hoher Ifen - weather permitting.
long_description:
Up a snaking valley that sets it at an almost antisocial distance from its closest neighbours, the tiny and very pretty hamlet of Rohrmoos lies next to the Starzlach river in what feels like the proverbial end of nowhere.  However, with moody cliffs that lead up to the Gottesacker Plateau and the rolling slopes of the Nagelfluhkette, it's this very sense of isolation that makes the area not just extremely attractive to look at but also a lovely and peaceful place to get out in nature.  
This run starts in the village before taking you up a forested road that leads to the Piesenalpe. From there it's a relatively short hop to the summit of the Piesenkopf followed by a somewhat chaotic descent through ankle-busting grassland to the track that eventually leads you back down to the village, your car, and a change of clothes.
Gorgeous views of the Ifen, Besler, the wider Nagelfluhkette, and the Allgäuer Hochalpen form the backdrop along the way, and needless to say, the route is also perfectly suitable for hikers... and can be done in reverse : )

title: Litton Cressbrook Loop
short_description: Get a taste of the Peak District in one shortish hike down dales, through woodland, and over the rolling hills, with a couple of picturesque villages too.
long_description:
This hike gives you a taste of the Peak District all in one shortish hike.

Through Tansley and Cressbrook Dale, through woodland with a small river (or dried river bed, depending on the time of year), and then up through the pretty daleside village of Cressbrook, and back over the rolling hills to Litton.

Note: the footpath on this route between Cressbrook and Litton includes a short section that is along the top of a steep side into the dale.  Care should be taken.

title: Howard Davis Park to Maritime Museum
short_description: This Jersey Heritage walk offers a glimpse into the life of one of Jersey's greatest philanthropists - Thomas Benjamin Davis.
long_description:
This walk offers a glimpse into the life of one of Jersey's greatest philanthropists - Thomas Benjamin Davis.  The son of a ship's carpenter he was a self-made millionaire, a friend of King George V, yet he never forgot the island of his birth.

Facing the statue of George V, bear left and follow the path to the Billiard Room, the only remaining part of Plaisance, the magnificent house bought by Davis in November 1937, and immediately knocked down. Inside we find a portrait of Howard Leopold Davis, Davis’ younger son, who was wounded in July 1916, on the first day of the Battle of the Somme and later died of his injuries.

Follow the path, and turn left through the gates to pass St.Luke’s Church. Davis was a choir boy here. One anecdote recalls Davis and Walter Braithwaite, the rector’s son, raiding the chestnut trees in the grounds of Plaisance. They were caught by the owner Joshua Falle, and, as punishment, Davis was made to clean the boots of the Falle household. On his release, Davis vowed to buy the property and knock it down!

Cross the road and continue on passing St Luke’s School. This was where celebrated portrait painter John Helier Lander and Davis went to school. Lander was commissioned by Davis to paint a portrait of George V, that Davis presented to Victoria College, and which was hung in the Howard Hall at the College.

Walk on along Dicq Road, bear left and cross into Havre des Pas. Continue past the Bathing Pool and follow the promenade beside the beach.

About halfway along is Allix’s Boatyard which stood here until the early part of the 20th century. The Allix family were both boat builders and boat owners, and it was on an Allix boat, The Satelite, that young Davis had a close call. The Satelite had run aground on the Haisborough Sands, 12 miles east of the Norfolk coast, and the Master fearing it was lost, lowered the long boat, with Davis in it, to receive the ship’s papers and other valuables. Within minutes a huge wave snapped the rope securing the long boat, and Davis was cast adrift in the North Sea. He endured 19 hours before being picked up by a Norwegian ship, The Urda. It is typical of Davis that years later, he sought out the crew of the Urda and rewarded them for saving him.

Climb the steps into the park, pass the TA Centre and then descend towards the harbour. Just after the Normandy Memorial, cross over to the white railings and turn right. The granite building that is now the base for the Jersey Rowing Club, was built as the boathouse for The Howard D, Jersey’s first motorised lifeboat. This lifeboat, another gift from TB Davis, has been restored and is usually moored opposite the entrance to the Maritime Museum.

Walk between the fishermen’s huts and emerge beside Le Havre aux Francaises. Descend the steps into the harbour and, using care, cross to the far slipway. In the late 1920s, Davis would over winter his 135 foot racing schooner Westward, in this harbour, the boat filling the entire length of the far pier. Built at Rhode Island by the Herreshoff Manufacturing Company for American millionaire Alexander Cochran, Westward had a number of owners before Davis bought her in the mid 1920s. TB Davis died in 1942. After the Second World War, no one was prepared to take on such an expensive yacht, so following his wishes, Westward was scuttled in Hurd’s Deep off Alderney in July 1947.


Maritime Museum

Discover all about Jersey’s maritime past in this uniquely interactive museum where you can see, touch, hear and even smell the exhibits.

Jersey’s landscape and history have been shaped by the sea and this museum tells the story of the Island’s unique maritime environment and rich seafaring past. Set by the historic harbour of St Helier, the Maritime Museum is all about seafaring, navigation and the elements, told through the stories of Jersey people.

Occupation Tapestry Gallery

Visit the award winning Occupation Tapestry, also located at the Maritime Museum, made by the people of Jersey to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the Island’s liberation.

The twelve panels of this richly coloured tapestry tell the story of life in Jersey during the Second World War. This community work of art depicts Islanders’ personal memories of the war and their experience of living under German occupation



For information on visiting the heritage attraction mentioned in this guide, including admission prices and opening times, visit the Jersey Heritage website www.jerseyheritage.org

title: Della Falls and Love Lake
short_description:
This hike in Strathcona Provincial Park features the highest falls in Canada. It is 15-km to the base of the falls and nearly 3 km to Love Lake.

The trailhead is accessed by boat, kayak, or canoe from one end of Grand Central Lake requiring a 33 km trip. Many choose to use the shuttle service.
long_description:
This hike in Strathcona Provincial Park features the highest falls in Canada (444 metres/1456 ft.); they are spectacular and a must see destination. It is a 15-km hike to the base of the falls with another hike of nearly 3 km to a viewpoint on the Love Lake-Mount Septimus Trail.
The trailhead is accessed by boat, kayak, or canoe from one end of Grand Central Lake requiring a 33 km trip, the other end of the lake.  Many choose to use the shuttle service (see Highlights below).
For those arriving by canoe, there are a few informal campsites along the lake. Scout Beach is a popular recreational site and possible place to launch a canoe (while cutting down on distance to paddle to the Della Falls trailhead). Most suitable camping areas are roughly 3/4 of the way to the Della Falls trailhead along the north shore. There is a rack for kayks and canoes at the trailhead.
The main camps are at the trailhead, Margaret Creek (6.7 km), and near Della Falls (14.2/14.7 km).  There is wilderness camping (12.2 km) on a small beach along Drinkwater Creek.
The main trail follows Drinkwater Creek named after a gold prospector who worked this area in 1899.  The first 10 km is essentially a rail grade interrupted by creek washouts and water damage causing many detours and walking on slippery rocks crossing creeks.  There is frequent water damage on the trail.  Bridging at Margaret Creek for example is higher up the creek for an easier crossing but creating quite a climb and descent. There are usually quite a few tree falls requiring ducking under, detouring, or climbing over. The trail is also overgrown in places.  From the cable bridge it becomes a rugged single track trail and a bit difficult to follow in spots especially the section just past the wilderness camp where the trail heads over large rocks that are part of an old rock fall from the high cliffs looming above.  Flagging is in place for wayfinding.  There are many pleasant sections overall and the tree cover is much appreciated for much of the hike.
The falls are at their best in mid July when glacial run off is at its peak. However, visitors in mid-August will find swimming in Love Lake to be much more comfortable!
Mud isn't a huge issue, but gaitors can come in handy due to thorny bushes that you may encounter on the trail.

title: Easy hike above Bran mountain resort (Măgura Peak)
short_description: A hiking route suitable even for beginners, with superb views over the valleys and hills near Bran and Moieciu mountain resorts, but also with a panorama of the Bucegi Mountains.
long_description:
The route starts with a sustained climb that lasts for about 15-20 minutes. Along the way, at a ”window” between the trees, you get an opportunity to pause and get a glimpse of the panorama that promises to open up above. Upon exiting the forest, you step into a meadow that during the summer is full of wildflowers - a rich splash of color. As you continue, still uphill, but somewhat parallel to the road below, the panorama gets more and more captivating. There are several other clusters of deciduous forests that alternate with meadows where you can see isolated, picturesque houses, some abandoned or occasionally inhabited.
From Măgura Peak (1375m) there is a wider perspective than in the first clearing, but in the same direction (towards Bran, Moieciu, and Bucegi). Depending on the weather, you can see even further beyond. From here, you can descend towards Moieciu village, and then reach the more touristy part of the town.

A typical house for the mountain areas

title: Short walking route Loonse and Drunense dunes
short_description:
This walking route is about 6.5 kilometres and will show you the west of the Loonse and Drunense heaths. 
.
long_description: The Loonse and Drunense Dunes is a beautiful nature reserve consisting of heathland, forest and sand plains. Especially the sand plains make the area special. The landscape is still changing as the wind keeps moving the sand. The heathland is also beautiful. A flock of sheep ensures that the heath stays short.

title: Dronningstien - The Queen's Hiking Trail Hardangervidda
short_description: Dronningstien is the Queen Sonja's hiking trail. It is also called Dronning Sonja's Panorama Tour and offers fantastic views over the Sörfjord and the glacier.
long_description:
"Queen Sonja's Panorama Tour" goes up to 1,100 metres über the mountains between Kinsarvik and Lofthus.
You have a fantastic view of the fjord and glacier on this mountain hike.
This mountain hike offers a fantastic view of the fjord and glacier, and there is the option of walking the mountain stairs. On the last leg of the Dronningstien down to the Sørfjord, you pass several thousand fruit trees.
This hike has everything Fjord Norway has to offer: Fjords, mountains, glaciers and unique views.
The hike on Dronningstien is a classic and fantastic day trip. Hardangervidda National Park on one side and spectacular views of Sørfjorden, Folgefonna and Oksen on the other. The trail was opened by Queen Sonja in 2013 and is the only hike that bears the title "Her Majesty Queen Sonja". This is one of the Queen's favourite hikes, and she has been to the area many times over the past 20 years.

short_description: There are plenty of options to trek from Brașov to Poiana Brașov, and this is one of them. An extremely accessible hike for anyone, in any season.

We started from Pietrele lui Solomon (at the end of the Schei area) and followed the Postavaru trail, for a slightly more rugged route. After exiting the forest into the wide and paved bike path, we simply followed it, without other turning points.
From Poiana Brasov, we returned to the old road - the classic route.

500 metres before the end of the loop, there is another short steep climb for the final sprint.

title: After-work round through Steig and Unterried
short_description: This easy jogging route contains hardly any inclines, runs exclusively  over asphalt and gravel paths and is therefore well suited as an after-work run.
long_description: The loop is ideal to recharge your batteries after a stressful day at work and to enjoy the tranquillity of the small villages of Steig and Unterried. It leads past idyllically situated farms, a wet meadow with rare plant species and through a sparse forest.

title: Erik Larsaberget
short_description: Small hike on the way to Arvidsjaur.
long_description: This short hike is located directly on the E45 and is well suited for a short stopover. After the initial forest road, the trail soon leads up to the summit on a beautiful hiking trail. There is a small lookout tower from which you have a good view of the wide hilly landscapes of Lapland. There is also a small shelter for a comfortable rest and protection against bad weather and mosquitoes.

title: The Bob Graham Round
short_description:
The Bob Graham Round is a 66-mile, 27,000 foot circuit of 42 of the highest peaks in the English Lake District - to be completed within 24 hours.

First done way back in 1932 by Bob Graham, hotelier of Keswick, at the age of 42, the 42 Peak Round has become a testing ground for the supremely fit.
long_description:
The Bob Graham Round is a 65-66 mile*, 27,000 foot circuit of 42 of the highest peaks in the English Lake District within 24 hours.
First done way back in 1932 by Bob Graham, hotelier of Keswick, Cumberland, at the age of 42, the 42 Peak Round has become a testing ground for the supremely fit. Each summer around 100 of the most highly tuned ultra-distance fell runners will attempt the 27,000 ft of ascent within the allotted 24 hours.

The Bob Graham round of 42 Lake District fells traversed within 24 hours is probably the most demanding test of physical fitness available to British Athletes or mountaineers. The rules for the Bob Graham 24 hour club state that the round can be attempted either clockwise or anti-clockwise. provided that the start and finish is at Moot Hall, Keswick.
http://www.bobgrahamclub.co.uk/

* The early pioneers settled on a figure of 72 miles with 27,000 feet of ascent. The use of mapping software and GPS devices has led to a re-evaluation of the distance of the 42 Peak Round. Mapping software gives figures as low as 61-63 miles. GPS systems (which have been carried and operated throughout several successful attempts) give a figure of between 65-66 miles

title: Via Transilvanica - Terra Dacica
short_description: A Via Transilvanica segment steeming with rich history, legends of fantastic beasts, and natural reserves; a route overseen from a distance by the ridges of the Retezat Mountains. The pristine beauty of the two national parks along the route takes some effort to discover. Additionally, you will admire two UNESCO sites: the Țara Hațegului Dinosaur Geopark, respectively the Dacian fortress Sarmizegetusa Regia.
long_description:
The stages of the route are average in length, with moderate elevation gain. Bigger challenges are the lack of water sources or supply stores. Given the novelty of the route in its tourist form, it might be harder to find accommodation in some villages, but locals are always helpful.
Some highlights of this stage are the dreamy landscapes with the mountain ridges, the scenic panorama captured on the edge of Fundatura Ponorului, the traces of dwarf dinosaurs, and the Sarmizegetusa Regia site.
If all goes according to plan - that is, if you follow the distances suggested by the organizers - you should finish the segment in a full week. If the landscape blows you away and off the route for a bit, or unforeseen events occur, the period can be extended.

title: A trip to the Vintgar Gorge
short_description: A linear and easy and short hiking route in the Vintgar gorge in northern Slovenia.
long_description: A magical walking trail in a vintage gorge that mostly passes over hanging wooden bridges, an experience full of shimmering water with mesmerizing colors. The route is relatively easy, short, flat and rich in views.

long_description: A short walk along the River Test to Sadlers Mill and then into Romsey via the Abbey.

title: Climbing the Lahner Kopf (2,093 m) by the Schrecksee
short_description: Get a bird's-eye view of the Allgäu's ridiculously idyllic Schrecksee on this moderate hike to the top of one of the several peaks that surround it.
long_description:
The Shrecksee is well known for its picturesque alpine setting and as a swimming spot - and it's for these reasons that the area can get crowded with visitors when it's warm.
The idea of bagging a peak I'd not yet been up was more of a lure for me than the lake and as I prefer to avoid crowds, I took it upon myself to start at 05:15 and to go in the middle of May when the water is still partially frozen. I was rewarded for my early start with a peaceful hike up to the summit and having the place almost entirely to myself. 
The views are fantastic and the hike is long enough to make you feel like you've earned that extra portion at dinner. Needless to say, there is also the option of adding extra summits to your trip, such as the Karsten Kopf or, as I did, the Knappen Kopf.

title: Easy trek on Pivnițele Mari Hill, Covasna
short_description: The trek that goes up to Pivniţele Mari Hill is accessible to anyone, including children. If you feel fit or you're on a bicycle, consider continuing the route, as it takes you to Pădureni village & lake.
long_description:
Pivniţele Mari (Great Cellars) Hill is a place of reference for the Hungarian community in Covasna County, also a place full of legends and history.
You won't find any explanatory signs on the spot, so we recommend that you research ahead about what you are going to see, especially if you don't know Hungarian (all the plates on the spot are in Hungarian).
Although you can also drive up there, a walk is preferable, so that you can also enjoy the scenery. Once on the hill, after passing through all the gates and inspecting all the alleys, just enjoy the panorama. On the plateau nearby, there is a wooden observatory where you can climb.
The walk to the Pivnitele Mari is an excellent opportunity to spend a few hours outdoors with the children; they will be delighted by the large grassy plateau, where they can run freely.

title: Sawston - Whittlesford Three Mile Loop
short_description:
Loop walk between the villages of Sawston and Whittlesford in South Cambridgeshire.

Be aware, you cross a busy road twice.
long_description:
Loop walk between the villages of Sawston and Whitlesford in South Cambridgeshire.
Be aware, you cross a busy road twice.

Although the current village of Sawston has only existed as anything more than a hamlet for 400 to 600 years, there is evidence for a settlement in the vicinity dating back to the early Bronze Age almost 5000 years ago. The northern high-ground in Sawston would have been the only vantage point from which to view the ancient Hill figures discovered in the Wandlebury section of the Gog-Magog hills.

Whittlesford village is situated on the Granta branch of the River Cam, seven miles south of Cambridge. Whittlesford Parkway railway station serves the village.
Listed as Witelesforde in the Domesday Book, the name Whittlesford means "ford of a man called Wittel", indicating the importance of a local ford across the river in the village.

title: The Limestone Way (South to North)
short_description: The Limestone Way is a long-distance bridleway in Derbyshire, England. It runs through the White Peak of the Peak District National Park, from Castleton south east to Rocester over the county boundary in Staffordshire. This route runs in reverse, south to north.
long_description: The Limestone Way is a long-distance bridleway in Derbyshire, England. It runs through the White Peak of the Peak District National Park, from Castleton south east to Rocester over the county boundary in Staffordshire.

title: Milton Country Park circuit
short_description: Milton Country Park includes a Visitor Centre with café, play-areas, viewing platforms, a sensory garden and sunclock.
long_description:
http://my.viewranger.com/uploads/storage/t_bf60df3419a96ec5c6c62f3ceae95a5b.jpgMilton Country Park is managed by Cambridge Sport Lakes Trust, who took over the management of the Park from South Cambridgeshire District Council in April 2008. Created from old gravel pits the 95 acre site offers a varied natural habitat interlaced with over two miles of paths, suitable for bicycles and wheelchairs, as well as those on foot. Dogs are welcome and can be walked off lead at the northern end of the park.

The Park includes a Visitor Centre with café, play-areas, viewing platforms, a sensory garden and sunclock.

The Park is open to the public 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. However the car park, the Visitor Centre, and toilet block are open from 8am every day of the year except Christmas Day.

title: Kemer - Kuzdere Track and Back to Kemer
short_description: Kemer - Kuzdere trail, which is one of the popular hiking trails in Kemer Beydağları, also includes the Selçuklu Hunting Park, which is the only Selçuklu structure in this bözone.
long_description:
Kemer offers special opportunities for nature lovers. Beydağları bölgesi region hosts popular routes known by many travellers. 
This route goes around the Kemer - Kuzdere trail, which can be considered as an intermediate route and is a popular route for nature lovers. On the route, it is possible to come across and make a historical visit to the Selç uklu Hunting Kö which is known for being the only Selç uklu structure in the region and attracts attention with its historical value. The route is normally 6.5 km, but the route here is slightly longer as it leads back to Kemer. 
After completing the main line of this route through forest paths, you go back on the same track until a certain point. However, after a while, you take the path on the right and reach Kemer by a different route.
The route ends at Kemer Kuğulu Park.

long_description:
The Kalmhoutse Heide nature reserve is located on the border between the Netherlands and Belgium. It is a beautiful nature reserve where you can go for lovely walks. The Kalmhoutse Heide is a diverse nature reserve. The landscape consists of heathland, fens, woods, meadows and sand dunes.

title: Knapwell - Lolworth - Boxworth
short_description:
Explore the Cambridgeshire countryside including the villages of Knapwell, Lolworth and Boxworth.

With heavy clay underfoot, parts of this route could become very heavy and sticky going in winter or after very heavy rain.
long_description:
Explore the Cambridgeshire countryside including the villages of Knapwell, Lolworth and Boxworth.

The route starts off on part of the Pathfinder Circular Walk, a waymarked circular footpath linking old RAF airfields. The walk commemorates the bravery of the many aircrew lost in the second world war while flying with the ‘Pathfinder’ bomber squadrons from local Cambridgeshire airfields.

At Childerley, we leave the Pathfinder route and head North, climbing slightly, towards Lolworth, before crossing more wonderful Cambridgeshire countryside as we make our way to Boxworth (past Boxworth Manor) and then back to Knapwell.

With heavy clay underfoot, parts of this route could become very heavy and sticky going in winter or after very heavy rain.

title: The Long March from Immenstadt to Kempten
short_description: We experience a beautiful hike through the Allgäu hills with many views and vistas. Despite its length, the tour seems entertaining. On the way there are several places to stop and great side trips.
long_description: The Allgäu hilly landscape awaits us with lakes, ravines, rushing streams, dense forests, wide pastures and pretty hills and villages. The area is bordered to the west by the Hauchenberg and Sonneckgrat hills and to the east by the Illertal valley. To the north it runs between Kempten and the Adelegg and slowly becomes flatter and flatter. The valley with Niedersonthofen and the lake of the same name divides the Hügelland into two halves. There we have also covered about half of the distance. We start our tour in Immenstadt, because here, due to the nearby mountains, the sun sets earlier than in Kempten. So we can safely set off a little later. The former royal seat invites you to take a short stroll before the tour begins, which takes no more than half an hour. On the way, there are several places to stop for a bite to eat, where we can enjoy the regional dishes. If we still have energy and muse after the long walk, we can take a detour into the centre of Kempten. However, we should allow two hours for this.

short_description: यह लूप ट्रेल काज़ीरंगा नेशनल पार्क के पश्चिम रेंज यानि की बागोरी रेंज में स्थित एक सुन्दर नेचर ट्रेल& nbsp;जिस पर सिर्फ जीप सफारी से जाना संभव है।
long_description:
काज़ीरंगा नेशनल पार्क भारत के असम राज्य में स्थित एक यूनेस्को (UNESCO) विश्व धरोहर है। यह प्रकृति और वन्यजीवों को पसंद करने वालों के लिए एक स्वर्ग जैसा ही है। काज़ीरंगा के पश्चिम गेट जिसे बागोरी रेंज भी कहते हैं अपनी जीप सफारी के लिए विख्यात है। असम राज्य पर्यटन और असम वन विभाग की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट से यह जीप सफारी बुक की जा सकती है।
यह निर्देशित दौरा (गाइडेड टूर) बागोरी रेंज के जीप सफारी पॉइंट से शुरू होकर वहीँ वापस आती है। 18 किलोमीटर लम्बी लूप यह ट्रेल घने जंगलों और झील के किनारे जाती है जहाँ हमेशा गैंडे, हाथी, हिरन, और कई सुन्दर पक्षी देखने को मिलते हैं।
इस ट्रेल पर हाईकिंग या साइकिलिंग करने की अनुमति है। सिर्फ काज़ीरंगा पार्क प्रबंधन द्वारा आयोजित जीप और हाथी सफारी ही इस ट्रेल पर की जाती है।एडवांस में बुकिंग करना अच्छा रहेगा क्योंकि इस जंगल सफारी की बहुत मांग है।

title: Black Forest Railway Adventure Trail
short_description: Varied tour along the Black Forest Railway, a technical masterpiece by engineer Robert Gerwig (1820 to 1885).
long_description:
The Black Forest Railway is one of the most beautiful and technically interesting railway lines in Germany. With 38 tunnels, the Black Forest Railway is one of the most tunnel-rich railways in Europe and at the same time the one with the fewest bridges. Construction of the railway was completed in 1873. To this day, the Black Forest Railway is one of the most famous mountain railways in the world and has become the model for many other lines. It connects Karlsruhe and Kreuzlingen over a distance of 250 kilometres. In the process, it overcomes a difference in altitude of 670 metres with a maximum gradient of 20 per mille. 
Our tour takes us along the large switchbacks between Triberg and St. Georgen. Along the way, the Black Forest Railway Experience Trail introduces us to the history of the construction and ongoing operation of the Black Forest Railway between Hornberg, Triberg and St. Georgen. Using vivid examples, the history of the Black Forest Railway comes to life and there are various stopping points dealing with the main topics of the Black Forest Railway

title: Betari River Trail
short_description: Among beautiful waterfalls and incredible caves, the Betari Trail is considered one of the most beautiful trails of the Parque Estadual Tur stico do Alto Ribeira – PETAR.
long_description:
Considered one of the most beautiful trails of the Parque Estadual Turístico do Alto Ribeira – PETAR, the Betari Trail has more than 7km of trail in the preserved Atlantic Forest that protects the river of the same name. The trail follows along the river, passing in front of the caves of the park where it has irrefutable marks of use by primitive men, such as the Cave of Dirty Water and Cafezal Cave, ending in the Andorinhas and Betarizinho Waterfalls.
One of the most beautiful waterfalls is the Cachoeira das Andorinhas, which has a fall of about 20 meters and its name is due to the birds, a species of swallow that nests and spends much time rushing the walls of the canyon that forms the waterfall. At the base of the fall there is a deep pool that you must be careful, but at the exit of the canyon you can swim and relax contemplating the view.

title: Santa's House in Rochers de Naye
short_description: This easy winter hike is ideal for families before Christmas. With views of Lake Geneva and the Alps, a special surprise awaits you: Santa Claus!
long_description:
What could be better than hiking in the mountains with your family during the holidays? This winter hike to the Rochers de Naye, just an hour by train from Montreux, promises to be an unforgettable experience.
The "Train du Père Noël", a charming cogwheel train, takes young and old to the foot of the mountain. After a short 15-minute walk, you will reach the summit of the Rochers de Naye at an altitude of 2042 meters. From here, you can enjoy a breathtaking panoramic view of Lake Geneva, the Alps and the Jura. The ridge path offers spectacular views and is easily accessible.
On the way home, make sure you stop off at the "Maison du Père Noël", where Santa himself awaits you from the end of November to the end of December, from Wednesday to Sunday. Children will receive a surprise gift and an original certificate.
Don't miss out on this magical winter experience!

title: The popular route 'Chersky Peak'
short_description: A varied and impressive hiking route at the foot of Lake Baikal to Chersky Peak. The route is very well known and quite easy to follow.
long_description:
The scenic route along the forest trail to Chersky Peak runs along the Khamar-Daban mountain range. The route is of medium difficulty and is suitable for all lovers of outdoor activities. There is a 'Pival' cafe along the route, where you can have a smoke break on the way. About half way along the trail there is a weather station where you can stop for the night and have a sauna.
It is not an insignificant fact that on this high-mountainous path, when there was no Trans-Siberian railway yet, caravans from Russia to Mongolia and China used to go there. This path is called the Starokomarskaya road. The peak itself was named in honor of the famous geographer and admirer of Siberia Ivan Dementievich Chersky.
The natural route to Chersky Peak passes through cedar forests, which give way to shallow vegetation and leads to the bare rocky peaks of 1st Golets and 2nd Golets. Not far from the summit rests Lake Heart in sublime silence. The view of the lake from the top really displays the heart – amazing!

title: Strelka Park, Yaroslavl
short_description: The main park in Yaroslavl, in its historic location, is undoubtedly Strelka Park.
long_description:
The place in Yaroslavl where the Kotorosl river flows into the Volga is called Strelka, and there is also a park with the same name «Strelka». Walking part of the park is about a couple of kilometers and will take a little time, but the impressions of the park, walking, will surely remain for a long time to come.
The park is divided into two parts: the upper parterre in Rubly Town and the lower parterre on the Spit.
In the park you can find such attractions as a monument to the 1000 anniversary of Yaroslavl, sculpture «Trinity» Stone where according to legend Yaroslavl was founded – its founder Yaroslav the Wise. And, of course, the gazebo on the waterfront – Kotorolskaya.

title: Brudleruta - a historical walking route that follows the bride and groom's journey
short_description: The tour is a historical walking tour and a collaboration between DNT and the Riksantikvaren. The collaboration makes old roads better known and more used. These tours offer great outdoor experiences and unique cultural heritage.
long_description:
The trip follows an old road between Kvinesdal and Sirdal. Sirdal and Kvinesdal. The tour takes you through a beautiful cultural and healing landscape and has several cultural and historical connections. This gives the trip an extra dimension. A "brudle" is an old word for "a bridal party". The special thing in this area of Norway was that a brudle was not only the bridal party itself, but also a line of stones that were laid one after the other on bare rock. Each person in the bridal party placed a stone so the number of stones reflects the number in the bridal party or bridal party, if you will. It is speculated that the smallest stones represent children. The tradition dates back to the 17th century and the last known bridge was laid in 1916.
The route is laid out as a round trip and it is possible to start either from Josdal in Sirdal, alternatively from Salmeli in Kvinesdal. The ruins are protected and must not be touched.
There are two different entry points to the circular trail as described below as stages 1 and 2.

title: England Coast Path - Skegness to Mablethorpe
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 26 km (16 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path ( ECP ) from Skegness to Mablethorpe is now open to the public. And offers beachside walk with sandy beaches and wide skies all the way along the route. Along with a cloud bar to view the clouds at Anderby Creek
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: Sendero del Desierto (PR-A 269)
short_description: The Rambla de Tabernas has been the setting for several Hollywood films and will guarantee you a breathtaking immersion in nature.
long_description: The Tabernas desert is a natural space protected since 1989 for its special beauty, which provides a dry place, but not of ecological interest. With more than 3,000 hours of sunshine per year and little rainfall (200-250 mm per year), temperatures are extreme here: minimum -5ºC in winter and maximum 48ºC in summer.The relatively flat Sendero del Desierto (PR-A269) is a natural area protected since 1989 for its special beauty. The relatively flat Sendero del Desierto (PR-A 269) allows us to explore this natural space along the paths of the Tabernas Desert, where many Western movies have been filmed. In fact, we start from a Mini Hollywood set and go with an abandoned place that simulates a Mexican city.

title: Olympic Coast North: The Shipwreck Coast
short_description: Seventeen contiguous miles of some of the prettiest and wildest coastline and beaches in North America await you on this adventure. Pass sea stacks, natural arches, caves and coves, reefs, tide pools, cliffs, and silver strands of spectacular sandy beaches. And visit two shipwreck memorials.
long_description:
Season: Year Round.
Contact: Olympic National Park, Wilderness Information
Center, Port Angeles, (360) 565-3100, www.nps.gov/olym;
Permits/regulations: National park entrance fee at Ozette Lake. Olympic NP wilderness camping permit required. Bear canister
required, can be borrowed from Wilderness Information Center or Forks Outfitters. No fires from Yellow Banks to Cape Alava. Dogs
prohibited north of Ellen Creek;

Special features: Wilderness coast, secluded beaches;
Special concerns: Car shuttle needed to do one-way. Some headlands can be rounded only at low tides, carry tide chart. Miles of slippery, rocky terrain;
GPS: Rialto Beach N 47 55.242 W 124 38.282. Ozette Lake N 48 09.275 W 124 40.132


Seventeen contiguous miles of some of the prettiest and wildest coastline and beaches in North America await you on this adventure. Pass sea stacks, natural arches, caves and coves, reefs, tide pools, cliffs, and silver strands of spectacular sandy beaches. Watch seals, scout for whales, listen to poolprobing oystercatchers and snag-sitting eagles add their own notes to the pounding surf. And visit two shipwreck memorials where voices in the wind speak of those who perished along this remarkable stretch of sea.


GETTING THERE

For southern access at Rialto Beach: From
Port Angeles, follow US 101 west for 55 miles
to the junction with State Route 110 (signed “Mora–La Push”), located 2 miles north of
Forks. Drive west on SR 110. In 7.7 miles, at
Quillayute Prairie, SR 110 splits. Take the
right fork (Mora Road) and proceed 5 miles to
road’s end and trailhead. Privy available. For
northern access at Ozette: From Port Angeles,
follow US 101 west for 5 miles to SR 112.
Follow SR 112 west for 48.5 miles, turning left
(2.5 miles beyond Seiku) onto Hoko-Ozette
Road. Continue for 21 miles to the Ozette
Ranger Station, car campground, and trailhead
(elev. 100 ft). Privy available.

ON THE TRAIL

Beginning at popular Rialto Beach, share this
classic coastline with beachcombers, dog
walkers (allowed on-leash to Ellen Creek),
and scores of Twihards from across the country.
Like most of the sandy stretches on this
hike, the going is easy during low tide and
slow and cumbersome during high. Admire
the huge driftwood logs lining the beach, but
never climb upon them during high tides. A
wave can easily jostle them loose, trapping
and endangering you.


At 1 mile, come to Ellen Creek, where
campsites can be found. The creek, like most
along the coast, has a rusty appearance due to
tannins in it—it is perfectly safe for drinking
(provided you filter or treat it). Pass a couple
of “shark teeth” sea stacks before coming to
Hole-in-the-Wall, a natural arch at 1.7 miles.
During low tides, strut right through it—otherwise
take the steep and short trail over a
bluff (elev. 70 ft) around it.


Pass a small cove and beach, with busy
campsites tucked among salty spruces. Plenty
of deer (cute) and raccoons (pesky) provide
company. The going gets rockier as the way
rounds two small headlands only negotiable
during low and medium tides. High-top boots
and trekking poles help keep you from slipping.
Offshore reefs, sea stacks, and Dahdayla
Island provide a dramatic backdrop.


Enter a quiet, protected, island-dotted cove
with good views north to prominent Cape
Johnson. Clamber over or around a tangled
mess of logs and rocks, compliments of a
recent slide, before, at 4.2 miles, passing the
small Chilean Memorial tucked on a bluff in
the trees. In November 1920, the Schooner
WJ Pirrie, while being towed, was cast aside in
a storm. The vessel broke in half and all but
two of the crew of twenty perished. The storm
victims were buried in a common grave near
the memorial. Campsites are nearby—sleep
peacefully if you can!


Next, round Cape Johnson along ledges
and rock and beneath cliffs—doable only duringa low tide. Immediately offshore is a mini Hole-in-the-Wall, a flattop island and a sea stack shaped like praying hands. In a receding
tide, oystercatchers probe for delicious morsels,
piercing the air with their high-pitched calls.
Pass a small cobbled stone beach before
rounding yet another headland (only passable
at low and medium tides), and then come
to a tough, slow-going section of rocks and
jumbled boulders. Finally, at 6 miles, reach a
section of smooth and easy beach. Pass good
creeks for drinking water, buoy-filled trees,
but no camps.


At 7 miles, climb steeply (use the rope)
over a small “pass” (elev. 40 ft) near a prominent
headland that can’t be rounded. Survey
a spectacular beach now spread out below.
On hard-packed sand, enjoy the walk, passing
“mountainous” headlands and flowerpot
sea stacks along the way—creeks and campsites
too.


At 8 miles is another headland that can’t
be rounded during high tides. A trail (with a
sand ladder) leads up and over this bluff that
was used during World War II as a lookout.
The view is amazing. Continue on more good
beaches interspersed with rocky sections,
coming to a creek at 8.5 miles. Snoop around
the creek’s north bank for rusting debris left
behind from the old Starbuch Mining operation.
Just beyond is Cedar Creek (decent
water) and good camps.


Continue north, rounding a headland at
low tide (using the overland trail at high), and
arrive at the wide, attractive sandy expanse of
Kayostla Beach at 10 miles. There are excellent
camps from just north of a small creek
to the Norwegian Memorial, site of the Prince
Arthur shipwreck in 1903 in which eighteen
mostly young Norwegian apprentices perished.
They were buried in a mass grave at the
memorial.


The Norwegian Memorial makes for a good
out-and-back trip from Rialto if a car shuttle
couldn’t be arranged—or, if you don’t care to
hike the next section north, which is one of
the roughest stretches of the Olympic Coast.
If continuing, take note: There are no
places to camp between Kayostla and Yellow Banks, nor are there any water sources; and
from Yellow Banks northward to Cape Alava,
campsite reservations are required and fires
are not permitted. The initial 4 miles beyond
the Norwegian Memorial are extremely rough,
with wet, slippery kelp-draped and barnacleencrusted
rocks and ledges and slimy downed
trees that can only be negotiated during low
tides. Hiking here is tiring and cumbersome
and requires your full attention, lest you slip.
Tide pools are abundant and so are crabs,
millions of them that seem to appear from
every exposed rock and pile of kelp. Offshore
rocks and sea stacks are missing from this
section, making the ocean feel that much
closer. At about 12 miles, pass an arch hidden
in the cliffs. At about 14 miles, the walking
gets easier as cobbles and then sand begin to
replace jumbled rocks.


At 14.6 miles, reach a creek emptying into a
crescent-shaped sandy beach flanked by big
Sitka spruce beneath the Yellow Banks bluffs.
Popular camps can be found 0.2 mile farther,
just north of the creek.


Continuing north, clamber over a headland
negotiable only during low and medium tides.
Look to the right for a small tunnel passage,
or round ledges on your left. Then emerge on
one of the longest, widest, sandiest stretches
of beach on the Olympic Coast. Farther north
along the beach, where the bluffs subside,
find plenty of campsites—water is plentiful,
and so are campers, most of whom come in
from Ozette Lake.


At 16.7 miles, pass the Ericsons Bay Trail,
which leads 2 miles east to Ozette Lake. At
17.3 miles, come to the Sand Point Trail just
shy of prominent Sand Point, where busy
campsites and a backcountry privy can be
found among salty windblown spruce and
shoulder-high salal.


Leave the surf for turf and take the Sand
Point Trail across boardwalks, through saturated
cedar groves. Gain 150 feet and arrive at the Ozette Lake trailhead, ranger station, and
car campground in 2.9 miles.


TRIP PLANNER
4.2 miles Chilean Memorial camps
8.7 miles Cedar Creek camps
10 miles Kayostla Beach camps
14.8 miles Yellow Banks camps
17.3 miles Sand Point camps
20.2 miles Ozette Lake trailhead


EXTENDING YOUR TRIP
Continue north along the coast 3 more miles
to Cape Alava and return via the Cape Alava
Trail. There are plenty of campsites at the
cape (reservations required). Good beaches
and easy walking can be enjoyed for another
1.5 miles north. Beyond that, to Shi Shi Beach,
the way gets rough again, headlands passable
at low tide only, rough overland trails, and a
potentially diffi cult ford of the Ozette River.
And you’ll need to pay to park at a private residence
if you plan on leaving a vehicle at the
Shi Shi end of the trip.



COASTING TO THE COAST: WILDERNESS THROUGH THE BACKDOOR
You’re standing on a gorgeous remote Olympic Coast beach after trudging over 10 miles of slippery rocks, soft sand, and rugged headlands—you waited patiently for low tides to safely proceed, and now you have this wilderness beach all to yourself. Well, not exactly.
Suddenly some folks appear out of nowhere, sweat-free and looking like they didn’t expend much energy to get here. Because they didn’t! They took a secret shortcut trail (thanks to the Internet, not that secret). By driving a maze of logging roads and then following a bootleg path a mere mile or so, they attained what you worked all day for.
I prefer my wilderness beach to feel like a wilderness beach. Shortcut trails diminish its wilderness characteristics and make it easier for less than environmentally friendly things to occur—such as large groups and partying. I understand that many folks can no longer backpack great distances, so getting to this beach would have been impossible for them the “right” way. And I have friends and acquaintances living in coastal communities who cherish these secret trails, and they respect these beaches and treat them well. These trails allow them quick access to the natural beauty in their backyards. But national parks belong to all Americans, and there are plenty of easily reached beaches within Olympic National Park. Olympic National Park’s wilderness coast is the wildest in the continentalUnited States. But shortcut trails seem to somewhat diminish that wildness.

title: Tretopper’n – den ultimate familieturen!
short_description: Tretopper'n - the ultimate family tour! Here you climb three small mountain peaks around Jønnbu: Anebunatten, Krintofjellet and Bøkstulnatten. These three make a great tour for the whole family.
long_description:
The peaks around Jønnbu are easily accessible and the walk between them is in varied and undemanding terrain. This is a perfect tour for families with children and others who want an easily accessible mountain tour with magical views and great mountain and mastering experience.
The peaks Anebunatten, Krintofjellet and Bøkstulnatten are situated at about 900 moh and the difference in height between the parking area and the peaks is about 175 m. Bø Turlag has a picnic area and a fire pit so that tired little feet can rest during the hike.
The tour is blue-marked and signposted with Tretopper´n. At the first trailhead, follow the trail west towards Anebunatten. At Grostulbekken you can take the path on towards Anebunatten or take the shortcut up to Krintofjellet via the narrow electric field. At the top of Anebudalen you turn left onto Anebunatten 878 moh. Then take the path back to the stile towards Krintofjellet 923 moh and to the viewpoint. From Krintofjellet the path leads you to the top of the steep Krintokleiva. From here you follow the path up to the highest peak: Bøkstulnatten 928 moh. from there you go steeply down to the rest area in "Bestemorssløyfa". Then you go down Bestemorsløyfa and the path back to the parking at Jønnbu.

title: Soğuksu Milli Parkı Doğa Yürüyüşü
short_description:
Soğuksu Milli Parkı Ankara'daki doğal güzelliklerden biri. Burada yürüyüş yapmak oldukça keyifli
Translate to English
long_description:
Soğuksu Milli Parkı, 1959 yılında ilan edilmiş olup Ankara ili Kızılcahamam ilçesi sınırları içinde yer alan 1.187 hektarlık alana sahiptir. Soğuksu Milli Parkı, İç Anadolu'dan dağlık Karadeniz bölgesine geçiş alanını oluşturması nedeniyle iki bölgeye has özelliklerden ve geniş orman alanlarından oluşuyor. 
Doğası bu kadar zengin olunca da Ankara yürüyüş rotaları denince akla gelen yerlerden birisi Soğuksu Milli Parkı ve çevresi. Ortalama 3 saatinizi alan bu yürüyüş rotası hazırlığınızı yapıp yola koyulmanıza değecek pek çok özellik barındırıyor. Yürüyüş, dağcılık, fotoğrafçılık, doğa gözlemi, piknik gibi her yönden sizi tatmin edebilecek rotalar listesinde. 
Soğuksu Milli Parkı'ndaki canlı çeşitliliği de oldukça fazla. Bu milli park içinde nesli tükenmekte olan ve Avrupa’nın en büyük yırtıcı kuşu denilen Kara Akbaba'nın da yaşadığı söyleniyor. Bu bölgede doğa sporları yapmaya gelenler de Kara Akbaba gözlem alanları, Kızılcahamam Dağ Lalesi ve Fosil Ağaç Jeositi gibi pek çok coğrafi ve doğal değeri deneyimleme şansı buluyor.
Bu rotayı deneyimledikten sonra doğanın keyfini çıkarabilir ve buradaki eşsiz coğrafi değerleri keşfedebilirsiniz.

title: Anello Passo Oclini - Corno Bianco
short_description:
Un anello breve e di difficoltà minima ma di grande impatto: un ottima uscita "di riscaldamento" in vista della stagione invernale.
Translate to English
long_description:
Un piacevolissimo anello nel paradiso invernale della zona dolomitica del Corno Bianco/Weißhorn.
La zona si anima con l'apertura degli impianti da sci del comprensorio "Passo Oclini/Jochgrimm" ma la pace che si può godere dopo le prime nevicate della stagione e prima dell'arrivo degli atleti sulle piste, è impareggiabile.
L'uscita è semplice, il dislivello è moderato ma, essendo l'itinerario breve, è tutto o quasi concentrato nella parte iniziale: non scoraggiatevi quindi dopo i primi metri perché la vista dalla cima (e anche lungo il percorso) ripagherà di ogni sforzo!

title: हाथगढ़ किला ट्रैक
short_description: हातगड किला महाराष्ट्र के नासिक ज़िले में स्थित है। क्योंकि यह गुजरात के सापुता रा से सिर्फ 6 किमी की दूरी पर स्थित है इसलिए गुजरात से इसकी ट्रैकि ंग करने में ज्यादा सहूलियत रहती है।
long_description: हातगड एक ऐतिहासिक किला है जो सापुतारा हिल स्टेशन के दक्षिण में गुजरात -महाराष्ट्र की सीमा पर खड़ा है। यह मराठा शासक छत्रपति शिवाजी महाराज ने बनवाया था। सह्याद्रि श्रृंखला के किनारे एक पठार में मलगभग 3,600 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित इस किले को गुजरात की तरफ से आने वाले मुस्लिम हमलावरों को रोकने के लिए बनवाया था। किले का आरंभ बिंदु सापुतारा-नासिक रोड में स्थित हातगड गाँव है। किले तक पहुँचने का अकेला रास्ता एक संकरे चट्टानी रास्ते से होकर गुजरता है। आखिरी चरण में करीब 200 सीढ़ियों को चढ़ना पड़ता है। किले के शीर्ष पर भगवान गणेश की एक मूर्ति और मंदिर स्थापित है। किले की ही पास मीठे पानी का बड़ा और एक छोटा तालाब भी मौजूद है। हातगड किले की हाइक मध्यम कठिनाई की है। यह अनुभवी और नौसिखिये हाइकरों के लिए समान रूप से उपयुक्त है। यह ट्रैक मार्ग अपेक्षाकृत सुनसान है क्योंकि हातगड गांव की आबादी केवल 3000 के आसपास है। इसी कारण से यह भारत के कुछ उन चुनिंदा ट्रैक में से एक हैं जिस मे अपने पालतू कुत्ते को भी साथ ले जा सकते हैं।

title: Oxburgh Hall
short_description: A walk around the woodland and meadow part of the grounds of this moated manor house, built by the Bedingfeld family in the 15th century. Don't forget to enjoy panoramic views from the gatehouse roof.
long_description:
Oxborough, near King's Lynn, Norfolk PE33 9PS

A romantic, moated manor house, it was built by the Bedingfeld family in the 15th century and they have lived here ever since. Inside, the family's Catholic history is revealed, complete with a secret priest's hole which you can crawl inside. See the astonishing needlework by Mary, Queen of Scots, and the private chapel, built with reclaimed materials. Outside, you can enjoy panoramic views from the gatehouse roof and follow the woodcarving trails in the gardens and woodlands.

title: Grand Corniche
short_description: Discover Côte d’Azur on one of the finest scenic routes in France. With its picturesque small towns and a dream-like coastline, Grande Corniche rates among the most spectacular roads of Southern Europe. You will even see ancient monuments alongside the route.
long_description: Driving along this winding road with breathtaking views over the coastline will give you a touch of freedom. Grande Corniche has a stunning scenery to it which makes you enjoy even more the ride. Gazing over the Côte d’Azur with its turquoise blue water we drive from Nice, a bustling seaside metropolis, to Menton, a tranquil city in the north-east of Monaco. Napóleon Bonaparte had this road constructed at the end of the 18th century for conquering Italy. Nowadays, Grande Corniche has left far behind its merely stratregic purposes and is even rated as one of the most romantic and picturesque scenic routes of Europe, a feast for the eyes and symbol of pure driving pleasure. That’s why it was chosen to be part of cult movies such as “GoldenEye“ or Alfred Hitchcock’s “To Catch a Thief“.

title: The wine road in Prahova
short_description: The wine road in Prahova County passes through several localities located in the picturesque Dealu Mare area, one of the most famous wine regions in Romania.
long_description:
The region has high winemaking potential due to a temperate microclimate and excellent position in relation to the sun, similar to the vineyard hills of Bordeaux or Tuscany.
Between Ploiești and Buzău, on the road that runs roughly parallel to the national highway, you'll cross entire hillsides of vineyards that stretch as far as the eye can see. To find out which grapes are grown on which side of the hills, you'll need to stop at one of the many wine cellars along the route. The oenologists will explain the production process - specific to each winery - and the particular characteristics of the wines.
The route can be covered in one day by car or in stages by bike. Autumn is the ideal time to visit, when the grapes are picked, but the sights are open all year round. Along the way, stops at several museum mansions can be included.
Some wineries also function as accommodation if you want to stay in the area.

title: On foot to the Traufbergalpe
short_description: The hike to the Traufbergalpe through the Traufbachtobel offers a lot of scenic beauty and good places to stop for refreshments.
long_description:
The popular route from Oberstdorf to Spielmannsau splits behind the Oberstdorf golf course. On one side of the Trettach runs the road popular with cyclists, on the other the more leisurely footpath through lush meadows and sparse forest, which we choose. Shortly before the small village of Spielmannsau, you enter the wild Traufbach ravine. A rocky path leads up along the rushing stream. At the upper end of the ravine we emerge from the shade of the Bäume, then it is not far to the Traufbergalpe. The alp was first mentioned in 1333 and was permanently inhabited at that time. Today the small hut makes a rustic, cosy impression. The last stretch up to the alp is very steep, but once you reach the top, the impressive view of the high Krottenspitze, under which the Traufbach rises, the Fürschießer, the Muttlerkopf and many other high peaks is worth the climb.
After a long rest with delicious bread on the alpine pasture, we start on the Rückweg. We decide against the descent through the ravine and instead continue along the steep slope of the Traufberg. At the highest point of the trail there is a beautiful vantage point where we can take a short breather and enjoy the view of the ravine below us. Then we descend again on the other side of the wooded slope. Once we have reached the bottom of the Trettach valley, we are soon back in Spielmannsau, where we can stop for a break if necessary.
From Spielmannsau down into the valley, we follow the road above the Trettach. Passing the small Christlesee lake with its clear water fed by snowfields, we then return to the starting point of our tour in a relaxed manner.

title: Bright Lake (Swan Lake)
short_description: The unfrozen lake - Svetloe - is one of the rarest places, summoning whooper swans for wintering. In late November, gatherings of white birds begin here, accessible to curious tourists.
long_description:
Light Lake, or Swan Lake, as it is also called, is small in size. It is only as deep as a tall man, about 100 m wide and 1000 m long. The uniqueness of Bright Lake does not lie in its size, but in the fact that the land feeds it with warm springs, and when the winter temperature is minus 40 degrees centigrade, the water in the lake is +5. The fact of warmth attracted the peace-loving bird. Maybe the fact that the Swan reserve and tourists feed the swans also caused unexpectedly mass arrival of such a gentle and attractive bird.
  With the arrival of swans, people, families, and anyone else who wishes to experience the magic of a live swan scene, begin to flock to Bright Lake. This version of Swan Lake is perhaps not staged. You won't see the great ballerinas or hear the romances of Pyotr Tchaikovsky, but you will feel the thrill of the original Swan Lake as it is in its original form, and you will definitely witness pure love, present-day fidelity and eternal beginnings.

title: Discovery walk on Măgura Ponds, in Măgura Zboiu nature reserve
short_description: Part of the Comana Natural Park, the Măgura Zboiu Reserve (i.e. the Măgura Ponds and the Zboiu Forest) could make for the perfect place for some relaxing walks.
long_description:
They "could" but right now they are not, and you won't find information about walking or trekking in this area. For now, only a couple of the ponds are popular among amateur fishermen.
The reserve includes 9 ponds set in a depression and surrounded by agricultural fields, orchards, and vineyards. Some people even got the chance to build private houses here. The most famous pond is Balta 9 Măgura, where fishermen come. One of the ponds belongs to Defense Ministry and cannot be seen.
The landscape is similar to that of the Delta, the biodiversity being just as rich, but less obvious or easy to spot.

title: Ažek waterfalls (Sochi)
short_description: The route «Ažek Waterfalls» in the Sochi National Park is one of the most beautiful. The wildness of the forest in which the trails to the waterfalls are laid out is stunning in its fairytale beauty.
long_description: Ažek waterfalls can be covered by a day-trip. The trails go through the colchic forest covered with boxwood. The forest along the river Ajek shows its rocks, gives water streams which are crossed by swinging dilapidated bridges and in some places without them. Nevertheless, the route does not tire, but with its picturesque tone it leads inevitably to the main goal – the lower and upper waterfalls. The upper waterfall is much bigger than it looks in the photo and reaches 22 metres. And all this natural heritage is situated 15 km away from Sochi. This is where you usually start to think about the idea of making a hike on this route. On the way to Azhek waterfalls one can meet not less famous Orekhovsky waterfall and the Star of Partisans. The author of the Star himself cast the concrete star on his own idea in a thick forest and left it to his grandchildren for restoration. Ivan Zikran – the creator of the famous «Zvezdochka» monument in the region, and his grandchildren who live in the village of Plastunka, now continue to paint it red.

title: Nebelhorn Mountain Run
short_description: A physically demanding mountain run up a beautiful Allgäu panoramic mountain.
long_description: The Nebelhorn mountain run is one of the most demanding mountain runs in Germany. The approximately 1,400 metres of altitude over a distance of just over 10 km are very steep in places. Although the course is technically easy, the steepest section of the trail on the mountain pine slope requires good stamina. The course record for the run is just over an hour. Even if this time is only achievable for absolute top runners, trained mountain runners should manage the distance in 01:30. For the way back, it is best to take the Nebelhorn cable car down to the valley, as the fastest way back is on foot and not very rewarding downhill.

title: Ridge hike from Hinterstein over 2 peaks to the Giebelhaus
short_description: Those who take on the sometimes steep ascent are rewarded on this tour with a magnificent view of the Allgäu High Alps and far into the Lech Valley. With a bit of luck, you may also see chamois.
long_description:
The Allgäu High Alps offer a fantastic nature experience with great views of the neighbouring Lech Valley. The tour should not be underestimated in terms of fitness or technique. A head for heights and surefootedness are a prerequisite. But the effort is worth it! Not only the Schrecksee, which invites you to cool off in summer, but also the views from the summit compensate. If you are lucky, you may even catch a glimpse of chamois. The tour is not particularly difficult from a technical point of view, but it is demanding from a physical point of view. There are no refreshment stops until the end of the tour, which is why it is highly recommended to take enough provisions with you. Surefootedness is required on the last 100m to the two summits. The path is not clearly visible here and should be chosen freely according to your own assessment. However, safety equipment is not required. The descent only requires a little care between the Schänzlescharte and the Sattelhütte. Again and again, loose stone fields have to be crossed.
A challenging grade.

title: 3 capitals – bicycle tour Lithuania Vilnius-Trakai-Kaunas
short_description: Three capitals on a single cycle tour: from today's capital Vilnius to the historic capital Trakai and the former temporary capital Kaunas
long_description:
On this 180 km long long-distance cycle route through Lithuania, you encounter culture with every step you take. Castles, monasteries, mansions, museums and of course churches line this cycle route. The tour starts at the Gate of Dawn in the "City of Churches" like Vilnius, the former Wilna is also called.
Vilnius is the current capital of Lithuania. But in former times it was the island castle Trakai and in the meantime also the city Kaunas, where the tour ends.
After an extensive visit of all churches and sights, we will go to Trakai Manor Vokė. Never heard of? But you have seen it often. It served as a film location for movies like "Anna Karenina" and "War and Peace".
We continue to the island castle Trakai. It was the capital of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania at the beginning of the 14th century.
The tour continues via the spa town of Birštonas and the Pažaislis Monastery to Kaunas. After that the route leads along the Memel to Šilutė (German Heydekrug).
