title: Skåla
short_description: Experience one of Norway’s classic hiking trails
long_description:
Skåla is a giant in Norwegian hiking history, visited by tourists for more that a 100 years. The trail takes you from the ocean up to 1,848 meters and provides great views of the local fjords and the Jostedalsbreen Glacier. On the top you will find Skålabu and Skålatårnet, DNT cabins where you can spend the night before going down again.
Skåla is a very demanding hike as you ascend 1,800 meters to the top. However, if you’re in good shape and have appropriate hiking footwear it is a very manageable hike on a well-maintained trail. In 2009, Nepalese sherpas built a stone trail along the most demanding parts of the hike, making climb a bit easier.
The original cabin at the top of Skåla, known as Skålatårnet, was built using local rocks and initially constructed in 1891. In 2016 an additional cabin, Skålabu, was added which doubled the capacity from 20 to 40 beds. Staying a night at the cabin is highly recommended for the amazing sunset and sunrise. 
Stay in one of the self-service DNT cabins on top of Skåla.
In Loen, you will find both Hotel Alexandra and Hotel Loenfjord. If you would prefer a cabin, or to camp, there is both Lo-Vik Camping and Tjugen Camping.
Alternatively you can stay in Stryn (which is a larger town than Loen) and stay at the beautiful Visnes Hotel.

title: Dörzbach
short_description: On our way from Dörzbach via Meßbach and Hohebach, there are three beautiful sacred buildings from different periods that are worth visiting. The tour runs through beautiful nature.
long_description:
From the 13th century Lutheran Holy Trinity Church, we walk across the market square, through the outer castle courtyard and cross the Jagst river. After the bridge, we turn left and take hiking trail no. 17. This leads us past the Eiskellern, over the Stäffele to Meßbach, where we reach the Catholic parish church "Zur heiligen Dreifaltigkeit". It dates from the rococo period (built in 1776) and is worth a visit for its altars and frescoes.
Then we continue on the hiking trail "No. 16". We pass the natural monument "Linde" and walk along the "Alte Poststeige" to the chapel "St. Wendel zum Stein". Already from the outside you can see why it is called that: The chapel, first mentioned in 1478, was built directly against the 30 m high tuff rock, which thus forms the back wall of the building. As early as the Late Latène period (150/100 BC to around the birth of Christ), the area served as a Celtic place of worship.
Now we walk on through the chapel forest to Hohebach to the Jagst bridge and the Jewish cemetery. On the cycle path, which runs parallel to the B19, we go past the black rock back to our starting point in Dörzbach.

images.caption: The chapel of St. Wendel zum Stein in Dörzbach.

title: Moor nature trail through the Viru raised bog
short_description: The Viru raba õpperada, the nature trail across the Viru high moor, which leads along a well-made plank path to a lookout tower from where you have a fantastic view.
long_description:
Virumoor is a relatively small raised bog. However, with a well-maintained boardwalk, information boards, resting benches and a lookout tower, it offers ideal opportunities to experience this unique groove.
The circular trail starts at the car park north of the E20 between Tallinn and Narva. From there, the trail leads into the forest. After a few hundred metres, turn left onto the tree path, which leads over a dune through the forest to the northern point of the moorland trail. At an information board, turn right onto the green and white marked path into the moor. The path is well maintained and mostly leads over planks to an observation tower.
Here you will find plenty of information about the raised bog habitat, the plants, the animals and the people in the raised bog.
The first viewing platform is accessible for wheelchairs and prams. The path from the tower to the car park is a well-maintained boardwalk that is barrier-free and suitable for wheelchairs and prams.

images.caption: Eine Eule im Wald - vielfältige Natur bei der Wanderung durch das Hochmoor

title: Hochwald Gourmet Marathon Saarbrücken
short_description: Whether for Sunday joggers, marathon professionals or spectators – the Saarbrücken Gourmet Marathon is a pleasure in many respects.
long_description: The Hochwald Gourmet Marathon is a flat, officially measured 10.55 km circuit through the most beautiful streets of the state capital Saarbrücken. The marathon course is run four times and the half marathon twice. In the team relay, each member of the 4-person team runs the course once. The mini-marathon is completed on a partial course.

title: Through the beautiful Gelpetal - Wuppertal
short_description: We follow the Gelpe, a tributary of the Wupper, through its idyllic valley.
long_description: Our tour starts in Wuppertal-Lichtscheid, in Müngstener Straße. First we head south into Obere Böhle and after a short while cross the state road, whereupon we reach Kapellenweg and Dorner Weg. We follow this through the Gelpe valley along the stream of the same name. In front of the Gelper Hof, where we also have the opportunity to take a rest, we follow the path to the right. We finally reach the Görresweg Hahnerberg, into which we turn left. After a few metres, we follow Rennbaumer Straße to the right and have already reached the destination of our tour, Hahnerberger Straße in Hahnerberg.

title: Through the Palace Park - Schwetzingen
short_description: We walk through the Schwetzingen Palace Gardens, of which Voltaire once said: „Before I die, I want to do one more duty and enjoy one more consolation: I want to see Schwetzingen again, this thought dominates my whole soul.“
long_description:
The Schwetzingen Palace Garden is a special feature among the palace gardens of Europe. It is one of only a few gardens to be divided into a French and an English section. The French garden is designed according to the strict geometrical rules of the Baroque and Decartes periods, while the English section is dominated by the Romantic forms of the Rococo and Classicist periods. While the first part is lined with parterres and bosquets, avenues and figure-heavy fountains and sculptures, the English part at the back is filled with ruins, temples and planned wilderness.
Another highlight of the garden is the mosque. It is in no way a real mosque and is only intended to satisfy the fashion for the Orient, which was very much in vogue in the second half of the 18th century. In 1870/71, when prisoners of war from the Maghreb were housed here in Schwetzingen, and after the 2nd World War by American soldiers, Islamic prayers were held here.
In general, one should take time for the garden, as the inhabitants of the old residential town have done since its creation. With the exception of the bathing area, the garden has always been open to the public. Under princely rule it was even free of charge.

title: Hornelen
short_description: The highest sea cliff in Norway
long_description:
Hornelen is well-known across southern Norway for the spectacular 860m cliff that rises steeply above the fjord. It is claimed that this is the tallest sea cliff in northern Europe. Hornelen has over the centuries also been an important landmark for ships at sea.
Hornelen is a very popular mountain, and several trails can be followed. Berle (southwest) and Hornskor (northwest) are the most popular trailheads. The north top is found 140m northeast of the summit. The big spectacular mountain wall is below the north top.

title: To the Freyung bee trail
short_description: This hike takes us to the newly created bee nature trail and at the same time through charming countryside to the most beautiful viewpoints in the region.
long_description: At the spa administration with the tourist information, we keep east and walk through Schulgasse to the town square. There, at the "Passauer Hof" inn, we turn left into the downhill Abteistraße and walk to the supermarket. Immediately we turn right into Schönbrunner Straße. Follow the road to the cemetery, where the well-signposted bee trail begins at the information board. It offers rest opportunities, wonderful views or even both at the idyllically located rest area with a view of Freyung. Back in Freyung, we turn left up Kolpingstraße. On Bahnhofstraße, where we pass the remarkable building of the district court, we go straight ahead to the town square with the town parish church.

images.caption: We experience wonderful views of Freyung in the second half of the Bienenweg.
At the market place in Freyung we keep to the right.
The bee trail begins at the information board near the cemetery.
The bee trail runs charmingly along the edge of the Grillabach.
Along the information boards we experience the beautiful and varied landscape.
At this resting place we can take a break in front of a beautiful backdrop shortly before the end of the bee trail.

title: Along the Breg to Donaueschingen
short_description: Along the Breg, which together with the Brigach is one of the two main source rivers of the Danube, a varied trail leads you to Donaueschingen.
long_description: At the starting point of the tour at the bus stop "Ortsmitte" in Hammereisenbach there is an information board about the hiking and cycling trail system as well as a detailed signpost. From here we follow the symbols of the Bregtalweg (yellow rhombus) along the main road through Hammereisenbach. At the end of the village, we meet the Breg for the first time. Here we see the ruins of Neufürstenberg Castle on the left. If you want to visit it, follow the signpost before the bridge to the left, a steep climb up to the Neufürstenburg ruins (approx. 0.8 km). All "hikers only" keep to the right and hike along the side road to the edge of the forest. At the fork, turn left in the Bregtal valley towards Wolterdingen. The path is very easy to find here, thanks to the continuous marking (yellow rhombus). We walk along the Bregtalweg (yellow rhombus) until we reach the forest car park. Here we follow the asphalt road to Wolterdingen. In the centre of the village, leave the Bregtalweg and follow a new marking (white line on a blue background) to the left across the Breg. From here it is another 7.5 km to Donaueschingen. After the bridge, walk along the main road to the right on the cross path - Schwarzwald-Kaiserstuhl-Rhein (red rhombus on a yellow background). After the small village of Wolterdingen, we head out into the open countryside. After passing the Weiherbach stream, leave the road and follow the agricultural road straight uphill to the edge of the forest. At the fork in the road at the edge of the forest, we turn left and after about 500 m we reach the Eichbuckhütte Wolterdingen, which invites us to take a break. We continue walking through a beautiful piece of forest and later along the edge of the forest until we come to a crossroads. We follow the trail marking "Schwarze Tanne auf blauem Kreis" straight ahead through the forest. Over slightly ascending and descending terrain, we continue straight ahead on wide paths until a small path branches off to the left. This is marked with a red diamond on a yellow background. Walk along the path downhill, turn right onto a wide path and continue straight ahead to Aufen. Pass the church on the right, then turn left again, following the main road. After 200 m, we leave the priority road and follow the signs to the left towards Aufen railway station (Buchbergweg). Here we cross the Brigach and follow the signs to the right towards Donaueschingen through a mixed deciduous forest on a beautiful and well-signposted forest path (red rhombus on yellow). Finally, we leave the forest and follow a footpath that leads across a meadow. After 250 m we reach the main road (Hindenburgallee). Follow this road to the right. Here you can already see the first signpost to the railway station. Now we continue along the Brigach, past the DB stop Donaueschingen Mitte/Siedlung. Finally, we leave the Brigach behind us and follow the signs to Donaueschingen railway station. From here it is only a few metres to Donaueschingen Castle Park and the "official" source of the Danube. In Donaueschingen there are numerous places to stop for refreshments. The bus takes us back to Hammereisenbach (every two hours, but ideally you should find out about the times before you start your hike!)

images.caption: We see impressive rock formations on our route.

title: Round trip through West Lithuania along the coast and through the country
short_description: The Samogitia region of Lower Lithuania (lit. Žemaitija) in the west of Lithuania is considered one of the most authentic regions of the country. The tour leads through cities and landscapes.
long_description:
The tour leads from Klaipeda, the former Memel along the Baltic Sea coast via Palanga to the small town of Šventoji.
Afterwards it goes into the interior and the province of Samogitia. The Samogitians (lit. Žemaiten) have preserved their character and dialect, which is known as persistant and stubborn. They were also the last European pagans to be converted to Christianity. Altars of their ancient pagan beliefs can still be found on the castle hills of the region. Apart from the heritage of Baltic mythology and local folk culture, traces of the Cold War can also be found here.
The tour reaches its easternmost point when it goes around the lake Plateliai. Here you will find the Cold War Museum and the Siberija observation tower with a view of the lake and the National Park.
The tour continues via the monastery town of Kretinga, for which you should plan some time, back to Klaipeda.

title: Glomnesfossen Waterfall
short_description: Glomnesfossen
long_description: The Glomnesfossen Waterfall is easy to spot as you’re driving around the eastern end of Oppstrynsvatnet Lake near Hjelle, with Segestad Mountain Farm perched above. The falls can be easily reached with a short hike, and the viewpoint offers a nice perspective back towards the lake. From the falls you can extend the hike with a visit to the farm, or further up into the Glomsdalen Valley.

title: Around the island of Wangerooge
short_description: We hike once around Wangerooge. The perfect tour to get to know the multifaceted North Sea island.
long_description: Wangerooge is the easternmost of the seven inhabited East Frisian Islands and lies in the Lower Saxony Wadden Sea. On our tour, we start in the main town at the famous Café Pudding and walk east through the town and the dunes. Then we walk around the island's airfield and on to the western jetty. Along the beach and through windy dunes we come to the beach promenade.

title: Geiersberg municipal forest near Deggendorf
short_description: We experience a relaxing and informative hike along a nature trail in the deciduous forest - with many beautiful views of the Danube and the old town.
long_description: The hike begins above the Church of the Assumption of the Virgin Mary. We follow the trail marking "Via Nova" and the black signs with white writing: "On the trail of nature". On a forest path with views of the Danube we walk to the Geiersberg church. Next to it is a Kneipp facility. Here we cross the road and follow the sign to the Heldenhain. Continue to the Wallner Villa with a rhododendron grove and views of the Danube. The path now winds uphill to a rest area, finally past a pond and back to the Geiersberg church. This time we choose the upper path, which leads us back along a field edge and an avenue of lime trees. At a vantage point, we once again enjoy the view of the old town.

images.caption: The trail offers beautiful views of the Danube.
We climb the stairs next to the sculptures.
A beautiful view of the old town of Deggendorf.
The Geiersberg church from the 15th century has an altar worth seeing and votive images.

title: A typical trip through the unusual Kolomenskoye Park in Moscow
short_description: Kolomenskoye Park is located a few kilometres from the centre of Moscow and is the city's natural landscape. The park's many attractions attract thousands of daily visitors.
long_description:
The park was formed on the site of the village of Kolomenskoye as far back as the 13th century. It is said that when Batyi burned Kolomna, its inhabitants founded a new settlement near Moscow, Kolomenskoye. In the 16th century, grandiose construction projects began in the village, which have survived to the present day. One of these structures – the Church of the Ascension has not only survived, but has also been included in the list of UNESCO.
  The top sights of Kolomenskoye Park, apart from the Church of the Ascension, under this colon:
Front Gate (Complex) 
The palace of Tsar Alexei Mikhailovich 
The Palace Pavilion of 1825
The cabin of Peter the Great
The courtyard
Church of the Ascension
Church of the Kazan Icon of the Mother of God
Church of St George with Belfry
Church of St George with Belfry
Church of the Beheading of John the Baptist in Dyakov
The Polovtsian stone tower (the tower is 900 years old, it came to the park from the burial mound of the Polovtsians
The Water Tower in Kolomenskoye
The Saviour's Gate (Rear gate) in Kolomenskoye
The park does not end at the Rear Gate, there is a deep and interesting story to be told as one strolls through the luxurious and regal fields of the park over time.

title: Edelmann ring path Kulmbach
short_description: This hiking trail forms an "outer ring" around Kulmbach and was named after the well-known Kulmbach local historian Hans Edelmann (1888 - 1973).
long_description: This hiking trail forms an "outer ring" around Kulmbach and was named after after the famous Kulmbach local historian Hans Edelmann (1888 - 1973). named. The extensive hike takes you through narrow stream valleys, deep forests and over open ridges. The Plassenburg Castle and the lookout tower on the Rehberg are worth a detour. We can take a break in the Mainau recreation area and relax with a refreshing swim.

images.caption: A detour to Plassenburg Castle is worthwhile on this tour.

title: The wine trail in Malsch
short_description: During a hike through the vineyards, we can learn about the essential steps of viticulture on numerous information boards.
long_description:
Among connoisseurs, Malsch has long been considered an insider tip among Germany's wine-growing regions. The Hummel wine, for example, which is famous beyond Germany's borders, is grown here. But the road to this fame, paved with countless medals, was long. Not at all like our hike, which we can complete in a good two to three hours. We can learn everything about viticulture, the different grape varieties and wine culture on various information boards.
After the hike, we recommend a visit to a Malscher Besenwirtschaft. These inns, most of which are run by winegrowers, are only open during certain months of the year, so you should inform yourself beforehand. Here you can get wine in all price and quality categories and also down-to-earth cuisine with often very large portions.

images.caption: Information boards explain the work in the vineyard.
We hike and learn on the Letzenberg .

title: Historical tour around Machnower See near Berlin
short_description: Following in the footsteps of the old estate village of Kleinmachnow, we enjoy magnificent views around Machnower See.
long_description:
Kleinmachnow, formerly a rural estate village southwest of Berlin, has developed into a popular place to live just outside the capital after reunification. As a former German-German border town, the village has numerous historical highlights to offer.
A short hike around Machnower See will take us in their footsteps. We start at the listed Kleinmachnower Lock on the southern bank of the Teltow Canal and turn east into the avenue by the forester's lodge. Every now and then we can enjoy views of Machnower See and after a few metres we reach the old forester's lodge, which invites us to take a rest. Rested, we continue our hike and pass the old village church, which was completed at the end of the 16th century. A look inside the building is worthwhile.
At Zehlendorfer Damm we turn left and walk past some houses of the former estate village. Now the path leads us to the north shore, from where there is a magnificent panorama over the lake. We cross the bridge, keep left and start our way back along the northern shore.
Those who still want to make a detour to the Hakeburg have a short but steep way uphill ahead of them. However, this effort is rewarded with wonderful views over the Bäketal nature reserve.
At the point where the Machnower See narrows, we keep to the right until we reach the road Am Hochwald. Now we turn left back to the Stahnsdorfer Damm and cross the Kleinmachnower Schleuse, our starting point, in a southerly direction.

title: Gremyachiy Klyuch (spring, Sergiev Posad)
short_description: Gremyachiy Klyuch —spring on the right bank of the river Vondiga 500 m south of the village Vzglyadnevo in Sergievo-Posad;district of the Moscow Region of Russia;
long_description:
The Goryachiy Klyuch is considered the largest and most famous waterfall in the Moscow region. It flows down the bluff of the Vondiga River in cascading forms and its height reaches 20 metres.
  Legend has it that the waterfall originated thanks to the prayers of St. Sergius of Radonezh. Now it is a popular place for pilgrimages and active tourism.
The legend says that the waterfall originated thanks to the prayers of St. Sergius of Radonezh.

title: Schmannewitz circular hiking trail
short_description: On this short loop we experience a lot of nature and the Dahl forest.
long_description: Our tour begins at the Schmannewitz forest swimming pool. From here we first walk in the direction of Schmannewitz, but turn right into the forest at the first opportunity. Now we follow the path to Brehm's Rest. Here we can take a break in beautiful nature. We continue along the path past the "Toten Magd" (dead maid) to the Jägereiche (hunter's oak), where we turn right onto the G-path and keep towards the Tabakskiefer (tobacco pine). When we reach the pine tree, we turn right again onto the Holzstraße, which leads us past the Hospitalhütte and the Käthe-Kollwitz-Hütte. Here we have the opportunity to stop for a break. After another half kilometre on Holzstraße, we turn right and soon arrive back at the starting point of our hike, the Waldbad Schmannewitz.

title: Bilskuppe Tour - Lauterbach
short_description:
This half-day hike offers us magnificent views as far as the Rhön.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
From the Wiegel holiday farm, we hike west up the hill in the direction of Hälsberg. At the end of a short asphalt path we have a wonderful view over Lauterbach and Rimlos.
On the right along the Hälsberg on the hillside we already have the Bilskuppe in view. On a clear day, the view from there stretches all the way to the Rhön hilltops. Continue to the end of the forest path, then turn right through the underpass of the B254. Passing ponds and areas of rough grassland with juniper plantations, we reach the foot of the Bilskuppe. Continue around the Bilskuppe in an easterly direction, from here you have a view of the special airfield at Wernges. Now the path leads in the direction of the Maar. After a short stretch of country road, we turn left onto the field path that leads above the Kalkberg. Passing a newly built stable, you reach the outskirts of Maar. The path leads through a new housing estate on the cycle path along the Bundesstrasse 245 (in Maar there are restaurants that are open all day). Continue in the direction of Lauterbach. We cross the railway tracks, then the main road. The path runs along the railway embankment and back to Rimlos via a wooden bridge.

title: Jogging Route Durach -  Weidach
short_description: The route can be started at will in the municipality of Durach and lead along the Ziegelholzweg in the direction of Kottern, past the Sinz bakery.
long_description: The jogging route is ideal for a warm-up training session or cardio unit. Starting in Durach, the route leads along a dirt road past the Sinz bakery to Kottern. You jog along the Durach airfield with a view of the local mountain Grünten and its associated mountain panorama. After reaching the traffic circle, the route continues into the center of Weidach. From Weidach, the route is oriented back to Durach, passing the sports fields of the Kempten district of Kottern as it crosses the village. After reaching the nearby Sinz bakery, the familiar dirt road is not taken again, but the bypass road towards St. Mang is followed until the next traffic circle. Once you reach the traffic circle, take the turnoff back towards the center of Durach. Once in Durach, you can either extend the route individually or return to your personal starting point.

images.caption: View in the direction of Durach.

title: Wonders of nature: the Wackelstein in the Bavarian Forest
short_description: Two "stone" highlights await us on this challenging tour through beautiful deciduous forest.
long_description: From the car park we follow the signs to the Wackelstein (hiking trail "84"). A scenic path leads us to the edge of the forest. We choose the right, very well-marked path, which leads idyllically through mixed forest steeply uphill. The path winds past rounded rocks, so-called "woollen bag formations", to the huge Wackelstein. We pass the information board and follow the signpost "71" downhill to a clearing with a bench. The path is flat until you reach a forest road, where you turn left. At a crossroads, we follow trail "61" to the "Steinernen Kirchlein", a kind of rock castle. The path now leads us steadily downhill and we reach the beginning of the tour again.

images.caption: The resting bench at the edge of the forest offers a beautiful view.
The "Steinerne Kirchlein" is a huge, granite rock castle that invites you to play hide-and-seek.
We return from the forest to the fields and the comfortable sandy soil.
At the road near Loh we have a wonderful view into the Dreiburgenland.
The tons of the approximately 300 million year old rock can be made to "wobble" by a vigorous hiker.
On a sandy path we reach the edge of the forest with a view over the fields.

title: Climbing Jebel Toubkal (4,167 m), Morocco
short_description: With an elevation of over 4,000 metres, Morocco's Jebel Toubkal is the highest peak in both the Atlas Mountains and North Africa and makes for a great few days away from the bustle of nearby Marrakesh.
long_description:
The typical ascent of Toubkal involves traveling very early to Imlil (or staying there overnight) and then trekking up to the Refuge Toubkal Les Mouflons (Jebel Toubkal Refuge) via the Sidi Chamharouch shrine to spend the night. This should be booked well in advance. 
The following day involves an early wake-up followed by the climb to the summit and then back down to the refuge. Depending on how you have timed it, some may choose to spend another night there while others will descend the valley back to Imlil the same day.

images.caption: Early morning ascending to the summit
Early morning ascending to the summit
There was quite a bit of haze from the top, sadly
The route up to the summit from the refuge
This little guy walked all the way down from the refuge with us

title: Le cirque d'Archiane à pied
short_description:
Du hameau d'Archiane, empruntez les sentiers situés au pied des majestueuses falaises du Cirque d'Archiane, entre roches, buis et sous-bois.
Translate to English
long_description:
Le cirque d'Archiane est devenu un lieu privilégié de nidification du vautour fauve. Les falaises, leur verticalité, leur étendue, leur nature calcaire et leur exposition sud, offrent un habitat exceptionnel. Le "sentier des vautours" permet de mieux comprendre la présence de quatre espèces de vautours présents dans le Vercors.
Translate to English

images.caption: randonnée dans le Vercors: Le cirque d'Archiane à pied

title: Walk in the heart of the Penitents - Les Mées
short_description: A discovery loop within a sensitive natural area: the Penitents at Les Mées. A hike with beautiful views over the Durance Valley, the Alps and the Signal de Lure.
long_description:
The San Peyre path, which borrows part of the Pénitents path, dominates the village of Les Mées and allows you to discover the pudding rock formations in an unexpected and spectacular way. It also offers a wide panorama over the Durance Valley and the Lure mountain. Although relatively short, the trail evolves on steep terrain and requires good footwear.
The Pénitents des Mées is both a site classified at national and departmental level as a Sensitive Natural Area. The aim of these classifications is to reconcile both the preservation of the site and its discovery by the public. This very high quality natural territory is also fragile and it is important to protect it by developing it.

title: Walking Tour Freyung
short_description: This tour takes you through beautiful countryside. A large part of the route is in the forest, but we also come to fantastic viewpoints.
long_description: From the car park of the "Marterberg" ski lift, we follow the path north along the edge of the forest and enjoy beautiful views of Freyung. We continue until we reach the information board, here we keep to the left on the steeply ascending narrow path. We always follow our marker "2" through the forest. In Geyersberg there are again beautiful views. Continuing downhill, the path leads after several kilometres to a refuge where we can take a rest. Finally, we walk to the right and reach the most beautiful section of our tour - with wonderful views. Our way back leads first uphill and again for long stretches through the forest. From the edge of the forest, we experience beautiful views to the north again on the last metres to the starting point.

images.caption: From the entrance to the forest of Kirchenholz, we look across small meadows.
Over hilly landscape we look towards Freyung.
On the final descent, Freyung and the mountains of the Bavarian Forest can be seen from afar.
At the southernmost point of our hike, we keep to the right at this fork.
The first ascent already offers beautiful views of Freyung.

title: Trail ride around Saint-Saturnin-de-Lucian via the Rocher des Vierges
short_description: Magnificent trail in the Hé rault which allows to cover the Rock of the Virgins and to cross the Canyon of the Devil and its landscapes worthy of an American Colorado. Unforgettable!
long_description:
You don't have to go far to get away from it all, and this outing delivers on that promise! From the centre of Saint-Saturnin-de-Lucian, you take a road section for about 1 km before joining the path that goes around the Mont Haut. On the way, you can see the Hérault valley or the Lobévois valley.
The route is a gradual ascent.
A gradual ascent leads further to the famous Rocher des Vierges with a magnificent 360° view of the Pyrenees-Orientales, the Vissou and the Pic Saint-Loup. We then take a part of the GR365 (Saint-Jacques-de-Compostelle) and then the PR to return to the starting point.

title: Förstersteig
short_description: This makes every hiker's heart beat faster: 15 km of fantastic forest paths with breathtaking panoramic views. Halfway along the trail, Bürresheim Castle invites you to visit and offers unique insights into the life of the nobility between the 15th and 20th centuries.
long_description:
Highlights:
Eiterbach valley with pond, Luisenplatz hut with overwhelming panoramic view, mighty basalt columns, Fünfkantstein, Nettetal, Bürresheim Castle, Nitztal, Scheidkopf with Eifel panorama

At the starting point in Mayen-Kürrenberg, a forest path in the shady high forest leads leisurely downhill through the Ruppental, then through the Eiterbach valley with its lively babbling brook. At the Eiterbachweiher pond, a shelter and benches invite you to linger. A moderate climb leads to the Luisenplatz hut with a fine panoramic view over Mayen, the Maifeld and towards the Rhine. The path continues to the Altener Tempelchen refuge with a view of the mighty basalt columns of the quarry opposite. Follow the paths steadily uphill to the Fünfkantstein (historic waymarker, with refuge). Downhill, there are magnificent views of Bürresheim Castle and the Nette Valley. Arriving directly at the Nette, after a short passage along the L83, the trail leads to the historic Hammesmühle mill and continues along the banks of the Nette and down to the Nitztal valley. The ascent on the back of a rocky ridge is followed by a forest passage through oak coppice to Schälkopf with a beautiful view of Nitztal. A serpentine path winds upwards to Kürrenberg. Along the edge of the forest, you pass paddocks and meadows to Scheidkopf - the beginning of the final panoramic festival of the circular tour with wide views over the Eifel landscape!

images.caption: We make good progress on the dirt road.
We are offered a view of a historical monument.
Look! There in the distance is Bürresheim Castle!
The stone with explanatory board is also a good place to sit.

title: From Bautzen to Grubschütz
short_description: A short walk through the city and along the Spree.
long_description: We start this leisurely little tour at the bridge on Uferweg. Here we cross the bridge over the Spree and walk along Fischergasse on the right. At Dresdener Straße, we turn right briefly and then immediately left again into Bleichenstraße. Passing the sports field, we now follow the Neuschen Promenade, which now leads us along the Spree on the Spreeradweg to our destination and turning point in the Bautzen district of Grübschütz. Here is our turning point and we go back the same way.

title: Papa Stour Circular - Full Coastline Route
short_description: Papa Stour is an isle off the west side of Shetland accessed by a 40-minute ferry ride from West Burrafirth Pier. So be sure to check the ferry timetables before planning your trip!
long_description: Embarking on the Papa Stour Circular walk is like stepping into a timeless Shetland tale, where the rhythm of the North Atlantic waves and the call of seabirds guide your journey. This circular trail on the remote island of Papa Stour offers a captivating exploration of rugged landscapes and ancient history. As you meander along the cliffside paths, dramatic vistas unfold, revealing sheer sea cliffs, hidden coves, and panoramic views of the surrounding archipelago. The island's rich Norse heritage is palpable, with archaeological remnants, including a medieval church and Viking longhouses, scattered along the route. The rugged beauty of Papa Stour, coupled with the tranquility of its coastal trails, creates an immersive experience that transports walkers to a bygone era, making this circular walk a truly enchanting adventure in the heart of the Shetland Islands.

images.caption: Looking towards Papa Stour from Ness of Melby
View across Papa Stour to Hurdiback

title: Luitpoldweg near Bad Hindelang
short_description: On the trail of Prince Regent Luitpold, we hike in a varied way from Hinterstein to Imberg.
long_description: From 1850 onwards, His Royal Highness Prince Luitpold, the later Prince Regent Luitpold, was the lord of the hunt in Bad Hindelang. His annual stays have left some traces here. The Luitpold Trail connects the hunting lodges in Hinterstein and Oberstdorf and leads past these and other historic places: his former hunting lodge, the natural swimming pool „Prinze Gumpe“, the Hotel Prinz-Luitpold-Bad with sulphur spring and finally über the Luitpoldhöhe towards Imberg. Here the Luitpold Trail leaves the Bad Hindelang area at the Löwenbach Tobel.

title: Garden Tour through Bad Aibling
short_description: An easy walk through the south of Bad Aibling with many opportunities to rest awaits us. In the Upper Bavarian spa town, we take a look at the beautiful front gardens, among other things.
long_description: From the car park opposite the leisure centre, we turn left into Heubergstraße. Cross the Triftbach stream and turn left into Kranzhornstraße. This leads us to the Mangfall. We take the path along the riverbank to the right and from now on follow the red signs with the number 10. We walk past gardens, a beach volleyball court (1) and a children's playground (2). At the pedestrian bridge over the Mangfall, we turn right and walk along a footpath and cycle path to the railway line. At the crossing with barriers, we cross it and turn right again into the concrete path on the other side. It takes us past the railway station, several places to stop for refreshments (3), the churches (4) and the town centre (5). We use the next level crossing and walk along Lindenstraße back to the recreational area.

images.caption: In summer, some of the gardens along Lindenstraße are a paradise of blossoms.
Our path first leads along the Mangfall.
There are cosy cafés in Kirchzeile in the centre of Bad Aibling.
Beautiful old houses can be found along Lindenstraße in Bad Aibling.
The old row of houses in the centre of Bad Aibling shows itself in the evening light.
In the city centre, this fountain can be found against a historical backdrop.

title: From Leisnig to Tragnitz
short_description: A romantic walk through and around the almost thousand-year-old town of Leisning.
long_description:
On this hike in the Saxon Burgenland we can visit Mildenstein Castle, which was already mentioned in 1064 and is therefore one of the oldest castles in Saxony. and is one of the oldest castles in Saxony. Oldest castle is the keep in the inner courtyard, which dates from the last third of the 12th century. The oldest evidence of the castle's construction is the keep in the inner courtyard, which dates from the last third of the 12th century. In the castle the world's largest gauntlet boot can be seen in the castle itself, made by two master shoemakers for the 950th anniversary of the town in 1996. by two master shoemakers.
Centre in the German countryside,
in the Sachsengaue,
Where golden stands the field,
Blooming the floodplain,
There, Wand'rer stand still,
Because I want to show you
Leisnig, my Leisnig,
Town on the mountain.

title: Cycling from Lindau to Constance along Lake Constance
short_description: This cycle tour from Lindau takes us via Bregenz, Rheineck, Horn, Arbon, Romanshorn to Kreuzlingen and finally to Constance. In addition to numerous cultural highlights, we can always take a break for a swim or simply enjoy the view of Lake Constance.
long_description: The route from Lindau to Constance takes us from Germany through Austria and Switzerland until we reach German soil again in Constance. For the most part, the tour takes us very close to the shores of Lake Constance. If we want to see the many sights along the way, we can also divide the tour into two stages or days.

images.caption: Lion pier at the port of Lindau
View of the Imperia statue from Constance City Park.

title: Elfstedentocht stage 2
short_description: Second part of the Elfstedentocht.
long_description: The second part of the Elfstedentocht takes you from Sneek to IJlst. IJlst is a smaller town than Sneek, but be sure to have a look around. There are many churches and windmills. IJlst is known as the green heart of the eleven cities. So there is plenty of greenery to be found and that makes the village exude a peaceful atmosphere.

title: From Neustrelitz around Lake Zierk
short_description: We circle the scenic Zierker See lake and experience the castle park and baroque town centre of the former royal seat of Neustrelitz.
long_description: Coming from the south, we walk along Strelitzerstraße towards the city centre. Streets from eight directions meet at Markt (1). We turn left and walk between the town café and the pharmacy through Schlossstrasse to the Schlosspark. At the Orangerie (2), which is also a restaurant, we turn right. We reach the pavilion and the shore of the lake. At the Bootshaus restaurant we keep to the right and walk along the former railway to the quiet Neustrelitz harbour. We follow the railway tracks and walk along the Zierk side road to the main road, turn left to the gardens and right into Wiesenthaler Weg. After 500 m you can take a detour to the lake at the small rest stop (3) near Zierke. In Torwitz, follow the signs to "Prälank" and walk along a narrow asphalted road to the village. At the bus loop, look out for the signs to the erratic block garden (4). A good 80 erratic blocks from the last Ice Age are gathered here. 500 m after Prauml;lank, the main road turns right and we walk straight ahead through the beautiful, paved avenue, past Hohenlanke to the Userin-Neustrelitz road. Here we cross the Kammerkanal. Immediately afterwards we leave the main road again and stay by the information board on the avenue. It leads us to Franzosensteg (5) - here it is worth taking a detour because of the beautiful view. Finally, we reach the Slavic Village (6), completed in 1998, which aims to bring the life of the early settlers to life for visitors. A path through a small forest leads to the boat harbour. We return via the park, the castle church worth seeing and the animal park with around 300 indigenous species.

images.caption: The Franzosensteg leads us to the shore of the Zierker See.
There is a beautiful view from the shore of Lake Zierk at Franzosensteg.
Through modern installations, we look out onto the jetty on the shore of Zierker See.
The centre of the baroque town of Neustrelitz is the market square with the town church.
On this avenue near Hohenlanke we reach the bridge over the Kammerkanal.
Coming from the market, we encounter the English castle park.

title: Round trip Obersprockhövel in the Ruhr area
short_description: On this family-friendly hike we experience the surroundings of Sprockhövel.
long_description: Our hike across the heights and valleys of the countryside around Sprockhövel begins in Obersprockhövel, Am Schmalenberg. From Löhener Straße we follow the Graf-Engelbert path into the forest with the signpost "X" or "X28". At a fork, we choose the right-hand path, which leads us slightly uphill. Now we orientate ourselves by the circle with wave, the sign of the Agendarundweg Obersprockhövel, which leads us past a farmstead over the district road and onto the Nockenbergstraße. Walk a short distance to the left before turning right at the first opportunity and choosing the right path again at the next fork. We follow the main path along the edge of the forest. After a left-hand bend, we enter the forest, go straight on at the first junction and turn right at the second. We now walk towards "Im Kreßsiepen" and reach the Kreßsieper Weg, into which we turn left and follow it over the Löhener Straße crossroads. Behind the crossroads, turn left into the forest onto a path that runs parallel to Löhener Straße. After a short while we return to this road and follow it to "Am Nockenberg". In the centre of the village, turn left and walk through the fields along Nockenbergstraße. Cross the road as soon as you see "Auf Leckebüschen" on the right. The main path now leads us straight back through the forest to "Am Schmalenberg". Via Oberdraing we return to our starting point.

title: Through the wine villages of Dittwar and Königheim
short_description: The varied landscape around Tauberbischofsheim - a patchwork of forests and fields, meadows and vineyards - makes this hike so charming. Embedded in it are the pretty wine villages of Dittwar and Königheim.
long_description: The starting point for this hike is the railway station in Tauberbischofsheim. We cross the tracks and walk south through the Glockengraben and Dittigheimer Straße parallel to the tracks until we meet the B27 federal road. On the opposite side of the road, we now turn right. First parallel to the main road, later to Dittwarer Straße, we walk sometimes along the edge of the forest, sometimes in the pine forest, until we reach the beautiful district of Dittwar, which we cross on Talstraße and Gissigheimer Straße. The baroque church of St. Laurentius is worth a look. At the last houses of Dittwar, we change to a field path to our right, which we follow for a while. We pass vineyards, of which the "Dittwarer Oelkuchen" vineyard enjoys a particularly good reputation. At a fork in the road near a group of trees, we take the right-hand path, then turn left and right again at the next four-way intersection and walk along the edge of the forest for a while. At the fourth fork to the left, we turn off, go right at the next opportunity and immediately left again. This path leads us in wide loops through the fields, meadows and vineyards until we meet the B27 again at Königheim. After crossing the main road, we walk through the wine village of Königheim with its 900-year-old wine press tradition. In spring and autumn, when the wine taverns are open, we can take a break at the Geier eco-winery. Shortly before a roundabout, we change again to the other side of the B27 and walk past the gymnasium on the left, then always straight ahead between the edge of the forest and the Brehmbach. A long way past the sewage treatment plant, a large piece of forest appears to the left of the main road. Here we cross the B27 for the last time and after a few metres turn left into the forest. We follow the path through the woodland over the Stammberg and further through fields and meadows to Tauberbischofsheim. The Stammbergweg, which we are now on, joins Königheimer Straße shortly before a roundabout. At the roundabout straight ahead, we reach the Glockengraben again via the main road, which brings us back to our starting point at the station. In the beer garden "Hexenkessel" or in the restaurant "Zum alten Türmle" we can end the hike in a cosy atmosphere.

title: To the Münzenberg castle ruins
short_description: This tour offers great views üover the village Münzenberg.
long_description: Münzenberg Castle is already a thousand years old. You can climb the tower and from there you have a good view over the whole village.

images.caption: Das innere Tor der Burgruine Münzenberg
Blick über Münzenberg von der Burg aus

title: Askara Round
short_description: Easy tour along the Jochberger Ache, past old farms and via the Roman road back to Hochberg.

title: From Höfen to the sunny island of Dobel
short_description: A hike towards the sun: Your destination, the climatic health resort of Dobel, is considered the "island of sunshine" in the northern Black Forest thanks to its location at 700 m above sea level and the intense sunshine.
long_description: We start our tour at the railway station of Höfen, a town with 1700 inhabitants, and cross the tracks twice on the right. We follow the blue rhombus to the "Sitzbankhütte" (bench hut) 2.4 km away. To do so, we go left up the road, turn left again immediately in the bend to continue hiking on a path to the right in front of the forester's house. We zigzag steeply up the path until we reach a farm track, the "Sitzbankweg", which we follow half left further uphill. We cross a wide forest path and continue uphill towards the "Sitzbankhütte". At Franzosenbuckel we still have half a kilometre to go. At the crossroads, we briefly turn right uphill and then immediately turn left again. At a small open space we finally reach the bench hut. There we can treat ourselves to a short break after the somewhat strenuous ascent. We then hike a little uphill and at the next junction follow the blue rhombus to the left in the direction of the Spitzhütte. Now we walk along the slope of the Unterer Eiberges at a height. Occasionally we can catch a glimpse of the elevated Dobel, our destination, on the right. In front of it stretches the Eyachtal, which we also have to cross. After another kilometre, we reach the small Spitzhütte, from where you can enjoy the wonderful view of the Eyach valley, before we follow the blue rhombus with the white bar to the Eyachmühle deep down in the valley. We make our way downhill and pass the "Tornado Stone". This reminds us that on 10 July 1968, a tornado came through here from Pforzheim in the late evening hours and destroyed over 100 hectares of the surrounding forest. Soon a narrow path, the Dobler footpath, leads us steeply downhill into the Eyachtal valley. We cross a forest path and soon come to the Eyachmühle, where we can take a leisurely rest or even stop for a bite to eat. The small settlement lies in wonderful tranquillity by the beautiful Eyach stream, which has cut deep into the valley. We cross the bridge, hike briefly on the road to Dobel up the slope to the left before turning left again onto a forest path that takes us to the Mannenbach. We walk up the valley on the Unteren Mannenbachweg along this wildly romantic stream. Here you can really enjoy the peace and seclusion with the gentle babbling of the stream. We finally reach the Oberen Mannenbachweg, which we follow briefly to the right before turning sharply right again onto the Carl-Postweiler-Weg (blue rhombus with white bar) to Dobel. We cross the Mannenbach stream directly below the Seltenbrunnen well. The natural forest path becomes narrower for a short time. We leave the forest and continue straight ahead, directly towards the village. When we reach the edge of the village, the blue rhombus leads us through the village to our destination, the Dobel Kurhaus. The bus (to Neuenbürg) and the S-Bahn will take us back to the starting point in Höfen (please check the journey times beforehand!). If you were on the road quickly and still feel like an excursion to one of the surrounding towns, Höfen is the best place to do so. The gold town of Pforzheim, for example, is well known for its jewellery industry and has interesting exhibitions in the jewellery museum. Or we can go to Baden-Baden to recover from the hike in one of the parks or in the thermal baths.

images.caption: A view into the Enz valley.

title: From Bad Düben to Torgau through the Düben Heath
short_description: This long day tour takes us through the Dübener Heide. If we also want to hike the route back, accommodation in Torgau should be considered.
long_description: We start our extended day hike in Bad Düben Neuhofstraße. From here, Gartenstraße and Waldhofweg lead us out of the town into the fields outside Bad Düben. We keep to the right and orient ourselves to the eastern tip of the forest, along the edge of which we walk until we enter the forest at a sharp angle. We soon meet the Söllichauer Straße, cross it and follow the main path through the forest and after a while further through the fields. We finally come to Authausen and walk through the village first on Kirchstraße and then further on Obere Hauptstraße. This main road now leads us straight on further out of the village and towards the forest, at the edge of which, however, we turn right and walk south between the forest and the field. We stay on this path before we take a bend at the last junction before Pressel, turn left towards the forest and take the next path on the right. As soon as we have left the forest, we are on the Alte Heeresstraße (old army road), which takes us east to Neumühle. We pass a lake on the left and choose the middle path, which now leads us through the forest for a longer time. It runs dead straight and crosses the district road after a while, before it leads us out of the forest again after a long straight stretch. Now we come to Rotzsch. We take Eilenburger Straße until we turn right into Akazienallee, which leads us out of the village again via Turmstraße. To the south we walk again towards the forest, at the edge of which we turn left and follow the path to the east and after a while in a southerly direction to Pretzschau. Here we turn left, leave the forest and walk through fields towards Weidenhain. We now walk along the Torgau road for a while, but do not follow it to the right out of the village, but take the field path that follows it, passing the two lakes on the left and continuing towards the forest. As soon as we reach the first trees, the path forks. We choose the one on the right. At the next fork, we follow the left one until we turn right at the second crossroads. We follow this path out of the forest and on to Ziethenhof, where we first turn onto Sandstraße and then left onto Mühlenweg. We continue along Bergstraße and Hohe Straße until we reach Zinna. We walk along Dorfstraße to the other end of the village and continue through the fields to Welsau, at the beginning of which we turn right and now come to Torgau via Molkereiweg and the outer ring road. The quickest way to get to the centre from here is to walk along the outer ring road to Warschauer Straße, turn left into it and keep walking straight ahead.

title: From Bad Staffelstein up to the Mountain of Franconia
short_description: On this tour we experience the "Mountain of Franconia", the Staffelberg not far from the spa town of Bad Staffelstein. We hike 250 metres uphill to the striking rocky peak before returning to Bad Staffelstein through the Lautergrund.
long_description:
Our starting point is at the cemetery in Bad Staffelstein, where we find sufficient parking space. First we follow the beautiful historic wooden sign "Staffelberg" and hike steadily uphill. We cross the "A73", the Frankenschnellweg, and walk on a gravel path through the beautiful meadows at the foot of the Staffelberg. Through a sunken path we finally reach the farm track, where we continue uphill before we reach the Staffelberg plateau. There, after the almost one-hour ascent, we have the opportunity to take a break in the Staffelberg-Klause, where we especially recommend the freshly roasted sausages or the "white cheese", or we can enjoy a contemplative stop in the Adelgundi Chapel, which was once a popular place of pilgrimage for the Franks. By the way: A hermit lived on the Staffelberg at the beginning of the 20th century!
Now we should not miss the detour up to the Staffelberg rock. We hike along the circular plateau trail up to the summit cross, from where we have a wonderful panoramic view as far as Bamberg, the Grabfeldgau, the Thuringian Forest and Franconian Forest and, of course, the two monuments of Banz Monastery and Vierzehnheiligen. Bad Staffelstein's local mountain was also once a Celtic town: the Celts lived in two settlement rings, and numerous excavations and finds today bear witness to the former Celtic town of "Menosgada".
  After visiting the "Querkeleshöhle" and learning about the legend of the cave from the information board, we start our descent. On the plateau we follow the sign to "Horsdorf" and walk downhill via the Karlsteig for about half an hour until we reach the pretty village, which has already won the national competition "Unser Dorf soll schöner werden". Here we also have the opportunity to stop at the "Alte Mühle". Now we have reached the Lautergrund, keep to the right along the village street lined with beautiful half-timbered houses and walk along the Lauter on a footpath and cycle path back to Bad Staffelstein. We pass under the Frankenschnellweg, the Hopfenmühle, before we walk right uphill after entering the town to the cemetery.

images.caption: The Staffelberg is the destination of our tour.
This signpost shows us the route at the start.

title: The Alpspitz Ferrata above Garmisch Partenkirchen
short_description: The Alpsitz via ferrata (Alpspitz Ferrata) is an easy via ferrata to one of the most shapely German peaks. The Osterfelderbahn makes the ascent and descent much easier. The view from the summit is fantastic.
long_description: The Alspitz Ferrata leads from the mountain station of the Osterfelderbahn (Alpspitzbahn) to the 2628 m high Alpspitze high über Garmisch Partenkirchen. The Osterfelderbahn makes the ascent and descent much easier. If you like, you can also ascend or descend on foot. The mountain station and a café near the valley station are located directly on the trail. The via ferrata is excellently secured and not too difficult. Beginners can also venture on this via ferrata with experienced guidance. The route faces north-east. If you want to enjoy the sun and the fantastic view at the summit for a long time, note the times of the last cable car descent.

images.caption: The Alspitze above Garmisch Partenkirchen photographed from the Osterfelderkopf.
The summit ridge of the Alpspitze above Garmisch Partenkirchen.
The Alpspitze with the mountain station of the Osterfelderbahn.

title: Perlberg Round
short_description: Medium-difficulty tour along the Sintersbach stream via the Perlberg and Hanslern back to Jochberg.

title: From Wangerooge to the bathing beach and the west
short_description: On this hike we get to know the highlights of the island.
long_description: This circular walk offers us the opportunity to get to know both places on the island of Wangerooge. We start in Wangerooge and walk past the island railway station and along its tracks to the island's small side villages, Badestrand and Westen. Here we should definitely take a look at the island's old west tower. Then we walk through the dunes back to Wangerooge.

images.caption: Even clouds in the sky make the beach landscape glow.

title: Circular hike around Mulfingen
short_description: This hike of just under 28 kilometres takes us around the community of Mulfingen past many beautiful sights.
long_description:
We start our hike in Mulfingen. Past the school centre, the reservoir hall and the sports grounds, we hike into the Roggelhäuser valley. We do not go all the way to the dam, but turn half-left shortly before to walk along the reservoir to the pre-dam. Here we keep half-left again and follow the Roggelhäuser Bach stream. After about 500 m, we come to an ascent in the forest on the left that leads us to Ochsental. In the village, follow the signs towards Zaisenhausen. Further on, we can make a detour to the honey well before hiking steeply uphill to Zaisenhausen. In the village, we turn left before the St. Nepomuk bridge and follow the grotto path to the Lourdes Grotto, the largest grotto complex in southern Germany. After visiting it, walk back a little and cross the St. Nepomuk or Ette bridge in the direction of the Staigerbach stream. Old stone bars along the way remind us of the early wine-growing in this region. Continue through the Altenberg development area towards the Staigerbach valley, which you reach after 2 km. There we turn right and after 50 m immediately left into the Pfingstberg forest. A little later, we cross the main road or above the ebm.papst company. Then we follow a dirt road that turns off to the right 30 m downhill.
On reaching the juniper heath, we can enjoy the beautiful view over the Jagst valley. Approx. 100 m after a sharp left-hand bend, we turn sharply right and walk up the hill towards Hollenbach. We come across the Löhleinsberg resettlement farms and turn left there. A little later we reach Hollenbach. Here we look at the 1000-year-old lime tree by the church before we walk past the Feinauer building yard through the Rißbach valley towards Ailringen. We pass the Rißbach dam and walk downhill along the stream to Ailringen. At the entrance to the village, a path branches off to the right and takes us over a short climb to the left to the cemetery. The special feature of this resting place are the wooden crosses. After a short detour to the historic town hall, we head through Ailringen towards Mulfingen. At the Mühlbeck company, first turn right over the Jagst bridge and then half-right up to the forest adventure trail, at the end of which we turn left and head downhill onto the Jagst valley cycle path. In Mulfingen you can visit the pilgrimage chapel of St. Anna.

title: Snowshoe tour from Grasgehren to the Riedberger Horn
short_description: This tour up to the Riedberger Horn (1787 m) is an Allgäu winter classic and, due to its position as the highest peak in the Allgäu flysch mountains, offers a magnificent panoramic view. summit of the Allgäu flysch mountains, it offers a magnificent panoramic view.
long_description: This snowshoe tour up the Riedberger Horn from Grasgehren is an unstrenuous enjoyment tour that is also suitable for beginners. The ascent and descent routes are south-facing, the descent allows for the descent allows for variations, and some sections may be sections may be moderately steep. The entire tour takes place on mostly gently slopes. Orientation is easy. In Grasgehren we also have the In Grasgehren we also have the opportunity to return to the restaurant.

title: The Ziegelhütter Trail around Waldmünchen
short_description: This walk takes us around the grounds of the old brickworks. We enjoy beautiful views of Waldmünchen and the surrounding landscape.
long_description: From the car park, we walk to the left in the direction of the miniature golf course. On the right-hand side of the path is an information board about the hiking routes that run here. Our path is marked red and white and is called "W 1". We follow the markings straight ahead and pass the miniature golf course. At the signpost tree we turn left. At the next fork we keep left, at the T-junction we go right. Soon we come across a very nice resting place on a small hill. We meet the country road, which we follow briefly to the right. At the next turn we orientate ourselves to the right, at the crossroads we turn right again in the direction of the beautifully situated Blumloh equestrian farm. From there we walk back through the forest.

title: From Bad Bibra to Krawinkel
short_description: On this somewhat easier tour we hike through forests to Krawinkel.
long_description:
Our hike starts at the car park next to the adventure pool in Bad Bibra. We follow the Biberbach stream to a petrol station, where we turn left out of town towards Laucha. At the turnoff to the lime works, we turn right and cross the railway tracks. We follow the right-hand path, the Alte Naumburger Weg, to the "Forst Bibra", keep to the right at a fork and reach the forest via a shell limestone plateau. Forst Bibra" has been a nature reserve since 1961. We now walk straight ahead along the old limestone quarry to Dr. Stockmann-Höhe. Here we take the left path in the direction of Karwinkel.
In Karwinkel, we walk along the village road through the village to the village pond, where we turn left onto a gravel path and cross a field path after a few metres. We follow a meadow path to the edge of the forest, where we turn right into the forest. Once we have crossed the forest, we go left along the edge of the forest across a meadow and back into the forest. After about 60 m, we turn left again and after a few metres we go right uphill again into a mixed forest. We soon reach the "Schöne Aussicht", from where we have a magnificent view of Bad Bibra and its surroundings. We continue along the path to the "Spitzen Hut" and turn right at a fork in the path and after a few metres turn right again towards Bad Bibra. At the edge of the forest, we turn left until we return to our starting point via the "Alten Naumburger Weg".

title: The Lac Blanc from the Col des Montets
short_description: THE mythical Chamonix hike with a breathtaking view
long_description:
Famous throughout the world thanks to the reflections of the Mont Blanc massif in its crystal clear water, Lake Blanc is accessible by various routes from the Chamonix-Mont-Blanc Valley.
Prepare yourself for an exceptional hike! Lac Blanc requires a bit of effort but you will be rewarded with a 360° panorama of the entire Mont-Blanc massif as well as the Aiguilles Rouges.

title: On the Knights' Hiking Trail around Waldkirch
short_description: An exciting hike suitable for prams - not only for families: on the knights' hiking trail with the wooden knight sculptures, you climb about 150 metres in altitude to Kastelburg Castle.
long_description: We start in front of the station entrance in Waldkirch and walk in the direction of Kastelburg. We cross the level crossing and follow the sign "Fußweg zur Burg" up the hill. After about 500 m, a wooden plaque with a stylised damsel points us to the knight's footpath to Kastelburg Castle. Here we turn right on the unpaved path to the hikers' car park (1). Behind the car park, the actual knights' trail begins - this children's trail was built in 2003. Eight knights made of wood and metal line the trail - first we meet knight Martin Malterer... After about 1 km, this path leads past other wooden knights to Kastelburg Castle (2). This castle was first mentioned in a document in 1289 and was built by the Knights of Schwarzenberg. Martin Malterer bought the dominion of Kastelberg in 1354 and thus also owned the Kastelburg until it changed hands again for lack of male descendants. At the beginning of the 16th century, the castle was badly damaged by a great fire and later renovated and rebuilt by the Staufers and Habsburgs. In 1634, the castle was plundered and destroyed. The remains of this castle complex are the ruins that still stand today. After numerous changes of ownership, the Kastelburg, or what remained of it, finally became the property of the town of Waldkirch in 1970. The circular path directly at the castle is unfortunately not suitable for prams, but it is worth seeing. After we have also "conquered" the castle, we walk back to the last crossroads in the forest. Here we keep to the right and walk along the circular path until we reach a large crossroads. We follow the Hohtannweg 300 m uphill. At a bench we continue our hike uphill on the narrower path until the next crossroads. At the crossroads, turn left towards Batzenhäusle. On a wide forest path we walk along the markings (red rectangle on a white background) until we reach a large crossroads and follow the signpost to the Obere Hütte (3), a wonderful barbecue area with a resting place and a refuge. Here we are still about 4 km from our destination and can treat ourselves to a break. Now we walk uphill on the Obere Winterhaldeweg (4). Soon we walk downhill again and hike (blue dot) towards the hospital. Again and again we can catch a glimpse of the town of Waldkirch and the Elz valley through the trees. Shortly before the first hospital building, we take a sharp right downhill on the Galgenbruckweg (5). Numerous benches invite you to enjoy the view through the forest to the castle and the town. This forest path leads comfortably downhill and joins the road at the entrance to Waldkirch at a church. We cross the railway crossing and the subsequent bridge. After the bridge, we hike to the left and continue on the footpath along the banks of the Elbe. This riverside path, the "Fritz-Schubert-Weg", is also a fish nature trail (6) with information boards. We eventually pass a school and continue walking until we reach a playground. Only a few metres after the playground, we take the road to the left and cross the bridge. If you want, you can also take a detour to the right into Waldkirch town centre with its half-timbered houses. By the way, Waldkirch has a very long town history. It was first mentioned in a document in 926 A.D. A significant date is the year 1300, when Waldkirch was granted town charter. In the Middle Ages, the walls and towers of Waldkirch were repeatedly stormed, besieged and conquered. After ore and silver mining in the Suggental district became unprofitable, gemstone cutting flourished, dating back over 500 years. In 1799, a new craft, organ building, took root. But we can already see our starting point, the railway station, which we reach after a few metres.

title: Koberner Castle Trail
short_description: Silence, romantic stream valleys and two castles await us on this hike near the Moselle.
long_description: Silence, romantic stream valleys and two castles await us on this hike near the Moselle. The Oberburg and Niederburg castles are not far apart on a mountain spur above Kobern. The Niederburg with its almond-shaped ground plan was built in the 12th century and destroyed in 1688. The upper castle was built at the same time as the lower castle on a Celtic fortification, but fell into disrepair much earlier. Thus, apart from the keep and the late Romanesque Matthias Chapel, only a few remains of the ring wall can be seen today. The hexagonal chapel was built around 1220/40 by the knight Heinrich II of Isenburg. It was intended to house the head of the apostle which the knight had brought back from a crusade. The relic has not been housed in the Matthias Chapel for a long time, but was but was transferred to Trier Cathedral in 1420 after several stops along the way.

title: Hiking according to Feng Shui around Lalling
short_description: This hike takes us through Germany's first Feng Shui Park with a bathing lake and along the nature discovery trail to Lalling.
long_description: We start from the car park to the bathing lake. Along curved paths we walk through the Feng Shui Park and leave it to the west of the tennis court. The signs "Naturlehrpfad" and hiking trail no. 1 (red circle with Roman 1) show us the way into the forest and across the Ranzinger Bach stream. A path leads us through sparse forest. We follow the road and cross the main road at Gerholling. There, trail no. 3 "Steinbruchsteig" leads us to a beautiful Kneipp facility. Then we follow the markings (green triangle) to the Lallinger church. Along the main road we reach a brick building and turn right, following the signpost "Gunthersteig". We return past the pottery, the football pitch and a facility for roller skaters.

title: Hain-Main-Danube Canal Circuit near Bamberg
short_description: This varied jogging route takes us from the edge of the cathedral city along the Main-Danube Canal to Strullendorf and back through the Hauptsmoorwald forest to the starting point at the Jahnwiese. The Laustrecke offers a beautiful combination of forest, meadow, river and magnificent views of the historic buildings of Bamberg's old town.
long_description:
We first walk into the Hain, Bamberg's city forest. Even in the Middle Ages a floodplain forest between the two banks of the Regnitz. In 1803, at the request of King Maximilian I Joseph, it was transformed into an artificial garden. English Garden in Munich into an artificial city park. city park. A small, idyllically situated pond in the heart of the grove is also one of the is one of the park's special features. In the summer, its shores are the haunt of numerous in the summer, and in the winter the Hainweiher is used as a skating rink. skating rink. In the neighbouring botanical city garden of Bamberg you can marvel at the rich variety of flora in the summer months. At numerous small temples, pavilions and monuments, the route continues along the Regnitz forest path through the tranquil avenues of the grove. Over the bridge at the Buger Spitze and along the Rhine-Main-Danube Canal we pass the village of Bug - here you will find several typical Franconian inns, which invite you to enjoy a cool beer outdoors in the summer months - to Strullendorf. to Strullendorf.
The first plans for the construction of the canal date back to the year Charlemagne and date back to the year 793. However, the idea was more than 1000 years later with the construction of the Ludwig Canal (1836 and 1846) between 1846) between Bamberg and Kelheim. After its destruction in the Second World War the construction of today's Main-Danube Canal began in 1960. Through its connection to the Rhine, it forms the intermediate section of the inland waterway between the inland waterway between the North Sea and the Black Sea.
From the banks of the canal we have a magnificent view of the elevations of Franconian Switzerland. Franconian Switzerland. On our right we always have the Regnitz and its typical floodplain in and its typical alluvial landscape. In summer you can see numerous numerous nature lovers bathing, sunbathing, cycling or rowing.
From Strullendorf we return along the opposite bank of the canal in the direction of Bamberg. direction Bamberg, where we first cross the Bamberg Hauptsmoorwald and later reach the later reach the Südflur. From now on, the horizon opens up to reveal the the beauty of Bamberg's old town. Next to the Altenburg we have fantastic views of the numerous historical buildings of the seven-hill city.
At the end of the tour we pass the Jako Arena - the Bamberg basketball team plays its Bundesliga home games in this impressive hall. their home games in the Bundesliga.

title: Walking Bad Grönenbach
short_description: This short Nordic walking tour takes us through the Bad Grönenbach forest.
long_description: In Bad Grönenbach, pastor Sebastian Kneipp was once present - we move on the Nordic Walking circuit through the Bad Grönenbach forest. The start is directly at the information board, where we can still get information about Nordic walking. We follow route 1, which accompanies us through the forest clearly recognisable on the marking sign. Soon we reach a station of the parallel forest adventure trail: the barefoot trail (1) entices us to take a short break without shoes. Continue following the markings, via the information station (2) to the geology display board (3), before we continue uphill to a fork, where we continue to walk left to the exercise board (4). Now follow the signs downhill and left back to the starting point.

The barefoot path offers a change of pace.

title: Hiking via Pic Saint-Michel and Col de l'Arc
short_description: At an altitude of 1966 m, Pic Saint-Michel is one of the Vercors' most emblematic peaks, dominating the Grenoble valley. The panorama over much of the Alps is exceptional!
long_description: This mountain circuit allows you to discover different types of environment in magnificent surroundings. The route takes in undergrowth, alpine meadows and lapiaz.

title: Small Spremberg Round
short_description: Through the pretty old town of Spremberg, situated on an island in the Spree, and along the banks of the Spree, we walk to such promising places as the Swan Pond and Love Island.
long_description: Through the pretty old town of Spremberg, situated on an island in the Spree, and along the banks of the Spree, we walk to such promising places as the Swan Pond and Love Island. In Spremberg's city park we can climb the Bismarck Tower, from whose viewing platform we have a magnificent view of Spremberg and the Spree Valley. If you still have time and feel like it, you can visit the castle on the market square after the hike or stop off at one of the restaurants.

title: Walking around Oberreichenbach
short_description: An easy Nordic walking tour on wide forest paths with different surfaces, without steep passages and with little difference in altitude. The tour is well suited for beginners.
long_description: We start our easy tour, ideally suited for beginners, at the Bechergass hikers' car park. We warm up and follow the yellow rhombus, which accompanies us on the entire tour, on an asphalted service road through the forest to the Heselwasenhütte. Now we continue on the gravelled Unterer Becherweg towards Becherberg, where impressive views of the Kleine Enztal open up. After about half of the tour, we can check our circulation here and do some exercises to strengthen ourselves. Via the Katzensteigle we come to a gravelled forest path that leads us towards Naislach. Shortly before the edge of the village, we turn right again into the forest, through which we finally reach the hikers' car park again. Here we check our values once again and then relax with some loosening exercises.

The view into the Kleine Enztal.

title: Walking tour around Portbail
short_description: Made at low tide, this circuit allows you to discover Portbail between the seaside and the village. Enjoy your walk in this little corner of Normandy!

title: Stick - Nordic Walking Nieheim
short_description: A beautiful trail through fields, woods and meadows with views of the Köterberg and the Teutoburg Forest.
long_description: A particularly beautiful trail, which leads partly as a grass path through the Buchholz. At the exercise sign, the magnificent view of the Köterberg and the foothills of the southern Teutoburg Forest awaits us. This running route is very attractive because of its changing landscapes with unobstructed views of forest, field and meadows. From spring to autumn, the splendour of the flowers enchants every Nordic walker.

title: Juniper Trail
short_description: Through unspoilt nature, juniper heath and all kinds of forest. If you want a bit more, you can combine the Juniper Trail with the Mountain Heath Trail to make a great circular tour.
long_description:
Highlights:
Renaturalised areas of juniper heath, wide views of the Eifel, Nettetal, Wabelsberg nature reserve, Büschberg.

The starting point of the dream trail is the Wabelsberg juniper hut at the upper edge of Langscheid. The trail leads through a beautiful heath landscape around the Wabelsberg with views of the wooded hilltops of the Eastern Eifel. Across the plateau, the trail leads past Langenfeld with its striking church (Eifel dome). Interrupted again and again by forest passages, it soon climbs as a meadow path to the Büschberg. The juniper heath, typical of the Vordereifel, invites you to take a short break at the beautifully designed rest area. Soon the trail dips into the forest, where a turnoff leads to the neighbouring "Bergheidenweg" dream trail. The wide forest path winds down, follows a lively stream and finally leads into the Nettetal valley. It is already a short uphill stretch on a grassy path with a view over the valley. The trail swings off into a tall beech forest, descends once more towards the Nette, before the final ascent through varied forest begins back to the Wabelsberger Wacholderhütte.
