title: Veluwe walking route
short_description: During this route, you will discover a small part of the Veluwezoom national park. This part of the Veluwe lies just above Arnhem.
long_description: The Veluwe is a protected nature reserve with no clear boundaries. Many animals such as: red deer and wild boar have chosen the Veluwe as their habitat. The Veluwe is also an area where many Hanseatic towns and castles can be found. Middachten Castle is near this route, so you could walk past it.

title: From Siusi to the Sciliar
short_description: The mountain tour on the Sciliar is very interesting from a scenic and geological point of view. From the summit we enjoy a magnificent view of the near and far summit regions of the Dolomites.
long_description: With 56 hectares, the Alpe di Siusi is the largest alpine pasture area in Europe. It is accessible by several cable cars and lifts. The Alpe di Siusi cable car takes about 10 minutes to reach the plateau, but we only touch the southern edge of the Alpe di Siusi. On the ascent we soon reach a station on the Oswald von Wolkenstein Trail. This Oswald was an important knight in the late Middle Ages. The next stage takes us to the Schlernbödelehütte, a hut built in 1961 by the Bolzano section of the German and Austrian Alpine Club. It was built to replace the Schlernhaus, which had passed to an Italian association. From the summit of the Schlern, the Petz, you have a wonderful view. The following peaks and mountain groups, among others, come into view: Rosengarten, Puez, Geisler, Piz Boe. On the way back, we take the Geologensteig trail via the Possliner Schwaige. At 10 different stations we can look at the prevailing rock strata.

title: Cheakamus Lake
short_description: Great views with little effort
long_description:
This is one of the easiest hikes in Garibaldi Provincial Park. The hike to Cheakamus Lake will offer you beautiful views of this turquoise lake situated in between towering mountains. The lake is fed by multiple glaciers and this is why it gets it's very special color. 
The hike to just the lake takes about an hour one way and you can choose if you want to continue all the way to Singing Creek Campground or if you want to just take a look at the lake and return to the parking lot. 
You can camp at Cheakamus Campground with 10 tent spots. Or you can camp further in at Singing Creek Campground with 6 tent spots. You need to pre-book overnight stays at these campgrounds.
There are food hang facilities at the campgrounds, but they may fill up so prepare to bring your own equipment as well

title: Black Tusk from Garibaldi Lake
short_description: Get up close with Black Tusk from Garibaldi Lake Campground
long_description:
Black Tusk Mountain is one of the most spectacular mountains in Garibaldi Provincial Park. Its jagged edges and deep black color is visible from far away and from several points along the Sea to Sky highway.
There are three main routes for hiking to Black Tusk. All three options are very long day hikes so consider staying a night at one of the nearby campsites before you do the final section up to the mountain.
This hike starts from Garibaldi Lake.

title: Store Blåmannen
short_description: Hike Kvaløya’s tallest and most demanding peak
long_description:
Store Blåmannen demands your focus and effort the entire trek, but at the top, there will never be a more exquisite experience. Not only will you have worked hard (therefore clearly earning that "kanelbolle" you were eyeing at the cafe this morning) but you will be overlooking some of the most magnificent scenery you can imagine.
Store Blåmannen is the highest peak on the island of Kvaløya, reaching 1044 moh and located in the middle of the island overlooking Kaldfjorden. This is one of the better-known hikes on Kvaløya and therefore well-marked and well-maintained. Keep in mind this is a more physically demanding hike but well worth the accomplishment at the top.
Kvaløya, “whale island”, just minutes from Tromsø, is located within the arctic circle and is the 5th largest island off of Norway’s mainland. This island boasts several fjords and 10 peaks higher than 700 moh, three of which are over 1,000 moh. The west coast of Kvaløya, Sommerøya, faces the open ocean and is the warmest area of the Tromsø municipality. It is hard to choose what stands out more on Kvaløya: the magnificent mountain peaks or the raw coastal beauty. 
Tromsø and Kvaløya both provide a variety of available hotels and airbnb’s. If you are looking for a special norwegian summer accommodation we recommend checking out Sommerøy Arctic Hotel, located on the western coast of Kvaløya.

title: Trail to the Fumaça Waterfall in the Chapada Diamantina
short_description: The Fuma waterfall, surrounded by majestic cânions and the exuberant nature of the Chapada Diamantina, is an impressive 340 metres high and is one of the most famous post cards of the region;
long_description:
If you want to get to know the Chapada Diamantina, this is a trail that cannot be missing from your itinerary. Stay in the bucolic village of Caeté-Açu, in the Vale do Capão, a perfect destination for those who want tranquillity and direct contact with the beauties of the region. From here, it is about 10 kilometres through valleys and rivers for an incredible experience at one of the most spectacular viewpoints of the Chapada.
The trail begins at the headquarters of the Associacao o de Conductores de Visitantes do Vale do Capão, a non-profit association that supports sustainable tourism and protects the environment of the Capão Valley. They also offer reception and guiding of tourists, a variety of information about the region, monitoring and assistance for visitors passing through this trail. You will be invited to enter your details in a control book and hire a guide if you wish. 
Read carefully the safety recommendations on the access à trail. Só é possible to start the tour between 8: 00 and 13:00 hours.

title: The Imbut trail
short_description: In the opinion of many, the Imbut trail is a must for hikers who walk the Gorges du Verdon...
long_description:
The "Wow" effect is coming! This hike requires a certain experience but what a pleasure for the eyes!
You will walk through the Styx du Verdon, a place where the gorges narrow to form a tortuous thread in the middle of the Verdon Canyon, before the waters of the Verdon River flow into the valley;of the Verdon disappear under a huge chaos of boulders overhung by 400 m peaks at the place called "l'Imbut" (the funnel in Provencal).
Some of the passages on the cliff face and through the boulders can be difficult. Although suitable for all seasons, some passages can be technical when it rains or in winter.
The route is not suitable for all seasons.

title: Kyffhäuser Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The International Kyffhäuser Mountain Run has been based in Frankenhausen since 1979 and has attracted numerous runners ever since.
long_description: The range of courses includes various distances: The so-called Kyffhäuser Mountain Marathon is the main race. In addition, distances of 6 km, 14.9 km and the half-marathon distance have to be mastered, whereby everything from running to walking/nordic walking to hiking is permitted. The Salomon Trail Running Cup takes place on the 14.9 km mountain run.

title: गौरीकुंड-केदारनाथ टरैक मार्ग
short_description: 18 किलोमीटर लंबा गौरीकुंड केदारनाथ ट्रैक एक तीर्थयात्रा मार्ग है जिसने हालिया समय म ें एक चुनौती पूर्ण हिमालयी नेचर ट्रेल के तौर पर युवा हाइकर्स के ब ीच  लोकप्रियता हासिल की है।
long_description:
भारत के उत्तराखंड राज्य में स्थित केदारनाथ चार धाम तीर्थों में से एक है। केदारनाथ शहर और मंदिर गर्मियों में मई से अक्टूबर तक खुले रहते हैं। हालाँकि यहाँ जाड़ों में भी आया जा सकता है लेकिन तब भारी बर्फबारी के लिए तैयार रहने की जरूरत है।
साल 2013 की विनाशकारी बाढ़ के दौरान गौरीकुंड-केदारनाथ मार्ग का अधिकांश भाग बह गया था। राज्य सरकार ने रामबाड़ा तक पुराने वाले ट्रैक की मरम्मत करी है और रामबाड़ा के बाद नया ट्रैकिंग रूट बनाया है।
गौरीकुंड से पहले पड़ने वाले सोनप्रयाग शहर में एक सरकारी चिकित्सा केंद्र उपलब्ध है। सभी तीर्थयात्रियों और पैदल यात्रियों को यहां से मेडिकल फिटनेस सर्टिफिकेट लेना होता है। सोनप्रयाग से घोड़े और पालकी भी बुक कर सकते हैं।
आपके सामान को केदारनाथ तक ले जाने के लिए पोर्टर्स (जिन्हे स्थानीय भाषा में पिट्ठू कहा जाता है) भी उपलब्ध हैं।वो आपके सामान की डिलीवरी सीधे आपके होटल में कर सकते हैं या आपके साथ साथ भी चल सकते हैं।
केदरनाथ मार्ग बहुत ही सुन्दर है। शहर शांत और अध्यात्म से भरा हुआ है। मंदिर अपने आप में पत्थर के काम का एक उत्कृष्ट उदाहरण है और 6000 मीटर से ज्यादा ऊँची चोटियों के बीच स्थित है।

title: Remstecken Koblenz
short_description: This beautiful jogging route, which is not particularly demanding, is suitable for anyone with a little fitness and jogging experience. The route is a five-minute drive from Koblenz city centre.
long_description: The tour leads almost exclusively through woodland and at the beginning even a short stretch on the Rheinburger-Höhenweg. There is a magnificent view of the Moselle valley at one point.

title: Rennesøyhodnet
short_description: A great hike with beautiful views of the islands surrounding Stavanger
long_description: Enjoy an easy hike to Rennesøyhodnet on Rennesøy island in the Ryfylke Islands. Just a 30-minute drive from Stavanger, this hike is easy to access and child-friendly. Walk through the farmlands and small forest out to the vista, providing incredible views of the surrounding ocean and islands.

title: Hovlandsnuten
short_description: Hike the stone steps to a cabin with a view over the Saudafjord
long_description: Hovlandsnuten is a very popular peak to climb near Sauda, with lovely views out over the Saudafjord. Stone steps laid by Nepalese Sherpas help ease the steep trail to the top. On the peak there’s a small cabin where you can shelter from the elements and admire the view.

title: Vinddalen to Skåpet
short_description: Enjoy an easy hike up the valley to the incredible modern cabins at Skåpet
long_description:
A nice, family-friendly hike up Vinddalen valley to the modern cabins at Skåpet. Make it an overnight stay at the new cabins or enjoy a day-trip up the beautiful valley.
Skåpet cabins - The DNT cabins located at the end of the hike. Visit the website to book the cabin or call +47 51 84 02 00.

title: Kvænan
short_description: Visit Senja's third highest peak
long_description:
Kvænan is a characteristic mountain with three pinnacle peaks on the southwest side of Senja island. It is Senja’s third highest peak and is situated on the Atlantic Ocean, so you will surely get some great views from the top. 
Flakstadvåg Camping is your closest accommodation option to this adventure. You can also choose to stay in Finnsnes which is about hour drive from the trailhead.

title: Aurlandsdalen
short_description: Hike a classic route through the lush Aurland valley
long_description:
The trail through the beautiful Aurlandsdalen (Aurland Valley), is considered one of Norway’s truly classic hiking routes. This popular hike between the small settlements of Østerbø and Vassbygdi traces the Aurland river as it descends through the valley, providing stunning views the whole way.
You’ll come across mountain farms, waterfalls and plenty of opportunities to soak up the Norwegian nature. It makes for a perfect day trip from Flåm where you can enjoy a post-hike beer and feast at the Ægir brewpub.
By starting in Østerbø the trail is downhill, making for a much easier hike and constant views down the valley. If steep climbs don’t worry you it’s certainly possible to start hiking from Vassbygdi and follow the suggested route in reverse. You could also choose to only hike as far as Sinjarheim to experience the valley without investing a whole day.
There are a range of accommodation options in Aurland and Flåm for all budgets. The historic Fretheim Hotel offers luxurious comfort for those looking to pamper themselves after a long hike.
If you prefer an early start, or are walking up the valley, you can stay at Aurlandsdalen Turisthytte which offers rooms and camping as well as meals and snacks.

title: Walking route dunes The Hague
short_description: This route is 12 kilometres long and takes about 3 hours. You enjoy walking through the dunes.
long_description: The dune area around The Hague is a real Dutch dune area. You walk along beautiful paths with occasional views of the sea. In between, you also walk through pieces of woodland where Scottish Highlanders graze. In short, it is a beautiful dune area where you can walk for hours. You walk back via the beach. This way you can really admire the sea.

images.caption: The dunes in the nature reserve

title: Skarvedalsvatnet Lake
short_description: Enjoy a family friendly hike to a beautiful mountain lake
long_description:
The mountain lake Skarvedalsvatnet is easily reached by a short hike through wild landscape. The contrast between the colorful heather and the rugged valleys created by the glacier higher up is a great reward for not too much effort.
This trail is suitable for families and those seeking a less demanding hike. The route leads through mellow terrain past a small waterfall and ponds. If you are lucky you might find a cloudberry or two.
Hov Hyttegrend offers cabins and facilities for tents, as well as shuttle services to Fossestien every morning in the high season.
Flatheim Farm is a traditional B&B. They offer comfortable beds and facilities for camping, as well as guided trips and a summer café with local refreshments.
In Balestrand you can find a choice of hotels, B&Bs and self-catering apartments. Historical Kviknes Hotel was the favourite of famous painters in the 1800s.
Near Sande on the the Sunnfjord side of Gaularfjellet, Villa Åmot offers unique cultural experience. In Jølster and Førde you will find both self-catering apartments and hotels.

title: Elfstedentocht stage 5
short_description: Today is the fifth leg of the Elfstedentocht.
long_description: Today you will cycle from Stavoren to Workum via Hindeloopen. Once again, you will cycle a stretch along the IJselmeer also known as the Zuiderzee in Friesland. It is definitely worth taking a break in Hindeloopen. This village, too, has beautiful old buildings that are a must-see. Once you arrive in Workum, it is also worthwhile to walk around the old town and the beautiful nature that surrounds it.

title: Around Nagel
short_description: The circular hiking trail leads to all the distinctive and noteworthy points around the municipality of Nagel.
long_description:
This tour offers nature lovers unique insights into the Nagel meadows and numerous special features of the flora and fauna. The adventure trail not only brings us closer to the beauty, diversity and uniqueness of the area, it is also intended to help local residents and holidaymakers alike learn about the evolved structures and historical developments of the village. On 36 information boards, the diverse nature, historical contexts and local peculiarities around the municipality of Nagel are explained in German-Czech. Of course, you will also find inns, restaurants and beer gardens along the route for a cosy stop.
Starting points:
Parking area at the community centre in the district of Mühlbühl, Kösseine hiking car park in the district of Hohenbrand, as well as in the districts of Reichenbach.

title: Stedjeåsen
short_description: Venture up a local trail for views of Sogndal and the Sognefjord
long_description: The trail up to Stedjeåsen is easily accessible from Sogndal center and offers views of the town as well as a lovely view of the Sognefjord near the top. The well-worn route is popular with locals on their daily workouts. While not a long or particularly steep trail, the path to the top is a steady climb and requires an average fitness level.

title: TransRarău Road
short_description: TransRarăul is the most spectacular road in Bucovina and one of the most beautiful mountain roads in Romania. The road is a favourite not only for motorcyclists but also for cyclists.
long_description:
The TransRarăul must be on the list of places to visit in Bucovina, both for the beautiful scenery and for the mountain hiking opportunities it offers.
Unlike the other well-known transmontane trails, the TransRarăul does not lead out into the Alpine plain. Much of the route runs through coniferous forests on good roads. Whether in a car or on a bicycle, on the TransRarăul you will not experience the adrenaline rush of dizzying peaks, but the tranquility of calming views. However, in the tight curves you can still experience the thrill of adventure.
What makes this road one of the most desirable in the country is the fact that it provides relatively easy access to some of the most important sights of the Rarău Massif - the Rarău Monastery, Pietrele Doamnei, Cabana and the Rarău Peak. On the opposite side there is also the possibility to climb to the Vf. Giumalău, not as easy to reach as Raraul.Before Cabana Rarău, a maximum altitude of 1500 meters is reached.

title: Burgazada Walking Route
short_description: Burgazada is a nature route that can be an alternative to nature routes.
long_description:
Burgazada is a very special place that you should definitely add to your list of places to visit in Istanbul. The island is frequently preferred both for its natural beauty and the activities it promises, such as yürüyüyüş.
This nature walking route is a route that does not tire you much in terms of distance while accompanied by the unique island view.  You start the route immediately after getting off the ferry pier. You can add many special places such as Sait Faik Abasıyanık Müzesi, one of the most visited places on the island, to your sightseeing list. The route starts from the shore of the island and connects you back to the ferry pier after a tour around the island.
If you are looking for nature routes in Burgazada, you can add this route to your list and start exploring the island.

title: Tagestour zu den Seen von Aricocha und Huacracocha
Prest
short_description: Hike up a mountainside at a bend in the Aurlandsfjord
long_description:
This trail, located a short distance from Stegastein Viewpoint, has to provide one of the most impressive fjord views in Norway. The viewpoint at the end of the trail sits at a bend in the fjord from where you can see back towards Aurlandsvangen and Flam, as well as further down the fjord towards Undredal and the entrance to the Nærøyfjord. From here, it’s easy to understand why the Nærøyfjord and the surrounding landscape is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Note that this hike doesn’t lead to the actual summit of Prest (1,478 meters above sea level), but to a viewpoint and cairn below the summit at 1,363 meters. While the hike is not too demanding, remember that the weather can change quickly in the mountains and rain and fog can make the trail tricky to navigate. Have enough clothing with you to stay warm and dry and take care on a slippery trail.

title: Balçova Thermal - Behzat Tepe
short_description: We start from Balçova Thermal Hotel böl;area and go up to Behzat Tepe, a popular destination for nature lovers, and from there back to the thermal hotel.
long_description:
Behzat Tepe is an indispensable point for nature lovers in Izmir. Anyone looking for nature routes in Izmir must have crossed paths with Behzat Tepe and the routes in the Balçova böl; region. Nature lovers have repeatedly tried the routes on this hill or if you are a beginner nature lover, you have definitely heard the name of this bölge and hill.
This route, which starts from the Balçova Thermal Hotel bölge, leads to Behzat Tepe and then connects to the thermal hotel again, is a route that you can add and experience as an alternative to your routes if you like nature walks. On this route, which also passes through the Monastery bölge, you can discover the magnificent view of the mountains and look at the city from the top. 
Although it varies according to your condition and your level of habituation to nature, the route is a difficult route. If nature walks are your indispensable part of your life, you should definitely set off for this route.

title: Finnskogleden along the border between Norway and Sweden
short_description: Finnskogleden goes through the lonely forests of the border region past swamps, lakes and rivers. The landscape is quite hilly and varied.
long_description:
The Finnskogleden is suitable for experienced hikers who have already gained experience with trekking tours lasting several days. The everyman's right gives you the opportunity to camp and rest at various places. Food must sometimes be taken with you, as shopping facilities are few and far between. Water can be taken from the various lakes and watercourses
.

title: Holiday Excursion in an Icy Ravine
Lake Zurich circular route: 2nd stage Adliswil - Horgen
short_description: The landscape around Lake Zurich is not only one of the most sought-after residential regions in the world, but also a hiking country that offers much pleasure and surprising contrasts.
long_description:
12,000 years ago, the Linth glacier shaped the basin of Lake Zürich into the landscape. The picturesque legacy of the ice was protected by the Römers, Alemanni and Habsburgs alike and has since become Switzerland's most privileged residential address.

The Zürichsee Trail shows the multifaceted region at its best. Along the way, there are historic towns and villages, castle parks and villa quarters, but also intact lakeside landscapes, extensive forests and wild ravines to discover. On its ten stages, the Zürichsee-Weg offers further enjoyment: several restaurants, from simple country pubs to gourmet restaurants, as well as first-class wineries are literally along the way. In addition, there are many sports and leisure facilities, museums, cinemas and B&Bs.

Thus, on the lake circuit, hiking purists, nature, culture and history lovers, gourmets and sports enthusiasts all get their money's worth in equal measure. The starting points of the hike can be freely chosen from the ten stage locations. For once, the destination is not specific places, but the path and its pearls.

2nd stage: Adliswil - Horgen

This hike is all about nature. It first leads along the Sihl, then through the Sihl forest and over the Seer lake to the Horgen path to Horgen. There are exciting insights into natural forests and great views of Lake Zurich.

title: Lay there louse
short_description: The trail leads through May meadows and high-montane fir-spruce forests and spruce forests to the subalpine forest level. Again and again there are views of the mountain range between the Vorderrheintal and the Glarnerland, of the Val Russein and the avalanche barriers of Sumvitg.
long_description:
For those interested in geology: We are in the Tavetsch Intermediate Massif. Not far to the south runs the Urseren-Garvera zone, a trapped remnant of the sedimentary packages that were shifted northwards and gave rise to the natural phenomenon of the Glarus main shift.

We take the post bus from Disentis to Perdomat. From there the trail leads first in a south-westerly, then in a south-westerly direction to the village of Cavardiras. The forest road leads through shady woods to Aclas da Cavardiras and the Caischavedra maypots. After passing through Dargun da Pardomat and Dargun da Falens, you soon reach the idyllic Lag da Laus. Like a pearl, this lovely lake lies embedded in meadows and woods and invites you to linger. A large woollen blanket, swimming trunks and towel, as well as enough provisions, should definitely be brought along for an extensive stay. Here you can switch off, forget the worries of everyday life and absorb the silence according to the motto: «Listen as you hear nothing» (Karl Valentin). The descent leads along the northern bank in an easterly direction, then north-west down to the hamlet of Laus. The last stretch from Laus is on a road to Falens and back to Pardomat Dadens.


.

images.caption: Columnar spruce at Lag da Laus

title: Lake Zurich circular route, Manegg - Adliswil
short_description: This first easy hike along the Sihl offers several spots for a picnic and a dip in the river. On arrival in Adliswil, the cable car takes you up to Felsenegg.
long_description:
The trail starts at Zurich-Manegg station and takes you directly to the Sihl, a river that flows at the foot of the Uetliberg before flowing into the Limmat in the center of Zurich. The path then continues in the shade of the trees at the foot of the Entlisberg forest, in a peaceful and refreshing atmosphere.
As you approach the small town of Adliswill, you will find picnic areas and benches that are perfect for resting for a moment with the sound of the Sihl lin the background.
The hiking trail then leads you directly to Adliswil trainstation. If you want to continue your excursion and head up high, an eight-minute walk will take you to the Adliswil cable car, which will take you up to Felsenegg. From there you have an impressive view of Lake Zurich and the surrounding area.
This hike is ideal in summer for a refreshing excursion near Zurich with family or friends.

title: Lake Zurich circular route: 4th stage - the royal stage
short_description: From the Richterswil Horn über the Etzel to the Pfäffiker Unterdorf: the King's Stage of the newly opened Zürichsee circular trail connects mountain and valley, agglomeration and rural province.
long_description:
The landscape around Lake Zürich is not only one of the most sought-after residential regions in the world, but also a hiking country that offers plenty of enjoyment and üsurprising contrasts. The Zürichsee circular trail with its ten stages shows the region from its different sides. It leads through historic towns and villages, castle parks and mansion quarters, but also through intact lakeside landscapes, extensive forests and wild ravines. The 124-kilometre SwitzerlandMobility route is well signposted (follow signpost number 84).

With an altitude difference of just under 800 metres and a length of 18 kilometres, the section between Richterswil and Pfäffikon deserves to be called the «Königsetappe». Before setting off, you can also take a dip. The lakeshore at Richterswiler Horn (a few steps from the station) offers ideal conditions for this. Then pack a towel and swimming trunks in your rucksack and tackle the climb to Schindellegi. There you say goodbye to the agglomeration of Zürich for a few hours. Because a few metres south of the tax havens on the left shore of the lake, another world begins: Central Switzerland with its cattle pastures, hills and moorlands (some of which are protected). The Alps behind complete the very photogenic landscape.
The best views are offered by the Etzel Kulm, at 1093 metres the culmination point of the hike. From here you can see the entire length of Lake Zurich. The descent is via St. Meinrad and Luegeten and finally you reach Pfäffiker Unterdorf. There you will find the most beautiful man-made shore area on Lake Zurich, which invites you to swim and enjoy.

title: Pedra Grande Trail
short_description: An trail in the midst of the Cantareira State Park where one can find one of the largest areas of native tropical forest in the world within the metropolitan region of Sãde;o Paulo.
long_description:
Arriving at the Parque da Cantareira, it is worth visiting the núcleo Pedra Grande. There begins the trail that leads to the Pedra Grande, a rocky formation with 1,010 m high. The Pedra Grande Trail is the main trail of the park and also the longest, with 9,6 km long.  It is all paved and with signs that indicate the direction to the viewpoint. Until é reach the viewpoint at the end of the trail, you &eecirc; will walk through native forest and pass through beautiful landscapes. After  several climbs along the way, you finally reach  the viewpoint, where é possible sight the Pico do Jaraguá, part of Guarulhos and, with great luck on clear days, even the Serra do Mar.
A little before reaching the viewpoint there is a fork where the trail turns to dirt and leads to the Carp Lake. This trail is 3km long, considering the round trip. At Lago das Carpas there is a children's playground, an area for snacks, including tables, and also has toilets.

title: Holsterberg - Nieheim
short_description: On this beautiful Nordic walking tour, we can let our gaze wander from the Nieheimer Warte and pass the beautiful little castle of Nordhausen.
long_description: This beautiful Nordic Walking tour takes us to the south-east of Nieheim. On the Holster Berg from the Nieheimer Warte lookout tower, also known as the Holsterturm. Holsterturm, we can look out over the surrounding area of the climatic health resort. The tour continues to the beautiful Nordhausen Castle. In the former ancestral home of the von der Borch family is now home to the GUTSKONTOR company. The castle can only be visited can only be visited from the outside.

title: The Steep Climb up to the World Heritage Site
short_description: The jagged border wall between Glarus and Graubünden has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 6 July. So it's high time to explore the spectacular landscape around the Tschingelhörner.
long_description:
The zigzag border wall between Glarus and Graubünden was made a UNESCO World Heritage Site on July 6 of this year. High time to get to know this spectacular region around the Tschingelhörner, and the Segna pass provides the best route for this purpose. On this direct route between Elm and Flims, you can admire the Tschingelhörner close up and from three sides. Shortly before 7.00 a.m. we alight from the post bus at the Elm Station stop and take the trail to Geren. There is located the valley terminus of the Tschingelen railway, the start of a trip covering 440 meters difference in altitude. If you wish to travel on this railway you should consult the timetable in the Internet or arrange for a special trip (+41 79 714 13 81). The journey is an adventure in itself, for you ride in an airy box across a deep ravine.
During the first four kilometers of our hike we are in the shadow the World Heritage and can note how the spot of sun created by the Martinsloch - a round hole in the cliff - moves rapidly toward the northeast. We come into sunshine after a bit more than two hours of walking and find ourselves in the Segnas pass. We sit on the terrace of the Mountain Lodge and enjoy coffee and pastry while admiring a magnificent panorama. Our trip down to the stony Las Palas high plateau traverses two snowfields and cliffs and is made easier with steel ropes and rungs set into the stone. From here we can see the Tschingelhörner and the Martinsloch from the sunny side.
As we have arrived sooner than expected, we won't go to the Cassonsgrat (Alternative A), where we would have caught the mountain railway to Flims, but rather hike along the «Camona da Segnas», as the path on the Romanic side of the pass is called. We picnic sitting on stones while viewing the Piz Bernina. Our goal of the post office in Flims (bus stop) takes more than two hours and traverses 1000 m difference in altitude.

Note(s)
You can stay at a couple of inns:
- The Segnespass Mountain Lodge, open every day from July 1 to August 10, on fair-weather weekends from mid-August to mid-October (www.segnespass.ch).
- The «Camona da Segnas», Flims

To arrive: Take the train to Schwanden and the post bus to Elm Station, Tschinglen railway (www.elm.ch, see «Bergbahnen»).
Return trip: post bus from Flims post office, train from Chur

title: From Wermsdorf to Lake Döllnitz
short_description: This hike takes us around Lake Döllnitz and through its idyllic villages.
long_description: Our hike starts at the Döllnitzsee dam in Wermsdorf at the inn "Zum Bahnhof". From here we walk along the shore of the lake to Reckwitz, where we cross the main dam of the lake and after crossing the main road we reach an eco-path. This leads us past the Schafteich to Mahlis, where we can stop at the "Laubental" restaurant. After the rest, we walk back to the lake and come across the main dam of the lake to its southern shore, from where we can make a detour to Liptitz via the Döllnitzseeweg. Back at the lake, we walk on to Göttwitz. Before we reach the village, however, we turn right onto the Liptitz road and come over the dam. We follow the path and after a small detour into the forest and another crossing of the dam we come back to Wermsdorf, the starting point of our tour.

title: Culture trail Appenzellerland
short_description: Hiking trail Kulturspur from Degersheim to Rheineck.
long_description: The hiking paradise of Appenzellerland, nestled between Lake Constance in the north and the all-surmounting Säntis in the south, offers you a new hiking and cultural highlight. Take up the trail and discover the most diverse facets of Appenzell culture. The 50-kilometre-long culture trail, marked in both directions, is a themed hiking trail. It leads through the lovely and typical hilly landscape of Appenzell, past 50 cultural objects.

title: Hiking route Hoge Kempen
short_description: This route is about 12 kilometres and takes 3 hours.
long_description: On this route, you will discover the north of the Hoge Kempen national park. The Hoge Kempen is the only nature reserve in Belgium to have national park status. The park consists of beautiful pine forests, drifting sands and heathland. You can go hiking and enjoy the peace and quiet.

images.caption: Viewpoint in the Hoge Kempen national park

title: From Bad Schwartau to Pariner Berg
short_description: This hike takes us from Bad Schwartau to Pariner Berg, where the Bismarck Column is enthroned. From there we can let our gaze wander over beautiful Holstein Switzerland and the wide Lübeck Bay.
long_description: Our hike begins at the car park opposite the Geertz senior citizens' residence in Bad Schwartau. Via steps, we pass the Wilhelmsquelle spring and enter the "Riesebusch" forest. We follow the forest path in the direction of Lange Hörn, where we come across a castle ruin that we can take a look at. On the left, we continue over a bridge towards Groß Parin. There we turn left, walk to Pariner Berg and climb up to the Bismarck Column. Parin Mountain is an ice-age terminal moraine of the Baltic Land Ridge and is 70.05 m high. It forms the northern boundary of the Lübeck Basin. The Bismarck Column was built in 1901/02 and from its almost 13 m high viewing platform one has a beautiful view over Lübeck and the Bay of Lübeck, Neustadt and Holstein Switzerland. After we have enjoyed the view over the beautiful landscape, we can stop at the restaurant "Pariner Berg". We walk back to Bad Schwartau via the "Dodenredder" path. Along the Horsdorfer Totenweg we come to the path "Am Küsterholz", at the end of which we turn left into Mozartstraße. Straight ahead we change to Kammansweg and cross it to reach Pariner Straße. A little later, we turn half left into Töpferberg and reach our starting point, the car park at the senior citizens' residence, via Eutiner Straße.

title: From Lauda on the Ramstal Panorama Trail
short_description: On this hike we experience the unique landscape in the south of the town of Lauda and enjoy wonderful views over large parts of the Tauber valley.
long_description: The car park at the mountain cemetery in Lauda is the starting point of our hike. On the asphalted Flürleinsweg we walk into the residential area of Ramstal, from where there is a beautiful view of the Oberlauda valley and the Altenberg vineyard, and cross it first on the Anne-Frank- and then on the Barbara-Brennfleck-Straße. The road turns into a grassy path on which we leave the village of Lauda. On the left on the slope is a baroque wayside shrine from around 1700, depicting the scene of the Mount of Olives. Our path leads upwards into the Ramstal-Hohlweg, at the end of which a bird sanctuary with a barbecue area invites you to take a rest. To the right of the wooden path, in the "Eisberg" biotope, protected plants and rare insects find a habitat between limestone banks, old vineyard walls and fruit trees. A few metres behind the barbecue hut, an asphalt path leads to the "Galgensteige", the highest point of our hike, where, flanked by chestnut trees, there is another wayside shrine. This one depicts Jesus carrying the cross. We turn left here onto a field path, which is also marked as the Main-Danube hiking trail. After an S-bend, we no longer follow the field path, but continue straight ahead on a grassy path leading downhill. Our route leaves the Main-Donau hiking trail a short time later and turns left into the forest path. On this path, we now walk briefly through the forest and always downhill towards Lauda. After leaving the forest, we have a beautiful view into the so-called Teilung Valley and of the "Galgenberg" natural monument to our left. Our view into the Middle Tauber Valley extends here from Königshofen with the Turmberg to the wine villages of Marbach, Gerlachsheim and Distelhausen. In the foreground we see the town scenery of Lauda. The panorama trail ends at an asphalted road, which we follow to the right until we reach the stairway of the mountain cemetery and thus return to our starting point at the car park. If the weather is good, you can take a refreshing swim in Lauda's open-air swimming pool.

title: Walk along the Wängibach
short_description: This short and easy hike begins in the Wängi valley. It offers one of the most beautiful and spectacular natural landscapes in the St. Gallen Linth region.
long_description: From the start of the hike along the Wängibach, you can admire the Speer, Europe's highest conglomerate mountain (1950 m). Its terraced bands of stone and meadows look like the tiers of a huge amphitheater. The Wängibach, which flows towards Rieden, impresses with its numerous waterfalls and pools. There are countless little corners along the banks that offer romance for adults and adventure for children: Make a fire, build dams and jump into the cool mountain water. For a picnic, follow the hiking trail 400 meters to the Speer, where small waterfalls, ponds, a large meadow and fire pits await you. The climb to Ober Bogmen, although steep, is well worth it: once at the top, an impressive view and the Bogmenalp mountain restaurant await hungry hikers.

images.caption: View of the summit of the Speer

title: Oberrot and its surroundings
short_description: On this short tour we experience the historical highlights of Oberrot's surroundings.
long_description:
The starting point of our hike is the sawmill museum in Oberrot-Badhaus. We walk up to the forester's lodge and go straight ahead through the forest at the first bend. Now we cross a meadow and reach the road towards Marhördt. Cross the road to the Marhördter Mühle mill and continue through the Marbachhalde to Marbächle. In Marbächle we turn left and follow the path down to Heidenbach. We follow the stream of the same name back to our starting point in Oberrot-Badhaus.
Oberrot is considered one of the oldest communities in the Limpurger Land. It is likely that it was first founded by the Franks as early as 650 AD. Worth seeing testimonies of Oberrot's long history are the old town and the moated castle surrounded by it.

title: From Auerbach to Rebesgrün
short_description: This short circular walk takes us from Auerbach to Rebesgrün and back again without any major climbs. Along the way we can enjoy some beautiful views.
long_description: Our hike starts at the upper railway station in Auerbach. From there we walk along the main road to Rebesgrün, where we turn right onto Rodewischer Straße. Behind the railway tracks, we take the next turn to the left and follow the path along fields. Then we walk into the forest, after a while we come across the "Verlängerte Steinbruchstraße" (extended quarry road) and continue straight ahead on this road. Shortly afterwards, the road bends to the right and continues to bend to the right. At the end of the "Verlängerte Steinbruchstraße", we turn left across a field and reach a railway line, which we follow to the right. At Obere Bahnhofstraße, we turn right and return to Auerbach and our starting point, the upper railway station.

title: Tour De Natur around Bad Salzschlirf
short_description: This hike takes us through the richly indented landscape in the west of Bad Salzschlief up to the hilltop, from where we can enjoy magnificent views.
long_description: The tour is marked with a red N on a white background and is easy to walk. It covers 12 km and takes in the spa gardens in the centre of Bad Salzschliff and the varied cultural landscape to the west of the town. We walk along the old border path between the district of Fulda and the Vogelsberg district and enjoy the magnificent view over Bad Salzschlirf to the Hohe Rhön from the hilltop with its sun observatory.

images.caption: We hike from Bad Salzschlirf to the Weiersberg.

title: Wildhorn tour
short_description: Five days between Valais and Bern, five days of spectacular views of the icy peaks of the Wildhorn, five days of pure nature.
long_description: The hiking days are very different and full of surprises: Paths carved into the rock face, steep ascents through scree, climbing up in the gravel, descending on four or five successive vertical ladders, many small mountain lakes, hiking among aconites and edelweiss, panoramic views of the glaciers of Plaine Morte, Diablerets, Mont-Blanc, Grand Combin and the peaks around the Val d'Hérens, crossing a labyrinth of white rocks, many waterfalls tumbling over the steep rock faces.

title: Walking Ebersberg
short_description: On this Nordic walking tour we can prove our endurance and also enjoy wonderful views.
long_description: We start our tour at Ebersberg station. From here we walk to Marienplatz and via Sieghart- and Semptstra;e and Richardisweg to Klostersee. There we turn left into the street „Am Priel“ and then walk to the right on Heldenallee (1) to the Museum Wald und Umwelt (2). Below the museum, follow the field path to the edge of the forest. At the fork in the road, keep left. Follow the red and white markings until you reach Villa Hubertus. Turn left here and after about 300 metres turn right through an avenue of apple trees. At the end, turn right again through an avenue of oak trees and then around Egglburger See (3) to Egglburger Kirche (4). Behind it we turn left and walk to the inn „Zur Gass“ (5). From here we walk the few metres to the left to the junction „Ebersberg über Weiherkette“. This takes us back to the station along the familiar path.

images.caption: Photo of the Forest and Environment Museum.
View of Egglburg Lake and Egglburg Church.

title: Von-der-Heydt Tour Wuppertal
short_description: This tour takes us past various legacies of the Wuppertal patron August von der Heydt.
long_description:
The stop "Am Arrenberg" is the starting point of our tour. From here we first walk along Viehhofstraße before walking up the hill ahead of us. We follow the signs to the cemetery of honour and can also make a short detour to the Von-der-Heydt tower, from where we can enjoy the view of Wuppertal-Elberfeld.
On the Erbschlöhweg we walk further south. The path takes us past the Von-der-Heydt summer house, where the builder of the observation tower we have just visited lived. August von der Heydt was a patron of the arts in the Wilhelminian period of the late 19th century, so that many artists and poets frequented the listed house; including Rainer Maria Rilke.
We follow the path further south and cross the state road. On the other side of the road, we pass the Burgholz Tunnel and come a little further to the Kaiser Oak, which was planted on 14 June 1871 by primans of the Elberfeld Grammar School in honour of the founding of the German Empire.
From here we continue for a short distance before we meet the path "Zur Kaisereiche", which we follow in the direction of Schwabhausen and Cronenberg, which we cross on Hütter Straße and the main street of the village. Via Schorferstraße we head out of Cronenberg again. We follow the path in the direction of Kohlfurth through fields and forest and thus reach the destination of our hike, the Kohlfurter Brücke, after some time. Here we have the opportunity to stop for a break at the Strandcafé or we can take a look at the origins of the tram in the Bergisches Land at the Bergische Straßenbahnmuseum, not far from the bridge.

images.caption: Historic shunting locomotive of the Bergische Museumsbahnen e. V. association.

title: Walking route around the Naardermeer
short_description: This route is 18.4 kilometres. During this route, you will walk around the Naardermeer.
long_description: The route starts at Naarden-Bussum station. From here, you walk a short distance through Bussum before discovering the beautiful nature around Naarden. You will walk around the Naardermeer lake and along the way you will encounter meadows, woods and fens. In short, a beautiful walk where you will encounter all kinds of things.

title: From Birx to Kaltenwestheim - Rhön
short_description: A short, fine tour through the Rhön Biosphere Reserve and over the highest village in the Rhön.
long_description:
A path branches off from the Birxer Straße halfway between Birx and Frankenheim. The end of this path is our starting point. First, the trail leads us to Frankenheim, the highest village in the Rhön. The 813 m high Ellenbogen allows wide views to the west. From Eisenacher Haus below the summit, we descend, first through forest, then across meadows and fields between the villages of Kaltenwestheim and Mittelsdorf.
From the heights above the Rhön town of Kaltennordheim, wide views open up into the Felda valley, which is dominated by the baroque Provost Church of the Assumption of Mary in Zella, among other things.

title: From Wittdün to Nebel - Amrum
short_description: On this hike we get to know the south of the island of Amrum.
long_description:
Our hike takes us to the village of Nebel, situated on the tidal flats. Today it is the largest village on the island and offers us Amrum's sights, such as the St. Clemens Church, the Öömrang Hüs, the windmill and the homeless cemetery.
In Süddorf, Amrum's oldest village, stands the distinctive Amrum lighthouse, which we can also visit during the summer months. From here we return to Wittdün, which was founded as a seaside resort in 1890 and is now the island's most important ferry port.

images.caption: A magnificent view of the sea.

title: On rollers through the Linth plain
Great pond circuit around Betzigau
short_description: The large pond loop leads without ascents most of the time along well-laid field paths and along enchanted streams.
long_description: Our starting point is the railway station in Betzigau. From there we turn left onto Gartenstraße and at the end immediately left again over the level crossing. A field path leads us to the left of the stream until we reach a fork in the road. Turn right here and continue along the field path over the small pond roundabout to the B12 main road. Behind a culvert, we continue westwards until we reach a stream. On the left side of the stream we walk in a northerly direction until we reach a bridge. Past the bridge, the trail continues in a northerly direction on a dirt road. Take the next opportunity to the right in the direction of Bogenried and Leiterberg. After the railway subway, continue south to Leiterberg. From there the trail leads back to Betzigau. The trail runs mainly on tarred roads and field paths. There are two inns in the centre of the village where we can stop for refreshments.

title: Around Wald - Land of 100 Waterfalls
short_description: Hiking in the land of 1000 waterfalls.

title: Zindlenspitz - a sheep in wolf's clothing
short_description: Beautiful tour with breathtaking panorama. The mountain is the namesake of the regional SAC section.
long_description:
«No chance to get up there», one thinks when one looks at the Zindlenspitz from the Wägital. For those with a good head for heights, however, this climb is not much more than a hard, but worthwhile walk.
The Zindlenspitz is like Jekyll and Hyde: from Rapperswil-Jona it appears to be a leaning hunchbacked cliff that at some point will drift into the Wägitalersee. Looked at from the Wägitalersee, it appears to be a stone needle resting on a broad base, and thus meant only for top climbers. From Glarus, on the other hand, one can see only steep meadows with a few cliffs.

Starting at the Wägitalersee, below the Blattenwald, one leaves the lake road and takes the hiking trail toward Aberli. After only a few minutes one is rewarded for rising early: the mirror-smooth lake now lies in the shade, while behind it Fluebrig and Aubrig are dazzling in the morning sun. Further attractions of this early stretch are knotty fir trees and very old sycamores.
Shortly before the Aberli, one branches off to the right in the Aberliboden direction. Here you can recuperate a bit before you start really going uphill. The stony and steep trail from the Aberliboden passes through the picturesque Bruchwald and finally through a rocky area. After ca. 1 3/4 hours one arrives at the first Zindlenalp. On Oberen Zindlen one can see into Glarus. At this point one has already mastered 900 of the total 1165 meters difference in altitude. The goal no longer seems threatening, for the trail passes through a steep pasture toward the peak. At the end are still three harmless crags, to be climbed on all fours. Far below lies the blue-green Wägitalersee, between Schiberg and Gross Aubrig one can see part of Lake Zurich, with Rapperswil-Jona and the Zurich Oberland in the background.
The first few meters of the descent lead one along the trail on which one has ascended, and then one turns left in the Rossalpelispitz direction. This trail is marked with the blue and white symbol that means there are a few especially steep passages ahead. They are outfitted with chains, however, and no problem for hikers with a good head for heights. If you wish, you can follow the ridge up to the Rossalpelistock peak. On the downhill journey one sees yet more sides of this mountain with many faces: craggy flanks and terraces and, from the Höhfläschen, an impressively large cliff.

Note(s)
How to get there: by car to Blattli, or by train to Siebnen and then postbus to Innerthal (plus 5 km).
Return trip: car from Blattli or postbus from Innerthal, train from Siebnen.

title: Walking route Loosdrecht lakes
short_description: During this walk you will discover the northern side of the Loosdrechtste plassen. You will walk over narrow paths with water on both sides.
long_description: The Loosdrecht lakes consist of several small lakes. You can take lovely walks and enjoy nature. Some lakes are busier than others. Some lakes are home to many birds, while others are mainly used for recreation.

title: From Reudnitz to Taura
short_description: On wonderful forest paths we hike under the green leafy canopy through the Saxon Burgenland near Reudnitz.
long_description: We hike in the Saxon Burgenland, but instead of old walls we enjoy wonderful nature experiences in the green, shady forest near Reudnitz.

images.caption: The soft forest paths around Reudnitz are great for hiking.

title: Jakobus-Weg Memmingen - Bad Grönenbach/Illerwinkel
short_description: A short stretch on the Way of St. James takes us to the south of Memmingen and on to Bad Grönenbach.
long_description: From Oettingen in the Ries, over the Danube and Augsburg, through the Allgäu to Nonnenhorn on Lake Constance, the St. James pilgrimage route in Bavarian Swabia, signposted with the sign of the scallop shell, leads. In 1987, the Council of Europe declared it the first European cultural route. For the region, it has been possible to find a route that follows the historical pilgrimage route. The Memmingen-Bad Grönenbach section invites you to take a detour across the Iller river.

images.caption: View of the fields around Kronburg Castle
The Nordic Fitness Park Bad Grönenbach offers a lot of information about walking on display boards.
The Goll organ from 1998 in St. Martin in Memmingen.
The view of the tower of St. Martin in Memmingen.

title: Tour de Schlatt- rustic pearl in the agglomeration
short_description: The festive walk starts in the middle of the Agglo at Kempraten railway station, below the Lenggis sleeping hut, which is now almost meadowless;
long_description:
Our holiday walk begins in the midst of the agglomeration at the Kempraten railway station, below the almost completely built up bedroom community of Lenggis. One immediately walks by a few examples of contemporary agglomeration architecture: first Thomas Schmidheiny's blue brick temple, then one-family houses with post-modern decor, carved wood decor in Black Forest style and unadorned blocks. A short climb 300 meters further on brings one to the Höcklistein vineyard, where grapes for ca. 70,000 bottles of wine are harvested every day, most of them Pinot Noir, RieslingxSylvaner and Räuschling varieties. The gravel trail wanders through the grapes toward Feldbach. Coming upon a large estate, one passes into Canton Zurich and arrives a few steps further at the Schlatt pond. Shortly before Feldbach, one must go north, past a farm and then on to the Schlattstrasse. A few meters further and one follows the Obere Chlausstrasse steeply uphill to the Schwösterrainstrasse. The walk along the hillside enables one to enjoy the view of the lake and the Alps. Then it is just a few steps downhill through the idyllic countryside to the Sageli-Felsenhof restaurant. One then has a choice of continuing over the Höcklistein back to the Kempraten railway station or wandering through Schlatt, thus sparing oneself an excursion to Ballenberg.

title: Wackersberg Round
short_description: The scenery is unbeatable: this tour takes us through gentle mountain forests, along the wild banks of the Isar and past picturesque Wackersberg.
long_description: From the car park we walk directly past the Cafe Forsthaus (1) and follow the well signposted Nordic Walking route 5, which is marked with a yellow arrow in a black circle. The tour leads us initially through the forest, partly also along the forest nature trail (2). We finally reach the Bohmerhof estate (3). There we walk down to the left in the direction of Bocksleiten. Here we cross the state road 2072 and follow the yellow arrow on the other side until we reach the Isar cycle path. On this path there is always the possibility to reach the nearby bank of the Isar (4) via small paths. At the first large crossroads we leave the Isar cycle path again. In Bibermühle we meet the state road again. We walk along it for a few metres before we climb up a steep forest path to the left. At the end of the path we turn left and walk on to Wackersberg (5) and back to our starting point.

images.caption: Achselköpfe and Brauneck and the Isar cycle path.

title: Yeni Foça - Kozbeyli
short_description: The route starts from Yeni Fo&ccedil'a and after a stop at Şaphane Fire Lookout Tower, it continues to Kozbeyli
long_description:
Foça böarea is a very charming böarea. In this bölge, the pleasure of having a walk against the magnificent sea view, shopping from the shopkeepers in the centre, and sipping coffee or tea against the sea is priceless. 
Fo&ccedil'a region offers routes in the blue waters for nature walks. There are paths and roads where green and blue meet and enjoyable görüntüs emerge. You can also catch the sea view from above with various routes that you can experience in the bölge.
Starting from New Foça, this route first stops at the tower. You have the opportunity to stop at the tower and rest for a while. Here again, you have the chance to take beautiful photographs. Then, when you follow the route, the route takes you to Kozbeyli. The route ends here.
You can also experience this route, which is one of the routes travelled by people in this böl;rüyüyüşçüs.

title: The hike along the ridge from Atzmännig to Steg
short_description: You have to cross ten mountains if you want to take one of the most beautiful routes in the foothills of the Alps. The highlights of the tour from Atzmännig to Steg are the Tweralpspitz, Chibarren and the highest mountain in Zurich, the Schnebelhorn.
long_description:
One must climb ten mountains when one hikes along one of the most beautiful routes in the pre-alpine region. The high points of the tour from Atzmännig to Steg are Tweralpspitz, Chümibarren and the highest Zurich mountain, the Schnebelhorn.

Corresponding to a tour including several mountains of 4000 m height in the Valais, we have the route from Atzmännig to Steg in the Töss valley. To be sure, they are at an altitude 3000 meters lower, and one does not need crampons or a rope. But the peaks called Schwammegg (1282 m), Rotstein (1285 m), Tweralpspitz (1332 m), Chrüzegg-Chümibarren (1314 m), Habrütispitz (1275 m), Rossegg (1254 m), Schindelberghöchi (1234 m), Schnebelhorn (1292 m), Hirzegg (1088 m) and Roten (1148 m) are also demanding. There are many drop-offs, and the commemorative crosses along the way remind one that fatal accidents are also possible here. The hike begins in Obere Atzmännig after a pleasant ride on the chairlift. Shortly after leaving the mountain terminus comes the first steep climb. Then one follows the ridge in the Rotstein direction. From there, one has a splendid view of the Toggenburg, Säntis and Churfirsten. One continues to the highest point on the route, the Tweralpspitz, and 20 minutes later one arrives at the Chrüzegg. The next descent passes through the mossy, dark fir forest to the Habrütispitz. From the Schindelberghöchi on one follows the border between St. Gallen and Zurich, and then comes the steep climb to the highest Zurich mountain. In the Restaurant Tierhag below the Schnebelhorn one can enjoy some well-earned nourishment, and then there are only two peaks more. An autumn hike in the beech woods around the Hirzegg and the Roten is delightful. From Roten it is only a short distance to the Hulftegg «motorcycle pass». Gravel paths and tarred roads bring one to Steg, where the train takes one back to the lowlands.

title: Winter hike to Alp Egg and toboggan run
short_description: At an altitude of 1200 meters, Alp Egg is a popular destination for sledgers in the Obersee region in winter, as it has good snow conditions.
long_description:
The night hike to the Alp Egg mountain restaurant is a classic in the Zurich-Obersee region. The ascent begins at the Ricken, Rittmarren stop. The lower part is often the most difficult because it thaws during the day and freezes again in the evening (watch out for black ice!).
After the Rittmarren clearing, you can soon see the light on the Alp Egg. The tiredness of the approximately one and a quarter hour ascent is quickly forgotten when you are only a few meters away from your destination and know that you will soon be rewarded with a good fondue or another Swiss speciality.
After the ascent on foot, the descent into the valley is quick but pleasant: it takes around 15 minutes to reach Rickenstrasse. Whether for nature lovers, families or adventure seekers - this winter hike above Gommiswald is ideal for young and old.

A varied walk through forests and along rock faces, this tour features unexpectedly beautiful views of the lake and the surrounding mountains. It is also exciting for children because it goes though an impressive and little-known canyon. This is a nice walk even if the weather isn't that great. Afterwards, the boat ride from Treib back to Beckenried is very relaxing.

title: Mouflon and giant stones around ravens
short_description: In a varied, fabulous landscape we discover mouflon, deer and roe deer.
long_description:
The Nature Park Centre is located in the middle of the village of Raben, the ideal starting point for our hike. We take the Mittelende road in a southerly direction, turn right a few metres at the fork in the road and then turn left into the Klepziger Weg. Lined by fields and meadows, we then enter dense pine and beech forests and follow the path straight ahead in the direction of the Zehrensdorf forestry district. At the next junction, keep to the right and after a few metres cross a clearing. Now we reach Zehrensdorf, a small settlement that is believed to have been abandoned due to a plague epidemic. We pass a walnut plantation and walk along the Zehrensdorf road towards the west through heathland and forest. Mouflon deer, a type of wild sheep with large horns, were released here in the 1980s, which we can observe if we are lucky.
We continue straight ahead until we follow a right-hand bend in a northerly direction. In the thicket we see the occasional erratic blocks typical of the Fläming, popularly known as giant stones. These date from the ice ages of over 100,000 years ago.
At the T-junction we turn right and continue our hike to the edge of the forest. There we turn right onto the field path and thus reach the starting point Raben again. Children can now let off steam here at the playground. For those who would like to learn more about the fauna and flora of this region, a visit to the nature park centre is recommended.

title: Medelserhütte
short_description: The Medelserhütte captivates with dynamic architecture and combines modern metal construction and the original stone part.
long_description:
From Disentis, take the post bus to Curaglia and hike from here. By car you can drive to Pardatsch in Val Plattas. Soon the Strässchen becomes an entertaining trail that leads to the hut (2524 m) in 3h 30min.

For the Rückweg to Curaglia there is another variant available in addition to the normal route. This is also marked in this route suggestion. For the time being, follow the Hüttenweg to Alp Sura. At the lower end of the valley floor of Alp Sura, keep to the left on the marked path. Climb up to the ridge of Grap Stagias and follow it downhill until you reach the road to Curaglia (3h 15min from the hut).

title: Trailrunning on the Multinskiye Lakes
short_description: Trailrunning is gaining momentum and the Altai Mountains are one of the right places for it. The route of Multinskie Lakes is very scenic and suitable for running on mountain trails with overnight stays at the lakes.
long_description:
This cascade of high-altitude lakes is remote from civilization, and lovers of outdoor activities will thoroughly enjoy their time here in the Altai Mountains. Multinskiye Lakes – is a chain of lakes echoing each other on the slope of the Katunsky Range. This place will transform all those who like active leisure.
  The Cascade family of Muntinska Lakes consists of the following names:
  Lower Multin Lake
Middle Multin Lake
Upper Multin Lake
Transverse lake
Early transverse lake
Glorious Girl's Lake
Firm Lake
The route also includes such lakes as Kuyguk, Akchan, Alla-Askyr, Kyrgyz and many others.
  The largest of the lakes is Nizhny Lake that is located at the height of 1700 m. For example, Lake Kuiguk is situated at the height of 2200 meters. The difference between them is 500 metres. What is not a cascade? Interested to see the cascade of wild lakes? Then come to Altai! And it does not matter what kind of activity you prefer, the assortment is vast: amateur hiking, mountaineering, horseback riding tours, bicycle rides, jeep rides and even cross-country trail runs.
The Maltese Lakes region – a symphonic paradise not only for sportsmen, nature lovers, but also for digital technology, which will leave a scenic memory for all to come.

title: Rifugio Saoseo
long_description:
The legend of the blue water and the reflected spirit
The water of Lagh da Saoseo is a brilliant light blue and a stone in the lake is reflected in it in the morning. Some say you then see the face of a ghost. A long time ago, the princess, who wanted to marry the prince with all her heart, finally saw it too. She threw blue flowers into the water, which is why the lake still has its colour. Only when she saw the ghostly face would she be allowed to marry him, said the prince. Maybe that still works today?

Access:
The Rifugio Saoseo, a converted farmhouse in the proud Puschlav style, can be reached directly by a call bus. Or with a nice hike on foot: you start in La Rösa (via Postbus from Ospizio Bernina), hike along a high-level path to Val di Campo and reach the small road to the Rifugio (See alternative A). To the right, a path leads along the stream, which is definitely worth taking. It leads through pine and larch forest, interspersed with alpine roses. After just under 2.5 hours you reach the Rifugio, near which lies the legendary lake.

Descent:
The hike back is via the Munt da San Franzesch. You climb 250 metres from 1985 metres to a plateau full of cotton grass. From "Aurafreida" you descend until you reach Pozzulasc after 3.5 hours. By post bus you get back to the station at Ospizio Bernina.

title: Up to the Alpe Gund
short_description: We enjoy a challenging mountain run up to Alpe Gund, but there are always flatter sections to take a breather.
long_description: On the ascent, we stick to forest paths and roads. Only the sections from the cemetery to the Hölzernen Chapel and from Almagmach to the Mittelbergalpe have steep to very steep inclines. On the way back down to the Steigbach valley, we use a wonderful hiking trail, which reminds inexperienced mountain hikers to be careful.

title: On the Höglandsleden from Nässjö to Mariannelund
short_description: Höglandsleden is a 450 km long long-distance hiking trail in the Swedish province of Småland. Following in the footsteps of the famous characters from Astrid Lindgren's children's books, one section leads from Nässjö via Eksjö to Mariannelund.
long_description: The six-day hiking tour takes us along Höglandsleden through the typical southern Swedish landscape with its numerous lakes, extensive forests, vast moors and heathland. The area west of Vimmerby is best known for the writer Astrid Lindgren, who was born there. Katthult Farm, where "Michel from Lönneberga" lived, Villa Kunterbunt, Bullarbü and Mattis Forest are all located here. Small campsites can be found at regular intervals along the trail, most of which are equipped with shelters, fresh water sources and firewood for campfires

title: Hike to Hochvogel - the spur mountain on the Austrian-German border, or the Matterhorn Algoja
short_description: Bavaria's Hochfogel (2,592m) stands out from its neighbouring peaks due to its pointed, irregular structure and attracts many climbers;
long_description:
The shortest route to Hochfogel from the Austrian village of Hinterhornbach.
The trip to the summit is 5 hours, back 3 hours. Perfect tour for the day off.
This is the perfect way to get to the top.
The trail to the summit passes through Fuchsensattel midway and already at the foot through Kalterwinkel (which means "cold corner" - and it's true, the sun hardly ever peeks through there, it creates a deep freeze in this place, silence, awkwardness)
.
The top of the mountain cracked in half in the last century. The crack is 60 metres deep, you can peek, the sight is sharp. The crack is growing in millimeters every month and the southern slope of the mountain is gradually crumbling down into the valley. One of the recently existing trails to Hochfogel has been closed because of the crumbling. So we detour through Fuchsensattel and Kalterwinkel. This route is slightly longer and colder, but much safer and possibly more exciting. The Cold Corner has to be seen and felt. It completely lives up to its name.
Although the mountain is cracking, the cross at the top of the safe side still symbolises complete safety on the mountain. The views, the vistas there, seem to gradually reveal themselves and silently speak to the eyes.

title: A hut on the move: Landi hut
short_description: Hike with a view to the Landi-Hütte
long_description:
In 1939, the SAC exhibited the fully equipped Leutschachhütte in Zürich at the national exhibition. Only afterwards was it dismantled stone by stone, beam by beam, transported and rebuilt in the Leutschach valley, where it still stands today.

Access:
To get to it, take the bus from Erstfeld to Intschi. From Intschi you can take the cable car to Arnisee at 1360 metres above sea level. From here it's hiking after all, an SAC hut is no hornusserhüttli. The beginning is made easy for you. At first the path leads almost level into the Leutschach valley. There, however, the path soon becomes steeper. From the deep blue Nidersee lake, you have to manage a final climb. The path leads you to the right to the Leutschach hut at 2208 metres über Meer.

After about 2 ½ hours you sit on the terrace, enjoy a cold drink or a hot chocolate and imagine not too vividly what it must have been like in the forties, when people carried stones in their backpacks instead of sandwiches to the top.

The Leutschachhütte is situated on a terrace with a great view. A few minutes down the mountain, the beautiful Obersee lake beckons.

Descent:
The normal descent takes 2 hours via the same path back to the Arnisee.
For sure-footed mountain hikers with good orientation, the longer variant (see variant A) is recommended. For details, please ask the hut warden.

title: Bonete Trail
short_description: Situated south of Ilhabela, the trail to Bonete Beach stretches along the coast of the island passing three beautiful waterfalls until you reach the paradisiacal Bonete Beach.
long_description:
Situated at the southern tip of Ilhabela, the Bonete Trail begins at the end of the asphalt road, in Borrifos. Visitors can follow a dirt road for another two kilometres until they reach the State Park gate, at the Sepituba Point. The landscape of the whole walk é ssima ssima e, besides being époss vel vel  observe  espeacute;cies of fauna and flora of the region &eatilde;O, there are small rivers where é poss´possível tomar banho em piscinas naturais de áágua crystallinas e observar ainda quedas d’áágua incrincrêndis.
The longest of all the trails in the Ilhabela State Park, the Bonete Trail is approximately 12 kilometres long just going. The trail takes from three to six hours, depending on the walking pace. As it is long, the visitors who take this path should leave early. Arriving at Bonete Beach, the return can be arranged with the boats of the "boneteiros", which take the visitor back to Borrifos.

title: Wildhorn tour: Geltenhütte - Wildhornhütte
short_description: This route from the Geltenhütte to the Wildhornhütte is a section of the popular Wildhorntour.
long_description: The Wildhorn tour is a very beautiful and scenic 4-day hike. You stay in SAC huts and mountain inns and hike between 8 and 17 km every day. The highlights are certainly the four lakes Lac des Audannes, Sanetschsee, Iffigsee and Lauenensee, which are all uniquely embedded in the magnificent mountain scenery. The tour can start at any of the four huts.

title: Picturesque Ohe Valley
short_description: A pleasure tour with only one small climb through the floodplain of the Mitternacher Ohe and with a view of the picturesquely situated Schönberg.
long_description: We walk past the information board in the direction of Kirchberg on Nordic Walking Trail 3 "Ohetal". On an ascending field path we reach Mitternach and the inn. The magnificent view accompanies us behind Schönberg to the turn-off at the Jägerstand. Follow the meadow path along the Ohe through an atmospheric valley to the bridge. Cross the bridge and head uphill through the spruce forest. Walking route "3" leads us to the hamlet of Panhof and down the road back to the Ohe. Directly after the bridge, we follow the course of the stream to a fireplace. We do not turn onto the forest path, but walk along the river to another forest path that takes us back to the car park on the left.

The hamlet of Panhof offers a magnificent view.
Every now and then you should linger and enjoy the atmosphere by the river.
A view of the climatic health resort Schönberg, the "Merano of the Bavarian Forest", is a constant delight.

long_description: The Holzgau suspension bridge is a rope suspension bridge that spans the Höhenbachtal gorge. It is the longest and most spectacular pedestrian suspension bridge in Austria.

title: From Bratwurst Country to the Linth Valley
short_description: The Tanzboden alpine inn is halfway between Toggenburg and the Linth region. It is therefore the ideal resting place on a hike from one valley to the other.
long_description:
The alpine restaurant Tanzboden lies halfway between the Toggenburg and the Linth valley. It is thus the ideal stopping point on a hike from one valley to the other.
You begin this hike at the Ebnat-Kappel railway station and wander upriver along the Thur riverbank for a few minutes. At Thurau you will cross a bridge and start upward, putting behind you the first of the 800 meters difference in altitude that separate you from the Tanzboden. More than half the dis-tance to Tanzboden traverses narrow, sometimes scarcely visible paths through blooming meadows. Of interest are the differences in vegetation as one climbs: in May the meadow grasses bloom up to an altitude of 850 meters, whereas at a height of between 850 and 1200 meters the grass is still re-covering from the long winter, and there are no blossoms to be seen. Further up, however, thousands of gentians and soldanels spring up between the brown winter grasses. Especially impressive is the Alp Ober-Abschlagen. The brutal name is quite in opposition to the charm of the place. On three sides the climb up to this alp is very steep, so it is the more surprising to find at the top a small, nearly flat pre-alpine paradise. From the northern part of this Alp you are rewarded with a magnificent view of the central Toggenburg. Ebnat-Kappel and Wattwil lie below you; to the east you see the Säntis and the Churfirsten. And now it is only a half hour from Ober-Abschlagen to the Tanzboden, the highest point of our trip. Finally, our hike continues over the Gubelspitz to Breitenau and Wielesch, where there is another alpine restaurant with a marvelous view. From the Wielesch, you'll climb steeply down into the Giegentobel and continue on to the Giegental. Finally, board the post bus in the village center of Gommiswald and ride to the Uznach railway station.

title: The Choice between Scree and Karst
short_description: Steep and technical hike with beautiful views of the Schwyz and Glarus Alps.
long_description:
From the Glattalp you have two choices of trails to Braunwald. The first is technically very difficult, because it takes you on a steep path across the large scree fields of the Furggele. The Bärentritt is also a challenge. This very steep trail snakes through rocks that appear from below to be impossible to climb. If you decide on this route you should have no fear of heights, be steady on your feet and very fit. The reward for your efforts are great views of the Schwyz and Glarus Alps. Fun also are the up to 500-meter long snowfields, on which you can slide, sitting on a plastic bag. From the Furggele (2395 meters) you can climb up to the Ortstock (2717) in 45 minutes, and have a view of more than 400 Alpine peaks.

If you are less interested in climbing challenges and like karst landscapes, start from the mountain terminus of the Glattalpbahn and hike to the north. A short climb will bring you to the Charetalp, where you'll be rewarded with spectacular views of karst fields around the Pfannenstock and the Bös Fulen. The Erigsmatt is your next goal, reached on very good paths without any ascents to speak of. Thereaf-ter, however, you will need firm footing on this route as well, for the rocky sections of the Nösseli and Bützi area hide crevices. Stop at the Gumen mountain restaurant, where you can sit on the terrace and fill your hungry stomach before you take the aerial tramway down to Braunwald.

title: Schönbielhütte
short_description: Hike with views of imposing glaciers to the Schönbielhütte.
long_description:
The Matterhorn surrounded by glaciers

If you want to see glaciers, you'll get your money's worth at the 2694-metre Schönbielhütte: just below the hut, the ice stream of the Zmutt glacier flows past. With a 15-minute walk, you can catch a glimpse of a hanging glacier rolling down from Dent Blanche. Close to the hut, Lake Howang with its turquoise water beckons you to splash around. If it's too cold, you'll be amazed at the frogs that jump into the cold water without hesitation.

Thanks to the mountain railways, the trail is also easy for smaller children who like to hike. The cable car takes you to the Schwarzsee, which is already at the foot of the Matterhorn. From here you hike about 400 metres downhill to cross the valley floor at Stafel. The trail continues on the opposite slope. Small lakes make the ascent entertaining, so that the 500 metres of ascent can almost be done on the side. The descent takes about 3.5 hours and first follows the ascent route, but then continues in Stafel straight along the sunny slope to Zermatt.

title: Alabama's Coastal Connection
short_description: Get a sense of the unique southern flair and enjoy Alabama’s stunning coastline on Coastal Connection
long_description:
The state of Alabama is best known as the “heart of Whisky and Dixie“, but there’s so much more to it. At its southern tip you can explore a spectacular coastline, marvellous wildlife preserves and taste the delicious local seafood. All this makes it especially attractive for outdoor enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.
The route leads you to the traditional fishing village of Bayou La Batre, two massive coast defense fortifications as well as two of the most picturesque landscape spots, Bellingrath Gardens and Gulf State Park.
On its nearly 110 miles, Alabama’s Coastal Connection offers you plenty of stopovers where you can have a break and take in the stunning scenery.

title: West Iceland
short_description: The first stage begins on the west coast of Iceland and stretches for almost 420 km to the fishing village of Hellissandur.
long_description: The route heads north from Iceland's largest airport in Keflavík and offers panoramic views of the Atlantic coast. About 180 km further north is Deildartunguhver, Iceland's largest and most abundant hot spring. Here the mighty forces of nature become clear: the rising water vapour is visible from afar. Only a few kilometres further inland we can marvel at the so-called Hraunfossar, a multitude of small waterfalls that pour into the riverbed of the Hvítá in an impressive play of colours. Towards the end of the day we pass the legendary Rauðfeldsgjá gorge, which still amazes its many visitors. The day's tour leads straight to the campsite of the tranquil fishing village of Hellissandur.
