title: Leglerhütte
short_description: On the alpine path to the Leglerhütte.

title: From the Niederurn Valley to the Linth Plain
short_description: The Hirzli is the northernmost mountain in Glarus. It offers great views and unique ridge walks.
long_description: The Hirzli is probably also the only place from which you can see the ends of Lake Zürich and Lake Walen, which are 65 kilometres apart (as the crow flies). The Hirzli is best reached from the Niederurner Valley, which can be reached by cable car from Niederurnen. The hiking trails in this region are uniquely beautiful. The Hirzli and Planggenstock mountains in particular offer almost everything that makes mountain hiking attractive. You change sides of the mountain several times, squeeze through rocky gaps, climb over boulders of Nagelfluh and admire gnarled fir trees that cling to the rocks with their roots like birds of prey. Despite all the exhilaration, however, you don't forget that a misstep can have dire consequences. Anyone who walks along this ridge path must be sure-footed and not afraid of heights. If you want to descend to Bilten, branch off to the north 200 metres west of the Planggenstock. From Büels, head towards Wasserboden, then steeply down through the Niderenwald forest to the Biltnerbach stream. The sound of the stream accompanies you through the damp and humid northern slope. Imitators should be warned of the slippery stones - and also of the many ghosts who, according to legend, inhabit this slope. If you want to hike the entire length of the beautiful Chämmli (west of the Planggenstock), take the path to Säden above the Muesalp. If you hike back to the Niederurn valley along this route, you will be rewarded by crossing the rustic river forest. There are large ferns, old firs and lots of moss to admire. If you are early and have good legs, you can continue to follow the ridge after the Chämmli and hike via Lauihöchi and Stockberg to Siebnen.

title: Glattalphütte SAC
short_description: From Schwyz on a varied hike to Glattalphütte SAC
long_description:
Access:
From Schwyz, first a large, then a very small post bus takes us to Sali, where we board an aerial cable car. So we arrive well rested at Glattalp, but there is no sign of a lake! So we set off on a hiking trail towards the east, where we finally discover our lake after a good quarter of an hour. To make sure we don't miss anything, we walk around it (time: 1.5h). We discover that it has an inflow, but no outflow. But don't worry, underground wells make sure that it doesn't overflow!

When we start to get hungry, we return almost to the starting point. Here, two huts invite you to rest: the Glattalphütte SAC and the Berggasthaus Glattalp.

Descent:
For the descent, we follow the path that takes us steeply but without difficulty via Mütschen down to Sali; 1 ½ h. Of course, we can also choose the cable car.

title: Tiefenbach corner
short_description: This hike with great views takes us from Bad Hindelang to Gailenberg and from there via the Bildstöckle to the summit of the Tiefenbacher Eck. There we are rewarded with a magnificent view of the surrounding mountain peaks before descending back down into the valley via the Baoleskopf.

title: Carschina Hut SAC
short_description: Hike from St.Antönien to the Carschinahütte SAC
long_description:
Access:
The post bus takes us from Küblis to St. Antönien Platz. A wide hiking trail climbs up to Alp Bärgli below the Chüenihorn. On its eastern side we traverse high above the valley, past the small Carschina lake, and after 2 hours we reach the Carschinafurgga. There the hospitable hut (2236 m) awaits us with a well-deserved drink (or a meal), which we have well earned.

Descent:
After this reinforcement we turn to the east and follow the path leading to Tilisunafurggli almost without any loss of height under the mighty walls of the Sulzfluh. After half an hour über alweiden und kleine Geröllhalden we come across the path coming from Partnun. We follow it, descending a little steeper, and soon arrive at the romantic Partnun Lake. Then the descent continues leisurely to Partnun (time required: 1 ½ hours). In another ¾ hours we can gain St. Antönien on foot. But we also have the possibility to order an alpine taxi at the Restaurant Alpenrösli (Tel. +41 (0)81 332 12 18) in Partnun.

title: Chamanna Lischana SAC
short_description: This hike requires stamina, but rewards you with fantastic views.

title: Chamanna da Grialetsch SAC
short_description: In the immediate vicinity of the hut, small lakes invite you to play and drink.
long_description:
Here, at about 2700 metres üater sea level, you can safely take a few steps on the mostly snow-covered glacier.

Ascent:
You can get to Dürrboden in the Dischma valley by bus or your car. On a good mountain path, past Lake Furgga, you reach the Fuorcla da Grialetsch, a wide-open pass, and a little later the Grialetschhütte (2542 metres über Meer), which is actually called Chamanna da Grialetsch. Romansh is spoken on the Engadine side of the pass. 1.75 hours are enough for this ascent.

Descent:
From the hut you can hike as a Rückweg üvia the Fuorcla Radönt to the Flüelapass. There the post bus will take you back to Davos. As an easy alternative, you can also walk back the same way you came. (Time required: 3h)

title: Through the Weißbach Valley
short_description: In the Wei;bachtal valley we come across mighty waterfalls, historic salt production sites, a glacier garden and a playground that is just made for little explorers. On the barefoot path you can test your senses and feel with your feet.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the Mauth car park. A field path leads to the edge of the forest, from where a path branches off to the left into the Wei&szligbachschlucht. This is only for walkers, but we still dare to take a short look into the narrow gorge. We go back and follow the forest path from which we turned off before. Along the Weißbach we now walk, mostly under shady Bäumen, to the village of the same name. Just before you meet the main road, turn left. After 200 m you come to a T-junction, turn left and cross the Wei&szligbach stream. Can you already see the playground? Now it's time for a bit of a romp before we move on to the next adventure station, a bar footpath. What can you find with your feet? We cross the stream again and walk to the left, very close to the bank. Can you spot the wooden figures at the side of the path? After another 700 m, we finally cross the Reiterweg and meet the Inzeller Stra&szlig. Along the country road you pass the small village of Nagling. Behind it, turn left and walk along a narrow footpath for a while. You pass the Trift Monument, which provides interesting information about the transport of wood on the water in earlier times. Large quantities of timber were once transported into the valley here. Can you hear the loud roar in the distance? These are the white water streams, which rush down a steep slope and impress us not only with their sight but also with their loud roar when the water level is high. When the water level is low, the brave can get really close to the waterfalls over the slippery rocks. Who wants to risk a little shower on a hot summer day?
We carefully cross the main road and on the other side we come across the remains of a historic brine pipeline, one of the oldest of its kind. Passing the pipeline, we hike uphill along the path and shortly afterwards encounter the Glacier Garden. Here the traces of the Saalach glacier, which dominated large parts of the region during the Ice Age, are still clearly visible. Particularly interesting are the traces of the so-called glacier mounds, a geological peculiarity. You can see cylindrical holes in the rock, sometimes up to 1 m in diameter, which were formed by swirling masses of water during glacial melting.
Now follow the signs to Weißbach to the right. On this path you will come across the remains of the old brine pipeline and finally the "Himmelsleiter" (ladder to heaven), whose 420 steps lead you back down into the valley. Back at the main road, we then hike back along the familiar path to Mauthäusl.

title: TransSemenic Road
short_description: The road between Slatina-Timiș and Reșița is more recently known as TransSemenic or the Banat Mountain Road. The route and the scenery can rank it among the most beautiful mountain roads in Romania.
long_description:
TransSemenicul passes through the foothills of the Semenic Mountains and through tourist spots such as Văliug or Gărâna. The asphalt is in decent condition, but riders may be surprised to find potholes, rutted or sandy sections along the route. The stretch between Slatina-Timiș and Brebu Nou is the best in this respect.
The moderate altitude of the road also makes it ideal for an endurance mountain bike ride. In the Prislop Pass you reach the maximum altitude (1000m). The landscape is one of deciduous forests that are beautifully coloured in the autumn months.
Probably the most spectacular area in terms of scenery is the one between Brebu Nou and Reșița, which passes at the foot of the Semenic Mountains. In addition to the domed peaks, the eye is delighted by the picture formed by the two reservoirs - Văliug (Gozna) and Trei Ape. Thus, the mountain trail can be combined with a swim or even a boat ride. The areas around the resorts offer possibilities for cycling routes.

title: East Iceland (Glacier Lagoons)
short_description: The southeast of Iceland is characterised by the vast Vatnajökull National Park. There are also two glacier lagoons, waterfalls and former lava fields to marvel at.
long_description: On the route through the southeast of the volcanic island we get to know Vatnajökull, Europe's second largest national park. Here we can marvel at the country's largest glacier and discover another legacy of the Ice Age: the fascinating glacier lagoons. One of them, the so-called Jökulsárlón, is even considered the deepest lake in Iceland and has served as a backdrop for several classic films. The sandy plateau of Skeiðarársandur makes it particularly clear that Iceland is also a land of contrasts. The wide expanses of sand contrast sharply with the island's fjord landscape. A real insider tip, on the other hand, is the idyllic Svartifoss waterfall, which can be reached via a short hiking trail.

title: Walking route Burgh-Haamstede - Westenschouwen
short_description: You walk from Burgh-Haamstede to Westenschouwen.
long_description: Of course, you also walk a large part through the dunes and along the sea. Couldn't be otherwise, of course, if you walk from Burgh-Haamstede to Westenschouwen. You will also walk a stretch through Zeeland's largest forest.

title: Cham - Muri
short_description: Varied hike from Cham - Muri

title: From Jungholz to the Gundalpe in Oberjoch
short_description: Hike with great views from Jungholz to Oberjoch/ Hindelang.
long_description: Enjoyable hike from Jungholz via Unterjoch to Oberjoch. There are many highlights in terms of nature and landscape. The tour always runs along signposted, developed and top modern hiking trails. On the way to the destination (Gundalpe) there are many opportunities to enjoy the view of the Allgäu landscape. There are also smaller rest stops (Vordere Sorgalpe) and small but nice towns and places to visit.

images.caption: On the way on snowshoes to Gendusas

title: Sedrun - Disentis
long_description:
After the railway station in Sedrun, you reach Bugnei on the level of the railway line in the direction of the indoor swimming pool and through various little-travelled neighbourhood streets. Now you are on the most beautiful section of the hike. On a sunny, wind-protected slope along the railway line, the path now leads to the picturesque village of Mompé Tujetsch. Here you have a beautiful view of Disentis with its impressive monastery.

After an easy descent, you reach Segnas, where you can make a short stop at the Ustria Crestas. Now you can decide whether you want to take the shorter route via Cuoz to Disentis or whether you want to extend the hike a little further via Peisel and Acletta (option A). After about 20 minutes, you will finally reach the railway station in Disentis, from where the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway will take you back to your starting point.

Note:
The valley hike is also well suited for families with smaller children who do not want to walk such long distances. Let your little ones ride along on a sledge: The gentle gradient makes it easy for you to pull the sledge and there is even a little downhill run every now and then.

Note(s)
The trail can be shortened as desired, see the MGB timetable, and can also be done well in the opposite direction.

title: GRP® Tour de l'Audomarois
short_description: The GR® de Pays Tour de l'Audomarois trail, located in the Caps et Marais d'Opale Regional Nature Park, is a 6-7 day walk starting from Saint-Omer.
long_description:
This itinerary is divided into several stages, crossing the Audomarois marshland, the only marshland in France to be both inhabited and cultivated, as well as various forests, notably the Tournehem forest.
The Tour de l'Audomarois hike, an approved GR de Pays, offers an opportunity to discover the region, and in particular the marsh of the same name, on a 123km loop. The route, which crosses the departments of Pas-de-Calais and Nord, immerses you in the beauty of the Caps et Marais d'Opale Regional Nature Park.
You can explore the former peat wetlands, which were transformed into market gardens in the 19th century. The modest dwellings of the cauliflower and chicory growers, along with the networks of canals used to drain the marshes, make for an exotic experience.
Walking through this natural region, walkers can also appreciate the biological diversity that unfolds along the way.

title: Teos Ancient City - Sığacık Teos Marina - Çamcaz Beach
short_description: We start from Teos Ancient City and walk to Sığacık Teos Marina, and from there we go to Çamcaz Beach, which is an example of the müthiş bays of Sığacık
long_description:
Routes that bring us together with nature and reveal the historical and cultural values of the region are always very valuable. If there is information that can be learnt on the route, if there are eye-catching intermediate points and if those routes bring us together with nature, greenery and blue at some point, you can enjoy it.
Starting from the Ancient City of Theos, this short route takes yürüyüy enthusiasts to one of Sığacık's beautiful deep blue bays, Çamcaz Beach. Of course, although the route itself is short, you need a little time for stops at intermediate points, visiting touristic spots, photographs. After the tour of the ancient city, we connect to Sığacık Teos Marina by travelling through a köy-like area where there are single settlements. After taking the air of Teos Marina and visiting the historical castle, we take a short, blue and green nature route to Çamcaz Beach.

title: Fenestrettes walk
short_description: A surprising walk in the Infernet cirque, then via the Fenestrettes: this astonishing path, built by the monks of Saint-Guilhem, corbelled above the void.
long_description:
In the heart of the Infernet cirque, a mineral setting with vertiginous cliffs, winds the caladé (paved) path of the Fenestrettes.
These masonry corbels were built in the 18th century to allow muleteers to pass through and gain access to the mounts of Saint-Guilhem-le-Désert and the Larzac causse.
Voted "Most beautiful path in the Hérault", it's the ideal complement to a visit to the village of Saint-Guilhem-le-Désert and offers breathtaking views.

title: Raven Run Nature Sanctuary Trail
short_description: Raven Run is a unique, 734-acre nature sanctuary dedicated to preserving the natural beauty of the Kentucky River Palisades and early Kentucky history
long_description: Over 10 miles of hiking trails provide access to streams, meadows and woodlands characteristic of the area.  Numerous 19th century remnants of early settlers, as well as over 600 species of plants, allow visitors to become acquainted with and appreciate the natural world.  Raven Run also accommodates over 200 species of birds throughout the year.

title: East Iceland
short_description: The tour goes from the interior to the east coast of Iceland and introduces some interesting sights, especially Egilsstaðir, the largest town in the area. The coastal region offers some secluded lookout points with panoramic views.
long_description: Over a total of 430 km, the fifth day's stage runs along the eastern coast of the volcanic island and first leads to Egilsstaðir, one of the country's largest cities and an important cultural and economic centre of Iceland. The stage then leads to the much quieter town of Seyðisfjörður on the idyllic fjord of the same name, before a short hike to the Hengifoss waterfall offers the opportunity for picturesque scenery. The Vatnajökull National Park also offers a splendid backdrop for souvenir photos. Some tips are available at the Snæfellsstofa Visitor Centre. The day's journey is rounded off with a stop at the coastal village of Teigarhorn, followed by a visit to the beach at Fauskasandur.

Untersee - Alteinsee - Alteiner Fürggli - Wiesen
short_description: From Arosa through the rugged nature of the Welschtobel, high up to the Alteiner Fürggli, out to Wiesen.
long_description:
The starting point for this beautiful mountain hike is the Unterseeplatz. Due to the orientation board and various signposts, this is a good starting point with detailed information.

The first short section leads us on the tarred road down to the sewage treatment plant. From there we follow the Welschtobelbach stream and cross it after about 1 km. The trail now begins relatively steeply, but evenly and leads through a beautiful mixed forest with leghorns, chestnuts, birches and gnarled stone pines. The high plateau «Uf Altein» lies at around 2,000 metres and invites you to take a first short rest before we cross the Alteinbach stream and continue to gain altitude until we reach the Alteinsee lake. We follow the narrow path, which is now relatively flat, walk across wonderful alpine meadows and finally climb another 250 metres to Alteiner Fürggli, the highest point of the hike.

We now have various options for descending the 1,100 metres of altitude to Wiesen. The most direct route leads via the Heinisch Alp and on to the Wiesener Alp to Wiesen. There are various places to stop for a well-deserved rest. The return journey to Arosa is by post bus via Lenzerheide to Chur, and then on to Arosa by Rhätische Bahn.

title: Prätschli Arosa - Ochsenalp - Tschiertschen

title: The Sass Rigais traverse (Geislerspitzen)
short_description: The traverse of the main peak of the Geislerspitzen, the Sass Rigais, is a demanding but extremely rewarding undertaking in the dreamlike scenery of the Dolomites combined with the adventure of a not too difficult via ferrata over a real three-thousand-metre peak.
long_description: The Sass Rigais is the main peak of the Geisler Group. It impressively separates the Villnößtal valley in the north from the Grödner valley in the south. The neighbouring peaks of the Puez Group, the Rasciesa and the Sassolungo are always impressively in view. The traverse of the three-thousand-metre peak - the Sass Rigais is, after all, an impressive 3025 m high - from the Wasserrinnental to the Mittagsscharte, i.e. from east to west, is an alpine undertaking, but the panorama during the entire tour is overwhelming. First the Sassolungo appears at our back, then the Geisler with Fermeda, Sass Rigais and Furchetta rise in front of us. To the right is the mighty Montischella. The panorama from the summit surpasses all previous impressions. The Marmolada and the mighty Sella massif are within reach. The view of the Villnöß valley to the north and the Raschötz is fantastic. The via ferrata is initially moderately difficult if you cross the Sass Rigais from the east (i.e. from the Wasserrinnental). A vertical and somewhat exposed passage awaits you right at the beginning, but it is well secured. Absolute surefootedness and a head for heights are a prerequisite for the entire undertaking. On both the east and west sides, there are some passages in easy climbing terrain (I, UIAA). There is also a risk of falling rocks in some places, so it is highly recommended to bring a helmet. Orientation is easy in good visibility, in poor visibility the ascent into the Wasserrinnental can be a bit more challenging to find. The Regensburger Hütte is an excellent place to stop and spend the night along the way. If you want, you can shorten the ascent with the Col Raiser cable car. It is a good idea to spend at least an entire weekend at the Regensburgerhütte. The touring possibilities are almost inexhaustible and worth the longest journey.

title: Easy climb to Florei refuge
short_description: Since its renovation, Florei refuge has become an increasingly "targeted" destination, especially since the route that climbs here is accessible to almost anyone. For a day out in the mountains with children, the refuge is the perfect destination.
long_description:
There are several trails that climb up from behind the Posada Hunting Museum, but only one is marked with a red band. This sign is an indication of a ridge route and yes, in reality, this easy route represents only a leg of the complete ridge route that crosses the Baiului Mountains.
And for the less trained, for children, or even for those who don't feel like covering a complicated route, but still want to feel a little taste of nature, the path that goes up to Florei offers enough.
In Poiana Florei, next to the refuge, there is a picnic area; on a clear day, you can hardly get enough of admiring the panoramas. You can confidently spend the night at the refuge if you feel like it.

title: The Skywalk via ferrata on the Hunerkogel (Dachstein)
short_description: The Skywalk via ferrata, which leads up to the mountain station on the Hunerkogel in the Dachstein region, is certainly one of the most daring via ferrata installations in the Eastern Alps. It leads almost in the fall line of the Sky Walk - a viewing platform next to the Hunerkogel mountain station - extremely exposed and spectacular directly up to the mountain station.
long_description: Opened in 2006 on the initiative of Karl Höflehner, the Skywalk via ferrata is certainly one of the most spectacular climbs in the Eastern Alps. Both for visitors to the Sky Walk platform next to the mountain station of the Dachstein glacier lift on the Hunerkogel and for the more extreme via ferrata climbers. Because anyone standing on the Sky Walk platform can see almost the entire upper part of the via ferrata through the window in the floor. The extremely exposed and difficult via ferrata leads upwards almost in the fall line of the Sky Walk platform. A total of 270 m of steel rope and about 60 step and grip bolts were used by the builders Prugger/Seebacher to create this bold via ferrata. The route itself runs along the south and south-east exposed wall of the Hunerkogel. Orientation is very easy, as for the greater part of the ascent you are literally tied to the path. The demands on strength and psyche are quite high, and there is no opportunity to take a break on the Skywalk via ferrata. It is therefore advisable to take a short webbing sling with a via ferrata carabiner with you to take some of the strain off your arms.

title: Berghäuser - Pass: Hahnenmoospass
short_description:
Diese leicht bis mittelschweren Wanderungen zeigen Ihnen die schönsten Wege und die gemütlichsten Berghäuser im ganzen Simmental. Lassen Sie den Alltag hinter sich und erleben Sie den Raum und die Zeit, die die Berge Ihnen bieten.
Translate to English
long_description:
These easy to moderately difficult hikes show you the most beautiful paths and the cosiest mountain houses in the entire Simmental. Leave your everyday life behind and experience the space and time that the mountains offer you.

Let yourself be spoiled by the hospitality in the mountain houses. Enjoy the food, mostly locally produced, the cheese from the nearby Alps or taste one of the homemade cakes.

One hike leads across the gentle meadows of the Lenk family mountain Betelberg, where you can discover the world of marmots in a playful way as well as admire the diversity of alpine flowers. Another path leads past the Lenkerseeli, the imposing Iffigfall to the idyllically situated Iffigenalp. Accompanied by the unique panorama of the Wildstrubel, Lenk's local mountain and pride, a trail leads from the Bühlberg to the Hahnenmoospass and Metschberg to Metschmad. In the picturesque Fermeltal valley near Matten at St. Stephan, a unique hike and a 4km-long scooter downhill fun trail await you. Other excursion destinations include the lovely Jaun Pass and the trail from cosy Oberwil to the Morgeten Alps, where old customs are still practised. The Stockhorn with its incomparable panorama of 200 Alpine peaks as well as the Jura, the Emmental and Lake Thun is another unforgettable experience.

Summarising the hikes and the mountain houses on the Simmental Mountain Houses Pass. Anyone who does not yet have the Berghäuser Pass in their rucksack should request it in advance from the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen or pick it up. The card can be presented to the staff for validation every time you eat in a mountain lodge or ride on a mountain railway. If you visit 7 of the 14 mountain lodges by the end of the summer season, you will receive an attractive gift at the Tourist Centres in Lenk, St. Stephan or Boltigen. With an additional ride on each of the three mountain railways, you will also be entered into the big prize draw at the end. The first prize is a Lenk mountain railway season pass.

1. Bühlberg mountain restaurant: The local bus will take you from Lenk to the Bühlberg mountain restaurant, where you can enjoy another meal with the Rytz family before the real fun begins. Please do not forget to validate your Berghäuser pass. In summer, you can watch cheese being made on the Bühlberg Alp.
2. Berghotel Hahnenmoos: After the first ascent, you can safely take a rest in the quietly located Berghotel Hahnenmoos. Valuing the Berghäuser pass is again the order of the day with the Spori family team.
3. Standhütte Metsch: The highest point of this hike has been reached, which is certainly a good reason to stop for a bite to eat.
4. Metsch: The Metsch cable car takes you back to the Lenk valley floor. The staff will again validate your Berghäuser Pass. From the valley station of the Metsch cable car, the local bus will take you back to Lenk village in 5 minutes.

title: Höhenweg-Steinwaldweg
short_description: We climb the highest mountain peaks of the Fichtelgebirge and see impressive rocky outcrops. Then we hike on the Steinwaldweg through the forest of the same name in the southern Fichtelgebirge.
long_description:
We start our hike in Schwarzenbach an der Saale and walk behind Hallerstein directly into the Fichtelgebirge. Over the Gro&szlig Waldstein we descend to Wei&szligstadt, which lies idyllically by the lake. The Rudolfstein is just the prelude to the Schneeberg, the highest peak in the Fichtelgebirge. But we will also hike the Nußhardt, the Hintere Messer, the Platte and the Hohe Matze on the Kammweg and enjoy the most magnificent views. On the way, we will experience the different types of rock - from granite and marble to slate and soapstone - as well as the large forest areas, which are partly interrupted by open plateaus. Near Wurmloh, at the Grosse Kösseine, the path changes its name to Steinwaldweg and leads north from Neusorg to the Steinwald. We cross the Kösseine, hike through Schurbach and past Pullenreuth. We continue through the forest to the Dreifaltigkeitskappe, the Wei&szligstein ruin and up to the Steinknock. We continue along the edge of the forest above the valley of the Wondreb, see Mitterteich and only need to cross Pleu&szlig to arrive at our destination in Waldsassen.

long_description: On this day trip we explore the north-east of the volcanic island of Iceland. We first circle the picturesque lake Mývatn, stop at an impressive viewpoint and then visit a cave that leads to an underground lake. Another insider tip is the Námaskarðpass, a sea of steaming vents and craters that make an impressive sight. The Krafla geothermal power plant, located on volcanic ground, is similarly impressive. The tour is rounded off with a visit to the Dettifoss waterfall and the spectacular Ásbyrgi gorge.

title: Westfalenwanderweg
short_description: The Westphalia Hiking Trail, managed by the Sauerland Mountain Association, takes us from the Ruhr region over the ridges of the Adrey and Haar strands, to the valleys of the Möhne and Alme, and into the Egge Mountains on the southern edge of the Münsterland Bay. We hike along hilly paths and trails that allow us to steadily gain altitude.
long_description:
We start our hike in Hattingen and cross the Ruhr near Witten, which we follow to Lake Harkort and Lake Hengstey. Now we continue to orientate ourselves along the course of the Ruhr to leave the Ruhr area in an easterly direction. However, we do not walk directly along its banks. Rather, between Dortmund and Schwerte, we head towards Lichtendorf and then south of Unna towards the northern outskirts of Wickede. At Günne we meet the Möhne and cross the Möhne dam on the dam wall. Except for a short detour to the Bismarck Tower (near Möhnesee), we walk steadily close to the shore and cross the dam again at Stockum. This takes us to the northern edge of the Arnsberg Forest and we follow the Möhne via Völlinghausen, Allagen and Belecke to Rüthen, with its well-preserved historic town centre. Now we take a north-easterly route to cross Büren and then enter a dense forest area to reach Wewelsburg. Again we go through a forest and then in the valley of the Altenau to Henglarn and Atteln. On a high path we come to Ebbinghausen and, surrounded by narrow strips of forest, via Grundsteinheim to Iggenhausen. In Herbram, the Egge Mountains tower up before us. We boldly step into it and hike in a northerly direction over the Ochsenberg, the Hausheide and the Dübelsnacken to Altenbeken, the finishing point of our beautiful and eventful hiking tour.

title: Piatra Craiului Mountains with kids: Casa Folea - Joaca Pass
short_description: Casa Folea (Folea Mountain Lodge) is an important landmark for those who want to try hiking towards the southern ridge of the Piatra Craiului Mountains or towards the traditional mountain villages at the foot of the mountain, above Bran. A hike up to Joaca Pass (Șaua Joaca) with the kids makes up for an excellent introduction to the secrets of this wonderful mountain.
long_description:
The ascent is mostly on a forest road wide enough to accommodate even two bicycles. It advances smoothly, past a few households, past more or less shabby fences, then through the forest. Closer to the pass, you come out into a generous clearing, where you can see the traces of some sheepfolds.
The effort seems easier with the beautiful natural scenery around you. In addition, ahead on the path, the ridge of Piatra Craiului begins to unfold. As you keep getting closer to the pass, the image of the ridge keeps widening. Only in the end you get to see the mountain in all its splendor. Of course, the mountain ridge is not visible in foggy or gloomy weather.
The route can be covered with children even in winter, with the right equipment and a little more care.

title: On the European Long Distance Trail E3 through Luxembourg
short_description: On the Luxembourg stage of the European Long Distance Trail E3, you hike from Perl/Schengen via Remichen, Grevenmacher, Echternach, Vianden, Clervaux and Wiltz to Esch-sur-Sûre and along the Sûre to Martelange on the Belgian border.
long_description:
The European Long Distance Trail E3 runs for several thousand kilometres from the Black Sea through Central and Western Europe to the Iberian Peninsula. Not all parts of the trail have already been completed and marked. The route is planned to start in Turkey and run through Bulgaria, Serbia, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia, Poland, the Czech Republic, Germany, Luxembourg, Belgium, France and Spain to Portugal.
This section starts at the border crossing from Germany to Luxembourg, more precisely in Schengen.
This section starts at the border crossing from Germany to Luxembourg, more precisely in Schengen. From there, you hike the first few days mainly on little-travelled asphalt roads and through shady forests. Highlights of this section are, on the one hand, the picturesque vineyards that stretch out on both sides of the Moselle and the Wolfsschlucht (Wolf Gorge) between Echternach and Berdorf.

short_description: You should add Sorgun Göleti and its stage to your list of places to visit in Ankara
long_description:
Sorgun Göleti is one of the most important values of tourism in Ankara with its densely forested forest area and natural landscape. Sorgun Nature Park and Sorgun Göleti, which are under protection in Ankara's Güdül province, have a very favourable area and nature for activities such as sports and recreation. 
While agriculture, animal husbandry and industry are important sources of income in the region, nature tourism has gained importance in recent years with the investments made in the region.
This approximately 7 km, two-hour hike route in the nature-inspired gölet phase is an ideal route to get away from the city life for a while. This area, which is rich in flora and fauna and home to many species, becomes an indispensable location for many people and photographers. 
Sorgun Göleti Nature Park also offers visitors many special opportunities such as picnics, camping and accommodation in bungalow structures.

title: Haldertobel
short_description: A special and hidden hiking route that includes a lake with mesmerizing hues, lots of flowing water, waterfalls and magical views that together make the hiking experience in the place one of the most magical in the upper Allgäu region
long_description:
A hiking trail hidden in a forest with idyllic landscapes and nature where you can find a lake with a gorgeous turquoise hue, a flowing stream that has shades of light blue-turquoise-green, waterfalls, whirlpools, rich vegetation, bridges and other surprises in nature. A great itinerary for those who love water and nature. One of the most beautiful and special routes in the region. Due to the fact that the route is less known, it is naturally less touristy, which makes walking it less busy and more relaxed.
The walking paths are often covered with stones as well as protruding tree roots and therefore you must pay attention to the road conditions when walking along the route, most of the walking is on the plain but occasionally includes uphill climbs which are mostly negligible. In addition to this and considering that the walk on the route is steep and occasionally includes several steps and climbing on small rocks, it is not accessible to wheelchairs or strollers.
The route is linear (one-way) but it is possible at any point to turn around and retrace the steps, but it is recommended to complete the route and only then come back as there are points of interest worth seeing all along it. You can start the route from both sides, if you are traveling with more than one vehicle, you can leave a collection vehicle on one side of the route, but walking the round trip route is recommended as it extends your stay in this wonderful place and gives a different and interesting angle on this lovely route.

title: Netzbachtalweg at the gates of Saarbrücken
short_description: The primeval forest outside the city gates - that probably only exists in the Steinbachtal/Netzbachtal nature reserve. Here, nature is allowed to do or not do what it wants and we can observe it doing so.
long_description:
This hike takes us through the "primeval forest at the gates of the city". The Steinbachtal/Netzbachtal area has been under nature conservation since 1997 and during this time has been transformed into the "green heart" of the Saar coal forest. In order to allow flora and fauna to develop undisturbed, economic use of the raw material wood is avoided there.
At the very beginning of the hike we pass the Jungfleischhütte, which originally belonged to the former hunting lodge "Philippsborn". After crossing the historic Wolfgarten, the idyllic Waldbach awaits us, along the banks of which we hike past the former Netzbach shaft. Shortly before the Netzbach flows into the Fischbach, we come to two still waters, the Rosenweiher and the Netzbachweiher. In the upper of the two, the Rosenweiher, conservationists have settled a beaver family. The Netzbachweiher is a popular place for excursions, especially in summer.
Through shady forest paths, we finally reach the starting point again, passing the Forsthaus Wolfsgarten.

images.caption: View over the Appenzell hilly landscape

title: Through Rhineland and Westphalia - Velbert
short_description: Our hike takes us across the Deilbach, which forms the border between the Rhineland and Westphalia.
long_description: The starting point of our hike is the old town of Langenberg. From there we walk south into Donnerstraße, which we follow for a short distance. We turn left into a park, which we cross towards Hordtstraße and now follow this past tennis courts into Panner Straße. Shortly after the sports field of the grammar school, we turn left at a swimming pool and now walk along the main path and Hüserstraße towards Rommel. Shortly before reaching the village, we see the Langenberg transmission mast on the left, which we pass along the edge of the forest and now walk in the direction of Hordtberg. At the end of the fields we turn left into the forest and soon reach the Bismarck Tower, from which we have an excellent view of the Rhineland and Westphalia, both separated by the Deilbach. At the Bismarck Tower we also have the opportunity to fortify ourselves in the associated restaurant. Via the cliff we return to the old town of Langenberg, the starting point of our hike.

title: Winerwanderung rund um Immenstadt
short_description:
Von Blaichach übers Bärenköpfle nach Immenstadt
Translate to English

title: "La Vélobuissonnière®" (V44) : Alençon – Le Mans – Saumur
short_description: A journey on the V44 in the heart of France through regions as rich as they are peaceful. Between history, rivers, medieval villages and gastronomy, this cycle route offers a calm and charming journey.
long_description:
5 arguments to get you started on this route :
250 km of cycling on quiet roads and greenways,
Villages with authentic charm,
A rich architectural heritage and varied landscapes,
The crossing of Alençon, Le Mans, La Flèche and Saumur,
The possible connection with 4 other cycle routes: the Véloscénie (Paris / Mont-Saint-Michel), in the north; the Loir Valley at La Flèche, La Loire à Vélo and the Vélo Francette, in the south.

title: From Anse Laborde to Porte d'Enfer
short_description: Through the hiking trails of the Loop, discover the richness of the North Grande-Terre territory!
long_description:
Starting from the beach of Anse Laborde, this second stage follows the Trace des Pecirc;cheurs northwards to the Pointe de la Grande Vigie.
From the Pointe de la Grande Vigie, go back down to the RD122 road, then at the road junction take the direction of Porte d'Enfer, the arrival point of this trail. <From the Pointe de la Grande Vigie, go back down to RD122 road, then at crossroads take direction of Porte d'Enfer, arrival point this second stage.

title: Chamanna Coaz
long_description:
This tour leads far into the Val Roseg, over the snow-covered Laj da Vadret up to the Chamanna Coaz. It is beautiful and long, but can be shortened at any time by taking a horse-drawn carriage ride. The interesting valley landscape of Val Roseg with its moraines and the view from Chamanna Coaz are impressive.

Note(s)
The horse-drawn carriage runs regularly from Pontresina to the Hotel Restaurant in Val Roseg.

title: Seebergsee
short_description: Lake Seebergsee is located in the Spillergerten nature reserve between the Simmen and Diemtigtal valleys.
long_description: You can reach it from Zweisimmen by first hiking to Oberried and then following the hiking trail to Hinder Chumi. The trail continues uphill to the Gubi hut before descending comfortably to the lake. After a final ascent to the double summit Stand, a steep zigzag path leads down to Schwenden.

title: Espírito Santo mountain trail
short_description: With a steep ascent that requires a little more effort, the Serra do Espírito Santo trail rewards visitors with a stunning view from the top.
long_description: Being one of the most incredible and beautiful trails of Jalapatilde;o, the Trail of Serra do Espírito Santo has an initial climb difficult, but in a short time é possible reach the top of the mountain and see the immensity of the region on top of the chapadão.The best time to climb the Serra do Espiacute;rito Santo is in the early morning to watch the sunrise. The journey begins in the early hours of the morning, when the night makes the climb less painful. <The initial climb is the most difficult part, as it has a steep wall that requires some physical effort from visitors. During path, there are several benches serve support to take breath of air and continue path. At end climb, you will be at main viewpoint Espiacute Santo Mountain, where can watch sunrise. From this viewpoint, another 3km walk until reach second observation point, see Jalapatildeo Dunes.

title: Chindbetti Pass
short_description: Scenically, this is a very beautiful tour, but you have to be prepared for a lot of noise.
long_description: The experience already begins on the ride up to Engstligenalp, which offers an impressive view of the waterfall and the rock. Now the route goes steeply along the Ärtelegrat with a view to the left of the Lohner and to the right of the Wildstrubel. Past the Schedelsgrätli, you skirt the bizarre peaks of the Tschingellochtighorn on scree. Following the Entschligegrat, you reach the Chindbetti Pass. From now on, the trail zigzags stonily at first, then later across meadows and partly damp ground back to Engstligenalp.

title: Giferspitz
short_description: The hiking destination, the Giferspitz, sits enthroned above the glittering world of Gstaad and the alpine meadows in the Turbachtal.
long_description: The hiking destination, the Giferspitz, towers unceremoniously above the glittering world of Gstaad and the alpine meadows in the Turbachtal valley. You start off in the direction of Alp Berzgumm, from there initially on a meadow ridge, later up the increasingly steep and rocky ridge to the summit. The view is magnificent. Continue past the Louwenehore, initially quite steep, then almost flat to the large Turnelssattel. The last part of the trail leads along the valley of the Turnelsbach, past Bachberg back to Turbach.

title: Along the Mare aux Vacoas Reservoir
short_description: The short tour leads along the Mare aux Vacoas reservoir to a forest adventure trail.
long_description: The Mare aux Vacoas reservoir, with a surface area of 2.5 km, is the largest drinking water reservoir on the island. In the forest you should definitely observe the Bäume, because here you can observe monkeys with a little luck. There is also a small resting place here where a few special plants grow, but unfortunately the tour was over for us at this point, as three young wild boars were blocking the way and we were not sure whether the mother might be nearby. Therefore we turned around and hiked back the same way. On the way back we continued to watch the trees and were rewarded. Several monkeys jumped through the trees, but unfortunately they were mostly too quick for the camera (or for me);

title: Giessbach Falls
short_description: On this tour, for once, the water plays the main role and not the mountains.
long_description:
Lake Brienz and the Giessbach, which cascades down an approximately 400m-high escarpment, are the focus.
The path immediately starts very steeply up in a zigzag, past the Grandhotel to the 14 cascades of the Giessbachfälle. The spectacle is particularly impressive when the snow melts.
Further on past the Schweibenalp, the trail descends through the forest to Hagweid. As soon as the forest clears, you have a clear view of the lake and the Brienzergrat. The trail continues along the lakeshore to the destination of Iseltwald, from where you can return by boat to the starting point.

images.caption: View of the fishing village of Iseltwald from Lake Brienz.

title: Hostalde Suspension Bridge
short_description:
Die Wanderung führt bergauf zu "Uf der Egge" und dann steil hinab nach Rohrbach, bevor man entlang des Flusses über einen wackligen Steg und zwei Hängebrücken die beeindruckende Hängebrücke Hostalde erreicht.
Translate to English
long_description: The destination of this hike is the impressive Hostalde suspension bridge. It is 153 metres long and 38 metres high. But before you can take a look at the structure, which was inaugurated in 2006, you have to climb a few metres. From the country road, the route goes uphill towards Zälg and finally through the Sackgraben to the highest point of the tour "Uf der Egge". After crossing 3 more ditches, the trail leads quite steeply down to Rohrbach. From here you hike gently along the river, cross a rickety footbridge and two shorter suspension bridges, towards your destination.

title: Tschentenalp
short_description:
Easy hike from Tschenten mountain station via Choleren gorge to Adelboden
.
long_description:
The first metres of ascent on this hike are comfortably covered by the mountain railway. From 1940 m.ü.m. the easy and beautiful trail leads downhill über Mösere through the Tschentetal valley to Ausser Schwand. The highlight of the tour is the visit to the Choleren Gorge, which offers a magnificent natural spectacle. The wild waters of the Tschentebach stream pour deep into the rocky gorge.
At the exit of the gorge, the Jungbrunnen invites you to take a short bath in the refreshing waters of the mountain stream.

title: Misterioasa pădure Hoia Baciu, versiunea non-horror
short_description:
Poate că pădurea Hoia Baciu de lângă Cluj nu e tocmai locul pe care cineva ți l-ar recomanda pentru o sesiune de forest bathing. Și totuși, uneori pădurea nu are nicio vină, iar legendele urbane sunt...doar legende.
Translate to English
long_description:
Dacă te încumeți să faci o plimbare mai lungă prin pădurea Hoia Baciu, vei descoperi un peisaj tipic unei păduri de foioase, cu multe specii de arbori, cărări mai înguste sau mai late, acoperite de covoare de frunze toamna, puncte de belevedere, sau poienițe. La capătul traseului se află Cheile Baciului, sub forma unor pereți argiloși, și Tăul Baciului, un mic lac.
Într-adevăr, pădurea are și arbori cu trunchiuri ciudate, care te pot duce cu gândul la diverse forme. Pe fondul legendelor urbane despre aparițiile sau fenomenele din Hoia Baciu, aceste triunchiuri pot căpăta conotații înfricoșătoare. La fel și în cazul unei atmosfere cețoase.
Turismul horror, care exploatează aceste legende urbane, și punctele în care se găsesc copacii atipici, stîrnește un mare interes, alimentat și de puterea autosugestiei.
Însă, în mod normal, pădurea Hoia Baciu și acest traseu sunt doar prilej de o plimbare relaxantă.
Translate to English

images.caption: Panoramă spre Cluj de la Hoia Baciu

title: Albristhorn
short_description:
Albristhorn-Wanderung: Von Sillerenbühl zu atemberaubenden Gipfeln und malerischen Alphütten
Translate to English
long_description:
From Adelboden - Oey (mineral spring) take the Silleren cable car to Sillerenbühl. From the mountain station, after a short descent, the ascent to the Laveygrat begins. Via Tierberg - Seewlehore - Sattligrat you reach the Albristhorn after about 3 to 3 1/2 hours. The descent is via Furggeli - Furggi (alpine hut) to "Im Hore". From here it is only a short distance to Aebi.

Note(s)
In early summer there can still be a lot of snow on the north side of the Seewlehore and the Sattligrat.
In autumn watch out for icing in this area.

title: Wandelroute natuur naast Nunspeet
short_description:
Deze prachtige route is 18,4 kilometer en duurt ongeveer 4,5 uur. 
Translate to English
long_description:
Tijdens deze wandelroute wandel je over de prachtige Veluwe. De Veluwe is het grootste natuurgebied van Nederland. Het gebied bestaat uit uitgestrekte bossen, heide, zandvlaktes en vennetjes. 
Je vindt er prachtige planten en dieren. Er is voor iedereen wat te doen op de Veluwe. 
Translate to English

title: Gypsy Refuge in early autumn
short_description: A classic ascent of the Bucegi, relatively popular due to the accessibility from Bran, with some challenges especially regarding the presence of wild animals. The route continues on to the Omu peak.
long_description:
If you're tempted by the route, expect a continuous, sometimes sustained, climb to your destination - in this case, the refuge. More than half of the route is in the forest. Many of those who have walked the route have reported wild animal tracks or noises...
On the way out of the forest & into the alpine hollow, there are two viewpoints, with a rather limited view. Afterwards, the views open up one and all.

title: From Bad Bibra to Steinburg
short_description: This easier tour takes us past mills and springs through Burgenland.
long_description:
We start our tour at the "Haus des Gastes" in Bab Bibra. Past the vicarage, we walk on the Domberg under the railway bridge in the direction of Steinbach. Behind the school, we turn left onto a path, which we follow straight ahead over a bridge to Steinbach. We walk along the village street through the village until we turn right at the last house towards Gutschbachtal. The path leads us along the stream to the "Kirstenmühle".
From here we continue through the forest to the "Gutschgrundmühle". After a few metres, we turn right in the direction of Borgau. We cross the picturesque village and, after some ups and downs, arrive at the castle park in Steinburg. Steinburg Castle, which once belonged to the von Münchhausen family, is well worth a visit. The path now leads us further along a spring and an old castle mill to Wallroda. We turn left here into the village street, which we follow through the village. We take the path in the direction of Bad Bibra until we turn left again at the village road, follow the road and thus return to the starting point.

title: Nordic Walking near Kempten
short_description: A walking tour in the west of Kempten awaits us. We experience a hilly landscape with idyllic farms and hamlets.
long_description: We start our Nordic walking tour at the car park at Kalbsangstobel. From the information board, we walk uphill along the road, turn right at the forest onto the footpath and then immediately left onto the path that runs along the deeply cut stream valley, the so-called Kalbsangstobel. Once on the mountain ridge, we continue to the right on the tarred road - past a lookout bench (1) in the direction of Prestlings (2). Behind the sidewalks, continue straight on until you reach Elmatried. There we walk half-right past the resting bench under a lime tree (3) and stay on the road down to Heiligkreuz. We pass the church (4) and an inn in Heiligkreuz and return to the car park via Tannach and Unterschmieden.

images.caption: The Church of the Holy Cross
A blaze of colour in cottage gardens.
A bench with a beautiful view.

title: Adventure Bus: Summit Climbing and Bathing Fun
short_description: On this crisp day hike, we are rewarded for the steep ascent to Gerenstein (Immenstädter Horn) with a refreshing swim in the Alpsee.
long_description:
Start point of the tour: Immenstadt train station
.
Arrival times for pilot ride 1 of the adventure bus Immenstadt train station: 08:35 am & 10:50 am
End point of the tour: Immenstadt train station
.
Departure times for pilot ride 1 of the adventure bus Immenstadt Bahnhof: 13:21 & 16:08
  Note: This tour was developed for the pilot test within the project "Flexible Adventure Bus for Sustainable Leisure Transport (FEB-NAFV)". It is therefore tailored to the timetable and stops of the adventure bus, which is currently not yet öffentlich verkehrenden. If you are interested in participating in a future pilot project in general, please contact us via research@outdooractive.com.

title: Training Round Allgäu SwimRun
short_description: The short training course for the Allgäu SwimRun is a circuit that can be run as often as desired. With a one-kilometre swim and five-kilometre run, the course is also suitable for beginners.
long_description: The training loop starts at the large car park for hikers on the southern shore of the Niedersonthofener See lake. After a leisurely flat roll-in on the path running alongside the road, the few positive metres of the loop follow. At the highest point of the route we follow the signs to the right towards the lake. From here we leave the asphalt roads and take a wide gravel road to the next small hamlet, where we turn right towards the campsite. However, we go around this on the left in the direction of the boat rental or bathing area. This is where the first swim starts to the bathing area of Niedersonthofener See, further to the south, on the other side of the lake. Back on land, follow the wide hiking trail for about 1.5 km along the shore to start the second swim at a "wild" entrance. The crossing of the lake to the bathing area on the opposite side is the longer of the two swims at about 700 metres. Back on land, you can start the second lap directly or walk back towards the car park.

title: Nordic Walking in the felt near Bad Aibling
short_description: A short Nordic walking tour through a moorland area. Shiny black pools and protected plants like the orchid line our path.
long_description: The tour begins at the Harthausen outdoor pool car park (1), which we leave to the right. We turn directly right again onto an asphalt path that leads us along the fence of the swimming pool. From now on, the tour is well signposted. In addition, boards provide information on the technique of Nordic walking (2). We pass a wayside cross (3), the asphalt pole track (4) and, towards the end, a refreshment stop (5). Most of the path leads through the groves of the moor with their numerous protected plants. The Harthauser Filze are a remnant of the so-called Inn-Chiemsee glacier. At first it left behind huge lakes, but these were gradually filled in by rivers. Bogs such as the Harthauser Filze then developed on the clayey, waterlogged layers.

images.caption: Evening mood over the country road on which we walk from Lohholz back towards the swimming pool.
Horsetails are a common plant species in moorland areas.
The trail initially leads through fields and pastures before branching off into the felt.
From the air, the boggy flat plains around Bad Aibling are particularly recognisable.
The granite artwork in front of the clinics is entitled "Monuments of Unbroken Hope".
Behind the felts, the first houses of Lohholz begin.

title: Tittling circular hiking trail
short_description: This circular hiking trail takes us through numerous small villages and hamlets and opens up impressive views of the surroundings around Tittling time and again.
long_description: We start our hike at the car park in Theodor-Heuss-Straße in Tittling. From here we walk past the Dreiburgenhalle up the hill. At the height of the church we come to the main road. Turn right into this street and a little later turn right again into Färbergasse. From here we follow the red and white marker "10" on the street "Insel" to Maseringer Straße. Here we keep to the left and after a few metres we reach Passauer Straße. Cross the road and turn right on the other side along the footpath into the district of Preming. There we turn left into Pretzer Straße. Shortly afterwards, we turn right and walk up to the Preminger Höhe. From here we can enjoy the view: from Tittling over the Englburg to Fürstenstein. Then we walk down from the Preminger Höhe via Wildenberg to Pretz. At the fork in the road there, we make a short detour to the left to the small chapel of St. Kolomann. From there we go back to the fork in the road and continue straight on towards Neukirchen vorm Wald. We finally reach the St. Kolomann church. Turn left at the church, then immediately right again and cross the Dettenbach stream. Cross the Haseläcker to the next crossroads and turn left. After a few metres we reach the village of Hof. There we stay on the main road and finally reach Farnham. Behind it we come to a through road, cross it and continue straight ahead on the other side along the road in the direction of Enzersdorf and Witzmannsberg. Shortly afterwards, however, we leave the road again and turn right into the forest. We continue to follow the red and white markings and thus arrive at the Maria Bründl pilgrimage chapel, which is also popularly called the Bründl chapel because a wooden well house with a spring inside stood next to it. In 1976, the wooden house was replaced by a stone one as part of the land consolidation, in which a spring still bubbles. From the chapel, we reach Witzmannsberg in just a few steps. Shortly after entering the village, we come across the through road again and turn left into it. Behind the "Zum Bründl" inn, we turn right into Grafenring and then immediately left again into Weiherweg. Leave Witzmannsberg on this road and walk down to Niederham. About 250 m after leaving the village, we turn right and finally reach Anschiessing. Here we keep to the left and reach the through road again at the Tittlingen district of Siebenhasen. Cross the road and continue on the other side on the footpath to the right - via Muggenthaler and Carossastraße to Hafnergasse. Finally, we hike up opposite to the Blümersberg - one of the most beautiful vantage points in the Lower Bavarian Forest. Until 2001, the mountain had a height of 571 metres. By building a long-distance water reservoir on the hill, it was "raised" again by almost five metres. From the Blümersberg we continue on the gravel path to the asphalted road, where we turn left. At Herrenstraße we keep left again. Always straight ahead, we finally get back to the church at the market place of Tittling via Dreiburgenstraße. The Theodor-Heuss-Straße leads us from here back to our starting point.

images.caption: View from the Blümersberg to the Englburg near Fürstenstein.
View from the Blümersberg to the Englburg near Fürstenstein.
The view of Tittling from the Blümersberg.
The St. Kolomann Chapel in Pretz.
The view from the Preminger Höhe to Fürstenstein.

title: From Berching to Eglasmühle
short_description: Along the Main-Danube Canal we experience Berching and its surroundings.
long_description: The Main-Danube Canal is the pivotal point of our tour. It had already been Charlemagne's intention to create a connection between the Main and the Danube, but it still took more than 1000 years until the first profitable canal was to be built between the two rivers. We hike along the Main-Danube Canal from Berching to Plankstetten, where we stop at the monastery tavern and enjoy a drink. where we can stop at the monastery tavern and visit the monastery church. Afterwards we return to Berching.

images.caption: The Main-Danube Canal is a wonderful place to hike.

title: On the tracks of Ötzi to the Similaun Hut
short_description: A high alpine tour that takes us through the Ötztal Alps. With an altitude difference of over 1,300 m, the mountain tour is not for beginners.
long_description: The Similaun Hut, which is the destination of our mountain tour towards Ferner, forms the transition between North and South Tyrol. For many mountaineers, it forms the "base camp" for the high tour of the Similaun. Ötzi - the Iceman - was also found very close to the hut. The ascent from Vernagt is the shortest and is one of the most beautiful hut hikes in South Tyrol.

title: Through the Anlauter Valley - Kinding
short_description: This romantic hike takes us to many chapels and the ruins of old castles.
long_description: On our hike we come to the Rumburg ruins. The high to late medieval fortress is located on a mountain above Enkering, a district of Kinding. There are many other sights along the way. Chapels, castles and ruins as well as the old towns of Enkering and Erlingshofen enhance the tour through the Altmühltal Nature Park.

images.caption: We hike through the Anlauter valley.

title: Crossing the Serra Negra
short_description: As part of the Transmantiqueira Trail, the classic Travessia da Serra Negra is the second stretch of the Itatiaia National Park Sector, and boasts incredible attractions.
long_description: This is the second section of the Itatiaia National Park Sector, and in this section, the Transmantiqueira Trail uses the layout of the classic Travessia da Serra Negra, starting at Posto Marcão. The trail continues in the direction of the Rebouças Shelter and then continues towards the base of the Pedra do Altar (2,665 m), which invites you to visit its summit, from where there is a 360 degree view. Then the trail crosses the Aiuruoca Valley from where you can see the Ovos da Galinha, the Pedra do Sino and the Cachoeira do Aiuruoca (40 m drop) which, being located at 2,450 metres, is considered the highest waterfall in Brazil. The trail continues towards Invernada and follows the Aiuruoca river until Serra Negra, a rural district of Itamonte (MG), where the overnight stay will take place. The second day begins with the tiring but scenic climb up Cavado Hill, and then slowly descends towards the village of Maromba, Resende (RJ), where it is possible to cool off in the waterfalls of the region.

Cachoeira do Escorrega, Visconde de Mauá, Itatiaia
Morro do Couto no Parque Nacional do Itatiaia, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil
Cachoeira das Flores no Parque Nacional do Itatiaia, Rio de Janeiro - Brasil

title: From Obersinn to the Dittenbrunner Höhe
short_description: This circular walk takes us on a comfortable forest path parallel to the Sinn to the Dittenbrunn farms and the view on the Dittenbrunn Heights.
long_description: From the car park, we follow the signposted cycle path north towards Bad Brückenau. The road takes us past the sports field until the cycle path turns right into a gravel path. Up and down we walk through beautiful high mixed forest and always parallel above the river until a bend brings us down into the Sinntal (1). We catch sight of the impressive railway viaduct (2), cross under it and turn left and walk parallel to the road. Soon we cross the Sinn again and reach a crossroads at the Dittenbrunner Höfe. The first path to the right, marked with the chess flower, leads under the ICE railway line. We walk steadily uphill until we reach the Dittenbrunner Höhe (3). Now we return to Obersinn on asphalt paths with a detour to the country inn (4).

images.caption: The view sweeps down to Burgsinn and Mittelsinn.
And again and again we encounter the most diverse plants and flowers.
On the Dittenbrunner Höhe, the horizon opens up for us.

title: Running from Krasnaya Polyana to Rosa Khutor via Estosadok
short_description: A light jog through the resort villages from Krasnaya Polyana via Estosadok to Rosa Khutor will complete your holiday in the Krasnodar region.
long_description: During a run, you can remember all the places you've been to and recall them in your mind. Holidays in places like Krasnaya Polyana are not to be forgotten. And if it was also passed with an active activity such as running, the holiday can be considered to have been completed in full. You may start a run at will from any village of Krasnaya Polyana and run in the direction your eyes take you. In this case we set off in the direction of Nadezhda waterfall, not far from the famous health trail. Good luck to all of you in your sporting endeavours and have a great weather on the way.

title: Leutkirch Walking Tour
short_description: On this Nordic walking tour we explore the south of Leutkirch.
long_description: This Nordic walking circuit is made for walkers who also enjoy endurance walking. Our route is signposted throughout with the red "9". From the car park we reach Herlazhofen via the footpath and cycle path. We follow the village road past the village square with playground (1) to the end of the village, where we follow the signs and turn into Spitzenrainweg (2). After 800m we follow the cross road to the left, after another 800m a path leads us to the right towards the forest. Through the forest, past Blindele See (3), we follow the signs to the main road. Walk 500m on the pavement to the left, past the hamlet of "Ewigkeit" (4) before crossing the road and returning to Leutkirch on the side road with little traffic. Here we walk first to the right and then to the left and straight on across the crossroads back to the car park.

images.caption: The view from the Spitzenrainweg is magnificent.
It is no longer "eternity" until we reach our goal!
The village square in Herlazhofen invites you to take a break.
This view of Leutkirch is offered from the Spitzenrainweg.

title: Hiking on the heights of Sorèze
short_description: A very nice hiking loop to do in the heart of the forest massif of the Haut-Languedoc Regional Natural Park in the Tarn. Beautiful views of the surrounding area await you!
long_description: This route will take you to the Oppidum de Berniquaut and then to the Mont Capel where the Orival stream flows, which you will find at the end of the walk, once you have returned to the village of Sorèze. The crossing of the Plateau de Causse will also be part of the discovery of the area.

title: Adventure bus: On the Stuiben
short_description: A challenging mountain hike (day tour) to one of the highest peaks in the Nagelfluh range with a stop at the Alpe Gund. For experienced hikers only!

title: Hike from Malente around the Dieksee lake
short_description: This hike takes us around the beautifully situated Dieksee in Holstein Switzerland. The "five-lake trip" by boat is recommended.
long_description: Our hike begins on the Diekseepromenade (1) in Malente. From there, we first head towards the Holm forest area and arrive at an open-air Kneipp facility on the lakeshore. The so-called mirror ponds (2) are the remains of a fish hatchery that Grand Duke Peter of Oldenburg had built around 1870 to breed noble fish. Here we can cool our feet before setting off for Niederkleveez. The landing stage for the "Fünf-Seen-Fahrt" (3) is in Niederkleveez. Via Gut Trollholm we walk on a narrow headland to Timmdorf. We cross the railway tracks in the village and then turn right. Straight ahead we pass the holiday farm Radlandsichten (4), where we can stop at the farm café or buy regional specialities and even Baden wine in the farm's own shop. It is also possible to visit the high ropes course from Easter to October on Saturdays and Sundays by appointment. After an extensive rest, we hike on and turn right to Neversfelde. A new lookout tower is soon to be built behind the village on the Holzberg. Via the Malenter Wildgehege (5) we return to our starting point, the Diekseepromenade.

title: Hiking to Maiden's Spit - a chic waterfall in Elbrus
short_description: The 30-metre long «Scythe of the Cherkessen Girl» spreads out from a mountain cliff forming a circus water show. The waterfall in Prielbrusiya «Maiden Spits» fascinates not only men.
long_description:
The waterfall itself rather resembles untangled hair than plaits. However, it translates from Karachaevo-Balkarian as «Maiden Braids». The waterfall is situated at an altitude of 2,800 metres and originates from the Gara-Byshi glacier. Mountainous water of the waterfall is purest and considered healing, though being near falling water is noisy. Noise of "spits" adds to the spectacular view and terrific atmosphere of the area. There are also views of snow-white peaks and alpine meadows for which the nature of the Caucasus is so famous.
Whoever has been to the area around the waterfall may recall episodes from the film Vertikal, starring Vladimir Vysotsky.

images.caption: Maiden Spits at the foot of Mount Elbrus. Kabardino-Balkaria
Devichiy kosy waterfall. Devichiy kosy waterfall. July 2007.

title: Viewing terrace on the sunny side
long_description: This tour is a great high-altitude trail that offers imposing panoramic views and leads past original Maiensäss settlements again and again. The tour can be shortened at any time, for example to Schmitten, Alvaneu or Brienz.

title: Motta Palousa viewpoint
long_description: The highlight of this hike is the breathtaking viewpoint Motta Palousa, which you climb from Cunter. The descent is via Alp Ozur and Aclas to Surava.

title: Hike into the Engadine
long_description:
The tour starts in Preda and leads to Lai da Palpuogna, supposedly the most beautiful spot in Switzerland. (Swiss TV audience 2007) From here you reach the Crap Alv Laiets, carved into the granite by the glacier, and on to the highest point of the tour Fuorcla Crap Alv. From here the trail leads downhill via Spinas to Bever.

title: Around the highest mountain on Usedom
short_description: The Golm forms the highest point on Usedom and is also a war gravesite that we can visit on our hike.
long_description: From the car park, we walk out of the village and reach a paved path that leads us to the left. We walk through rough pastures and discover information boards on flora and fauna along the way. Our route follows the "green triangle on a white background" marking. After a wooded section, we come across an abandoned cemetery at the edge of the path and soon see the first houses of Kamminke. At the edge of the village, the path leads us to the left. But we should make a detour to the harbour (1). From Kamminke you have a wonderful distant view of Swinemünde Forest, which is already in Poland, and the Szczecin Lagoon. Our tour now continues in a northerly direction. We pass a restored windmill and descend along a sunken path to the road. Follow this to the inn "Zum Kellerberg" (2) with its beer garden. Opposite the inn, the path then leads to the Golm memorial. More than 20,000 victims of the bombing raid on Swinoujscie in March 1945 are buried on the slopes. There is a viewing platform at the highest point of the site (3). Here we can look out over today's Swinoujscie (Swinemünde) in Poland. From this point, a small, steep path leads us down, which turns into a wider path and brings us to the main road. There is little traffic on this road and we reach a turn-off to the left into the forest on the right-hand side of the path. At the first junction, we turn right and reach a signpost to Garz. Now choose the short path and you reach a bench with a beautiful view at the edge of the forest (4). We follow the "green dot on a white background" marking, reach the road to Garz, follow it on the footpath and thus return to the car park.

images.caption: In Kamminke there are many well-preserved fishermen's houses with the typical reed roofs.
We discover a lovingly restored windmill along the way.
A beautiful path takes us from the memorial's vantage point back down the Golm.
From the harbour in Kamminke we can overlook the entire Szczecin Lagoon.
More than 20,000 victims of the bombing of Swinoujscie in March 1945 are buried on the hills of the Golm gravesite.

title: High altitude hike Val Tuors
short_description: This high-altitude hike leads into Val Tuors.
long_description:
You hike among stone pines and larches along the tree line. The chairlift takes you from Bergün up to Darlux and then on foot uphill to Alp Darlux. The trail runs steadily up and down to the highest point at Lena Secha. From here it goes downhill past Alp digl Chants to Chants.

title: Julier Hospiz - Fuorcla d`Agnel - Val Bever- Bever
short_description: Hike through the Val d`Agnel up to the highest point of the Fuorcla d`Agnel and on to the Chamanna Jenatsch.

title: From Dietfurt onto the Kreuzbergweg
short_description: This hike takes us from Dietfurt through the forest to beautiful vantage points from where we can enjoy a wonderful view of the Altmühl valley.
long_description: Starting from Dietfurt's market square, we begin our hike and turn right into the Kellergasse. Via Bergstraße we leave the town area and continue our way in the forest. After a while we reach the "Herzogstand" lookout point, from which we can overlook the Altmühl valley and Dietfurt. Our path leads us for a longer time through the forest, over the plateau and through the villages of Stetterhof and Hebersdorf to Oberbürg. From there we hike down into the valley of the Weiße Laber and arrive at Unterbürg. The river shows us the way for a while in the direction of Dietfurt. Then we continue along the "Ochsensteig" to the heights around Hainsberg with the Oldenburg ruins and across the plateau along the edge of the forest to Kreuzberg. At the cross we have a beautiful view of Dietfurt. Downhill we walk past the Mariengrotte back to the town. Finally, we can make a detour to the Franciscan monastery before we reach our starting point again, the market square.

title: Danube Cycle Route to Passau
short_description: On this varied cycle tour from Vilshofen to Passau, our path always runs along the Danube.
long_description: We start our bike tour in Krankenhausstraße at Vilshofen station. From here we now set off in an easterly direction. We follow the white-green signpost "Tour de Baroque - Donauradweg". We cycle past the hospital, cross the railway tracks and the Wolfach river and finally leave Vilshofen. Via Witzling we reach Hausbach and finally Hattenham. Soon we reach the Sandbacher Straße. We turn left into it - again following the white-green signs. A short time later we arrive in Sandbach. From here on, our cycle tour follows very unconventional paths for a short time: We turn left into the Förgengassl and cycle through it down to the ferry bridge on the Danube (1). There we ring the bell to call the ferryman. He then takes us across the water to the other side of the river. Here we cycle to the right along the Via Danubia (2) - an old Roman road. It runs the entire length from Bad Gögging via Regensburg, Straubing and Deggendorf to Passau. At the timber mill near Besensandberg, we cross the Stettinger Bach stream and shortly afterwards also the Deichselbergbach stream. We finally come across the through road and continue cycling on the cycle path to the right along the Donauleite. Soon we turn off the road again and now cycle to Gaishofen. There we pass the small chapel and then cycle on to Irring. From here our tour leads along the Danube again, on quiet paths under the huge motorway bridge (3). Shortly afterwards we reach the through road again. We continue, over the Gaißa and past Zieglstadl to the end of the cycle path. There we turn left towards Wörth and at the same time follow the white-green signpost "Donauradweg" again. Shortly after crossing the Wörther Bach stream, a cycle path and footpath begins again, on which we continue to Ranklhofweg. At this point we reach the other side of the road through a subway. There we continue cycling in the direction of Passau until we reach the Kachlet hydroelectric power station (4). On the bridge directly at the weir we now cross the Danube a second time. On the other side we turn left and after a few metres we reach the city of Passau (5). From the entrance to the town, however, we still have to cover a few kilometres to our destination, the main railway station: We first pass under the railway bridge and continue over the Hammerbach (6). At the asphalted road, we keep to the right and cross the thoroughfare at the traffic lights. On the other side we then continue on the cycle path in the direction of Passau. Behind the goods station, we turn right into Bahnhofstraße. After a few metres we reach our destination. From the main station we now have the opportunity to explore the city extensively - and there is always something worth seeing. After all, the three-river city lies at the confluence of the Danube, Inn and Ilz rivers. It is also a border town with Austria and a university and festival city. The Italian baroque cathedral houses the largest cathedral organ in the world. Also worth seeing are the Veste Oberhaus, the Salvator Church, the Niedernburg Monastery and numerous museums. In the Roman Museum, for example, the late antique wall remains of the former Boiotro fort are preserved. We also have the opportunity to take a short boat trip on the Danube from the nearby landing stage before finally returning to Vilshofen by train from Passau.
