title: Entry of the Wiesn Festival Hosts
short_description: The Munich Wiesn is officially opened every year with the procession of the festival hosts. Watching is an experience!
long_description: In 1887, the now traditional procession of the Wiesnwirte took place for the first time. Colourful and splendidly decorated horse-drawn carriages of breweries, innkeepers, bartenders and waitresses are accompanied on their procession by the music bands of the festival tents and arrive at the festival grounds of the Munich forms the official start of the Oktoberfest around noon. As soon as the festival hosts have arrived on the Theresienwiese, the Lord Mayor of Munich taps the first beer barrel in the Schottenhamel festival tent at 12 sharp. Together with the exclamation "O'zapft is", the Oktoberfest is then officially opened.

title: Christenberg Extra Tour from Münchhausen
short_description: On this moderately difficult tour, we hike through the Burgwald forest up to the Christenberg, an old Kesterburg.
long_description: Apart from crossing the village of Mellnau, this Hesse extra tour leads almost exclusively through the forest, which, however, rarely appears dark due to the numerous sparse pine trees. Right at the beginning and just before the ruins of Mellnau Castle, the route runs along the edge of the forest for a short distance. The forest is very diverse: pines, spruces and beeches mix to form a varied potpourri. In addition, there is heather at the edge of the path and some marshy areas with mosses and rushes. Most of the trail is on gravel paths.

title: Hiking with kids near Borsa: Cascada Cailor
short_description: The path that goes up from Borșa to Cascada Cailor (Horses' Waterfall) promises some good-quality hours spent with the children outdoors, at the foot of the Rodna Mountains. At the end of the route, everybody is rewarded with the view of the impressive waterfall where legend has it that many horses drowned.
long_description:
Although accessing the alpine plateau by chairlift seems more tempting to many, taking the longer route through the forest, by foot, isn't just about killing time, but rather about spending time outdoors.
The route starts at the end of an asphalted road. Following the red triangle signs, you quickly enter the forest and continue on a forest path, slightly ascending until you reach the waterfall. The path is slightly paved for a start, then you only have a dirt path. In case of light rain, you can still take this route, so don't be intimidated by bad weather.
Children will have fun admiring the views, the flowers, the thick forest, and finally, the waterfall.
A few meters before the waterfall, you'll reach a spot suitable for camping (off-camping, of course); further on, there's a gazebo perfect for picnicking with a million-dollar view. You even have toilets nearby, rudimentary ones, but very useful.

title: Trail to Janela do Céu in Ibitipoca
short_description: This is the most famous circuit of the Ibitipoca State Park, in Minas Gerais. Not only because it goes to one of the most stunning viewpoints in the region - the Janela do Céu - but also because it is possible to see most of the natural wonders of the park, such as peaks, caves, waterfalls and natural pools.
long_description:
The Ibitipoca State Park is located in the municipalities of Lima Duarte and Santa Rita de Ibitipoca, and offers 3 circuits for its visitors: the Water Circuit, the Pico do Pi&atildeo Circuit and the famous Céu Window Circuit, which surrounds almost the entire park.You will get to know the peaks of Cruzeiro and Lombada, the highest point of the Park with 1768 meters of altitude, several caves, the stunning Janela do Céu, which gives the circuit its name, and several other waterfalls and beaches on the two rivers that cross the region, Rio Vermelho and Rio do Salto.
The highlight of this Conservation Unit, and what arouses much curiosity, é no doubt the colour of the water, of a golden-brown hue. 
Before starting your adventure, visit the official website of the Park to obtain correct and updated information on the opening hours, the maximum number of visitors and prices.

title: Bivio - Septimer Hospice - Lunghin Pass - Maloja
short_description: The tour starts in Bivio and leads via the Septimer Pass, then up the left flank of the valley to the Lunghin Pass to the triple watershed of Europe.
long_description: From here, the water flows into three different oceans. The Eva dal Lunghin, later Eva da Sett flows into the Julia, then into the Rhine and finally into the North Sea. The Inn flows into the Danube and the Black Sea. The Maira flows through the Bergell, joins the Po, which finds its destination in the Adriatic Sea. From the Lunghin Pass, the hike goes past the Lägh dal Lunghin down to Maloja.

title: Nordic Walking in the Deisenhofen Forest around Oberhaching
short_description: In the chessboard-like Deisenhofen forest, we can easily determine the length of our route. So there is something for everyone's running taste.
long_description: From St. Stephen's Church we walk to the left into Kübergstraße until we reach the park. Behind the park and after a residential area we come to the railway gates. Always straight ahead, along the railway and the "Eisenbahnstraßl", we walk through a subway into the Kirchweg until we reach the St. Ulrich Chapel (1). We walk past a large riding stable and can fortify ourselves at Café Momm (2) halfway along the route. We turn left to Portenläng and take the middle path into the forest behind the farm. We go straight on until we reach the wooden well, where we turn left. After a rest area (3) with a pond, we reach a residential area. We walk downhill along Leonhardiweg, past the chapel (4) into Lanzenhaarstraße. Here our tour can end in one of the cafés around the church.

title: Around Lauterbach Tour
short_description:
On this tour we experience the surroundings of Lauterbach.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
From Ferienhof Zinn we start the hike in the direction of Alteberg. There we pass the former quarry, home to the Schmelz stables and their horses. The path continues above the quarry to the vantage point with a magnificent panoramic view of the hills around Lauterbach.
Then the trail continues to the game reserve. Now our path leads to the southern side of the Alteberg, past Schrebergberg gardens to the Vulkanradweg (volcano cycle path), which we follow to the former Blitzenrod railway station. We leave the cycle path and cross the Lauter. In the district of Blitzenrod überqueren we cross the Bundesstrasse 275 and walk through the settlement to the edge of the forest. Follow the path to the top of the Hainig (409 m above sea level). The lookout tower was built in 1906/07, it is surrounded by almost 1000 year old oak trees, hollows and the remains of a stone rampart.
We leave the Hainig in a northerly direction and reach Lauterbach, cross the B 254 – Fuldaer Str. Our path leads to the bridge where the Lauter and Brenderwasser rivers meet. We continue past Lauterbach railway station, through an old, then a new industrial area to the cycle path on the B254. At the Steinmühl we cross the main road and follow the Brenderwasser to the railway line. Cross the water and walk along the railway embankment to Rimlos.

images.caption: Our tour leads across meadows and streams.

title: The Huntepadd near Dötlingen
short_description: This hike leads along the Hunte, which is completely natural in this section, through the Wildeshauser Geest Nature Park to the "Glaner Braut" megalithic tombs.
long_description:
Our hike begins at the old village school at Karkbäk. From there, we first head towards the centre of the village. In the Pastorenwald, at the spring, we turn right into the beech forest, through which we reach the steep bank of the Hunte. We briefly leave the forest and walk across a field, at the end of which we turn left and walk along the edge of the forest. After crossing the Hunte, we continue straight ahead for a short distance and then turn left. Now we continue straight ahead and into the forest, which thins out after a while on our left. Here we turn left to the four large stone graves "Glaner Braut". The two larger mound beds and the two smaller passage graves are differently preserved and date from the Neolithic period (approx. 5000 to 2000 BC).
Now our path continues straight ahead, apart from a few bends, and we cross the Hunte again. We then follow our path until the Heideweg branches off to the left. Stay on this path and a little later turn right onto Badbergsweg, which takes us straight on to Dötlingen. We walk a short distance on the Heideweg again, which finally ends on the Dorfring, where we keep left. Another time we turn left and find ourselves again at the Karkbäk and walk back to our starting point, the old village school.

images.caption: Along the route we come across magnificent thatched-roof houses.

title: From Bötzingen over the Vogelsang Pass
short_description: This tour offers you outstanding views: The Neunlindenturm on the Totenkopf rewards you with its wonderful panoramic view of the Black Forest, the Vosges and the Kaiserstuhl region.
long_description: We start at the railway station in Bötzingen, follow the signposts in the direction of Vogelsang and walk along Gottenheimer Straße (red triangle) into the centre of the village. Shortly after crossing an intersection, we turn left into Bergstraße and after about 100 m follow the red triangle trail markings to the right. We leave the road and follow the footpath on the Seelenbergpfad (1). This runs along a stream and leads to a residential road, which we follow to the right (red triangle) until we reach the village. On the main road we turn right and just before the church of St. Alban (2) we turn left again. On a farm track we now head into the vineyards. We follow the path marking with the red triangle (half left). The path climbs slightly and runs above a phonolite quarry (3). Here, about 15 million years ago, magma rose in a volcanic vent and cooled down. The resulting greenish-grey volcanic stone, phonolite, is quarried here and used as building or construction stone. About 400 m after the quarry, we follow a path uphill to the left and continue hiking along the blue dot marking through a wooded area to a crossroads with a shelter. There we turn left and cross the road. On the opposite side of the road, we walk up the car park ramp to the rest area at the Vogelsangpass (4). The blue rhombus on a yellow background now leads us further in the direction of Gierstein, until after about 500 m we reach a crossroads with a bench at the edge of the forest. Here we follow the forest path uphill to the left in the direction of Neunlinden. Passing old boundary stones, we go uphill on the ridge, sometimes steeply. After a particularly steep ascent, we reach the rest area in front of the Neunlinden tower (5). This lookout tower was built in 1900. The climb is worthwhile: after the steps, you are rewarded with a fantastic all-round view: in suitable weather, the view reaches not only to the nearby TV tower, but also to the entire Kaiserstuhl, the Black Forest and the Vosges. After this view, we walk back on the same path for about 1.5 km until a trail marker with a green dot points us down the path to the right in the direction of Wasenweiler. We come to a wide forest path (Hundskehlenweg), cross it and walk straight on along a small clearing (this path is also signposted as a Nordic walking route). Follow the green dot until you reach a transmission mast. Shortly after this, we keep to the trail marking with the blue dot and go sharply left downhill in the direction of Bötzingen (we walk under a power line). Now we stay on the forest path, which partly also leads along vineyards, until we come to a narrow vineyard road at the Bötzingen Schützenhaus. Follow this road past vineyards and fields into a right-hand bend. Turn left behind this bend and then right after the stream. Before a flood retention basin (6), we cross the stream again to the right and follow the Weinbergstraße to a large information board. Here we turn left. At the foot of the Seelenberg, we finally reach the first houses of Bötzingen. We follow the road until we reach the crossroads we already know. Here we turn right into the Seelenbergstraße. The red triangle marks the rest of the way back to the railway station: Turn left at the next crossroads to the main road. Follow this to the right to the station.

title: From Günzach to Kaufbeuren
short_description: Through the beautiful Ostallgäu we experience a varied hike from Günzach to Kaufbeuren.
long_description: At the beginning of our tour we visit the source of the Östliche Günz. We are on the east side of the Günzacher Steige, which the Züge climb with ease today. At Günzach station it finds its high point at 801 m. This makes it the highest double-track station in Germany. Through forests along the railway line we reach the Lange Weiher. Around Aitrang the landscape opens up. We enjoy the views of the Allgäu Alps. Behind the village we climb to the Bergmang-Alpe. We follow the wooded hillside until we leave it and descend to Oberbeuren. We cross the district and reach the old town of Kaufbeuren. On the eastern edge is the railway station.

title: Walking the long ridge to Oshlak (Maja e Oshlakut)
short_description: Scenic and not too challenging walk to the summit of Maja e Oshlakut over one of the longest ridges of the Sharri Mountian foothills.
long_description: The long ridge of Oshlak thrones over the Lumbardhi i Prizrenit valley and extends all the way from the pass village Prevalle almost to Prizren. The ascent from Prevalle takes you partly steep but never too challenging through lush pine forests and finally beyond the tree line to the minor summit of Maja e Arnenit. From their we follow the sheer endless ridge to the highest point, the summit of Maja e Oshlakut. The views up here are breathtaking, extending across the high peaks of the Sharri Mountains to the south and all across the Kosovo Field. Also, as the Sharr Mountains National Park is rich with brown bears, it is not unlikely that you get to see one of the furry fellas from up on the ridge. The descend first follows the ridge back the way you came before descending into the slopes above Prevalle without having to climb up to Arnenit again.

title: From the Madlener Haus to the Wiesbadener Hütte
short_description: On this hike we collect enchanting impressions of the mountain world of the Silvretta on the easy ascent path. On the Rückweg üvia the Sommerweg we enjoy everything one level higher.
long_description: The Silvretta is a cross-border mountain group. The countries of Austria and Switzerland are involved. On the Austrian side, the border between the federal states of Vorarlberg and Tyrol runs through the area östlich of today's Silvrettastausee. Most of the peaks are at an altitude of over 2500 metres. This means that you are permanently above the tree line. The best known is the Piz Buin at 3255 metres. It is the highest peak in Vorarlberg. Between 1925 and 1930, the Illwerke built the Vermunt reservoir a little lower down towards Partenen. During the 2nd World War, work then began on the Silvretta reservoir. Since 1954, Partenen in the Montafon and Galt in the Paznaun valley have been connected by the Silvretta High Alpine Road. This has a length of around 25 km. It is thanks to this construction work that we can now easily reach the Bielerhütte, the highest point of the Alpine road, by car. From November to May, however, this connection is closed. Europe's only boat service at an altitude of over 2000 m operates on the Silvretta Reservoir.

images.caption: The water rushes out of the Klostertal.
View across the reservoir into the Ochsental valley.
View down to the Madlener Haus.
Mountain view from the Wiesbadener Hütte.
Silvretta reservoir from the summer path.

title: Wil - Giessenfall
short_description: Leave Wil south-west towards Wilen, always following the Toggenburger Höhenweg.
long_description: You soon find yourself on a forest path in the direction of Giessenfall - Dietschwil. Along the stream you reach the idyllically situated Giessenfall, where you can enjoy a picnic on the square above the fall. If you prefer a restaurant, hike on to Dietschwil and return along the same path (15 minutes each way). At the Giessenfall you hike in the direction of Letten - Altbach, mostly following the Altbach in the forest, to Engi and back to Wil.

title: जूनागढ़-ऊपरकोट किला ट्रैक
short_description: गुजरात के जूनागढ़ शहर का ऊपरकोट किला ट्रैक पूरी तरह से एक अर्बन ट्रैक है ज ो शहर से होते हुर किले तक जाता है।
long_description:
जूनागढ़ शहर एक पूर्व रियासत है जो की गुजरात राज्य के जूनागढ़ जिले में स्थित है। यह प्रसिद्ध गिरनार पहाड़ों की तलहटी में स्थित है। जूनागढ़ अपने इंडो-इस्लामिक वास्तुकला, ऊपरकोट किला, जैन तीर्थ स्थलों, बौद्ध गुफाओं, पानी की बावड़ियों, संगीत, संस्कृति, और गुजराती खानपान के लिए जाना जाता है। प्राचीन समय में इन स्थानों में जाने के लिए जूनागढ़ के आसपास कई नेचर ट्रेल थी जो शहरीकरण के कारण अब डामर की पक्की सडकों और सीढ़ियों में बदल गयी हैं लेकिन इसके बावजूद भी इन स्थानों में पैदल यात्रा करने का आकर्षण कम नहीं हुआ है।  
ऊपरकोट किले तक की ट्रेल भी मुख्यतः अब एक अर्बन ट्रेल है जो जूनागढ़ के बस स्टेशन से होकर किले तक जाती है। मार्ग का ज्यादातर हिस्सा शहरी सड़कों से होकर गुजरता है हालाँकि बीच बीच में प्राकृतिक रास्ते और नेचर ट्रेल भी पड़ती है।
ट्रैक मार्ग का अंतिम गंतव्य ऊपरकोट किला है जो अब एक जीर्ण शीर्ण अवस्था में है। इस किले और जूनागढ़ शहर को मौर्य साम्राज्य के यशस्वी सम्राट चंद्रगुप्त ने गिरनार पहाड़ी की तलहटी में स्थापित किया गया था। किला जूनागढ़ के पूर्व में स्थित है और इससे पूरे जूनागढ़ शहर और साथ ही गिरनार पहाड़ियों का भव्य दृश्य देखा जा सकता है।

title: Wil - Wildberg
short_description: Hike through impressive gorges along the Thur from Wil to Wildberg and back.
long_description: From Wil railway station you go via Rickenbach to Schwarzenbach. In Schwarzenbach, take the path towards Benzenau - Degenau - Jonschwil. You hike through an impressive gorge and then along the Thur to Jonschwil (in wet weather we recommend the route via Schwarzenbach - Degenau). From Jonschwil the route climbs to Wildberg. There you are rewarded with a magnificent view. Leave Wildberg in the direction of Bisacht - Oberuzwil - along the pond to Bettenau. Continue over the Bärensberg - Schwarzenbach and the Thurau back to Wil.

title: Hike to the highest mountain in Denmark - Scandinavian Summits
short_description: You don't have to be a passionate mountaineer to hike to the summit of Møllehøj. The highest elevation in Denmark is just under 170 meters above sea level and the walk there is short.
long_description:
The highest mountain in Denmark is called Møllehøj. In the past, the highest elevation was thought to be Ejer Bavnehøj, where a monument in the form of a lookout tower was erected. Ejer Bavnehøj is well signposted and easy to find. There is also a car park, public toilets and a kiosk.
From the car park, walk down a dirt track to the right of the kiosk until you come to a gate. Open the gate and close it after passing through. On the back of a stable, a path leads a few hundred metres to the summit. The peak Møllehøj is marked with a millstone, as Møllehøj means Mühlenhöhe. From here you have a beautiful view of the Dänische Alpen.

images.caption: Møllehøj summit marked with a millstone
View from Ejer Bavnehøj to Møllehøj
The path to the summit of Møllehøj leads past a stable
Fischingen monastery church with St. Idda chapel

title: Wil - Nollen
short_description: Circular hike through meadows and forests from Wil über Nollen back to Wil.
long_description:
From the station, walk in the direction of Uerental. From Uerental the path leads through meadows and woods. Once you reach the top, it is worth taking a look back at the old town of Wiler. In Wuppenau you tackle the climb up Nollen. There you are rewarded with an impressive view that stretches from Lake Constance over Thurgau to Wil, and from Fürstenland to Herisau. Above, the Alps stretch from Vorarlberg to Alpstein and Glarus. On the Rückweg üvia the settlement of Leuberg to Zuzwil you can enjoy the wonderful view again and again. In Zuzwil, take the path over the Lindau, through the Nieselberg forest to Känzeli / Neulanden and on to the old town of Wiler and the railway station.

title: Lönspfad
short_description: Secluded little paths and tracks await us, which we will follow from the Eggegebirge through the hilly Teutoburg Forest. Hermann Löns (1866 - 1914) is the patron saint of the hiking trail. He was a well-known poet of nature and local history and made great efforts to explore and protect nature.
long_description:
Stage 1: Horn-Bad Meinberg/Leopoldstal - Berlebeck (20 km)
We start our hike at the railway station in Leopoldstal and walk in the valley of the bubbling Silberbach past the Silbermühle and the Kattenmühle. After we have reached the Strothe along the Hohlestein, we follow it to Kohlstädt. At the Hohlestein is the Hohlsteinhöhle, which was already explored in 1779. It is not open to the public, however, as it is a protected natural monument and provides shelter for numerous species of bats. From Kohlstadt, the hike continues to Kreuzkrug and up to the highest point of the entire tour (shortly before Berlebeck). Berlebeck, the finishing point of the first stage, is a little off the beaten track in the valley of the Berlebecke.
Stage 2: Berlebeck - Oerlinghausen (20 km)
After a visit to the eagle station in Berlebeck - a bird park and very popular destination - a short climb takes us back to the Lönspfad. We cross the Klöppingsberg and pass the transmitter on the Bielstein. We touch Augustusdorf only briefly and then walk along above the Senne military training area. There may even be tanks on the way here, but we are rewarded for the brief noise with wide views of the Senneland landscape. Soon silence returns and we hike along lonely paths, which can be a little sandy from time to time, to Oerlinghausen. Here the Lönspfad ends at the Archäologisches Freilichtmuseum.

title: Over the Litzner Sattel
short_description: On this mountain tour, the focus is on experiencing glaciers and their legacy during their retreat. On the descent we hike through a typical, impressive and seemingly untouched high valley with small moors, fells and side arms of the main stream with clear water.
long_description: The Silvretta is a cross-border mountain group. The countries of Austria and Switzerland are involved. On the Austrian side, the border between the federal states of Vorarlberg and Tyrol runs through the area östlich of today's Silvrettastausee. Most of the peaks are at an altitude of over 2500 metres. This means that you are permanently above the tree line. The best known is the Piz Buin at 3255 metres. It is the highest peak in Vorarlberg. Between 1925 and 1930, the Illwerke built the Vermunt reservoir a little lower down towards Partenen. During the 2nd World War, work then began on the Silvretta reservoir. Since 1954, Partenen in the Montafon and Galt in the Paznaun valley have been connected by the Silvretta High Alpine Road. This has a length of around 25 km. It is thanks to this construction work that we can now easily reach the Bielerhütte, the highest point of the Alpine road, by car. From November to May, however, this connection is closed. Europe's only boat service at an altitude of over 2000 m operates on the Silvretta Reservoir.

images.caption: First green on the descent into Klostertal.
View from the Tschifernella to the Vermunt reservoir.

title: Lahnhöhenweg Westerwald variant (right or north of the Lahn)
short_description: It's not so easy to decide between the two variants of the Lahnhöhenweg: The route on the Taunus side is perhaps a nose ahead in terms of scenery due to the romantic Jammertal, Mühlbachtal and Schweizertal valleys, but the Westerwald variant follows the narrow valley of the Lahn directly and offers the more spectacular views on its rugged basalt plateau. Here we opt for the Westerwald.
long_description:
The Westerwald variant of the Lahnhöhenweg leads from Wetzlar to the right or north of the Lahn to where the river flows into the Rhine. The section from the source of the Lahn in the Rothaargebirge mountains to Wetzlar (see route) is not dealt with further here.
We start our hike at one of the most beautiful rivers in Germany and walk from Wetzlar along the Oberbieler Grundbach up to the Schäferberg. Now several small villages alternate with dense forests and narrow stream valleys. In Löhnberg we cross the Lahn and continue hiking on the opposite bank until Weilburg. A narrow bend in the river leads us around Weilburg Castle, which we should definitely visit beforehand. Up to Aumenau we continue southwards on a hilly stretch above the rustic valley. We follow a few river loops through Runkel, where the castle and the half-timbered houses exude a very special charm. In Limburg, the route briefly changes banks again. Here, apart from the beautiful old town, there is above all the cathedral to see, which was once embossed on the back of the 1,000 Deutschmark note. We have already covered a good part of the Lahnhöhenweg and with Diez we reach not only Rhineland-Palatinate but also the very scenic lower Lahn valley. Passing Altendiez, Geilnau and Scheidt, we reach Laurenburg, with its castle of the same name. Now we descend to the Lahn and then up past Dörnberg. In Obernhof we can taste the wine of the region. A little later we pass through the small town of Nassau and are then back on the Höhenweg to reach Bad Ems - the healing springs there will be a boon for our feet. We hike along the Old Post Road on the mountain ridge and leave the Kitzelsberg, Mittelberg, Geierkopf as well as the Mehrsberg behind us. It is not far down to Lahnstein. This is where the Lahn flows into the Rhine - a perfect end to our hike.

title: Wiler Tower
short_description: Circular hike from Wil to the Wiler Tower.
long_description: From the railway station, walk to Stadtweier, then follow the hiking trail and via Unterer Rebweg to the Trotte der Wiler Ortsbürger. From there you walk up to Burgstall, then along the edge of the forest to the tower on the Hofberg. The Wiler tower is 34 m high, has 189 steps and offers a fantastic panoramic view of Toggenburg, Fürstenland, Thurgau and Lake Constance. Go back past the Kaiserhütte and down the Kaiserlindenweg to the Hänsstrasse. There you turn left into Bergtalweg and follow it down to Stadtweier. Then the path leads back to the station - with a detour into the beautiful old town.

title: Wil - Three-well
short_description: Through forest and vineyard from Wil to Dreibrunnen
long_description: From the train station, head to Dreibrunnen. The baroque pilgrimage chapel Maria Dreibrunnen is known far beyond the region. At the small pond we follow the hiking trail through the forest to Bronschhofen and on to Wiberg. At the old wine cellar, where an oak cork still stands from 1653, the Rückweg begins, which leads along the vineyard to Wil. At the town pond, it is worth taking a detour into the historic old town.

title: कालेसर नेशनल पार्क में बॉम्बे पुर ट्रेल
short_description: हरियाणा राज्य के यमुना नगर ज़िले के छछरौली शहर के पास स्थित बॉम्बेपुर गाँव की यह ट्रेल 2.4 किलोमीटर की 'आउट एंड बैक' ट्रेल है। शानदार कालेशर नेशनल पार्क के अंदर का यह ट्रैक हाइकिंग, ट्रैकिंग, और बर्ड वाचिंग के लिए बढ़िया है।
long_description:
यह नेचर ट्रेल शानदार कालेसर राष्ट्रीय उद्यान के अंदर ले जाती है। हरे-भरे जंगलों और जैव विविधता वाला वातावरण इस ट्रेल की पहचान है। इस ट्रेल में कई पक्षी भी दिखने की संभावना रहती है। कालेसर राष्ट्रीय उद्यान की बॉम्बेपुर गाँव से शुरू होने वाली यह ट्रेल राजाजी नेशनल पार्क की परिधि में है।
ट्रेल की बात करें तो यह 'आउट एंड बैक' किस्म की आसान स्तर वाली ट्रेल है। पूरी ट्रेल में हलकी चढ़ाई है। शुरूआती हिस्से में सड़क से ट्रेल के आरंभ बिंदु पर आना पड़ता है और फिर उसके बाद की पूरी रास्ता एक सुन्दर नेचर ट्रेल है। जंगल और घने पेड़ों से करीब साढ़े तीन किलोमीटर रास्ता तय करने के बाद ट्रेल एक दूसरी सड़क से मिल जाती है जिसे ट्रेल का अंत बिंदु मान लेना चाहिए और जहाँ से वापस लौट आना ठीक है। वैसे कालेसर नेशनल पार्क में एक लम्बी लूप ट्रेल भी है जिसकी जानकारी यहाँ पर है।

images.caption: यमुनानगर जिले के बॉम्बेपुर गाँव में कालेसर राष्ट्रीय उद्यान को जाती हुई नेचर ट्रेल, हरियाणा, भारत।
छछरौली शहर के बॉम्बेपुर ट्रेल पर कालेसर राष्ट्रीय उद्यान का घना जंगल, यमुनानगर जिला, हरियाणा, भारत।

long_description: Without particular difficulty, this route is a good idea for a walk around Eyguières.

title: 16th DYNAFIT Transalpine Run 2021 - 6th stage: from Klosters to Scoul
short_description:
Long, intense and technically challenging, the 6th stage of the 16th DYNAFIT Transalpine Run powered by Volkswagen R (TAR).
Start: Klosters sports and event arena (1,210 m). With a view of snow-covered mountain peaks of the Silvretta, the trail initially follows the Landquart river slightly uphill. Surrounded by three-thousand-metre peaks, including Piz Buin, the teams run through the Vernela valley up to the highest point, Fuorcla Zadrell (2,759 m). This is followed by a technically very demanding downhill; the finish is near the train station in Scoul.

title: Crossing the Korab Mountains - Stage 2: Caje - Radomire

title: Engelssteig
short_description: Hike through one of the steepest vineyard slopes in Europe
long_description: In Bühlertal (Rastatt district), leisure enthusiasts can expect a short but special tour through one of the steepest vineyard slopes in Europe: the "Engelssteig" offers a variety of special features in a small space - fascinating dry stone walls, open rock formations, historic single vineyards and, of course, unique views as far as the Rhine plain and the Black Forest. For demanding hikers, a via ferrata variant is offered on the approximately one-and-a-half-kilometre-long trail. The trail is open from 1 April to 31 October.

title: Otterepass - rarely walked and challenging
short_description: Mountain hiking trail to Fildrich. Scenically very beautiful, but equally demanding pass from the Entschtligetal üover the Niesen chain into the farthest part of the Diemtigtal. The long, steep ascent to the top of the pass and the subsequent no less brisk descent require a good physical condition. Longer sections on hard surface near settlements.
long_description:
From the Bim bus stop, stop a short distance out of the valley at Achseten. There is a legend surrounding this impressive river crossing: Franz, secretly engaged to his master's daughter, was surprised together with her by a terrible thunderstorm. A bolt of lightning hurled the cattleman into the depths. However, the death was interpreted as murder and Franz was innocently executed. Full of grief, his fiancée jumped from the high footbridge into the abyss. Now a path branches off to the right and leads past a chapel, climbing steeply up to point 1316 in the Spisse Rinderwald (Spisse = narrow piece of land). The Frutigspissen on the eastern slope of the Niesenkette are bordered by deep torrent meadows. A road with a slight gradient leads to the huts Im Schwand. From here you have to prove your stamina. In countless hairpin bends, the mountain path winds steeply up the loosely wooded slope interspersed with gullies and waterfalls to the Ottere hut group. From the uppermost hut, the trail goes steeply upwards - sometimes without a path - into the marshy alpine hollow of Stirple,
which is bypassed in a large curve. Below the Erbithore river, a good mountain path leads up through a scree slope to the Otterepass. The view of the
wide ring of peaks, which stretches from the Wetterhorn to the Wildstrubel, is impressive, but the deep view of the route that has been covered so far also arouses amazement. Ahead, the Türmlihore, Rauflihorn and Spillgerte group separate the Diemtigtal from the Färmeltal. The pass path now first falls into the high hollow of Obertal and turns, passing a rocky band in a large loop, towards the Oberberg on Alp Chilei. Beautiful stream motifs are a delight on the descent to Mittelberg, where the alpine stream is crossed. The path climbs a wooded steep step in many twists and turns before turning out of the valley to the Hindere Fildrich hut and the huts of Vordere Fildrich. The view of the alpine basin framed by the rocky towers of the Gsür and the Türmlihore is impressive. The remaining 4 km, first to the right, then to the left of the lively Fildrich, via Egg to Grimmialp (terminus of the post bus route) is unfortunately on asphalt for lack of an alternative.

title: From Old Faithful Geyser to Morning Glory Pool
short_description: A wonderful, magical and mesmerizing circular tour that includes a huge amount of hot and colorful mineral pools, geysers and other natural wonders.
long_description:
One of the flagship routes in Yellowstone Park, during the route that includes walking on a system of wooden bridges, you will pass a huge number of pools and thermal hot springs as well as geysers that are a few meters apart. The pools and springs are often characterized by shimmering water with mesmerizing hues. The route begins with a visual look at the huge Old Faithful geyser, where along any path you choose you can enjoy several geysers from which water and smoke erupt. The culmination of the route is a particularly colorful pool called "Morning Glory". A particularly experiential travel route with rare sights and a fictional spectacle.
This itinerary is a must for travelers to Yellowstone Park. The route is organized and therefore suitable in principle for walking even with strollers.

title: High trail variants on the Hahnenmoos Pass
short_description: Unique circular hike across the hills around the Geils valley basin. After a steep ascent over the Gilbachegga to the Sillerenbill, there is a wonderful hike over the Sillererken and through the Hahnenmoos to the Hahnenmoospass. The views towards Lake Thun and the Obersimmental are magnificent. The trail continues to Luegli on the flank of the Regenboldshorn without any major differences in altitude. The descent to the Bergläger takes place in various stages. At the end, the hike along the lively Gilsbach stream is cosy. Almost entirely on a natural path. With the inclusion of public transport, various options make it possible to customise the circular hike.
long_description:
From the Gilbach bus stop, follow the road branching off to the west for 600 metres. Now keep to the wooded mountain ridge and take the very steep, rough path up to the Gilbachegge. The loosened forest cover at this point allows splendid views of Adelboden and out through the Engstligental valley. You soon come across small ponds where rare dragonflies cavort. As the gradient eases, you reach the mountain station of the Adelboden-Sillerenbühl cable car. What a view! Along the Niesen chain you can see as far as the Thunersee region. On the opposite side of the valley, Elsighorn, Bunderspitz, Chlyne and Gross Lohner tower above, and Wildstrubel and Wildhorn mark the horizon to the south. According to the Seybuch, Alp Sillere provides enough food for 301 cattle units for 10 weeks.
On the alpine road, descend into the ridge depression and on a wide, gravelled path, always staying on the ridge, into the eastern flank of the Lavey Ridge. From Vordersillere the trail leads in gentle ups and downs over flowery grassy paths and through washed-out gullies to the mountain hotel on the Hahnenmoospass (after Geilsbühl 30 min). The view over the high moor depression to the Wildstrubel-Wildhorn massif is magnificent!
The path is almost level and continues to the Alprprücken, which leads down from the Metschstand, and into the flank of the Regenboldshorn to the Schatthaus Ufem Blatti (to Geilsbüel 45 min). Fields of alpine roses line the path, which reaches the ridge rib again at Luegli (after Lurnigegga-Geilsbüel 1h). Here you can enjoy a magnificent view of the ski areas around Geilsbüel. The descent to the alpine floor of the Lurnig is initially quite steep and leads between mighty stone leaves to the alp Bütschi, where the trail changes the side of the valley and leads through the lower fringe of the scree slopes under the almost frighteningly wild towering Bütschiflue. When you meet the road, you head west towards the valley floor. With varying gradients, the trail quickly descends over mountain meadows and through woodland to the intermediate station of the Silleren cable car in the Berglglinger. The last section of the hike along the rushing Gilsbach to Gilbach is also a pure pleasure.

title: About the Belpberg
short_description: A panoramic hike across the wide plateau of the Belpberg to Chutzen, the most beautiful vantage point in the area.
long_description:
On the flatter part of the Moränenrink, close to the lovely Gerzensee, the route leads up to the former official seat of Seftigen on the edge of the Thunersee basin. Parts on hard surface, also outside towns.

From Belp railway station you first descend via the Gürbe to the village centre. The castle, today the seat of the Seftigen office, and the church, which once belonged to the Interlaken canons, are worth seeing. From the edge of the village, keep straight on to the wooded northern flank of the Belpberg. Pass the Breiten farm and begin the extraordinarily steep ascent to Hohburg Castle. Around the castle hill you continue to gain altitude. Only sparse remains of the walls still bear witness to the early fortress of Belp, which dominated the approaches to the Aare and Gorge valleys. The ascent to the small hamlet of Hohburg demands a few more drops of sweat. Now begins the splendid hike across the Belpberg plateau. Via pt. 797 (to Fuchsacher-Münsingen 1h30; to Simmleren 50 min) and lime trees, you strive towards Chutzen, whose characteristic spherical lime tree soon becomes visible (to Riedli-Belp 1h15). The panoramic view over the Aare valley into the Emmental hills, to the Oberland snow giants over Lake Thun and along the Stockhorn chain into the Gantrisch and Gurnigel regions is magnificent. A panorama board provides information. The Chutzen restaurant is in the hollow ahead, and you descend to the Simmleren slopes. On the level path you reach Nessleren (to Münsingen 1h15; to Toffen 1h 20), then the path leads through the Rohrholz forest to Gerzensee. The high village on the sunny, panoramic flank of the Belpberg has always been the preferred area of the Bernese patrician families who built their country residences here. The New Castle is now a study centre for the Swiss National Bank Foundation and is therefore not accessible. The idyllic Gerzensee, which has been a nature reserve since 1965, is part of the castle property. Its shore can only be accessed at the bathing places at the southern end of the lake. After the New Castle, follow the road leading to Kirchdorf for a few steps. At the lakeside shop, a road turns off to the mountain train of the Büelen. Splendid view of Gerzensee and the lake (after Thalgut-Wichtrach 25 min). The view becomes even more extensive in the rear section. The church tower of Kirchdorf already comes into view. At the beautifully situated cemetery you reach the stately village with its old buildings worth seeing (to Jaberg Kiesen 40 min; to Mühlethurnen 55 min).
Fertile farmland is crossed on the hike through the hollow of the Limpacht valley via Noflen and Blattacher to Seftigen.

.

title: Trütlisberg Pass - high moors and a wealth of flowers
short_description: Charming pass hike from the Obersimmental into the Lauenental valley in view of the young, partly glaciated northern flanks of the Wildstrubel-Wildhorn area. The distinctive moorland areas with corresponding vegetation are also impressive. The route is largely identical to the route recorded in the inventory of historic transport routes. Little hard surface.
long_description:
Lenk, once «Bedli», today a spa centre, is particularly proud of its healing springs. As early as 1689, the mayor and council of the city of Bern granted permission to «turn a sulphur well into a spa». At that time, nobody knew that the Balm Spring was the most important and strongest sulphur spring in the Alps. In the modern spa centre built in 1977, the health-promoting properties of this water can be optimally exploited. Legend has it that the name Lenk is associated with Longinus, a refugee of the Theban Legion. More likely, however, is the derivation from «a der lengen Egge», an outlet of the Oberlaubhorn.
From Lenk railway station, walk a short distance down to the Simmebrücke and into the village centre. From the church, a slightly ascending pavement leads to the entrance to the Wallbach Gorge. Via steps and stairs you walk through the most impressive part of the gorge, which gives you an insight into the striking erosion forms that the water has washed out over the millennia. Now follow the well-maintained path up many steps in the wooded gorge slope to Berghaus Wallegg. Along a barely visible water pipe, the so-called water path leads through the wooded gully flank to the footbridge over the mountain stream and on the opposite slope steeply up to the pastures In der Siten. First a road leads, then a path over flowery, in places marshy mountain meadows to the Undere, then on to the Obere Lochberg. The impressive moorland landscape at the Truuml;tlisbergpass is interspersed with Knabenkröder, woolgrass and Arctic rush. Beautiful view from the pass into the Wildstrubel and Wildhorn area and into the valley of Lauenen. The gypsum fields of the Gryde on the nearby Stübleni appear snow-white. The panoramic view from the nearby Tube (2106 m; 15 min) is more comprehensive.
Maintaining the previous direction, the trail now descends steeply over the pasture slope to the hut of Vordere Trütlisberg, where the timberline is reached. Forest and pasture alternate in a pleasant rhythm in the further descent to the hut group Uf der Flue. Shortly after crossing the Schwarzbächlis and the Mülibach in the Rütschli, the trail describes a large loop and finally leads along the latter down to the village centre of Lauenen. This is included in the federal inventory of sites worthy of protection.

title: From the seclusion to the high altitude health resort
short_description: Mountain hiking trail to Grütschalp and enjoyable hike into Soustal.
long_description:
600 m difference in altitude have to be overcome to reach Chüebodmi. The steep ascent, however, is made easier by shady mountain forest along the entire length. Now follows an enjoyable hike up into the Soustal valley and through the Spryssewald forest to Grütschalp. The views of the Jungfrau Group are unique from the Grütschalp-Mürren hike, on which you also cross the young Staubbach stream. Only a few metres of hard surface. If you use the Isenfluh-Sulwald cable car, the ascent is shortened by 1h20.

The densely packed houses in the centre of Isenfluh partly have façade paintings that are native to the Frutigland region. Up in the village, at the former Hotel Jungfrau (now the Geneva Bible School), the view of the Jungfrau Group is incomparably beautiful. Now branch off slope-wise from the Strässchen and climb in many zigzag turns, without crossing the stream, through loose woodland to Sulwald (5 min to the cable car station). If you take a few steps out of the forest, you again experience a magnificent view of the mountains of the Lauterbrunnen Valley.
A slightly gentler ascent, then once again over a steep section, takes you to the rocky ridge of Chüebodmi and thus also the highest point of the hike (to Suls-Lobhornhütte 45 min; üvia Suls-Sousegg to Sousläger 2h). Deep crevices in the rock bed indicate the constant movement of the rock masses. Over the karstified alpine soil, the trail now descends gently to the Sulsbach stream and after crossing it - partly in the forest - into the Soustal valley. The vertical rock layers of the Gälbe Schopf stand above the flat pastureland of the Soustal, and the peak of the Schilthorn becomes visible at the far end of the valley. Cross the Sousbach stream on a narrow footbridge and climb slightly to the upper huts in the Sousläger. In a hollow on the lower left is Flöschwaldseeli, surrounded by dark firs. The path now descends gently around the outflow of the Marchegg through the Spryssewald to the railway station on the Gruuml;tschalp high above the Lauterbrunnen valley. A wide footpath then leads to the gurgling and babbling young Staubbach stream and through beautiful mountain forest to Winteregg station. Soon the path runs parallel to the railway line and leads effortlessly to the world-famous health resort of Mürren.
The views across the valley to Wengen, the Männlichenkette mountain range and the Jungfrau group never fail to captivate hikers, and encounters with äsend chamois are not uncommon here.

.

title: Panoramic view between Spiggegrund and Gorneregrund
long_description:
Mountain hiking trail from Spiggegrund/Schwand to Golderli. A varied hike through forests and over alpine pastures to the Aabeberg, which offers a surprisingly beautiful panoramic view. This panoramic ridge forms the dividing line between the deeply incised valleys of the Spiggebach and the Gornerewasser. The ascent and descent are very steep, but short. A pleasant contrast to this are the valley walks along the wild mountain streams. Hard-surface sections near settlements and in the valleys.

A few steps from the Post bus stop in Kiental, the hiking trail branches off uphill from the main road and leads flatly along the edge of the forest into the valley, later climbing more steeply below the Fluh. In the deep ravine, the waters of the Spiggebach roar and rush, and a newly constructed hiking trail follows the rushing mountain stream in the Spiggegrund. Later, the path moves further and further away from the stream and visibly gains height. Shortly before Schwand, the stream is crossed. Now the Aabeberg trail branches off at right angles from the valley route, winds its way up to the houses in many hairpin bends and then climbs through a ravine and forest to Chanzel. The deep view into the valleys of the Spigge and Gorneregrund with their pastures, forests and alps and the panoramic view of the peaks are already overwhelming. Between the light limestone rocks you climb up to the Sennhütte and the highest point of the Aabeberg (to the Golderehorn 10 min; be careful: steeply sloping walls!). You are surprised to find such a gentle, wide alp up here. The alpine dairymen call the rounded grassy hump "dr Näcke" (neck). And what a panoramic view it offers: Northwestwards, peaks and valley incisions form repeating triangular shapes. The melodic triad of the Posthorn sounds up from the Griesalp bends (the steepest post bus route in Europe). Across the valley, the Dünde Falls roar, eastwards the waters of Hohkien thunder down to the valley, and Gspaltenhorn and Blüemlisalp form the crowning end of the valley!
On returning to the ridge saddle at Chanzel, the descent is as steep as on the ascent on the Gornere side. Only in Gälmli are the knee joints spared a little on a short slope traverse, and the trail winds steeply again to Golderli (to Griesalp 10 min; through Griesschlucht, Pochtefall, to Tschingelsee 40 min; via Griesalp-Mittelberg to Hotel Alpenruhe, mountain trail, 1h45). Without crossing the stream, descend along it, cross the little road and turn into the flank of the Gornere on the track, which gradually narrows into a path. Lake Tschingel was only formed in 1972, when a violent thunderstorm blocked the valley floor with 6 m of debris and mud. At the northern end of the lake over the Gornere water and Bir Alperue past the hotel, sometimes to the left, sometimes to the right of the rushing mountain stream via Losplatte back to the village of Kiental.

title: Lower Yosemite Fall (HE)
short_description: An easy and short hiking route leading through a forest with huge redwood trees to a lower and frontal view of the lower Yosemite Falls
long_description:
This hiking route is circular as well as flat and you can get a good view of the lower Yosemite waterfall from below. The strength and flow of water in the waterfall is affected by the melting of snow water and therefore the strength of the flow in the summer months is significantly weaker than in the period immediately after the snow melts. The road to the observation point passes through a shady redwood forest where you can see a number of huge trees as well as wild animals that roam the forest.
Since it is an orderly and relatively wide route, it is accessible and comfortable for walking with strollers.

title: N.A. Nekrasov Museum-Reserve
short_description: Shouldn't we visit Nikolai Alekseevich Nekrasov at his estate in the village of Karabikha, south of the city of Yaroslavl?
long_description: The whole country knows about Nikolai Alekseevich and his famous poem To Whom It's Good to Live in Russia will tell us more about him. But does everyone know that it was in this manor house that he created one of his poems here near Yaroslavl? And who has heard about the estate in the village of Karabikha? Probably not many. Our today's route is to visit the literary man Nekrasov, a great friend of Fyodor Mikhailovich. Perhaps it was here, in Nekrasov's room, that Dostoevsky sat with his admonitions about the still future powers and possibilities of Nekrasov, who is already departing from us.

A short and pleasant hiking route from which there is a great panoramic view of the yellowish Yellowstone Canyon. Due to the fact that this route includes a descent and an ascent of several steps, it is not fully accessible to wheelchairs or strollers. A recommended itinerary for those who want to enjoy a great view of the Yellowstone Canyon in a relatively short walking distance - you can decide according to time and personal ability how many of the scenic points scattered on the boardwalk you want to visit, but if you want to get to the "artist's point" you will have to cross the entire boardwalk - from this point There is a great view of the Yellowstone Falls as well as the Yellowstone River into which they flow.

title: Up the Mountain of Mountains
short_description: The Niesen, the balanced natural pyramid of the Pre-Alps, is rightly considered the most beautiful mountain on Lake Thun. At 2362 m from sea level, it offers one of the most magnificent panoramic views from the edge of the Alps.
long_description:
From the Oey-Diemtigen station, first head inwards into the valley, over the railway line, follow the station grounds out of the valley for a short distance and at the end of the valley, turn off towards Hasli. A path zigzags up over meadows and through forest to Bruchgeeren. The path follows the little Bächlein into the rocky basin of the Geeri formed by the Drunengalm and Fromberghore. After a steep section, you change via the Bächlein to the hut on the Obere Bruchgeerenberg. Continue on the sheep pasture über Pfadspuren direction Felskessel until just below the hut on Unters Geeri and out onto the Bergrippe sloping down from Fromberghore. The view from the edge of the ridge into the Simmental, the Stockhorn chain and the Aare valley to the high hills on the outskirts of Bern is remarkable.
Turning into the Chummli, the western flank of the Niesen dominates the picture, sloping evenly down to the Alpbachgraben. The next two kilometres are flat. Below the impressive Fromberghore north face, the Bettflue, the trail crosses grass, scree slopes and marshy areas and finally reaches the hut on the Obere Stalden (to Bergli-Wimmis 2h20). The destination can no longer be missed. The path winds in wide bends up the evenly sloping pastureland. In the gap between Niesen and Fromberghore, the Doldenhorn becomes visible as the first high alpine peak. Once again the trail turns north to Schafboden (to Ahorni-Wimmis 3h), runs parallel to the ridge in the uppermost part of the ascent and leads past the Berghaus to the viewing terrace on the Niesen. The view is incomparable: countless pre-Alpine and high-Alpine peaks from Titlis to Mont Blanc border the horizon. The view across the Central Plateau and to the Jura, Vosges and Black Forest is just as fascinating as the view down to Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.

images.caption: On the way from Diemtigtal to Hoschüpfen

title: In the Färmel Valley - "on a par" with nature
short_description: Mountain trail to Färmelberg. Very impressive mountain hike high above the Färmel valley on the sunny flank of the Spillgerte group. The Rückweg leads off the road on the valley floor of the Färmeltal along the Färmelbach stream out of the valley. It is rare to find mountain villages that have retained their traditional character so intact. In autumn, when the leaves of the sycamore maples glow golden yellow and a deep blue sky rises above the mountains, the colour palette is complete. Nature trail.
long_description:
From St. Stephan station to the main road and out of the valley to the village of Grodey. Now climb uphill through the Bifang. To the left and right of the road are splendid Simmental huts. Follow the ditch of the Zälgbach stream through the forest and steeply uphill to the fork in the Gandbodewald forest and the first terrace above Gfellweideni.
The view of the Spillgerte group, Albristhubel and Albristhorn, the Lenk mountains and the Bernese Oberland-Waadt border region is magnificent. Almost level path on soft meadow path to Dachbode (after Färmel/Stalde 30 min). The view becomes even more extensive here and extends from the nearby rocks of the Spillgerte inwards through the Fauml;rmel valley, into the Lenk valley floor and into the Wildstrubel-Wildhorn area.
A narrow slope path now runs almost horizontally through spruce stands, scree cones and wide avalanche paths - a delightful hike. For the particularly observant, there is much to discover: orchids in the rock debris, Apollo butterflies in the warm updraft, poisonous aspivipers sometimes in the middle of the path! Climbing through marshy pastureland, you reach the alp Am undere Bluttlig (after Färmel/Büel 45 min). The path now climbs steeply in the direction of Grimmifurggi (crossing into the Diemtigtal) up to the alp Am obere Bluttlig. The effort is rewarded with a wonderful hike through the Färmelmeder (highest point of the tour described): Rauflihorn, Türmlihore, Gsür and Albristhorn impressively close off the basin of the Färmelberg, whose valley floor is reached after a steep descent. This is followed by an exceptionally tranquil valley hike lasting a good one and a half hours. A hiking trail inaugurated in 1994 makes it possible to enjoy this hike away from the road. Over meadowland and through forest, you follow the wild Färmelbach stream. Past the scattered settlements of Färmel/Büel and Stalde, the descent to Matten is quite steep. A hiking trail also allows hikers to walk back to the starting point of the hike in St. Stephan (45 min).

title: Through the Gelten-Iffigen nature reserve
short_description: Enjoyable, but quite strenuous Üübergang from the rear Lauenental über the Tungelpass into the Iffigtal. The scenery along the way is extraordinarily varied: wetlands, alpine meadows, fens, barren rock and scree landscapes, a quiet mountain lake and sparse mountain forest lie along the way. Südlich des Tungelpasses felsige, ausgesetzte jedoch mit Haltseilen gesicherte Wegstrecke. Only at the beginning of the hike a bit of hard surface.
long_description:
Start at the bus stop Lauenen, Geltenhorn. After the Geltenhorn restaurant, ascend along the little Bächlein in the direction of the forest. Via Usseri and Inneri Tüffi you move gently upwards away from the valley floor, where the wide reed beds are striking. Wonderful views of the firns on the Wildhorn, the Geltental and the rock pyramid of the Spitzhorn. At the Gürütschi footpath, you reach the Vorsass junction at pt. 1430, a descent option to the post bus stop at Lake Lauenen. The path now climbs more steeply and zigzags through the rocky slopes of the Holzersflue up to Alp Chandelungel (junction at Pt. 1899 on the left towards Tungelpass). Now the trail continues mostly without a path up to the Stierentungel mountain inn and then in a large curve through the wide Stierentungel alp. The path is almost level as you pass a pronounced fen and reach the Tungelpass. A stone wall marks the border between the districts of Saanen and Obersimmental. The drivers call the pass «Stigellegi». The 700 m high wall of the Niesehorn towers mightily. Head straight for it and enter the lowest band of the Stigle. The path is blasted into the rock and secured with wire ropes. Nevertheless, caution is advisable! Zigzag up to the Stigelschafberg. The flowers in the rock debris and in the rocks along the path are beautiful. Through a rocky hollow you reach the highest point of the hike at 2381 m (to the Wildhornhütte SAC 45 min). Now the Iffigsee, a good 300 m lower, becomes visible, to which you descend over pastures of sheep, marmots and cattle. Shortly after the end of the lake, the trail branches off. The more pleasant variant leads past a pothole and over the panoramic Egge down to the Groppi and over an alpine road on the valley floor to the hospitable Iffigenalp.



.

title: On the Stockhorn-Gantrisch panoramic high trail
short_description: A high-altitude hike with great views on the southern flank of the Stockhorn-Gantrisch range, just above the timberline.
long_description:
After the very steep descent from the panoramic summit of Stockhorn to Baachegg on a good mountain path, there is a much-travelled mountain trail that promises undivided enjoyment. The Stockhorn-Leiterepass panorama trail is rightly considered one of the most beautiful mountain trails in the Alps. Natural path throughout. Round trip tickets available. The trail is closed from Schiterwang during military shooting. The diversion via Blattenheid-Oberwirtneren to the watershed is marked and requires an additional hiking time of 45 min. For information on military shooting, please call 031 324 25 25.

The ascent from the Stockhorn cable car mountain station to the viewing platform on the Stockhorn is short but steep. The panoramic and panoramic views are overwhelming. You can also see the largest part of the high trail to the Leiterepass. From the starting signpost at the panorama restaurant, take the paraglider launching ramp to the edge of the west ridge of the Stockhorn (via the stranded ridge to Oberstocken-Chrindi 1h; caution: climbing sections! Only suitable for experienced mountaineers who are free from giddiness and sure-footed). Here you turn at an acute angle to the north and descend very steeply on a good mountain trail at the foot of the Stockhorn wall to Baachegg and via a pasture path to the Oberi Walalp alpine hut.
Now the actual hut trail begins on the almost continuously steeply sloping southern slope of the Stockhorn-Gantrisch chain. In gentle ups and downs over pastures and through short forest sections, finally passing through a boulder-strewn alley, you reach the terrace of Alp Chuelouenen via Stierenhütte and Äust. Slightly ascending, the path crosses a long succession of harrows and meadows. The botanical diversity is great on these scarcely grazed, sunny steep slopes. Bird species whose main breeding grounds are in the Southern Alps can be observed here. And the scenery is magnificent: over the ridges and humps of the Simmen and Diemtigtal valleys, the chain of the High Alps from the Wetterhorn (left of the Stockhorn) to the Wildhorn is visible. The path runs somewhat more slowly on the flank of the Chrummfaden and Nenenflue between Schiterwang and the Leiterepass (via the Morgetepass to the Untere Gantrischhütte 1h40). A plaque at the top of the pass commemorates the young people from various countries who built the mountain trail in 1972/73.
A wide mountain trail now leads down into the alpine basin of Obernünenen, framed by the mountain flanks of the Gantrisch and the steep slopes of the Nünenenflue. From here, take the road to the post bus station on the watershed (to Gurnigel/Berghaus 30 min).

title: From the Aarelauf to the village of the three Federal Councillors
short_description: A varied hike through beautiful woods, through wide farmland and over panoramic hills to the cosy village of Schüpfen, where the simple village fountain commemorates three important citizens;
long_description:
On the way a unique forest moor, an ancient church and an original inn. Hard surface in the settlements and on the descent from Schüpberg.

In the Middle Ages, a castle and a small town stood above the narrow neck of the Aare loop near Bremgarten. Both were completely demolished by the Bernese in 1298 for reasons of competition. The castle was rebuilt by the Knights of St. John of Münchenbuchsee, but had to make way for the present baroque castle around 1780 (private property). The early Romanesque church, on the other hand, was spared. It is considered one of the most popular wedding churches in the canton.
From the bus stop Bremgarten/Schloss of line 21 to the road junction at the castle and then slightly uphill towards the terrace edge of the Birchi. Take the stairs up to the large walkway.
Looking back, you can enjoy a magnificent view of the town, the Bantiger and the mountains. The protected large moorland pond - the Büsselimoos - in a clearing in the Riederenwald forest is no less enchanting (Pt. 574, to Reichenbach/Fähre 25 min, -Unter Zollikofen 40 min). Passing the magnificent hills of Niderlindach, you reach Kirchlindach, whose very pretty church dates back to the 8th century. Particularly worthy of note are the colourful murals from the 14th and 15th centuries as well as the vicarage (17th century), the oven house (1816) and the vicarage barn in the immediate vicinity. The climb to the Buchsacher farm (to Ortschwaben 40 min; to Meikirch 1h20, -Schüpfen
2h40; to Münchenbuchsee 50 min) is very scenic. A very refreshing forest hike ends at Schüpberg (to Münchenbuchsee 1h10) with a double surprise: the splendid view towards Bucheggberg and Jura and the original inn along the way.
The descent to Schüpfen is unfortunately largely on asphalted road.

short_description: The Via Francigena is one of the oldest pilgrimage routes in Europe, with the holy tombs of Peter and Paul in Rome as its destination. Known primarily as a long-distance hiking trail, this variant can also be cycled.
long_description: The Italian section of the Via Romea Francigena (full name), largely corresponds to the European long-distance cycle route EuroVelo 5. The route presented here, however, is only one variant to enter the historic pilgrimage route in the northwest of Italy.

title: Where town and country shake hands
Heilklimaweg 3: Valentinsweg from Weiskirchen
short_description: Long trail with flat and moderate climbs.
long_description: Via the Valentinsweg, we cross the Schlittenbachtal valley until we reach the district of Konfeld. Here we turn left and follow the path. After crossing a stream, we turn right. Pass a barrier and continue straight ahead. After about 500 m the path climbs. Here it goes uphill until we see a signpost "Hochwaldkliniken". At this sign we turn left and pass a hunting lodge. Further on, we come across another hunting lodge ("Viorel"). Here we take a sharp left turn. Continue straight on until you reach a prominent oak tree. From here we go down to the right until we meet a flagstone path. After about 200 m, we turn left and cross a meadow. On the other side of the meadow, we again follow a flagstone path to the left. At the end of this path, we have to turn right towards the Schlittentaler Bach stream. From here on, we follow the course of the initial feeder trail in the opposite direction.

title: Family trip to the lake and the crystal cabin (Christlessee)
short_description: A short, relatively easy walking route suitable for families that starts south of the pastoral town of Oberstdorf and goes up to the magical crystal lake and the authentic cabin next to it.
long_description: A relatively short linear hiking trail that ascends towards a transparent lake with mesmerizing shades of deep blue/turquoise. The walking route is on a wide asphalt road suitable for walking even with prams (the ascent at the beginning of the route is a bit steep but after a few tens of meters it becomes moderate). Near the lake there is a typical Bavarian cabin that functions as a restaurant serving local food with authentic music playing in the background, next to the cabin there is a small playground. The route is accessible for walking with strollers and is suitable for walking in all seasons of the year.

title: Walk between Lagnes and the Mur de la Peste
short_description: A relatively short walk between the Monts de Vaucluse and the Luberon with the discovery of the village of Lagnes and beautiful panoramas on the heights.
long_description:
The route starts here in the direction of Lagnes on fairly wide but not shaded paths. It is after a good km that we come across denser flora and narrower paths. You then quickly join the discovery circuit giving information on geology, plant dynamics and cultural and cultivation practices. 
You then reach the historic village of Lagnes and the ruins of its ancient castle. You continue again on the discovery trail before gradually climbing to the heights to enjoy magnificent views over the valley.
The return journey takes you to the village of Lagnes and the ruins of its ancient castle.
The return journey is on a more or less stony and maintained path with a view of the Luberon massif on the right.
An interesting starting point for lovers of hikes that allows you to discover the region, its fauna, flora and rich history.

title: On the Felsenweg from Höchenschwand to Waldhaus
long_description:
Start of the hike at the tourist information in Häusern. Recommended: visit to the nature sports centre with the 42 m high Rothaus-Zäpfle tower with viewing plateau and magnificent panoramic view.
Hike through the village along the panorama road to the Kreuzstein hiking car park with barbecue hut. A forest nature trail also starts here. Between the Kreuzstein and the Fohrenbachmühle, hike along the wildly romantic Felsenweg through the largest Bannwald forest in Baden-Württemberg. At a height of 100 to 200 m above the Schwarza valley, the path winds along the steep slope, partly as a narrow path. Some of the narrow paths are additionally secured. Past the water rock with views into the Schwarza valley and the opposite heights with the village of Brenden and varied fauna, the trail leads past the "Harzerhäusle" shelter down to the Fohrenbachmühle mill. This route makes the hiker's heart beat faster.

The Fohrenbachmühle was already mentioned in 1328 and belonged to the Leinegg estate until 1770. In earlier times, the farmers had their grain milled in the mill, today the Fohrenbachmühle is operated as a sawmill.

Here you now have to decide whether you want to hike along the Fohrenbach directly, past the Auhütte and the Flöschbächle, via the Flöschkreuz hikers' car park to the Brauereigasthof Waldhaus and fortify yourself or see variant. From Waldhaus there are good bus connections to Höchenschwand or Waldshut. With the KONUS guest card, all holidaymakers can use the bus and train free of charge.

Note(s)
Recommended: Hiking shoes with a good tread sole, hiking clothing, rain protection.

title: Eidechsspitze
short_description: Scenic mountain tour on the Eidechsspitze in the Pfunderer mountains
long_description: The Eidechsspitze in the Pfunderertal valley is one of the most popular peaks among South Tyroleans: at first moderately difficult, then high alpine, the trail winds through meadows and forests and later exposed to the summit. From Terenten we climb along a rushing mountain stream to the cosy Tiefrastenhütte, then on to the idyllically situated Kompfoßsee and up to the Eidechsspitze via beautiful but challenging mountain trails.

title: An easy trip for families that includes an impressive waterfall, bridges and activity stations in Paneveggio (south of the Dolomites)
short_description: A wonderful hiking route for families in northern Italy with a lot of water passing through a forest with several information and activity stations as well as a suspension bridge overlooking a spectacular waterfall as well as a wooden bridge with glass windows in the floor
long_description:
Here is a circular hiking route that passes through the Paneveggio Gorge in the southern Dolomites. A relatively easy hiking route accessible to strollers where you can enjoy it as part of a family trip, but you can also enjoy it in any other vehicle. Since the route is circular, you can decide for yourself in which direction to walk, but the route marked here first passes through the suspension bridge overlooking the impressive waterfall that descends by several steps, then continues through a forest and towards the end passes over the impressive wooden bridge with glass walls and floors. Along the way in the forest there are explanations (also in English) as well as several activity stations that include binoculars and experimentation with several topics related to trees.
A great hiking route for those looking to experience powerful nature within a short walking distance and easy difficulty.

title: Veados Waterfall to Mambucaba - Gold Trail
short_description: Úfinal stage of the Gold Trail that runs between the Cachoeira dos Veados in the heart of the Serra da Bocaína to Mambucaba in Angra dos Reis
long_description:
The Gold Trail in the Serra da Bocaina National Park, é one of the most traditional mountain walks in Brazil. Situated between Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, this walk é long and challenging, but at the same time not so demanding.  The route é done in 3 days and starts at the entrance of the Bocaina National Park and follows through the preserved Atlantic Forest of the Serra da Bocaina and Mar, until é Mambucaba, in Angra dos Reis. It takes about 6 hours of walking a day and there are several natural and cultural attractions.
On the third stretch of the Gold Trail, you cross the Mambubaba River. One of the most beautiful and historical parts of this stretch are the ruins of the original bridge made of stones in the colonial period. At the lower part of the trail, one can glimpse huge granite walls on the other bank, as well as space to refresh ourselves in the shade of majestic ancient white fig trees.The end of our journey é the “Ponte de Arame”, already close to Mambucaba and the beaches of Angra dos Reis.

title: The big Malsch round near Wiesloch
short_description: On this medium-length hike, we discover the heart and surroundings of the wine village of Malsch.
long_description: The village of Malsch near Wiesloch in the Kurpfalz is known for the quality of its wines. The Letzenberg is the most important vineyard and also one of the main attractions of our hike. On it is the pilgrimage chapel, which was built in 1902 in the historicist style. The heights of the Letzenberg were the destination of annual pilgrimages to St. Wendelinus as early as 1296. A Eucharistic celebration is held here every week on Tuesday evenings. The village of Malsch itself is full of small and large inns, which are often affiliated with the various wineries. In these taverns you can usually get good, inexpensive food and wine in large quantities. They are only open during certain weeks of the year, so you should find out in advance where you can stop and when.

title: From Grünbach around the Mitternacher Ohe
short_description: This tour impresses with the beauty and tranquillity of nature, picturesque river valleys and villages with old farmsteads.
long_description: Our starting point is the chapel at the village square in Grünbach. We follow the village road past the playground in the direction of Abtschlag. Shortly after a left-hand bend, our hiking trail branches off to the right. The hike is very well marked throughout as a circular trail "11". The route leads through a small wood and across fields up to Abtschlag. At the first house we turn left, walk to the road in the village and follow it to the left. At the village exit sign, we turn right onto the gravel path. In the forest, we cross a stream and shortly afterwards turn left at the fork. The path leads steadily downhill in a large curve and becomes a meadow path shortly after a turning area. Here we take a rooty path to the left down into the valley of the Gernbach stream. We finally turn right and walk on a slightly ascending forest path parallel to the stream. We come across a road, turn left and immediately turn left again onto the road to Innernzell. We follow this road for only about 75 m before we turn right and walk parallel to the Bernecker Bach stream. At the first fork, we keep left and the path leads us quite steeply out of the valley until we reach the edge of the forest. A field path with a beautiful view of the Gernbach valley and the Bavarian Forest takes us up to "Ort". At the chapel, we turn left and walk through the hamlet to the road that branches off to Innernzell. Walk along this road past the red deer enclosure to the edge of the forest. Here we change to the forest road to the left. Turn left at a fork in the road. We follow a meadow path across fields, here we have a beautiful view back to "Ort". Finally, we re-enter the forest and walk to the right in the direction of Lungdorf. We walk through the village with pretty houses and a small wooden chapel with a cosy resting place. At the end of the village, we turn left onto the gravel path with paved lanes and hike straight down through a wet meadow area. Just before we reach the Gernbach stream, we follow the markings to the right. Now we continue downhill along the stream until the path seems to end in front of a river. A little to the right of this point we can cross the wide part of the Mitternacher Ohe on a wooden footbridge. But maybe we just want to linger a while at this enchanted place, watch the water and admire the purple-blue aconite growing here. On the other side, the path leads uphill and turns into an asphalt road. At the road junction before Kleinarmschlag, we keep left and follow the road down through the forest. After about 600 m, the signs point us to the left onto a gravel path to the former mill. We cross a bridge and arrive at the old stone-built building. Here we find another pretty wooden footbridge, over which we walk to the other side of the stream and follow the signs to Grünbach. A narrow path leads steeply uphill through the spruce forest. At a junction, we continue uphill and soon reach the edge of the forest. Then we go through the forest for a bit, we step out of the forest and walk to the right on a field path back to Grünbach. In the distance we see Kirchdorf in the forest. We reach Grünbach and can admire some beautiful horses of the Haflinger breed. Then we pass the large, neat farms with the typical round gates and come back to the chapel. There is a hermitage on the outskirts of the village where we can end the hike in comfort.

A great hiking route that includes a panoramic view of the Alps, animals, and a lot of water throughout, all within a very short walking distance. The route is one-way but the round trip takes less than an hour. Parts of the route are shaded and it is largely accessible to strollers. The spaces along the route also allow a comfortable and fun spot to have a picnic along the route.
In the winter months you can watch the lakes when they are frozen, a spectacular sight.
