title: To the midday view over the Iller
short_description: This walk takes us to a magnificent view üover the Iller towards Mittag, Steineberg and Stuiben.
long_description: We follow Bahnhofstrasse to Marienplatz. To the north is Klosterplatz. Behind it on the left we cross the Hauptstrasse. The second street on the left is Gerbergasse. This brings us to the Ach. From the museum of local history we follow Mühlhaldeweg to Tanachstra&szlig. We keep going up to the Hochhäusern. There you can take a footpath to the old people's home. Keeping to the right, we reach the Zollbr cke. We enjoy the magnificent view, the destination of today's tour. On the other bank we follow the curve of the Kreisstrasse. Before the B19 we turn right into the forest path. Along the Bundesstrasse we reach Rauhenzell. Walk through Buchwaldstrasse southwards to Weidachweg. Here we descend to the quarry ponds. Along the south bank we reach the Iller. We cross and keep straight on to the school centre. Alongside the railway line we walk s dw rts to Salzstrasse. Behind the roundabout and St. Nicholas Church we are back at Marienplatz and later through Bahnhofstrasse at the railway station.

title: The Twillbäke Valley near Visbek
short_description: The tour takes us through the idyllic valley of the Twillbäke near Visbek.
long_description: Our hike starts at the town hall in Visbek. There we can get our bearings from an information board. We follow Wildeshauser Straße for a short distance and then turn left into Birkenwald Straße. This takes us to the Lohe road, where we also turn left. At a fork in the road, we keep diagonally to the right, reach the forest and walk to the left along the edge of the forest. Our path meets the Schillmühle path, which we follow to the right. We go through the forest; we leave a field on the left and after a while we reach a crossroads. Here we take the path that branches off from ours at almost a 90° angle. We then reach the edge of the forest, turn right and walk between forest and field in a northerly direction. The path soon leads us into the forest again, where we walk to the right after a few metres and shortly afterwards to the left. On a straight stretch we now alternate between forest and field and we come across the Endel path, which we follow straight on. On the right, you will pass a lake and go halfway round it to the right. After a few metres, we turn right again, keep to the edge of the forest and soon reach the Bullmühle and its ponds. Now we walk in the direction of Siedenbögen, there we turn right and thus come to the Wildeshauser Straße. We leave this to the left, pass the Hubertusmühle and the tennis courts before we get back to the Wildeshauser Straße, which brings us back to the town hall in Visbek.

images.caption: The town hall in Visbek, starting point of our hike.

title: Marktleuthen 2
short_description: This beautiful hike takes us over the Galgenberg and through the Eger valley.
long_description: The circular walk takes us from the market square to the Galgenberg, where we have a wonderful view of the Eger valley and the Kornberg, Epprechtstein and Waldstein. On a clear day we can see as far as Bohemia. We hike through the picturesque Eger valley back to Marktleuthen.

images.caption: Town hall and Protestant church in Marktleuthen, the starting and finishing point of our tour.

title: Around the Hopfensee
short_description: Popular circular hiking trail around the Hopfensee lake with many beautiful views of the Alpine panorama.
long_description:
To reach the lake, pass the sports fields on the right. Behind the wooden bridge over the Rohrweiherbach stream, Lake Hopfensee welcomes us with a resting bench and a fantastic view (1) of the Alpine panorama.
We walk to the right through the reed belt on the wide path, cross the wooden bridge over the Hopfenseeachen and always follow the signs for the "Hopfensee-Rundweg".
  Several benches with beautiful views invite you to take a rest. Behind a shelter (2), the trail enters the forest and continues to the campsite (3) in Hopfen am See.
Here you will find the first bathing opportunity and playgrounds. In the village, the trail leads us along the lively promenade by the lake with numerous refreshment stops for the hiker. We can also make a short detour to the castle ruins.
  Thanks to its shallow water depth, the Hopfensee is one of the warmest lakes in all of Bavaria.
  Besides the lido, surfing, sailing, fishing and a boat hire service, among other things, complement the range of activities on offer around the lake.
The village of Hopfen am See belongs to the town of Füssen and is geared towards spa and recreation with its renowned health resorts, Kneipp sanatoriums and specialist clinic for rehabilitation.
  All treatments for a successful Kneipp cure are offered on site, for example also the public Kneipp treading pool.
  When we reach the lido (4), it is not far back to the starting point of the tour.

images.caption: Many idyllic places invite you to linger.
Right at the beginning of our walk, we look down on Lake Hopfen from the bridge over the Rohrweiherbach stream.
In Hopfen am See a promenade leads along the lake
In Hopfen am See we find numerous leisure activities such as this boat rental.
Our path leads through the reed belt at Lake Hopfen.

title: Views and insights close to the city near Eschwege
short_description: This hike impresses with its often changing landscape formations. The attraction of this tour is not the view from viewing balconies, but the recurring high points that allow a wide view over the entire Werratal.
long_description:
Our hike begins in Eschwege at the tourist information office.
Direction southwest, after 50m turn left directly at the brewery into Klosterstraße. At the end, turn slightly right across Neustadt into the Botanical Garden (002). It is worth taking a tour here.
But take the first path on the right up to Gartenstraße. Cross the street immediately to the left on the pedestrian crossing, turn left again and immediately right into Lagemarckstraße (towards the Federal Police). After just 15 minutes you have escaped the city and walk past the Federal Police accommodation on the left down to Zelchersbach (003).
Continue straight ahead on a narrow asphalt road towards Grothepfuhl (also known as Hepper Heide). At the fork in the road, we continue straight ahead along the gravel/meadow path.
We reach an asphalt road, which we cross and continue along the gravel path opposite through slightly hilly terrain. After a short while we arrive at the glider airfield (004).
Continue past the clubhouse on the asphalt road to the left to the old Friedrichsruh estate (005). Up on the right is the Regener Hütte (006), a symbol of the bond with Eschwege's twin town.
To the right, stay on the asphalt road for a bit, take the first path to the left on a path that leads into the forest (007).
We then walk through beautifully structured field landscape to Oberdünzebach. The Dünzebach babbles beautifully in a low-lying stream bed (008).
The Bierschenk country inn (009) is right next to the beautiful church with a pretty forecourt.
Leaving the church on the right, continue along the asphalt road, cross the Dünzebach stream and turn half-left uphill towards the balloon launch site (010).
Directly behind it, turn left onto a gravel path and follow it to the road, then walk 100 m downhill to the left and then uphill to the right until you reach a hollow. There you keep left and immediately right again on asphalt roads. You reach the connecting road Ober/Niederdünzebach and continue to the right. Walk along the road Am Bache until you reach the bridge railing at the end, turn left, walk to the other side of the road and immediately turn right at the church (011).
The path continues towards Leuchtberge along the right-hand row of houses. It bends down to the right, we take the first field path that joins to the left.
The next field path leading off to the left is the traditional path to the saddle, the incision between the large and small Leuchtberg, but we continue straight on to a bench (012). Directly at the bench, a little-known path leads up to the saddle on the left. We rejoin the wide track, keep to the right and immediately turn right into the forest car park.
Here there are various possibilities to explore the Leuchtberg area. However, we take the wide path uphill to the Schäferhalle junction. Here a level path branches off to the right, which leads us further to Bonifatiusblick (013). We continue along the wide path to the left and turn right at the first opportunity down onto a path. This leads us in serpentines downwards. We disregard the path coming from the right and reach an asphalt road, which we follow upwards to the view of the lakes.
The signposting Rundweg 3 shows us the way down along the path and we pass the Felsenkeller restaurant (014). This is also a popular cyclists' and hikers' meeting place.
We continue along Leuchtbergstraße, pass the rowing house, the anglers' home and the Werra bridge and continue straight ahead along the narrow asphalt path. Continue straight ahead to the Werrabrücke bridge, where you can already see the signs back to the tourist office (015).

title: Crescentia Hiking Trail: Landscape, works of art, inner contemplation - from Kaufbeuren to Irsee
short_description: We walk in the footsteps of St. Crescentia of Kaufbeuren.
long_description: Devotees of St. Crescentia of Kaufbeuren have been able to walk in the footsteps of Maria Crescentia Höß (1682-1744), a nun from Kaufbeuren, since May 2003. The so-called Crescentia Pilgrimage Trail leads from Kaufbeuren through the East and Lower Allgäu to Ottobeuren and Mindelheim and offers a triad of impressions: Allgäu landscape, significant works of art and inner contemplation. The Kaufbeuren-Irsee section is presented here.

images.caption: Near Kaufbeuren we hike through beautiful nature.
Interior of the monastery church in Irsee in Ostallgäu.
The former Benedictine monastery of Irsee in Ostallgäu.

title: Hiking route National Park Maasduinen
short_description: This walking route is 13.3 kilometres and takes about just over 3 hours.
long_description: The Maasduinen nature reserve is the longest river dune belt in the Netherlands. It is a beautiful nature reserve that has evolved over the years. This area was also formed during the last ice age. During your walk, you will pass heathland and fens, and of course through the beautiful forest.

images.caption: The fens of the Maasduinen nature reserve

title: FEB-NAFV Parking Haldertobel-Sennalpe Derp 1:45h
short_description:
Easy hike über lush alpine meadows to the Oberberg alpine dairy and down to the Derp alpine dairy

title: Over the midday to Gunzesried and through Haldertobel
short_description: We enjoy numerous views of Immenstadt, the Allgäu Alps and the Gunzesrieder Tal valley. We then hike through the romantic and lonely Haldertobel.
long_description:
Immenstadt is located at the north-eastern end of the Nagelfluhkette and parts of the town area still belong to the newly created Nagelfluhkette Nature Park. So it is not surprising that we repeatedly come across the typical rock, the Nagelfluh, on the entire tour. Even in the first metres of ascent after the cemetery, we are offered fantastic views over Immenstadt. Further up, we can see the entire Illertal valley all the way to Kempten. From the fork in the path to Alpe Oberberg, we see the Upper Illertal and the Allgäu Alps spread out before us. At Bärenkopf, a plaque points out the last bears in the region that were shot up here. On the descent to Gunzesried, we get to know the fascination of the valley of the same name, where numerous thrillers have been filmed. Above the village, we hike through an old hollow alley, which used to be used by horses to supply the higher alps.
The Haldertobel, through which we descend towards Blaichach, impresses with its flora. Towards the end, we reach the reservoir, which is used by the Bosch company for energy generation.

images.caption: View from the Bärenkopf to the Steineberg.

title: Lake Constance-Königssee Cycle Route
short_description: The Lake Constance-Königssee Cycle Path runs over a distance of 420 km in six stages from Lindau to Schönau am Königssee.

images.caption: Ausgangspunkt des Bodensee-Königssee-Radwegs ist die Stadt Lindau
Staufeneck Castle near Piding in Berchtesgadener Land

title: GR120 - Coastal footpath
short_description: The GR 120, which is just over 200km long, links the Belgian coast with the Baie d'Authie, which forms a natural border with the Somme department.
long_description: Crossing the departments of Nord and Pas-de-Calais, this path runs along the coastline of the Côte d'Opale, offering a diversity of landscapes including dunes, long sandy beaches, dykes, promenades and harbour sites.

images.caption: Aerial view of Cap Blanc-Nez - Côte d'Opale

title: Short Walk with Beautiful Scenery of Odenwaldshule
short_description: Absolutely beautiful short walk through the Harry-Potter-like streets of Odenwaldshule and a refreshing stroll with a perfectly-placed bench, offering you a breathtaking view over the pasture with happy cows and the deciduous forest of the valley
long_description: Short but refreshing walk through the lovely landscape of this beautiful valley.

title: Lake Hiking Tour around Kißlegg
short_description: This easy hike takes us past four picturesquely situated ponds of the Kißlegger Weiherkette.
long_description: From Immenried we walk past the church of St. Ursula via the Hohlgasse and the street "Zur Holzmühle" to the Holzmühleweiher. It is the first of the four ponds we reach on our hike - they are all connected by bog formation. Always following the white-black marking "W22", we continue to Langwuhrweiher. Behind it we turn left and reach the small Hasenweiher. At the fork in the path, we turn left and then immediately left again into the forest. We finally meet the road again, keep left and continue to Brunner Weiher. At Brunner Weiher, we turn left onto a forest path, arrive again at Holzmühlweiher and walk from here back to Immenried.

images.caption: The Langwuhr Pond in the Rain

title: Walk through the Albufera Natural Park
short_description: This is a relatively short walk to discover the essence of this unspoilt area of the Valencian coast: the Albufera Natural Park.
long_description:
Near Valencia, the Albufera Natural Park is the perfect place to escape for a day and reconnect with nature while enjoying the seaside. It consists of a large freshwater lake of more than 2,800 hectares on which you can navigate by borrowing one of the boats.
The park is located in the heart of the region.
Let yourself be guided by the multiple marked routes punctuated by information panels on the fauna and flora (in Spanish and Valencian only)! The itinerary also offers a passage on the beach to dip your feet in ;)

title: Orchid circuit around Külsheim near Tauberbischofsheim
short_description: On this tour through fields, forests and meadows near Külsheim, we can discover 55 orchid species and other protected plants along the way.
long_description: With the Külsheim castle behind us, we walk along Kirchbergweg past the cemetery and continue straight ahead into Uissigheimer Straße, which leads us out of the town. At the next opportunity, we leave the road to the right onto a field path. The area around Külsheim is known for its abundance of orchids. If you look closely, you can discover the exotic-looking plants, which are also native here in Germany, in this intact natural landscape. We take the second path to the left, two crossroads later the path to the right, then again the second path to the left and thus reach the edge of a forest through the fields. There we follow the path into the forest and come to a T-junction, where we take the left option. After a bend to the right, we continue straight ahead for a while, then we reach a four-way intersection, where we take the left option. Behind a field we walk along the opposite edge of the forest on the left, but soon leave it behind us. At the third junction, we turn right, again towards the forest. In the shade of the trees, we follow the path and come across the country road from Külsheim to Tauberbischofsheim. After crossing the road, we turn left parallel to the road for a short distance before turning right into the field at the third opportunity and walking straight ahead. After a while, we pass a piece of forest again. Where the edge of the forest leaves our path, we take the next turn to the left and walk towards the forest. At the first trees, we take the right path, which first leads us along the edge of the forest, then into the forest. There we turn right at the next opportunity and walk straight on until we reach a T-junction. There we turn left and continue straight ahead through the forest. At the second four-way intersection, we orient ourselves to the left, turn right at the next T-junction and come to a fork in the path, where we keep left. On this path we finally leave the wooded area and come back to Külsheim passing the sports field on the left. We come across the country road that we have already crossed elsewhere, follow it for a short distance and then turn right into Wolferstetter Weg. From there we turn right into Haagstraße, then diagonally left along Römerbadweg and via the main road and Uissigheimer Straße back to Kirchbergweg, which takes us back to our starting point at Külsheim Castle. We can stop for a bite to eat in the picturesque old town of Külsheim at the end of the walk.

title: Short Trailrun via Hölzerne Kapelle in Immenstadt i. Allgäu
short_description: Trailrun with waterfalls along the way
long_description: This can be a nice trailrun for beginners. It requires very short time of hard effort and one gets plenty of time to enjoy amazing views with a relaxed pace. I went during a rainy day and ran on wet trails. But it was completely safe. The peak of the trail was almost flat with nice view of other mountain peaks. The trail had waterfalls along the way (when coming down) and it was quite beautiful.

title: On the beach at Warnemünde
short_description: On this tour we experience the wide sandy beach, Warnemünde's landmarks and the forested cliffs with a view of the sea.
long_description: From the old lighthouse in Warnemünde, we walk along the 530 m long pier to the green and white lighthouse (1). From here we have a wide view over the sea and can admire huge freighters and cruise ships leaving the harbour via the Warnow. To the east of the river is the marina with a smart housing estate. To the west, a wooded coastal strip, the Stoltera, slopes steeply down to the sea. Our tour leads in the direction of this nature reserve. We walk along the 150 m wide, slightly curved beach of Warnemünde past colourful beach chairs to the landmarks of the fashionable health resort - the 37 m high lighthouse built in 1898, which can be climbed from May to September, and the restaurant hall with its boldly curved roof. Finally, we pass the high-rise "Hotel Neptun" with its bathing and wellness park and then a row of respectable villas. The beach becomes increasingly narrower and is accompanied by beach forest with tall, bizarre beech trees and cliffs. After about 4 km, a marker points us to the "Wilhelmshöhe" restaurant (2). We turn into the forest area and after about 20 m we can climb the stairs to the inn. From the cliff we can enjoy the view of the sea during a rest. Our path leads us back along the cliff (3) through shore forest. Again and again, viewing platforms open up views over the sea. We walk along the nature trail of the planets. The trees eventually become smaller and more crouched. Then we reach the beach promenade (4), pass the Haus des Gastes and walk straight towards the lighthouse. On Alter Strom and in the parallel street there are small gabled houses that convey the atmosphere of the former fishing village.

images.caption: View of the coastal strip "Stoltera", which is under nature protection.
The old river is the best place to experience the flair of the former fishing village.
The beacon at the end of the long breakwater shows freighters and cruise ships the way to the harbour.
The path leads along the beautifully curved bay with wooded cliff edge.

title: Adventure bus: From Gunzesried through Haldertobel
short_description: Short, leisurely half-day hike through the impressive Haldertobel with a stop at the Sennalpe Derb.
long_description:
Start point of the tour: Gunzesried
Arrival times for pilot ride 1 of the Gunzesried adventure bus: 09:01 am & 11:17 am
Tour end point: Blaichach (Bosch) 
Departure times for pilot trip 1 of the adventure bus Blaichach (Bosch): 13:06 & 15:53
  Note: This tour was developed for the pilot test within the project "Flexible Adventure Bus for Sustainable Leisure Transport (FEB-NAFV)". It is therefore tailored to the timetable and stops of the adventure bus, which is currently not yet öffentlich verkehrenden. If you are interested in participating in a future pilot project in general, please contact us via research@outdooractive.com.

title: Round the Schliersee
short_description: Whether in, on or around the lake: this easy hike allows us to experience and enjoy Schliersee in a variety of ways.
long_description: From Schliersee station we walk down to the lake. We follow the white signpost with the black ship. Shortly after the Kurzentrum (1), we turn right into the Kurpark. We keep to the red signs "Schliersee Kurweg". At the end of the Kurpark, we turn left at the boat rental (2) and continue from there to the Schlierach. Cross the Schlierach and continue to the left, always following the green sign "Kurweg rund um den See - K1". We stroll along the lake on Westerbergstraße until we reach Fischhausen. We keep passing small barbecue areas (3) and bathing beaches (4). From Fischhausen we follow the red signs "Schliersee Kurweg" back to Schliersee. Shortly after entering the village, we pass a forest playground (5). From here we walk on to the boat landing stage (6) and finally back to our starting point.

title: Mittag up and down from immenstadt
short_description: Starting point is the bottom of the Mittagbahn. We follow the official hiking signs for one kilometer through the forest! Then the scenery opens up and we cross some fields. From There on there is a s shaped hard road for bikes and in parallel a walking path through the forest. After reaching the Rathaus am Mittag we continue a stony road passing some small alpine houses. Finally we reach the top where the Mittagbahn Bergstation is.

images.caption: Mittag up and down from immenstadt

title: Hiking near Lake Tarnița with ascent to Piatra lui Lucaci
short_description: A moderate, marked circuit that runs along Lake Tarnița, climbs to the Piatra lui Lucaci viewpoint, and returns fairly gently through the forest to the starting point.
long_description:
The reason for the popularity of this route is perhaps that many people are attracted by the beauty of the landscape at the viewpoint.
The walk on the route next to the lake is similar to a stroll. Interesting views of the water open up at some points and you can admire the cottages on the other side. The path has slight ups and downs, but nothing prepares the hiker for the strenuous climb to Piatra lui Lucaci. The dense forest provides shade and can offer shelter in case of rain.
The climb to the viewpoint takes 15-20 minutes, depending on your pace, and is very steep. But the effort is amply rewarded by the beautiful view of the greenish peaks of the Gilău-Muntele Mare mountain range.
For the continuation of the circuit, you climb for another 10 minutes or so through the forest. On the plateau, a view of the Turda Gorge opens up. The second part of the trail leads almost exclusively through the forest without offering anything spectacular, changing from a path to an ATV or cart track. You eventually reach the same point where you started.

images.caption: Potecă deasupra Pietrei lui Lucaci, spre Agârbiciu
Încă vreo 3km până la barajul Tarnița

title: Lake Louise Lakeshore Trail
short_description: This is an easy, short and flat hiking trail, which leads along the beautiful Lake Louise Lakeshore.
long_description:
The hiking trail on Lake Louise’s promenade is suitable for those who want to enjoy a panoramic view of the lake on a leisurely walk suitable for every level. This is a one-way route that is also suitable for walking with buggies and the whole family. It is well worth walking the entire boardwalk (about 2.5 miles) as the other side of the lake is shallow, different and exciting.
As this is a one-way trail, you can return whenever you want to by following the exact same route back to the trailhead.

title: Mooswald Tour in Freiburg
short_description: This Nordic walking trail leads through the Freiburg Mooswald. In the forest area close to groundwater, you pass canals and small weirs.
long_description: We start at the Wolfswinkel forest car park, leave the forest playground on the left and walk along the airfield (1) up the Wolfsbuck (2) to a road. Cross the bridge and walk through the forest to the "Große Richtstatt" (3). Here we walk to the right. At the next fork, keep to the left. An interesting alternative at this point is to continue along the "Langer Damm". But we follow the path until it bends to the left. Here a dirt road branches off to the right and we continue on it. At a T-junction, we keep left until our path meets a well-maintained path. Here we continue to walk on the left. Immediately afterwards, another path branches off to the left. We follow the so-called canal path (4) over a bridge to the "Große Richtstatt". Now we walk to the right until we reach the city embankment (5), where we walk to the left back to the forest playground.

title: Wildalm-Runde
short_description: Challenging tour along the Sinterbach to the managed Wildalm and back past the Luegeggalm.

title: Katharina Wall Route around Alzey Schafhausen
short_description: This medium-difficulty route takes us around the Alzey district of Schafhausen.
long_description:
We start walking at the Schafhausen starting point. From the car park we walk along the Selz river for a while. Then the Katharina Wall Route takes us to the vineyards of Schafhausen. We should take a break on the "Galgenber" and enjoy the magnificent view of the Alzeyer Land. Past the "Trinkbare Landschaften" vineyard, the trail leads us back to the starting point.
Schafhausen, the oldest district of Alzey, was first mentioned in 897 AD. Viticulture has played a major role here for hundreds of years. The products of the winegrowers can be sampled and tasted throughout the village.

images.caption: The landscape around Schafhausen is an old wine-growing area.

title: Bivio - La Motta - Pra Miez - Dam
Family Friendly Hiking Near Lake in Immenstadt
short_description: Short hiking route near an Am Kleinen Alpsee in immenstadt
long_description: Am Kleinen Alpsee is nice place for short walk in immenstadt. The starting point of this route can be reached by city bikes, bus or car. If you are interested then you can enjoy here lunch and swimming. You can go for cycling also.

title: Bivio - Stallerberg - Juf
short_description: Hike from the village of Bivio on the Julier Pass up to Juf, the highest settlement in Europe that is inhabited all year round.
long_description: The destination of this hike is Juf, the highest, year-round inhabited settlement in Europe at 2117 metres above sea level. The trail leads from Bivio via Stallerberg to Juf. It is the link between Bivio and the German-speaking area, as the entire Avers Valley was settled by German-speaking Walsers.

title: Wangen - Around Primisweiler
short_description: The trail takes us mostly along field, forest and meadow paths and only only short stretches of asphalt around Primisweiler.
long_description: The trail leads us mostly on field, forest and meadow paths and only on short stretches of asphalt around Primisweiler. The Argental valley is touched as well as the Blausee and Mittelsee lakes. The ascent out of the Argental with magnificent views of the other side of the valley characterises the trail as "easy to moderately difficult". Sturdy footwear is strongly recommended.

images.caption: Blue Lake is the name of this gem.
The natural bathing lake "Blausee" is on our way.

title: Summit tour from Wertach to the Grünten
short_description: This physically demanding tour takes us to the Grünten, the "guardian of the Allgäu". At the top we are rewarded with a fantastic view.
long_description: Starting at the Starzlach in Wertach, we hike via the Kimmerle Alpe and the Vordere Kölle Alpe (refreshment stop) to the Grüntenhütte. From here it is a small but steep climb to the Jäger monument and the summit. Directly at the summit it is rocky, so you should have good shoes and be sure-footed and free from vertigo.

images.caption: A fantastic view from the Grünten is reward for the effort of the ascent.

title: Ådalstinden Øvre Stordal
short_description: Super Hike from Seljebotn to Ådalstinden (1433) and down the other side to Langsætrane. The trip can of course be taken up and down from both places.
long_description: From the trailhead by Seljebotn Gård follow the tractor road until you see a sign to Valldalsetra. From here you will see the markings (red DNT signs) until you reach the tree limit. From here the path is unmarked but fairly easy to follow.

images.caption: fotturer i Møre og Romsdal: Ådalstinden i Øvre Stordal

title: Walking tour near Altreichenau
short_description: This walking circuit leads us first on a level railway track that has been converted into a hiking trail - on the second half it gets sporty thanks to short climbs.
long_description: South of the parish church, a path by the cemetery leads eastwards to the Adalbert Stifter cycle path. We walk along the former railway line for about 2 km and pass beautiful views. At a Jesus cross, we cross an asphalt path. In the valley we cross the Brennerbach stream, then our path leads uphill and with several changes of direction through the forest, we follow the "Nordic Walking Round 2". We cross the Brennerbach a second time and now have to tackle some very steep ascents. The signs finally lead us back to the Adalbert Stifter cycle path in Altreichenau. Here we turn right until we see the Catholic parish church and leave the hiking trail.

images.caption: At Pleckenstein, the "Nordic Walking Trail 2" branches off from the Adalbert Stifter Trail.
After the second crossing over the Brennerbach, we are faced with the steepest section of the trail.
The path leads us only slightly uphill out of Altreichenau.
We start our Nordic walking tour at the Catholic parish church.
The path along the former railway line offers a variety of views.

title: Barefoot hiking trail through the Hohe Fläming Nature Park near Bad Belzig
short_description: The almost 9-kilometre-long barefoot hiking trail near Bad Belzig takes us through the Hoher Fläming Nature Park and allows us to feel nature up close under our feet.
long_description:
The trail was opened in 2015 and is well signposted. We only have to follow the signs with a large footprint. It is a normal hiking trail that has been tested for its suitability for bare feet. But with or without shoes, we enjoy a beautiful landscape.
If we decide to walk barefoot, we can expect a variety of surfaces on the trail, from soft moss to meadows to warm sand.
Besides the liberating feeling of walking barefoot, the path offers us other advantages: We strengthen our circulation, ensure good blood flow and strengthen our foot muscles. If you are walking without shoes, you should definitely plan more time (about 3 hours in total).

title: Four-day trip through three countries and around Lake Constance
short_description: "When I see the lake, I don't need the sea anymore!" This saying probably best sums up what it means to vacation at Lake Constance. In fact, you pass through three countries during one bike tour: Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

title: In the Odenwald from Schriesheim to Heidelberg in the Neckar Valley
short_description: Our Odenwald tour from Schriesheim to Heidelberg offers a good mix of fresh forest air, imposing ruins from ancient times and beautiful views of the student city of Heidelberg.
long_description:
The wine town of Schriesheim lies at the end of the Schriesheim Valley in the Neckartal-Odenwald Nature Park. Schriesheim's landmark is the Strahlenburg, which rises above part of the old town. The present-day ruin became famous mainly because Heinrich von Kleist included it in a romantic scene of the knightly play "Das Käthchen von Heilbronn" from 1810. In this scene, the Kräthchen confesses her love to Count Wetter at the Strahlenburg.
We continue hiking uphill through secluded forests to the Weißer Stein inn - this stage will be the most strenuous part of our tour, so we rest at the inn and enjoy coffee and cake. From here it's downhill and we have more sights to look forward to.
Only the remains of the foundations of the old St Michael's Monastery on the Heiligenberg in Heidelberg remain today. The monastery was founded as early as the 9th century as a branch monastery of the Lorsch Monastery, but was abandoned in the 16th century. The ruins offer us a beautiful photo opportunity.
Not far from the Michaelskloster is the Thingstätte, which we should not miss under any circumstances. Built by the Nazis between 1934 and 1935, it strongly resembles a Greek theatre and was originally intended as a propaganda stage. But the Nazis quickly lost interest in the colossal structure after they discovered radio, which had become widespread, for their propaganda. Nowadays, the facility is used for open-air concerts and other events.
As we continue on our way towards Heidelberg, we pass the Bismark Column, which was built on the Heiligenberg in 1903. The name goes back to a competition held by the student body in 1899. The competition aimed to erect as many fire columns as possible, as one can be found on this tower.
In Heidelberg itself, it is of course worth taking a walk through the beautiful old town with its cosy alleyways, as well as heading up to the castle, taking a look at the Heiligengeistkirche and walking across the old Neckar Bridge. From Heidelberg's main railway station we can comfortably depart again.

images.caption: The Kanzelbach in the old town of Schriesheim

title: Red Round Waldmünchen
short_description: This beautiful loop takes us through the forest at the foot of the Cerchov on ground steeped in history and offers a few surprises.
long_description: We walk from the information board to the left into the forest. At a fork there is a beautiful lime tree with a bench. Shortly afterwards we reach the charcoal pile, which is operated for demonstration purposes. At the next fork we pass a nice place to rest. We can also rest here by the stream on the way back. The path later meets an asphalt road, which we follow to the right for a short while and then turn directly to the right. As we learn from an information board, the Austrian mail line used to run here. After a long climb, we now turn right onto a narrower path. The trail now leads well signposted through the forest. On the left side of the path is a nice resting place at a spring. Soon we reach the outward route and walk back the way we came.

images.caption: The former Austrian court mail line.
In this part of the route we walk along the former Austrian court postal line.
Beautifully situated site by the stream with mill wheel.
At the beginning of the trail we walk on a wide forest path.
This plaque informs us about the Austrian court mail line that used to run here.
The charcoal kiln gives an insight into how charcoal burning used to be practised in this region.

title: Hochschwarzwälder Hirtenpfad
short_description: The 8 km long premium hiking trail "Hochschwarzwälder Hirtenpfad" leads along flowering meadows and sparse forest edges around the typical Black Forest hamlet of Raitenbuch.
long_description: Our hike begins on the Raitenbucher Höhe and leads us along meadow and forest paths. We reach the valuable Urseemoor and catch a magnificent view of Lenzkirch. We descend into the Urseetal, cross the Stoffelbächle stream and follow the path in the high forest uphill again to Zinsmoos. We pass the rest area at the Alter Ahorn, where we treat ourselves to a break. We then hike along the sun path above the high pastures until we reach the highest point of the tour and return to the starting point a short time later.

title: Along the Rosenweg near Weilheim
short_description: This Nordic walking tour requires fitness and technique, but compensates with a panorama as far as the Swiss Alps.
long_description: Our starting point is at Weilheim town hall. The Rosenwanderweg leads us down into the Haselbachtal (1). Via the Mittelweg (red rhombus), we walk steadily uphill in the direction of Nöggenschwiel and reach the Wasserfall junction. We leave the Rosenwanderweg for the time being and take the Mittelweg through the Heubachtal valley to Heubach (2). Above the hamlet, the Mittelweg joins the district road at the Apollonia Chapel (3). The road leads to the rose village of Nöggenschwiel. At the Roseneck (4), turn right along the Rosenweg to the Hohfluhfelsen. Via a gorge path through the Schwarza valley we reach the Ziegelgraben (5). We descend to Schnörringen via scenic meadows and a beautiful forest path. Via the Schnörringen wayside cross, a driveway leads us over the Geisberg to the Fridolin Chapel Dietlingen (6). Take the scenic high trail along the connecting road back to Weilheim.

images.caption: You need to be fit and sure-footed at the waterfall.

title: Hiking route Texel National park
short_description: This route leads you through the nature reserve on Texel.
long_description: During this route, you will walk through the dunes and the beach of Texel.

title: Around the Bichelstein near Hengersberg
short_description: On beautiful forest paths we get uphill to a plateau near Oberaign and with a view of the Deggendorf plain via Kerschbaum back again.
long_description: Our tour begins at the car park with information boards. We follow the black signs with curved arrow for the "Haas-Fertigbau-Trail" and walk uphill along the road, out of the village. We follow a forest path through the forest to an information board about heart rate measurement and strengthening exercises. At a second board, a narrow, steep path leads us to a plateau. We cross the mountain meadow with a view of the Brotjacklriegel and meet a road. It leads us past a farm on the left. With a wonderful view over the hilly country, we walk on to Kerschbaum. At the entrance to the village, we turn right onto the gravel path that leads us past an old farm into the forest. We reach a pilgrimage chapel and return to Grattersdorf.

title: Dolomites High Altitude Trail 3
short_description: Challenging, panoramic high-altitude trail with impressive high-mountain scenery throughout from Villabassa in the Puster Valley to Longarone in the Italian province of Belluno.
long_description: The Dolomites High-Altitude Trail No. 3, like trails 1, 4 and 5, represents a crossing of the eastern Dolomites. However, the crossing takes place next to the eastern main ridge, so that large differences in altitude must be expected between the individual stages. Ten days should be expected for the ascent of the "Way of the Chamois". The high-altitude route places high demands on its walkers - this includes very good orientation skills, but also a high degree of strength, endurance and surefootedness. Some of the high-altitude trail has exposed via ferratas and free climbing passages (up to level II difficulty). Special features of the High Altitude Trail No. 3 are its contrast between the lonely mountain world and the hustle and bustle of the tourist destinations, as well as the often appearing evidence of the First World War. The trail crosses or touches the characteristically quite different Dolomite groups such as the Braies Dolomites, Sorapiss Group, Marmarole, Pelmo-Rite and Bosconero Group.

title: Loop in Quiberon between wild coast and port
short_description: This beautiful walk allows you to explore the interior of the peninsula through sandy paths and wild coastline to the port of Quiberon.
long_description:
We propose to start this walk from the interior of the land near Kernavest. You set off in a westerly direction. You soon come across the Locmaria Tower, an old maphore. It is in fact the highest point of the peninsula. 33m. Climb the tower and enjoy a 360° view!
From the tower you gradually reach the coast and then walk along the wild coast towards the south. The views are magnificent over the ocean and Belle-Ile en Mer. The coast is chiselled and rocky.
The road is very long and winding.
Once in Quiberon, you can enjoy the sandy beaches and the many small restaurants, before heading back north through small residential streets and then paths.

title: Trail to Pedra do Sino in Teresópolis
short_description: Climb to the highest point of the Serra dos Órgãos, with 2,275 meters of altitude. The view from Pedra do Sino é is spectacular, being possible to contemplate the mountain ranges of the Serra, the Guanabara Bay, the city of Rio and part of the Paraíba Valley.
long_description:
The trail to Pedra do Sino é considered a classic of Brazilian mountaineering and can be done in 1 or 2 days, with overnight stay at the Shelter 4. Places to stay overnight at the Shelter or in the camping area must be booked in advance on the site or at the Park gate, as well as the purchase of tickets.
This é the most famous route from the Teresópolis headquarters of the Serra dos Órgãos National Park, which was created in 1939 and é one of the most famous and visited conservation units in the country´s.

title: Kiziluzum - Nif Mountain Summit
short_description: Nif Mountain is always on the list of nature lovers in Izmir. This route, which starts from Kızılüzüm, reaches the summit of Nif Mountain and provides the same route again
long_description:
Nif Mountain, one of the 19 mountains named Olympus in ancient Greece, is of great importance for nature and mountaineering enthusiasts. Located in Vişneli Köyü east of Körfez, this moist mountain is 1510 m high and dominates the Kemalpaşa province of Izmir.
There are many alternative routes for those who will climb to the summit of Mount Nif. Of course, the mountain region comes with its difficulties. It is recommended to be careful whichever route you take.
This route starts from Kızılüzüm and goes up to the summit of Nif Mountain and then back down to Kızılüzüm using the same nature trail. It is a very long and difficult route. It is not recommended to do this route unless you are an experienced hiker or mountaineer.
Nif Mountain, known for being close to the sea, has a wonderful natural texture. Depending on the season, it reveals unique landscapes dominated by green or white.

title: Three imposing peaks - the Iseler, the Kühgundkopf and the Kühgundspitz
short_description:
The 1876-metre-high Iseler lies south of Oberjoch, between Bad Hindelang and the Tannheim Valley. From the village of Oberjoch, you only have to climb 700 metres to the summit. It is a beautiful panoramic trail with great views from the Iseler summit over a narrow, exposed ridge path to the Kühgundkopf. Further along the ridge we hike along the German-Austrian border from the Iseler over the Kügundkopf and the Kühgundspitz. 
These 3 peaks with magnificent mountain panorama are unforgettable. Kühgund traverse dangerous in the wet, not recommended. 
Info: a mountain railway runs from Oberjoch to an altitude of 1550 metres.

title: To the Neuenfels Ruin near Buggingen
short_description: This tour takes you through the woods and vineyards of the MarkgrÃ?ferland. Starting from the tranquil winegrowing community of Muggardt, you walk through old forests up to the Neuenfels ruins.
long_description: We start our tour at the car park before the village of Muggardt at a triangle of paths under an old lime tree. From there we follow a farm track, the Obermattenweg, straight uphill. From this path we soon turn right onto a small path, the „Bettlerpfad“, and follow the yellow dot marking/the black „X“ in the direction of Badenweiler/Schwärze. After a small dip and a small counter-ascent along the edge of the forest, we hike into the forest. But before that, it is worth taking a look back, as the beautiful panorama of the foothill zone is on offer. At the end of the „Bachmattweg“, which we are now walking along, we turn right onto a wide forest path and follow the geological nature trail (1), which is marked with informative signs. At the end we reach a small hill, the so-called „Schwärze“ (2). From there we have another opportunity to enjoy the view. Now we walk back a few steps on the forest path we came from until we reach a path marked with a „Z“ and „N“, which first leads along a stream up to the Neuenfels ruin. After a cut in the terrain, the path joins a wide forest path, the Neuenfelser Weg. Follow this and orientate yourself to the left by the markings „B2“/orange. Uphill, a branching path soon leads us to the ruin. After about an hour we reach Neuenfels Castle (3), built around 1250, which was the seat of the knightly dynasty of the same name until the 16th century. Thanks to extensive renovation work, the castle has been accessible again since 1995. From the high castle walls there is a magnificent view of the Markgrindel region with the Kastellberg and the tranquil wine villages of Ballrechten, St. Illgen and Betberg. On clear days, the view reaches as far as the Münsterberg of Breisach and further into Alsace. A panorama board helps us to find our way. After the detour to the castle, we return to the path and continue towards Sulzburg. Soon we meet a wide forest path where we turn right. We follow this path along the slope through a few bends. This path later joins a forest path where we continue to the right. We hike downhill to the edge of the forest. There, the far-reaching Bäume and the beautiful view invite you to take a break. We then continue – without marking - into the vineyards, where we meet the Markgräfler „Wii-Wegli“ (4) below, the course of which runs through Muggardt and the surrounding vineyards. We follow the markings with the red rhombus and the yellow grape on the left. The Rückweg to Muggardt leads us through idyllic vineyards. The sun-drenched Muggardter Südhang is known for its exquisite wines. The course of the path is clear, the „Wii-Wegli“ finally leads sharply to the left, through a small forest, uphill into the next vineyard. We pass an old vineyard dating from 1766, hike around a mountain ridge, pass through the tranquil village of Muggardt and finally return to our starting point. We also recommend a visit to one of the numerous small village festivals that take place from spring to late summer. Particularly worthy of mention is the Muggardter „Harzchabbe Fescht“.

images.caption: A magnificent view can be enjoyed from the Neuenfels ruins.

long_description: The trail leads through the Fulltorfta recreation area, across the Kvesarumsån River and past the Hanakällan spring. The route continues over a hill and through a bog where carnivorous plants grow. Today's destination is the campsite Ekeröd, where we can marvel at some stone circles of a prehistoric burial ground;

title: Through the Madonnenländchen near Külsheim
short_description: Pleasant and panoramic hike from Külsheim Castle over the Stahlberg and through the idyllic Madonnenländchen.
long_description: We start our hike at Külsheim Castle. The first castle in Külsheim was built around the year 1000 by the bishops of by the bishops of Würzburg. The current castle dates from the from the 12th century, but is marked by reconstruction work in the 16th and 17th centuries. and 17th centuries and today houses the town administration. On our way through the "Madonnenländchen" we pass a Marian grotto and enjoy magnificent views of the Tauber valley and the Külsheim heights from the Stahlberg.

images.caption: We hike on pleasant paths through Madonnenländchen.

title: Via Transilvanica - Terra Banatica
short_description: The last but one leg of the Via Transilvanica route passes through the enchanting mountainous Banat micro-region, crossing the Semenic - Caraş Gorges National Park and passing by the edge of two other national parks.
long_description:
This leg covers only Caraş-Severin county, which makes it an excellent opportunity to fully explore the area.
Some stages of the route are, according to the official guide, shorter. Especially in the first days, you enter several former industrial cities, an opportunity to notice their evolution after the closure of the steel factories till the present day.
Given the small gradient of most trails along the route, less active trekkers have a good chance of actually finishing most trails on the route. And if you dare to try this route by mountain bike, the distances will seem even shorter!
Among the attractions along the way are the Caraș Gorges, the Izvoarele Nerei UNESCO reserve, the Comarnic Cave, the Croatian village of Carașova, Poiana Mărului lake & meadow, Gozna or Trei Ape lakes.

Caraș Gorges, Anina Mountains - Iabalcea plateau

title: From Steibis to the Eineguntkopf
short_description: The Eineguntkopf (also called Rohnehöhe) is 1,639 m high and is ideal as a beginner mountain, or to start the touring season.
long_description: This snowshoe tour to the Eineguntkopf leads us to typical Allgäu Nagelfluh rocks, as they can also be found at the Hochgrat only 5 km farther east. The tour to this peak is particularly suitable for beginners, as the ascent and descent route are on predominantly wide, never steep meadows and pastures in southern orientation.

title: Tour of Legoland Germany in Günzburg
short_description: Full-day tour for the whole family
long_description: On this tour we experience the most beautiful attractions in Legoland Germany in Günzburg. We will travel to Venice, Neuschwanstein and Munich, to the land of knights, to the land of adventure, to the land of pirates with Mini-Sea-Life and have fun in the Lego x-treme area.

title: The Oleron path
short_description:
The Chemin d'Oléron is a hiking trail inaugurated in July 2023, offering a loop of just over 100 km around the island of Oléron.
This coastal route allows hikers to discover the island's diverse landscapes, including dunes, beaches, forests, vineyards, salt marshes and picturesque villages.
long_description:
The route can be divided into 5 stages of 18 to 25 km, or 7 stages of 11 to 19 km, depending on the hiker's preferences and level. It is advisable to plan your itinerary according to your ability, and to book accommodation in advance, especially during peak tourist periods.
Notable sites along the way include the Chassiron lighthouse, the Château-d'Oléron citadel, the port of La Cotinière, as well as views of Fort Boyard and the Moëze-Oléron reserve. The trail also crosses protected natural areas, offering an authentic experience of the island.
The Chemin d'Oléron is reserved exclusively for hikers; bicycles and other two-wheelers are not permitted on this route. Cycle and bridle paths are available elsewhere on the island for cyclists and horse riders.

title: Over hill and dale through Bruck and Brech near Alfdorf
short_description: This tour first takes us along the Limes hiking trail to the Bemberlestein. Then we hike through the Götzenbach valley and over the Schelmenklinge and return to Pfahlbronn via the villages of Bruck and Brech.
long_description: Along the Limes hiking trail, we repeatedly encounter remains of the Limes and its watchtowers. There are thematic panels at these stations, about the Romans and their impressive border system. Our path leads through the typical forest landscape in the Knollenmergel and Stubensandstein. On the On the Liassic plateau we enjoy the far-reaching view of the Swabian Alb.

title: From Tann to Dermbach - Rhön
short_description: From idyllic Tann, this stage of the Hochrhöner leads us through a hute forest and over the Gläserberg to Dermbach.
long_description:
Our hike starts in the middle of the town of Tann at the town gate. The town gate is the real landmark of the town, because the massive building from the 16th century immediately catches the eye of every visitor to the town. Inside - in the so-called Wachtstube - there is a small and very interesting exhibition that informs about the history of Tann. We walk off in a northerly direction to the market square.
The old town of Tann is small, but worth seeing. Within a few metres of the market square you will find the open-air museum Rhöner Museumsdorf, next to it the Tann Nature Museum, the three castles (the Blue, the Red and the Yellow Castle), which are not individual buildings but form an overall complex. And of course the half-timbered buildings, the Elf-Apostel-Haus being particularly noteworthy here.
The Marktstraße turns into the Steinweg and at the fork in front of the head we continue on the Friedhofsweg. At the end of this road we turn right into "Am Rothenhauck". As soon as this path describes a right-hand bend, we go straight on. From here, the Hochrhöner climbs back up to the Hesse-Thuringia border. The hiking trail follows a former GDR flagstone path southwards. We pass the Dietgeshof apple wine tavern into the Tann-Dietgeshof and the Tanner Hute. This panoramic plateau northeast of Tann has served as pastureland since time immemorial.
We follow the signs for the "Hochrhöner" hiking trail (an "Ö") in the direction of
Andenhausen. Shortly before the village, at the fork, the western route of the Hochrhöner meets the eastern route again. The road goes around the Katzenstein, which offers views of the baroque Zella Monastery. A barracks of the GDR border guards is left to decay. Across meadows, the route heads towards the Arnsberg. At the edge of the forest, the Hochrhöner turns right into the valley, only to ascend immediately on the opposite slope in a right-hand curve to the Waltersberg. A sharp bend brings the hikers to the Rhönklub hut on the Gläserberg. The Gläser offers a wonderful panoramic view; on a good day you can see not only the Hochrhön but also the Hohe Meißner and the Thuringian Forest. On the steep descent to Dermbach, a surprise awaits in the forest: vertical limestone cliffs under which the Hochrhöner runs.
The Hochrhöner does not lead us directly into Dermbach, but we simply walk on to the centre of the village and can treat ourselves to a little refreshment at the end of our tour.

Please note: The path through the impressive rocky area above Dermbach should only be walked in good weather. In wet or even icy conditions, there is definitely a risk of falling, as the path winds very narrowly around the rocky precipices.
Tip for Hochrhöner hikers: The trail over the Dermbacher Klippen is an exciting alternative to the main trail over the Staudtblick. Length: 0.3 km / approx. 5 min walking time (one-way). At the end of the section, at the Fatima Chapel, you will find the last path symbols ("Ö" ) at a fork.

images.caption: Fountain with typical regional half-timbered house in the background.
The Renaissance town gate of Tann was built in 1557.

title: History of Stadtsteinach
short_description: The trail leads us along the Steinach into the idyllic Steinach valley, past the Nordeck castle ruins and back again on the other side of the stream.
long_description: On this hike we learn a lot of interesting facts about the history of Stadtsteinach. After passing the chapel at the Partheimühle, the oldest building in the town of Stadtsteinach, we hike to the Salem spa clinic. The buildings were The buildings were formerly used as a poster recreation centre, later as Federal Border Guard and Bundeswehr barracks. Via the Steinachkanzel vantage point we reach the Nordeck castle ruins. Built on a rocky spur The castle, built on a rocky spur, was used by the diocese of Bamberg to secure the borders and supply roads in the Steinach valley. In a deed of sale from the year 1151, the castle was first mention of it in connection with the town of Stadtsteinach. It was destroyed destroyed in 1552 during the Peasants' War. The traditional cutting mill, which we finally pass, is still used for woodworking, and opposite is the former mining and metallurgy office. The Franconian Forest area was home to numerous ironstone and copper mines. copper. Ore mining ceased in autumn 1834.

title: Walk through the Swiss Pine Park at Hochzeiger
short_description: Leisurely stroll through the newly created ZirbenPark on the Hochzeiger in the Piztal valley
long_description: The Swiss stone pine, also known as Swiss stone pine, is a tree of the high Alps, where it is mainly found in the function of a protective forest. From June 2015, a newly created adventure trail will lead from the middle station of the Hochzeiger cable car through a small section of the forest and will delight hikers young and old with its various visual and hands-on stations.

title: Hirschberg
short_description: This tour takes us first past the Polite café through the Hirschbach ravine. Then we hike up the Kräherwand to the Hirschberg, before we hike back to Bad Hindelang via the Steinköpfle and through the Zillenbach­tobel.
long_description:
This hike is not to be underestimated. Even though it is only about 8 km long, you still climb almost 750 metres of altitude. In the Hirschbach and Zillenbach gorges we experience beautiful nature and from the 1456 m high Hirschberg we can enjoy a magnificent view. The Polite café offers us a place to stop along the way, where we can fortify ourselves.
If you would like to hike a little longer, you can make a detour from the Hirschbachtobel to the Hirsch-Alpe and then continue the route as described above.

title: Singers' Meadow Nature Trail around Buttlar
short_description: We walk along the beautifully designed nature trail through a magnificent landscape.
long_description: We follow the signs of the nature trail. The path is well marked up to the Singers' Meadow. The marker sign is a fox. We enter the forest via the Pfarrlinde and soon reach the first information board. At the display on red deer, a rest area invites you to take a break. We reach the Sängerwiese meadow. At the crossroads behind the refreshment stop, we walk past the Park of the Trees of the Year to the left. At the following T-junction we go right, at the next junction left. We take the first path to the left and reach the forest, where the path branches three times. We choose the middle path and walk until we reach a junction where we turn left. The path leads us out of the forest along the Hubengraben to Buttlar.

title: The Parisians: Trocadero, Eiffel Tower and Invalides
short_description: From the Trocadero to the Invalides via the "Iron Lady": the Eiffel Tower
long_description:
A walk that will take you from the Palais de Chaillot (or Trocadero) to the gates of the Invalides, which was erected under Louis XIV to house war invalids via a visit to the Eiffel Tower, the iconic symbol of Paris.
During your visit to the Eiffel Tower, and if the weather permits, you will have a unique view of Paris.
At nightfall, the Trocadero esplanade offers a unique view of the illuminated Eiffel Tower.

title: From Afur to Tamadite Bay and back
short_description: Via a partly narrow trail, this route leads from the village of Afur through a small gorge to the sea at Playa de Tamadite. The black sand beach invites us to take a break, for example with a picnic, or we enjoy sunbathing and listening to the crashing waves of the ocean.
long_description: Afur lies in the middle of the Anaga Mountains. The watercourse that winds its way from the village to Tamadite Bay is guarded by barren rocks, over which a trail leads moderately up and down. We enjoy repeated views of the sea and the bay, the destination of the easy hike. Arriving at Playa de Tamadite, we walk barefoot through the black sand for a while and feel the waves on our feet. Through the gorge with beautiful views of the mountains of the region, for example to the well-known Roque de Taborno, we return to Afur.

title: Snowshoe: Middle Hörnle from Unterammergau
short_description: This snowshoe tour on the Mittlere Hörnle is suitable for snowshoe hikers who have just started as well as an introductory or enjoyable tour in high winter.
long_description: The Mittlere Hörnle above Unterammergau offers mostly open slopes with a gentle to moderate incline in a south-facing direction. This snowshoe tour is particularly suitable for beginners. Touring professionals know how to appreciate the wonderful winter landscape, especially after fresh snowfall. With the Hörnlehütte we also have a place to stop for refreshments (a small turn to the north is necessary for this). Orientation is easy.

title: Hiking circuit: Neulos peak from Saint Martin de l'Albère
short_description: An ascent to the highest point of the Albanian massif where you can enjoy an exceptional panorama from both sides of the border.
long_description:
<The Pic de Neulos marks the border between France and Spain. Culminating at an altitude of 1256 metres, it offers a unique view Roussillon plain on one side north Catalonia other, with bay Rosas in particular.
This route takes part of the famous GR10 trail which crosses the Roussillon valley from the north to the south.
This route follows part of the famous GR10 which crosses the Pyrenees chain from one side to the other.

title: From Sternberg via the Ursula Chapel to the Bavarian Tower
short_description: On this tour we hike through the woods around the Kapellenberg and at the end we may enjoy the wide view from the more than 30 m high Bayernturm.
long_description: From the castle, we walk in a northerly direction out of the village and reach a fork, where we keep to the right. Shortly before a bench at the edge of the forest, a path leads us into the forest. We follow the markings with white "X" on a blue background. Soon we reach a forest road, cross it and a little later come across the St. Ursula Chapel. A path leads us downhill to the edge of the forest. We reach a crossroads and keep to the right. The path now leads us to another junction, where we turn right. Through an extensive stretch of forest we reach a clearing. Here a path points to the Bayernturm. We walk past the mountain inn on the right, where we can also stop for a bite to eat. Afterwards, a steep path leads us back down to Sternberg.

images.caption: At the Saint Ursula Chapel we can take a first rest and enjoy the silence at this place.
Sternberg Palace is one of the most important baroque buildings in northern Franconia.
On the descent to Sternberg we have another beautiful view in the direction of Bad Neustadt.
At the foot of the Kapellenberg are these two old trees with a resting bench and wayside shrine.
The Bayernturm is not necessarily beautiful, but with a height of over 30 m it is an imposing vantage point.

title: The stone guards of the Olkha Plateau
short_description: The centuries-old and unique in their aestheticism creations of nature – rocky remnants spread out in the Baikal Territory, 60 km from the capital of Eastern Siberia – the city of Irkutsk. The Olkha Plateau – is a one or two day hiking or cycling route across a plateau with numerous rock residues. The artistic forms of these rocks also have fairy-tale names, such as Vityaz, Idol, Turtle, Old Woman, Old Fortress, Camel, Bear, Mirrors and many others. These rock formations were formed by weathering and are preserved for lovers of the outdoors in their natural forms.
long_description:
The spectacular route starts from the Orlenok station and flows in the same direction as the Bolshaya Olkha River. The first and the main natural monument on the route – Vityaz rockery, which is about 8 km away. It is worth mentioning that every year in September a festival of bardic songs takes place there.
  Vityaz – it is the most popular and accessible cliff overlooking a large part of the plateau and neighbouring cliffs.
 .
From here one can follow the nature trail to the rock outcrops of Idol, Turtle and subsequently reach the next rock outcrops with fairy-tale names such as The Old Woman and The Fortress. Why Old Woman? Because the cliffhanger does resemble a certain old woman who was unwittingly caught unawares and disturbed in her invaluable daily routine.  
 .
The world of stone sculptures doesn't end there. You can then explore the Bear Rocks, the Mirror Rocks and many more.
  This fantastic Olkhon plateau is also not far from Irkutsk.
  Nature is like a fairy tale, it creates cultural riddles with its winds and we wonder about them later.

title: मुन्नार-एराविकुलम नेशनल पार्क साइकिल टूर
short_description: प्राकृतिक सुंदरता से भरपूर पश्चिम घाटों में स्थित मुन्नार शहर से एराविकुलम रा ष्ट्रीय उद्यान तक की साइकिल यात्रा एक बहुत रोमांचक अनुभव ह ै।
long_description:
यह रोड साइकलिंग दौरा केरल राज्य के खूबसूरत पहाड़ी शहर मुन्नार जिसे दक्षिण भारत का कश्मीर भी कहते हैं से शुरू होता है। मलयालम भाषा में मुन्नार का मतलब होता है तीन नदियाँ क्योंकि यहाँ पर मदुपेट्टी, नल्लथन्नी और पेरियावारु नदियों का संगम होता है। पश्चिमी घाट में करीब 5300 फ़ीट की ऊंचाई पर बसा मुन्नार एक बेहद लोकप्रिय हिल-स्टेशन है जो चाय बागानों से ढकी हुई पहाड़ियों से घिरा हुआ है। यह ब्रिटिश राज के दौरान छुट्टियां बिताने के लिए संपन्न अंग्रेज़ परिवारों और अफसरों की पहली पसंद हुआ करता था। मुन्नार में सैर करने के लिए कई गंतव्य जैसे की एराविकुलम राष्ट्रीय उद्यान, सलीम अली पक्षी अभयारण्य, लक्ष्मी हिल, कन्नन देवन पहाड़ियाँ, और चाय बागान मौजूद हैं।
इस साइकिल यात्रा का गंतव्य केरल का पहला राष्ट्रीय उद्यान, एराविकुलम राष्ट्रीय उद्यान है जो मुन्नार से लगभग 11 किमी दूर स्थित है और नीलगिरि तहर नामक जंगली भेड़ की एक अनोखी और लगभग विलुप्त प्रजाति के लिए प्रसिद्ध है। मुन्नार से एराविकुलम तक साइकिल चलाना एक बहुत ही रोमांचक गतिविधि है। साइकिलिंग के लिए उपलब्ध सबसे अच्छा रास्ता चाय संग्रहालय सड़क (टी म्यूजियम रोड ) से होते हुए केरल राज्य राजमार्ग 17 है, जो  नार्थ-आउटलेट रोड और मुन्नार-उदुमलपेट रोड भी कहलाता है। यह कानन देवन पहाड़ियों, एराविकुलम नेशनल पार्क गेट, अन्नामलाई हिल्स ,और पलानी हिल्स के पास से गुजरता है। इस रोड में घने हरेभरे जंगलों के साथ साथ वन्यजीवों को देखने का अवसर भी मिलता है।

title: The Wirral Way
short_description: This 12-mile-long trail runs along the Wirral Peninsula, offering breathtaking views of the River Dee and the Welsh Hills. The path is suitable for both walking and cycling, making it a versatile option for outdoor enthusiasts.

images.caption: On the Wirral Way near Willaston

title: Trekking from Patnus-Bhira Village to Devkund Falls
short_description: Devkund Falls is a popular hiking and picnic spot for families, nature lovers, and casual tourists.
long_description:
Devkund Falls is located in the village of Patnus/Bhira in Mangaon Taluk of Raigad District of Maharashtra State. It is believed that it is the source of the famous Kundalika river. Although it is a popular hiking route and tourist destination throughout the year, however, during the monsoon, the arrival of tourists increases greatly.
This trekking route is about five kilometres long and relatively easy. The route is full of greenery and well signposted. The village has a registration desk at the beginning of the trail where every hiker is required to register for safety reasons. Taking a local guide is also essential. There is no way to skip these two prerequisites.
The track from Patnus village to Devkund waterfall passes through streams of water and fields en route. After about half an hour comes Bhira-Lake. Moving further from here one has to cross two small water streams in the next 45 minutes. After 20 minutes of this, one has to climb a small hill. After climbing the hill,  one reaches an open place. There are small stalls selling snacks, juices, and water. You can stop here and have rest and breakfast. 
Another hike of approximately one kilometre from the tea stall area takes you to the magnificent Devkund waterfall.
Devkund waterfall is very beautiful. It falls into the lake from a height of about 80 feet. This one day track is a must to enjoy with your friends and family.

images.caption: hike in Maharashtra: Trekking from Patnus-Bhira Village to Devkund Falls

long_description: A linear walking trail in the Upper Galilee, about 7 kilometers long, which starts north of the settlement of Yaraon and ends at the outskirts of the settlement of Dishon. The route is rich in Mediterranean landscapes as well as rich in water.

title: Historical highlights between Beilngries and Berching along the Main-Danube Canal
short_description: On this extended hike along the Main-Danube Canal, we pass two historic town centres, a chapel, a fortified church and a monastery. Again and again we enjoy views of the Sulz valley and the famous waterway.
long_description: This extensive circular hike begins in Beilngries. We cross the little river Sulz and soon reach the Main-Danube Canal. A small chapel and the fortified church of St. Michael von Biberbach are on our way, as is the Plankstetten monastery complex. Berching is a small walled town with a charming medieval centre. Our starting point and destination, Beilngries, is also charming with its historic old town and several opportunities to complement this eventful hike with a visit to a museum.

title: Thermal pool on the southern bathing line
short_description: Soaking in warm water after a long roll is always a turn-off. This thermal loop connects the 19 thermal baths of the southern part of Hungary in the framework of a multi-day cycling tour.
long_description: From the Croatian border through Serbia to the Romanian border, from Inner-Somogy through the Villányi Mountains to the heart of the Alföld.We could call the tour differently, because we pass through many beautiful places worth seeing. But what could be better for your health than cycling in the fresh air and then a well-deserved rest in a thermal pool?! In Hungary, we are so lucky that the thermal baths are one after the other, so the geological and cultural wonders of rural Hungary are both physically and mentally recharging for the traveller. And the Villány, Pécs, Hajós-Baja, Kunság and Csongrád wine regions offer fine wines for the open-minded hiker. And the Southern Region offers the natural wonders of the Danube, the vastness of Bácska and the diversity of Szabadka.

title: Von Niederthai über Brand Richtung Grastal(-see)
short_description:
Von Niederthai hinauf zum Aussichtspunkt Brand und über die Mahdeben ins Grastal zurück nach Niederthai – eine ruhige und besinnliche Naturwanderung abseits vom Alltagsstress.
Translate to English
long_description:
Diese Rundwanderung beginnt in Niederthai im malerischen Ötztal und führt dich auf abwechslungsreichen Waldwegen zunächst sanft, später steiler, hinauf nach Brand. Dieser idyllische Aussichtspunkt belohnt mit einer atemberaubenden Sicht über das Ötztal und die umliegende Bergwelt. Weiter geht es auf der Mahdeben entlang, einem aussichtsreichen Plateau, das nicht nur beeindruckende Weitblicke, sondern auch eine unberührte Alpenflora bietet. Die Mahdeben ist ein ruhiger Ort für eine Rast, um die Seele baumeln zu lassen und die Natur zu genießen. Von hier führt der Weg steil ins Grastal hinab, ein ruhiges Tal mit malerischen Almwiesen, das sich besonders im Herbst in strahlenden Farben zeigt. Schließlich geht es zurück nach Niederthai, wo man den Tag entspannt ausklingen lassen kann. Die Tour bietet eine gelungene Mischung aus abwechslungsreichen Wald- und Wiesenwegen, ruhigen Naturerlebnissen und faszinierenden Ausblicken und ist ideal für Naturliebhaber, die die Stille abseits der großen Wanderwege suchen.

title: Via the Königsjodler via ferrata to the Hoher Kopf at the Hochkönigsstock
short_description: The Königsjodler via ferrata has become an extreme classic among iron routes within a very short time. It is extremely exposed, extremely long and extremely difficult. But the panorama is sensational and huts reward the tired conquerors with a place to stop for refreshments.
long_description: The Königsjodler via ferrata on the Hochkönigstock is an iron route of superlatives: extremely long, extremely steep, extremely exposed, extremely varied and very difficult! More than 1700 metres of climbing and a constant up and down in very to extremely steep terrain - if you also consider the ascent and descent - make very great demands on your physical condition. The route is mainly south-facing (some passages have other exposures). Orientation is easy in good visibility, but orientation on the descent through the Birgkar can quickly become a challenge in poor visibility. The descent should also be done with great caution in case of wetness or residual snow. If you are late or tired after a successful ascent, the Matrashaus on the Hochkönig is a good place to spend the night. The climb is absolutely unsuitable for beginners due to its length, its persistent difficulties and the walking passages in difficulty level I (UIAA). The panorama with the Eastern Alps during the ascent of the entire climb is hard to beat.

title: In the footsteps of the Olympic athletes through the mountains of Krasnaya Polyana
short_description: This short hike will take us past all the major alpine venues of the XXII Olympic Winter Games in Sochi.
long_description: The decision to host the 2014 Winter Olympics in Sochi set in motion a series of lasting changes in the region around Krasnaya Polyana. Where in 2006 only one ski area with only ten kilometres of slopes awaited visitors, today there are four modern ski centres, as well as all the alpine venues for the Olympics. Within a radius of just 20 km, all the facilities for competitions in the disciplines of: Bobsleigh/sled, cross-country skiing/biathlon, ski jumping and all freestyle and downhill competitions. It is precisely the fact that all the alpine venues are located on such a small area that we want to take advantage of and make a short trek along the most important Olympic sites.

title: Around Weissenstein Ruin in the rain
short_description: On this varied tour around Weissenstein Ruin, we experience the granite rocks of the Pfahl and many beautiful views of the Bavarian Forest.
long_description: We walk between the Weißenstein ruins and the chapel on a path into the forest, staying to the right of the "Pfahl", a quartz reef. Finally, we reach the asphalt road to Kattersdorf on forest paths. In Kattersdorf, we watch out for the turn-off to the left downhill to "Großseiboldsried". On the asphalt road towards Eggenried we enjoy a beautiful view, but after 300 m we leave the road and walk on the forest path to Großseiboldsried, where we can rest at the chapel and enjoy the beautiful view. 100 m after leaving the village, our path leads up to the left into the forest (signposted "Weißenstein"). We reach Weißenstein via paths with great views, where we can stop for a break at the Burggasthof.

title: Pond circuit around Fischbach
short_description: The Fischbacher Weiherrunde offers us not only recreation in an idyllic landscape, but also information about fish farming and the animal species that live there.
long_description: Our loop begins at the church of St. Jakob in Fischbach. We walk downhill along the road and uphill again at the vicarage until we reach the end of the village. Here we keep to the left and cross the district road. Soon we turn onto a gravel path and reach the first information board of the circular route. There we keep to the right and finally reach the Lapisweiher. At the crossroads we reach the second information board. We follow the hiking trail "18" and walk past the Leer-, Kram- and Büchsenweiher. At the crossroads with the third information board, we turn left and follow the path to the district road. We cross this and reach Brunn. At the Gasthof "Zur Sonne" we keep left, leave the village and finally reach Fischbach and the parish church again.
