title: 5 days through south-eastern Franconian Switzerland
short_description: With good reason, the German Hiking Association has declared this tour to be one of the most beautiful German circular hiking trails: because in five days we discover the southeast of Franconian Switzerland on 100 densely wooded kilometres. The route is quite hilly and also has some challenging climbs in store for us - for which we are then mostly rewarded with fantastic views of the surroundings.
long_description:
Stage 1: Pegnitz - Behringersmühle (22 km)
From Pegnitz, on the eastern edge of the Fränkische Schweiz, we hike über the Schloßberg to the Püttlach, which we will follow through the rock town of Pottenstein to Behringermühle. The idyllic valley of the small river is of particular scenic charm.
Stage 2: Behringersmühle - Bärnfels (21 km)
The Wiesent river takes us to Gö&laday;weinstein. We then hike in a long curve to Bieberach and then head east again to Bärnfels. <Stage 3: Bärnfels - Obertrubach (24 km)
Über den Hirschbühl we hike to the small village of Hammberbühl in the picturesque valley of the Brubach, where we will see several Mühlen. Past Egloffstein and Thuisbrunn we return to the Trubach valley and follow the course of the river to Obertrubach.
Stage 4: Obertrubach - Schermshöhe (21 km)
We hike back along yesterday's route to the Schlöttermühle and cross the Trubach here. Several ascents await us on the way to Hiltpoltstein. Then we hike through sparsely populated areas via the Schlo&szligberg and the Klausberg to the village of Spies. Now we walk along the Hohe Reut, the highest elevation in the Fränkische Schweiz, to the finish of the stage.
Stage 5: Schermshöhe - Pegnitz (26 km)
On the last stage we also climb many a peak. Behind Plech we enter the Veldensteiner Forst, one of the largest coherent forest areas in Bavaria. Only when we have left behind the countless pines and spruces and some exciting hills do we arrive back in Pegnitz, the starting point of our circular tour.

images.caption: The southern view of Pottenstein Castle.

title: Small round around the Egglburger See
short_description: A small, family-friendly tour around the Egglburger See lake. Varied for children and with an inn with a small terrace at the end of the trail.
long_description: The leisurely route around Lake Egglburg leads through a nature reserve and is popular with locals and tourists alike. After you have overcome the eastern shore with its beautiful lake view, a smaller path leads through a section of forest. Here you will find a pleasantly refreshing climate even in summer temperatures. Afterwards, an easily passable, partly asphalted and gravelled road leads to a meadow, which can be crossed on a well-trodden path and leads the hiker directly back to the starting point of the tour.

title: Bad-Gögging Fishing Trail
short_description: Informative nature trail, about fish in the region, as well as various other topics about the natural and cultural landscape.
long_description: On a circular route that starts in Bad Gögging on the Abens and leads via Neustadt back to Bad Gögging in the old spa gardens, we find 23 information panels. Using the example of the Abens and the Danube, a watercourse system is presented as well as various topics on the natural and cultural landscape at the watercourse. These include, for example, agricultural use with the hop cultivation typical of the region, the special features of the moors and the Bad Gingen springs and early cultivation of the landscape by the Romans. The nature trail focuses on the fish species characteristic of the region, their special features and lifestyles.

title: Round tour of Duisburg's inner harbour
short_description: This tour takes us through Duisburg and around its inner harbour, for which the city is internationally famous. A walk around the harbour basin shows how history is brought to life in an attractive mix of historic buildings with modern architecture.
long_description:
This tour takes us through the old town and around Duisburg's inner harbour. The old town was originally surrounded by a medieval city wall. With industrialisation, the city grew beyond these walls. The outer and inner harbours were built on the site of the old arm of the Rhine, which had silted up and served as a transport route for grain and timber. With mills and warehouses, the centre of the German grain trade was established at Duisburg's inner harbour around 1900. After the Second World War, the inner harbour lost its importance, and in the 1970s the old granaries were threatened with demolition. Today, architects, artists and urban planners are redesigning the inner harbour into an attractive urban quarter that combines working, living and leisure. Special attractions include the MKM Museum Küppersmühle für Moderne Kunst, the attractive gastronomy row, the Kultur- und Stadthistorisches Museum and the round trips through the world's largest inland harbour from the Schwanentor footbridge.
    The inner harbour is the largest inland harbour in the world.

images.caption: Remains of the Duisburg city wall at the inner harbour.

title: Lake hike in the Accursed Mountains - Leqinat
short_description: The first time I walked this route I was so impressed by the crystal clear blue water of the two mountain lakes. If you want to have a relaxed mountain hike with stunning nature you should definetly try this one out.
long_description: The route starts in the village of Kuqishte from where you begin the path up to the village of Leqinat on a road with little traffic. You will walk for an hour on the asphalt road through deciduous and coniferous forest until you arrive at the Resturant Leqinat. From there you enter a path that takes you through the coniferous forest, along a rock wall up to the lake Leqinat. Arrived at the lake, you can decide whether to take a short break, or if there are many people, to continue to the smaller lake. You go down to the second lake and start the descent. Before the second lake you leave the Peaks of the Balkans Trail and follow a small path down, which is badly signposted, but there are no turnoffs. You follow the path until you come to a forest road that is currently being converted to an asphalt road and walk back down into the Rugova Gorge.

title: Hiking Around Darlik Dam
short_description: Darlık Dam, located on the Istanbul - Şile road, is a popular location for many nature lovers and hikers. This route around the dam is just one of the alternatives.
long_description:
Darlık Dam is frequented by those who want to have a pleasant time and enjoy activities such as picnics and camping activities, especially on weekends. This dam, which has many hiking routes around it, becomes very crowded when the weather gets better. 
The hiking routes around Darlık Dam are suitable for many nature lovers. The route followed in this article is one of the alternative routes around Darlık Dam. Since it is not excessively long, it can easily be done with friends and family as a nature activity on a Sunday day. If you catch the season well, you can take great nature photos and plan a picnic for relaxation.
Many routes such as this route around the Darlık Dam offer a great opportunity to escape from city life. If nature and hiking are a passion for you and you are looking for alternative routes, this is a route worth trying.

title: Forest Gorge Trail
short_description: Idyllic stream valleys, primeval alluvial forests and majestic beech forests. On narrow paths we hike through enchanted forests, past Roman relics.
long_description:
Highlights:
Feisternachtbachtal, Limes (UNESCO World Heritage), ancient giant trees, high beech forests, paths mostly through idyllic stream valleys.
The starting point is the Feisternachtbachtal car park. The trail crosses the L309 and the Hillscheider Bach stream and leads above the stream through medium-high mixed forest past steep rock cliffs and the fish ponds of the Tannenhof farm. The trail crosses the L309 again. The trail climbs in serpentines and continues up the valley along the Hirzbach stream. Through old high forest, the trail goes gently at first, later steeply upwards around the Kuckucksberg. At the top, the trail turns left through old beech trees (beech cathedral): Ancient tree giants with a special growth habit. Turn right along a narrow path to the middle Pedelweg (detour to the Pedel refuge possible). The trail now descends under ancient giant trees, past the waterworks to the Bembermühle mill. The following ascent leads to the Limes wall hidden in the forest, a relic from Roman times. Even before the first houses of Höhr-Grenzhausen, the trail circles the flank of the Puschenkopf almost parallel to the altitude and continues to the Saustallkopf. The path now descends in wide serpentines into the Feisternachtbach valley, crosses the stream and leads down the left bank to a small lake with a hut and further back to the starting point.

title: Randonnée à la Sainte-Baume par le Joug de l'Aigle
short_description:
Un beau parcours de randonnée passant par des points emblématiques tels que le Saint-Pilon, avec une vue spectaculaire sur la Provence, le Joug de l’Aigle, offrant une crête rocheuse imposante, et le Pas de Villecroze, un passage pittoresque dans la forêt.
Translate to English
long_description:
Dès le départ, les randonneurs s'engagent sur un sentier qui grimpe progressivement dans une forêt dense de hêtres et de chênes, caractéristique de ce massif. La fraîcheur de la végétation contraste avec la chaleur souvent présente en basse Provence.
En continuant la montée, le sentier rejoint le Saint-Pilon, à environ 1000 mètres d’altitude, qui est marqué par une croix en pierre. De là, la vue panoramique est saisissante, avec une vue à 360° sur la Provence, du massif de la Sainte-Victoire jusqu’aux Alpes, et par temps clair, jusqu'à la mer Méditerranée. Ce lieu de contemplation invite à une pause bien méritée avant de poursuivre l'ascension.
Ensuite, le sentier serpente vers le Joug de l’Aigle, un sommet emblématique du massif. Cette crête rocheuse offre un paysage minéral contrastant avec la végétation des versants inférieurs. La traversée de cette zone exige un peu de vigilance en raison de son relief escarpé, mais elle ravira les amateurs de sentiers alpins.
Le chemin redescend ensuite vers le Pas de Villecroze, une section plus ombragée, nichée dans la forêt. Ce passage, relativement étroit, permet de redescendre en douceur vers la vallée par le "Sentier Merveilleux" tout en étant entouré de magnifiques arbres centenaires. La descente est progressive et permet de profiter d'une belle tranquillité avant de rejoindre le point de départ, le parking des Trois Chênes.

title: Spessart Trail 2: "Over mountain and valley to the Main".
short_description: The Spessart Trail is divided into Spessart Trail 1 and Spessart Trail 2. The Spessart Trail 2 described here takes us over hill and dale to the River Main through the most beautiful landscapes of the Spessart.

title: On the trail of the Teutonic Order around Bad Mergentheim
short_description: The 300-year presence of the Teutonic Knights in Bad Mergentheim has left its mark on the town and its surroundings. This hike through the beautiful Mergentheim countryside takes us past evidence of their history.
long_description: The starting point of our hike is the Deutschordensschloss (Castle of the Teutonic Order) in the centre of Bad Mergentheim, which housed the High and German Masters of the Teutonic Order for over 300 years. Our path leads through the castle grounds and the castle park, which is laid out as an English landscape garden, towards the Tauber. We cross the river and then turn right into Lothar-Daiker-Straße. Parallel to the Tauber, we now pass the open-air swimming pool and the sports facilities to Igersheim. We cross the town by keeping to the right at the entrance to the town, first along Erlenbachtalstraße and then Bahnhofstraße and, after crossing the B19 federal road, turn right into Bad Mergentheimer Straße, which takes us across the Tauber again. Directly behind the river, a forest path branches off to the left and takes us to Neuhaus Castle. Neuhaus Castle used to be owned by the noblemen of Hohenlohe-Brauneck until it was taken over by the Teutonic Order and used as an armoury and armoury. At the castle, we turn left and walk across fields and along rows of trees and hedges towards the B290. We always have the Wartturm on the Kaiserstraße, the former army and trade route, in view. It used to serve the Teutonic Order as a lookout tower. Our path meets the main road, but we keep to the right and hike back to Bad Mergentheim on the Alemannenweg. If you like, you can make a detour to the Wartturm (watchtower) from where you have a great view. Passing the old cemetery, we return to the centre of Bad Mergentheim and the Deutschordensschloss. Finally, a visit to the Deutschordensmuseum is a good idea. In addition to the largest coherent exhibition on the Teutonic Order, exhibits on the town's history, the Eduard Moerike cabinet and an extensive doll's house collection are on display here.

title: The beautiful corners of Schöneck
short_description: On this hike we experience a lot of forest and the village of Eschenbach.
long_description: Eschenbach belongs to the village of Schöneck in the Saxon Vogtland. The farming village is situated in a valley at an average altitude of approx. 650 metres. This hike is all about an experience in the "green": It starts at the Schöneck town park, the rest of the route runs mostly through the forest.

title: White Rock - top hiking in the Crimea
short_description: The mountains of the Crimea are beloved by many travellers. White Rock is a Crimean stone beauty that has become the calling card of the Belogorsk district.
long_description: White Rock – is a great vantage point with beautiful views of the surrounding area and also for filming films. Headless Horseman and other films were filmed here. There is also a cave in the rock which is called the Golden Hole. In spring, forest peonies bloom in the valley behind the White Rock, and the slopes are covered in a beautiful motley carpet. The mountains are blue to the south of the White Rock, and the steppes stretch all the way to the horizon in the north. Not far from the mountain an 800 year old oak grows, it was named Suvorov's oak. In 1777 the rock was the location of Alexander Suvorov's headquarters. And today it is a playground for curious tourists looking for a fantastic experience.

title: Surkanda Mata Temple Hike
short_description: This is a pilgrim hike through a well-maintained nature trail on the airy hills of Mussoorie in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, India.
long_description:
Surkanda Mata Temple is situated at a distance of about 42 km from Mussoorie city. This temple is situated on the Mussoorie-Chamba road in Uttarakhand. The starting point of this hike is a place named Kaddukhal which is also the last designated vehicle parking and the start of this trek. This beautiful temple is on a nature trail that runs almost 2 kilometres from Kaddukhal. The trail is short but steep and needs good endurance on the hiker's part. Luckily the facility of the cable car (trolley system) is now available and is generally much utilised by old people.
 This pilgrim trail is very beautiful and full of natural scenes.  Dense forest and panoramic views of snow-laden peaks are the main features of this trail. The Surkanda Mata temple is an important Shaktipeeth and pilgrimage. The summit temple is very beautiful and peaceful. One gets a complete 360-degree view of the surroundings from the summit. Several major Himalayan mountain ranges and the cities of Dehradun, Mussoorie and Chakrata are clearly visible from here. In short, this trail is great for a short but enjoyable hiking trip.

title: Rain and forest around Marienthal
short_description: On this challenging tour, we hike through quiet, extensive forest areas and discover many cultural highlights along the way.
long_description: Our day tour starts at the car park in front of the Wittmann inn. We find a panoramic map of the region on the left side, which we walk past and take the path through the village. Here we meet the marking "Red triangle on a white background" which will accompany us on our tour. The houses are soon behind us and we reach the Marienkapelle chapel at the edge of the forest. On a path we hike up the Gailenberg to Franzenshöhe. In the lower part we cross a forest path three times. Afterwards, the path leads us through a beautiful beech forest directly to the summit. There are now 200 metres of altitude difference between us and the starting point at the inn in Marienthal. On Franzenshöhe we find a stone roundel that was built at the beginning of the 20th century and served as a lookout point, but is now overgrown. We use the Peilstein for a good view of the surrounding countryside. A path leads us from the roundel in a westerly direction to this rock, from which we can see as far as Schwandorf and over the Upper Palatinate Lake District in good weather. After this detour, we continue south on the slightly sloping gravel path and reach a crossroads. Here we find a covered resting place and can take a rest. Our path leads us straight on to a junction that takes us right into the now denser forest. We walk across another junction, past large groups of boulders, up the Hohenstein. There we find a signpost to the Riedelhöhe. We turn left onto the path and discover the brick observation tower, which dates from the same time as the structure at Franzenshöhe. After climbing the tower, we return to the path and a little later reach the Wackelstein on the right. Strong hikers can make this granite block wobble with a chain. After these two sights, the path brings us to another crossroads, where we now turn left. A signpost here points us to Grafenwinn. Shortly afterwards, the path branches off. We keep to the right and walk on the gravel path through beautiful mixed forest over another junction and follow the markings "Red triangle on a white background". At a fork, we keep to the left and emerge from the forest and onto a meadow for the first time. A little later we reach a road and on it the village of Grafenwinn. Turn left at the chapel. At the hamlet of Hirtberg, we keep left again and reach Dürmaul. Passing the small cross on a stone pedestal, we now hike back up the mountain. At the beginning of the forest, we leave the road and hike right across the path onto a forest path that leads us to the left along the flank of the Jugenberg. Soon we meet the road again and follow it. In Eckartsreuth, we can make a detour to the Jugenberg mountain inn for a snack. You will find it at the end of the village. The trail continues along orchards through Gunt to Hof. In the centre of the village we can visit the castle "Hof am Regen" from the 12th century. At the fire station we turn left and at the following crossroads we keep to the right. We reach Stefling and walk up the unpaved road at the crucifix. Here we have the opportunity to take a look inside the castle. We leave the village in a westerly direction on the cycle path and reach an iron bridge at the Regen, which we cross. After the bridge, we turn left and walk along the banks of the Regen. Via the hamlet of Weißenhof we reach a ferry landing stage. There we have to call the ferryman, who eventually takes us to the inn. Here we have earned a hearty snack and can recover from the efforts of our day's hike.

title: Advent Window Tour through Ellhofen 2021/2022
short_description: Every year during Advent, the entire village of Ellhofen in the Allgäu region becomes a large Advent calendar, welcoming visitors from near and far.
long_description:
Just like a real Advent calendar, another "little door" is opened every day in the Ellhofen Advent calendar. However, these little doors are spread all over the village - and the respective residents of the participating windows give free rein to their creativity as to what they imagine and present on the Christmas theme.
During the period between 1 December and 6 January, visitors can wander through the wintry village on the basis of the tour suggestion shown here and, while doing so, examine the lovingly decorated Advent windows.
The route presented here with its itinerary represents the "best possible" itinerary when all 24 Advent windows are open. If not all windows are open yet (i.e. before 24.12.), it is best to put together the appropriate/desired route yourself on site.

title: A ride in the cable car and from there a trip to the Zabenza and Drakenza lakes in Ehrwald
short_description: A magical panoramic walking route from the top station of the Ehrwald cable car to Seebensee and Drachensee.
long_description:
A magical hiking route with panoramic views towards the Alps and Mount Zugspitze. During the route you pass an animal, flowing water and two lakes with a mesmerizing appearance.
The walk to the first lake (Seebensee) is not particularly difficult, but still includes several climbs, but nevertheless, thanks to the variety of stopping and refreshment options on the way, it is definitely suitable for those in basic fitness. Further down the road there is a path suitable for walking with baby strollers, but it must be taken into account that it includes climbs and it is not paved.
The continuation of the walk to the upper lake (Drachensee) is more challenging and is not suitable for everyone as it includes a relatively steep and cobbled ascent and is therefore also not suitable for walking with strollers). The walk is challenging but definitely worth the effort!
It is possible and recommended to stop at one of the alpine huts on the way and enjoy the atmosphere and the local delicacies.

title: The golden signpost near Bodenmais
short_description: This Nordic walking tour takes us along the Rothbach stream to the Bodenmais district of Mais and back. On this varied tour we walk through forests and meadows.
long_description: We start at the southern edge of Bodenmais and follow the markings of the "Eon Trail" along the Rothbach. We cross the road and enter the forest again. We can catch our breath on a bench. On a meadow near Bergwinkl we enjoy the view over the valley. At the village of Mais, we cross the through road and follow the hiking trail to Mooshof. At the entrance to the village there is a stone cube in which an artist has carved the golden signpost. We continue and turn right into the forest. Behind the glass factory, we walk along a meadow to the outskirts of Bodenmais and on to the Rothbach stream. We follow it back to our starting point.

title: Hike around Kirchdorf
short_description: This extensive hike takes us through the quiet, varied recreational landscape of the southern Bavarian Forest Nature Park.
long_description: We begin our hike in Kirchdorf im Wald. We first take a look at the parish church "Mariä Unbefleckte Empfängnis" (Immaculate Conception), which was built in the Baroque style at the beginning of the 18th century on the walls of a Gothic predecessor building. The interior houses a high altar, pulpit and side altars in rococo style. The showpiece of the high altar is the 1.5 m high figure of the Mother of God from around 1480. Since the High Middle Ages, believers have been making pilgrimages to the place of Mary in Kirchdorf. The pilgrimage is said to have reached its peak during the 30 Years' War, with 15,000 pilgrims a year coming to the miraculous image. It was not until the beginning of the 19th century that the flow of pilgrims slowed down. Today, the only pilgrimage to Kirchdorf is on Kirchweihsonntag, the last Sunday in August, from the neighbouring parish of Innernzell. We walk downhill on the Kirchberg road, where we can already enjoy a beautiful view of the foothills of the Bavarian Forest on a clear day. Further on we meet the road to Bruck. At the sign for the town, turn left onto a dirt road. At the houses of Bruck, we turn left and walk across the sloping terrain to the chapel of Bruck. There we cross the Brucker Bach stream and keep left on the ascending path to Abtschlag in the direction of the forest. We pass a bench and several death boards. The tradition of erecting boards of the dead was widespread in Bavaria, Württemberg, Switzerland and Austria in the 19th century. Today, this form of commemorating the dead is only found in the Bavarian Forest and the Upper Palatinate Forest. Once upon a time, the deceased were actually fixed on them and they were lowered into the grave on them. To commemorate the dead, people redesigned the board after the burial and placed it in the hallway, for example, at a place where the deceased frequented or travelled during his or her lifetime. We continue along the edge of the forest, enjoy beautiful views and orient ourselves towards the nature trail. Through the forest of the Pfaffenberg we finally reach an asphalted road after about 2 km. We turn left towards Abtschlag. At the "Gasthaus Niedermaier" we go left, after 150 m we pay attention to the path on the right. After 300 m it leads us past a wayside cross. The path forks before the forest at Grünberg. Here we first walk uphill to the left at the edge of the forest until we reach a crossing path, walk right there and arrive at an elevated tank. Passing it on the right and going downhill again, we keep left at the edge of the forest and walk along the road to the beautiful village of Grünbach. There we turn right at the last house, and after 100 m the path splits into three directions. We choose the path on the far left and walk on it to Gschwendtermühle. In the next village, Fürstberg, the "Josef Braumandl" inn invites you to take a break. Now walk uphill to Eppenschlag, cross under the main road and finally turn left along the road into the village. Turn left at the church square before turning right at Marbacher Straße. In Marbach, we keep to the right on the Auenstraße to Sommerau. There we look out for three letterboxes in front of the Klopferbach stream and choose the path to the left uphill. This path leads us into the forest and always uphill until we reach a wide forest path. Here we go left, further up the mountain. At Kohlstatt we come across isolated farms and a sign "Privatweg" (private path). Before this, we use the path on the left and walk along the meadow. At the end of the meadow, we keep to the main path and from now on follow the signs to "5" and "Kirchdorf". We now walk downhill with many changes of direction until we reach Kirchdorf. When we reach the village, we turn right onto Aubergweg and Wilhelmstraße to the church.

title: Hesse Extratour Ronshausen
short_description:
Mixed forest in pure culture, mountain ranges, places with fungi, mosses and
ferns, picturesque valleys with wide expanses of meadow, streams and
Fishing ponds make for a varied hike.
long_description:
East of the two historic half-timbered towns of Bad Hersfeld and Rotenburg a. d. Fulda lies the almost thousand-year-old village of Ronshausen on the old road link between the Fulda and Werra rivers above the Hönebacher Sattel. Its district has a lot of high mixed forest interspersed with charming fir trees.
Through three idyllic valleys, Marbach, Steinbach and Silzerbachtal, the circular walk leads into the high forest stand, past mighty veteran trees, and along sections of the Steinbachtal adventure trail and the Iba nature adventure trail. It can be walked on both sides without a map.
After a third of the way, you can take a short detour to the "Friedrichshütte", a secluded administrative building of an ore smelter that is now a restaurant and bears witness to the former importance of copper slate mining for the region. In 1840, the famous fairy tale poet Wilhelm Grimm wrote to a friend: "It is a beautiful, quite Hessian region, lonely, quiet meadows between serious forests; in the evening, the blue, red and green flames of the copper ore shine from the smelting furnaces.

long_description: This moderate but very satisfying hike of around 6 hours takes you through an interchangeable landscape that delivers some dramatic views across the Allgäuer Hochalpen and Tannheim Valley, two summits and a good burn of calories.

title: Taganai National Park - Lower Taganai Trail
short_description: «Taganai» — is one of the popular national parks in the South Urals. The park is loved by tourists because of its rocky, unique and bizarrely shaped areas.
long_description:
The Taganai National Park is located in close proximity to the Ural town of Zlatoust, 150 km from Chelyabinsk.
The length of the hike in «Taganai» along the Nizhny Taganai Trail to/from Dalny Taganai is 65 km. Depending on your possibilities and interest, the trekking can be broken up into several sections and days. There are many scenic places to visit on the trail. It includes such mountains as the Mont Blanc (Taganay), the Three Brothers tract with very fashionable brother-rocks which have been standing in their places for centuries with their mysterious origin.

title: Cozia autumn beauty
short_description: Cozia Mountain is extremely beautiful in autumn since it's mostly covered in deciduous forests that show off their most wonderful colors in this season.
long_description:
There are several mountain routes that you can take to explore this mountain, each one as beautiful as the other, and all similarly challenging.
The one we tried draws a circuit of almost the entire mountain, passing by several panoramic viewpoints, plus the Cozia mountain hut at the top. Except for the area around the top, which is dominated by fir trees, for the rest of the hike, you only admire deciduous trees, steep valleys (mostly dried), lush vegetation, and a few shabby, unusable refuges.
Even for the most trained mountaineers, the huge path gradient stays challenging. However, with lots of patience, even trained children can take this route or part of it.

title: Through the Dämmelwald in Wiesloch
short_description: The forest nature trail on the edge of Wiesloch is intended to point out the diversity of the forest habitat and to provide information about the most important animals and plants typical of the Dämmelwald with text and picture boards along the way.
long_description:
The approx. 67 ha Dämmelwald is a recreational area close to the city. The name goes back to the word "dam". The character as a spring wet floodplain forest is determined by the clayey subsoil that dams the surface water.
Depending on the season, there are always new aspects for the hiker. The texts are printed on the boards of the nature trail and offer the visitor the possibility to read up and deepen what he has seen.

title: Winter hike on the Oeschinensee
short_description: This winter hike offers the opportunity to admire the snow-covered landscapes of the Bernese Oberland. Highlights include Lake Oeschinen and the Blüemlisalp massif.
long_description:
Lake Oeschinen, a blue jewel in summer, transforms into a silent icy landscape in winter. Nestled in the Blüemlisalp massif, the valley remains mostly in the shade of the low winter sun, creating an almost arctic atmosphere. The winter hiking trail is signposted with pink signs and leads you from the sunny Oeschinen mountain station through the ski area down to the frozen lake.
After a gentle descent, you reach the wide expanse of ice, which is safe to walk on when it is still cold. A short detour to the north side of the lake reveals a special natural spectacle: a frozen waterfall forms an impressive ice tower. The way back leads either across the lake or through the snow-covered fir forest back to the mountain station, where you can take the chairlift or the toboggan run down to the valley. Sledges can be hired from the sports store at the mountain station.

title: High altitude hike against a sublime mountain backdrop
Healing Climate Trail HM5
short_description: Fancy a hike with a panoramic view of the Rhine-Main region that is not only climatically attractive? Then the Hohemark hiking portal in Oberursel, easily accessible by S-Bahn, offers just the right thing! In addition to 4 other easy to moderately difficult tours, the challenging circular hike HM5, which leads through lush fir forests up to the Altkönig, is particularly appealing. There, "Mainhatten" is practically at our feet and the Großer Feldberg also greets us with its striking towers. A worthwhile stopover is the Fuchstanz with refreshments before we hike back through the dreamy Heidetränketal valley.
long_description: Get out into nature - it's child's play at the Hohemark hiking portal. Depending on your personal preferences, you can choose between 5 differently strenuous circular trails.HM5 is particularly charming, but also by far the most demanding circular trail. At first the trail leads us through the foothills of Hohemark, but soon we get to breathe in the cool, fresh forest air. The slowly decreasing temperature during the ascent provides climatic stimuli, which are also visually supported by beautiful views. We strive uphill in wonderful shade and our fitness is put to the test, especially when we climb the Altkönig. Almost at the top, the mighty Celtic stone wall awaits us as a cultural treat. After the descent, we can replace some of the calories we have burnt at the Fuchstanz with a hearty stop in the forest before we hike leisurely downhill. In the Heidetränke valley, a lively stream accompanies us back to the starting point in a mild valley climate.

short_description: We learn a lot of interesting facts about the animal and plant world during our hike on the nature trail at Schiederhof.
long_description: We start our circular walk at the information board at the car park, which explains the individual stations of the nature trail in more detail. Now we walk down the path into the forest, always following the markings "White seven on a red background". Soon we come across the first sign, where we learn interesting facts about the "balance of power" between ants and humans. A total of nine stations explain nature to us in a vivid way. At the third signpost we reach a place with a wonderful distant view of the western forest regions. As we continue, we pass the "bounce" station and the wooden xylophone. Finally, we come out of the forest again. At the crucifix, we turn left and reach the Schiederhof inn again.

At the end of our hike, we come across a crucifix on the side of the path, typical of this area.
The nature observation trail for us through beautiful deciduous forest.
At the beginning of the nature trail we get an overview of the individual stations on our way.
At this station we can try out for ourselves whether we have the jumping power of a hare or that of a deer.

title: To Ice Age giants and the Burgäschisee
short_description: A varied hike through forests, wide meadows and over panoramic hills to the large erratic boulder on the Steinhof and to the settlement site of Palaeolithic man at Burgäschisee.
long_description:
A varied hike through forests, across meadows and over spectacular heights to the large erratic block at Steinhof and the Palaeolithic human settlement by the Burgäschisee. Accessible throughout the year, this route is not just of natural and historical interest; the opportunity to bathe by the Burgäschisee also means plenty of amusement. Even those interested in politics will get their money's worth, as the Steinhof of Solothurn forms an enclave within the territory of Bern. Few hard surfaces outside the towns and villages.

From Herzogenbuchsee station, walk along Bahnhofstrasse and take the ring road to Maria-Waser-Strasse. This street is named after the author who spent her childhood years in Herzogenbuchsee. Now turn into the nearby Löliwald. A beautiful pathway runs southwards through the light beech forest like a natural pergola, with benches to rest and enjoy the fine views through to the open air. At the edge of the forest, cross the road and railway line to reach the houses of meadow. There is a magnificent view across the hedge-lined Önz plain to the church tower of Aeschi and the Jura. The route continues through the meadows along the railway line and crosses the Önz. It is hard to believe that this harmless little stream can swell into a raging river after storms, which is why its once winding course was (unfortunately) straightened and diverted. Stay in the same direction at the Rain farmstead and continue along the edge of the forest, then return to the Önz and follow the course of the stream. At Hermiswil there is a diversion to the little Solothurn village of Steinhof. On the left, not far from the Löschmagazin adorned with a coat of arms, stands the giant erratic block, the «Grossi Flue». This rock arguably gave its name not only to the village but also the House of von Stein, whose water castle stood by the Burgäschisee.
Back in the centre of the village, continue westwards and descend the steep slope to the outskirts of the forest. Walk along the edge of the woods (once again following the cantonal border), then cross the Aeschi-Seeberg road and take the almost level path into the Hinterholz (25 minutes to Seeberg) before descending to the country road. Cross the road and walk down to the nearby Burgäschisee. As a result of silting and the lowering of the water level in 1943, the original lake became a humble basin. This revealed the two lake dwelling settlements to the East and West, while a similar settlement had already been known to exist on the North shore. The bathing beach offers a welcome opportunity for refreshment towards the end of the hike.
From the nearby hamlet of Burgäschi (20 minutes from Aeschi), return by the Burghölzli and Eichwald to Niederönz and the starting point in Herzogenbuchsee.

title: Hadrian's Road: Fort Segedunum (Wallsend) - Newcastle
short_description: A stage of the walking and cycling route that runs along the banks of the River Tyne, part of a larger network of trails that roughly follow the line of the wall built by King Hadrian between Wallsend (E) and Bowness-on-Solway (V) & 122-124.
long_description:
The route is known as Hadrian's Way or Route 72 Hadrian's Cycleway and signed as such. Sometimes the routes coincide, but there are also stretches where they diverge.
You start at the fortress of Segedunum and visit it, which is where the construction of the wall, symbolically called "the place where the frontier of Rome began", began. Here you can see portions of the original wall, and the museum projects possible aspects of the original wall.
Another piece of the wall, reconstructed, lies to the west of the fort, on Buddle Street. Although this route doesn't include the street, if you want to follow it more or less in a straight line, you'd walk right along the line of the wall.
&Iirc;instead, the National Trail, i.e. this one, takes you through almost deserted areas, often overgrown, so also a little wilder. You don't get very interesting views, but rather a long walk.
The most interesting points on this route are the start and finish: the fort and the entrance to Newcastle with its elegant quayside.

images.caption: Segedunum, reconstructed portion of Hadrian's Wall

title: Village idyll around Guben
short_description: We hike for around 30 km through the dreamy meadows, forests and lakes of Lower Lusatia.
long_description:
The starting point of our hike is the central town of Guben, situated on the Polish border. The city was badly affected during the war, as the historic centre, which is now located in the Polish sister city of Gubin as a result of the forced partition, was almost completely destroyed. Until the 1990s, Guben was known for its hat and cloth-making industry as well as for the production of chemical fibres.
We start our circular walk near the Guben railway station at the junction of Sprucker Straße / August-Bebel-Straße. We leave the village via Sprucker Straße, "Altsprucke" and Birkenallee and hike through forests and across fields, half-circling a pond in the direction of Deulowitz.
From Deulowitz we hike in the direction of Schenkendöbern Lake. We walk halfway around the lake on the left and then make a short detour to the village of Atterwasch to see the old village church. Back in the forest, we walk mostly along the edge of the forest - first a long left-hand bend and later straight ahead - towards the village of Bärenklau. Here we can marvel at a natural monument, the over 1000-year-old oak tree. From Bärenklau, the trail leads north to Lübbinchen, which is picturesquely situated at the Krayne reservoir. We walk along the B320 main road for a short distance before the path leads us back into a forest area on the left. We continue through the pine forest to Grano, the next village. Here we pass the "Granoer Hammer", a former mint. We continue across meadows and through forests to Wilschwitz, our last idyllically situated village before Guben. Via Wilschwitzer Weg, Cottbuser Straße and Karl-Marx-Straße, we return to our starting point in Sprucker Straße.

title: Col du Pillon - key to the Diablerets region
The Imperial Town Trail near Weißenburg
short_description: The Reichsstadtweg connects the towns of Weißenburg and Pappenheim. It is marked "S 7" throughout and crosses the Frankenweg, the Main-Donau-Weg and the Altmühl-Panoramaweg in its course. We return by train.
long_description:
The town of Weißenburg dates back to the Roman fort "Biriciana" and the associated settlement. One of the total of four gates of the camp, the Porta Decumana, can be visited today in reconstructed form. It is part of an archaeological park founded in 1990 on the undeveloped area of the fort.
In Weißenburg, it is also worth making a detour to the Ellinger Tor. Of a total of three town gates, it has survived the test of time until today and has already adorned two stamps of the German Federal Post Office. The main tower dates from the 14th century and was extended around 1510.
Above Weißenburg lies the Wülzburg. The former Benedictine monastery was converted into a Renaissance fortress in 1588 and today houses a school with a boarding school for women's social professions.
The St. Gallus church in Pappenheim was built in the 9th century and is one of the oldest buildings in Franconia.

title: Scheidegg waterfalls - a world of experience for young and old near Lindenberg
short_description: The Scheidegg waterfalls are among the 100 most beautiful geotopes in Bavaria.
long_description: The Scheidegg waterfalls are among the 100 most beautiful geotopes in Bavaria and are an ideal destination for families. The water of the Rickenbach falls over two mighty rock steps into the depths: 22 m and 18 m high, the two waterfalls are close to each other and can be admired from several vantage points. In addition to the natural spectacle of the waterfalls, there is a water playground and interesting facts about an ancient water technology to see

title: Over the old Gemmi Trail
short_description: The most frequented pass route from the Bernese Oberland to the Valais. It is particularly impressive because of the high alpine scenery, the impressive distant view of the Valais Alps and the unique view from the Gemmi Pass.
long_description:
From Kandersteg railway station on the village side along the railway embankment in the direction of the valley. Through the underpass to Bütschels and on a beautiful footpath between the Kander bank and the edge of the forest in the direction of the valley. At the bridge on this side of the river, continue and at Eggeschwand take the Gemmiweg, which soon rises sharply. In many twists and turns, the so-called Walliskehren, up to Stock, the former terminus of the Gemmi railway. Beautiful views of the Gasteretal, Balmhorn and Doldenhorn.
Now the paths branch out: while one leads through a hollow über Sunnbüel to Spittelmatte, the historic path leads through sparse forest übers Stierenbergli and along the wild Schwarzbachschlucht gorge up to Spittelmatte. The Arvenseeli are hidden in the pine trees to the right of the path and are well worth a detour. Now the path turns, climbing more steeply, to the Schwarenbach mountain hotel, whose guests include Guy de Maupassant, Alexandre Dumas, Mark Twain, Lenin and Pablo Picasso.
The hike through the typical circular landscape to the Daubensee lake in an almost completely vegetation-free area is delightful. On the Gemmi Pass you are suddenly confronted with the magnificent ring of Valais mountain peaks from the Mischabel to the Weisshorn, Zinalrothorn, Matterhorn and Dent Blanche to Mont Collon. From the hotel you can enjoy a thrilling view of the thermal spa town of Leukerbad, almost 1000 m below. The descent on a good mule track over the steep Gemmiwand is entertaining but very steep.

À la limite du Parc naturel régional de la Sainte-Baume, ce circuit de randonnée mène au Pilon Saint-Clément et à la Barre de Cuers. La vue panoramique est saisissante !

long_description:
Du village de Néoules et son château du 16ème siècle, le parcours permet de rejoindre les crêtes par des sentiers et des pistes au milieu de la Garrigue.

title: Through the Frutigspissen to Adelboden
short_description: Scenic and educational hike along the Engstlige and to lonely farms. The Frutigspissen are on the eastern slope of the Niesen chain.
long_description:
Many game trees have eaten deeply into the soft shale rock that is present here. That is why the usable land between them is only narrow (Spisse = narrow land). Today the Spissen are largely developed and the narrow old Spissen path is partly blocked, which is why the first third of the hike is on the Engstligeufer. Also at the end of the hike, a longer section on hard surface.

From Frutigen railway station, head west to the Engstlige and follow it into the village. Now cross the bridge and follow the western bank of the river. Shortly before Öy, the path moves away from the rushing and murmuring water. After crossing the Gantebach, you turn back towards the river. The continuation through floodplain forest and along gravel bars as well as along the Hostalde bridge to Rohrbach, where you ascend to the Adelbodenstrasse, is extraordinarily varied. The ascent through the forest to the Gempele terrace is extremely steep, where you reach the Spissenweg on the edge of the deeply cut Chratzeregrabe. With only a slight difference in altitude, the trail now turns into the ditch, leads to the particularly narrow Spisse Chratzere and back through a deep cut to Linter. The constant change between tree-covered grassland and open mountain meadows has a soothing effect. On the way on via Ladholz, the path crossing the ditch becomes narrower and narrower. At Otterebach you cross the municipal border between Frutigen and Adelboden. Gross Lohner and Wildstrubel already seem within reach. Via Egereschwand and Ussere Schwand you reach Adelboden.

images.caption: View from the Elsighorn to the Ladholz Spisse

title: Around the Häftli nature reserve
short_description:
Mühelose Wanderung um das seiner Form wegen treffend benannte Naturschutzgebiet Häftli. 8 km weit führt der Uferweg der Alten Aare entlang. Mannigfaltig sind die Einblicke in die fast vollständig unberührte Natur. Dieses Bild lässt die Grösse der Naturlandschaft des Seelandes ahnen, welche vor der Juragewässerkorrektion vorwiegend von Wasser und Moor geprägt war. Unterwegs wenig Hartbelag.
Translate to English
long_description:
Effortless hike around the Häftli nature reserve, aptly named because of its shape. The riverside path leads along the Alte Aare for 8 km. The views of the almost completely untouched nature are manifold. This picture gives an idea of the size of the natural landscape of the Seeland, which before the correction of the Jura waters was predominantly characterised by water and moor. Little hard surface on the way.

Located in the bottleneck between Städtiberg and Aare, Büren a. A. is one of the particularly well-preserved Bernese country towns. We leave the town on the wooden bridge. We walk along the riverside path first to the mouth of the Alte Aare into the Nidau-Büren canal. Then around the swimming pool back to the Alte Aare. The narrowing path leads along the row of trees on the bank. The foremost Jura chain rises very close. At the houses of Witmatt, the course of the river turns to the west. A wide, pleasant path leads to the edge of the village of Meinisberg.
Low on the banks of the Aare, an excellently laid-out footpath opens up the most beautiful parts of the Häftli. It runs between open fields and the narrow riverside forest of alders, poplars, ash trees, oaks, birches and willows. In the Cheer, a fireplace invites you to linger. Past the Kybi Ranch, you reach the road coming from Safnern. You now follow the tarred road along the canal. The detour to the observation tower in Häftli leads to the exact spot where the former Zihl flowed into the Alte Aare. Two orientation boards provide information about plant and animal life. The return path first leads along the road, then it's back to Büren via Meienried.

title: Tour full of contrasts over the Ammerten Pass
short_description: The hike over the Ammerten Pass combines a wealth of contrasts: the trail runs across lonely alpine meadows, rugged scree slopes, along thundering waterfalls and ends in a lovely, wide valley floor. Because of the very steep descent to Ammertent, the route should only be followed in dry weather. Practically natural surface throughout.
long_description:
From the cable car mountain station, the wide plateau of Engstligenalp is crossed in a westerly direction past the mountain. The trail then begins to climb - gently at first, then more and more, until it finally overcomes the barren grassy slopes on the Ammerten ridge in steep hairpin bends. A fantastic panorama awaits you at the top of the pass: looking back, you can see the mighty Lohnergruppe and the wildly craggy Tschingellochtighore above Engstligenalp, and ahead you can see the uppermost part of the Simmental valley: The narrowly cut Ammertetäli stretches between the Ammertespitz and the foothills of the Wildstrubel, with the flank of the Oberlaubhorn, overgrown with grass and forest, rising in the background.
Before the descent, you first follow the broad ridge for a few minutes, after which the path descends very steeply on rocky slate. When it is wet and snowy, this surface is very slippery and offers little grip; the hike should therefore only be made in dry weather. From the Ammerten-Schafberg area onwards, the trail is less steep, first on grass, then over gravel and stable rock slabs. The route always stays on the right side of the Ammertebach stream. Shortly after reaching the timberline, it branches off to the right, leads in a slight counter ascent to Ammerte and from there down to Stalde. Close by is the Barbara Bridge with the roaring waterfalls of the Simme. Along the river you reach the destination, Lenk railway station, through the wide valley floor via Rotebach and past the Kurs- und Sportzentrum (Kuspo).

title: My Dunwich trail running circuit, Suffolk Coast & Heaths AONB
short_description: Get out on the footpaths and trails and explore the extensive woodland, heaths, and wetlands around Suffolk's historic coastal village of Dunwich on England's East Coast.
long_description:
While the beach might be the draw for most visitors to Dunwich, the wild spaces of Westleton Heath, Dunwich Forest, and the wetlands are what appeal to trail runners - or one at least.
This 10.5-mile circuit takes in all these elements and makes a nice change from most of the other running routes available in Suffolk; and while the sea is not the main feature of the trip, there is always the option of cooling off by or in it afterward. 
Conditions underfoot are partly sandy for a lot of the run, but there are also long stretches of grass and a boardwalk in the forest. The elevation profile is much as one would expect in Suffolk: flat as a pancake. 
In all, a pretty good and varied run. Have fun.

title: Saynsteig
short_description: In search of traces of the knights and Romans in Sayn. The trail leads along shady forest paths and natural trails to impressive rocky cliffs. Quiet forest sections alternate with fabulously beautiful views far into the Rhine valley and the Eifel.
long_description:
Highlights:
Sayn castle and palace, former Premonstratensian abbey of Sayn, wide views from Oskarhöhe and "Loh", UNESCO World Heritage Site Limes with reconstructed Roman tower, magnificent stream meadow landscape in the idyllic Brex valley, beautiful forest paths.
The starting point is Sayn Castle, opposite the princely castle park. If you don't park at the castle but at the abbey church, you can get to the start via Brexbachstraße. Via the castle terrace, the path leads up to Sayn Castle, where you can already enjoy the first magnificent view. Continue on a straight path until you reach the Oskarhöhe. Here you will find great views of the abbey church, the romantic "Alt-Sayn", the Rhine valley and the Eifel. The trail crosses the L306 and reaches the edge of the forest at Ottilienhöhe. Now it goes downhill, across a side valley to the Brexbach stream, through a varied stream meadow landscape to the scout camp. A narrow path leads up and meets the Rheinsteig trail. The trail continues uphill to the Upper Germanic-Raetian Limes World Heritage Site with the reconstructed Roman tower. Now the almost level forest path allows you to relax, and the Meisenhof invites you to stop for a break. The following passage across open fields again offers great views over the Rhine Valley. Then the trail descends to Sayn. From the footbridge over the Brexbach, past the Heins Mühle mill museum, it is only a few steps back to the castle.

Again and again we come across historic walls.

title: Panorama trail Gantrisch: the tip for connoisseurs
short_description: A magnificent ridge walk over the wooded hills on the border with the Pre-Alps. Recently renovated section of the former Vevey-Lucerne-Rorschach Alpine rim route.
long_description:
The starting point of the hike, the Gurnigel mountain hut, already offers a unique view of the Gantrisch chain with its rugged rocky outcrops. After a short climb over an alpine ridge, the view expands to the long foothills of the Alps from the Stockhorn to the Ochse and into the Lake Thun basin. The trail now leads through a beautiful mountain forest on an almost level path around the Selib mountain to the ridge path that descends into the Selib mountain saddle.
In a gentle climb you soon reach the Schüpfeflue, the highest elevation on the Pano rama trail. The panoramic view of the extensive forest area, Guggershorn and Schwendelberg, across the Mittelland to the Jura hills and the peaks of the Gantrisch chain is wonderful. In the forest, the trail descends steeply to Süf tenenegg (to Schwefelbergbad 1h) and über Süftene (to Selital-Schwarzebüel 20 min), climbing gently again to another excellent vantage point, Pfyffe (to Schwarzebüel 30 min). The magnificent view of the scattered hamlets of the municipality of Rüschegg is particularly fascinating.
.

In two steep steps you now descend to the hollow of the Horbüelpass (to Otteleuebad 20 min. -Sangernboden 1h15; to Sänggi-Riffenmatt 1h10). Sometimes along the edge of the forest, then again across open pasture, the ridge trail descends to Hällstett (to Sänggi- Riffenmatt 1h10). On the way, you can enjoy the magnificent panoramic view again and again: from Nüneneflue to Kaiseregg, the limestone peaks line up and behind the glistening waters of the Schwarzsee, the jagged rings around the Breccaschlund rise up.
The descent üvia Warmesite (to Brönnti Egg-Hirschmatt 1h10, Mittlisti Site to the Zollhaus bus stop is steep.

title: Nature trail around Niculițel
short_description: When you're in Dobrogea, choose this nature circular trail near the town of Niculitel. It's an easy hike that children will also enjoy.
long_description:
The route is generous in steppe landscapes specific to the territory. You cross areas with downy oak, meadows, and rock clusters. From several viewpoints, you'll be able to spot the Danube Delta or the Saon Monastery.
According to the official route, on the outskirts of the town, there is also the possibility to pitch a tent, off camping, in a place called "La Cimitir".
The route is marked with a blue dot.

title: Sauerland-Höhenflug (Altena - Röhrenspring - Korbach)
short_description: The Sauerland-Höhenflug is considered one of the most beautiful hiking trails in Germany and leads mainly on mountain ridges once across the Sauerland to the Hessian town of Korbach. We have the choice between two different starting points: One route starts in Altena, the other in Meinerzhagen - both then meet in the Homert Nature Park.
long_description:
Here we describe the complete Sauerland-Höhenflug from Altena to Korbach. The alternative entry point in Meinerzhagen, including a map, can also be found on this portal.
We start our hike in the far west of the Sauerland, near the Bergisches Land. From Altena Castle, we walk in a wide arc past Ihmert and through the Neuenrad town forest to Neuenrade. Impressed by views that stretch for kilometres in places, we pass Altenaffeln and reach Hagen, flanked by Krusenberg and Justenberg. Now we continue in a southerly direction around the Schomberg and to the Röhrenspring hiking triangle. Here the alternative route with the starting point in Meinerzhagen meets our path. Through the Homert Nature Park we hike steadily up the mountain ridge to Wenholthausen. Now the forest gradually thins out and we cross several small stream valleys and a beautiful sunken path on the way to Reiste and Bad Fredeburg. High mountains, lookout towers and the secluded solitude of nature characterise the following section of the route to Hallenberg. Here we turn north to reach Medelon past Liesen. The idyllic valley of the Orke accompanies us in the direction of Küstelberg. We then hike over the Kahle Pön, the northernmost point of the Sauerland-Höhenflug, to Düdinghausen. A true river hike awaits us on the last few metres, as along the Bräumecke, Aar and a small side stream we reach Goldhausen and climb the Eisen-Berg. This brings us to the gates of Korbach, where the high-altitude flight ends.

title: The Gamchi - an unspoilt pearl
short_description: The circular hike from Griesalp to Gamchi leads across alpine pastures with great views to an impressive high valley formed as a wide basin. Craggy slopes and mighty rock formations characterise the face of this barren, largely untouched landscape.
long_description:
From the bus terminus at Griesalp, you alternate between narrow mountain paths and gravel roads used for alpine farming to Dünde-Mittelberg and from there über the Underi to Oberi Bundalp. The sparse landscape is full of charm: Extensive scree slopes and floodplain forests are a feature of the landscape, with cattle cavorting on extensive alpine pastures in between. A much less steep ascent takes you to the Bundl;ger and finally to the Oberloch, where the scenery changes abruptly: Behind a hilltop, the wide basin of the Gamchi opens up. The thin sward is interspersed with wide debris cones of several wild boars. The magnificent landscape offers charming silence and wonderful views. At the end of the valley you can see the Gamchi glacier and above it, between the Gspaltenhorn and the Bluuml;emlisalp massif, the sharply cut Gamchilücke.
On a narrow but not too steep mountain path you descend to the Gamchihütte on the valley floor, then up üover the Gamchibach stream out of the valley to Bürgli. Impressive rock formations bear witness to the elemental forces to which the rock was subjected during the folding of the Alps. Above the Bundstamm, instead of taking the alpine path, you take the path that leads down to the Gamchibach, but stay on the right side of the stream and at Steineberg you reach the path again that leads to Golderli. From there, it takes just a few minutes to get back to Griesalp.

images.caption: The rock faces in the valley of the Gamchi stream

title: In the footsteps of Queen Victoria on the Osborne Estate
short_description: A very enjoyable walk that elegantly complements the tour of the Osborne Estate on the Isle of Wight, the summer residence of Queen Victoria and Prince Albert, and one of the Queen's favourite residences;
long_description:
The tour starts from the terraced gardens of the palace, an opportunity to admire the circular fountains, the flower gardens, a superb pergola. As you walk away from the building, look back to take in the palace in all its grandeur.
The walk follows, in the first part, the path that the Queen and her children used to take every day to the sea, to the little bay that is now called Queen's Bay. This walk was one of the Queen's favourite moments of the day, when she made various notes in her diary about the surrounding nature and her mood.
The small beach that opens up after about 800 metres of paved road served as a place of worship for the queen and where her children learned to swim. Swimming is not allowed, but if you're on holiday with the kids, the little ones can play on the beach. There's also a café with teas, ice cream and English pastries, as well as the Queen's elegantly restored dressing room.
You can arc back through the forest, still on the cobbled road, in a very gentle climb. Admire the trees, listen to the birds and watch the silence - that way you're likely to get a deer in your path!

images.caption: Osborne House, view from the alley leading to the beach

title: On the Panorama Trail Kiental-Lake Thun
short_description: Long, panoramic hike with no major differences in altitude from the idyllic Kiental valley via the sunny Faltsche and through the shady Suldgraben to the panoramic balcony of Aeschiried. High above the deep blue Lake Thun, the route leads through forests and over alpine pastures down to Därligen, offering many views and vistas along the way.
long_description:
Ideal hiking trails, forest roads and access roads alternate at irregular intervals. Short hard-surface sections also outside the settlements.

In Kiental you leave the bus stop out of the valley and climb, sometimes on the alpine road, then again via shortcuts, to the Hubel huts. The subsequent hike through flowery hay meadows is a delight. Looking back, you can see the firn fields of the Blüemlisalp glistening in the sun. A gentle up and down leads to the large alpine dairy Härggis-Allmi, from where the view expands to the toy-small houses in the Kandertal and the Niesen chain. Through the Haasele forest you cross the Richebach ditch and soon descend to Faltsche on an unfortunately asphalted road. Via Weeggers, the path is now almost level as it enters the Suldtal valley. At Suldweid you cross the stream and enjoy the lush vegetation (nature reserve) as you hike out of the valley.
After the short climb to the valley road, you soon reach the Aeschiried lookout point, from where you can enjoy a magnificent view of Lake Thun. The continuation along old alpine paths and newer forest roads to Hellbode and, along the lower edge of the marshy Lammweid, down to Chüngstuel is pleasant. On the way, Sigriswilgrat, Sieben Hengste, Beatenberg, Niederhorn and Harder were only glimpsed, but now the whole lake landscape from Thun in the west to Brienz in the east can be seen. You still have to cross the Leissiger Bachgränben, which is flooded after thunderstorms and during snowmelt (a new suspension bridge crosses the Spissigraben), but from Meielisalp you can already sense the near destination of the long hike. With a splendid view of the Bödeli and the Harder, you descend via Egghubel to Därligen on Lake Thun.

Circular hike to the Napf
short_description: This circular hike leads around the Fankhusgraben to the "Rigi of the Emmental", the Napf. This cone of debris is a geological remnant from the Miocene period and offers impressive panoramic views.
long_description:
From the Fankhaus bus stop in Leen, the route leads uphill through forest and pastures, past the Steli and Ober Stutz farms to Chrüzbode. The trail then leads along the ridge that marks the border between the cantons of Bern and Lucerne. A short climb to the summit of the Champechnubel is worthwhile to enjoy a spectacular view of the Prealps and High Alps. On the eastern side, you can see Lucerne's Grosse Fontannetal, which is famous for its amateur gold panning.
The contrast between the two cantons can be seen in their forest management after the storm of 1999: Bern removed the damaged trees, while Lucerne let nature take its course and gave the Napf area a wild character.
At the summit of the Napf, there is a panoramic view over the tangle of valleys of the Emmental and the Lucerne hinterland, against the backdrop of the Alps and the Jura. The initially steep descent then turns into a pleasant panoramic trail that leads back to Fankhaus via Unter Höhstullen and Buechli.

images.caption: View from the summit of the Napf in the Emmental

title: Ödemiş Gölcük Plateau - Gölcük Lake
short_description: A plateau covered with forests and a göl located right in the middle of the plateau... Located at an altitude of approximately 1100 altitude and formed by tectonic movements, the natural feature Gölcük Gölü çphase is located in the centre of the plateau.
long_description:
Gölcük Gölcük Gölü located in the province of Ödemiş in Izmir attracts attention with its natural beauty. In addition to its natural beauty, this place is also of great importance with its historical, cultural, cultural, and natural richness. The region is also important with its proximity to Birgi, an important settlement of the Aydinogullari Principality and Ottoman period, and Sart, the centre of the Lydian Kingdom. It is also known as a region where horse breeding was widespread during the Karamanoğulları Principality.
Gölcük does not disappoint those who want to do activities such as nature walks, camping and picnics. If you are looking for nature walks routes in Izmir, it is possible to find routes with göl and mountain views in Gölcük Plateau and Gölcük Gölü çphase. 
This route is just one of the routes you can do during the day. On the route, you have the opportunity to enjoy the view from the top of the hill and get a different perspective of the mountains.

title: Medieval sites on the Aare riverside path
short_description: A splendid riverside hike, alternating between the left and right banks of the Aare.
long_description:
The starting point of the hike is the picturesque medieval town of Wangen a.A. with its beautiful gatehouses and the old, covered wooden bridge. Along the way are Aarwangen Castle and Wynau Church. The destination is Murgenthal in Aargau. Wonderful river landscape on the way. Little hard surface outside towns.

From Wangen a.A. station through the plane tree avenue to the historic centre of the town and through the Zytgloggeturm and Brückentor to the covered, wooden bridge. A short detour westwards to the vicarage (the former Benedictine abbey) is worthwhile. Now the right-bank and left-bank routes separate (both signalled). The route described here has less hard surface and offers a better view of the town. Beyond the bridge on a paved path along the river bank, along the swimming pool and the army area, across the canal and on a natural path downstream. Later, this path narrows to a narrow path that leads directly to the Walliswilsteg on the banks of the Aare. Here the right-bank path from Walliswil bei Wangen joins. The two villages of Walliswil on this side and the other side of the Aare have the same name origin, as in earlier times foreign settlers who used the Celtic-Roman language were called Walen or Welsche.
A road now leads through the particularly charming landscape to the Berkenbrücke. As you cross the bridge, you have a beautiful view of the Vogelraupfi, an artificially raised breeding and resting place for water birds in the middle of the Aare (nature reserve) due to the power station damming. The angle near Stadnoenz, where the wild Önz pours into the mazy flowing Aare, is also particularly beautiful. From a small promontory, there is an impressive view over the water and the varied riverbank landscape to the blue-green Jura with its striking riverbank. Soon, high-voltage power lines spoil the beautiful picture. At the Bannwil power station, the water masses thunder down into the depths - an impressive spectacle. Over the weir you change to the left bank of the Aare and after 400 m branch off again onto the riverside path. The pretty little church of Bannwil sits enthroned on a spur above the long street village with its splendid old farmhouses. In Niderfeld, the path becomes a narrow path again and after the large loop of the Aare, you can already see Aarwangen Castle reflected in the water. This was once a moated castle and later served the Bernese as a bailiwick. Along the right bank of the broadly flowing Aare you reach the nature reserve of the Ober Wynau power station, the Wynauer Rank, one of the most beautiful natural river landscapes, and the church of Wynau. It is one of the oldest churches in the Oberaargau (around 1100). In 1912, wall paintings were discovered in the choir that had been destroyed during the Reformation. The renovation of 1979 brought about an extensive return to the Romanesque style. St. Urban bricks (13th century) set into the wall indicate that the building belonged to the monastery. In Murgenthal, you climb up from the bank of the Aare to the railway station in front of the beautiful covered wooden bridge.

title: Tateyama Chinguruma Road (Tengu-daira horizontal road) From Murodo to Tengu-daira
short_description: As the name suggests, this is a horizontal path with very few ups and downs, but it is well-known to those in the know for its beautiful colours, with chinquapin in summer and autumn leaves in autumn.
long_description:
This is a leisurely downhill course that takes about 30-40 minutes to reach Tengudaira Sanso. Compared to other trails such as the Mikuriga Pond Circular Course and the course up Mt Oudake, there are fewer climbers on this course and it is well known by those in the know. However, those who come to Murodo without mountaineering gear can easily walk here and enjoy the natural flower garden of chinguruma in summer. Once you have landed in Murodo, you should first gather information at the Tateyama Nature Conservation Centre on the flowering status of the flowers and any remaining snowfall. The trail to Otani/Tengu-daira initially descends along a steep wooden path. After a short descent to an altitude of around 2300 metres, the path changes to level cobblestones. Please note that entry to Jigokudani (Hell Valley), which is halfway along the trail, has been prohibited since 2011.
On entering the Chinguruma Road (Tengu-daira Horizontal Road), you are greeted by a natural flower garden with lovely white Chinguruma flowers spreading out on the mountain slopes during the summer season. Compared to Murodo, which attracts many visitors, this route is less crowded, so you can take your time to appreciate the flowers and enjoy the surrounding wilderness. Not only the flowers, but also the gases and sea of clouds rising up from below at a height of 2000 metres, coupled with the magnificent European Alps-like scenery around, are fantastic and beautiful. If you are lucky, you may even spot a thunderbird.
One word of caution when boarding the bus at Tengudaira after hiking. If you want to take the Tateyama Kogen Bus from Tengu-daira to Murodo, you need to make a reservation at the Tengu-daira Sanso near the bus stop.

title: High altitude hike over the Churzenberg
On the Napfbergland border trail
short_description: Wonderful hike from the Ilfis to the Emmental, on the border between the cantons of Bern and Lucerne. Enjoy magnificent views of the surrounding mountains and valleys along the way.
long_description:
The Kambly cookie factory and the changing art exhibitions make Trubschachen famous far beyond the country's borders. But the charming old buildings along the road towards Langnau are also worth a visit. From the train station, cross the Ilfis and follow the river to the mouth of the Trueb, where a steep path leads up through the forest. At Bärgenhüsi, you reach a steadily ascending road that leads past Houenenegg. A road leads steeply up to Chäserenegg, where the path narrows to an alpine path and runs along the cantonal border to Rämisgummen on the mountain ridge. A breathtaking panoramic view awaits you here.
Following the border, the hiking trail meanders over the eastern flank of the wooded Pfyffer and leads down to Grosshorben. From there, it climbs up to Wachthubel, where the trail runs just below the ridge. Here, the Schrattenflue, Schibengütsch and Hohgant are close enough to touch. The hike ends in the picturesque village of Schangnau, idyllically situated at the end of the valley.

title: On the Jura High Trail
short_description: Long hike over the crest of the Chasseral range. Green meadows, woods, pastures with groups of trees and the tree-free hillside provide a pleasant change of scenery;
long_description:
Part of the Jura Trail Dielsdorf (ZH)-Hauenstein-Weissenstein-Chasseral-Ste-Croix-Col du Marchairuz-Borex (VD), which is one of the most frequented continuous routes in Switzerland. Natural surface throughout. For the Frinvilliers-Les Coperies-Place centrale variant (natural path), allow 3h40.

From the Frinvillier-Taubenloch stop down to the little village of Frinvillier. At the time of the Römer, two important roads crossed here. One led from Avenches über die Montagne de Diesse to Solothurn, the other from Petinesca über die Pierre Pertuis to the Rhine. Cross the Suze on the bridge and after a few steps turn onto the path that leads steeply uphill in the forest. At Les Coperies, the landscape changes to the typical pastureland of the area. A gentle ascent takes you via La Ragie to the southern ridge of the Chasseral. On the panoramic high trail, you reach the Cabane du Jura and the Classe de Pierrefeu hiking trail junction. Past the pasture stables Les Colisses, the trail leads over several humps to the crossroads above La Neuve and the mighty directional and television antenna on the Chasseral. At 1607.4 m, its summit is the highest point in the Bernese Jura and at the same time the second highest elevation in the Swiss Jura. The panoramic view is total and overwhelming, especially when a sea of fog envelops the lowlands of the Mittelland in autumn.

images.caption: Stone walls in the Chasseral region

title: Forest nature trail on the Murg Münchwilen
About Mont Sujet
short_description: Wonderful hike over the mountain ridge south of the Chasseral chain. Two stately farm villages with typical Jura houses frame the tour. On the way, open pastures with groups of trees and a magnificent view of the Chasseral and the Alps. Hard surface only in the area of the settlements.
long_description: At the bend in the road south of the centre of Orvin stand the so-called Maisons des Sarrasins, supposedly the oldest houses in the village spared by the fire of 1724. The village with its typical Jura houses, the beautiful fountains (19th century), the pretty inn signs and the proud church (1722) is well worth a visit. From the centre of the village, head uphill to the Jurassic Trail and follow it first below, then above the road across mountain pastures to Les Prés-d'Orvin. Shortly after the Bellevue bus stop, a wide track branches off the road to the left and leads in large loops up to the Noire Combe farm. Through a pasture hollow, at the Bergerie du Bas, you reach the hollow between the two Mont Sujet peaks, which also bears the name Noire Combe. At the Bergerie du Haut, you climb on an indistinct path directly to the highest point of the western summit of Mont Sujet. The panoramic view does not need to fear comparison with that from the Chasseral: the lakes of the Jura fringe, the Central Plateau, the Pre-Alps and the High Alps show themselves from their most beautiful side. The descent is in a south-westerly direction to the Combe Robin farm. A somewhat bumpy forest path leads down to La Rochalle, where you first follow the road towards Diesse, but then turn westwards across a wooded pasture and through an avenue to the well-preserved village of Nods.

images.caption: View from Mont Sujet to the Chasseral summit

title: Through the impressive Combe Grède
short_description: Mountain trail in the Combe Grède. On the ascent, a high limestone wall is climbed in the narrow gorge on rocky steps and metal ladders. Over high pastures you reach the Chasseral crest with its magnificent views. The descent leads across sparse mountain pastures and through dark fir forests to the valley floor. Hardly any hard surface. The Combe Grède is not passable in winter! Caution is also advised in bad weather.
