title: Where Bern almost still borders France
short_description:
Sehr schöner Übergang aus dem oberen Vallon de St-Imier über den südwestlichen Zipfel der Freiberge an den Doubs. Der Wanderweg quert drei gänzlich verschiedene Landschaftstypen: Da ist das Hochplateau der Freiberge mit seinen weiten Weiden. Dann geht es durch die engen bewaldeten Comben längs des Baches La Ronde. Und schliesslich endet die Route am stillverträumten Stausee des Doubs im Biaufond, an der Grenze zu Frankreich. Bergwanderweg ab La Ferrière. Wenig Hartbelag.
Translate to English
long_description:
Very beautiful crossing from the upper Vallon de St-Imier over the south-western tip of the Franches-Montagnes to the Doubs. The trail crosses three completely different types of landscape: There is the high plateau of the Franches-Montagnes with its wide pastures. Then it goes through the narrow wooded Comben along the stream La Ronde. And finally, the route ends at the tranquil Doubs reservoir in Biaufond, on the border with France. Mountain trail from La Ferrière. Little hard surface.

Renan is the highest village in the St. Immer valley, called Le Vallon by the locals. From the station, keep above the railway line out of the valley and turn towards the woods at the edge of the village. Soon a track branches off into the forest. Past the drinking water reservoir, it overcomes the 100 m difference in altitude to the La Puce mountain inn, where the plateau is already reached. Follow the asphalt road in a northerly direction. But only 10 min later, along a bushy hedge, you turn into a faint depression, follow a pasture wall and cross the pasture on indistinct tracks to the houses on the edge of the Combe du Pélu. A low Jura fold separates the Combe from the plateau of La Ferrière. From the saddle of the hill, you can easily make out the mostly trackless continuation across the pasture past the Sous les Planes farm, but the nearby houses of La Ferrière serve as an orientation aid. Immediately after the station of La Ferrière, a neighbourhood road turns left away from the main road and descends into the Combe du Valanvron to the stream La Ronde. The direction of the hike is now set, as the route always remains at the bottom of the valley. Via Le Fief, and later along the banks of the muddy Cul des Prés pond, you descend steadily. The wild, stony Combe de Biaufond is conquered via ladders, footbridges and stairs. On the marshy valley floor with a heavily overgrown pond, a footpath leads to the houses of Biaufond, which are already in the canton of Jura. The romantic landscape with the lovely reservoir is incomparably beautiful.

images.caption: Peace and quiet: On the Doubs near Biaufond

title: Through two gorges to the winegrowing village of Twann
short_description: Varied hike through the wooded Combe du Pilouvi to the vast former high moorland plain of the Montagne de Diesse.
long_description:
Prächtige view of the Jura dörferns at the foot of the Chasseral and Mont Sujet. Prêles is the start of the wild Twannbach gorge, through which you descend steeply to the shores of Lake Biel. Take care in both gorges in wet weather (risk of sliding!). Hardly any hard surface.

From the train or boat station in La Neuveville in front of Bern House. Then walk through the picturesque old town through the town arch to the Tour Rouge. Now past the Catholic church, vineyards and water fountains on a stairway up to the Château. This bears witness to the tensions between the counts of Neuchâtel and the prince-bishops of Basel. The counts had built a border fortress in Nugerol (near Le Landeron) around 1260. The bishops did the same 20 years later with the «Schlossberg». Around 1312, the town of Neuenstadt was built below it. The counts responded in 1325 by building the small town of Le Landeron.
After the road loop, climb into the forest and stop in the narrow Combe du Pilouvi, which also forms the border with Canton Neuchâtel. A steep climb crosses the road that leads to Lignières in Neuchâtel. The path continues more gently upwards to a clearing (beautiful view of Lake Neuchâtel) and slightly downwards to the Bas de la Praye farm. The path is almost flat as it crosses the edge of the vast Montagne de Diesse. In Prbecirc;les, the trail first continues parallel to the Lamboingstrasse, then a good road leads to the entrance to the wild Twannbachschlucht gorge, through which you reach the winegrowing village of Twann.

.

title: On the Lake Biel shore path
Route planned on September 25, 2015

Forest paths, far-reaching views, feelings of happiness.
Atmospheric ridge walk along the Schönbuch ridge with magnificent views into the Ammer valley and of the elevations of the Swabian Alb. Beautiful vantage points, resting benches, barbecue areas and refreshment stops round off the tour
.
long_description: On an atmospheric ridge walk along the southern Schönbuch ridge from Herrenberg to Unterjesingen, the Schönbuch presents itself as a light riparian forest. Again and again, breathtaking views open up into the wide Ammer valley, down to the magnificent meadows of the "Swabian orchard paradise" and to the bluish shimmering wall of the Swabian Alb. Wonderful resting benches invite you to enjoy the view, and there are nice places to stop at various points.

title: Across the language border
short_description: A varied hike over the Montagne de Romont, the mountain ridge between Montoz and Bözingenberg. Ascents and descents are in the forest, the main part of the trail is in park-like Jura meadows, which make hiking a real pleasure. Little hard surface.
long_description: From the Reuchenette-Péry station in a southerly direction to the bridge ücke over the Le Terbez stream. On the sunny side lies the stately village of Péry, which is mentioned in documents as early as 884 as a donation to the abbey of Moutier-Grandval. The 2 km long and equally wide rocky basin of the Rondchâtel gorge is considered a particularly beautiful example of a cross-cutting through a Jura fold. Beyond the stream, a steady but steep wooden path leads through the forest of Le Bambois to the pastures of Les Oeuches (pt. 918) and gently downhill to the village of Plagne, situated in an elevated position on the sunny slope. After an ascent over pastures and through a strip of woodland, you are in for a wonderful hike through a park-like landscape with scattered holiday homes. The view across the Aare valley to the Bucheggberg, the hills of the Emmental and the Alps becomes more extensive with every step. Shortly after the mountain inn on the Montagne de Romont, you reach the highest point of the hike at the Bern/Solothurn cantonal border. The boundary stones deserve attention. The linguistic border has already been announced with German field names. On a shady forest path, the trail descends over the mountain ridge to the Wäsmeli car park. In a few minutes you reach the Stierenberg mountain inn on the Grenchen-Grenchenberg road.

images.caption: Gentle Jura ridge with park-like landscape

title: From Hinterstein to Schrecksee (outdooractive-podcast-Tour 1)
short_description: We walk along an alpine trail with wire rope insurance in places to the Schrecksee lake in the Allgäu High Alps.
long_description: We set out on this challenging hike from the southern end of Hinterstein. This hidden mountain village has preserved its original character over the centuries and offers a wonderful backdrop with the Allgäu High Alps nature reserve. On our way to the Schrecksee lake, we experience the full spectrum of this fascinating and rugged landscape. This picturesque lake is the only Alpine lake with a real island. Its water is icy cold all year round - perhaps that's where the name comes from. Green slopes stretch across the plain from the slopes of the peaks framing the lake. And if you're lucky, you can spot marmots and chamois. In this unsurpassed idyll we can recover from the rather steep ascent - but: it's worth the effort!

title: Grimsel Pass - in the footsteps of the muleteers
long_description:
Mountain hiking trail from Guttannen. A hike through the Haslital brings back the days of the muleteers. The wild nature, the sights along the way (Guttannen Crystal Museum, Gärstenegg Crystal Cave), the technical achievements (reservoirs in the Grimsel region) and the hospitable rest stops make hiking the historic Grimsel Route an experience. Due to the danger of avalanches, the route can only be hiked from mid-summer to late autumn. Little hard surface.

From the Innertkirchen station or post office, the route initially follows the banks of the Aare into the valley. From Achistein via Üsseri and Inneri Urweid to Boden, the route follows the historic mule track, reactivated in 1992-1995. In the village of Boden, you cross the Grimselstrasse and the old Aare bridge to the farmstead Under der Hoflue. Here the old mule track becomes visible again. In the hamlet of Sunnsyten, access is possible to Guttannen, where almost every house around the post office square is decorated with a meaningful saying in Haslimund style. Guttannen used to be an important stopping place for mule traffic. This was organised down to the last detail. An "alpine caravan" comprised several pack mule units (a pack mule servant with four pack mules). At the beginning of the 18th century, it is said that more than 200 pack animals crossed the pass every week. In bad weather, so-called "Lägelträger" (Lagel = oval wooden vessel for transporting wine; 2 Lägel = 1 Saum) stood in, carrying man loads of 50 kg (!). Via Bärfallen and Tschingelmad, the trail continues without an excessive ascent to the beautiful stone Schwarzbrunnenbrigg and, climbing more steeply, past the power station headquarters to Hotel Handegg.
Interesting features on the following route: At Säumerstein, the muleteers joined together in larger groups because of the difficult terrain. The Hälen Platten, a glacier-cut area, was considered the most arduous part of the Grimsel Trail (steps chiselled into the rock with inscription: 1838 L. Agassiz).
Interesting view of the pass road, where a hanging footbridge was originally planned around the stick. However, Marzoli, the foreman responsible for the section of road, preferred to trust his black powder and unceremoniously blew away the rock in 1894 (hence the name Marzolisflue). Also worth seeing are the photogenic stone Böglisbrückli and the Gärstenegg crystal crevice (book in advance on tel. 033 982 20 11), the flagstone path carved into the rock along the Räterichsbodensee, the dam at the Grimsel Hospiz, which is soon to be raised by 23 m, finally the fjord-like landscape of the Grimselsee and the panoramic view of the Bernese, Uri and Valais Alps from the Grimselpass summit. The descent to Obergesteln in the Goms is scenic, but requires an additional hiking time of 2h.

title: वसुंधरा फॉल्स ट्रैक
short_description: वसुंधरा फॉल्स एक पौराणिक झरना है जो बद्रीना थ-माना-सतोपंथ ट्रैकिंग मार्ग पर स्थित है। ऐसा माना जात ा है की महाभारत युद्ध के बाद जब पांडव स्वर्ग जा रहे थे तो सहदेव ने यहाँ पर अ पने प्राण त्यागे थे।
long_description:
वसुंधरा जलप्रपात भारत के उत्तराखंड राज्य के चमोली ज़िले में स्थित एक जलप्रपात है। यह बद्रीनाथ-सतोपंथ ट्रैक मार्ग पर पड़ता है और भारत के आखिरी गाँव माणा से 6 किलोमीटर की दूरी पर है। 400 फीट की ऊंचाई से गिरने वाला यह झरना कुछ ही दूर बहती हुई विशाल नीली अलकनंदा नदी में जा कर मिल जाता है। आमतौर पर बद्रीनाथ मंदिर आने वाले अधिकांश यात्री इसको देखने भी ज़रूर जाते हैं।
वसुंधरा फॉल्स का सबसे अच्छा ट्रेल मार्ग माणा गाँव से शुरू होता है। माणा भारत का आखिरी गाँव है और बद्रीनाथ शहर से सिर्फ 5 किलोमीटर दूर है। बद्रीनाथ शहर से माणा तक पैदल या फिर किराये की टैक्सी से आना संभव है। माणा गाँव में अलकनन्दा नदी और सरस्वती नदी का संगम होता है जिसे केशव प्रयाग तीर्थ कहते हैं। इसके ऊपर चट्टान का एक प्राकृतिक पुल बना है जिसे भीम पुल कहते हैं। यही भीम पुल वसुंधरा फॉल्स ट्रैक का आरंभ बिंदु है।
वसुंधरा फॉल्स का ट्रेल मार्ग कुल 5 किलोमीटर लम्बा है और अच्छे रखरखाव वाला है। यह ट्रेल मार्ग सरल से मध्यम कठिनाई स्तर वाला है। यह ट्रेल बहुत ही सुन्दर है। पूरा रास्ता नीली ठंडी अलकनन्दा नदी के किनारे से होकर गुजरता है। यहाँ की हिमालयी हवा बेहद साफ़ और स्वास्थ्यवर्धक है। झरने के आसपास का लैंडस्केप भी सुन्दर और जादुई है जो हाइकर्स को बहुत पसंद आता है।
वसुंधरा फॉल्स का ट्रैक तड़के ही शुरू करना चाहिए ताकि वह पर ज्यादा से ज्यादा समय गुजारा जा सके और शाम को आराम से वापस माणा गाँव या बद्रीनाथ लौटा जा सकें।

images.caption: माणा गांव का भीम पुल वसुंधरा ट्रैक का आरंभ बिंदु है, चमोली जिला, उत्तराखंड, भारत।
माणा गांव का प्रवेशद्वार और पृष्ठभूमि में दिखती हुई वसुंधरा फॉल्स की ट्रेल, उत्तरांचल, भारत।

title: The Kali via ferrata for children in Ramsau am Dachstein
short_description: The Kali children's via ferrata on the Sattelberg (1253 m) near Ramsau am Dachstein is perfect for spending an eventful day with children.
long_description: The Kali via ferrata on the Sattelberg was set up especially for children. However, it is also a challenge for adults, because the most difficult part of the route is C/D! The boulders over which the trail was built are exposed on the east side of the wooded ridge of the Sattelberg above Ramsau am Dachstein. The descent leads along a nature and environmental adventure trail that has also been set up especially for children. Orientation is easy as the trail is excellently signposted and so is the nature trail. The Sattelberghütte is a refreshment stop directly on the trail. The old flour mill near the entrance can be visited every Friday.

title: Gentle hills - hospitable houses
short_description:
Ausgiebige Höhenwanderung über den langen Weiderücken des Montoz. Mit Ausnahme des Aufstiegs nur geringe Höhendifferenzen. Unterwegs reichhaltige Rundsicht von den Vogesen und vom Schwarzwald über die Bergketten des Jura bis zur Aare-Ebene und zu den Alpen. Für Stärkung sorgen zahlreiche Berggasthäuser. Wenig Hartbelag.
Translate to English
long_description:
An extensive high-altitude hike over the long meadow ridge of the Montoz. Except for the ascent, only slight differences in altitude. On the way, a sumptuous panoramic view from the Vosges and the Black Forest over the Jura mountain ranges to the Aare plain and the Alps. Numerous mountain inns for refreshment. Few hard surfaces.

Ascend southwards from Tavannes station to the source of the river Birs and continue towards Pierre Pertuis. A forest track now leads steeply upwards to the mountain pasture of Le Grimm, then on a grassy track to the cabin (Montoz hut). The view of the villages of Tavannes, Loveresse and Reconvilier as well as Le Fuet, Bellelay and Tramelan slightly further away is impressive. Then pass through a stretch of woodland to reach the Métairie de Werdt mountain restaurant with its magnificent view of the Chasseral mountains, the Seeland and the Alps.
Via the Métairie de Malleray on the northern mountain range of the Montoz, one reaches the SAC hut «La Rochette» in the immediate vicinity of the highest point of the Montoz (1,327 m). A special treat awaits as the hike continues across meadows and past the mountain farms of Bergerie de Bévilard, Montagne de Sorvilier and La Bergerie to Pré Richard. The closeness of the language border becomes clear from the dual names of the farmsteads. An asphalt path now leads past the mountain restaurant of La Bluée (Tiefmatt) to the other side of the ridge and onwards to Längschwang. At this point one branches off to the South and reaches the Untergrenchenberg.

title: Through the home of the greatest clown of all time
short_description:
Abwechslungsreiche Wanderung durch die sanfte Flanke des Moron. Unterwegs malerische Jura-Dörfer - darunter der Geburtsort des weltberühmten Clowns Grock -, weite Weiden, lichte Hochebenen und dunkle Wälder. Längere Hartbelag-Strecken in den Dörfern, auf dem Plateau von Champoz und vom Ausgang der Combe Fabet weg.
Translate to English
long_description:
Varied hike through the gentle flank of the Moron. Along the way, picturesque Jura villages - including the birthplace of the world-famous clown Grock -, wide pastures, light plateaus and dark forests. Longer hard-surface stretches in the villages, on the Champoz plateau and away from the exit of the Combe Fabet.

Reconvilier used to be mostly agricultural. The horse market in Chaindon, where the village's church is also worth seeing, was particularly important. Today it is considered an important industrial centre of the Tavannes Valley. From Reconvilier station in a north-easterly direction up through the village, down to the stream La Trame and somewhat steeper up to Loveresse. The well-preserved farming village of Pontenet is almost at the same altitude. The view of the Tavannes valley and the Montoz and Moron mountain ranges is magnificent. Now begins the gentle, partly trackless ascent through the pastures and wooded clearings of the Pâturage du Droit. At point 867 you cross the Malleray-Moron road. Keeping the same direction, you pass the Sous Moron farm and reach the almost unspoilt farming village of Champoz.
Once again, you have to take the road towards Moutier for 1.3 km before a track leads along the valley floor through pastures with groves of trees. In the wild gorge of the Combe Fabet, the path becomes increasingly bumpy. Finally, it joins the main Perrefitte-Moutier road. Follow this past the Chalière chapel to Moutier railway station.

title: Via the Arlberg via ferrata to the Weißschrofenspitze in the Lechtal Alps
short_description: High above St. Anton am Arlberg runs this long, difficult and exposed via ferrata. Always following the course of the ridge it ends at the Weißschrofenspitze, but there is still a There is, however, a crisp descent in the direction of the mountain railway.
long_description: The Arlberg via ferrata leads high above St. Anton am Arlberg over a ridge almost two kilometres long to the Weißschrofenspitze. From the summit of the Weißschrofenspitze, a quite difficult descent path leads in the direction of the mountain railway. With the Arlberg cable cars, you can shorten the ascent and descent times enormously, but you are bound to their operating times. The trail always runs along the ridge. A stable weather situation is therefore a prerequisite for an ascent. The trail is excellently secured and partly very exposed. There are restaurants at the cable car stations where you can stop for a bite to eat. The panorama with the surrounding mountains is fantastic throughout the entire tour. On a clear day, you can even see as far as Lake Constance. Orientation is easy in good visibility, but in poor visibility it quickly becomes a challenge between the Vallugagrat mountain station and the entrance.

title: Via the Johann (south face) via ferrata to the Dachsteinwarte
short_description: The Johann (Südwand) via ferrata on the Hohe Dachstein is a particularly varied and interesting, but also very difficult and long climb.
long_description: The climb to the Dachsteinwarte via the Johann- or Südwandklettersteig promises wire acrobatics at its best. The "Johann" is a very long, strenuous and varied via ferrata. The key section is right at the beginning of the entry (E): a slope has to be climbed. The route to the entrance also requires full concentration, because there is often old snow here and climbing sections up to I (UIAA) have to be overcome. It may be advisable to bring light crampons and an ice axe. The route runs along the south-facing exposed face of the Hohe Dachstein. Orientation is easy up to the top of the wall, but the approach to the start is only marked in places. In poor visibility, finding the mountain station from the Seetalerhütte can be a challenge. The protection on the Johann via ferrata itself is impeccable. 700 m of wire rope and 250 step pins make the "Johann" a via ferrata highlight for very skilled via ferrata walkers. Strength, endurance and a head for heights are prerequisites for the "Johann". As we leave the trail directly at the Seetalerhütte (also known as the Dachsteinwartehütte), it is a good idea to reward ourselves with a stop there.

title: Cachoeira do Sossego Trail in the Chapada Diamantina
short_description: Discover the largest waterfall of Rio Ribeirão, in the Chapada Diamantina, and enjoy the adventure that é get to this beautiful waterfall.
long_description:
The trail begins in the town of Lençóis and has about 14 kilometers. It is considered a moderate level, but you have to be very careful at the end of the trail, as it goes along the rocks of the river. After the physical exhaustion, you will be rewarded with the beautiful Sossego Waterfall, a 20-meter high waterfall that forms a large natural pool, perfect for bathing. Its waters fall in the middle of a cânion formed by the Ribeir ão River and the rocks around it are great places to sunbathe after bathing in the cold waters. On the way back, the route passes by the famous Ribeirirão do Meio, a natural slide created by the river, surrounded by several pools for bathing.
The presence of guides is not mandatory, but often recommended, as the trail is not well marked. A guide will also add more value to your experience by bringing history and information about the place.

title: Climbing up the Tămașul Mare Peak, in Piatra Craiului Mountains
short_description: The route to the peak of Tămașul Mare is one of the most ignored in Piatra Craiului Mountains, but only those who try this climb get to see some unique panoramas with the main mountain ridge.
long_description:
The path climbs mercilessly through the forest for almost half of the route. About 15 minutes before the summit, you get to a clearing from where you can capture the first image of the Piatra Craiului ridge.
You then reach a place that seems to be the top; it is not: you still have 100 meters to climb to reach the signpost.
Then follows a rather boring descent, through a lot of wild vegetation, a clear sign of its unpopularity. However, its offers some breathtaking panoramas, rarely seen by hikers.

title: Valley circuit around Bad Liebenzell
short_description: This Nordic walking tour is ideal for advanced walkers. Starting from Bad Liebenzell, you have some uphill sections, great views and the wildly romantic Lengenbach valley ahead of you.
long_description: We start our Nordic walking tour at the Bad Liebenzell train station and turn right into the Kurpark, which we walk through to its end. Bad Liebenzell is situated in a sunny extension of the Nagold valley. The castle from the 13th century is a striking landmark. We cross the B463 on the right and walk along the Bad Liebenzell/Beinberg connecting road for a while before turning left onto a farm track marked with a blue rhombus into the Kollbachtal valley. We walk alongside the stream until we reach the Kollbach bridge, then continue to the Kollbrunnen. From there we walk steeply uphill on the Goldschmiedweg to Zainen and reach a hikers' car park. We now follow the signs for tour "4" to the Kohlplatte with its refuge, cross the road and walk to the sports field. Continue to the rest area at the Rohrbrunnen, from where the yellow rhombus trail markings lead us to the Maisenbacher Sägmühle. Through the wild and romantic Lengenbach valley, we return to Bad Liebenzell railway station.

title: The Imst via ferrata on the Maldonkopf in the Lechtal Alps
short_description: The Imster via ferrata on the Maldonkopf is one of the classics of modern sport via ferratas. 800 metres of climbing await ambitious via ferrata climbers with breathtaking views.
long_description: The Imster via ferrata on the Maldonkopf (2632 m) was already established at the end of the 1980s. Nevertheless, it can already be described as a sport via ferrata. Excellent protection, breathtaking routing and exposure are the characteristics of the via ferrata. The route is mainly south-facing, the descent is on east-facing passages. With the Muttekopfhütte, the Latschenhütte and the Untermarkter Alm, there are several places to stop along the way. These can also be used as a base. The descent can be ideally combined with a ride on the Alpine roller coaster and shortened. The cable car can also shorten the ascent. For the most part, orientation is easy. In poor visibility, however, the descent can be problematic.

title: From Untersteinbach through the Steinbach valley and up the Wilfersberg mountain
short_description: This hike takes us into the picturesque surroundings of Untersteinbach. We enjoy magnificent views over the Steinbach valley and from the Wilfersberg.
long_description: We start our hike at the outdoor pool car park in Untersteinbach and first walk downhill along the Dorfgartenweg. Then we briefly follow the Fleinersmühlenweg to the right and turn onto the "HW8" (main hiking trail 8). This leads us past the old sheep barn to the red dot path, which shows us the way towards Renzen. At the former sawmill Renzen, we change from the red dot trail to the right onto the circular trail no. 12. We hike in serpentines over the Eichhornshof, Braunenberg and the Strohberg to the edge of the forest and there we meet the "HW8" again, which we follow to the left. After approx. 1 km, turn half-right into a sunken path and up to the Wilfersberg heights. We continue on the "HW8" and walk to the right along the steep slopes. A little caution is required here. After about 1.5 km, we come to a fork in the road and leave the "HW8" to the right to continue on circular trail no. 12. After a few hundred metres, we turn right into a sunken path. The circular trail no. 12 leads us constantly to the right until we reach the edge of the forest, from where we have a very beautiful view of the Steinbach valley. We continue to the Strohberg, where we change to the left onto the "HW8". Through the vineyards we reach Untersteinbach and follow the "HW8" to the market place and the church. If we pass between the church and the vicarage, we come to the "Venedig-Brückle". We pass the sports facilities and the tennis courts and turn right towards the sports home. From there it is not far to our starting point, the outdoor pool car park.

title: Appalachian Trail (Triple Crown of Hiking)
short_description: The Appalachian Trail runs for almost 2190 miles in the east of the USA, crossing 14 states.
long_description:
Every year, three million visitors follow in its footsteps: The Appalachian Trail is probably one of the best-known long-distance hiking trails in the USA. It leads through the Appalachian Mountains in the east of the country. Together with the Pacific Crest Trail (PCT) and the Continental Divide Trail (CDT), the Appalachian Trail (AT) is one of the three triple-crown trails in the USA.
The Appalachian Trail starts and ends at Springer Mountain in Georgia and Mount Katahdin in Maine. Every hiker can decide for himself in which direction he wants to go. This tour starts in Georgia and then describes the route through North Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Vermont and New Hampshire to Maine.
Along the way, there are a multitude of accommodation and catering possibilities. Again and again small to medium-sized towns and cities are crossed. An alternative to staying overnight in a hotel/hostel is camping (which is permitted in many designated places along the AT) or staying overnight in one of the more than 250 small, mostly half-open shelters.

title: Vrancea Mountains: Two peaks in one day (Lăcăuți & Goru)
short_description: You have at least two reasons to try this route: it reaches the highest peak in the Vrancea Mountains and it's typical of this massif in terms of landscape and overall experience.
long_description:
In addition, it is also the easiest way to climb Goru Peak (1785 meters). You also check off Lăcăuți Peak, about halfway along the route.
The route is basically a neverending forest road, for the most part, with short rhythm breaks on the climbs to the two peaks. Hikers only come here every once in a while, which is obvious by the abundant vegetation that blocks access, the numerous wildlife traces or the deep all-surround silence.
On clear days, from the top of Lăcăuți, you can see all the way to Penteleu, Ciucaș, or even Bucegi Mountains. Similarly, on top of Goru, you can admire almost all the ridges of the Vrancea Mountains.

title: Border experiences between Füssen and Pfronten
short_description: On our tour we experience lonely forest stretches, picturesque mountain lakes and fantastic views of the Allgäu mountains. Between the Salober-Alm and the Falkenstein we cross the border to Tyrol several times.
long_description:
Füssen is a picturesque small town on the Lech River, not far from the Austrian border. Its history dates back to Roman times. At that time, Füssen was located on the Via Claudia Augusta Roman road. The small old town centre with its many pretty houses, the churches and the town castle are well worth a leisurely stroll. The proximity to the royal castles and the numerous spa facilities still attract many holidaymakers. Last but not least, the surrounding, very charming landscape leaves unforgettable impressions.
On the site of today's castle, there was once an ancient Roman fort and then a castle. Around 1500, it was transformed into a castle. The paintings on the façades in the inner courtyard are particularly worth seeing.
The Baumgarten town park belonged to the monastery of St. Mang from the 14th century. Around 1900, the grounds were acquired by the city of Füssen and transformed into a public park. A special feature is the old water reservoir. It was built in the shape of a castle with a tower and battlements. Many rows of lime trees line the paths.
The Alatsee gained renewed fame when it became the setting in a detective novel about the inspector Kluftinger. Its special location, framed by gentle wooded hills, is popular with hikers, bikers and swimmers alike.
The location of Falkenstein Castle is very exposed and therefore particularly vulnerable to storms and lightning strikes. Therefore, it was decided to build a simple robust multi-storey house with a gable roof. In 1884, King Ludwig II acquired the site and wanted to have a robber baron's castle built there. However, his bold ideas never got beyond the planning stage. The original model can now be seen in Neuschwanstein Castle. Further information can also be found in a small museum room at the castle hotel.
The Marian Grotto below the Falkenstein castle ruins is dedicated to the veneration of Our Lady of Lourdes.

title: Tsaritsyno Park - a walk through the Tsar's park!
short_description: The park area of the Tsaritsyn estate dates back to the reign of Catherine. In fact, she is the initiator of this huge and dizzying architectural ensemble;
long_description: As the palace was ready to receive the chief guest of the Russian state, Catherine the Great, Her Majesty's visit arrived. On the first night the Tsarina rejected it; the reasons for this are now being elucidated. The old architect Vasily Bazhenov was removed and a new architect - his pupil Matvey Kazakov - appointed. It is not known what or who the Tsarina did not like in the palace. However, now the museum-preserve has got the people's pleasure, you can walk around the large-scale park with historical buildings of artistic beauty.

title: The Leukerbad via ferrata on the Daubenhorn
short_description: The Leukerbad via ferrata leads through the southeast slopes of the Daubenhorn and is the longest via ferrata in Switzerland. In addition to some ladders, the via ferrata climbers can even expect a cave to cross!
long_description: The Leukerbad via ferrata leads through the high and almost entirely vertical slopes of the Daubenhorn (2941 m) in the Valais Alps. There are two variants, one of which is considerably shorter and can be climbed as an independent undertaking. In combination, these variants make up a via ferrata that makes considerable demands on fitness due to its length and difference in altitude. Exposed on the southeast side, the route leads partly via long ladders and even spectacularly through an approximately 100 m long pit through the wall. The Gemmi cable car facilitates the descent and, depending on the variant, also the ascent. The Berghotel Wildstrubel on the Gemmi Pass is a place to stop for refreshments directly on the trail. Orientation is usually easy. You should take enough drinks with you.

title: Hiking in Saint-Céneri-le-Gérei
short_description: A hike to Saint-Céneri-le-Gérei, one of France's most beautiful villages, at the crossroads of three départements: Orne, Sarthe and Mayenne, in the heart of the Alpes Mancelles.
long_description: The route passes through rolling hills and landscapes. The paths are generally well-maintained, but you are advised to wear comfortable hiking boots to navigate the sometimes rocky or uneven trails. There are a few refreshment points in the small village, but you're also welcome to bring your own picnic - a picnic area is available not far from the village, on the banks of the river. Most of the route is in wooded areas, and several sections run alongside the river, providing extra comfort for hikers in summer.

title: Steinkart circuit between Bad Griesbach and St. Salvator
short_description: On this hike we take a detour into the Ice Age. We walk in the footsteps of the Celts along dreamlike forest paths - past bizarre rock formations.
long_description: We start our tour at the car park on the road between Bad Griesbach and St. Salvator. We cross this and follow the white-green marked circular trail number 6 on the other side. In Steinkart we come across an asphalt road and turn left into it. We pass Geisberg am Wald and turn left behind the village towards Dobl. At the fork in the road behind the small chapel at Dobl, we keep to the right and hike through the forest to Adlmörting. Here we walk a few metres along the asphalt road, but then turn left again onto a field path. This leads us into the forest again. After a long left-hand bend, we finally turn right onto a small path. This takes us past the Hohlen Stein (1) - a Stone Age dwelling cave, as evidenced by numerous finds of shards and tools. Soon we reach a wider forest path again, onto which we turn left. At the next fork in the road, we keep to the right. We always follow the forest road straight ahead, but then turn right again shortly before the through road. We now descend into the "Schärengräben" and from there up again to a wide forest road, where we turn right. At the next fork we keep left again and hike straight ahead for almost 2 km. Finally, however, we turn sharply left and walk down to the through road. Cross the road and turn right onto the gravel path on the other side. At Lindenweg, turn left to the main road and turn left again to reach the monastery church of St. Salvator (2). From here we walk back to the crossroads. There we turn right into Luisenburgstraße. We walk straight ahead and finally enter the forest again. We now keep climbing uphill and turn left uphill at the fork in the road. At the small clearing, we keep to the right, following the white-green signpost to the cult stone (3). From there it is only a few metres until you reach a wide forest path again. Continue along this path to the right. Shortly afterwards, however, we take another sharp turn to the left. This is how we reach the Luisenburg (4). This is a bizarre formation of quartz conglomerates - a sedimentary rock. The site once served the Celts as a place of worship and sacrifice. We finally come across a forest road again and turn into it to the right. At the wide forest road, we keep left, but turn right again shortly before the through road. At the next fork, we continue to the left, turn right at the forest kindergarten and reach the "Steinernen Schwammerl" (5) - a rock formation that resembles a mushroom. From here, the trail continues downhill. In the right-hand bend, we turn left. At a wide forest path we keep left and shortly afterwards right again. We now walk straight ahead until we reach a crossroads. There we have the possibility to take a shortcut. To do so, we would have to follow the white-green marking "A6" to the left. Otherwise, we turn sharply right at this point and come to the golf course (6). There we continue to the left up through the Schwarzholz. At the edge of the forest, keep left and walk along it for a while before turning into the Schwarzholz again. Always following the markings, we then return to our starting point after a few minutes.

title: GR34 The Customs Trail - Brittany's most celebrated hike
short_description: The GR34 or the customs trail, is the most well known of France's coastal paths. It was voted "Favorite Trail" by the French" in 2017.
long_description: From the Bay of Mont Saint-Michel in the English Channel to the Pont de Saint-Nazaire in Loire Atlantique, the GR34 travels 2000 km along the Breton coast without ever leaving the sea of sight. Both one of the most emblematic French long-distance hiking trails and one of the most maritime, it is also a path full of history that winds its way along the coast and the Breton heritage in a breathtaking natural setting. Walking along the GR34 is one of the best, if not the most invigorating, ways to capture the spirit of Brittany, from the coasts of Emerald and Pink Granite to the Gulf of Morbihan, via the Abers of the tip of Finistère and the coast of South Finistère. Once a path that allowed customs officers to travel along the coast to prevent smuggling, today a peaceful hiking trail frequented for the beauty of its landscapes.

title: Towards the mouth of the Danube in the Black Sea, in Sfântu Gheorghe
short_description: A walk worth taking at the end of the day, which takes you through the town of Sf. Gheorghe and the mouth of the Danube (Sf. Gheorghe canal) into the Black Sea.
long_description:
Although the Sulina canal's spill point into the Black Sea is much more promoted, it is harder to get there on foot, preferring boat trips. Well, here you have the opportunity not only to admire the phenomenon in peace and quiet, without too many tourists, but also to get into the water, possibly to take a swim here.
The walk can continue along the shore, then follow a fairly visible path back to the locality and along the edge of the Green Village complex, then into the centre.
The route is also included in a chart of recommended walking/biking routes in Sfântu Gheorghe, so that tourists can alternate hours of sunbathing with more challenging activities and possibly spot birds nesting in the reeds.

This hike is just over 12 kilometres and will take you about 2.5 hours.
long_description: Most people will never have heard of the Koelbroek, but this is a beautiful nature reserve near Venlo. It is a marsh area with special flora and fauna. When you walk through the area, you will also see the Everlose brook. This stream was dug for agriculture.

title: Spring hike via Kronburg Castle to the Pommersau in Illerwinkel
short_description: This wonderful spring hike leads via Kronburg Castle, the Hoher Rain to the Iller river. There you can admire unique meadows of mullein in spring.
long_description: When the snow has disappeared in March and the first rays of sunlight warm the ground, a unique spectacle takes place every year in the so-called "Pommersau" on the Iller: Thousands of marchflowers cover the ground and those who appear at the right time can enjoy this white carpet of blossoms. Ideally, you should combine this hike with a visit to Kronburg Castle. The highest elevation of the municipality, the Hoher Rain, is on our way and on its crest there are cultural-historical sites: a Celtic high altitude sanctuary is assumed to be there and the remains of a castle complex can also be explored there. This hike then takes us downhill for a while to the hamlet of Oberbinnwang, from where we can reach the Pommersau with its mullein trees in a few minutes. On the way back to Kronburg via the hamlet of Hackenbach, we cross the so-called "Freigraben". In the Middle Ages, if a criminal crossed this ditch, he had escaped the jurisdiction of the Kronburg courts and could no longer be prosecuted by them. At the end of our round we can stop at the Schweighart brewery inn in Kronburg. If we still have energy, we can take a tour of the Swabian Farm Museum in Illerbeuren and enjoy a café in the rustic atmosphere of the Gromerhof.

title: सुखना झील का साइकिल दौरा
short_description: यह ट्रेल मार्ग असल में सुखना झील के किनारे बनी हुई एक पक्की सड़क है जो की सा इकिलिंग और झील के सुन्दर दृश्यों का मजा लेने के लिए एकदम बढ़िया है ।
long_description:
यह ट्रेल मार्ग एक डामर की पक्की सड़क है जो सुखना झील के किनारे पर मौजूद है। सड़क एकदम समतल और बढ़िया है। पूरा रास्ते के दौरान झील और उसके हरियाले से भरे किनारे दिखाई देते हैं। प्रवासी पक्षी भी झील में तैरते हुए दिख सकते हैं। सुखना झील में टूरिस्ट बोटिंग भी होती है और कभी-कभार राज्य स्तर के खिलाडी भी बोटिंग का अभ्यास करते दिख जाते हैं।
यह ट्रेल बेहद आसान है और बच्चे, बूढ़े, जवान सभी इसका आनंद ले सकते हैं। ट्रेल पार्किंग स्थल से शुरू होकर सुखना लेक व्यू पॉइंट तक जाती है जहाँ से सुखना झेल और इसके परिवेश का सुन्दर दृश्य दिखाई देता है। बसंत के दौरान या फिर मानसून के ठीक बाद के महीने यहाँ आने का सबसे बढ़िया समय हैं।

short_description: Easy walk to cross the gorge of the Río Mindo back to the starting point of the Tarabita. The great views of Cascada Nambillo are a real highlight that should not be missed.
long_description: Sure, your ticket includes the tarabita ride there and back. But since you have already crossed the gorge hanging by a somewhat questionable thread once, why not hike back to the starting point? Ruta 1 takes you from the Tarabita down into the gorge of the Río Mindo, where spectacular views of Nambillo waterfall await you. title: Neviges Cathedral and Hardenberg Castle in the Ruhr Area
short_description: Our cultural tour takes us from the Neviges Dome of the Rock to Hardenberg Castle.
long_description: We start our hike in front of the mighty Neviges Cathedral. From the Felsendom we follow the Löher Strasse and the Hardenberger Weg northwards. We pass a small French garden on the left, after which we cross the railway tracks at the next opportunity, walk a short distance down to the right and meet the Zwingenberger Weg. After a few hundred metres we walk through Zwingenberg and follow the path in a right-hand bend into the fields. Straight ahead we come to Neviges and cross the railway tracks again. Via Elberfelder Stra&szlig we reach Hardenberg Castle, a baroque building that also included the French garden we passed at the beginning of our walk. After visiting the castle, we return via the Hardenberger Weg to the Nevigeser Felsendom, the starting point of our tour.

title: Small forest circuit Sanitz
short_description: We hike from the "old village" in Sanitz towards the north. Our round leads over sandy aisles through a beautiful forest area.
long_description: We walk around the church clockwise. Beautiful old houses surround the church from the 13th century. Inside the fieldstone building we discover early Gothic wall paintings. We now follow Fritz-Reuter-Straße to the right and turn right into the street "Hof Sanitz". On the left of the path we see a very beautiful pond (1) with benches. We follow the road until it joins John-Brinckmann-Straße. Turn right here. We walk straight ahead over a level crossing and a traffic light junction. The road "Waldweg" leads us out of the village. At the edge of the forest on the right is a farmstead (2) with a beautiful old barn. A sign dates the building to 1896. We now walk straight ahead on a sandy path into the beautiful forest. When the weather is right, mushroom pickers can find something here. At the first crossroads, we turn right into the reservoir aisle. At the next fork, we follow a very beautiful path to the left. At a raised hide, the path joins another one, here we go to the right. At the next junction we turn left. Soon we meet a small asphalt road, which we follow to the right. Cross the road and continue straight ahead along a forest path. This leads us to the beautifully situated hamlet of Klein Freienholz (3). At the crossroads on the edge of the village, turn right. Here a bench (4) with a wonderful view invites us to take a break. At the next fork, keep to the left. We reach the Ribnitzer Straße, which we follow to the left. At the main road in the village, we turn right and then left into John-Brinckmann-Straße. We return to the starting point the way we came.

title: Agulhas Negras Peak Trail in Itatiaia Park

long_description:
The Itatiaia National Park, created in 1937, was the first park in Brazil and isá open for visitation every day of the year. In the High Part, the schedule for entry é from 7:00 àt 14:00 hours, being able to stay until àt 17:00 hours.
The trail begins at the Rebouças Shelter, which is 3 km from Posto Marcão, the gateway to the Upper Part of the Park. Skirting the small dam of the Abrigo, it is only 1.4 km to the base of the peak, a easy, flat and well signposted path, which already offers beautiful views of the region. After the base, to climb to the peak, the path has a higher level of difficulty, because it will be necessary to climb to the top. If you do not have experience with climbing and do not know the route, the ideal é hire a guide for greater security and a richer experience in detail and history.

title: Caving trail near Mühlbach
short_description: The cave trail leads us through the forest over the Mühlbach spring cave. On information boards we learn interesting facts about the cave and its exploration.
long_description:
The Mühlbachquellhöhle near Dietfurt is a water-active river cave of considerable dimensions. Since it is not possible to turn it into a show cave, an above-ground caving trail was designed, with a total of 18 information boards explaining what is happening about 100 m below the forest floor. In addition, children can actively experience the work of a speleologist at some of the stations. The cave trail is marked throughout as hiking trail no. 6.
The hike starts at the church square in Mühlbach. From there we walk past the Obermühle to the Mühlbach spring. Then we walk uphill through the Mühlbach Gorge and on to the Kopffelsen. Here we have a wonderful view of the Kopffels massif, the Mühlbach and Altmühl valleys. We hike through a mixed forest, pass a first small sinkhole and reach the "Bierweg". Dolines are hollows in the terrain that are formed by the erosion of limestone in the subsoil. Soon we pass larger sinkholes, from where we can make a detour to Eutenhofen. Otherwise, we continue walking in the direction of Wildensteiner Straße. The path leads us slowly downwards, along the edge of the Sommerberg forest. From a dry grassland area, we have a last beautiful view of the valley over Dietfurt before we return to our starting point, the church square in Mühlbach.

title: Mining trail at Kobelsberg - Wiesloch
short_description: Mining and its influence on the region around Wiesloch are presented at 19 stations.
long_description:
For around 2000 years, mining in the Wiesloch and Nußloch districts was a defining feature of the social structure, landscape and composition of the communities' soils. Mining was mainly for lead, zinc and silver ores. It was not until 1954 that the mining of pan-blende zinc ore and galena was finally stopped due to the increasing drop in prices.
The connections between nature, economy and social life are to be made clear on the circular route on the subject of "Mining in Wiesloch".

title: Mozart Catão Trail in Serra dos Órgãos National Park
short_description: Beautiful and easy trail in the headquarters of Teresópolis of the Serra dos Órgãos.
long_description:
The trail crosses small streams and forests until you reach the Alexandre Oliveira viewpoint. This viewpoint has a beautiful view of the city of Teresópolis, the Trecirc;s Picos State Park and the Granja Comary. The names of the trail and the belvedere pay homage to two climbers who were born in the city of Teresópolis, killed while trying to climb the south face of Aconcágua, in 1998. In addition, Mozart Catão was the first Brazilian to reach Everest, the highest mountain in the world.
<The Teresópolis Headquarters of PARNASO has a good infrastructure and offers various attractions to its visitors: cafeteria, souvenir shop, picnic area, camping and, course, several trails in direct contact with nature. The Visitor Center an Interactive Room, computers multimedia presentations thematic games, model that explains the characteristics Park highlights main places, as well rich flora fauna.

title: Around Enzklösterle
short_description: On our long circular hike around Enzklösterle, we explore forests, streams, moors and glacial forms. Again and again, beautiful huts invite you to take a cosy rest.
long_description: Impressive views along the Enz

title: Through the Wolf's Den
short_description: This hike takes us from idyllic Rhens to the Oberes Mühlbachtal meadow and up to the Kriesenkopf Rhine Heights. We then return to Rhens via the "Wolfsdelle" sunken path lined with gnarled trees.
long_description: On our hike, we can enjoy the charming distant view of the UNESCO World Heritage Site Upper Middle Rhine Valley or explore the half-timbered idyll of Rhens with the historic Königsstuhl. The Wiesengrund Oberes Mühlbachtal and the Rheinhöhe Kriesenkopf are also on our way. It is also worth taking a detour to Marksburg Castle and Ehrenbreitstein Fortress in Koblenz.

images.caption: Cows graze on the lush meadows.
Picturesque half-timbered houses line the alleys.
This proud Marksburg castle watches over our path.

title: Long-distance hiking trail E1 in the Celle region
short_description: This hike of just under 60 kilometres requires a good level of fitness. It leads through the beautiful heath landscape, where some burial mounds can be found. The Lönsstein, the medieval village in the Müden (Örtze) game park and the Rixförde estate are recommended.
long_description:
Coming from Wietzendorf, the long-distance hiking trail E1 leads over the Häteler Berg, through the Wietzer Gehege to the Wietzer Berg (Lönsstein). The trail continues past the Tilly lime tree to the heath village of
Müden. From Müden youth hostel we continue along the Örtze to Hermannsburg. Heading south, we follow the path via Hiesterhof, Dehningshof, Severloh and the Citronenberg to Wildeck. After the Kohlenbach forester's lodge, we come to the Celle district of Scheuen. Via the glider airfield and past the orchid centre we reach the youth hostel in the district of Klein Hehlen. The Wilhelm-Heinichen-Ring takes you across the river Aller. Through Neustädter Holz we walk to Hambühren and from there to the Rixförde estate. Here we leave the Celle region. Via Fuhrberg and Wedemark we reach the Steinhuder Meer.

title: Five Waterfalls Hike | Tarabita Mindo - Ruta 3
short_description: Popular hike from the Tarabita cable car to five different waterfalls in the cloud forest above Mindo.
long_description: This easy, yet spectacular little hike takes you from the adventurous Tarabita cable car to a row of five beautiful little waterfalls. All cascadas can be accessed, so it is worth bringing bathing suits and, preferably, water shoes or trekking sandals, so you can take a refreshing shower in the pouring stream. The nature along the path is stunning, with bromelias, orchids, and a wild variety of trees on both sides of the way. It is advisable to start early - not just because of the weather, but also because there are usually hordes of visitors after 10 in the morning.

images.caption: Waterfall in the cloud forest above Mindo

title: Itaimbezinho Canyon trail - Aparados da Serra National Park
short_description: Discover the beautiful Aparados da Serra National Park and have an incredible experience at the top of one of the largest crags in Brazil.
long_description: On this trail you will hike to the top of the Itaimbezinho cânion, in the Aparados da Serra National Park, which is located on the border of the states of Rio Grande do Sul and Santa Catarina. The route includes 2 main trails in the upper part of the Park: the Cotovelo trail, about 6 km long, and the V&Acte trail, a little over 1 km long. These are flat trails, well signposted and can be done with the whole family. Bring plenty of water and snacks for a picnic!

title: From Templin around Lake Templin
short_description: Our hike takes us past the city wall and around the Templin city lake. We return through the medieval town of Templin.
long_description: We leave our car in Seestraße at the Templin town harbour and walk straight ahead along Seestraße with the Templin town lake on our right. Before we start our circular walk, we recommend a stroll through the medieval town of Templin - preferably along the well-preserved town wall with its three Gothic brick gates. As we walk along Seestraße, we see parts of the town wall on our left and eventually pass the Eichwerder Tor (1). We walk straight ahead over the Pionierbrücke bridge and turn right into Weinbergstraße after the bridge. We take the path on the right towards the lake, following the sloping green markings "Rundweg Templiner Stadtsee" and "Bruchsee" towards the Fährkrug. In the forest we keep to the left and reach the shore path of the Templiner Stadtsee. We now pass the refreshment stop Kaffeegarten Seeblick (2). We walk straight ahead along the northern shore of the lake and pass a rest area (3) with a beautiful view of the lake. Where Lake Templin merges into Lake Bruchsee, we come out of the forest and walk across a meadow to the Gleuenbrücke bridge. Turn right over the bridge and continue straight ahead to the road. Now we walk a short distance to the right along the road parallel to the railway tracks to Fährkrug (4). In Fährkrug we go right under the railway bridge, following the sloping green markings, back to the Bruchsee. Our hike now leads us along the southern shore of the lakes back to Templin. We pass a shelter (5). Soon we see the first houses of Templin. We leave the lakeside path and walk on the right along the pavement of Prenzlauer Allee through the town of Templin. We walk straight ahead to Seestraße, turn left and are back at the town harbour.

images.caption: From the Pioneer Bridge we have a very beautiful view of the Templiner Stadtsee.
The historic town of Templin is framed by its fully preserved medieval fortifications with Gothic brick gates.
Rural tranquillity and beauty can be felt at Knehden Bay, where the town lake merges into the Bruchsee.
The Templiner Stadtsee is an elongated channel lake with steep banks.
The Gleuen Bridge connects the Bruchsee with the Gleuensee.
At Templin town harbour we find the steamer landing stage and a boat hire shop.

title: From Groitzsch to Profen
short_description: Across fields, through forests and along streams, our tour takes us from Saxony to Saxony-Anhalt.
long_description: The Schützenplatz in Groitzsch is the starting point of our tour, from where we walk west until we reach the forest. From here we follow south through the forest on a small path along the Schwennigken. When we reach the "Bettelsteg", we cross it and now continue on the west bank of the Schwenningen until we catch sight of the Slavic rampart of Altengroitzsch on the left after a few hundred metres. After climbing and exploring the rampart, we continue to follow the path in the valley to the south, first through a piece of forest and then uphill to the left in a sunken path. We keep to the right again towards Schwennigke until we can see the village of Gatzen and turn off towards Saasdorf. At the village pond, which we soon reach on our way, numerous benches invite you to rest. We now continue on the country road from Groitzsch to Zeitz, which takes us over the Gatzener Höhe. Passing the Gatzener Gasthof on the right, we reach Gatzen. At the village church we turn south on a footpath towards Löbnitz-Bennewitz. After about 200 m, we turn right and walk along the narrow footpath to the end of Löbnitz-Bennewitz. We cross the Schwennigke again on field paths and turn left behind the "brick pits" and the remnant of the floodplain forest onto a path between trees and field. First to the south, later to the west, our path leads past small lakes and through fields to Profen. Here we reach the centre via the market and Pegauer Straße and can now return from here to our starting point in Groitzsch along the same path.

title: To the castle and the Königstuhl - Heidelberg
short_description: On this moderately difficult tour we experience Heidelberg Castle and the Königstuhl. Parts of the route can be covered with the mountain railway.
long_description:
We start our tour at Heidelberg's Bismarckplatz. We walk along Sophienstraße to the right in the direction of Friedrich-Ebert-Anlage. We start our ascent on the Wolfshöhlenweg, which leads us up in serpentines into the forest. We can take a rest at the "Sieben Linden". The path to the Königstuhl is well signposted on path stones. We walk to the left, cross a road and follow the path.
After the crossroads at the birch bank, we continue straight up towards Molkenkur. At the next fork in the path, we turn left and, at the road junction, right into Molkenkurweg. We reach the mountain railway station here, with which we can shorten the way to the Königstuhl.
Otherwise, we turn right into Felsenmeerweg and left at the next fork. After a while we reach the Rindenhäuschen, from where we have a fantastic panorama of Heidelberg and the Rhine plain. We continue towards the Felsenmeer and follow the path to the Felsenmeer hut. At the following fork, we turn right towards "Hohler Kästenbaum" and soon reach it.
From here we turn right into the Hohlener Kästenbaumweg in the direction of the Königstuhl and follow this path until we reach the Königstuhl hikers' car park. From here we quickly reach the Königstuhl with restaurant and mountain railway station.
To the right of the viewing platform, the Himmesleiter, a stair-like, unmarked forest path descends. At the end of the Himmelsleiter, we turn left and continue towards Heidelberg Castle. To the left of the castle, we take the steps down to Kornmarkt and return through the pedestrian zone to our starting point, Bismarckplatz.

images.caption: The venerable castle towers over Heidelberg's old town.

title: Heilklimaweg 2: Vitalis route Weiskirchen
short_description: Long trail with flat and moderate climbs, but also some steep passages.
long_description: From the Parkhotel, we walk to the left to the end of the spa pond. There we reach the entrance to the Holzbach valley via Burgstraße and Kirchenweg. Following the course of the stream, we come to the Kneipp facility, above which we turn right. Then we go straight on to the street "Im Hänfert". Here we turn left again and enter the footpath to the Hochwald clinics. Past the Hochwald clinics and beyond the bus turning area, we reach a paved path, which we now follow. Above the hunting lodge "Viorel" the path makes a sharp bend to the left. Passing the shelter "Four Birches" we continue straight ahead on the ascending path. At the next fork, we turn left and follow the path, which now descends again, to the bus turnaround. From here we walk the initial feeder route in the opposite direction back to the Parkhotel.

title: Around Maria Bildhausen near Münnerstadt
short_description: Those who prefer Nordic walking sticks to golf clubs will get their money's worth on this circular tour around the 18-hole course.
long_description: We leave the golf course on the left and soon come across the markings with a red triangle on a white background, which we follow. Soon we reach a pond (1), past which we walk towards the edge of the forest. There we find a hunters' path, where we turn left and now head uphill into the forest. Turn left at a crossroads. Now a paved forest path follows, which takes us around a right-hand bend. At a crossroads we find the memorial of a military cemetery (2) and here we walk down again to the left to the golf course. Finally, we turn right to the Maria Bildhausen monastery (3). We turn left at the gates and get back to the car park via the road to the golf course. We can stop for a bite to eat at the golf restaurant "Am Rindhof".

images.caption: Those who still feel like playing golf after the Nordic walking trail are in good hands in Maria Bildhausen.
Soldiers who died of their severe injuries in the Maria Bildhausen monastery were buried at this memorial.
In the nearby Maria Bildhausen monastery you can relax in the gardens.
Under old lime trees, you can take a cosy rest in the monastery inn.
An artificial pond has been built at hole 7, which we walk past.
There is also a chapel of the monastery on the golf course.

title: Oberdorf Forest near Waltenhofen
short_description: On this leisurely walk through the Oberdorf forest, we enjoy wonderful views of the Stoffelberg and Niedersonthofen Lake.
long_description: The forest loop trail starts at the hikers' car park in Bergstraße in Oberdorf. We walk in a westerly direction on Niedersonthoener Straße into the Oberdorf forest and turn off the road after approx. 400 m onto a forest path. We follow the signposts and cross the Nierdersonthofener Straße at the edge of the forest. From here we walk in a wide curve with a wonderful view of the Stoffelberg and Niedersonthofener See back to the starting point. At the "Hasen" inn in Oberdorf, we can end the hike in a cosy atmosphere.

images.caption: We walk through a beautiful forest.

title: To Mörike's mountain church near Laudenbach
short_description: On this beautiful loop near Laudenbach, we pass a mountain church that inspired Eduart Mörike to write a poem.
long_description:
From our starting point at the sports field in Laudenbach, we turn left into Marienstraße and then immediately right behind the small roundabout and the railway tracks. On the left, a cross path with many steps leads up through the shady mountain forest to a Marien pilgrimage church, about which Eduart Mörike once wrote:

O dearest church beyond compare,
on your mountain all alone,
in the forest, where lime trees between oaks
around the choir the May shade stray.

From thy green lawn rise
the old pillars rise splendidly,
of dragons, griffins, leafy boughs
rich to the last flower-knob.

In the mountain church we can still admire a magnificent alabaster tomb of Count Melchior von Hatzfeld. Here we follow the circular trail no. 5 to the right, first through woods and later through fields, over the edge of the Vorbachtal valley to Honsbronn. After crossing the small village, we continue on trail no. 5 through the "Hammelsklinge" fields back to the mountain church. There, the steps of the Way of the Cross bring us back to Laudenbach, where it is still worth taking a short tour of the village. Here you can see a former moated castle with a tithe barn, a beautiful village church and the "Herkelsturm".

title: Monheim and the Altmühltal Nature Park
short_description: The small town of Monheim lies in the middle of the Altmühltal Nature Park and forms the centre at the "border triangle" of Franconia, Swabia and Old Bavaria. Our hike takes us through the gentle plateau formed in the Jura to the east of the town. Besides forests and meadows, we pass the idyllic villages of Ried, Warching and Wittesheim.
long_description: The small town of Monheim lies in the middle of the Altmühltal Nature Park and forms the centre at the "border triangle" of Franconia, Swabia and Old Bavaria. Our hike takes us through the gentle plateau formed in the Jura to the east of the town. Besides forests and meadows, we pass the idyllic villages of Ried, Warching and Wittesheim.

title: Hiking from Weavers' Bastion to Postăvaru Cabin (the Blue Road)
short_description: The “Blue Road” mountain route is listed among the light hikes that connect Brașov to Poiana Brașov via the Postăvaru Cabin. Although long, it is a route accessible to anyone, in any season, practicable with the MTB as well.
long_description:
On the Tâmpa side, the “Blue Road” - named so after the blue band signposts - follows the legendary Knights Road, which once connected the former Brașovia fortress and one end of the Schei borrow with the lower fortress. Leaving the Knights Road behind in Tâmpa Saddle, you continue walking for a while, slightly upwards, until facing the real ascent - somewhere after Poiana Stechil - on a quite steep path.
The landscape is quite uniform along the route, the forest of deciduous mix with conifers turning into one only of firs and pines at the end of the route. The trails are mostly generous, with no surprises. The length of the route can discourage beginners or families with children, but it is a challenge for mountain bikers or for trail runners.
In winter, there are chances to start on the dry and weathered path from the Weavers' Bastion and to find snow as deep as a few tens of centimeters in Poiana Ruia. From here you can easily descend to Poiana Brașov or continue to the Postăvaru Cabin.
The other two main hiking routes that connect Brașov to Poiana Brașov are the Red Road and the Yellow Road.

title: Hiking in the Ostertal Tobelweg
short_description: A lovely hiking trail in a forest and next to a stream, wooden bridges and several wonderful waterfalls
long_description:
A beautiful hiking route where a wonderful nature experience awaits you that includes a lot of flowing water and several waterfalls of different sizes.
Most of the walk is in the forest and therefore wonderful even on warmer days. We chose to do a circular route, but it is also possible to go back and forth on the same road and then return at any given moment back to the car. The walk on the route includes several sections of stairs but there are several benches along the way as well as a wooden gazebo with benches and a table where you can have a light meal.
Those who choose to complete the circular route will pass by a wonderful local restaurant where there is a fun playground for children (note that it is closed on Wednesday-Thursday). You can start the route from two parking lots - the route shown here is from the lower parking lot (called: Gunzesrieder Säge).
The route is not accessible to strollers or wheelchairs.

title: Zicker Berge circular route on Rügen
short_description: A dreamlike hike in the "Rügen Alps". Gentle hilly landscapes with fantastic views, coastal sections worth seeing and remarkable vegetation and biodiversity await us.
long_description: Our tour begins directly in the centre of Gager. At the roundabout, we follow the hiking trail signs "Rundweg Zicker Berge". We follow the paved road in a westerly direction, which later turns into a sandy path and becomes a trail at the beginning of the nature reserve (1). Short forest stretches alternate with smaller meadow areas. A wonderful variety of plants accompanies our path, which gains height almost imperceptibly. The path leads directly to the remarkable cliff (2) from where we have a wide view over the Rügen Bodden. The path becomes steep again for a short while before it leads leisurely down into a notch valley, the Nonnenloch (3). From here it is only a few minutes' walk to the western beach. The short, quite steep but paved descent is rewarded by an idyllic narrow coastal strip. Some of the boulders in the shallow water are as big as a man. Back on our path, we follow the hiking trail signs slightly uphill and walk below Zicker Berg towards Groß Zicker. The lush green of the wide mountain landscape merges with the deep blue of the Bodden landscape in a fascinating way. Our path leads along a sandy path through the pastures directly towards the village of Groß Zicker in the distance. In the centre of the village we come across the parish widow's house (4). Today it is used as a meeting place, museum and gallery. Following the main road, we meet the hiking signs again on the left. Passing the church, we climb up to the 65 m high Bakenberg (5). From up here, the beauty of the Zicker mountains can be enjoyed again in a panoramic view. Now we follow the path downhill back to our starting point.

images.caption: The steep coast at Zickersche Höft.

title: Schloßberg-Ulrichstein Tour - Ulrichstein-Helpershain
short_description:
On the tour we are offered a magnificent panoramic and distant view of the Hessian low mountain landscape.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
The hike runs from Helpershain in a southerly direction through the valley of the Katharinenbach to Engelröder Strasse. The trail continues west along the edge of the forest into the headwaters of the Katharinenbach stream and on through the high fir forest.
On reaching the edge of the forest, you can already see Ulrichstein with the Schlossberg. Pass the equestrian centre and the Burgblick holiday village and continue along the road past the town hall and the town hall to the Schlossberg with the Vogelsberg garden. The walk continues around the Schlossberg past the cemetery and the Vorwerk Museum. In front of the church there is an opportunity to stop at the Groh restaurant.
The path now turns left again and passes Cafe Knopp. Once you reach the main road, the path goes downhill a little before turning right again. Passing the sports field and the tennis courts, you now reach the headwaters of the Ohm. Once you reach the edge of the forest, the trail continues in a north-westerly direction through a tall fir forest and across the road into the Stumpertenröder valley. Surrounded by high fir forest and rippling waterways, the hike leads through the Hegwald forest to the Nonnenwiesen meadows. A varied landscape with hedges, fields and meadows is hiked through. Köddingen appears behind the mountain slope. Pass a barbecue hut and continue over the next hilltop to Helpershain.

title: On the Luther Trail from Tambach-Dietharz to Paulinzella
short_description: Three-day hike on the Luther Trail from Tambach-Dietharz via Gotha and Arnstadt to Paulinzella
long_description:
The Luther Trail is an extensive network of paths that criss-crosses the whole of Thuringia and connects many stations from the life of Martin Luther. The three stages of this tour are 45, 37 and 33 km long, making them day-long tours for ambitious hikers. Those who want to take a little more time and marvel at the local sights should divide the tour into several days.
Highlights of the section between Tambach-Dietharz and Paulinzella are, on the one hand, the stations from the life and work of Martin Luther - for example, the Luther Fountain in Tambach-Dietharz. The famous composer Johann Sebastian Bach has also left some traces along our way, especially in Arnstadt. The natural landscape on the Luther Trail changes from the dense Thuringian Forest to open, agriculturally used areas to picturesque river meadows.
