title: Weinheim Bay Route - Alzey
short_description: On this medium-difficulty trail we experience the natural monument "Weinheimer Trift".
long_description:
We start our tour at the Weinheim sports field and first walk past the "Weinheimer Trift", a well-known natural monument. A large variety of well-preserved fossils were found in this sand pit, which can be used to document what living conditions were like on the subtropical coast of the Weinheim Bay.
We continue towards Erbes-Büdesheim along the vineyards. At their height we are offered an excellent panorama. We continue past the "Zeistück" until we reach the starting point again.
By the way, Weinheim is the largest district of Alzey and was already mentioned in documents in 772 AD.

title: From Bautzen to the reservoir
short_description: A pleasantly short tour takes us to the Bautzen Sea.
long_description: We start our hike at the "Alte Kaserne" (old barracks) in Bautzen, from where we first walk a short distance along Gerberstraße. From there we turn into Spreegasse and cross the Spree after a right turn in the direction of Oehna. Here we cross Breitscheidstraße, which we follow until we reach the Spreeradweg. We now follow this and the beach promenade to our destination, the Gottlobsberg with its viewing pavilion. Along the lake, boards inform us about interesting details of the reservoir, the "Bautzen Sea."

images.caption: Bautzen Reservoir - View of the dam wall from the pavilion.

title: Diamond Hill
short_description: Short,  not too difficult hike up a beautiful scenic mountain in Connemara.

images.caption: Parts of the trail go over wooden footbridges

title: Lindberg round
short_description: This Nordic walking tour takes us along forest paths around the holiday resort of Lindberg. The route leads us through varied and charming nature.
long_description: If we are standing on the Anger with the youth centre behind us, we orientate ourselves towards the Mühlbach. We follow the signs "Läufer" on our tour. When the asphalt access road to Blumenthal leaves the forest, we turn right onto the field path. Here we cross the Mühlbach for the second time. We reach an asphalted forest road leading parallel to the main road to Zwiesel. Here we turn left until the signpost "Frauenau" leads us westwards. We enjoy views of the church Hl. Familie in Unterzwieselau on the beautiful path. At the ponds we turn left. Here we have the option of going straight on to the church and on to Oberzwieselau to the castle. However, we follow the "runner" back to our starting point.

images.caption: We cross the Mühlbach a second time on the way to Zwiesel.
The path to Unterzwieselau offers numerous views.
Our path winds through the lovely landscape.
The trail from Zwiesel to Unterzwieselau offers beautiful views.
At the ponds there is the possibility of an excursion to the church of St. Family in Unterzwieselau and the castle in Oberzwieselau.
Our tour starts at the youth centre of the local history society.

title: Walk around the lake of Guéry
short_description: This hike in two loops allows you to explore the surroundings of the Lac de Guéry, the highest lake in Auvergne, in the heart of the Massif Central.
long_description:
Highly appreciated by fishermen, the Guéry lake is also a small paradise for walkers and hikers in the Puy de Dôme.
Every year when the lake is frozen, fishermen from all over France and neighbouring countries indulge in an original practice: ice fishing. An unusual event where each person digs his or her own hole in the ice with a gimlet, then casts his or her line spotted with an earthworm, a moth or a small livebait for a good winter fishing trip!
The route taken through the lake is a very interesting one.
The route taken alternates between undergrowth and plains without losing sight of the Lac de Guéry.

title: From the Old Market in Tawang to the city's monastery
short_description: A short but impressive hike in Tawang leads from the Old Market up to the famous Tawang Monastery, the oldest and largest Buddhist monastery in India.
long_description:
The trail begins in the hustle and bustle of the market, which invites you to shop. From there, the path gradually leads uphill through picturesque alleyways and small places of worship, which offer a first insight into the spiritual culture of the region. During the hike, you can always enjoy beautiful views of the valley and the surrounding mountains, which shine in lush green and snow-covered peaks on a clear day. The Giant Buddha statue of Tawang is also always in view.
After just under an hour, you reach the imposing Tawang Monastery, which sits enthroned at an altitude of 3,000 meters. The yellow roofs and traditional Tibetan decorations are impressive even from a distance. Inside, visitors can expect a peaceful atmosphere, prayer flags fluttering in the wind and monks going about their daily rituals. An ideal place to experience the tranquillity and spirituality of the region before making your way back.

images.caption: On the way to Tawang Monastery

title: Round tour - From the Gunzesrieder Säge to the Wiesach
short_description: This circular hike leads from Gunzesrieder Säge in the direction of Wiesach and via the Winkelwies Alpe back to the small community.
long_description: This tour takes us over four and a half kilometres along the Ach, over forest and meadow paths through the fairytale landscape of the Nagelfluh Park. At an altitude of 1,400 metres, a magnificent view awaits.

title: From Hansegisreute to Oggenhausen near Heidenheim
short_description: This longer loop takes us to Oggenhausen and back.
long_description:
Always follow the hiking sign from the Hansegisreute car park along the Heintalweg to Oggenhausen. Pass under the motorway and then over the road bridge to reach the centre of Oggenhausen with its brewery, Protestant church and town hall. The Protestant church of Oggenhausen
was built in the 18th century in the place of the Wendelinskapelle in the baroque style. If you like, you can stop off at the Oggenhausen brewery. Founded over 300 years ago, King Wilhelm I of Württemberg handed over the Königsbräu brewery to the Majer family in 1827, who still own it today. After the rest, we first follow the Oggenhauser Hauptstraße to the north and then left along the Erzstraße to the bypass. Cross the bypass and walk under the motorway on the Schnaitheimer Weg. After 50 m turn left and at the next crossing turn right and walk straight uphill for about 1.5 km. At the top we turn left again until the Osterholz residential area is visible. At the edge of the forest, we come across the signpost that leads us to the starting point.

title: Hike to the viewpont on the Csere-hegy
short_description: It s nice afternoon hike for families, who are interested in the great view of the lake Balaton, with a little historical spice.
long_description:
From the Csere-hegy you can see lake as you never seen from the beach.  From the Viewpoint you can see the whole east part of the lake.

Your starting and ending point is the old pub of the village where you can get a refreshment. You will see on the way an old stone mine. From Alsóörs they used to export red sandstone in the old times. Going trough this track you will find maybe the youngest Amphitheater and the Red Rock Natural trail. 

The Viewpoint itself is a historical sight, built in 1935 at the former borders of Zala and Veszprém county. First named from Miklós Horthy, the former govenor of Hungary. You will find the Horthy family's banner above the entrance.

images.caption: Alsóörsi Amfiteátrum I Varázserdő - Varázserő (Regina Tv, Alsóörsi magazin)

title: Walking around Kirchzarten
short_description: A medium-difficulty Nordic Walking tour, for the most part on a forest floor that is easy on the joints; short, medium-difficulty ascents; beautiful views of the valley on the way to the highest point.
long_description: From the car park, cross the main road and walk straight ahead towards the glider airfield (1). Behind the information boards, we cross the bridge and then turn right. At the fork, follow the red NW route. After the pasture, we go uphill on a narrow path. We follow the now wider path through the forest, along the pasture with a view of Geroldstal (2), the highest point of the tour. There you will find an information board. We pass the board on the left, shortly afterwards we turn right and finally reach the hollow way on the left to the pilgrims' inn St. Laurentius (3). There is also a chapel built in 1737. We continue downhill, turn left before the mountain bike technical course, walk along the pilgrims' path (4), which leads in 14 stations along 100-year-old Stations of the Cross up to the chapel. At the playground and the water treading place (5), our path finds itself in the open valley again. Behind the playground, turn left to the bridge, cross the stream and return to the car park.

images.caption: The view falls into the Geroldstal valley while walking.
Our Nordic Walking tour is well signposted.
Imposing views await us in an exposed position.
Wonderful views accompany us all the way to the highest point of our tour.

title: Ugental and Schoss Hellenstein
short_description: This tour takes us through the beautiful Ugen valley before we enjoy the views of Heidenheim an der Brenz from Hellenstein Castle.
long_description: Surrounded by woods and meadows, the route first leads through the beautiful Ugental valley near Heidenheim an der Brenz. Via Mergelstetten you return to the Nature Theatre and Hellenstein Castle. The origins of this fortress high above Heidenheim on the Brenz go back to the 11th century. In the 16th century, the castle burnt down and was rebuilt. Today, only ruins and a staircase tower rebuilt in the 19th century bear witness to the actual Hellenstein Castle. The carriage museum and the so-called Kindlesbrunnen are worth seeing.

images.caption: Schoss Hellenstein in Heidenheim an der Brenz.

title: Triemli-Uetliberg trail run
short_description: An ideal trail for anyone looking for nature and a sporting challenge. This activity is also easy to reach by train from Zurich.
long_description:
The trail from Triemli railroad station up to the Uetliberg is a varied route that will delight beginners and experienced runners alike. From Triemli station, the trail joins the official hiking trail and leads steadily uphill through forests and clearings along the ridge. On a clear day, you will be rewarded with a breathtaking view of Zurich and the Alps from the summit of the Uetliberg.
The descent is either along the same route or via the path below the ridge, which leads via Rosswald. It takes you back to the starting point on narrow and sometimes technical paths. The route offers a perfect mix of sporting challenge and nature experience in the immediate vicinity of the city.

images.caption: View through the forest from the Uetliberg

title: Nordic Walking near Marktoberdorf
short_description: A very beautiful Nordic walking tour: From Hochwieswald via Rieder we walk past Kohlhunden and the historic Pest cemetery.
long_description: We start our Nordic walking tour from the car park at Hochwieswald. We follow the sign "R1", which is located by the information board, and cross the main road. At the end of the branch road, we continue to the right along the old country road to Rieder. At the fork in the road just before Rieder, keep left. At the "Dorflädele" (1) we cross the main road and walk towards the church (2). Walk past the church on the right and pass a small fish farm (3). Finally, we keep going in the direction of Marktoberdorf/Kuhstallweiher. We walk out of the village. Behind a hill is the Kuhstallweiher (4). At the car park, we turn right onto a path and walk through the forest until we come to a forest path and finally turn left towards the Pest cemetery (5). From here we hike back.

images.caption: On the old country road to Rieder.

title: Hiking at the Appy pond - Ariège
short_description:
A very nice out-and-back hike, with magnificent views of the Ariege Pyrenees and a nice break on the banks of the Appy pond.
About 2h15 for the ascent and 1h45 for the descent.
long_description:
The hike is on a relatively steep climb, but which is ultimately fairly steady and without major difficulties.
The lower part is more stony and rocky. The end of the descent on the way back can actually be a bit difficult. 
The middle section offers superb panoramas, especially at the level of the big rock overlooking the valley, with views of the Massif de l'Aston, the Pic de Rulhe or even in the distance the Pic Carlit.
The last part on the flat to reach the pond is pleasant. With a divine break at the edge of the fresh water.
The last part on the flat to reach the pond is pleasant.

images.caption: Hiking in Ariège at the Appy pond

title: Wanderather
short_description: Pure enjoyment of nature! The trail leads through wide meadows with spectacular views, quiet valleys with bubbling streams and even juniper and broom heaths. For a stretch, it follows the Jodokus pilgrimage trail, combined with a detour to the artistically decorated pilgrimage chapel of St. Jost.
long_description:
Highlights:
Viewing trails Wanderath-Welschenbach, Hohe Warte-Wanderath and Welschenbach-Acht, Achterbach Valley with Black Madonna and Jodokus Fountain, St. Jost pilgrimage chapel, Kramershardt juniper heaths on the southern slope of Hohe Warte.

From the church in Baar-Wanderath, the trail leads through fields, meadow areas and wooded hilltops with beautiful panoramic views to Welschenbach. A slight ascent through the forest follows, then again open fields, meadows and great nature trails. The route descends leisurely through the heath landscape and along forest and field paths into the Achterbach valley. The path leads along the babbling brook to the Black Madonna devotional site with fountain and small bridge. Together with the Jododokus pilgrims' path, the trail follows the Achterbach (detours to the worthwhile pilgrimage chapel of St. Jost are possible). Back at the junction, the trail continues upwards in the Nitzbach valley, along beautiful slate rocks. At the Welschenbach stream, the trail leads into the denser forest, past an old quarry. After crossing the stream and ascending, there is a great view of Virneburg Castle at the edge of the forest. The trail continues uphill through meadow passages, then to the juniper heath at Hohe Warte. The trail circles the Hohe Warte and then descends along its western edge. In the valley, the path goes uphill on a natural path back to Wanderath.

images.caption: In the church, you should definitely take a look at the ceiling painting.
It's nice and shady in the forest.
Big round bales of straw as far as the eye can see.

title: Dzukou Valley
short_description: नागालैंड और मणिपुर की सीमा में फैली हुई जुकू (दजुकू) घाट ी समुद्र तल से 2452 मीटर की ऊँचाई पर स्थित है। रोलिंग पहा ड़ियों वाली यह सुन्दर घाटी पूर्वोत्तर भारत के मुख्य आकर्ष णों में से एक हैं।
long_description:
नागालैंड की सबसे आकर्षक घाटियों में से एक ज़ुकू (दज़ुकू) घाटी अपनी हरी पहाड़ियों, घने जंगलों, पानी की ठंडी धराओं और डज़ुकौ लिली जो केवल ज़ुकोउ घाटी में पाई जाती है, के लिए प्रसिद्ध है।
जुलाई के पहले दो सप्ताह ट्रैक के लिए सबसे अच्छे हैं क्योंकि यह आमतौर पर ज़ुकू (दज़ुकू) घाटी में फूलों का मौसम होता है। लेकिन साल के बाकी समय भी घाटी बहुत खूबसूरत रहती है।
नागालैंड में ज़ुकू (दज़ुकू) घाटी की ट्रैकिंग के दो रास्ते हैं - एक ज़खामा गाँव से और दूसरा विस्वेमा गाँव से। ट्रेल की शुरुआत में मौजूद पंजीकरण कार्यालय में प्रवेश शुल्क का भुगतान करना पड़ता है जो भारतीय हाइकर के लिए 50 रुपये और विदेशी हाइकर के लिए 100 रुपये है।
दोनों ही ट्रेल कुछ किलोमीटर तक कंकड़ वाली सड़क है। अगर अपने सही ट्रैकिंग जूते नहीं पहने हैं तो आपके पैरों को परेशानी हो सकती है। ऊबड़-खाबड़ ट्रेल के बाद करीब एक किलोमीटर तक खड़ी सीढ़ियों पर चढ़ना पड़ता है जो थका देने वाला है। लेकिन घाटी में प्रवेश करते ही यह सब भूल जाता है क्योंकि सामने अनछुई प्रकृति, साफ़ ठंडी हवा, और मंत्रमुग्ध करने वाली पहाड़ियाँ, से सामना होता है।
यहाँ घाटी में सिर्फ बुनियादी सुविधाएँ हैं। एक छोटे गेस्ट हाउस में 2 डॉरमेट्री और 5 निजी कमरे हैं लेकिन बिजली के अलावा कोई सुविधा नहीं है। पास की नदी से पानी लाना पड़ता है। इस गेस्ट हाउस में बेसिक खाना परोसा जाता है। शिविर स्थान भी हैं जहाँ तम्बू लगाया जा सकता है। वैसे इलाके में एक नया गेस्ट हाउस बनाया जा रहा है।
संक्षेप में कहा जाए तो नागालैंड की अछूती प्राकृतिक सुंदरता का अनुभव करने के लिए ज़ुकू (दज़ुकू) घाटी का दौरा सबसे अच्छा है।

Guest House in Dzukou Valley built by the Government of Nagaland
View of the Dzuko Valley in Summer in Northeast India
भारत में पदयात्रा मार्ग: जुकू (दजुकू) घाटी ट्रैक

title: Hiking in the Jura via the Belvédère des 4 lacs and the Pic de l'Aigle
short_description: A superb loop hike in the Jura allowing you to discover the Grand Maclu and Petit Maclu lakes and to enjoy a magnificent panorama of the surrounding area from the Belvéd'4 lacs and the Pic de l'Aigle.
long_description:
This hike starts from the south car park of the lake of Ilay by a path without difficulty. The latter allows you to walk along two of the four lakes, the Grand Maclu and the Petit Maclu. We then reach the Maclu lakes car park which can also be a departure point for this circuit.
The route is easy to follow.
You walk along a road for a few metres before starting the most physical part of the route, a steep climb for 300m. Then, a more gradual ascent allows you to reach the famous Belvédère of the 4 lakes before continuing with the one of the 3 lakes. On a clear day, it is not unusual to see the summit of Mont Blanc!
Finally, you continue to climb a little further to reach the famous Pic de l'Aigle, a very nice place for a picnic break for the view it offers. If you wish to avoid the fringe places of the route, it is also possible to find a pleasant spot to break the crocodile ;)
The hike ends with an all downhill path for more than 2 km to reach the car park.

images.caption: Lakes of Grand Maclu and Petit Maclu
View from the Pic de l'Aigle
Walk along one of the 4 lakes
Lac de la Motte or Lac d'Ilay and Lac du Grand Maclu

title: Views over Bolboci Lake, in the Bucegi Mountains
short_description: A route ignored by many because it does not promise stunning heights or fairytale landscapes. However, it is recommended as a leisurely hike, for beginners and even for families with children, alike.
long_description:
The route starts and ends at Bolboci Cabin. From here, we went up a forest road to the former Podu cu Florile cabin. The marked path starts a few meters before the cabin, on the only visible path going upwards all of a sudden.
We climbed slightly steeply at first, but only for a short time until we reached the base of the plateau. Here, you find the Lucăcilă sheepfold. We walked below the Lucăcilă peak, among generous junipers, seeing the main ridge of the Bucegi Mountains always to our right.
Almost without realizing it, once we arrived in the saddle near the summit, we were already at over 1800 meters. On a clear day, from here you can see the Leaota Mountains, the Piatra Craiului Mountains, the Iezer-Păpușa Mountains, and some glimpses of the Făgăraș Mountains.
Here we turned right, following the signposts and focusing on the Tataru Peak, already visible in front of us. Still, the circuit does not reach this peak - it turns right again, near an iron cross. This is also where the signs change to a red triangle.
We arrived far too quickly in the fir forest, and then on a grim path. The route descends quite steeply to the asphalted road circling the lake.

images.caption: The first few meters of the path
The guiding sign, for the most part
The open plateau of the Bucegi Mountains
Descending into the riverbed, towards the end of the route
Signpost where the route ends, entering DJ714 towards Bolboci

title: Filzkunstweg in Tisens/Südtirol
short_description: Kleiner Rundspaziergang von 30min ohne große Anstrengung und Kenntnisse/Kondition
long_description:
Wir starten die Tour beim Alpwell Hotel Burggräfler in Tisens und laufen links den Weg entlang.
Es handelt sich hier um den Filzkunstweg, der Weg ist deutlich beschildert.
Auf dem Weg kommen immer wieder Filzobjekte, die schon sehr ramponiert aussehen - Alles ist vergänglich.
Auf knapp der Hälfte der Strecke kommt eine kleine Kapelle, St. Christoph, leider ist sie nicht geöffnet.
Danach führt uns der Weg durch den Wald, an weiteren Filzkunstobjekten vorbei, wieder zurück zum Alpwell Hotel Burggräfler

images.caption: Der Filzkunstweg zeigt uns immer ein paar Objekte

title: Ponholzerweg around Michaelsneukirchen
short_description: This Nordic walking tour impresses us with magnificent views and beautiful forest areas.
long_description: From the car park at the fairground, we walk to the end of the village and reach the hamlet of Glöcklswies in an open area. Passing a pasture with goats and sheep, we reach a fork where we turn left towards the forest. We follow the marking "Wanderweg 100". Our path leads us through the deciduous forest. At a fork we keep to the left. We walk across a meadow past the Knotthof and reach Ponholz. Here we turn right into the road and keep left at the end of the village. Through Noth and past Jammer und Elend we enter the forest. There a path on the left leads us past a chapel down the slope. We return to Michelsneukirchen via the farm in Pfaffengschwand and can stop at the Stubenhofer inn right next to the church.

images.caption: At Ponholz we enjoy the view over the Bavarian Forest Nature Park.
Our Nordic Walking Tour leads via the Kohlmühlbach to the Knotthof.
In Glöcklswies we are greeted by a particularly beautifully designed crucifix.
The names of these hamlets date back to the demarcation of the border between Bavaria and the Upper Palatinate in 1326.

title: In the west of Hünfeld
short_description: This tour takes us through the charming Hünfelder area to the beautifully situated Molzbach. Via Großenbach we walk back along the Hasel.
long_description: We follow the Klosterstraße uphill and orient ourselves to the left in the direction of Molzbach. The "red wedge on a white background" marking leads us out of the village. At a crossroads we follow the "black wedge" to the right. In Molzbach we walk in the direction of the church. At the village square with rest area, we walk to the left into Oberdorfstraße. At the end of the village we walk to the left. Follow the asphalt road to the right. Behind a wayside shrine, we take the paved path on the left. In Großenbach, we follow Rößbergstraße to the left and turn right along Lichtweg to St.-Antonius-Straße. Here we walk briefly to the left and follow a footpath and cycle path to the right along the Hasel and the Haselsee through the Bürgerpark back to the starting point.

images.caption: Our way back runs along the Haselsee.
We walk towards the beautiful village of Molzbach.
In the centre of Molzbach, this beautiful rest area invites you to take a break.

title: Easy hike to Poiana Brașov on the Rellow Road path
short_description: If you are looking to cross from Brașov to Poiana Brașov on foot, neither too fast (Red Road) nor too long (Blue Road), but still with some challenges, try the Yellow Road.
long_description:
This route, suitable for young and old alike, starts at Solomon's Stones.
In the first part, the route cuts several times through the wide gravel path that also connects Brașov with Poiana, and which seems more like an easy promenade that you can enjoy, by yourself or with your family, on foot or by MTB.
The first deviation leads you on some improvised stairs, welcome for a little variation. The second detour leads you through Poiana Nisipului, where the ascent is still barely felt. The third break in the wide path brings a few steep climbs to Poiana Drester and beyond. You have an opportunity to see a barely visible panorama towards Brașov above Poiena Drester, and soon you come out into the wide path connecting most of the trails leading to Poiana Ruia, and then to Poiana Brașov, with a detour to Postăvaru Cabin.

title: Funny Stag Tour
short_description: Route from "10° 14' 26" East, 47° 34' 38" North" to "Akams, 87509 Immenstadt im Allgäu".

title: Around the Egidiberg near Sankt Englmar
short_description: The Egidi loop takes us through forest and across meadows, with beautiful views of Pröller, Käsplatte and Obermühltal.
long_description: From the start, we walk uphill to the road from Sankt Englmar to Grün. First we stay on the left of the road, then we cross it and walk on the path with the white "5" in the green square to the small forest chapel of St. Bernhard. We now follow the sign "3" to Grün. There the "Kramerwirt" invites you to take a rest. We now walk left on the path to the summer toboggan run and finally cross the through road. From the further path we enjoy wonderful views. We go down to the Egidibach, then climb the western flank of the Kapellenberg. The Leonhardisteig takes us directly to the Leonhardskapelle chapel. When we reach the asphalted Kapellenweg, we keep to the left and return to our starting point.

images.caption: Once we have left the green, we reach a beautiful field path with interesting views.
The path leads steeply down from the Egidiberg to the Grün district.
We come across these death boards on the way to St Bernard's Chapel.
On our way we reach the small forest chapel of St Bernhard.
The Egidibach is the lowest point of our tour, from now on it is steeply uphill.
We reach the pilgrimage church of St Leonhard after a steep climb.

title: Around the Nonnensee near Bergen
short_description: A popular meeting place for runners is the Nonnensee lake in the north of the district town of Bergen. Our Nordic walking tour takes us on a loop around the Nonnensee.
long_description: In the north-west of the district town of Bergen lies the 75-hectare Nonnensee. The Nonnensee is a popular meeting place for runners on the island of Rügen and so our Nordic walking tour takes us on a loop around the Nonnensee. We start at the car park on the B96 on the eastern shore of the Nonnensee. We walk on the path to the right, counter-clockwise around the lake. At the beginning we walk straight ahead along an old chestnut avenue. At the end of the avenue we have a very good view of the bird breeding area (1). Walk right through a gate and then straight ahead again parallel to a stream. Straight ahead we pass a small wood to reach a lookout tower (2). From the top we have a very good view of the Nonnensee. Lake Nonnen is a meltwater lake that was formed during the last ice age about 10,000 years ago. In order to use the area of the lake for agriculture, the lake was drained for decades. These intensive drainage measures have severely endangered the animal and plant population. After the pumps were shut down, the water level rose again and Lake Nuns formed anew. Today, Lake Nunnery has become one of the most important nature reserves in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania as a breeding area and habitat for native birds. Now we walk straight ahead along the foothills of the Jarnitzer Gehege and come to the northern tip of the lake (3). We walk to the left on the cycle path in the direction of Bergen. Now we walk along the west side of the lake, pass a few houses and have a good view of Bergen from here across the lake (4). Continue straight on around the lake and pass the second lookout tower with a rest area (5). On the path parallel to the B96 we reach our starting point again.

images.caption: An old chestnut avenue leads along the Nonnensee.
The Nonnensee covers an area of 75 hectares.
As a breeding area and habitat for the local bird life, Lake Nun has become one of the most important nature reserves in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.
From two lookout towers, you can easily observe the rich bird life on Lake Nunnery.
The Nonnensee is a protected bird breeding area.

title: Natural Pools of Caixa D'Aço Trail in Trindade
short_description: Easy trail located in the village of Trindade, in Paraty (RJ). The beautiful natural pools of the Caixa D’Aço (or Cachadaço) are famous for their áclear and warm waters.
long_description:
This beautiful region is located in the lower part of the Serra da Bocaina National Park, surrounded by a rich vegetation of the Atlantic Forest, and with the mountains of the Serra do Mar in the background.
Although it is possible to reach the natural pools by boat, é much cooler to go by trail and thus have an even deeper contact with nature. The trail   also passes by other beautiful attractions of the village of Trindade that à worth being visited, as the Praia do Meio and Praia da Caixa D'Aço. The island of Trindade and the natural monument Cabeça do Índio, which divides the states of São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, can also be spotted along the way.
<The PARNA of Serra da Bocaina does not charge an entrance fee or require authorization to visit these attractions and there is no time control for entry exit visitors.

title: Explore the cliffs and east coast of Bornholm - 100km Sightseeing
short_description: Bornholm has a lot to see. That's why I recommend planning 4 to 5 days for this tour. Here, it is not only the way that is the goal, but the many places and nature.
long_description:
First we head north from Rönne along the west coast of Bornholm. The route takes you through various small fishing villages to the large ruins of Hammershus Castle. For the first overnight stay, I recommend Allinge after about 27 km.
The next morning we head to Gudhjem, a busy town with hygge cafés and cute shops, especially in the high season. From here, a detour inland to Østerlars Rundkirke is a good idea.
On the third day, you drive along the north coast to Svaneke, known throughout Denmark for its good craft beer, handicrafts and all kinds of sweet things.
Back you go from Svaneke in a southerly direction to Aarsdale, from where you drive across the island back to Rönne. On this trip, you pass the natural sights of Rokkestenen, Paradisbakkerne and the Rytterknægten lookout tower. The tower stands on the highest mountain on Bornholm.

images.caption: View from Hammershus to the south
Gudhjem on the north coast of the island of Bornholm

title: Vashisht-Bhrigu Lake Trek
short_description: Starting from Vashisht (a scenic village) to Bhrigu lake (a sacred ancient lake), this beautiful and serene hiking trail offers a genuine experience of the hilly landscapes of the Kullu district of Himachal Pradesh in India.
long_description:
Bhrigu Lake is a clean, gorgeous, high-altitude alpine lake that has long been the subject of Hindu myths. The lake is named after the great ancient sage Maharishi Bhrigu, who meditated here. The lake has long been a favourite destination for campers, hikers, and other outdoor lovers.
As most hikers still use the traditional trail beginning in Gulaba village to reach Bhrigu, this trail from Vashisht hamlet (also known as Bashisth) to Bhrigu Lake is new and relatively unknown. The Vashisht-Bhrigu track is a very attractive trek route, and one feature that sets it apart from the Gulaba-Bhrigu trail is its gorgeous surroundings and dense forest.
This trail starts from vast alpine grasslands, which are covered in snow in winter and vibrant Himalayan flowers in summer. These meadows are also home to herds of wild horses, as well as goats and lambs owned by local shepherds. During winter one can see these cute animals grazing on the soft grass of these meadows. The middle segment of the trail passes through dense pine forests with fragrant air which is supposedly very healthy for the lungs. The last section of the trail offers a breathtaking view of the Pir-Panjal and Dhauladhar mountain ranges, both of them which are part of the Indian Himalayas.
One immediately feels a meditative calm and soothing peace when arriving at the lake. Numerous campgrounds are available nearby where hikers can spend the night. Several well-known campgrounds are found close to Bhrigu Lake, including Cheeka, Jobra, and Pandurupa.
It is an excellent place to elope when you are bored and tired of the commercialised hill stations of Himachal Pradesh.

images.caption: The beautiful Bhrigu Lake located in Manali at Himachal Pradesh, India.
View of Pir Panjal Mountain range from the Bhrigu-Lake trail in Himachal India
Vashisth Temple is the starting point of the Bhrigu Lake Trek, Manali, Himachal Pradesh, India.
The beautiful nature trail of Bhrigu lake during summers in Himachal Pradesh, India
Campers in Rola Koli Camp Site close to the Bhrigu Lake, Himachal Pradesh, India.
long-distance hike in India: Vashisht-Bhrigu Lake Trek

title: From Altstädten to Oberstdorf
short_description: We enjoy a varied, but mostly very easy tour from Altstädten to Oberstdorf.
long_description: From Alstädten we walk up to the beautiful view. From there we continue to the Mahlerwinkel. We cross the villages of Unter-, Obertalhofen and Au. Then we climb up to the Schöllanger Burgkirche. Via Rubi we finally reach our destination Oberstdorf.

title: Adventure hiking trail near Thalkirchdorf
short_description: On this tour we walk along the adventure hiking trail at the foot of the Hündlekopf and enjoy the wonderful views of the Nagelfluh Nature Park. During the tour you have the opportunity to get to know the forest with its inhabitants.
long_description: This wonderful round tour takes us from Thalkirchdorf to the Schwändle inn. From there, we take the adventure hiking trail to the Hündle mountain restaurant and the Berkäserei cheese dairy. During the tour you have the opportunity to get to know the forest and its inhabitants.At the foot of the Hündlekopf we can see the 1834 m high Hochgrat. We then walk back to Thalkirchdorf via the Hochsiedel-Alpe.

title: Alb Panorama Trail near St. Blasien
short_description: The Alb-Panormaweg is a Nordic walking route for nature lovers. It follows historical paths. Once upon a time, charcoal burners were on the move here.
long_description: Our Nordic walking route is well signposted, takes us up the road to the game reserve (1) and continues straight ahead at first. We soon walk to the right, and come to a crossroads via a left-hand bend. We take the left path downhill and leave it again after about 100 m to go uphill to the right. The path eventually leads steeply downhill to a road, which we cross. Immediately afterwards, we walk towards a bridge on the right. After this, we turn left to the sawmill (2), take the "Unterer Sägeweg" (3) to the left at the edge of the forest and choose the right, steep path at the first fork. We reach a pulse measuring point (4) with an information board. Here we continue to walk to the left until we reach the Kohlpatte (5). We continue, following the left fork, before we come out of the forest in St. Blasien at the clinic (6). Here we follow the black Nordic Walking signs, walk through the village and finally reach the game reserve again via an ascent.

images.caption: Our route leads over this bridge through St. Blasien.
St. Blasien offers many shopping and refreshment options.
This view of St. Blasien is offered from the Kneipp facility.

title: In the Bernried Angle
short_description: An easy walking tour with many views of the surrounding countryside awaits us. We walk on soft meadow paths and along a stream.
long_description: From the tourist information office, we walk north in the direction of Böbrach. Shortly before the town exit sign, we follow the blue marking "Nordic-Walking Trail leicht" (easy) and trail no. 2. On a meadow path, we reach the weir and look back to the Bernried church. We cross the footbridge and follow the course of the stream. On soft, scenic paths we reach Böbrach. We reach the Sagstetter inn and turn left onto the road, cross the main road and pass a memorial cross with a rest area on the way to Krin. The path to Krin offers us a magnificent view. In the village, we turn left onto the road and follow it downhill. At the crossroads we turn right and via Innerirlach we reach Bernried again.

images.caption: We pass beautiful farmhouses and large fruit and walnut trees.
View from Krin, the highest part of the tour.
At the weir we have a beautiful view back to the Bernried church.
The road goes downhill across fields.
At the hunter's stand, follow the path along the edge of the field across the meadow.

title: From Hattingen to Schwelm
short_description: On this varied tour, we cross beech forests with holly as undergrowth, hike along lonely asphalt roads and enjoy narrow field and forest paths. At the beginning we take a look into an old railway tunnel and then climb the Bismarkturm.
long_description:
This tour takes us from Hattingen first to the Schulenbergtunnel, which was one of the artificial structures on the railway line from Hattingen via Sprockhövel to Wuppertal-Wichlinghausen. It is 195 m long. It was opened in 1884 and closed in 1984. Since 2008 it has been open again for cyclists and pedestrians.
The Bismarkturm was built in place of an old, dilapidated wooden lookout tower. wooden lookout tower. The tower was inaugurated in 1901. From the top you have a magnificent view of Hattingen and the Ruhr valley. In the farm shops of the two Köller and Berger farms offer a wide range of homemade specialities. specialities. A visit is definitely worthwhile! A small restaurant invites invites you to linger. The route then takes you across fields and meadows to Schwelm. and from there by public transport back to the starting point.

images.caption: View over Hattingen from the Bismarkturm.

title: Waterfall Trail in Cantareira Park
short_description: Very beautiful trail, totally immersed in a large remnant of Atlantic Forest, situated in the Cabuçu N cleo Cabuçu of the Cantareira State Park in SP.
long_description:
The Núcleo Cabuçu is located in the municipality of Guarulhos, in São Paulo, and was opened to the public in 2008. The park offers good infrastructure with parking, toilets, picnic areas, a Visitors' Centre and four beautiful nature interpretation trails.
The Cachoeira trail é the longest, about 6km (round trip), and é well signposted. Here, we join the Cachoeira trail with the Jaguatirica trail, which passes beside the beautiful Cabuçu Dam, a historic Brazilian construction.
The Cantareira State Park é divided into four núcleos and was inaugurated in 1963. In 1994, it was declared part of the Green Belt Biosphere Reserve of the city of São Paulo by UNESCO.

title: UrMeerPfad near Gerstetten
short_description: On the UrMeerPfad in Gerstetten we walk over a fossilised cliff that is over 150 million years old. Informative panels provide interesting insights into the history of the earth.
long_description: On the 14-kilometre round tour from Gerstetten to Heldenfinger Kliff and back, we experience exciting insights into the history of the earth. The tour ends with a visit to the reef museum.

title: Hiking to Stupa in Kathmandu
short_description: Hiking to Stupa in Kathmandu
long_description: This is the nearest hiking route from Kathmandu which is the capital city of Nepal. You can reach to the starting point by public bus, taxi or own vehicle our destiny is in middle of the hill so you have to go on height. Road condition is not so good especially on rainy season but you will have lots of fun and advanture during your journey.

title: Hike around the Kellersee lake near Malente
short_description: This hike takes us very close to the shore of the Kellersee lake in the middle of Holstein Switzerland. We can observe numerous animals or simply enjoy the idyllic lake. Afterwards, it is a good idea to take the "Kellersee trip".
long_description:
Our hike starts at the Haus des Kurgastes in Bahnhofstra&szlig in Malente. From there we walk into Kampstra&szlig, which we leave to the right into Rosenstra&szlig. At the next opportunity we turn left into Lindenallee, which takes us to the pier of the Kellersee-Fahrt. Here we follow the Wobbensredder to the right and cross the Schwentinebrücke. At Eutiner Stra&szlig we turn left and pass Gut Rothensande. As we continue on our route, we take the first turning and walk towards Prinzenholz and the Eutin-Fissau landing stage. Our path leads us very close to the shore and we can enjoy some beautiful views over the Kellersee. We continue along the Prinzenholzweg to the Eutin-Sielbeck landing stage. Now we leave the Kellersee for a short distance to reach the Ukleisee. There is a car park and the Jagdschlösschen on the Ukleisee. Take the „Rundweg 5“ to Sielbeck and then the Landstrasse to Eichkamp. On our way to Malente we always stay close to the water. When we reach Kellerseeestraße, it is not far to Kellerseepromenade and Janusallee, where the pier of the „Kellersee-Fahrt“ is located. We return to our starting point, the Haus des Kurgastes, on Kampstra&szlig.
Tip: If we still have time and feel like it after the long hike, we can take the „Kellersee-Fahrt“.

title: „Codrii Iașilor” nature trail
short_description: The route aims to educate hikers about the geological, faunal, and floristic heritage of the Dealul Repedea Reserve, but also to pump up some civic blood into locals and tourists about the need to protect the forest known as the Codrii Iașilor.
long_description:
The idea for this trail belongs to a local civic group that constantly works to protect what is left of the historical forest that once formed a green buffer between Iași and Vaslui, and which today falls victim to the interests of wood loggers.
The walk starts from the observatory built by Green Peace Romania in the Bârnova-Dobrovăț Forest and follows a path through the forest, checking off 10 information panels.
Many people climb Repedea Hill for the panoramas. The broadcast tower here is a well-known landmark in the local community. But the nature trail allows for a more in-depth discovery of the importance of this reserve and the adjacent forest. Along the way, can learn about the biodiversity of the place, admire some centuries-old trees, better understand their role in this ecosystem and maybe even decide to get involved in saving the forest.

images.caption: A generous panorama from the observatory
The observatory installed by Green Peace at Repedea Hill

title: Circular trail in the Vilsengtal valley near Vilshofen
short_description: Impressive flora and rare animal species: on our hike through the picturesque Vilseng valley we can experience and enjoy both.
long_description: We start our hike at the car park in Furtgasse. From here we walk down to the Vils (1) and continue on the footpath to the leisure and recreation centre (2). Behind it, we turn left, following the white-blue route "1". In this way we reach the Schlehberg district and finally also the Vil power station (3). From here on, we can discover small remnants of the old railway embankment (4) again and again on our way. Shortly after the turnoff to the Taferlsee (5), which is well worth seeing, we come to a road, turn right and cross the two bridges over the Vils. On the other side, we walk along the left bank of the Vils via Grafenmühl (6) and past the Taferl Chapel back to Vilshofen.

images.caption: A view of the Vils - in the background the mill of Grafenmühl.
The railway bridge and the town parish church.

title: "Climbing Experience" in the Bärenfalle Climbing Forest
short_description: The focus of this tour is on climbing fun through the Bärenfalle climbing forest.
long_description: By chairlift from the valley up to the bear trap. From there, a short walk to the climbing forest. Especially due to its exceptional location, the climbing forest is one of the most exciting climbing gardens in the Allgäu.

title: Accursed Mountains - Vjellak peak
short_description: Close to Peja your way starts to climb up Vjellak peak and goes down to stunning Rugova Gorge. It gets quite steep, but you will be happy to catch beautiful views over Peja city.
long_description: This peak overlooking the city of Peja, and is part of the Accursed Mountains range situated to the north of the town. It is a good peak as mountaineers from Kosovo and beyond summit it throughout the year. The trail to the peak begins from the city centre and progresses through the hills and mountains that offer beautiful landscapes and panoramic views of the Dukagjini flatlands before reaching the summit of Vjellak at 2,014 m. From this point you can see most of Kosovo’s territory on a clear day, as well as the mountain ranges of the Accursed Mountains in Montenegro and Albania. For those that want to continue with the hike, the trail connects to alternative routes that lead towards the villages of Rugova, namely the North to West hiking trail mentioned previously, which connects to Montenegro, as well as the trails of the Peak of Balkans and the Via Dinarica.

title: The St. Andrew's Chapel of Kleinvach - Eschwege
short_description: The idyllically situated St. Andrew's Chapel in Kleinvach is the destination of this hike.
long_description:
At first, the trail goes comfortably uphill and you soon get a glimpse of the Fürstenstein estate.
The trail then descends to the Werra and the benches. Here you meet a lot of enterprising people in the season.
The path leads up into the forest and then continues idyllically through light woodland above the cycle path.
Out of the forest there is a beautifully situated bench immediately on the left.
If you want, you can walk straight on for 10 minutes to Kleinvach and dine on excellent home-style dishes at the Zur Linde inn.
Through field paths we then reach the St. Andrew's Chapel with the Kleinvach cemetery. Only the road noise is a little disturbing when the wind blows from the west.
The detour to the nameless mountain behind the cemetery is definitely worthwhile, as you get to see large perforated stones and limestone rocks.
On returning to the bottom, you go to a small cemetery in the middle of the forest, a truly tranquil place.
You step out of the forest and walk down a path onto the cycle path.
Soon you have reached the benches again and walk directly along the Werra past Albungen in the direction of Jestädt. The vineyards with the striking rock formations are worth seeing. We soon return to the starting point via a beautiful grassy path and then a small climb.

images.caption: One of the rocks in the "vineyards" near Jestädt.
The St. Andrew's Chapel in Kleinvach is our destination.

title: From the Walloon town of Otterberg to the Stone Cross
short_description: From the picturesque Walloon town of Otterberg, we hike over the heights of the Geisberg to the Stone Cross. Via the war memorial with its magnificent view and through the adjacent sweet chestnut forest, we return to Otterberg, where a visit to the abbey church rounds off the hike.
long_description: From the picturesque Walloon town of Otterberg, we hike over the heights of the Geisberg to the Stone Cross. In fine weather, the asphalt path is a popular route for hikers, cyclists and inline skaters from the surrounding area. On stormy days, you can watch children flying kites here. The trail leads through beautiful mixed forests back to Otterberg, where we can make a detour to the war memorial with a magnificent view over the town. The adjacent sweet chestnut forest is a paradise for chestnut collectors in autumn. Due to the warm climate in the Palatinate, this tree, which is actually Mediterranean, thrives particularly well here. At the end of the tour, you should definitely explore the picturesque old town of Otterberg. The small town, which was founded by Cistercian monks and brought to economic prosperity by Walloon religious refugees, has many old half-timbered houses, narrow alleys and cosy squares with cafés and restaurants to offer. And with the Romanesque abbey church - the second largest church building in the Palatinate after Speyer Cathedral - the small town has a real architectural highlight.

images.caption: Over the heights of the Oberen Geisberg we hike in the direction of the Lauerhof.
The fountain in front of the market square shows important chapters in Otterberg's history, with the restaurant "Zur Krone" in the background.
The abbey church towers over the houses of Otterberg's old town.
Saint Bernard of Clairvaux commemorates the founding of the town as a Cistercian monastery.

title: Steinberg Tour - Schlitz-Willofs
short_description:
Slightly strenuous tour on easily accessible paths through a lot of forest.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
We start from our guesthouse in the direction of the main road Schlitz-Lauterbach. We cross this road and walk to the forest in the direction of Steinberg. Uphill through pine forest we come to the well-known forest crossroads Wulf-Böhmcker-Platz. The crossing
leads to 5 places (Schlitz, Burghausen, Niederstoll, Ützhausen, Bad Salzschlirf) here many hikers have already chosen the wrong path.
We take the 2nd path on the right to the Sattelstein ascent, then left downhill. If you want to hike to the Sattelstein, you have to go uphill for about 1500 m. Here a 10 x 10 m basalt with horse hooves awaits us. Legend has it that a knight once played dice with the devil for his life here. The knight won and the devil fled with horse's feet onto the stone. Hence the marking of these horses' feet.
Back to the farm tour, turn left downhill through high mixed forest towards Bad Salzschlirf. In Bad Salzschlirf we have many sights. Now we walk in the direction of the Schlitz cycle path along the edge of the forest to Ützhausen with a view into the Schlitz valley. In Ützhausen on the cycle path there is a farm on the left, here our hiking trail passes the farm on the left towards the forest. The farm has its own butcher's shop with farmhouse sausage specialities. Purchasing is possible. In the forest, the trail goes slightly uphill to the right, then right again over the Melmberg and left towards Wulf-Böhmcker-Platz back to Willofs.

title: Tennengebirge traverse from Stegenwald to Wengerau
short_description: From Gasthof Stegenwald via Pitschenbergtal, Wenger Scharte and Tauernscharte to Wengerau.
long_description: Our tour starts in the Salzach Valley and leads through the picturesque Pitschenberg Valley and the impressive karst plateau of the Tennengebirge Plateau past the Tauernkogel to the head of the Wengerau Valley near Werfenweng. The trail is extremely varied and you pass through the most diverse vegetation and altitude zones that the Northern Limestone Alps have to offer. Of course, various summit points (Tiroler Kogel, Mittleres Streitmandl, Eiskogel, Tauernkogel) can be reached along the way - as long as you have enough stamina and strength. In any case, the entire Pongau lies at your feet and the panorama up to the peaks of the Hohe Tauern is indescribable. The hut keepers at the Leopold-Happisch-Hütte and the Dr.-Heinrich-Hackel-Hütte cater for your physical well-being. Provided you are fit enough, the route certainly offers many unforgettable impressions of the Tennengebirge and the surrounding landscape.

title: El Chorro Valley Hike
short_description: Gradual hike offering featuring panoramic views, shaded forests and a short steep section to keep you on your toes!
long_description:
El Chorro is a world-class climbing hotspot and the gateway town to the incredible Camanito Del Rey hike. This hike is a great way to explore the valley of the town if you are spending the weekend in the area and a worthwhile addition to doing the Camanito Del Rey if you have some more time.
Most of the route follows a dirt road through a pine forest and is clear to follow. The hike is suitable for hikers of all levels, although, be wary if you do not have a good head for heights as the descent runs along a cliff edge and is exposed and wind speeds can pick up.  The cliffs themselves are quite spectacular!

images.caption: Sheer cliffs of the El Chorro valley.

title: Walking Around Lake Eymir
short_description: Anyone looking for nature routes in Ankara should discover the natural beauty around Eymir Gölü
long_description:
Eymir Gölü is a popular spot for many Ankara residents. Göl and its surroundings offer nature lovers many trails and paths of easy and medium difficulty where they can cycle or walk. 
While the trail that wraps around the direct phase of the day is quite beautiful, there are many routes where you can get away from the day phase a little bit and go to more forested areas and higher altitudes. When you experience these routes, you witness different landscapes.
Starting from one end of the Eymir Gölü, we try this 10-kilometre hike route that dives into forested areas and connects us back to the other end of the gölü. The route offers us wonderful views and panoramic views. On our way, we rest and take photos at the points that offer us beautiful nature views and we gather energy by eating our snacks. The route motivates us to experience other routes around the route.
If you're looking for a Sunday night activity, try this route with friends.

title: Bischofsgrüner Heilklima-Runde 2
short_description: Well signposted, this loop takes us through the nature spa park: here we can refuel at the "place of strength" and also pass a wetland biotope.
long_description:
Short circular walk through the nature spa park to the "place of strength" and a wetland biotope with gentle climbs.
In the "Place of Power" you can find your way to inner harmony and physical and mental balance through deep relaxation and tranquillity. The special powers of this place were discovered in May 1996 by the radiation seeker Lothar Meinhardt from Kempten.

title: Günzach - Kempten
short_description: On this hike we enjoy beautiful views of the Allgäu Alps and visit an old ruin.
long_description: From Günzach we hike along the railway line to the hamlet of Kürbsen. Behind it we catch our first glimpse of the Allgäu Alps. We reach a former ski jump. Via the mountain ridge we reach the Weihler Flesch and further on to the ruins of Wagegg. We walk through the meadows and hamlets to Kempten and after crossing the town we reach the railway station.

images.caption: Technocell Dekor GmbH & Co. in Günzach
An der Bahnlinie westlich von Günzach
Erinnerung an die Waldschanze von Wildpoldsried
Sankt Ulrich Kirche in Kempten Ost

title: Bischofsgrüner Heilklima-Runde 3
short_description: This circular trail combines healing climate hiking with a forest adventure trail: we do good for ourselves and learn at the same time.
long_description: This circular trail combines healing climate hiking with a forest adventure trail. We hike in the shelter of the forest with ascents of only a few metres in altitude and often moderate gradients.

images.caption: Forest experience and healing climate await us on easily walkable paths.

title: Valtellina Trail
short_description: The 114-kilometre-long Sentiero Valtellina makes it possible to walk or cycle along the Adda River from Bormio to Colico on Lake Como.
long_description: The Sentiero Valtellina (Valtellina Path) is a bicycle and pedestrian route that follows the course of the River Adda from Bormio to Lake Como (or vice versa) and is one of the most beautiful and interesting tourist attractions in the area. Along the mostly flat route, one can admire the landscapes of the Valtellina, with its characteristic villages, vineyards, castles and protected areas.

images.caption: Confluence of the Adda into Lake Como, near Colico, the end point of the Sentiero Valtellina

title: Heilklimaweg 1: Harp Spruce Weiskirchen
short_description: Long loop with flat and moderate climbs.
long_description: From the Parkhotel, we walk to the left to the end of the spa pond. There we reach the entrance to the Holzbach valley via Burgstraße and Kirchenweg. Following the course of the stream, we come to the Kneipp facility, above which we turn right. Then we go straight on to the street "Im Hänfert". Here we turn left again and enter the footpath to the Hochwald clinics. Past the Hochwald clinics and beyond the bus turning area, we reach a paved path, which we now follow. Above the hunting lodge "Viorel" the path makes a sharp bend to the left. Passing the shelter "Four Birches" we continue straight ahead on the ascending path. Pass the next fork and continue in the direction of "Vier Eichen". Past "Vier Eichen" we go downhill again in the direction of Weiskirchen. At the second junction we turn right. After about 20m we see a sign "Harfenfichte". We follow the path until we reach the hunting lodge "Viorel" again. We now walk the initial feeder trail in the opposite direction back to the Parkhotel.

title: North Baltic Sea Hiking Trail: From Rendsburg to Westensee
short_description: The Nord-Ostsee-Wanderweg (North Baltic Sea Hiking Trail) runs for around 115 km from Meldorf on the North Sea to Kiel on the Baltic Sea. The scenic route runs through the marshes and the Geest, along the Kiel Canal into the eastern hills of Central Holstein. We hike the fourth stage from Rendsburg to Westensee.
long_description: The starting point of the tour is at the Rendsburg foot tunnel, which passes under the Kiel Canal. On the south side of the canal we follow the path to the left to the railway bridge and suspension bridge in Osterrönfeld. Here we walk to the right along the railway bridge, under the ramp and cross the B202. Then turn left into Aspelweg and reach the foot of the railway embankment. Behind the first footpath, our path branches off to the right and leads across fields, through the Stadtmoor and the Wilde Moor to Bokelholm. In the village we cross the railway tracks and the main road and follow the path across the Mühlenau, the A7, past Wittenkamp and the Nordmoor to the Rümlandteich. The pond, closed off by trees, invites you to take a rest. South of it, the trail continues through woodland and past the Emkendorf estate, which is well worth seeing, to Brux. From here it is not far until we reach our stage destination Westensee in the middle of the Westensee Nature Park.

title: Nature and culture between Beckstein and Königshofen
short_description: On the nature and culture trail we walk around the Störenberg and the Frauenberg and enjoy the beautiful view of the valleys of the Tauber and Umpfer.
long_description:
From our starting point "Weinstraße, Ecke Königshofer Weg" in Beckstein, we follow the Königshofer Weg out of the village and climb straight up a hill on an asphalt path. There we find a rest area and a board with the overview map of the nature trail. The nature and culture trail is intended to provide an overview of the history, landscape and nature of the Tauber valley. With a beautiful view of the Königshöfer Turmberg, we walk a short distance along the hill. We do not follow our path, which now describes a right-hand bend, any further, but hike straight ahead on a grassy path. Along the path we find interesting descriptions of the nesting boxes placed there. At the first of a total of ten stations on the nature trail, we have a wonderful view of Königshofen and Marbach.
We follow this path downhill until we reach the chapel, turn right there into a narrow path and reach the road to Lauda via a steep staircase. Instead of following this, we take a sharp right directly onto the "Roter Weg" and pass a beehive standing on the side of the path to our right. A short climb follows along beautiful dry stone walls, at the end of which we can look back at Unterbalbach, Königshofen and the Turmberg. After a short distance, we see a vineyard and the Umpfertal valley with the village of Sachsenflur. We descend a wooden staircase to the left to a narrow path, which we follow with a view of Beckstein. Another flight of stairs brings us steeply down to just before the wine road that leads to Beckstein. Here we turn right, hike past the quarry uphill again and come back through the vineyards to Königshofer Weg and our starting point at the street corner.

title: Hiking up to Piatra Mare Cabin on the Family Road
short_description: One of the easiest - though not the shortest - route that goes up from Dâmbu Morii (DN1) to Piatra Mare Cabin is the Family Road (Drumul Familiar). The width of the path and the moderate climb recommend this route for children, in any season, even if the effort must be dosed due to the length.
long_description:
The Family Road is, for the most part, a forest path winding through the coniferous forest, crossing over streams of water, passing by water springs and wooden benches, revealing soothing landscapes and plenty of fresh air.
The route does not pose orientation problems and can be done in winter, with appropriate equipment. The climb is quite smooth, maybe just slightly steeper starting with the last clearing where the sign shows another 30 minutes to the cabin. The only disadvantage of this route may be its length, but the benches are there for you for a few minutes of well-deserved rest.
Those who dare or feel fit can test this route by mountain bike or even trail running.

images.caption: The wide path of the Family Road
The last clearing, before reaching Piatra Mare Cabin

title: Wiedhag-Alpe
short_description: The varied hike offers us nature experiences at the Schleierfall and in the Wildbachtobel, magnificent views from the summit station of the Iseler cable car and numerous places to stop for refreshments in the huts and alps above Oberjoch.
long_description: Past the picturesque Schleierfall (veil fall), we hike along the Bergwachtweg (mountain watch path) and the Palmweg (palm path) up to the Iselerplatzhütte and the mountain station of the Iselerbahn. Via the Wiedhagalpe and the Gundalpe we descend to Oberjoch - the highest mountain village in Germany. Finally, we descend through the romantic Wildbachtobel to Bad Oberdorf.

title: From Gunzesried to Blaichach along the Gunzesrieder Ach river
short_description: This hike leads along the Gunzesrieder Ach, past small flowing waterfalls from Gunzesried to Blaichach.
long_description: The starting village of Gunzesried lies in the heart of the Nagelfluh Nature Park. The easy hike runs along the idyllic torrent, the Gunzesrieder Ach. The route takes us along fairytale forests and colourful herb meadows to Blaichach. The evening ends there in a cosy atmosphere.

title: Gold Trail - Mambucaba Way
short_description: Trail considered one of the most classic in the country where it is possible to learn more about the history of the Paraíba Valley and see the exuberant nature of the Atlantic Forest up close.
long_description:
The Gold Trail in the Serra da Bocaina National Park, é one of the most traditional mountain walks in Brazil. Situated between Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, this walk é long and challenging, but at the same time not so demanding. Also known as Caminho de Mambucaba, this trail was opened by the Indians, but in colonial times it was covered with stones, placed by slaves.
The route é done in 3 days and begins at the entrance to the Bocaina National Park and continues through the preserved Atlantic Forest of the Bocaina Mountains and the Sea, until é Mambucaba, in Angra dos Reis. It takes about 6 hours of walking a day and there are several natural and cultural attractions, such as the stone path of slaves, but the main attractions are the rivers and waterfalls along the way, among them the Santo Isidro Waterfalls and the impressive Veados Waterfall, a giant of 200 meters stuck in the middle of the forest.

title: BACKBORD Tour
short_description: During this very leisurely walk, the anticipation of oven-fresh cake and freshly ground coffee is the focus of the activity :). If you have a guilty conscience after this indulgence, you can continue your walk towards Zempin through the wonderfully fragrant forest and let your soul dangle on the fine sandy beach. TIP: This short tour is also suitable for dogs, especially for letting off steam on the beach.
long_description: Today's destination of this walk is the Cafe Backbord in Zinnowitz, followed by a walk along the beach. Easy walk along the lakeside promenade and through the centre as well as along the shallow, fine-sand beach.

title: Bauberg Round
short_description: Difficult tour along the Antlassweg to the Baubergalm and via the forest path to the Jagawurz as well as the managed Bruggeralm back to Jochberg.

title: Around Mount Eitan
short_description: A relatively short, easy and circular walking route around Mount Eitan, which is located west of the city of Jerusalem.
long_description: The walking route around Mount Eitan is a circular route of approximately 7 kilometers starting from the Steph parking lot. Walking on the path is considered relatively easy and is mostly accessible to strollers. The route is rich in landscapes, coniferous trees and seasonal vegetation.

images.caption: A typical path in Mount Ethan

title: The shortest hike from Brașov to Poiana Brașov (Drumul Roșu)
short_description: A short hiking route, extremely accessible to anyone, no matter the season; also a well-maintained forest road, popular among hikers, mountain bikers, and trail runners alike, with multiple options for variation.
long_description:
The Red Road - after the red band that marks it - is the fastest access road from Brașov to Poiana Brașov. In addition, from Poiana, you can continue onwards (though with more effort) to Postăvaru Cabin and to the Postăvaru peak.
„Drumul vechi al Poienii” (the old road to Poiana), as this route is also called, connects the „Pietrele lui Solomon” area to one end of Poiana Brașov resort (Poiana de Jos). Even after the inauguration of the asphalt road, it stayed just as wide as before, and just as popular both among the tourists willing to take a few steps and among the locals.
It is an ideal trek to do with children, with the family, with your dog, no matter the weather (even in the rain, for amateurs). Depending on the season, but especially in the autumn, the forest and the path hold a diverse and special charm for photographers.

images.caption: 🚶♂️La pas👉Spre Poiana Brașov - Drumul Vechi Al Poienii (12/08/2021) ASMR [Tur Complet]

title: Around the Passower Lake near Lübz
short_description: Lake Passow is a jewel in the Mecklenburg Lake District. We also discover the beautiful Passow Castle on this tour.
long_description: From the outside, Passow Palace (1) appears rather inconspicuous. It is an example of pure, unadorned classicism. An old Slavic castle used to stand on this site. The round tower foundations can still be seen today in the historic wine cellar. The entrance hall of Passow Castle alone, which was a hotel until 2015, is worth a visit. The entire entrance area is laid with the finest marble. The fantastic ceiling and wall paintings are by the Italian artist Anselmo Pellicia. Our walk takes us from the palace through the English Garden down to the lake. We follow the small, inconspicuous path on our left. It leads us directly along the lakeshore. We come across countless small bridges through dense undergrowth. At the open-air swimming pool (2) the path clears. The beautiful lawn for sunbathing naturally offers a short rest. From the open-air swimming pool we follow the field path to the left of the lake. The path leads in a wide round to Weisin. It goes through sparse beech forest along the Alte Elde nature reserve. Shortly before Weisin we turn right onto a small road. Through the trees you can see the Weisin Lake on the left. A little later you reach the unusual white church of Weisin (3). A bell from 1450 is hidden in the half-timbered tower. Just a few steps further is the Weisin manor house (4). From here, we take the same path back to the bridge over the Alte Elde (5). A small path takes us to the western side of the lake. We walk along the densely wooded lakeshore. Soon we have reached the castle park (6) and Passow Castle again.

images.caption: The entrance hall of Passow Castle is very impressive.
Such quiet places can be found all around Lake Passow.
The stylish ambience at Passow Castle is a real feast for the eyes.
The Weisin church is striking for its colour.
There are plenty of photo motifs here.

title: A biotopic affair - Weissach im Tal
short_description: On the biotope nature trail we are introduced to the most important habitats for the native plants and animals at 17 locations.
long_description:
If you want to combine a hike with an exciting nature trail on the local flora and fauna, this rather long loop from Weissach is just right for you. In the cultural landscape around Weissach we can visit numerous preserved or newly created habitats. These include the brook with its riparian vegetation and floodplains, orchards, dry and lean meadows, hedges and field margins, wetlands, hollow paths, individual trees and a multitude of other small habitats. The route runs mainly along country lanes away from main roads and through small villages and is therefore easy to walk at any time of year.

title: La Tête des Chaudières
short_description:
La Tête des Chaudières vous offre un beau point de vue sur les sommets environnants du Vercors et bien au-delà !
Translate to English
long_description:
Cette randonnée commence bien raide. Le sentier débute à droite des pistes de ski alpin, à l’ombre de la forêt, il est pentu dès le départ et ce jusqu’à la cabane de Combeauvieux (1795 m, 500 m de dénivelé).
De là, prenez à droite, direction le Pas de la Balme, le sentier est plus régulier, il est en balcon jusqu’au col. L’effort sera vite récompensé surtout si vous apercevez des marmottes et des bouquetins, souvent nombreux à cet endroit. Le panorama qui s’ouvre devant vous est splendide : Mont Aiguille, Grand Veymont et la barrière de falaises du balcon est.
Au Pas de la Balme, l'itinéraire par en direction de la Tête des Chaudières.

title: Snowshoe: Alpspitze from Garmisch-Partenkirchen
short_description: The Alpspitze, situated above Garmisch-Partenkirchen, is a challenging spring tour destination for snowshoe tourers with its distinctive triangular summit structure.
long_description:
Anyone looking at the 2629 m high Alpspitze from the valley will wonder where the snowshoe-compatible ascent route to the triangular summit structure should lead. Nevertheless, it is one of the much-travelled spring classics, especially for ski tourers. A long, partly exposed summit ridge with wire rope protections awaits us, forcing us to walk the 300 metres to the summit. The tour on mostly east-facing slopes is only recommended when the firn is safe, but never after heavy fresh snowfalls or even windy conditions during the previous days.
Orientation is easy when visibility is good and there are tracks. With poor visibility and no tracks, however, it quickly becomes a challenge between the Stuibensee and the summit. In total, there are about 1100 metres of ascent. With the Kreuzalm and Hochalm, there are two places to stop for refreshments on the descent.

images.caption: View of Garmisch-Partenkirchen from the summit of the Alpspitze.

title: Snowshoe tour around Bad Wiessee
short_description: Easy snowshoe tour starting in Bad Wiessee. The route runs partly along the shore of Lake Tegernsee.
long_description: This snowshoe hike begins directly on the lakeside promenade of the spa town of Bad Wiessee and passes the iodine-sulphur bath after just a few metres. Along the Breitenbach we hike uphill to the Freihaus Brenner and shortly afterwards reach the Prinzenruf vantage point with a view of the wintry Tegernsee. From here we return to the lakeside promenade, where there are more places to stop for refreshments with a great view of Lake Tegernsee.

title: From Pico dos Marins to Pico do Itaguaré
short_description: As part of the Traverse from Pico dos Marins to Pico do Itaguaré, this trail crosses the crest of the Mantiqueira mountain range with privileged sceneries and unforgettable nature.
long_description: As the second day of the Marins-Itaguarpe Traverse, this trail is the hardest part of the traverse which follows all the time through the Mantiqueira ridge. With lots of ups and downs and many more technical stretches with rocks along the way, we reach the summit of Pico do Marinzinho. Soon after leaving Marinzinho, we reach the second most technical part of the walk. It is a very vertical descent of about 8 meters. <The trail continues steeply downhill towards the first valley floor before Pedra Redonda. From there é possípossible to observe Redonda still far away on mountain à front and, further still, separated by a huge valley, imposing Itaguaré.After some more ups and downs, couple of valleys an additional 2,7km walking, we arrive at clearing for camping. The climb peak all in rock climbing, including simple climbing pitch about 3 meters high. The view from top is simply sensational.
