title: Buchholz - Nordic Walking
short_description: This difficult Nordic Walking tour takes us through Buchholz near Nieheim.
long_description: This Nordic walking loop is only for experienced walkers. The route, which is marked with a 3, leads over 13 km through the Buchholz near Nieheim. The route goes steadily up and down.

title: Summit strikers on the Hochzellberg near Bodenmais
short_description: A beautiful distant view of Bodenmais is one of the attractions of this tour. On a high plateau we see many plants that have become rare.
long_description: At first, only a slight incline awaits us on the forest path, but we soon test our fitness on a steep section. At a fork, we turn left (white arrow on red ground) and follow the path until we come to a rest area. From here we look down into the valley to Bodenmais. We continue walking past overgrown rocks and reach the plateau of the Hochzellberg. High grasses grow on this area, where wild cocks live. A sign tells us how to take our pulse. On the left side we can see the Großer Arber. We enter the forest again and hike to a covered shelter. From here we go down along the forest path until we reach a crossroads on the right, where we return to our starting point.

images.caption: The Hochzellberg plateau is hardly overgrown.
Many rocks on the route are overgrown.
From this bench we have a great view of Bodenmais.

title: Round trip around Inishmaan
short_description: Round the middle of the three Aran Islands in Galway Bay.

title: From Bad Staffelstein to the former Banz Monastery
short_description: This tour takes us from the spa town of Bad Staffelstein up to the former Benedictine monastery of Banz, which today serves as a conference centre for the Hanns Seidel Foundation. Several places to stop for refreshments as well as the AquaRiese adventure pool and the Obermain Therme await us along our tour.
long_description:
Our tour starts at the car park at the spa gardens in Bad Staffelstein. We orientate ourselves on the road towards the north and cross under the railway line at the platform subway before keeping left at the station. On the opposite side of the road, we use the pavement to continue walking north. We cross the bypass on a bridge and reach Schönbrunn on the footpath and cycle path, which we walk through in a northerly direction. Shortly after entering the town, we turn left off the footpath and cycle path and walk beautifully along Schönbrunner See, a quarry pond, before we reach the adjacent Reundorfer See. Here we also find a bathing opportunity that is popular in summer. Now we keep to the left and cross the Main at the weir. The town of Coburg has been generating electricity here for over 100 years. In Hausen we keep to the right for a short while before we hike steeply uphill through the forest to Banz. The steep section demands a lot of us, but we are rewarded with a stop at the monastery restaurant - or with the magnificent view from the church steps. Today, the monastery serves as a conference centre for the Hanns Seidl Foundation, which has close ties to the CSU. The Banz monastery library was world-famous before secularisation. The spacious inner courtyard of the monastery is also impressive - or the museum with treasures from Duke Max of Bavaria.
Finally, we make our way back to Bad Staffelstein and walk along the road on the footpath through Neubanz, always steeply downhill to Unnersdorf, where the "Berggasthof Banzer Wald" invites us to stop for a break on the wonderful open-air terrace with a view of Banz. In Unnersdorf, we first turn left and then walk straight ahead until we cross the Main bridge before turning right at the sign "AquaRiese". At the adventure pool we have the opportunity to stop for a break or to take a dip in the indoor pool or the adjacent outdoor pool. We return to our starting point in a few minutes through the nearby spa park, but should not miss the opportunity to take a rest in the impressive graduation house. At the end of the tour, we can also relax in the Obermain Therme.

images.caption: In the spa gardens we have a wonderful view up to the Staffelberg.
In the beer garden at the Berggasthof Banzer Wald, we have a magnificent view of Banz Monastery.
The impressive monastery complex in Banz is our destination.

title: Snowshoe: Hochplatte in the Ammer Mountains
short_description: This snowshoe tour to the Hochplatte (2079 m) is a scenic äußerst delightful undertaking, which, however, requires a good physical condition due to the distance to be covered.
long_description: The Hochplatte in the Ammer Mountains offers us everything we expect from a snowshoe tour: Wonderful scenery and a varied ascent. However, we should not underestimate the tour to the Hochplatte, stable conditions are a prerequisite, as some of the slopes are quite steep. The orientation of the slopes, on which we move up and down, is mainly east-facing. Orientation is quite easy in large parts. However, if there are no tracks and visibility is poor, it can be a challenge. Due to the distance to be covered, fitness is required.

title: On the energy trail to the Linachtal reservoir
short_description: The circular walk takes us along shady forest paths to the Linachtalsperre near Vöhrenbach. This architectural monument is unparalleled in Germany.
long_description: Our circular route is lined with 20 information boards about the power station, the ecology of the valley and the restoration of the dam wall. The starting point is the power station built in 1924 in Art Nouveau style, which has been faithfully restored. We always follow the yellow rhombus until we see the dam wall after about an hour. The Linachtalsperre is 143 m long and 25 m high. When the lake is dammed, the crown can be walked on and offers a beautiful view of the course of the Linach and the lake. After electricity production was abandoned in 1969, the water was completely drained in 1988. Thanks to a Linachtalsperre supporters' association, the dam has been completely renovated since the 1990s. Today, the power station can supply up to 400 households with electricity. In the meantime, an idyllic recreation area has grown up around the lake. After we have inspected the impressive structure with its 13 towers and twelve piers, we walk back along the other side of the valley. At the small, large gatehouse, the above-ground slope pipeline ends and a downpipe directs the water into the turbine house. Behind the house we hike about 150 m uphill and then partly very steeply downhill until we reach our starting point again.

images.caption: The imposing dam wall of the Linachtalsperre.
A bench in front of a granite rock invites you to take a rest.
At the end of our tour we arrive back at the Turbine House.
Numerous information boards accompany us on our way.
This is where our tour starts: the Turbine House.
Views of the Linachtalsperre open up at many points.

title: Schönbrunn drinking water dam in the Middle Thuringian Forest
short_description: We hike around the Schönbrunn Dam and can admire the crystal-clear water surface.
long_description:
While walking around the Trinwassertalsperre Schönbrunn, we mainly walk on gravel and asphalt paths and pass numerous mountain meadows. Again and again, we are offered great views of the artificial lake and the surrounding area.
In the largest nature reserve in the Thuringian Forest lies the Schönbrunn drinking water dam with its calm and crystal-clear waters. The dam serves to supply drinking water to the regions of Suhl, Hildburghausen, Ilmenau, Meiningen and Schmalkalden. In total, it supplies 230,000 consumers in southern Thuringia with drinking water. Another function is flood protection.

images.caption: Most of the tour leads over gravel or asphalt paths.

title: Lewis Mountain – Big Meadows (Appalachian Trail)
short_description: Hike on the Appalachian Trail from Lewis Mountain Campground to Big Meadows Campground in Shenandoah National Park
long_description: Shenandoah National Park covers part of the Blue Ridge Mountains in the US state of Virginia. The park is long and narrow, with the wide Shenandoah River and Valley on the west side and the rolling hills of Virginia Piedmont to the east. Our hiking trail leads us on about 14.5 km through the natural landscape worth seeing.

images.caption: Sunrise at Shenandoah National Park, VA
Forest path in Shenandoah National Park, VA

title: Around the Brunnschlag near Heilbrunn
short_description: This tour takes us through beautiful forest areas around the Brunnschlag and offers us wonderful views of the surrounding countryside again and again.
long_description: From the war memorial, we start our tour in the direction of the pilgrimage church and leave Heilbrunn in a westerly direction. We walk through the forest, keep left at a crossroads and reach an open area with good distant views. The path leads us to a junction where we first keep right and then take the path to the left into the forest. Follow the markings "Green triangle on white background" and after a long stretch of forest you reach an open space with a beautiful view. At the crucifix in the hamlet of Kesselboden, we enter the forest again. We finally reach a hut where we can take a rest. Finally, we cross the junction again and walk along the edge of the forest so that we get back to Heilbrunn on the same path.

images.caption: Our tour leads through wooded areas with very soft, pleasant ground to walk on.
Two main hiking trails converge at the crucifix.
Believers have been making pilgrimages to the Marian pilgrimage site of Heilbrunn with its fountain of grace since the 17th century.
The stations of the "Seven Sorrows of Mary" accompany us on our journey.
The parish church in Heilbrunn is a well-known place of pilgrimage to the Virgin Mary.
From the open space we enjoy the magnificent view over the Pilgramsberg with its church.

title: From the Hercules to the Hessenschanze near Kassel
short_description: This medium-difficulty loop takes us from Kassel's landmark, the Hercules, through the meadows and forests of the Habichtswald Nature Park to the Hessenschanze, a former sports field of the "Hessen" club before World War 1.
long_description: The start of our hike is the Hercules, Kassel's landmark visible from afar in the beautiful Bergpark Wilhelmshöhe. We can visit the Hercules for a small fee and climb up to the dome, or we can just walk around to the other side and enjoy the magnificent panorama of the park with Wilhelmshöhe Palace and the city of Kassel. First we walk past the car park towards the edge of the forest. On the left, use the passage in the pasture fence and walk down the pasture to the bridge over the Ahne. At the seating area, turn left into Kastanienallee and follow it to the crossroads at the former Bundeswehr depot. Here we keep to the right and then immediately turn left again in the direction of Kleiner Auskopf/Douml;rnberg village. When you reach the edge of the forest, turn right at an acute angle and follow the signs to "Forsthaus Haide", which is soon on the right-hand side of the path. At the turnoff to the Höllchen (on the left), we continue on the right in the direction of the Igelsburg horse breeding farm. Before continuing, we can make a small detour to the Silbersee. It is somewhat hidden in the forest, but is signposted. At the Igelsburg, our route takes us on the Förstersteig trail to the left again into the forest. Soon we reach the Ahne, the lowest point of the trail. We bypass the Hühnerberg to the northwest and now follow the signs to the Erlenloch. Once you have reached the former quarry hole and the inn of the same name, hikers who have become tired can take the bus back here (line 110). Those who are keen on hiking follow the path to the Blue Lake (small detour) and on to the Rasenallee car park and the Hessenschanze (both are signposted).

title: Tour from Hohenschwangau around the Alpsee lake
short_description: The Alpsee lake at the gates of Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau lies in the midst of a dreamlike setting with impressive architectural monuments.
long_description: From the car park, follow the signs for "Alpsee" and walk along the wide, asphalted access road past numerous restaurants and hotels to the Alpsee. At the lakeshore (1), walk to the left, follow the signs for "Badeanstalt"/ "Marienmonument" and stay on the footpath directly on the lakeshore. Looking back, you can see the Alpsee against the backdrop of the castles of Hohenschwangau and Neuschwanstein. After the bathing establishment (2), a narrow path winds along the stony and rocky western shore - with fantastic views again and again (3). You pass a Marian monument (4) until you reach the north shore (5). Here it becomes a little more strenuous, as the path climbs slightly and then drops again soon afterwards. The tour ends with a visit to Hohenschwangau Castle or the impressive Neuschwanstein Castle.

images.caption: The path on the western shore of the Alpsee.

title: Iarna, prin Rezervația de ghimpe de la Comana
short_description:
Cele câteva trasee marcate din Parcul Natural Comana îți oferă prilejul să străbați pădurea în lung și-n lat în orice sezon. Dacă mergi iarna, ai parte de multă vegetație uscată, dar colorată, și de multă liniște.  
Translate to English
long_description:
Traseul acesta e doar una din multiplele posibilități de a explora pădurea Comana. De altfel, cam prin orice parte ai lua-o, peisajul e unul asemănător: trunchiuri dese de arbori, poteci destul de late, jocuri de lumini printre ramurile golașe cu câteva frunze încă atârnând de ele.
Iarna, potecile generoase din pădure nu mai sunt luate cu asalt de mountain bikeri, așa că mulți vin aici să-și plimbe câinii în voie.
Zgomotul de fond e asigurat de foșnetul frunzelor, de scârțâitul trunchiurilor sau de păsările care au rămas să ierneze aici. Vegetația e puțină, însă frumusețea locului e compensată prin liniștea multă. Cu puțin noroc, se pot observa animale sălbatice (ciute sau mistreți).
Pe final de traseu, am făcut o oprire și la observatorul ornitologic și la Fântâna cu Nucu.

title: Marconi in Connemara
short_description:
There are two historical highlights on this short hike: The remains of an old Marconi radio station (with counterpart in Newfoundland), and the place where Alcock and Brown landed after their first transatlantic flight (from Newfoundland)
.

title: TEST 14 - The lodgepole pines of Armo.
short_description: Armo is one of seven villages in Valvestino, five of which belong to the municipality of the same name (the others are Bollone, Moerna, People and Turano), and two to Magasa (the one with the municipal seat and Cadria).
long_description:
One of the characteristics of the vast forest areas distributed around the village of Armo is the presence of the Scots pine forest, probably the result of artificial planting carried out by the Austro-Hungarian administration at the beginning of the 20th century, for the purpose of hydrogeological protection of the landslide western slope of Mount Pralta. In the pine forest, now mixed with broadleaf trees, some pines preserve signs of the resin harvesting that was once carried out to conduct trade with the Venetian Republic, which worked this natural material with fire to produce turpentine and pitch for use in caulking ships.
An excursion itinerary starts from Armo and leads through the pine forest, in a natural setting of water, rock and impressive woods.

title: #adidasterrex 1.100 Km Challenge EN
short_description: I'm not much of a hiker, but I'd like to complete the 1,000 km challenge on Outdooractive in 2023 (so far I've only ever managed around 500 km a year). I want to hike a total distance of 1,100 km, which is approximately from my hometown of Weiler to Cuxhafen. The idea is to slim down massively in the process. That would be my dream project for 2023.

title: Transbucegi Road
short_description: The Transbucegi road connects Sinaia (Dichiu Hut) and Piatra Arsă Hut in the Bucegi Mountains. Together with other Transmountain roads, it is one of the most beautiful tourist attractions in the country.
long_description:
Transbucegi is one of the most beautiful roads in Romania. Its accessibility and superb scenery make it one of the busiest mountain roads with an exit in the Alps. The Transbucegi is shorter than the famous Transfăgărășan or Transalpina, but with equally spectacular viewpoints. Tourists come here in large numbers, most of them by car.
Now, after the recent asphalting, the Transbucegi has become accessible not only to mountain bikers, who are in any case on the mountain plateau, but also to mountain bikers. For the latter, the trail stops at the hut, where the path is paved. For mountain bikers, the route can continue to Babele or to Vârful cu Dor, then Sinaia.
The maximum altitude on Transbucegi is reached at the Piatra Arsă hut (1950m). From here, beautiful views of the entire plateau open up, with the Coștila relay being very visible.

title: La Grande Sure via the Grande Vache pass
short_description: This hike, which starts at the Col de la Charmette (cul de sac) in Proveysieux, offers exceptional Alpine panoramas that are sure to impress.
long_description:
From the Col de la Charmette parking lot, head towards the Chalet de la Charmette and take a forest track uphill to the Col de la Grande Vache.
From the Col de la Grande Vache, descend to the Col de la Sure, then make a round trip to the summit of the Grande Sure (approx. 1 hour). Continue the loop through the mountain pastures to Hurtières, then the eponymous col.
Continue south to the Vavarey meadow, then descend to the Col de la Charmette.

title: Jogging round Blaichach
short_description: We enjoy a varied, medium-difficulty jog from Immenstadt via the Rieder-Alp and Schwanden into Blaichach. We return along the Iller river.
long_description: Shortly after the start, a first strenuous climb awaits us. Behind Riederalp we run down a long flight of stairs until we reach Schwanden, where we climb up again. Here we reach the highest point of the route. The route descends steadily to Blaichach railway station. On the way back to Immenstadt, the terrain along the Iller is almost all flat. Here, depending on your mood, we can go at a pleasant to strenuous endurance running pace.

title: Lake Constance circular hiking trail from Lindau to Nonnenhorn
short_description: The hike, which is very manageable in terms of time, offers beautiful views üover Lake Constance. We walk through picturesque parks and gardens, which are laid out between excellently maintained villas and the lakeshore. In Wasserburg, the castle awaits us with its fantastic location on the peninsula next to the church. At the end, Nonnenhorn offers a visit to an old wine cellar. If you do the trail in winter, you will be pleased to know that the B&Bs in Lindau and Wasserburg have opened their outdoor facilities for walkers during this time, which shortens the route slightly, but enriches it with more beautiful passages.
long_description:
Lindau is a town with a very eventful history. Its special location on an island in Lake Constance contributes to this flux. Lindau has been particularly influenced by shipping, the salt trade and railway traffic over the last few centuries. The journey by train alone, over the embankment to the terminus, is an experience without equal in Europe. It is not comparable with a trip to the island of Sylt, as this is a lake. Leaving the station, it is only a few steps to the harbour, which has become famous all over the world for its harbour entrance, the lighthouse and the Bavarian lighthouse. A stroll through the city takes you past pretty town houses and numerous churches and towers. Maximilianstrasse is particularly worth a visit.
The Lindenhof Park in Bad Schachen and the Villa Lindenhof were laid out between 1842 and 1845. Today the entire area is owned by the town of Lindau. It is the largest park in the area of the Lindau villas. The Schweizerhaus, which was built in the 19th century as a servant's house, is also located there. It is particularly impressive with its many carvings on the balconies and facades.
In Wasserburg, the peninsula offers a unique photo backdrop formed by the castle, a church and other buildings. Calendars often feature a view taken from the seaside. This is particularly possible from a ship. However, the jetty and a wide-angle lens are also very useful if you want to capture the scenery from the water side.
The Weintorkel in Nonnenhorn is an old wooden wine press dating from 1591 and has been a listed building for several decades. It is freely accessible and can be visited at any time. During the Christmas season, a nativity scene is set up in it.

title: Transylvania road trip: The Bethlen family heritage houses
short_description: The road trip takes you through the legendary realm of Transylvania, to explore it from a historical point of view - namely, visiting the manor houses that belonged to the Bethlen aristocratic family. The family members have been owning large domains in the region, since the 14th century. If history isn't your thing, this is an excellent opportunity to stop in lesser-known places, taste local wines, and admire enchanting landscapes.
long_description:
Why the focus on the Bethlen family?
Because several noblemen in the family occupied high positions within the Principality of Transylvania, in the medieval period. Two Transylvanian princes came from the family. The reign of Gabriel Betheln (1613-1629) remains of reference for the domestic economic drive, but also for the aggressive foreign policy.
Legend has it that the Bethlen family ended the dominance of the dragon serpent in the villages around Sighisoara. An ancestor of the family tricked a snake that was hiding under one of the hills near Criș into eating lime and thus cause his death. Hence, the family coat of arms depicts a snake and is visible in all the residences along the route.
All manor houses on the route are among the most representative and well-preserved mansions with Renaissance architecture in Romania. What's more, the one at Cetatea de Baltă has kept its function as a vineyard manor, being located in the middle of the main Transylvanian vineyard, owned by Jidvei nowadays.

title: Midday hike in the footsteps of Carmen Sylva
short_description: When the sun is beating down you can retreat to the hillside, following the walk that perhaps even Carmen Sylva (Elizabeth of Romania's literary pseudonym) took.
long_description:
This hike offers an opportunity to get back to nature and enjoy the fresh air and forest scents. Stroll along the narrow paths and discover a lookout point with a gazebo located on Queen Elizabeth Rock, which locals call Mala Fortica.
Here's the story that led to the creation of this promenade: King Carol I of Romania, a guest of Villa Amalia, once got lost during his daily horse ride through the forest below Veprinac, probably in 1896, during his first stay in Opatija. This prompted him to go the next day to the district director, Baron Arthur von Schmidt-Zabierow, to enquire why the paths were not better maintained and marked. When Zabierow confidentially explained that there was simply no money, Carol gallantly presented him with a rather large sum needed to solve the problem. The money was spent, and construction of the first trail was completed in 1901.

title: Circular trail from the Freyburger Alpe to the Besler
short_description: Starting from the Freyburger Alpe, the route leads from the Lochbach valley to the Besler.
long_description:
The circular trail starts at the Freyburger Alpe and leads across fields and wooded areas below the Besler ridge. We climb the Besler from the far side.
The descent from the summit begins with a short climb. Via the Obere and Mittlere Gund-Alpe we make our way back down. Back at the Freyburger Alpe, you can reward yourself with a hearty snack or a tasty piece of cake in summer.

title: Crossing Petrópolis - Teresópolis: Day 2
short_description: The crossing between the two mountain cities of Petrópolis and Teresópolis in Rio de Janeiro is one of the most famous in Brazil and is also considered one of the most beautiful;
long_description:
Included in the National Park of Serra dos Órgãos - PARNASO - the recommended duration of the Traverse é of 3 days, so that you can take greater advantage of its stunning landscapes. There is a total distance of 30 kilometres between the two sites, reaching an altitude of 2,275 metres.
The second day of the Traverse connects the two shelters of this route: the Açu Shelter and Shelter 4, at Pedra do Sino. But before starting the walk, the day begins with a spectacular sunrise on the Serra dos Órgãos, which can be contemplated from the Pedra do Açu or the Portals of Hércules.In this stretch it is essential to use a GPS, especially if it is a foggy day, and safety climbing equipment for the more difficult stretches. The Park recommends the presence of an experienced guide.

title: Oze Hatotai Pass - Ozegahara
short_description: Ozegahara is located at an altitude of approximately 1,400 metres and is cool even in summer. It is easily accessible from the Kanto region and is one of the most popular meccas for hikers in Japan. The course from Hatotai Pass on the Tochigi Prefecture side to Ozegahara is one of the standard courses among the many hiking trails in Oze.
long_description:
Hiking in Oze involves a wide variety of trails and hikers need to plan their route according to the season, the plants they want to see, the scenery and how they want to get to Oze. Hatotai Pass is one of the three entry points into Gunma Prefecture. From late May to June, Oze is beautiful with clusters of Mizubashou, a typical flower of the area, and until early August, the area is coloured with colourful flowers. The autumn colours can also be enjoyed from late September to early October. The entire route is approximately 17 km long, but if you are not confident about your fitness, you can skip the round-the-clock route towards the Research Park or turn back to the starting point at the Ushikubi junction.
Right from the start, you will walk on a slightly steep path through a primeval beech forest. The path is a delight for hikers during the season of fresh greenery and autumn leaves. Walk on stone pavements and wooden steps, but be careful after it has rained, as they can be slippery. Occasionally you can see Mt Jibutsu on your left through the trees, and about 10 minutes after the start, the path becomes flat and wooden. In the Temmasawa marshland just before Yamanohana, Mizubashou (Asian skunk-cabbage) blooms in spring, albeit in a small area. When the Kawakami Bridge comes into view, Yamanohana is just a short distance away. After passing the Yamanohana Visitor Centre, there are no toilets until the Ryugu Hut. The Research Sample Garden next to Yamanohana is located in the westernmost part of Ozegahara and is a marshland where the nature of Oze is concentrated and untouched by humans. There are two wooden paths that go around the marshland: a major circuit course, which takes about 40 minutes, and a minor circuit course, which takes about 20 minutes. In spring, Mizubasho (Asian skunk-cabbage) is beautiful and there are newts, tadpoles, dragonflies and other creatures in the ponds.
The course from Yamanohana to Ryugu Crossroads is a walk along a wooden path stretching over the marshland with Mt Shitsubutsu in front of you, and can be considered the main route in Ozegahara. The area past the Kawakami Bridge in Hara in particular offers a panoramic view of the marshland of Kami-tashiro. Crossing the Kamino-Ohori River, you enter the Nakadashiro of the three divisions of Ozegahara (Shimo-Tashiro, Nakadashiro and Kami-Tashiro). Hiuchidake can be seen in the distance. When you eventually reach the Ushikubi branch, go right to the Ryugu crossroads. Walking along the wooden path along the river, you will be greeted by Mizubashou and Nikkoukisuge in the spacious landscape typical of Oze. The Ryugu phenomenon can also be seen in this area, where the flow of the waterway is sucked underground and disappears to form subterranean water.
From the Ryugu Crossroads to the Yoppi Suspension Bridge, around the end of June, the 'Yamadori zenmai' (mountain lily) shows its beautiful fresh green appearance. The panorama of white birch trees, Mt Shitsubutsu and Hiuchidake that can be seen on both sides is also beautiful. After crossing the Yoppi Suspension Bridge over the Yoppi River, which has abundant water, there are many small and large ponds and you can walk to them on a wooden path. On the way back to the Ushikubi Branch, you will pass through one of the most famous areas of Nikkoukisuge in Ozegahara. As there are relatively few people passing by, it is a place where you can take a leisurely stroll through the marshland. Once you reach the Ushikubi junction, the rest of the trail changes the way you came to Hatotai Pass. Just before the Hatotai Pass, the path climbs rather steeply, so watch your step to avoid slipping.

title: The circuit of lakes in mountain Banat
short_description: The mountain landscape surprises even the traveller who has lived in the area for some time; and this cycle route is a little gem in the otherwise diverse menu of outdoor activities in the region.
long_description:
The route does not fall into the category of classic cycle tours, where you can ride relaxed and focused towards your next destination, knowing where you will spend the night at the end of the day. It's more of a route that challenges you to clearly calculate your distances and dose your effort.
And the scenery isn't sensational, but rather sensory and eye-opening. Especially as you pass through an area marked by mining operations, and the tourist attractions are more anthropogenic phenomena: reservoirs, tailings ponds, traces of former mines, industrial museums.
The natural landscape is marked by the karst character of the relief of the Semenic-Carasului Valley Nature Park: caves, gorges, limestone rocks with strange shapes, all surrounded by centuries-old deciduous forests, which are said to hide treasures (according to some legends).
The route also passes through several villages populated by Croats, where daily life goes on at the same leisurely pace as in Romanian villages, but in a different language.
Experiences to consider on the route:
visits to the Locomotive Museum in Reșița, Anina Museum Centre and the Mineralogy Museum in Ocna de Fier
water sports on Lake Dognecea
food prepared by the Kibuț (a culinary experience combined with a visual and auditory experience to match; it may seem more expensive, but it's worth it)

title: The forts of the Authion
short_description: Here is a very nice walk between the sea and the mountains in the Mercantour National Park! In any season, the view is breathtaking all along the route
long_description:
This loop of more than 2 hours takes you to discover the Authion forts on the borders of the Vésubie, Bévéra and Roya valleys. You will have the opportunity to visit the summits of the Pointe des Trois Communes, Forca and Mille Fourches, which offer magnificent panoramas between the Mediterranean Sea and the Mercantour massif. The Southern Alps offer an exceptional setting!
The old military forts will mark one of the highlights of this hike. These fortifications were the subject of a border between France and Italy from the end of the 19th century to the end of the Second World War. The Authion massif occupied a strategic position and an important role in the defence of the county of Nice.
Accessible to all, this loop hike rich in history is sure to leave its mark! So don't hesitate to put it on your to-do list!

title: A trip to the source of the tuff (Quelltuff)
short_description: A circular hiking route that starts from the village of Lingenau in western Austria and leads to an interesting and unique geological phenomenon in Austria and in general!
long_description:
A particularly surprising hiking route in this area starts from the outskirts of the village of Lingenau, in the Vorarlberg region of western Austria and leads to a wooden boardwalk from where you can admire a unique natural phenomenon of a yellowish tuff rock with special shapes known as "the source of the tuff". On top of the yellowish tuff-limestone rock, small waterfalls flow harmoniously into the stream in the valley. This is an amazing, beautiful and special natural phenomenon that is worth seeing. The tuff rock found in this route is considered the largest of its kind in Europe north of the Alps!
The hiking route starts on the plain and passes next to some houses located on the outskirts of the village (you have to park near the T-intersection of roads 205 and 6 since the access road that reaches the beginning of the trail is for tenants only and there is no parking there). Further on there is a descent on an asphalt road that very quickly connects to a natural path from which wooden steps descend leading to the viewing promenade on the tuff stone. Please note that the nature of the trail is not accessible to wheelchairs or strollers, but with supervision children can also navigate it.
In order to easily find the point where the route starts, it is recommended to open the map attached to this route in the Outdootactive app .

title: Stage 4 KR: Wasserkuppe - Gotthards
long_description:
Past the distinctive dome of the Radom, the trail goes along the north side of the Wasserkuppe to the airmen's memorial. Below the aviation monument at the edge of the forest, the Hochhöner leads steeply down to Abtsroda. On the way you will pass:
- Fliegerdenkmal (926), certainly the most famous monument in the Rhön is also the most beautifully situated. It has to do with the history of aviation on the Wasserkuppe: after the First World War, motorised flight was not allowed in Germany, but gliding was. And so the Wasserkuppe became a "Mecca" of gliding. The monument, erected in 1923, evokes the importance of flying for Germany, so it has a strong nationalist background. - Edge of the forest - ski lift station (743)
- Poppenhausen-Abtsroda/eastern edge of the village - country road junction (698)
- Weiherberg (786), it is definitely worth climbing up to the summit cross slightly above the hiking trail: the view of the Wasserkuppe and the western Rhön is breathtaking. - Enzianhütte car park (745)
- Enzianhütte (739)
- Grabenhöfchen (688)
- Bubenbader Stein (704), The Bubenbader Stein is part of a larger group of basalt rocks scattered in the forest here. - Milseburg (835), next to the Wasserkuppe certainly the most famous mountain in the Rhön. Beautiful rocky peak (fantastic panoramic view!) with an old crucifixion group (which has been here since 1756). There has never been a "castle" here, but the mountain was inhabited in Celtic times, as the ring walls around the Milseburg show. Next to the summit is the small Gangolf Chapel. - Milseburg car park (661)
In the Oberbernhardser Höhe nature reserve, gentians bloom. The Hochrhöner runs in wide loops through the forest until it reaches the village of Langenberg. Around the hilltop of Ulrichshauk and past the sports field on the edge of Schwarzbach, the trail descends to Gotthards.

title: Hiking in the forests around the Homola observation deck by Modra, the Little Carpathians
short_description: If you're looking to go hiking in the Little Carpathians, this gentle circular route in the Modra area is a good option. It takes you from the car park in Piesok to the Homola observation deck (Veľká Homoľa) and then into the calming and lush setting of the surrounding hills.
long_description:
Also known as the Lesser Carpathians, The Little Carpathians make up a range of forested mountains about 100km long that you can easily reach from Bratislava. 
While there are limitless options available to explore the hills, this is a hike I planned while holidaying in nearby Modra - and I thought it was pretty good fun. 
The route includes Veľká homoľa, which at 710 m is the 8th highest peak in the range. There's an observation tower on the summit that offers excellent views across the Danube Lowland and further into the mountains themselves. The route then loops around various trails and roads to eventually bring you back to Piesok. 
In all, I felt it was a good taster of the Little Carpathians and an easily accessible option for anyone wanting to escape the bustle of Bratislava.

title: Hiking around Lac de Paladru
short_description: This hiking itinerary is an invitation to discover Lac de Paladru and the surrounding area!
long_description:
Choose your starting point for the tour of the lake, which can begin from any of the four villages: Charavines, Bilieu, Le Pin or Paladru.
This magnificent "Lac Bleu", renowned for the beauty of its surroundings and the clarity of its waters, was sculpted by the mighty Rhône glacier during the Ice Age. Situated at an altitude of 500 metres, in the heart of wooded and agricultural hills, it is the fifth largest natural lake in France. Its shores were home to one of Isère's earliest human communities, dating back to 2700 BC (the Neolithic village of Les Baigneurs). Several sites in the region have been classified as "protected natural areas".
In each of the four villages (Charavines, Le Pin, Paladru, Bilieu), you'll find shops, public toilets and a beach (with the exception of Bilieu).

title: Schneekopflauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The Schneekopflauf ends on the summit of the same name, with the last stretch still involving the difference in altitude between 711 m and 978 m.
long_description: In 1924, the very first Rennsteiglauf led from the Schneekopf plateau to Schmiedefeld. Today, the route has been reversed by the organisers: now it's 12.7 km from Schmiedefeld via the Großer Finsterberg up to the Schneekopf.

title: Circular hike suspension bridge - Haltuson
short_description: Experience pure Valais: circular hike Haltsuon with suspension bridge and Suon, past sculptures and through picturesque landscapes
long_description:
The Haltsuon circular hike in the canton of Valais is an unforgettable nature experience. The starting point is the cable car in Unterbäch. From there, the trail leads through the picturesque village, past fascinating sculptures on the sculpture trail. The route leads to the imposing Milibach suspension bridge, which brave hikers crossed.
The trail continues along the old path towards Eischoll, and at the westernmost point of the hike, a short stretch is covered along the road before rejoining the hiking trail. The relaxing accompaniment of the babbling Haltsuon stream accompanies hikers through dense forests and picturesque meadows on the way back to Unterbäch.
This tour offers the opportunity to enjoy the beauty of Valais to the full and is suitable for both beginners and experienced hikers. The hiking time is around 1 hour and 10 minutes, and there is both an ascent and a descent totalling 214 metres. The Haltsuon circular hike is a journey through unspoilt nature and the idyllic Swiss countryside, offering the opportunity to experience the region in all its splendour.

title: Karwendel Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The legendary Karwendel mountain run celebrates its tenth anniversary in 2010. In addition to the 10.6 km, the runners also have to cover a proud 1381 metres in altitude.

title: Oberelbe Marathon - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The RENTA Oberelbe Marathon takes place between Königstein and Dresden - as the name suggests over a distance of 42.195 km. The programme also includes a half marathon, a 10 km run, a 10 km walking course and a 3.7 km mini marathon/company run.
long_description: Every year, the Salomon company combines several traditional trail running events in a cup ranking. The running events take place in Germany's most beautiful landscapes and lead over renowned routes such as the already legendary Karwendel route. Once again, running and mental limits are tested as professional runners or ambitious hobby joggers take on one or the other trail under their soles.

title: On the Wine Tauber Hiking Trail near Wertheim
short_description: This beautiful hike through the vineyard landscape in the Tauber valley takes us past a former Cistercian monastery and a legendary collection of stone crosses.
long_description:
The Wine Tauber Hiking Trail connects the former Cistercian monastery of Bronnbach, the wine village of Reicholzheim, the village of Waldenhausen and the town of Wertheim on a 20-kilometre loop. It is divided into two circular tours that can be hiked individually or as a large loop.
We hike one of the two loops from Bronnbach to Reicholzheim and back via the Schafhof. This section of the trail is marked with a "white bunch of grapes over a white river on a red background". The starting point is the former Cistercian monastery in Bronnbach (Tauber). On an information board we can learn interesting details about the monastery founded in 1151. We walk a short distance along the country road towards Reicholzheim before turning right on a path into a small wood. At the other end of the small wood, we turn left, walk straight along the edge of the wood and then left until we reach a vineyard. We almost go around it, walk straight ahead for a while between meadows and fields and then turn left towards Reicholzheim. Here, on the old high trail between Reicholzheim and Bronnbach, shortly before entering the village, we pass the stone cross nest. It is the largest known collection of stone crosses in Germany - 14 stone crosses made of sandstone, set in a red sandstone retaining wall. An information board provides more detailed information on the history of the crosses and the bloody legend surrounding them. In Reicholzheim, we first walk along the street "Am Felder", then turn right across the "Steiggärten", later turn left and walk out of the village above the cemetery. Our path through a meadow and forest landscape describes a right turn and soon meets an asphalt road. Follow it to the right and take the left path at the next fork. This leads us parallel to the Geißbergstraße around the village of Reicholzheim until we come close to the stone cross nest again. As our path ends there in a dead end, we change shortly before to the parallel path that runs to the left of ours. At the next junction we turn sharp left and walk straight on through fields and vineyards into a wooded area and turn right there until we reach the Schafhof farm. Here we turn left, then keep to the right and after a while we meet the country road again east of Bronnbach. This leads us back to the right to our starting point at the monastery, where we can stop at the Klosterhof inn to finish.

images.caption: In the Tauber valley near Bronnbach.

title: Tegelberglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The run up the Tegelberg is regularly organised by TSV Schwangau and SC Füssen.
long_description: Every year, the Salomon company combines several traditional trail running events in a cup ranking. The running events take place in Germany's most beautiful landscapes and lead along renowned routes such as the legendary Karwendel course. Once again, the participants will be able to test their running and mental limits, whether they are professional runners or ambitious hobby joggers, on one or other of the trails.

title: Around the Panzerwiese in Munich
short_description: "Um die Panzerwiese" is a beautiful running circuit through a nature reserve that is not - like other parks in Munich - overrun by people. Here you can enjoy the peace and quiet and nature - right on the outskirts of Munich. Football fans will be thrilled by the great view of the Allianz Arena.
long_description:
The Panzerwiese is a heath area in the north of Munich. The name comes from its former military use. It was only in 1994 that it was by the city, although 20 years earlier people had already enjoyed walking there. people had already enjoyed walking there. No trees or shrubs grow on the meadow. A total of about 180 plant species have been found there, 23 of which are, however, threatened with are threatened with extinction. In addition to the flora, the Hartelholz and the Panzerwiese also offer flora, but also provide a habitat for various animal species, such as the partridge, habitat. Here, too, 35 species are already on the Red List. Since 2002, this area has been a nature reserve and has been designated by the EU as a Flora-Fauna-Habitat area. The Panzerwiese is bordered in the north by the Hartelholz, which reaches as far as the A99 motorway, to the east by the Ingolstädter Straße (B13), to the south by a residential area along Neuherbergstraße and to the west by Schleißheimerstraße.
From the Panzerwiese, you have a great view of the Allianz Arena. of the Allianz Arena. Especially in the evening hours of a match day, the red or blue illuminated blue illuminated football arena is a great sight.

title: Cycling from Cernavodă to Eforie Sud/Vama Veche
short_description: A 3-day bike tour to the seaside resorts, with cobos and overnight in a tent. The route goes mostly on secondary roads, a little off-road, and the scenery crosses fields of poppies, rapeseed, sunflowers and small villages.
long_description:
Coming from Cernavodă station with the bike ready, after crossing the Danube, a first steep climb awaits us on the way out of the city. It is a sign that the route will not be smooth at all, despite the fact that we are on our way to the sea, so to zero altitude. Besides, the whole route is up and down, and only the view relieves from the physical effort. Often, even the wind blowing from the front poses problems.
The road, which is quite good, winds over small hills, through almost deserted villages, through woodland streams, and there is relatively little traffic. The communes along the route are an opportunity to stop often and refresh yourself whenever you feel the need.
If you go in early summer, as we did, the fields of poppies, rapeseed and sunflowers will keep you company for a long time. At some point the windmills come along.
On the first day, you arrive in the Dobrogea Gorge, which you might want to take an hour to explore. And if you arrive at sunset, it's all the more beautiful.
On the second day you already get very close to the seashore and start to feel the salt air.
The road gets a little better, this being a sought-after road for tourists to Corbu or Vadu. You can stop in Corbu at a cherhana. By evening you should already be in Năvodari/Tuzla, and even have a swim, if the water temperature allows it.
From here on, the way to other resorts is up to you. Just crossing Constança can be a bit tricky, but you can rely on the map. If you don't stop in Eforie, the road to 23 August is the main road, so it's also very busy. In the following resorts you can get off and pedal along the cliffs.Especially between 23 August, Olympus, Neptune, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn it's a pleasure to cycle close to the sea. Of course, if the resorts are not very crowded; which is possible in the off-season.

title: Walking around Ruhstorf
short_description: This easy Nordic walking tour takes us to the picturesque Ruhstorfer See lake - with many wonderful landscape impressions.
long_description: We start our tour at the Ruhstorf town hall. From here we follow the yellow markings (orange route). Passing the Marienkirche (1), we reach the Kleeberger Bach, the Passauer and finally the Bergstraße. We turn left into this and after a few metres turn right again onto a meadow path. Follow the orange markings to Rottersham, pass below the Nikolauskirche (2) and turn right into the first field path after leaving the village. We cross the Rott (3) and finally reach the Ruhstorfer See (4). Walk along the lake to the left and take a short detour to the "Gasthof zum Moarbauer" (5). Otherwise, turn right and walk past the Frimhöring timber mill (6) back to Ruhstorf.

images.caption: The Church of Our Lady in Ruhstorf.

title: Small, leisurely hike with a stop for refreshments at the Alpe Rothenfels
short_description: The small, leisurely loop starts in Immenstadt at the AWO retirement home and leads along forest and meadow paths past the Alpe Rothenfels and a great view over the Allgäu Alps;
long_description:
Nice circular hike that does not require any physical exertion - also very suitable for families.
Small, pleasant tour with a great place to stop for refreshments. The trail leads through woods and across meadows and offers a great vantage point with a view of the Allgäu Alps. The trail is generally accessible all year round - however, it is recommended mainly in the summer months. As the circular hike does not require any physical effort, it is also ideally suited for families.

title: Short walk Schiermonnikoog
short_description: You will walk through the town and nature of Schiermonnikoog.
long_description: Schiermonnikoog is the last Wadden Island in the Netherlands. This Wadden Island consists for the most part of a national park.

title: Goldsteig
short_description:
The longest and most diverse long-distance hiking trail in Germany!
The Goldsteig is the longest quality trail in Germany. Many and grandiose views, fascinating forest and river landscapes and varied scenery characterise the trail
.

title: From the Nature Park Centre to the Gschwend Waterfall
short_description: Short and leisurely stroll from the shores of the picturesque Alpsee Lake to the village of Gschwend with its cascading waterfalls.
long_description:
This scenic short hike takes you from the shores of Lake Alpsee into the Nagelfuh Nature Park. Alternating between side roads, narrow paths and forest tracks, this route offers magnificent views of the lake, impressions of traditional agricultural architecture and finally a dreamy waterfall that cascades down a small rock face made of the very Nagelfluh conglomerate that gives the nature park its name.
An easy walk that might be a little slippery when wet. In the nature park and especially within the biotopes around the waterfall, please behave respectfully towards nature and local residents. Accessible all year round, except in snowy conditions.

Access to the path is via the lake by boat (tickets should be booked in advance), kayak or canoe, which can be hired on-site.

title: Rusca Trail
short_description: The Sentiero Rusca (Rusca Path) is a path of historical-religious importance that connects Sondrio to the Passo del Muretto (2,562 m), which connects the Valtellina to the Engadine in Switzerland.
long_description:
The trail owes its name to Nicolò Rusca, archpriest of Sondrio, who was forcibly taken to Switzerland by the Grisons in 1618 and tortured to death.
The route is suitable for bicycles and mountain bikes up to Chiesa in Valmalenco, after which it is only possible to proceed on foot. The positive altitude difference exceeds 2,000 metres, so it is a demanding route. It is also recommended to cover it in 2 (or 3, if necessary) days.

title: Hiking: Roche Brune

At the start of the Gorges du Bret, you take the laces of a paved path lined with retaining walls that date from the exploitation of quarries. Then the path alternates between wooded and grassland sections to the top of Roche Brune.
The path is a very pleasant one.

title: Coastal path - the coves of Porteils from Collioure
short_description: A must-see path when staying near Collioure, along the rocky coast with small coves and beaches.
long_description:
The path starts from the centre of Collioure and climbs first along the road to Fort Miradoux (military area). Unfortunately it is no longer possible to take the coastal path at the very start of Collioure following a tragic accident in the past.
Then you walk along the coast via the Fort Carré, the superb Ouille beach and then the preserved area of Racou. The views are magnificent. Be careful, the various passages with stairs and ascents/descents can be trying for those with physical problems.
The return journey between Racou and the beach is a real challenge.
The return between Le Racou and the Ouille beach is done quietly along the small stream of Ravaner, then on your steps of the outward journey to finish.

title: Alternative route to Poiana Brașov via Stejerișul Mare Peak
short_description: There are many paths that take you from Brașov to Poiana Brașov, and this is one of them. A less crowded path, preferred only by the locals, and only up to a point; it reaches the Stejerișul Mare Peak, in the homonymous botanical reservation.
long_description:
The trekking path starts quite close to Brașov downtown, at one end of Warthe Hill, and goes parallel with the national road that heads to Poiana Brașov, but above it. The wide path is preferred by cyclists in summer, but in winter it is a perfect opportunity for solitary walks, in the company of your partner or your dog, in almost complete silence.
The landscape is predominantly forested, with small clearings, such as the one where the Troița Junilor Roșiori stands, offering views over Brașov and Mount Tâmpa.
Approximately halfway through the track to Poiana Brașov, you come across a sign. From here, you follow a path (rather intuitively) to the top of Stejerișul Mare Peak (960m). Standing on the rock there, you can clearly see the town of Ghimbav and a small part of Cristian.
In the last stage of this route, we didn't continue to Poiana Brasov, but crossed the national road and followed the red triangle sign that leads at the end of the Schei neighborhood, through Vâlcelul Dracului. The path might not be that popular in winter, and it gets steeper and rockier towards the end, where caution is required.

title: FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path (Tour 4)
short_description: A tour in Brandenburg specially adapted to the needs of cyclists and inline skaters. Good asphalt conditions, no cars and flexible division of the stages of varying degrees of difficulty make this tour suitable for families as well as for endurance athletes.
long_description: The FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path (Tour 4) is one of the sporting attractions in the region. You can join the route at various places, the circular route is well signposted throughout. There are many places of interest along the way, such as castles, monuments and, of course, the idyllic forests of the region. At just under 42 km, this stage is a large section of the entire network of the FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path, which at just under 100 km is the longest continuous route of its kind in Europe.

title: Trekking - Donbai - Hotel Plate or UFO - Mussa Achitara Mountain
short_description: Dombai is a popular alpine resort village in the Karachay-Cherkessia Republic. And the Tarelka Hotel or UFO at Mussa-Achitar Mountain has been attracting tourists for 40 years.
long_description: Dombai — a small village in Karachay-Cherkessia, but its scope for active enjoyment and sport is grand. There is hiking over short distances and trekking with backpacks and tents over long distances. All the different options for skiing and other gear are here too. Fans of wild speed mountain biking or real mountain biking will find their happiness in the mountains of Dombaj. And for everyone else, and for most lovers of the great outdoors, there is a genuine natural surprise: the terrain is rich with wild places, lakes, mountain rivers, singing waterfalls, photographically stunning white mountain peaks, and onions covered in green carpets. All this was explored by many mountaineers in the middle of the last century to open a spa place here for a good reason, – to give this heavenly spot to us who wish to see what they were discovering for us.

title: Altmühltal Panorama Trail
short_description:
The most beautiful trail through the Altmühltahl Nature Park.
Stop and find peace, feel your own rhythm and sense the vastness of the Altmühltal Nature Park. Mighty rugged dolomite fields, unique and sun-drenched juniper heaths, gentle river valleys and extensive forests - the land is richly blessed with magnificent natural spectacles and an eventful cultural history that is reflected in the many pretty towns.

title: One-day hike from Brașov (Noua) to Crucuru Mic peak
short_description: Crucuru Hill draws a fairly long passage between the Noua neighborhood in Brașov and Poiana Brașov or the Postavaru peak. Crucuru Mic is the closest peak to the city.
long_description:
This hike partially covers the route leading from the Noua neighborhood to Postavaru. It takes about 5-6 hours to complete and reaches Crucuru Mic and Crucuru Mare peaks.
Being a winter day, so less light, this hike reached only the first peak. Tough, it can hardly be called a peak. It is not marked in any way - not even by signposts. That might indicate that it has nothing special, and is only indicative.
The route has about two steeper climbs, through rich vegetation (regardless of the season) - about 15 minutes from the starting point and about halfway through the ascend. In addition, the climb is continuous, without flat parts, so the effort must be dosed. Although the reached altitude is not high, the abundant vegetation and the steep path will take their toll.
Apart from the panorama that opens at the beginning, above the Noua district, before entering the forest, the rest of the hike goes deeper into a sea of trunks with deep roots and rich crowns. In some places, the route may seem monotonous, but it makes for a very quiet, invigorating hike, just the perfect Sunday outing.
The descent to the Răcădău neighborhood is quite steep for about half the distance.

title: Maintalhöhenringweg
short_description: The Maintalhöhenringweg follows the course of the Main around the Spessart - from Aschaffenbürg via Wertheim to Gemünden. It repeatedly climbs up the mountains of the Spessart and then descends again into the Main valley. This hilly route is quite demanding in parts and requires good planning despite the numerous overnight accommodation options.
long_description:
Stage 1: Aschaffenburg - Hofstetten (21 km)
We take a day to visit Johannisburg Castle, the Basilica of St. Peter and Alexander and the Pompejanum in Aschaffenburg and then begin our hike on the Maintalhöhenringweg. Heading south, we cross the Obernau forest on steep paths, go to Sulzbach am Main and then hike through the Hutmannswald forest. Finally, we climb the Plattenberg and reach the destination of today's stage behind the Kirchhöhe.

2nd stage: Hofstetten - Großheubach (26 km)
From Hofstetten we hike up to the Heinchsthöhe and then down again into the valley of the Elsave, which flows through the village of Rück. We go up again and along the edge of the forest to the Klingenburg ruins near the town of the same name. The view into the Main valley generously compensates us for the previous exertions and we soon follow the course of the Main to Großheubach in a relaxed manner.
3rd stage: Großheubach - Dorfprozelten (23 km)
Today we turn east and hike high above the Main valley through the seemingly endless woodlands of the Spessart. Past the Engelberg monastery, we follow winding paths to the village of Collenberg. Behind the Collenberg ruins, the trail climbs steeply once more and then leads down to Dorfprozelten.
4th stage: Dorfprozelten - Wertheim (22 km)
Through Stadtprozelten, Faulbach and Hasloch, we hike along two large Main loops to Wertheim. The steep slopes offer fantastic views over the Main and its side valleys.
The fifth stage is in Wertheim.
5th stage: Wertheim - Martkheidenfeld (16 km)
Today we first cross the Eichwald forest in a north-easterly direction, cutting short a long loop of the Main. Behind the municipality of Triefenstein, we visit the Triefenstein monastery and then cross the Main, paying attention to the traffic on the state road. The last section of the trail is also on an asphalt road.
6th stage: Martkheidenfeld - Lohr a. Main (21 km)
On this stage we can look forward to a relaxed pleasure hike, as we walk directly along the Main to the Snow White town of Lohr am Main. Only the asphalt surface that accompanies us over long stretches detracts a little from the pleasure.
7th stage: Lohr a. Main - Gemünden (22 km)
After we were able to rest a little yesterday - as far as the altitude metres are concerned - today we are faced with two challenging climbs. From the Sohlhöhe, however, we experience a magnificent view of the northern Spessart. Apart from the mills on the Sindersbach, we will hardly see any traces of human settlement during the rest of the hike and should therefore provide for water and provisions. The Maintalhöhenringweg ends in Gemünden, the gateway to the Spessart and Rhön.

title: हदसर किला ट्रैक
short_description: हदसर किला ट्रैक पुणे के जुन्नार शहर में स्थित एक खूबसूरत मार्ग है जो अनुभवी और नौसिखिये दोनों ही किस्म के हाइकर्स के लिये अ च्छा है।।
long_description:
हदसर किला जिसे पर्वतगढ़ किला भी कहा जाता है, लगभग 2000 साल पहले जुन्नार के सातवाहन राजवंश द्वारा बनवाया गया एक प्राचीन किला है। वर्तमान समय में पुणे जिले के जुन्नार शहर के हदसर गांव में स्थित इस राजसी किले को बनाने के पीछे का मुख्य कारण एक लाभदायक व्यापार मार्ग की रक्षा करना था जो नानेघाट-सोपारा-कल्याण के माध्यम से मावल इलाके तक जाता था।
हदसर किला कई मायनों में महाराष्ट्र के दुसरे के किले से अलग है, उदाहरण के लिए - प्रवेश द्वार का आकार, संतरी के लिए कमरे , वर्षा जल जलाशय, किले को जाने वाली रॉक-कट सीढ़ियाँ और सातवाहन शैली की वास्तुकला। इस विशाल किले को एक ही चट्टान से तराश कर बनाया गया है।
किले के शीर्ष से इलाके का विहंगम दृश्य दिखाई देता है। किले के पास एक विशाल झील मौजूद है। झील के बगल में विशाल वर्गाकार टैंक खुदे हुए हैं हो वर्षा का पानी जमा करते थे। हदसर किले के दक्षिण में एक शिव मंदिर है जबकि किले के उत्तर में भवानी मंदिर और हनुमान मंदिर है।
हदसर किले की यात्रा मध्यम कठिनाई की है। यह अनुभवी और नौसिखिये हाइकरों के लिए समान रूप से उपयुक्त है। जहाँ अनुभवी हैकर्स नानेघाट-जीवनधन-शिवनेरी-लेन्याद्री से हदसर तक की चार दिवसीय लंबी पैदल यात्रा कर सकते हैं वहीँ शुरुआती हाइकर्स शांत हदसर गांव से किले तक एक दिवसीय हाइक कर सकते हैं।
यह ट्रैक मार्ग अपेक्षाकृत सुनसान है क्योंकि आसपास के हदसर गांव में केवल 2000 से कम निवासियों की आबादी है। इसी कारण से यह मार्ग भारत के कुछ उन चुनिंदा ट्रैक में से एक हैं जिसमे आप साथ के लिए अपने पालतू कुत्ते को भी ले जा सकते हैं।

title: Short run around the Kaufering reservoir
short_description: Running from the sports center in Kaufering along the Lech via barrage 18
long_description:
This short run starts at the sports center in Kaufering and runs along the Kauferinger Lechstausee. It is a good idea to park there either by bike or car to start the run.
The route starts over the Lech and then briefly through Kaufering village until you finally reach the Jedermann Weg along paddocks. The route has a total of three climbs along meadows and woods. The first is the longest ascent, which you pass on the way to the barrage. There are two more short but steep ramps on the way back.
The path surface is mainly tar and some gravel.
There are refreshment stops directly at the sports center as well as at the Lech bridge. If you wish, you can combine the run with a few lengths in the nearby swimming pool.

title: From Willofs to Schlitz
short_description:
On this tour we can either walk directly from Willofs to Schlitz, or make a detour to the mysterious Sattelstein.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
Our hiking trail begins in the centre of Willofs. We walk out of the village on the street called "Alte Schule". From the junction with the mountain road, the trail is marked with 2 blue crossbars and leads to Niederstoll. After walking through the Willofser Feld and the forest, we reach a crossroads with six paths in the forest. Here we have to decide whether to hike to the Sattelstein, which is about 3 km more there and back. If we hike to the Sattelstein, we turn right and follow the sign „blauer Ring“ and further the sign Sattelstein.
The Sattelstein is a rock shrouded in legend. Here, the devil is said to have tempted a pious human soul with a knife. But because the devil lost, he rode his
three-legged mule with a mighty leap into the air, leaving his mule's tracks in the stone.
Or we turn left in the direction of Schlitz. Follow the blue ring road through the forest to Karlshof, which used to belong to the Counts of Schlitz. At the traffic sign „End of the 30 zone“ we turn right from the signposted path in the direction of „Hochseilgarten“. Passing the high ropes course, we stay on the tarred field path and walk in the direction of Schlitz, which we will see after the high ropes course, until we reach the first houses. On this path we can already see our destination, the Ferienhof Trier.

title: Heiligenwald Tour - Lautertal
short_description:
This short tour with only a slight incline is also suitable for beginners.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description: We start at the holiday farm in a northerly direction. Cross the Schotten-Lauterbach main road and follow the path in the direction of the wind turbines. After crossing the Brenderwasserbrücke, we turn right into the Heiligenwald forest. Gradually ascending, we cross the Heiligenwald and leave it on a hill. Following the path, we pass various wind turbines (approx. 70 m high) and enjoy the good distant view in the direction of Rhön and the Felda valley. When we arrive at the district road towards Helpershain, we walk again on sloping paths towards Engelrod. On the way to the holiday home, we pass the Engelrod church.

images.caption: Magnificent views await us on our tour.

title: Panorama round hike Jungholz -Kappeler Alpe - Pfronten Kappel- and back
short_description: Panoramic circular hike in the foothills of the Alps on interesting, easy paths with several places to stop for refreshments.
long_description: From Jungholz in the direction of Pfronten, we enjoy great landscapes, mountains and vantage points. Everyone becomes aware of the nature, water, stone and meadows in the Tyrol and Allgäu that these surroundings hold. Along the well signposted and developed paths we progress to the first partial destination, the Kappeler Alpe. After a short stop, we pass through villages like Kappel and Pfroten, which are characterised by their tradition. Later, along the river Vils, we walk again towards Jungholz. Arriving at the final destination, we reflect on our unique impressions and enjoy this great experience.

title: Exploring the bays and beaches of Bandar Khayran on foot, Muscat
short_description: Take a wander, grab a beach, have a swim, top up your tan, and be back home in time for lunch.
long_description:
While it's always been a popular place to visit for folks with boats (my dad taught me how to water ski here as a kid), the bays and beaches of Bandar Khayran (spelling varies) are nowadays just as accessible to anyone with a car, a pair of legs, and the willingness to take a walk. 
The waters are calm and clear and apart from the occasional speedboat, it's a fantastically chill area to spend a few hours- or even a day- with lots of snorkeling and fishing potential and a whole lot of UV. 
The route I have plotted is kind of a freestyle effort, but it's still a pretty true reflection of what you see in the photos and the location of the beach I would often hang out on- there just isn't a discernable path to follow. The truth is, you can go anywhere you fancy, including swimming across to the island, which has a great bay for snorkeling at its ocean-facing end. 
So grab a towel, pack some cold beverages and check out this especially azure little corner of Muscat's coastline.

title: Arboretum trail - Cardeilhac forest
short_description:
The 13-hectare Cardeilhac forest includes an arboretum created in 1913.
Designed to test new forest species, it now boasts over 100 species from 4 continents.
long_description:
The Arboretum de Cardeilhac is a haven of peace for hikers in search of nature and serenity.
Its shady paths wind through a rich collection of trees, combining local species, rare species and exotic varieties. Every step is a discovery, where the diversity of plants invites you to marvel at the beauty and richness of the forests.
Whether you're a botany enthusiast, an amateur photographer or simply a lover of the great outdoors, this place is an ode to nature in all its forms.
To enhance the experience, educational panels line the paths, revealing the secrets of trees and their essential role in ecosystems.
A stop at the Maison de l'Arboretum is a must: it offers captivating exhibitions, themed conferences and courses to deepen your knowledge of the forest and its current issues. After a stroll, the picnic areas offer the ideal setting for a gourmet break in the open air.
Accessible and welcoming, the Arboretum de Cardeilhac is a place where young and old alike can explore at their own pace. Dogs are welcome, on a leash, to share these moments of complicity in the great outdoors. Open from May to October, this corner of unspoilt nature is an invitation to slow down, breathe and reconnect with an environment of striking beauty. Pack your walking shoes and set off to discover a unique and inspiring place!

title: Rundweg mit oder ohne Hund über den Kalvarienberg in Sonthofen
short_description: Kurze Runde mit oder ohne Hund auf den Kalvarienberg in Sonthofen mit Bergblick Richtung Grünten, Oberjoch, Sonnenköpfe und Hörnergruppe.
long_description:
Der Kalvarienberg mit ökologischem Kurpark in Sonthofen befindet sich auf historischem Grund. Hier wird eine alemannische Ursiedlung und Gerichtsstätte vermutet. Auf dem Treppenweg (auch Kreuzweg) steht am Ende eine Kapelle, welche 1650 von Bürgern erichtet wurde. 1924 wurde sie als Gedächtniskapelle für die Gefallenen des 1. Weltkrieges neu erbaut. Hier befindet sich auch ein Kreuzweg mit mehreren Stationen. Unser Blick hier ist in Richtung Grünten, Oberjoch Sonnenköpfe.
Auf dem Kalvarienberg befinden sich auch einige Infotafeln (Flachsanbau im Allgäu, Welche Bäume und Tiere gibt es im Allgaeu...) besonders für Kinder geeignet und eine grosse Spielwiese. Im Winter lässt es sich hier auch gut Rodeln.
Später auf der Runde kommen wir an der Generaloberst Beck Kaserne der Bundeswehr vorbei, leider befindet sich hier ein Betonneubau, der weniger einladend wirkt, aber von hier aus haben wir einen Blick auf das Rubihorn.
Einige Gehminuten weiter haben wir dann, bei tollem Wetter, Blick auf die Hörnergruppe und gehen über eine schöne Wiese wieder runter, vorbei an der Kulturwerkstatt, in die Stadt.

title: खीरगंगा ट्रैक, हिमाचल प्रदेश, भारत
short_description: हिमाचल प्रदेश की पार्वती घाटी में बसा खीरगंगा बहुत मनमोहक स्थान है। यह बर्फ से ढके हिमालय और पार्वती नदी की सुंदरता से घिरा हुआ एक लोकप्रिय हाई किंग स्थल है।
long_description:
खीरगंगा (जिसका अर्थ है खीर की नदी) भगवान शिव के निवास स्थान के रूप में जाना जाता है। यह एक आम धारणा है कि भगवन शिव जो हिंदू पौराणिक कथाओं में सबसे शक्तिशाली देवताओं में से एक है, ने इस स्थान पर ध्यान लगाया था।
खीरगंगा हिमाचल प्रदेश के कुल्लू जिले में स्थित है और हिमाचल में सबसे लोकप्रिय पर्यटन स्थलों में से एक है। मणिकरण शहर से लगभग 22 किलोमीटर दूर स्थित यह स्थान अपने ठंडे झरने और साथ ही साथ गरम पानी की कुंड के लिए जाना जाता है।
यह ट्रैक मार्ग बहुत सारी भौगोलिक फीचर्स जैसे की घाटी, घास के मैदान, पहाड़ी पगडंडिया, खूबसूरत गांव और सेब के बागों का मिश्रण है। खीरगंगा ट्रेक मार्ग में कुछ एक भोजनालय हैं जो भारतीय और चीनी और कॉन्टिनेंटल भोजन परोसते हैं।
यह मार्ग हिप्पी किस्म के लोगो का बहुत पसंदीदा है और यहाँ बहुत सारे इस्राली पर्यटक भी आते हैं। आसपास का इलाका भी बहुत दर्शनीय है और कसोल, बुनबुनी दर्रा, मणिकरण, रुद्रनाग झरना जैसे कई अन्य दर्शनीय गंतव्य भी हैं।

title: Adventure hike for families to a playground in the forest
short_description: Interesting hike, especially for children, with playgrounds, wooden sculptures, biotopes along the way and easy rope-secured sections. Walking time indicated for families with children (plus breaks).
long_description: There is a lot to experience on this family-friendly hike at the foot of the Grünten near Burgberg: From the quarry it goes through the gloomy mixed forest up to the vineyard with an actual small summit cross at the lookout point. The exposed but not difficult Haldenweg leads with great panoramic views of the Hochalpen to the Holzer-Pfad, an adventure trail with a playground in the forest. Here you can romp, climb and learn a lot about the traditional wood craft. Via the pleasant panoramic path with charming wooden sculptures and several resting benches, we return to the quarry, where two more highlights await: the kids can cover the last meters over rope walks and balance bridges. Directly before the parking lot, we turn right to the quarry lake, a wild biotope where, depending on the season, frogs, newts, dragonflies and birds can be observed.

title: Manali Wildlife Sanctuary Circuit Trek
short_description: This circuit trek starts from the Manu-Mandir temple in Old Manali town and passes through the dense forests of oak, pine, chestnut, and walnuts inside the famous Manali Wildlife Sanctuary and finally returns back to Manu Mandir.
long_description:
Manali Wildlife Sanctuary is a small but important wildlife sanctuary in Himachal Pradesh, located in the catchment area of the Manalsu River. Trekking has been taking place in this sanctuary for many years and it is one of the favourite treks of all the nature lovers visiting Manali.
The trail starts from Manu Mandir in Old Manali, about 3 km from Manali and then passes through a classic semi-alpine forest consisting of various tree species such as birch, pine, oak, chestnut etc. There is a camping place right at the beginning of the trail. The trail also features waterfalls, viewpoints, and huts.
The difficulty level of the trail is easy which is suitable for beginners and experienced hikers. There are also a few other trails nearby that lead to other places within the sanctuary. This track route, which is about 11 kilometres long, can be completed in 5 to 6 hours.

title: From the Schafbachalm via the Oberwiesalm to the Faistenauer Schafberg
short_description: Varied hike in the Salzburg Osterhorn group from the Schafbachalm to the Faistenau Schafberg mountain
long_description: The Schafbachalm is picturesquely situated in the middle of the forest area of the Osterhorn group. It is quite easy to reach (toll road from Tiefbrunnau) and is the ideal starting point for our hike - in winter the access road is also used as a toboggan run. The area around Faistenau has always been a popular destination for excursions, with the Faistenauer Schafberg being a relatively easy, yet attractive and panoramic summit destination. The summit offers a magnificent panoramic view of the lakes of the Salzkammergut and as far as the Hochkönig and Dachstein. Schafbachalm and Oberwiesalmen are interesting places to stop along the way and also offer exciting play equipment for families or children.

title: Te Araroa
short_description: The long-distance path "Te Araroa" crosses both of the islands of New Zealand from north to south. On a length of 3500 km we enjoy the wild countryside between Cape Reinga and Bluff.
long_description:
If you want to take the whole tour, you have to budget 50 to 80 days on each island – depending on your personal fitness level and the weather conditions. If this is much too long for you, "Te Araroa" offers a lot of possibilities for one- or multiple day tours through the wonderful nature of New Zealand as well.
The way can be walked into both directions. Walking from North to South, it is best to start between end of September and December – then there is a fairly high change of having good weather conditions at critical points of the route. Especially the mountain area on the southen island is not easy to cross and therefore not recommended after april. 
Since the countryside through which the "Te Araroa" leads is often deserted and wild, it is very important to have knowledge of routing and navigation. You should also know how to cross rivers without tools, how to put up a tent, which first aid equipment you should always take along and how to prevent undercooling.

title: बिनसर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य ट्रैक (2)
short_description: यह एक अनछुई ट्रेल है जिसमे न तो कोई प्रवेश गेट है न ही प्रवेश शुल्क । यह राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 307A के बगल से सीधे बिनसर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य में जाती है।
long_description:
बिनसर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य उत्तराखंड राज्य के अल्मोड़ा शहर से लगभग तीस किलोमीटर उत्तर पूर्व में स्थित है। यह छोटी लेकिन बेहद सुन्दर सैंक्चुअरी 64 वर्ग किलोमीटर में फैली है और हिमालयी वनस्पतियों और जीवों का घर है।
बिनसर अभयारण्य के निचली भागों में देवदार और चीड़ के जंगल हैं जबकि ज्यादा ऊंचाई पर जाने पर हिमालयी ओक, बुराँश और शाहबलूत (चेस्टनट) के जंगल मौजूद हैं। कई स्थानिक और प्रवासी पक्षियों भी देखने को मिलते हैं।
बिनसर वन्यजीव अभयारण्य की खास बात है की यहाँ पर हाइकर्स के लिए सभी कठिनाई लेवल की बहुत सारी ट्रेल हैं। सबसे ज्यादा प्रसिद्ध जीरो पॉइंट और बिनेश्वर महादेव मंदिर की ट्रेल हैं।
इस पेज में दिखाई हुई ट्रेल एक अपेक्षाकृत अनजानी ट्रेल है क्योंकि इस के शुरुआती बिंदु पर पहुँचने और पार्क करने में कठिनाई होती है। इसलिए यह एक अनदेखा रास्ता है और अभयारण्य के अनदेखे दृश्य पेश करता है। इस ट्रेल की शुरुआत में हलकी चढ़ाई और अंत में तेज ढलान हैं। यह एक बंद गोलकार यानी की लूप ट्रेल हैं ,जो घने जंगल में दस किलोमीटर जाने के बाद अंत में शुरुआती बिंदु पर वापस आ जाती हैं।
पगडंडी की शुरुआत में एक रेस्तरां और होटल है जहाँ से प्रावधान (स्नैक्स, पानी, खाना) खरीदे जा सकते हैं। यह 4-5 कारों की छोटा पार्किंग स्थल भी देता है। बिनेश्वर महादेव मंदिर की लोकप्रिय ट्रेल के विपरीत इस ट्रेल पर कोई वन विभाग ऑफिस नहीं है। आप अपनी कार से बाहर निकल कर 2 मिनट में बिनसर सैंक्चुअरी के अंदर घुस सकते हैं और हाईकिंग शुरू कर सकता है।
यह सलाह दी जाती है कि अंधेरा होने से पहले अपने वाहन पर वापस लौट आएं ताकि जंगली जानवरों से आमना समाना न हो हालाँकि आज तक ऐसी कोई घटना रिपोर्ट नहीं की गयी है।
