title: Şile Saklıgöl
short_description: Doğaseverler için mükemmel bir nokta Saklıgöl. Haftasonu aktivitesi olarak yapılabilecek bu rotayla birlikte hem gölü keşfedebilir, hem de yorucu olmayan bir yürüyüş gerçekleştirebilirsiniz.
long_description:
İstanbul'dan fazla uzaklaşmadan biraz doğa havası almak ve şirin yerler keşfetmek mümkün. 
Şile'nin Karamandere Köyü sınırları içerisinde bulunan Saklıgöl, doğası ve göl çevresindeki tatlı işletmeleri ile sizi pişman etmeyen bir gezi rotası. İştah açan göl manzarası eşliğinde çayınızı yudumlayabilir, kahvaltı yapabilir ve bu kısa doğa rotası için yola koyulabilirsiniz. Saklıgöl yolu üstünde köylülerin kurmuş olduğu tezgahlardan alışveriş yapmak ve insanlarla iletişime geçmek de rotayı daha çekici hale getiriyor.
Zamanlamanızı doğru yaptığınız takdirde harika doğa manzaraları sunan bu rota mutlaka denemeye değer. Yeşilliğe doyacağınız ve şirin göl manzarasına kendinizi bırakacağınız bu rota hafta sonu şehirden kaçış ve huzur bulma anlamında tatmin ediyor. 
Rotayı hafta sonu yapıyor, rota öncesi veya sonrası tesislerde biraz vakit geçirmek ve göle karşı çayınızı yudumlamak istiyorsanız erken gitmeniz önerilir. Aksi takdirde yer bulmak zor hale geliyor.

title: Hopp Schwyz - on the Great Myths
short_description: It goes up Schwyz's local mountain. A beautiful circular hike that becomes a mountain tour with the part of the ascent. In good conditions you have a panoramic view of Lake Lucerne and far into the Swiss Alps with many three-thousand-metre peaks.
long_description:
A beautiful day hike up Schwyz's local mountain awaits us. The tour is actually not particularly demanding, but beautiful to walk. Only the actual ascent to the Grosser Mythen, which begins at the level of the mountain station of the cable car from Brunni, requires surefootedness and stamina. It is steeply uphill. But the effort is worth it. The summit is served by a small hut - be sure to try the Nussgipfli!
If you look closely, you will even discover the small meadow on the shore of Lake Lucerne where, according to legend, the Rütli oath was sealed.

title: Von Günzach nach Durach
short_description:
Abwechslungsreiche Wanderung durch die Allgäuer Landschaft mit vielen Blicken in die Ferne.

Vom Bahnhof in Günzach Wandern wir durch den Wald Richtung Wilpoldsried. Östlich des Ortes laufen wir über Frohnschwenden, Meggenried und Leiterberg nach Betzigau. title: Exploring the old village of Wadi Bani Habib, Jebel Akhdar
short_description: Explore the timeless setting of this abandoned Omani village by Jebel Akhdar, in the heart of the Al Hajar Mountains.
long_description:
Anyone visiting the Saiq Plateau and Jebel Akhdar should consider adding a short trip to the old settlement of Wadi Bani Habib to their agenda. 
This easy-to-visit, tourist-friendly spot provides a snapshot of what village life was like for the people of the Al Hajar mountains before the arrival of oil wealth and the subsequent modernisation of Oman in the 1970s. 
I wouldn't consider this a route per se. You're really just wandering around and exploring on your own, but please keep in mind that while the buildings may appear completely abandoned, some of them still function as mosques or are used for storage purposes by farmers, so please be respectful of this.

title: Moreno Hill Trail
short_description: Incredible trail with lots of green Atlantic Forest in the centre of Vila Velha, where adventurers can enjoy incredible moments and a beautiful view of the whole region.
long_description:
The Morro do Moreno is 184 meters high and is located at the end of Praia da Costa, next to the hill where the Convent of Penha is. For those coming from Vitória to Vila Velha by the Third Bridge, it is on the left side, while the Convent is on the right side. From May 2021, a bill was approved making the region an environmental conservation unit of the municipality.
In total, round trip, the Morro do Moreno has 1.3 km. The initial part é paved, then becomes a dirt track, with small stones. Some stretches are flat and others are more steep but without much difficulty. The tip é go by the side of the coaminho, to enjoy the stretches with shade.The whole path  é filled  by the exuberance of the Atlantic Forest  where we find beautiful  stretches, with fauna and flora of típicas, and other points  where  one has an incredible view of the whole region.

Morro do Moreno, Vila Velha, Espírito Santo

title: Wachau World Heritage Trail: From Aggsbach Markt to Emmersdorf
short_description: Picturesque bell towers, wonderful panoramic views and a picturesque castle ruin await us on this entertaining hike on the Wachau World Heritage Trail from Aggsbach Markt to Emmersdorf.

title: Bog walk: Viru raba vaatetorn
short_description: Varied hike in the Laheema National Park, which leads through forest and moor landscapes typical of the region.
long_description:
The first half of this short hike leads through a sparse pine forest, which gives little hint of the moor landscape in the second part. The path through the moor is made of wooden planks throughout and, in addition to the beautiful view, there are also some information boards about the formation and the flora and fauna along the way.
At about two-thirds of the way along, there is an observation tower that gives a rewarding overview of the area. From here on, the last part of the path through the moor is much wider and also suitable for prams and the like.

title: The Quintessential Cambridge Circular
short_description: This circular walking route through Cambridge takes you from the riverside paths of Jesus Green, through the vibrant open space of Parker's Piece, and along The Backs, offering scenic views of historic college architecture and the River Cam.
long_description: A delightful walking route through Cambridge starts at Jesus Green, a spacious park known for its tree-lined avenues, picturesque pathways, and the River Cam running alongside. Begin your stroll by following the path along the river, passing the historic Jesus Lock, and enjoying views of punters gliding by. Continue south towards Parker's Piece, a vast open green that serves as the heart of the city, famous for being the birthplace of modern football rules. Here, you can take in the lively atmosphere, often filled with students, families, and locals enjoying picnics or playing sports. From Parker's Piece, head west toward The Backs, a series of lush, manicured lawns that back onto some of Cambridge's most iconic colleges, including King's, Trinity, and St John's. Walking along The Backs offers stunning views of grand architecture, ancient bridges, and serene riverside scenes, providing a perfect blend of natural beauty and historic charm. The route ends with an idyllic stroll along the Cam, where you can pause to admire the famous King’s College Chapel and the graceful Mathematical Bridge, capturing the essence of Cambridge’s enchanting landscape.

images.caption: Avenue of London Plane trees on Jesus Green, Cambridge, England

title: Stinky Mountain Nature Trail
short_description: The Stinky Mountain (a loose translation for the local name Puturosu Mountain) nature trail aims to illustrate the natural wonders of the Ciomatu-Balvanyos nature reserve, respectively around Puturosu Mountain (1143m).
long_description:
The trail has two parts, differing in distance and difficulty level, so hikers are advised to be aware of the details of the trails to know which one suits them.
The first part takes about 1.5 hours and displays panels with useful details about the deciduous forests in the area, the bats nesting in the caves here, and the volcanic relief of the Harghita Mountains.
On this trail, you reach the Sulphurous Cave, which you can enter for only about 2 meters - beyond that, the gas smell is very strong.
Slightly higher up, there is also the Alum Grotto. The Alaun stone or block contains potassium and aluminum sulfate. Due to its multiple properties, the Alaun stone has many uses, both in the household and in the cosmetics or ceramics industries.
The first part of the nature trail then descends to the Balvanyos complex.
Those who are willing and able can continue with the second part of the route. It is longer and a little more difficult and leads to the Bird Cemetery and the Buffogo Mash. This part is only recommended for those in good physical shape.

title: EuroVelo 19 - The Meuse cycle route
short_description: European cycle route, La Meuse à Vélo (Meuse by bike) crosses the French county (or département) of Ardennes using the greenway called the Trans-Ardennes.
long_description:
Running along the towpath beside the Meuse River from Remilly-Aillicourt to Givet, this cycle route was voted Véloroute de l'année (Cycle Route of the Year) in 2011.
The rugged landscapes here have inspired countless legends. Remarkable architecture also marks the way, such as the vast Château-Fort of Sedan and the grand facades of Place Ducale square in the town of Charleville-Mézières.
The route is mostly developped on designated lanes for cyclists.

title: Itinerary in the wild animal park of Landsberg
short_description: A hiking route that passes through a lovely forest where you can observe animals up close!
long_description:
A relatively easy trip that offers a fun time in nature for all family members! During the trip you will be able to observe wild boars in a natural habitat as well as enter a special area where reindeer roam freely. The moose must not be fed, but you can certainly pet them if they come towards you. The park also has lovely lakes as well as a playground with water games.
The walk on the route is accessible to strollers , it is mostly flat but there are occasional short and reasonable climbs. Large parts of the route are shaded, so it is comfortable to walk on it even on warmer days and on slightly rainy days.

title: Exploring historic Garni by foot, Armenia
short_description: An easy day trip from Yerevan, this compact hiking route around the Garni Gorge has plenty to offer lovers of history and nature.
long_description:
A stone's throw away from Yerevan lies the small town of Garni, which is perhaps best known for its 'Pagan' temple - the only classical structure that remains in Armenia and one that stands in stark contrast to the Orthodox Christian architecture that is so synonymous with the rest of the country's heritage landscape. However, For those wanting to get properly into the outdoors, there is more to Garni, including its gorge and the beautiful hills of the Khosrov Forest State Reserve. The hike up to the ruins of the Havuts Tur Monastery is also worth doing for the views, tranquility, and historical interest alone.
So, if you fancy escaping the bustle of Yerevan, lace up your boots and see what Garni has to offer.

title: The wine road through Muntenia and Oltenia
short_description: The wine trail through Muntenia and Oltenia is an excellent opportunity to spend a weekend in a different way if you come from Bucharest, Sibiu, Pitești or Craiova and don't know what to do somewhere relatively close to your city.
long_description:
The route goes from the plains to the high subcarpathian hills to reach a less explored tourist area in Romania, but particularly beautiful - the Oltenia Subcarpathians, at the foot of the Căpățânii Mountains.
The range of activities is centred around wine tastings from the Sâmburești or Drăgășani vineyards. The additional activities that can be included in such a route are suitable for both adults and children, and include an amusement park, visits to an ethnographic museum with a specific viticultural theme or the admiration of the Oltenești cule near Horezu.
To add to the atmosphere, we also have a recommendation for accommodation in an olteneasca cottage.

title: Hike to the Cascades du Hérisson in the Jura
short_description: An essential hiking trail in the region to discover the Hérisson waterfalls which follow one another along the path. A "hiking" favourite in the Jura massif!
long_description:
From the Maison des Cascades, this round trip hike invites you to discover the different waterfalls, one after the other, along the Hérisson river.
All different, the most impressive waterfalls by their height and flow remain the Eventail (65m), the Grand Saut (60m) and the Saut Girard (35m).

title: Winter Hiking to Käse Hütte
short_description: Hike to the Käser Hutte in Balderschwang from late winter. With the snow alreadyá melting and like fluffy snow, a hike like incredible winter shoes.
long_description: Ascent started in Bodensee Hütte where we left the car. The beginning is quiet, but after a few meters we start to climb steeper climbs. As we were wearing snowshoes, this made the climb easier. The view is breathtaking. We made a bigger contour before reaching the Hütte for a small path less steep. Then we returned by the shorter path and the tip é let the snowshoes slip and control the balance. This way we descend even faster. Fantastic day at the farewell of the snow.

title: From Lake Louise to Lake Mirror and Lake Agnes
short_description: A medium-length one-way hiking trail that starts at the famous Lake Louise passes along Mirror Lake and continues up to Lake Agnes and the adjacent Teahouse.
long_description:
The trail is considered one of the most popular hiking trails on Lake Louise. It is suitable for those who are looking for a more accessible alternative to the "Plain of Six Glaciers Trail." The route is ideal for anyone who enjoys long walks with some moderate ascents.
The road mostly runs through a shady forest. It is, therefore, suitable for hiking on hot days as well as on days with light rain or snowfall. On this route, two breathtaking lakes, waterfalls, wild nature and animals await travelers. The ascent of the route is moderate and includes a series of wooden steps. A great trail full of character and natural scenery awaits you.
The way back is the same route back to the starting point, so you can end your tour whenever you want. On the other hand, if this route was not challenging enough, you can take a turnoff to the Plain of Six Glaciers Trail.

title: Sauerland-Höhenflug (alternative entry: Meinerzhagen - Röhrenspring)
short_description: It is not without reason that the Sauerland-Höhenflug is considered one of the most beautiful hiking trails in Germany, because it leads along mountain ridges with a view all the way across the Sauerland to the Hessian town of Korbach. Altena and Meinerzhagen are two attractive starting points.
long_description:
Here we describe the alternative entry of the Sauerland-Höhenflug from Meinerzhagen to Röhrenspring. The rest of the route to Korbach can also be found on this portal.
We start our hike in Meinerzhagen in the valley of the Volme and can already see the first highlight of the tour after just a few metres: The Badinghagen moated castle emerges between the Bäumen. The spring valley behind Hösinghausen marks the entrance to the Ebbe Mountains and we hike along the ridge of the same name über the Nordhelle, the highest peak of the Ebbe. We continue from mountain to mountain to Windhausen and then again on the ridge through the seemingly endless forest, which offers fantastic views every now and then. At Lenhausen we cross the deeply cut Lenne valley and then, thanks to the wonderful landscape, we are perfectly motivated to tackle the challenge of the Hohe Hardt. Now the trail winds gently uphill via Faulebutter and the Tröttberg to the Röhrenspring hiking triangle. Here, in the Homert nature park, we meet up with the Sauerland-Höhenflüg variant starting in Altena and can either continue hiking there or west to Korbach in Hesse.

title: Plain of Six Glaciers Trail
short_description: A medium-long hiking trail that starts at the famous Lake Louise and continues to an incredible glacier panorama
long_description:
Known as the "Plain of Six Glacier Trail," it is one of the most touristy and popular hiking trails on Lake Louise. The length of the path is approximately 7 kilometers and includes a gradual ascent of about 500 meters, making it suitable for experienced hikers only.
Along the way, you can expect breathtaking views of the surrounding mountains and, of course, the glaciers as well as plenty of running water, waterfalls and wildlife. The ascent on the trail is mostly moderate, but some single climbs are a little steeper but not very long. The path is a great hiking tour rich in nature and landscape.
If you still haven't had enough after the tour, you can make a side trip to Mirror Lake and Lake Agnes on the way back.

title: Small hike from Vorderhindelang through the Hirschbachtobel via the Kellerwand back to Vorderhindelang
short_description: Beautiful, varied tour along the Ostrach, then change the valley side further through the Hirschbachtobel and over the Kellerwand back to Vorderhindelang.
long_description: We follow a lightly gravelled path along the Ostrach river to the valley station of the Hornbahn cable car. Here we change the side of the valley, mostly over beautiful gravelled meadow paths, until we reach the main road 308. We cross this road and now walk gently at first, later steeper and more steeply through the Hirschbachtobel. Here there are always wonderful views of waterfalls and rock formations. After leaving the Hirschbach, we come to a crossroads at the foot of the Hirschberg wall. To the right we could go into the short gorge part of the Hirschbachtobel and then on to the Krähenwand. Today we want to turn left and continue to the Kellerwandweg, from where there are always wonderful views of the Ostrachtal. Finally, we cross the Zillenbach stream and approach Vorderhindelang and our starting point from the north.

title: Sentiero degli scoiattoli da Santa Cristina ai piedi del Seceda
short_description:
La classica strada di accesso dal fondovalle ai prati del Seceda, lungo il panoramico Sentiero degli Scoiattoli.
Translate to English
long_description:
Il percorso si snoda tra i boschi sopra l'abitato di Santa Cristina Valgardena. Il Sentiero degli Scoiattoli, in particolar modo, scorre in parte parallelo alla strada forestale che dal fondovalle accompagna al Rifugio Gamsblut.
La partenza dell'intero percorso è al parcheggio Pescosta, da qui si imbocca subito il Sentiero, che permette di vedere, tra la vegetazione, fantastici scorci del Sassolungo e del Sassopiatto, oltre che delle cime circostanti. La salita è costante e non impegnativa.
Dopo poco più di due chilometri, si raggiunge il Rifugio Gamsblut, punto perfetto per una pausa, con anche un piccolo parco giochi dedicato ai più piccoli. Potete qui decidere se tornare al punto di partenza seguendo nuovamente il Sentiero (oppure la forestale parallela) oppure se proseguire raggiungendo uno o più dei rifugi e delle baite che costellano i prati ai piedi delle Odle. Qui le alternative sono innumerevoli, certamente una delle più gettonate è la salita in direzione Seceda, per ammirare uno dei punti più panoramici e conosciuti delle Dolomiti.

title: The Cambridge University Botanic Garden
short_description: A walking route through the Cambridge University Botanic Garden offers a serene escape into a world of diverse plant life and tranquil landscapes.
long_description: Start at the Garden’s entrance, where pathways lead you through a variety of themed gardens, from the colorful Winter Garden to the lush Rock Garden filled with alpine plants. As you stroll, enjoy the peaceful Lily Pond, vibrant flowerbeds, and towering trees of the Beech Collection. The route winds through the elegant Systematic Beds, showcasing an array of plant species arranged by their evolutionary relationships, and concludes at the Glasshouses, which house exotic plants from around the world. This walk provides a perfect blend of nature, science, and tranquility in the heart of Cambridge.

title: Continental Divide Trail (CDT) - Triple Crown of Hiking
short_description: With over 5,000 kilometres along the continental divide of the USA, the Continental Divide Trail is one of the longest long-distance hiking trails in the world.
long_description:
From the Mexican border in the south to the Canadian border in the north, the CDT crosses a total of five states: New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Idaho and Montana. After the first section through the New Mexico desert, the trail becomes much more challenging in Colorado; the Rocky Mountains await us.
&Uml;ber the rugged high mountain landscape of the Rocky Mountain National Park, we reach the Wild West of the USA from Wyoming, where lonely wilderness awaits us until we enter the world-famous Yellowstone National Park. With a bit of luck, we may encounter bison along the way.
Finally, the CDT takes us through the northern states of Idaho and Montana as well as Glacier National Park on the border to Canada. And this one has it all again: Breathtaking mountain ranges and impressive mountain lakes form a perfect end to the trail.

images.caption: On the CDT we cross the Loveland Pass in Colorado

title: Sheep Mountain via the Gates of Heaven
short_description: Strenuous but very scenic hike over the Himmelspforte to the Schafberg with 360 degree views over the Salzkammergut and several lakes! Downhill with the steam locomotive!

title: Meuse-Rhine Route North Route
short_description: On the Maas-Rhine Trail, we walk past all the major maars of the Eifel in the Rhineland-Palatinate part of the route.
long_description:
We start our hike in Roder in Luxembourg. The path leads us to the border river Our between Germany and Luxembourg. Here our path branches into two variations.
On the northern Meuse-Rhine Trail, we hike along the Our to Ouren in Belgium and from there on to Bleialf and Prüm to Mürlenbach in the valley of the Kyll, where both trails join again.
From here, our route leads right across the varied, enchanting landscape of the Eifel. Via Gerolstein, Daun, Ulmen and Mayen, we reach the Weinfelder Maar near Daun, which invites us to take an extensive break. Passing the Meersfelder Maar near Manderscheid, we hike on to the Pulvermaar near Gillenfeld and the largest volcanic lake in the Eifel, the Laacher See.
At Andernach we finally meet the Rhine and have reached the destination of our hike.

images.caption: The Geysir Andernach (formerly Namedyer Sprudel) is the largest cold-water geyser in the world.

title: GR® 10 - Crossing the Pyrenees from Hendaye to Banyuls
short_description:
The GR®10 is a signposted long-distance footpath that crosses the Pyrenees from west to east, from the Atlantic to the Mediterranean.
About 900 km long in total, it represents a magnificent classic for walkers.
long_description:
The GR®10 starts in the beautiful greenery of the Basque Country to end in the Mediterranean scrublands of Banyuls.
<You will cross the most beautiful natural sites of Pyrenees, valleys, peaks, passes and lakes, among which :The Iraty forest, Pic du Midi d'Ossau, Cirque de Gavarnie, Gaube valley, Lac d'Oô reserve Néouvielle, Ars waterfall, Capcir plateau Bouillouses lake, Canigou massif...
A great classic, we tell you!

title: The Red Gully theme trail
short_description: An easy walk to the spectacular geological monument Râpa Roșie on the edge of Șebeș, with a possible return on Via Transilvanica. Anyone can walk this route, in any season.
long_description:
The route starts in the centre of Sebeș and follows a dirt road parallel to the national road, arriving relatively easily and quickly at the roadside. It is possible to climb to the viewpoints at the edge of the natural monument for beautiful panoramas.
The information panels that make up the themed trail provide valuable details about dinosaur fossils from the Cretaceous period (i.e. the period in which the site was formed), as well as the flora and fauna of the present day.
For variety, întour can be made on the route marked with the orange VT, part of the Via Transilvanica hiking trail. This section is not part of the theme trail itself.

title: Mariposa Grove
short_description: An extraordinary circular hiking trail that leads through a huge sequoia forest in the south of Yosemite National Park in California. The highlight of the route: "Grizzly Giant", one of the largest, most impressive and famous trees in Yosemite Park.
long_description: Right at the beginning of the route, we can admire huge sequoia trees standing at the roadside - the ideal spot for taking pictures! In the middle of the route is the main attraction of this Tour and Yosemite Park in general: The sequoia, known as the "Grizzly Giant", is one of the largest in the world at 64 meters! The route is mostly flat but includes some short climbs with easy to moderate gradients.

title: Dharamkot to Mcleodganj Trek Route
short_description: A short but very beautiful walking route that starts from the popular Morgan Place in Dharamkot and leads to the Tibetan Temple near McLeodganj.
long_description:
The starting point of this trek Dharamkot is a small hill town in the Kangra district in the Indian state of Himachal Pradesh. Dharamkot offers sweeping views of the Kangra Valley and the Dhauladhar ranges. It is also the base camp of Kareri Lake and Triund Trek. 
Unlike the nearby town of Dharamshala, which is now a fully commercialised tourist trap, Dharamkot is still untouched by urbanization hence a hidden secret among nature lovers and the hippie community. Here one can find discerning tourists who want to move away from the hustle-bustle of Dharamshala and just nest calmly in the lap of the truly silent Himalayan terrain.
The endpoint of this trek McLeodganj is also a suburb of Dharamsala. It is the refuge town given by India to many Tibetan citizens displaced after the occupation of Tibet by China. It is also the headquarters of the Tibetan government-in-exile and the residence of the Dalai Lama. It is a beautiful and peaceful city with an air of a tranquil Buddhist lifestyle.
One can travel on foot from Dharamkot to Mcleodganj which is about 3 km by a footpath. On this page, you will find the description of that short but beautiful walk that transport you back to a bygone time.

title: Hiking to Dombay-Ulgen - Chuchhur Waterfalls - Chuchhur Pass
short_description: Dombai is a popular mountain resort village in& the Karachay-Cherkess Republic. The Chucchen Pass, with its views of the mountain peaks of the Caucasus Mountains, is one of the easiest to access.
long_description: Dombai — a small village in Karachay-Cherkessia, but its scope for active enjoyment and sport is grand. There is hiking over short distances and trekking with backpacks and tents over long distances. All the different options for skiing and other gear are here too. Fans of wild speed mountain biking or real mountain biking will find their happiness in the mountains of Dombaj. And for everyone else, and for most lovers of the great outdoors, there is a genuine natural surprise: the area is rich with wild places, lakes, mountain rivers, singing waterfalls, photographically stunning white mountain peaks, and onions covered in green carpets. All this was explored by many mountaineers in the middle of the last century to open a spa place here for a good reason, – to give this heavenly spot to us who wish to see what they were discovering for us.

title: Schwarzwassertal, Melköde, Herzsee
short_description: Leisurely loop with wonderful views, moderate ascent, good refreshment stop at Alpe Melköde in summer, fantastic little lake on the route
long_description: The route starts at the large parking lot of the Ifen cable car, leads along alpine paths through the entrance to the Schwarzwassertal valley, past the Herzsee lake towards the Alpe Melköde, where you can fortify yourself for the return journey along the picturesque Schwarzwasserbach stream.

title: The theme trail Forest Stories - Jiu Valley
short_description: Under the guise of a walk through the forest guided by the Alunița squirrel, the route is similar to that of Buila-Vânturarița, the focus being, of course, on the natural specificities of the Jiu Valley.
long_description:
Walkers are invited through 11 information panels to learn stories about the deciduous forests of the Jiu Valley, elements of the households in the area, details about orchards and pollination of trees or elements that distinguish the gorges from a gorge, or trees from each other.
The trail has been specially designed for children in grades IV to VI. But any nature lover is welcome on the trail, which can be walked even in winter, especially as this national park remains a little explored and promoted area beyond the monasteries in the gorge.

title: The "12 Apostles" nature trail
short_description: The "12 Apostles" nature trail in the Călimani Mountains admirably adds to the local natural landscape and helps any hiker stopping by the information panels gain a deeper understanding of the places they see.
long_description:
Perhaps precisely because of this route (Gura Haitii - 12 Apostles rock group), which is one of the most popular and accessible routes in the Călimani Mountains, they chose to set up the nature trail here.
The panels along the route tell you about the volcanic origin of the Călimani Mountains, the formation of the group of rocks with mysterious human faces that are now called the 12 apostles, or the biodiversity of the place. One of the most interesting stories on the trail may be the "milk route": it follows the process of milk production starting from the source, i.e. from the sheepfolds located up in the mountains.
The trail is accessible and spectacular both in summer and winter.

title: The Tour of the Isle of Arz
short_description: In the heart of the small sea, translation of "Morbihan", the Island of Arz reserves to the hikers its wild paths along cut out points, its maritime panoramas with the multiple facets on the islands of the Gulf of Morbihan and its beautiful sandy beaches at the bottom of the creeks.
long_description:
Easily accessible by boat from Séné or Vannes with the company Bateaux Bus du Golfe, the island of Arz is also called the island of the Captains because of its many sailors and captains who sailed the oceans during the 19th and 20th centuries. 
The trail is not marked PR (short walk) but it is easy to find your way along the coast.  Winter tip: take the trail in the opposite direction and return by road, very wet sections have been signposted from the east side.

title: Hike to Parashar lake and Temple
short_description: This popular and scenic hiking route leads to the Parashar lake and the three-storied Parashar Temple, situated at an altitude of about 8700 m (29000 ft) near Mandi town of Himachal Pradesh in India.
long_description:
Parashar Lake is a relatively lesser-known secret in the Mandi district of Himachal Pradesh. This mysterious holy lake and a pagoda-style temple are located in the bowl-shaped Parashar Valley. A one-day hiking trip from Dewari village near Mandi town is the best way to reach this picturesque location. However, note that there are some other routes to reach Parashar Lake apart from the one shown here, and it is even possible to drive directly to Parashar in a small car.
The beautiful nature trail from Dewari village to Parashar lake passes through dense forests and offers clean air and pristine, untouched nature. It is a mildly upsloping point-to-point trail, and most hikers rate it as "easy to moderate" on a difficulty scale. 
Parashar Lake is associated with the sage Parashar, and it is believed that he did penance here in ancient times. According to some legends, Bhima, the mighty warrior of the great Hindu epic Mahabharata, built this lake after returning victorious from one of the bloodiest battles in human history- the Kurukshetra war.
There are two very mysterious facts associated with this lake. The first is a floating island on the lake that keeps changing its position. The second bizarre claim is that the depth of Parashar Lake has not been measured to date, despite several attempts by scientists and divers. 
On the banks of the lake is a grand, three-story temple built by Raja Banksen of Mandi in the 13th century in honour of Sage Parashar. It is a beautiful pagoda-shaped temple built in Pahari-Himalayan architecture.
Tents are allowed near Parashar Lake. There is also a forest guest house with comfortable rooms. They also provide tents if you want to stay in them. There is also a PWD rest house nearby. The temple's dharamshala (inn for pilgrims) also provides rooms and food to hikers. There is also a small shop and restaurant nearby that sells groceries and home-style food.
To sum up, this is an ideal location for a quiet, contemplative hike in mother nature's lap and must be done if one is visiting Mandi.

title: From Jungholz to the Sorgschrofen
short_description: Promising, difficult mountain tour with a view to the surrounding Alps.
long_description: Jungholz's local mountain is perfect for starting a worthwhile mountain tour. On the way up you can already enjoy the view of nature and the surrounding area. Once at the top, you will be rewarded with a fantastic view into the distance. Sometimes there are running boards and steep climbs to be mastered. The tour is only recommended for sure-footed and experienced hikers and mountaineers.

title: Around Lauterbach
short_description: The walk, which is technically demanding at times, takes you mainly through a closed canopy and is therefore highly recommended for the summer.
long_description: We walk from the car park on the road to the right in the direction of Hotel Tannenhof, cross the road after about 20 m, turn onto the path marked with a yellow rhombus and follow the Nordic Walking sign. On a somewhat demanding ascent of about 250m we have the opportunity to test our fitness. We continue on a relatively flat forest path that leads into the village and across a factory site. Passing the Maierhof inn, we enter the forest again. After about 2.5 km we come to a small viewpoint, the Elisabethfelsen. We continue uphill to the summit. We continue walking on a gravel road. Finally, the signposting with a small yellow rhombus leads us back up the slope to the right and we meet the signposted path „Route 2“. We stay on the easily accessible forest path for a good 2 km until we reach the village again. We keep going in the direction of Kammermartinsdobel (yellow rhombus). From the playground we walk along the road again and return to the starting point.

title: Panoramaweg am Oberstdorfer Ortsrand
short_description: Relaxed circular route with beautiful views over Oberstdorf
long_description: The route on the outskirts of Oberstdorf leads along the Stillach and Breitach rivers over extensive meadows and forest tracks to the village of Jauchen. Various vantage points over Fischen and Oberstdorf along the route, as well as the village chapel of Jauchen, are the highlights of this relatively relaxed loop, except for a short ascent.

images.caption: View through the forest to Jauchen

title: Autumn mountain hike in Ciucas - Zăganu & Gropșoarele peaks
short_description: Ciucas Mountain is accessible and beautiful in any season. We had perfect weather for this fall tour. This is a route that avoids crowded areas, offering some superb panoramic views.
long_description:
The path starts near Cheia, so parking your car is easier. However, you have to do a little research on the map to find exactly where you have to turn off from the main road towards the starting point. 
The first part of the hike is sustained, but quite relaxing climb, through coniferous forests. In the first clearing, you can see the traces of a sheepfold, which is probably inhabited a few months a year. There is also a picnic area here, and a pit stop for reenergizing is even recommended, before the real ascent.
The view opens towards the Grohotiș Mountains across the valley or to the Ciucaș peak.
The next stage is a long, almost continuous ascent to the ridge. You cross clusters of fir trees, groups of rocks shaped by winds, and the Zăganu peak where you'll see a signpost.
While advancing towards the Gropșoarele Peak (1883m) you have a single more exposed passage, secured with chains. 
Gropșoarele - the second highest peak in the Ciucaș Mountains - is almost as popular among hikers as the Ciucaș Peak, being easily accessible from Muntele Roșu (about 2.5-3 hours). The path is steep both uphill and downhill, but beautiful and welcoming for all hikers.
Once we reached the Muntele Rosu Cabin, we followed another poor trodden and quite wild path through the forest.

title: Cemetery Ridge trail
short_description: Clear Creek Metro Park, Rockbridge
long_description: Clear Creek is the farthest Metro Park from downtown Columbus (45 minutes) but worth the drive. Its location in the Appalachian foothills makes for steep but spectacular hiking. The Cemetery Ridge trail (2.5 miles) gets the hiker’s heart racing as it quickly ascends hundreds of feet. Wind through forest and prairie before connecting to the Hemlock Trail for a much-welcome 1.5 mile return descent through mature hemlocks and white pines.

images.caption: hiking trail in Ohio: Cemetery Ridge trail

title: ”The chamois of Retezat” nature trail
short_description: The Retezat Mountains have several trails suitable for families with kids like a crash course intro to what mountain routes mean. The ”Chamois and their neighbors” nature trail is one of them. One fun particularity of the route: each panel contains a riddle that challenges the hiker to keep climbing.
long_description:
The six information panels on the nature trail tell you about the flora and fauna of the Retezat National Park. Each panel also includes a riddle, and the answers can only be found by hiking the next stage of the trail.
The highest point of the trail is reached in the Ciurla saddle. Here, you get to admire a superb view of the Retezat ridge. Further on, you climb steadily, not steeply, but not necessarily easy peasy either, through coniferous forests, juniper bushes, and on rocky paths.

title: Todtnau waterfall from top to bottom
short_description: A short hiking route that starts at a point above the Todtnau Falls and descends through the forest towards the observation platform on the Todtnau Falls
long_description: A pleasant and relatively not difficult semi-circular hiking route that begins with a descent through a wooded area, next to flowing water towards the Todtnau Falls. On this route you can see the point where the falls begin to descend into the valley and enjoy the view of the falls from the observation deck as well as the special view from the reclining benches.

title: Trekking around Çamkoru Nature Park and Pond
short_description: Gölet, trails in the forest surrounded by greenery, silence and peace... The trails in the forest around the Çamkoru Göleti in Ankara should definitely be tried
long_description:
Çamkoru Nature Park and Nature Park sheds light on the nature and natural beauty that Ankara has to offer. Every nature enthusiast who does nature sports and who is looking for a nature trail in Ankara must have travelled here. There are different hiking trails in the forest in the Gölet çphase.
This route is just one of the routes you can try in the gölet phase. Our route starts right next to the göl and ends near the göl again after following the path through the forest. You can plan a joint trip to this route where you can enjoy the magnificent nature of Ankara and enjoy this route with your friends. The pleasure of the route is different when you go with a group of friends or family.
If you are interested in photography, you can also take good photographs thanks to the magnificent scenery and the presence of lush green trees. Of course, the colour of this natural beauty changes depending on the time interval you visit and the route changes to a completely different colour in winter.

title: The route of the tunnels in the Jiu Valley
short_description: The route follows the Baleia Valley, along which a hydrographic development was started during communism. The tunnels that can be seen along the route and the unfinished dam are part of this abandoned project.
long_description:
It is clear that the engineering project to supply water to the localities in the Jiu Valley has not been completed, even though work continued after 2000. Fortunately, the development of this unique route at least takes advantage of the landscape left after its abandonment. Thus, the route can be interesting for those who are passionate about industrial heritage, abandoned buildings or hidden places.
On the way, you pass through or along three tunnels, along the Cascade and the Dracului Cave, and towards the end you reach the sources of the Whale River. Close to the dam you can also see a rock formation with an anthropomorphic shape, similar to a sphinx.

title: The route of the ruins on the Ungur Valley, Vulcan
short_description: The trail that leads to the traces of stone settlements above the St. Nicholas Hermitage in the Ungur Valley is a gentle walk, mostly through the forest, and a welcome alternative for those who are unable to make more demanding hikes in the Vulcan or Retezat Mountains.
long_description:
The route starts on a forest road, up to the St. Nicholas Hermitage, and then continues on a paved road along the Ungur Valley.
The dominant landscape is a forest one, mainly walked by locals or hikers from the area.
The forest has been known for a long time and it is supposed that this was one of the roads where the herds used to go up to the mountain. 
The name of the route comes from the traces of settlements at the end of it. Their unknown history has led to various urban legends explaining their origin. And these speak of stone villages încropite by Italian immigrants who cut wood îin the area, a military camp of the First World War, or a simple shelter for animals.
The Ungur Valley waterfall though small, can be spectacular if it has flow.

images.caption: Entering the trail with the information board

title: The Path of the Sculptures (Hatzerim Forest)
short_description: A short semi-circular hiking route with cultural value that goes through the Hatzerim Forest, surrounding Kibbutz Hatzerim
long_description: The Path of Sculptures in Hatzerim Forest offers an easy trip of about 4.5 kilometers with desert views and nature. Scattered along the road are about 40 sculptures created by Israeli artists. The road was initiated by the artist and curator Marga Fistein and her husband Israel who invited the best Israeli artists to place on the sides of the road and in the surrounding hills, works that express an artistic statement relating to the environment and the space.

title: Grand Canyon Track
short_description: A beautiful short route not far from Blackheath. Ideal for experiencing the wonders of the Blue Mountains without straying too far from civilization.

title: The Waterford Greenway
short_description: The Waterford Greenway is a spectacular off-road trail that follows the route of an old railway line from Waterford City to Dungarvan.
long_description: This flat, well-paved trail is perfect for walking and cycling, offering breathtaking views of the Comeragh Mountains, coastal cliffs, and lush countryside. Highlights include the impressive Kilmacthomas Viaduct, the Ballyvoyle Tunnel, and the scenic Clonea Strand. The Greenway is accessible for all ages and fitness levels, with plenty of picnic spots and cafes along the way.

title: Camino del Norte: Galizano - Somo
short_description: The route describes a very small section of the Camino del Norte, between the towns of Galizano and Somo, and covers an extensive beach area and a coastal area, both ideal for a half-day walk.
long_description:
Once you reach the small town of Galizano, you drive through it in almost complete silence, with very few signs to indicate whether you are on the right road. Follow the arrows to Playa Galizano for safety. But you won't reach the local beach, and you'll come across other trails to guide you along the coastal path.
The trail traverses more than half of a huge expanse of land probably cultivated in the warm season. The path goes quite close to the edge of the stables and you have the sea constantly churning at your feet. The roar of the waves breaking against the hard rock is the only sound you hear for long.
You leave the Playa de Langre behind and head towards Loredo. You won't see the town, but you may pass through an exclusive neighbourhood of villas on the edge before descending through a grove of pine trees and past the Loredo campsite towards Playa Loredo.
The last stretch is all beach - fine sand, small waves, groups of surfers, locals walking their horses, the Bay of Santander in the distance and the Picos de Europa ridges.

Descent to the beach in Somo

title: Cachoeira que Engole trail in Trindade
short_description: Easy walk to get to one of the most famous attractions of the village of Trindade, in Paraty (RJ).
long_description:
The trail is well signposted and is located in the beautiful region of the lower part of the Serra da Bocaina National Park, surrounded by a rich vegetation of the Atlantic Forest, and with the mountains of the Serra do Mar in the background.
Leaving the village of Trindade, you will also pass the beautiful and famous Praia do Meio. The official name of the trail is "Cachoeira Pontal" and on the way you will have the opportunity to refresh yourself in several waterfalls such as Pedra que Engole, os Dois Irmãos, o Escorrega e o Poço Fundo.The Pedra que Engole é without doubt the most famous attraction of the trail and consists of a rocky formation where é possible to follow the waters of the river and pass under the stone. Certainly an impressive experience that is worth the trip! <The PARNA of Serra da Bocaina does not charge entry fees or require authorization to visit these attractions and there is no time control for exit visitors.

long_description: An experiential and water-rich hiking route that leaves from Kibbutz Ein Horesh, passes by Nahal Alexander and surrounds the magical Hefer Reservoir, surrounded by a network of water pools located in a 300 dunam park. There you will find rich vegetation, animals and birds, an observation point and a tiny island in the heart of the Great Reed. Those who want to extend the route can also combine walking along the path of Nahal Alexander. The trip is free.

title: Amazing Swiss alpine views from Saxerlücke
short_description: Experience the thrill of the Saxerlücke hike, where rugged peaks, stunning alpine meadows, and panoramic vistas come together for an unforgettable mountain adventure
long_description:
The hike from Staubernkanzel to Saxerlücke and then to Hundsteinhütte SAC offers a breathtaking alpine adventure through the heart of the Swiss Alps. Starting from the Staubern cable car station, hikers will journey across scenic meadows and steep rocky paths, climbing steadily toward the dramatic Saxerlücke pass. Along the way, stunning panoramic views of the Säntis massif, Pizol, and the Churfirsten mountains reward your efforts. The hike concludes at the cozy Hundsteinhütte SAC, a traditional Swiss mountain hut that provides a welcoming rest after a challenging but rewarding journey. 
This hike is a stunning exploration of the Alpstein region in Eastern Switzerland, known for its jagged peaks, lush valleys, and high-altitude meadows. Starting at Staubernkanzel, you'll ascend towards Schwende-Rüte, where the landscape begins to transform, giving way to alpine terrain and sweeping views of the Toggenburg valley below. The path becomes steeper as you approach Saxerlücke, a mountain pass that offers incredible vistas of the surrounding peaks and valleys. The final descent to Hundsteinhütte SAC provides a gentle end to the hike, with spectacular views of the Swiss mountains. The hut is an ideal spot to rest, enjoy traditional Swiss alpine food, and immerse yourself in the peace of the Swiss Alps.

title: Schneeschuhtour auf den Lusen
short_description: Winter circular hike in the Bavarian Forest National Park from Waldhäuser via Martinsklause, Teufelsloch and Sommerweg to the summit of the Lusen, return via Lusenschutzhaus and Winterweg
long_description:
Beautiful winter hike in the Bavarian Forest National Park with snowshoes or touring skis. The route is well signposted and leads past the Martinsklause, used for wood drifting, the Teufelsloch - a sea of boulders with an underground stream - and the Glasarche, a cross-border art object.
On the 1,373 m high Lusen you have a wonderful view of the winter landscape of the Bavarian Forest. The descent leads past the Lusen shelter, which invites you to take a break.

title: शिचिलिंग-सोपोना झील ट्रैक
short_description: सोपोना झील ट्रैक हिमाचल की स्पीति घाटी में माने गाँव से 5 किलोमीटर दूर स् थित एक मौसमी ग्लैसिअल झील का ट्रैक है जिसमे झील, गॉंव, घाटी, और स्थानीय लैंडस्केप का पूरा आनंद मिलत ा है।
long_description:
सोपोना झील का ट्रैक हाइकर्स के बीच में एक 'छुपा हुआ रत्न' है। यह झील काज़ा और ताबो गाँव के बीच में स्पीति घाटी में मौजूद है। स्पीति घाटी के अनेक दौरे कर चुके हुए कई अनुभवी हाइकर्स को भी इस ट्रैक के बारे में नहीं पता है। कुछ हाइकर्स जिनको थोड़ा बहुत जानकारी है वो यहाँ पहुँचने में होने वाली यातायात समस्याओं की वजह से यह दौरा नहीं करते हैं।
हाल के सालों में मानगोंगमा और मानेयोंगमा गाँवो में होमस्टे की सुविधाओं और क्वालिटी में बढ़ोतरी होने से इस ट्रैक की जागरूकता बढ़ी है। माने गाँव तक पक्की मोटोरेबल सड़क मौजूद है और यह राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 505 के बिल्कुल करीब है। क़रीब पांच किलोमीटर लम्बा यह ट्रैक माने गाँव से शुरू होता है और सोपोना झील तक जाता है। ट्रेल अधिकांश जगहों पर कठिन और हलकी चढ़ाई वाली है। यह एक रखरखाव वाली ट्रेल नहीं है। झील ग्लेशियर के पानी से बनी है। मार्च से जून महीनों में पिघलती बर्फ के पानी से झील भरना शुरु होती है। जुलाई से अक्टूबर तक पिघलता ग्लेशियर और मानसून इसे पूरा भर देते हैं। नवंबर से फरवरी तक झील का पानी गायब हो जाता है। मौसम जो भी हो इससे इलाके की प्राकृतिक सुंदरता कमी नहीं आती है क्योंकि स्पीति घाटी का लैंडस्केप हर बदलते मौसम में एक नयी सुंदरता दिखता है।

title: Hike to Comarnic Cave via Carasova
short_description: A moderately difficult hike through a beautiful landscape of caves to Prolaz and on through fairytale forests to the Comarnic cave.
long_description:
The tour leads from the village of Carasova through a hilly and wooded landscape to the Comarnic Cave, which is the longest (4040m) and one of the most beautiful caves in the Banat Mountains and is a protected nature reserve. The opening hours of the cave are Saturday and Sunday between 10 am and 6 pm. From Monday to Friday, a guide is available for groups of five or more.
For up-to-date information, visit the website of the Semenic-Caras Gorge National Park. The entrance fee is 10RON.

title: Canyon des Gueulards et Gorges d'Omblèze
short_description:
Découvrez les Gorges d'Omblèze et le Canyon des Gueulards au travers cette randonnée pittoresque.
Translate to English
long_description:
Cette magnifique randonnée vous fait découvrir le milieu des gorges et leurs étroites falaises. Le pittoresque Canyon des Gueulards avec ses passages étroits et ses cairns ne vous laissera pas indifférent, l'eau y est rare, contrairement aux Gorges d'Omblèze.

title: England Coast Path - South Bents to Amble
short_description: This route is part of the England Coast Path National Trail.
long_description:
The 71 km (44 miles) stretch of the England Coast Path ( ECP ) from South Bents to Amble is now open to the public. 
  The England Coast Path is happening because of a completely new right of access that gives everyone the legal right to explore our coast for the very first time. It is much more than just a path, it gives access to beaches, cliff-tops, and most of the wonderful habitats around our coast. You can see the open sections and how they relate to the other National Trails here.
  Coastal sections of existing National Trails will become part of the England Coast Path in time. This will give the Trails better protection when the coast erodes. The Trails won't lose their own identities though, they will still be National Trails in their own right and the signage will be the same, but you may see new signs saying 'part of the England Coast Path'.
  You can find out about the other National trails on the official National Trail website.

title: From Kleinmachnow along the Teltow Canal into No Man's Land
short_description: On this tour, we are reminded of German-German history.
long_description:
Kleinmachnow, formerly a rural estate village southwest of Berlin, has developed into a popular place to live just outside the capital after reunification. In addition to various architectural masterpieces, this former German-German border town has above all contemporary history to offer.
Our hike begins at the Kleinmachnower lock, a listed building, on the lower level. We now head west under old oak trees along the Teltow Canal into the Dreilinden district. To do so, we cross under the new motorway bridge. Via the Bäkehang road we reach Stolper Weg and turn left. After a section of forest, we reach the old border strip - today a wide meadow landscape. We now enter the former no-man's land and cross the old motorway on the former West Berlin side. At the next junction we turn right and start our way back.
Take Teerofendamm on the right and walk along Max-Planck-Allee to the area of "Checkpoint Bravo", the former border crossing point. We walk left along Albert-Einstein-Ring until we reach Stahnsdorfer Damm. Via this we finally return to the lock, our starting point.

title: Night hike back to Immenstadt
short_description: Approx. 10 km eventful hike with some highlights, such as the Haldertobel at night.

title: Mühlrüti - Schnebelhorn - Meiersalp - Libingen
short_description: Easy mountain hike to the highest mountain in the canton of Zurich, with several ascents and descents, which are nevertheless easy to manage.
long_description: We hike along the Toggenburger Höhenweg to Langenwis, then we branch off and climb üvia Berlig to the Älpli. Another ascent takes us through the Grosswald forest to the Roten. We already have a view of the Tösstal, the Tannzapfenland and the Hörnli. After the descent to Hirzegg, there is a longer ascent to the Schnebelhorn, where we enjoy the fantastic view. Our path is somewhat steep and leads to the Meiersalp mountain restaurant and on alpine paths via Steinweid to Libingen. Before we start our journey home by post bus, we take a look at the parish church of St. Gallus, which was built in 1769 by Ferdinand Beer from the famous Vorarlberg family of master builders. The attached rectory and today's St. Nicholas Chapel were part of the Benedictine nunnery founded in 1760 and moved to Glattburg in 1781.

title: Libingen - Chrüzegg - Libingen
short_description: One of the most frequented routes in the «Mosliger Birg», the hiking area around the Schnebelhorn. The ascent and descent are somewhat steep.
long_description:
Libingen lies in a basin below Chrüzegg and Schnebelhorn and belongs to the municipality of Mosnang. We descend into the Lohtobel to the Holzbrücke, which was built in 2001 by two apprentice carpenters as a test. Now the ascent to the Alpli begins. At the Hugenalp mountain restaurant we admire the unique view. We continue on the geological trail to Schwämmli. The peculiar soil structure is explained on information boards. Slightly uphill we reach the well-known hiking destination Chrüzegg. Twenty hiking routes lead from Goldingertal, Ricken, Toggenburg and Toggenburg to Chrüzegg. The view of Lake Zurich, Glarus and Lake Constance is surprising. The mountain guesthouse was rebuilt in 1998. The very steep descent leads via Untere Chrüzeggalp to Alp Ober Zrick, then we hike on a flat natural road in the forest along the Dietfurterbach stream. At Jonenholz the Dietfurterbach is crossed one last time and after a somewhat steep ascent we reach the village of Libingen

title: Kirchberg - Mosnang - Chromen - Lichtensteig
short_description: Easy hike through the Altoggenburg. The tour can easily be broken off en route.
long_description:
Documentary records über the municipality of Kirchberg exist since the 8th century. Before we begin the hike, we pay a visit to the Heiligkreuz Church, which was built in 1879-80 and is considered the most festive baroque church in Toggenburg.
We leave Kirchberg in a southerly direction and hike üover the Hüsligs to Müselbach, then we climb up through the Wartwald forest to Wart. The ascent is rewarded by a magnificent view of the Säntis and the Churfirsten. The descent via Chrimberg to the Gonzenbach, which rises below the Schnebelhorn, is not too difficult. The trail climbs again, and via Winklen we reach the stately village of Mosnang «in the arms of pre-Alpine hills that form the borders to the cantons of Thurgau and Zürich». The villages of Mosnang, Mühlrüti and Libingen belong to the municipality of Mosnang. Masinang was first mentioned in a document in 854. In the High Middle Ages, a Romanesque church was built, of which the tower has survived.
The hike continues along the slope under the ski lift to Dottingen. After a descent via Chromen - Heui, we reach the Dietfurterbach, which rises below the Chrüzegg and flows into the Thur at Dietfurt. Via Ritzentaa we go to Äuli and the Thur. On the way to the Gurtberg we come across a turnoff to the Thurschlucht gorge, which is recommended for a visit. Soon we reach the historic market town of Lichtensteig. A detailed visit is worthwhile.

title: Janelão Cave Trail in the Peruaçu Caves National Park
short_description: The spectacular Janel Cave is the most famous attraction of the Caves of Peruaçu National Park in the north of Minas Gerais.
long_description:
The Parque Nacional Cavernas do Peruaçu é an important Brazilian conservation unit, due to its inestimable geological and archaeological heritage. The Park has several archaeological sites with prehistoric cave paintings and more than 180 caves and grottos, the most famous of which is the Janel Cave, with 176 meters high.
<Right at the beginning of trail you will pass by Sítio Ateliê Janelão, a rocky wall covered with several thousand-year-old paintings that tell story human presence in Peruaçu Valley. Other highlights are Clarabrica Heart, vegetation and unique landscape inside cave second largest stalactite world, Ballerina's Leg, 28 meters high.
The Park has free entrance, but the tours must be previously booked and the hiring of a guide is mandatory.
