title: Bazenheid - Kirchberg - Iddaburg - Fischingen
short_description: After several small ascents, the Idda Castle is reached on this easy hike.
long_description:
Bazenheid, first mentioned in a document in 775, belongs to the municipality of Kirchberg. The neo-Gothic parish church was built in 1894. We walk in a southerly direction to the Eichbüel and climb up to the village of Kirchberg. The Heiligkreuz Church, built in 1879-80, and the stately parish hall are worth seeing. We continue via Bruggbach to Tüfrüti, then climb to Geisswald and after a descent reach the embroiderer's village of Gähwil, which also belongs to the municipality of Kirchberg. Üvia Neuhus - Chalchtaren we hike to the Lämmlisgarten and the Iddaburg pilgrimage church, which stands on the site of the medieval Toggenburg, the ancestral castle of the Counts of Toggenburg. Idda, the wife of Diethelm IV of Toggenburg, lived here around the middle of the 12th century. According to historical sources, she was later, as a widow, an inclusress in the Fischingen monastery. A brochure about the legend of St. Idda is available in the church.
We descend through the Burgwald forest to Hüttenstetten and reach the Murg on a steep road, which we follow to Fischingen - unfortunately on a tarred road. In Fischingen we visit the monastery church founded in 1138 by Bishop Ulrich II of Constance. In 1848 the monastery was abolished.

images.caption: Fischingen Monastery from the perspective of Iddaburg Castle

title: Mühlrüti - Hulftegg - Hörnli - Mühlrüti
short_description: The Hörnli is a very well-known hiking destination in the Zürcher Oberland and can only be reached on foot. Two steep ascents and descents have to be mastered.
long_description:
Passing the St. Joseph Church built in 1764, we hike in a östy direction along the back Erbach stream to Langenwis, followed by a somewhat rigorous ascent to the well-known Hulftegg. We leave the Toggenburger Höhenweg and walk on the Hörnliroute in a westerly direction to Schlattberg. The TV tower on the Hörnli is already visible from afar. Via Storchenegg we reach the Regelsberg nature reserve, which was handed over to the Nature Conservation Society by Maggi in 1985.
The second ascent begins at Silberbüel: there are still a few stairs to climb, then we stand on the Hörnli viewing mountain in Zurich and enjoy the magnificent panorama. The descent to Silberbüel follows the same path as the ascent, then we change to the canton of Thurgau. From Chaltebrune to Alewinde we use the road, then we branch off to Holestei and reach Tobel through the Tobel forest. We cross the Murg and climb a little to the Gwilerstrasse. Via a meadow path we reach Bechten and the starting point Mühlrüti.

title: Walking route Loevestein Castle
short_description: During this walking route, you will walk past three ancient fortified towns. You will also walk past Loevestein Castle. This walking route takes about 4 hours.
long_description:
This route runs through a beautiful river area. As a result, you will also have to travel part of the route by ferry. During the route you will walk past old ramparts and old city gates. 
Slot loevestein is a beautiful castle that was used as a state prison. One of the most famous people who served time there is Huge de Groot. Hugo de Groot managed to escape by means of a book chest. The castle was also part of the water line. 
.
Further, you will walk past many city gates and a beautiful windmill. You will also see ravelins. These are small islands in the moat. They used to be used as defences. Nowadays you will find allotments.

title: Wil - Littenheid - Fischingen
short_description: Easy hike through unspoilt countryside, mostly on natural paths. Short ascents and descents, suitable from spring to autumn.
long_description: We hike to Wilen and follow the slightly elevated edge of the forest to the hamlet of Ägelsee, then we follow the elongated Riet to the village of Littenheid, which largely consists of buildings of the psychiatric clinic. On the short hill path we change to the other side of the valley. After an easy ascent with a beautiful view of the idyllic Moosweier, we return to the plain. From the hamlet of Anwil we hike on the Schwabenweg to Bürgle, bypass the hill on a slightly ascending path and arrive near the St.Martinsberg chapel, whose history dates back to the 10th century. We cross the forest and reach the village of Fischingen. The monastery was founded in 1135 by Bishop Ulrich II of Constance. The first patrons were the Counts of Toggenburg. The present monastery church was built in 1684-1687. The Idda Chapel attached to the north side commemorates the legendary life story of the Count Idda of Toggenburg.

title: Wil - Nollen - Gampen - Wil
short_description: Easy day hike to surprising viewpoints. Suitable for all seasons. The hike is mostly on natural roads away from heavy traffic.
long_description: Before the ascent to the old town, we hike left to the idyllic town pond and take a look at the imposing front of the old town hall with the mighty courtyard at the end. Via the Unterer Hofberg - Städeli - Langegg we climb up to the Üerental, then we hike through a natural meadow landscape to the nearby forest and again up to the Heid. In good weather, the view of the mountains is overwhelming. A rather steep path leads us down to Wuppenau, which we only touch on the edge. Back up we go to the hamlet of Grueb and on a beautiful hilly path to the village of Hosenruck. Through a splendid chestnut avenue we reach the well-known panoramic mountain Nollen. The view goes from the Central Plateau over Lake Constance and the Alpstein to the Glarus and Bernese Alps. The Rückweg leads us past the Waldwis hut through the Hagebuechertobel to the Zuzwil village stream, which we follow upwards. Via Tüfenwis we go to Gampen, and through the well-kept Nieselberg forest we reach the first buildings of Wil. In the upper suburb we pass through the Schnetztor gate onto the courtyard square. The landmark of Wil is the mighty courtyard, which was founded in the 12th century by the lords of Toggenburg as a castle and later used as the residence of the princes of St. Gallen. The town church and the magnificent Baronenhaus (baron's house) dating from 1795 are also remarkable. The stately late Gothic courthouse is also worth seeing, as are the many well-preserved houses with full-length arcades.

title: Wil - Zuzwil - Bischofszell
short_description: Easy day hike through a well-kept landscape, with surprising views of the Mittelland and the mountains. The historic old towns of Wil and Bischofszell are interesting.
long_description:
In a northerly direction, we walk through the pedestrian zone up to the old town, which is well worth seeing and is characterised by closed rows of houses with leafy gardens and the mighty courtyard. Through a gate we descend into the upper suburb. In order to reach the Nieselberg, the turn-off «Spital» must not be missed. At the top, a magnificent view of the Fürstenland awaits us. Along the forest we reach the village of Zuzwil, first mentioned in 761. Past the «Roten Haus» or tithe house, we head towards the Thur to Städeli - Oberhueb and past the Geissberg vantage point to the Benedictine monastery of Glattburg, first mentioned in 1167. In the 17th century, it became the property of the Swiss Confederation, and in 1781 the Benedictine convent founded in Libingen moved to Glattburg.
After a short descent into the ravine, we climb to the hamlet of Ebersol and hike through the extensive Hohrain forest to Niederhelfenschwil. The parish church, first mentioned in 903 and rebuilt in 1786-87, is worth seeing. We descend to the Kobesenmühle and continue to the magnificent timber-framed building «Mühle». At the farm «Letten» we reach the Thur and the eight-bay crooked bridge, which was completed in 1487 and is one of the most important late medieval bridge buildings in Switzerland.
Bischofszell impresses with its structural layout and various splendid buildings, such as the town church of St. Pelagius, the ornamental building of the St. John the Baptist.Pelagius, the graceful town hall, the Grubenmannhäuser from 1743-1745 on Kirchgasse or the slab mosaic on the arched tower, which depicts the homecoming of brave Bischofszeller from the Battle of Gubel, 1531.

title: Schwarzenbach - Thurauen - Niederbüren
short_description: Beautiful hike along the Thur from Schwarzenbach to Niederbüren.
long_description: We hike to the Schwarzenbacherbrücke, but turn right before the bridge and cross the gravel pit area. A beautiful forest path leads us to the Thur meadows of Nieder-stetten. We continue along the Thur to the Gillhof and to Brübach. We cross the Thur and follow it on the left to the Thurhof. The former Schülerheim was built in 1778 by Johann Ferdinand Beer as an inn and customs house on the Brücke. From here we climb up to the hamlet of Ehrenzell and the Glattburg. The Benedictine monastery of St. Gallusberg was formerly the ancestral seat of the Schenken von Castell. In 1781 the convent, which had been dissolved in Libingen, moved to Glattburg. The hiking trail continues to the hamlet of Ebersol. We hike through the Hohrainwald forest, turn right and through the Chriesihalden to the Kobesenmüli, a former grain mill with an attached residential house from 1698. Since 1987, it has housed the Wilhelm Lehmann Foundation with wood sculpture works. We walk down to Goldplatz and via the Thur we reach Niederbüren.

title: Uzwil - Wildberg - Eppenberg - Flawil
short_description: Frequently visited hike over the most beautiful hills of the Fürstenland, suitable for all seasons.
long_description: We leave Uzwil in a westerly direction and climb up the steep forest path to Vogelsberg. After the forest, a wonderful view opens up to Toggenburg and the Wil region. Downhill to the idyllic Bettenauerweier. We hike to Jonschwil, birthplace of the St. Gallen poet Notker Balbulus, who is commemorated by a monument on the site of the former Jonschwil castle. We continue via Burg - Hori to the Wildberg vantage point, where a beautiful view of Toggenburg, the Churfirsten and Alpstein awaits us. The trail continues to the Bisacht retirement home in Oberuzwil and the hamlet of Eberwis. Here we branch off to the right and hike through the forest to Eppenberg. In fine weather, the view stretches far across Lake Constance. A short descent brings us to Riggenschwil. Before reaching the village, we turn right and hike via Engi - Rudlen - Botsberg to Flawil.

title: Wil - Kirchberg - Bazenheid
short_description: Easy hike, with lots of variety through areas close to nature, occasionally überraschend wide views.
long_description: We hike towards Wilen and follow the railway embankment to the edge of the forest in the Au. Past the hamlet of Engi, we reach the romantic Altbachtal valley. We walk past the powder huts until the markings point us into the ravine. At the footbridge, our path branches off to the right and leads along the natural stream through damp, loamy slopes to the Giessenfall. Mostly a harmless channel, the stream can flood after thunderstorms. We bypass the natural spectacle via steps and follow the beautifully laid out path to Dietschwil. On a meadow path we climb to the Schallenberg, where a beautiful panoramic view of the Alpine world awaits us. Through the hamlet of Schalkhusen we reach Kirchberg. In addition to Kirchberg, the villages of Bazenheid and Gauml;hwil also belong to the Alttoggenburg municipality. We take a look at the Catholic church Heiligkreuz, which was built in 1748-51. For the last section of our hike, we use the road that runs east-west along the church, but immediately turn right onto a side path and enjoy the beautiful view as far as Bazenheid.

title: Zuzwil - Zuckenriet - Oberbüren
short_description: An easy hike through lots of forest for the whole family.
long_description: From Zuzwil the trail leads up to the vine forest. Up and down we hike to the hamlet of Rörlibad. Through Haldenholz and Tobelholz, where we enjoy the magnificent view of the Alpstein, we reach Zuckenriet. The castle of the same name from the 12th century towers above us on the left. The trail continues through the Büelwald forest to Eggetsbüel and Niederhelfenschwil. We leave the village in a southerly direction and hike through the Hohrainwald forest to the hamlet of Ebersol. Downhill to the Billwilerbrücke from 1904, on which we cross the Thur. Via Sonnenburg we reach Oberbüren.

title: Schwägalp - Hinterfallenkopf - Ennetbühl
short_description: Mountain hike to the primeval landscape at the source of the Necker between the Luteren and Necker valleys.
long_description: On the Schwägalp pass we climb briefly and hike üover soft forest paths to the Chräzerenpass, the earlier Üübergang between Toggenburg and Appenzellerland. Perhaps we will discover the carnivorous sundew by the wayside in the moor or enjoy the bright colours of the boys' herbs. On the alpine road the path now climbs gently to Alp Horn, then it becomes narrower. Passing under rocky outcrops we reach the still young Necker. A short ascent brings us to Alp Neuwald, then we descend through pastures to Ofenloch. Enormous rock walls and deeply eroded rock pans form an urtic, wild landscape. We climb up to Alp Ellbogen and on to Hinterfallenkopf. A magnificent view rewards us for the effort. We hike on to the upper Schirlet, to Alp Ji and via Hübschholz to the rear and front Chlosteralp. These alps used to be owned by the monastery of St.Gallen. Note the mighty maple trees, which have reached a biblical age. Via Alp Gössigen we reach Feissenmoos, one of the highest farms in the Luterental. An old road leads down to Brüggli and further üvia Risi to the village of Ennetbühl.

title: A trip to the Externsteine nature reserve
short_description: A light circular walking route in the Externsteine nature reserve, in central-western Germany
long_description:
This hiking route passes by giant rocks with impressive shapes as well as around the lake located at their feet. Through stairs fixed in the rock you can climb the rocks and enjoy a view of the park from above as well as a bridge connecting two of the rocks.
Itinerary is recommended for those looking for a short and easy trip. The route is not paved but its conditions and width allow walking with strollers as well as with wheelchairs. At the beginning of the route there is a visitor center with an interactive exhibition, and a small kiosk can also be found there.

title: From Krummenau up to the Speer and back down to Nesslau
short_description: Challenging day hike from Toggenburg up to the Speer, the highest Nagelfluh mountain in Europe.
long_description:
We climb the first ascent comfortably on the Wolzenalp sports railway, the valley station is not far from the starting point of our tour at Krummenau railway station.
The hiking trail leads us along the high moor past the Wolzenalp mountain restaurant and over fens with springy peat soil and bright moor flowers up to Alp Bumoos. Hiking steadily higher, we reach the Bützalpsattel on a ridge path. The landscape now becomes rocky and mountainous, and we bypass the Schwarzi Chöpf rock band to the south. The summit of the Speer is now within our grasp. We still have half an hour to climb before we can immortalise ourselves in the summit book and enjoy a well-earned rest at lofty heights. The view is breathtaking in every direction.
On the way down to the valley, we first hike back the same way to the Bützalpsattel, then descend to the Alp Hengst mountain inn. The rest of the descent takes us down into the idyllic Ijental valley to a small reservoir. Shortly afterwards, we leave the alpine road in the direction of Laufenweid. Via Bürzlen we descend to Nesslau. The train takes us quickly back to Krummenau from Nesslau.

title: Panoramas over Targu Neamt: the citadel and the Heroes' Monument
short_description: A "Sunday walk" for locals turned into a relaxing route for tourists, and a pleasant way to add to your visit to Neamț Citadel a more demanding activity that children will enjoy to the fullest.
long_description:
The route marked with a red band starts from behind the Casa Arcașului motel, the benchmark starting place to climb to the citadel. This is actually the old road that those living in the citadel used to take.
However, few tourists continue beyond the citadel. So you and your group, if any, will be a step ahead by continuing along the crest of the hill where the citadel stands. After a smooth leg, there is an uphill part (the only more demanding one) that takes you to a clearing with a spring. On the edge of the clearing, you can find wild berries so look out for them if you happen to come here in the summer.
The trail turns right and begins to descend gently towards the Heroes' Monument/Mountain Hunters' Monument. On the way down, do not miss the viewpoint from where you can admire the entire city of Târgu Neamț and the nearby towns.

images.caption: Bridge to the main entrance into the Neamt Citadel
In the forest, close to the Heroes' Monument

title: Wattwil - Regelstein - Ebnat-Kappel
short_description: Pre-Alpine mountain hike to the well-known hiking destination Regelstein.
long_description:
We walk along the Thurweg in the direction of Ebnat-Kappel. After just under two kilometres we leave the Thur and go up to the right to Rickenhof and Schönenberg. From Vorder Schönenberg we walk on the meadow path along the ridge to the upper Büntberg. Here we enjoy the view over the valley, the towns of Wattwil and Lichtensteig as well as the Churfirsten, the Säntis and the Stockberg. At the lower hut we find a nice fireplace.
Now the hike takes us through a nature reserve of special beauty, with numerous small fens and meadows. We discover special flowers and grasses along the way that only thrive in moorland areas. After a longer forest section, we climb up to the Regelstein via the upper Hüttenbüel on pastures. Enjoy the view in all four directions!
The Rückweg leads downwards über moorland forest area to the Oberbächen alp with alpine farm, then we go alternately über pastures, through forest and flowery meadows down to Unterbächen. The hiking trail brings us to the Ebnat-Kappel railway station via Müslen and Relis.

images.caption: Regelstein: View of the Glarus region

title: Ebnat-Kappel - Dance floor - Ebnat-Kappel
short_description: Leisurely circular hike with great views of Lake Zürich.
long_description:
After the railway underpass überqueren we cross the Thur and climb on the hiking trail über Relis to Müslen. Depending on the time of year, the boggy meadows are home to knapweed, cotton grass, bulrushes and many other typical bog plants. After Müslen the path leads through the forest to Unterbächen and up to Oberbächen, then slightly downhill through the Bächen forest to Stotzweid. The last ascent takes us past the Gubelspitz up to Chüebodenegg. On the way along the panoramic path we enjoy the magnificent view down to the Zürichsee. With the Thurtal, the Churfirsten and the Alpstein in front of us, we hike on the nature trail down to Alp Buechschittli and on to Obere Abschlagen, then through the forest and over another beautiful meadow down to Nestel. We leave the road at Orlen and hike via Nestenberg - Büchel back down to the double village of Ebnat-Kappel. At the Thurau we cross the Thur and reach the railway station along its right bank.



.

title: Wattwil - St. Gallenkappel - Schmerikon
short_description: After the ascent, the scenic trail leads slightly downhill towards the Obere Zürichsee.
long_description:
Wattwil is the headquarters of the internationally renowned Heberlein Group, whose foundation stone was laid in 1835 by Georg Philipp Heberlein with a yarn mill. However, its most prominent citizen is the Toggenburg farmer and poet Ulrich Brägger (Näppis Ueli), who died in 1798.

We hike to Enetbrugg and über the Ratzenloch to the Iberg ruins. On the right is the Maria der Engel monastery from 1621, the best-preserved enclosure in the canton. Via Schlosswis - Schlossweid we reach Laad. The house with the two painted signs dates from 1641. Above Laad we leave the road and climb to Heid. From here the view sweeps from the Säntis über the Churfirsten to the Glärnisch. Slightly downhill via Hinterlaad to Bodenwis and along the road via Oberricken to the farming village of Walde with the sturdy St. Anthony's Church built in 1834. At the hamlet of Widen we turn off onto the road to Rüeterswil and cross the road at the St. Ursula Chapel built in 1810. Not far from the hamlet of Ruadheriswilare (Rüeterswil), the Sancti Galli capella, a chapel in honour of St. Gallus, which gave the village of St.Gallenkappel its name, was built in the Middle Ages. The Grubenmann Church, built in 1754, the cemetery chapel, consecrated in 1667, the rectory, a cubic baroque building, and the Wirtshaus zum Rössli, built in 1757, are worth seeing. Below the church, we take the meadow path to the hamlet of Geretingen and follow the path on the left side of the stream. Below us the deep ravine of the Goldinger Bach, on the left Mürtschenstock, Glarus Alps and Gross and Klein Aubrig. We hike to the wooden bridge built in 1830 ücke over the Goldinger Bach, down to the former mill and up to the renovated little church of Neuhaus. Then we branch off through the Risifeld to Bürstli to the Goldberg. On the Bürgitalstrasse we descend to the lakeside village of Schmerikon.

title: Brunnadern - Wilkethöchi - Bergli - Degersheim
short_description: Easy mountain hike to well-known excursion destinations such as Gerensattel, Wilkethöchi and Fuchsacker.
long_description: We hike to the covered wooden bridge ücke over the Necker and climb the steep slope to the Oberberg, cross the wooded slope and the adjoining pasture and go to the shed on the slope. The alpine path leads steeply uphill to the Gerensattel. We quickly gain altitude in the closed beech forest. On the Wilkethöchi, a clearing offers us a wonderful view of Hemberg and Schönengrund as well as the steep rocks of the Alpstein. We continue along the slope through the Kubel forest to Kubelboden, where we cross the Dicken - Degersheim road. In front of us rises a massive boulder, the «Züblisnase». To the right of it, our path leads to Hönenschwil and up to Bergli. After crossing the forest, it is worth making a detour to the nearby Brunnershöhe, where a magnificent panoramic view awaits us. We hike on to the Gampen farm and arrive at the well-known excursion point Fuchsacker. We reach the pretty village of Degersheim with its two churches from the beginning of the 20th century via meadows and through the mixed forest.

title: Wattwil - Köbelisberg - Scherrer - Wattwil
short_description: Easy mountain hike with a steady ascent to the Köbelisberg viewpoint.

title: St. Peterzell - Landscheidi - St. Peterzell
short_description: Easy hike to Dicken, Bergli, and via Landscheidi on the opposite hillside to Chäseren.
long_description: Culturally interested visitors first visit the baroque Catholic Church of St. Peter and the provost's building dating from 1722 and 1767. We leave the stately village past the schoolhouse über Ober Baumgarten and hike a short distance along the St. Peterzell - Dicken road, then climb up to Schafwis. Across lush meadows we reach Mietschwendi and via Waldegg the village of Dicken. We pass a beautiful log cabin and continue uphill via Hönenschwil to the Bergli mountain restaurant. After another short ascent, we hike to the right on the scenic mountain path via Gägelhof - Hochwacht to Landscheidi and reach the well-known Jakobsweg (Way of St. James). Slightly uphill we reach Arnig, where again a beautiful view of Speer, Glärnisch and the Alpstein mountains awaits us. We stay on the ridge path until we reach Berghaus Chäseren, then we use the road to Ämisegg and back to the spa town of St.Peterzell.

title: Hemberg - St. Peterzell - Wilkethöchi - Degersheim
short_description: Leisurely hike with architectural highlights and magnificent views of the Alpstein.
long_description: From the village of Hemberg, the hiking trail leads us to the hamlet of Hofstetten with its stately 17th century houses. We hike down to St.Peterzell, which welcomes us with the Red House from 1622 decorated with baroque paintings. After an interesting visit to the Catholic baroque church of St. Peter and the provost's building dating from 1722 and 1767, we hike on to the Mühle, up to the hamlet of Enzenberg and somewhat steeper to the Gerensattel. Through the forest we go up again to the Wilket, then we reach the Wilkethöchi on the ridge with a wonderful view of Hemberg and Schönengrund as well as the steep rocks of the Alpstein. We hike through the Kubelwald forest down to Kubelboden and the Bergli inn. After crossing a forest section, at the signpost location, it is worth making a detour to the nearby Brunnershöhe, where a magnificent panoramic view awaits us. We continue hiking to the Gampen farm, branch off to the right north of it and come to the well-known Fuchsacker excursion point along the forest path. We reach the pretty village of Degersheim via meadows and through the mixed forest.

title: Brunnadern - St. Peterzell - Brunnadern
short_description: Easy hike üvia the adventurous Neckiweg through the Choltobel. The second part is dedicated to culture.
long_description: We leave the village at the covered wooden bridge ücke over the Necker and hike past the Neckertal riding stable with its Icelandic horses to the covered hiking trail bridge to Spreitenbach. Along the Neckiweg we come to the Choltobel and Ober Reitenberg. This ravine can be bypassed via the signposted hiking trail via Gössel. From Ober Reitenberg we go down ürt via Niderwil to Rohrbachtobel, then we climb up to Hofstetten to the old, stately 17th century houses. We march past Bädli down to St.Peterzell, where the stately Red House from 1622 welcomes us with baroque paintings. A visit to the Catholic baroque church of St.Peter and the provost's building from 1722 and 1767 is worthwhile. After taking in the beauty of the village, we continue via Farnboden to Furth. On the opposite slope there are two 17th century tower houses. From Furth we walk along the Necker via Siggetschwil back to Brunnadern.

images.caption: One of the two Türmli houses

title: Around the Hallertau
short_description: The almost 215 km long circular route in the Ingolstadt area leads on flat paths along smaller and larger rivers.
long_description: There are few small climbs on the cycle route in the district of Pfaffenhofen. The route mostly leads along cycle paths or side roads with little traffic and is therefore well suited for families.

images.caption: The area is known for hop growing

title: Mill hiking trail
short_description: We can look forward to an eventful exploration tour through the Schlaube Valley Nature Park, past the numerous mills of the Schlaube. We hike to Neuzelle and on wooded paths back to Müllrose.
long_description:
Stage 1: Müllrose - Siehdichum (13.5 km)
The first stage leads from Müllroser See, with the lake of the same name, via Ragower Mühle to Siehdichum. Again and again we pass small lakes and enjoy the path through the forest.
Stage 2: Siehdichum - Wirchensee (15 km)
After leaving Siehdichum, we can explore the Schlaubequelle spring and a nature trail in Dammendorf. Then we pass the Brehmsdorfer Mühle (today an inn) and the Kieselwitzer Mühle (today a fish farm). The beautiful hiking trail is surrounded by bogs, meadows and small woods. The nature park exhibition at Wirchensee with the Schlaubemühle marks the end of today's stage.
Stage 3: Wirchensee - Neuzelle (16 km)
Past large and small boulders, we hike leisurely through the forest to Neuzelle and pass the Schwerzkoer Sägemühle. The famous Black Abbot is produced in the brewery of the baroque Neuzelle Monastery - the beer and spirits can be tasted during the guided tours!
Stage 4: Neuzelle - Kieselwitz (13 km)
Today we take the Rückweg and can visit the farmers' museum in Möbiskruge by appointment. From here to charming Kieselwitz, the route is leisurely through the forest and past meadows.
Stage 5: Kieselwitz - Müllrose (25 km)
The last and longest stage of the Mühlenwanderweg takes us along Lake Oelsen to Grunow-Dammendorf. Now we follow the Demnitz to Mixdorf and then hike back to Müllrose, the starting point of our tour, on the already familiar route along Lake Müllrose.

title: Wildhaus - Chreialpfirst - Zwinglipass - Wildhaus
short_description: Challenging mountain hike über the Mutschen summit, with fantastic views über the Rhine valley, all of Liechtenstein, Vorarlberg and down to Lake Constance.
long_description: On the Schönenbodenstrasse we hike to the valley station of the Gamplütbahn and continue on a somewhat steep footpath über the Flürentobel (Variante A) directly to Alp Tesel. However, we can also take the train to Gamplot and reach Alp Tesel on an alpine road under the mighty Schafbergwand via Alp Fros. A long, slowly ascending valley lies before us, through which we climb to the Mutschensattel. From there, the short climb to the Mutschen summit (option B) is worthwhile - it offers us a fantastic view üacross the Rhine valley, to the Bündner mountains, Luziensteig, Liechtenstein, Vorarlberg with Feldkirch and down to Lake Constance and Germany. From the Mutschensattel we take a hike over the Chreialpfirst to the Zwinglipass under the mighty Altmann. Down we go to Chreialp and on a romantic zigzag path to Teselalp. Everywhere we find beautiful alpine flowers in a wonderful environment. On the path we know from the ascent we reach the Gampl restaurant via Fros and then by train or on foot to Wildhaus.

images.caption: View of Wildhaus and the Churfirsten mountains

title: Wildhaus - Gamserrugg - Voralp
short_description: Geological circular trail with information boards über the formation of the Churfirsten.Bergwanderung.
long_description:
From Wildhaus we ascend to Oberdorf or use the railway. Via St.Gallerweid we hike up to Freienalp, then along the railway up quite steeply to the Gamsalp mountain station. This is where the geological trail around the Gamserrugg begins. On the Chäserrugg trail, the path climbs gently to the Gamserrugg saddle. Depending on the time of year, alpine flowers such as fire lilies, türkenbund, alpine anemones and ostrich bellflowers bloom in the steep rocky slopes. Even the moon rue, a small plant that already blossomed 60 million years ago, can be found here.

Further along the Geological Trail we hike downhill to Obers. Above the Nideri, Piz Sol and Ringelspitz, the highest mountain in St. Gallen, can be seen, with the Principality of Liechtenstein and Voralberg on the left. The many Romanesque field names such as Galfer, Schlawitz, Garschella or Plisen tell us that the alpine pastures here were already used over 2000 years ago.
&Uml;ber Alti Hütte we reach the Galfer, then descend slightly to the Schwanz. Here we branch off to Vorderstöcken and hike through the Risiwald forest down to Voralp and the lake of the same name.
From Voralp the post bus takes us down to Grabs and back to Wildhaus.



.

title: Wildhaus - Gamsalp - Lüsis - Walenstadt
short_description: Mountain hike with major differences in altitude, therefore only recommended for experienced mountain hikers.
long_description: From Wildhaus to Gamsalp we take the chairlift. On the Geological Trail we climb up to the saddle, then descend via scree slopes and rocky slopes to the top. Those interested in geology can observe the interesting limestone formations here, which were polished off by the earlier glaciers. The trail continues down through a steep rocky gully, followed by a short steep ascent to the Nideri pass. In front of us is the Seez valley with the villages of Berschis, Flums and Mels, above which is peak after peak. The descent, which is very steep in places, leads over scree slopes, special caution is called for here. However, the sight of the wonderful flora that accompanies us makes you forget about the mud. At the Kurhaus Lüsis we enjoy the view of the steep slopes of the Churfirsten and the Walensee, some 800 m below. For the descent to Walenstadt, we use the road to Talenel and take the direct hiking trail into the town.

title: Unterwasser - Iltios - Selamatt - Starkenbach
short_description: Beautiful and varied hike with views of the Churfirsten mountains from Unterwasser to Starkenbach.
long_description: We leave Unterwasser on the old state road and climb steeply on the hiking trail, past the site of the once famous ski jump, to Schwendi. We hike past the Schwendi lakes to Hinterseen. In the Seichbergwald forest we meet the Höhenweg, which we use to Iltios and Alp Selamatt. At the chairlift station is the first picture and text board, which tells a legend. We now follow the Sagenweg, which takes us across beautiful alpine meadows. Other legend stations invite you to linger and occasionally take a look at the mighty Churfirsten. From Thurtalerstofel we hike down to Schluchenseeli, then climb over a rocky ridge to Breitenalp and Steinhüttli. At the foot of the Selunerrugg, the path branches off to the Wildenmannlisloch. Information boards tell you in detail about the geology and history of the holler system. If you are not afraid of dirty clothes and have good lighting, you can penetrate far into the interior. After the interesting detour, we climb up to Strichboden to the alpine hut «zum wilden Mannli». We continue on the alpine road to the mountain station of the Selunalp cable car. Those who want to avoid the steep path down to Starkenbach use the cable car (option A), the others descend on the wide, roughly gravelled alp path through the Selunwald forest to Alp Hofstatt. Along the edge of the forest and pastures we reach Säss, and via a short stretch of meadow we reach Starkenbach.

title: Halgåleden - Wanderung am Brattfallet Wasserfall in Värmland
short_description:
Der Halgåleden beginnt und endet am Brattfallet Wasserfall. Er führt durch liebliche Natur zwischen Wasserfall und dem Fluss Klarälven und ist in verschiedenen Längen wanderbar.
Translate to English
long_description:
Der Wanderweg Halgåleden ist eigentlich ein kleines Wandergebiet mit der Möglichkeit verschiedene Wanderwege mit unterschiedlichen Streckenlängen zu wandern. Vom kleinen Spaziergang bis zur zweistündigen Wanderung ist für alle etwas dabei.
Man parkt direkt am Brattfors Wasserfall. Danach geht es in einem kleinen Bogen erstmal stromauf. Die Gegend war früher ein Industriegebiet mit Eisenhütten, der Fluß Halgå wurde bis in die 1970er Jahre zum Flößen von Holz genutzt.
Dann kehrt man wieder zum Brattfallet Wasserfall zurück und setzt dann die Wanderung Richtung Süden durch lichten Wald zum Fluß Klarälven hinunter fort. Dort hat man einen schönen Ausblick auf den mäandernden Fluß. Anschließend geht es in einem Bogen zurück zum Wasserfall. Entlang des Wanderweges liegen zwei Windschutze. Am Brattfallet gibt es zwei Picknick-Plätze sowie eine einfache Toilette.
Translate to English

images.caption: Der Wanderweg ist gut zu erkennen und beschildert und markiert
Wanderung in Värmland: Halgåleden - Wanderung am Brattfallet Wasserfall in Värmland

title: Wildhaus - Voralpsee - Werdenberg - Buchs
short_description: Varied and scenic hike from Wildhaus to the tranquil Voralpsee lake to Buchs
long_description: From Wildhaus we take the chairlift to Oberdorf or climb up on foot. Above Oberdorf we walk through the forest to the St.Galler-Weid and over varied alpine pastures to the Älpligatter. On the road we reach the alp Ölberg to the Lochgatter. Here we leave the road and hike down through the beautiful alpine meadows to Gamperfin. Nearby is the Turbenriet, a raised bog of national importance. We follow the road to Berghaus Voralp and make a short detour to Voralpsee. We owe this bijou to a prehistoric rockfall. The special feature of this lake is that it has no outflow above ground. At the Höhi car park, we take the path towards Chalchofen and follow the Rheintal-Höhenweg to Lidmäl. Below Rogghalm, we turn left onto the Rhine Valley-Höhenweg. Below Rogghalm, we turn into Grubenwegli, which leads us through the beautiful Bannwald forest. At the forest exit in Gruben we enjoy the beautiful view of the St.Gallen Rhine valley and the Principality of Liechtenstein. Via Vorderegg, Ober- and Untergatter and past the disused quarry on Egeten we reach the pretty little town of Werdenberg. A sightseeing tour is worthwhile. Along the lake we reach Buchs.

title: Alt St.Johann - Hinterrugg - Chäserrugg - Wildhaus
short_description: Mountain hike, only for hikers who are used to mountains. - The demanding ascent is rewarded by a magnificent panoramic view from the highest peak of the Churfirsten.
long_description: Alt St.Johann dates back to the foundation of the monastery «St.Johann im Thurtal» in 1150. The monastery was abandoned after a fire in 1626. We climb up via the hamlet of Espel and the Pfruendwald or use the chairlift (option A) to Selamatt. From the Selamatt mountain inn we hike to the Zinggen, then right along the outskirts of the Hinterrugg to the Hinterlücheren. At the alpine hut we branch off to Alp Gluris, where the actual mountain trail begins. A rich variety of flowers, including the Eastern Alpine gentian, accompanies us through the Gluris valley. At the Glurissattelgrat we enjoy the first deep view of Lake Walen. On the zigzag path we climb the steep western flank to Hinterrugg. After we have had our fill of the magnificent panoramic view, the descent begins with a crossing of the 400 m long Rückens to Chäserrugg. The descent continues eastwards over a somewhat steep slope and then more gently over the battle slopes to the saddle and Gamsalp. From here we take the chairlift down to Wildhaus. If you are fit enough, you can hike down to the valley in just under two hours via Freienalp - Oberdorf (option B).

title: Stein - Gulmen - Stein
short_description: Mountain hike, past a hundred artificial waterfalls, over beautiful fens and up to a little-known mountain peak.
long_description:
From Stein we hike up über Dörfli to Eggli. On the hiking trail we follow the Dürrenbach in the forest, past a hundred artificial waterfalls. These smaller and larger structures were built over the last hundred years to break the power of the water. At Badhus we leave the Dürrenbach and continue climbing through the Dürrenbach forest and again üover small fens up to the Vorder Höhi and on the summit path to the Gulmen. The view is breathtaking! The descent brings us down to Alp Hüttlisboden. On the Toggenburger Höhenweg we enjoy the magnificent view of the Walensee area. Passing Alp Furgglen, we leisurely reach Stöcklersiten, where a shady fireplace invites you to rest. We descend through the Schletteren forest to the Hagegg and down through small meadows and pastures to the Tergeten farm. A short time later we cross the bridge over the Wissthur, walk past the Säge and Stocken to Stigen and return to Stein via Hinterbüel and Büel.



.

title: Unterwasser - Tierwis - Säntis
short_description: Challenging, panoramic mountain hike from Unterwasser to the Säntis
long_description: Along the Säntisthur we hike to the Chämmerlitobel and the waterfalls with the impressive rock galleries built in 1927. The natural spectacle is particularly impressive at the time of snowmelt. The route continues uphill to Ennetthur and via Chuuml;eboden to the hamlet of Laui. Via Alpli we climb to the alp Thurwis and on the partly steep path via Wannen - Chlingen - Spitzbergli to Tierwis. Depending on the season, we can observe marmots, chamois and even ibexes. The view from Tierwis to Schwägalp and over the wide Hügelland is magnificent. After a steep ascent we reach a high plateau with interesting cracked Karren rocks and deep rock gullies. Another easy ascent brings us to station 2 of the Säntis cable car, which can be used for entry and exit. Then the rocky path winds its way up in short hairpin bends to the Girenspitz. Via the Giren ridge we descend on the path secured with wire ropes to the Blauschneelücke. Then follows the last steep ascent, over partly iron steps, also secured by ropes, to the tunnel entrance of the Säntisgipfel.

title: Sörmlandsleden, Etapp 3 - Tyresta National Park
short_description: A beautiful route in Tyresta National Park, 20 km from Stockholm, with scenic views, lush forests and tranquil lakes, perfect for hikers and nature lovers.
long_description:
This trail is part of the Sörmlandsleden, a long-distance hiking trail in Sweden. This section has around 11 km and you can easily follow its orange markings. The route meanders past lakes Bylsjön and Årsjön, offering pleasant fire pits and resting spots. Hikers will see a mix of old spruce and pine forests with rocky outcrops, while the northern sections showcase broad-leaved trees and younger woodlands. Natural cold-water springs can be found along the boundary of Tyresta National Park and the  Nature Reserve. 
The Tyresta National Park, located just south of Stockholm, is known for its stunning natural beauty and diverse ecosystems. Covering over 1,000 hectares, the park features ancient forests, shimmering lakes, and rugged rock formations. It's a haven for outdoor enthusiasts, offering hiking trails, wildlife viewing, and tranquil picnic spots. The park is also home to a variety of flora and fauna, making it a perfect destination for nature lovers.

title: Nesslau - Speermürli - Ijental - Nesslau
short_description: Varied hike in the pre-Alpine landscape.
long_description:
On the road we climb up to Laad. Shortly after the Egg farm we leave it and hike up via Eggli to Windbläss. Another gentle climb awaits us, then we have a nice, quiet stretch ahead of us. Without any major differences in altitude, we now hike below the Blässchopfgipfel on an elevated trail via the Heumooserhöchi and Seilchöpf to the Alp Vorder Elisiten. We climb a few more metres and soon stand at the Schilt crossroads. To our right we see the stubby slope of the Speermürli, and to the left the peak of the 1950 m high Speer, the highest Nagelfluh mountain in Europe, towers into the sky.
We continue hiking to Bütz and walk üover the ridge to the rustic alpine inn Bütz. After the rest break we descend üvia Stofel - Hagloch - Heidlen and Stafel into the Ijental. Shortly after the small reservoir we leave the road and hike über Laufenweid - Bürzlen down to the Thur. On the way to Neu St.Johann we visit the baroque church of the former Benedictine abbey. This is considered one of the most important post-medieval monastery buildings in the canton of St.Gallen.

title: Spaziergang über Burgberger Weinberg & Agathazeller Moor
short_description: Abwechslungsreicher Spaziergang mit schönen Aussichtspunkten und viel Natur. Kann beliebig ausgedehnt oder abgekürzt werden.
long_description: Burgberg - Waldspielplatz - Panoramaweg Richtung Weinberg - Weinberg - Waldweg - Agathazeller Moor - Burgberg

title: Bernhalden - Tierwis - Schwägalp
short_description: Challenging but rewarding mountain hike. Standing on the highest peak in the municipality of Krummenau and admiring the view is a highlight on a clear, sunny summer day.
long_description: From Bernhalden on the Schwägalpstrasse we hike üover the beautiful alps of the Luttertannen to Dunkelboden and further up üover Bumoos - Unterhofeld to Oberhofeld. Now we enter alpine territory. Via the scree slopes at Schwarzchopf and Gamschopf we climb up to Lauchwis. Up to the Stosssattel we have to overcome another steep meadow ledge. Under the climbing rocks of the Köpfe in front and the Silberplatten, we reach the rock slabs of our destination through a spacious terrain. If we follow the mountain trail markings exactly, we reach the summit without any problems. The summit book proves how many mountain hikers cherish this destination and come by again and again. We descend to the summit along the same route, something else would be too dangerous. We then hike across airy pastures to Tierwis, the well-known mountain inn on the ascent to Säntis. This area is known for its numerous gorges and stone boulders, but also for its wonderful alpine flora. The descent from Tierwis to Schwägalp is well marked and a pleasure for experienced mountain walkers.

title: Short walking route Terschelling
short_description: This route runs through the forests of Terschelling;
long_description: This 5 km route shows you a part of the forests of Terschelling. The nice thing about this route is that you walk around a bunker area.

title: Nesslau - Luttertannen - Schwägalp
short_description: Easy, varied hike to the foot of the Säntis massif, with rare flowers along the way depending on the season and almost exclusively through moorland of national importance.
long_description: From Neu St.Johann we climb up the «Bergligässli» over meadows and past beautiful farms to the Strick junction and the Schwendi farm. This is the start of the Schattenhalb-Riede with its very special flora. High above the Luterental valley, the path leads flat over the boggy soil of the slope meadows to the Rietbad sulphur spring. Strengthened by a sip of sulphur water from the centuries-old healing spring, we reach the large alp of Luttertannen in a good hour üvia Läuis - Laad - Wald. Over flowery alpine meadows we go to Dunkelboden. A little above the alp room we find the signpost towards Schwägalp. The path leads us past the huts of the Stelzenboden Alps to the Dreckloch. After a few metres on the tarred road, the trail turns off to the right, along a small meadow, over wet meadows to the Gmeinen Wisen and over the Nettenfeld to the Schwägalp.

title: St. Gallen - Teufen - Appenzell
short_description: A varied day hike, highly recommended in autumn when the weather is bright above the fog. Appenzell as a hiking destination offers numerous sights worth seeing.
long_description:
Passing the church of St. Georgen, we reach the slightly higher situated Brand and through the shady forest to the Wattbach. Here we cross the city and cantonal border. There is a strenuous climb to Schäflisegg. At the top of the hill there is a magnificent view of the Alpstein. On the narrow hiking trail we descend to the stately village of Teufen, where the important builder Hans Ulrich Grubenmann was active in the 18th century. He built a large number of churches and bridges in eastern Switzerland from 1740 to 1783 with his brothers Jakob and Johannes. He also redesigned the Reformed church in Teufen in 1776.

After the church, the trail leads through the village of Schönenbüel and on the new wooden bridge ücke over the Rotbach to the hamlet of Göbsi. The area is hilly, as it cannot be otherwise in Appenzellerland, up to Saul. We hike via Rellen to Egg and descend through the sunny slope to Appenzell. Halfway, on the right, on a prominent hill stands the ruin of Clanx Castle, built in 1210, at times a refuge for the Abbot of St.Gallen. The castle was destroyed by the Appenzellers in 1402. The typical scattered settlements with pretty Appenzell farmhouses are striking, many with large shelters near the buildings.

title: St. Gallen - Mörschwil - Horn
short_description: Easy hike, from the eastern end of the St.Gallen high valley between the Goldach and Steinachtobel gorges to Lake Constance. The tour has practically no ascents and is therefore very suitable for families. It is particularly recommended at flowering time.
long_description:
In the Neudorf district, we skirt the neo-Baroque parish church of St.Maria from 1913 on Brauerstrasse and pass the botanical garden to Guggeien Höchst, where we enjoy a first far-reaching view of Lake Constance. We hike through the shady Höchsterwald forest in the direction of the valley until we reach the stately farmhouses in the hamlet of Vorder Staag. Continue along a field path to the old Watt castle estate, first mentioned in 1273 and once the property of the Wuerttemberg General von Spitzenberg. The castle wing and estate are still inhabited today. We reach the village of Mörschwil, first mentioned in 811 as Maurini Vilari. The renovated parish church of St. Johannes Baptist, built in 1699 on the walls of the church consecrated in 1510, is worth seeing.
Through beautiful orchards we hike via Beg-getwil to Horchental, cross under the SBB line and branch off to Nonnentobel. We pass under the motorway through the Tübacherholz and Saxerholz to the Ruhberg, with a beautiful view of Lake Constance and the walls of the Franciscan convent of St. Scholastika, built in 1616 under Abbot Bernhard zu Rorschach.
We leave Tübach past the church and hike in an eastern direction to the hamlet of Aach, cross the main road to the Mülhof and arrive in the Thurgau enclave of Horn via the railway crossing.

title: St. Gallen - Hundwiler Höhi - Gonten
short_description: The hike first takes you over hilly terrain, followed by a longer ascent to the beautiful Hundwiler Höhi viewing mountain.

title: Rorschach - Eggersriet - Vögelinsegg
short_description: The hike offers cultural and historical insights into the past and is invigorating due to the diversity of the landscape.
long_description:
From Rorschach harbour we hike to the former Benedictine monastery of Mariaberg, which was built in 1847 under Abbot Ulrich Rösch, destroyed in 1489 and completed after the death of Abbot Ulrich, around 1525. The planned relocation of the St.Gallen monastery to Rorschach did not take place. Since 1864, the monastery has been owned by the Canton of St.Gallen, today a teacher training centre.

Our hike continues to the 13th century St. Annaschloss, once the seat of the nobles of Rorschach. In a south-westerly direction we hike past the hamlets of Büel and Leh üvia Alpenau to the viewpoint «Spitze» and down to Eggersriet, whose striking «Grubenmann church» is visible from afar. To the west of the church, we hike through a newly built district and over meadow paths down into the Goldachtobel and to the Aachmüli. An old wooden bridge spans the Goldach, where gold is still said to be found today...
The ascent takes us to Speicherschwendi and over the Kohlhalden mountain ridge to the historically significant Vögelinsegg. Here, on 15 May 1403, the people of Appenzell defeated the opposing troops of the Abbot of Gallen Monastery. A monument commemorates the great event. Once again we enjoy a magnificent panoramic view over Lake Constance.

images.caption: The tour offers great panoramic views over the lake

title: Goldach - Kaien - Heiden
short_description: The strenuous climb up the hills of the Appenzeller Vorderland is compensated for by a unique panoramic view.
long_description: We leave Goldach in a southerly direction and hike via Hohrain and through the Witenwald to Iltenriet. Via the Grauen and Sennweid huts we climb to Spitzen, one of Eggersriet's vantage points with a magnificent view of Lake Constance and the Alpstein. We head in an easterly direction to Würzwallen and über the historic Reichsstrasse to Riemen. We cross the main road and walk along forest edges and through meadows to the crossing at the Naturfreundehaus. Another unique view of the city of St.Gallen and the Fürstenland compensates us for the ascent. The descent via Ober Hüchi, Schwantelen and Ober Brunnen leads us to the «Biedermeier» village of Heiden, which was uniformly laid out after the village fire of 1838. At the Postplatz stands the striking church, which was rebuilt in 1937 after another fire. The tower can be climbed and offers a unique panoramic view. In the park, a monument commemorates the founder of the Red Cross, Henry Dunant, who spent his last 23 years in Heiden.

title: Gossau - Wissbachschlucht - Flawil
short_description: The Wissbach Gorge is a wild and romantic side valley of the Glatt between Gossau, Flawil and Degersheim. A covered wooden footbridge leads hikers safely through the gorge. A paradise for families with children.
long_description:
Through the south exit of the railway station underpass we hike to the hamlet of Rüti and descend on the footpath to Tobelmüli. We cross the Glatt and enter the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. The ascent to the historic hamlet of Schwänberg, first mentioned in 821, really gets our pulse racing. In 1396 the hamlet came to the Abbey of St.Gallen and thus to the Meieramte Herisau. Since 1459 it has belonged to the municipality of Herisau. Worth mentioning are the mighty old town hall with its striking timber-framed building and the 17th century chimney in the house to the west of the «Sternen».

In a westerly direction, the hiking trail leads into the Wissbach Gorge. Below the gorge, the stream takes up a wide area. We walk to the wooden footbridge and climb up the right Nagelfluh slope. The water flows down the eroded rocky gorge with great gusto. At the top of the gorge is again the calm, wide stream that rises not far from Schwellbrunn. The path leads past a fireplace. At the hamlet of Tal überqueren we cross the road and climb to the hamlet of Schöllen. On the way to Alterswil, a wonderful view opens up into the Fürstenland and the lower Thurtal. We hike along a small hill to the Landberg and along the road to the village of Flawil.

title: Rorschach - Heiden - Walzenhausen
short_description: Hike with unique views of Lake Constance, the Rhine Valley and Vorarlberg.
long_description:
We leave Rorschach railway station through the platform underpass in a southerly direction and walk along the tracks to Wiggen. Here we turn right and hike uphill to Wartensee Castle. Heading uphill, the trail leads us through the forest to the Wienacht-Tobel station of the Rorschach-Heiden railway and, continuing slightly uphill, to the village of Wienacht. Along the slope, through the forest, we reach Unterau and hike past the forest park and through the northern part of the village to the historic post office square of the spa town of Heiden.
From the post office square we head in a southerly direction to the lido, to the Sägerei, to Bissau and to the Bänziger on the edge of the Neienriet. In this area, when the two half-cantons of Appenzell were formed, the confession of the property owners decided on the cantonal affiliation.
After an easy climb, we pass the old people's home to reach the reservoir on the edge of the forest north of Blatten and ürgen to Gerschwendi with a magnificent view of the Rhine valley and Vorarlberg. The hike continues über Gebert, past the Gebertshöchi, to the Rosenberg, where we once again enjoy the far-reaching view of Lake Constance and the Rhine delta, before descending to the spa town of Walzenhausen. The cogwheel railway Walzenhausen - Rheineck or the post bus will take us back to the valley.

title: Arbon - Rorschach - Rheineck
short_description: This route is part of the international Lake Constance circular trail, especially recommended during the fruit blossom season - but also suitable as a winter hike.
long_description:
Arbon has been settled since the early Stone Age. In the 4th century, the fort Arbor Felix was built by the Römer.
We hike to the lake and through a magnificent avenue of trees to Steinach, ücross the river of the same name and reach the Horn enclave along the harbour and lakeside facilities. After the lido, we leave the Seeweg, cross the Seestrasse to the railway crossing and walk past allotments to Hornerholz and the railway bridge over the Goldach. We turn left to the Goldach lido and follow the lakeside path to Rietli harbour and Rorschach harbour. The granary and warehouse, built in 1746, is the landmark of Rorschach and houses, among other things, the local history museum. Through the harbour and beach area we reach the main railway station, use the subway and walk behind the station along the tracks to Wiggen. Then it's slightly uphill to Wartensee Castle, a former servants' castle of the Abbey of St.Gallen from the 13th century. Passing under the Rorschach-Heiden railway, we reach the Kreienwald forest and Buechstiggass, then hike along the ridge with a unique panoramic view to Greifenstein Castle from the 16th century (now privately owned) to the Steiniger Tisch. An easy descent takes us to Buriet. At the Schiff inn we cross the state road and the Steinlibach stream and hike under the railway line along the Steinlibach stream via the Langenhag commercial district to Rheineck railway station.

title: Gossau - St. Pelagiberg - Hauptwil
short_description: Easy hike across Fürstenland to the St.Gallen - Thurgau cantonal border. After a short descent to the Sitter, the ascent to the Hauptwiler Weiern and Hauptwil railway station soon follows.
long_description:
We hike to the hamlet of Lätschen and üvia Andwil to Ober Arnegg. After a small climb to Rüti, we descend to Ronwil. In the distance is the striking church tower of the farming village of Waldkirch, whose name refers to the early existence of a church and which was first mentioned in 879. Worth seeing is the «Kreuz», a striking timber-framed building from 1720. We cross the village and hike to the Egelsee and on to the Hasenbergweier. A rest area invites you to take a break. At Lauften, we use the road for a short time, then we branch off and reach the spa and pilgrimage town of St. Pelagiberg through the forest, which is dominated by the St. Pelagius pilgrimage church from 1487 with important ceiling paintings by Josef Eichholzer.

Through beautiful orchards we descend to Gertau on the Sitter. Here you can cross the river with a ferry. We hike downstream to the hamlet of Tobelmüli, then climb up to Wilen and the Hauptwiler Weiern, the collective name for the five ponds Horber-Weier, Rütiweier, Horbacher-Weier, Gwand-weier and Hauptwiler Weier. We enjoy the idyllic nature reserve and reach the historic village of Hauptwil, which received the Wakker Prize in 1999. Sights worth seeing include the castle from 1664, the «Türmli», the old castle tavern from 1665 or the 17th and 18th century workers' houses, which are among the äoldest of their kind in Switzerland.

title: Gossau - Tannenberg - St.Gallen
short_description: Numerous hiking trails lead to the Tannenberg, at its foot are the villages of Andwil, Waldkirch, Bernhardzell, Engelburg and a little further away Gossau and Abtwil.
long_description:
We use the southern railway station underpass and hike to Oberdorfbachweg and on to Bruggwis. On a bridge we cross the SBB railway line to the Mettendorf district and through the Matterwald to Gruenholz. Via the hamlets of Hinterberg and Rötelbach we reach Hohfirst and climb to Tannenberg. The magnificent panoramic view of the Appenzell region with the Säntis massif, the canton of Thurgau and Lake Constance invite you to linger.
On the tarmac road, head in an easterly direction to the hamlet of Locherhof and along a beautiful hiking trail to the hamlet of Secki. A garden road leads to the Schönbüel. On the neighbourhood road we reach the village centre of Engelburg. Engelburg belongs to the political municipality of Gaiserwald, which also includes the villages of Abtwil and St.Josefen. There is no village of Gaiserwald. The names Gaiserwald and Waldkirch indicate that the forest area has always been large.
Just a few metres below the church we leave the road and descend via Oberhalden - Rüti - Sitterhüsli to the Hätterensteg. The last ascent to Rosenberg gets us going again before we reach the centre of St.Gallen with the descent on the Schlösslitreppe.

title: Gossau - Niederbüren - Bischofszell
short_description: Easy hike from the Glattal into the Thurtal with a visit to the historic town of Bischofszell in Thurgau.
long_description:
We hike in a northerly direction to Lindenberg with a resting place «table and Bänk» under the mighty lime trees. After a short panoramic view of the Alpstein and the canton of Thurgau, the trail continues to the hamlet of Lätschen. Passing the hamlets of Erlenhof and Bächigen, we turn left to Henessenmüli, a time-honoured farm with a restaurant, mill and sawmill. In the night of 22nd to 23rd February 1985, the inn burnt down to the ground and was rebuilt in the old style. The old sawmill is put into operation from time to time for viewing.
Behind the barn, the hiking trail leads to the Schnart, where we cross the road to Niederbüren and enter the Diggetwald. The trail leads us to Tannwisen and the farming village of Niederbüren. From there we hike to the Thur dam. We often have to share the path to Bischofszell along the Thur with bikers and riders. Nevertheless, it is fascinating to follow the rushing river, which rises in Wildhaus as the Wildhauser Thur and in Thurwis as the Säntisthur and flows into the Rhine at Flaach.
Shortly before Bischofszell, at the stone arch bridge dating from 1487 - renovated as a footbridge in 1972 - we leave the idyllic Thur landscape and climb up to the historic town of Bischofszell, which lies on a terrace at the foot of the Bischofberg üabove the confluence of the Sitter and Thur.

title: The wine road through Vrancea
short_description: The wine route through the historic region of Moldova passes, first of all, through Vrancea. As an extension of the Dealu Mare wine-growing area, the Dealurile Vrancei wine-growing area includes the famous Panciu and Odobești vineyards.
long_description:
To taste the wines of Vrance, you pass through the picturesque area of the Curving Subcarpathians. The landscape is dotted with vineyards, which produce some of the best white wines in Europe.
The wine trail through Vrancea takes you to several small wineries from the old large wine production units concentrated around the town of Odobești. You'll have the opportunity to taste wines from established varieties such as Chardonnay or Aligote, as well as wines specific to the area - Șarba, Plăvaia or Galbena de Odobești.
Your trip can be enriched with short stops along the way, and in this respect, Domeniile Panciu could pleasantly surprise you with the facilities of the resort they offer.
The Vrance area is one of the wildest and most surprising in terms of natural beauty. That's why we also recommend a trip to Lepșa to admire waterfalls, gorges and a beautiful themed trail.

title: coastal views and old military paths on Babina glava
short_description: Long, strenuous hike to the summit of Babina glava with stunning views over the coastal mountains of Budva in Lovcén National Park.
long_description: Close to the coastal city of Budva, this hike is perfect for those who enjoy a long, adventures walk and are keen to get to the heart of Lovcén Natioanl Park. Starting from the village of Brajici on the Budva-Cetinje road, this hike follows mostly old military trails up to the open high plateau overlooking the coast and the surrounding mountains. Babina glava might not be a spectacular summit in itself, but it is one of the highest points on the plateau and offers and unforgettable panorama. This is truly one of the most beautiful hikes you can do along the coast of Montenegro.

title: Route 66
short_description: For decades, Route 66 has been fascinating motorsport and travel enthusiasts alike. The famous freeway extends over almost 4,000 km and is considered a symbol of unlimited freedom. This tour presents you a couple of sightseeing spots along the road and leads you all the way to California’s picturesque Pacific coast.
long_description: The famous panoramic route starts in Chicago (Illinois) and leads you through six federal states to the sunny coast of Santa Monica (California). However, the actual route is not the original one, even if it’s called “Historic Route 66“. It’s more a touristic route which consists of sections of the former freeway. Nonetheless, it seems like Route 66 hasn’t lost anything of ist appeal. And with all the stunning sights and tourist attractions along the way, such as Grand Canyon, Las Vegas or the sunny coastline of Santa Monica, that doesn’t come as a surprise. Besides, there are other interesting stopovers like “Route 66 Hall of Fame“ and “Route 66 Museum“which give you an interesting insight into the history of Northamerica’s most famous freeway.

title: Traseu tematic „Natura sub lupă” (Parcul Sticlăriei, București)
short_description:
Traseul tematic din Parcul Sticlăriei din București propune o incursiune în subiectul zonelor naturale urbane (de care și parcul aparține) și a speciilor caracteristice acestora, cu acces pe parcul în care te plimbi.
Translate to English
long_description:
Traseul are 15 opriri. Prima se află la intrarea în parc, în care se povestesc câteva lucruri despre istoria locului; ultima, pe insulița din mijlocul parcului. Aici se ajunge pe două poduri opuse, iar trecerea lor e prilej de observare a păsărilor care cuibăresc în stufăriș.
Majoritatea panourilor au o structură informativă, unele fiind ușor interactive, invitând la atingere, rotire, deschidere.  
Dacă vii aici cu copiii, aceștia vor găsi multe elemente naturale care le vor atrage atenția. La opririle dedicate păsărilor, într-o zi fără aglomerație cei mici pot avea surpriza să le și surprindă cu ochiul liber (desigur ghidați).

title: Trip to Geroldsauer Wasserfall
short_description: A relatively short circular hike leading to the Geroldsauer Wasserfall in the north of the Black Forest
long_description: A relatively easy and short hiking route leading through wooded landscapes next to flowing water towards the Groldsauer Falls. A suspension bridge, an observation deck, flowing water, waterfalls and rich vegetation await you on the route. A great and less visited hiking route for those looking for a refreshing trip in front of the landscapes that characterize the Black Forest.

title: Neckertaler Höhenweg (Stage 1)
short_description: On the way on the Neckentaler Höhenweg.
long_description: From the village of Mogelsberg, the route climbs up to Wilkethöchi with an impressive panoramic view from the Vorarlberg to the Bernese Alps. Past the former embroiderer village of Dicken, the route leads up to the Bergli restaurant. Afterwards the trail ührt over the Höhenzug with various vantage points and restaurants and follows the well-known Jakobsweg for a while. Then it descends to the St. Gallen-Appenzell border village of Wald-Schönengrund.

title: Neckertaler Höhenweg (Stage 2)
long_description: The climb up the Hochhamm and across alpine pastures to the Hochalp is rewarded by the panoramic view of the mighty Säntis massif and far beyond Lake Constance. On top of that, the cosy inns on both of them invite you to take a break. The varied Appenzell Alpine Trail continues towards Schwägalp. At one point the view of the Appenzellerland becomes clear, at another time of the Obertoggenburg. From the Schwägalp pass, there are post bus connections to Toggenburg and Appenzellerland.

title: Flawil - Magdenau - Tufertschwil - Lütisburg
short_description: Easy hike from Untertoggenburg to Alttoggenburg. One of the most beautiful hiking routes over the Schauenberg and Winzenberg.
long_description:
The «industrialist and embroiderer village of Flawil» is first mentioned in 858 as «Flawilare». We hike in a southerly direction to Büelwis and climb past the Magdenauer Höchi through the forest to Magdenau, which is dominated by the Cistercian convent founded in 1244 with the former parish church of St.Verena. We follow the road for a while and reach the Schauenberg via Spilberg - Alenschwanden and the well-known vantage point Winzenberg, from where you have an excellent view of the Alpstein and Toggenburg. On the «Windrädliweg» we hike to Tufertschwil. The chapel of St. Fridolin from 1537 and the district building from 1653 are worth seeing.
We follow the road again for a while and descend to the village of Lütisburg at the confluence of the Thur and Necker rivers. The Necker is crossed by a covered wooden bridge from the 19th century and the Letzibr bridge from 1969, the Thur by the covered wooden bridge from 1789 and the new Thur bridge from 1997, and the Gonzenbach by the Guggenloch railway bridge, built between 1870 and 1875 as an iron structure and renewed with a stone structure in 1945. The Catholic parish church of St. Michael stands on a castle hill. It was built with stones from the castle in 1810/11.

title: Rutines mountain pasture hiking trail
short_description: This 4.2 km route invites you to discover the rugged beauty of the mountains while offering a tranquil immersion in nature.
long_description:
The hike starts in La Rosière, a picturesque village in the Giffre valley, in the heart of the French Alps. Right from the start, the trail leads you through a landscape of alpine meadows, bordered by coniferous forests. The well-marked path offers a gentle, gradual ascent, ideal even for inexperienced hikers.
As you climb gently, you'll be rewarded with spectacular views of the surrounding peaks and verdant valleys. The wealth of local wildlife is also a highlight of the route. Keep your eyes peeled for marmots warming up in the sun, chamois frolicking between the rocks, and maybe even birds of prey in flight. Chirping birds and the sound of wind in the trees add to the serenity of the experience.
The arrival at the Rutines mountain pasture is a highlight of the tour. This peaceful spot, with its lush green meadows and traditional wooden buildings, offers magnificent views of the surrounding mountains. It's an ideal place to take a break, enjoy a picnic and relax while admiring the Alpine scenery. The view of the surrounding mountains and valleys is particularly impressive and invites contemplation.
The return to La Rosière is a descent through wooded areas and clearings, offering a new perspective on the landscape you saw on the outward journey. The descent is generally gentle and easy, allowing you to savor the last picturesque views before returning to the starting point.

title: Toggenburg High Trail (Section 6)
short_description: Day 6 - On the Toggenburg Hiking Trail
long_description:
To Wil, the hike is no longer too rigorous. From Mühlrüti we climb to the legendary vantage point of St. Iddaburg, where in the 12th century Count Heinrich is said to have pushed his wife Idda, accused of adultery, into the abyss. The innocent survived the fall and then decided to dedicate her life to God alone as a hermit.
The trail continues to Dietschwil, then we hike to the Giessenfall and reach the Thurweg at Wurenholz, which we follow to the Äbtestadt Wil.

title: रंगमलाई मंदिर ट्रैक
short_description: यह एक छोटी लेकिन सुन्दर ट्रेल जो की पहाड़ी के ऊपर बने हुए एक छोटे मंदिर तक जाती है ।
long_description: यह एक मंदिर तक जाने वाली खूबसूरत ट्रेल है जो चट्टानों और झाड़ियों से होकर एक पहाड़ की चोटी तक जाती है। ट्रेल आउट एंड बैक प्रकार की सिंगल ट्रेल है। आरंभ बिंदु से अंत तक एकतरफा दूरी लगभग 1.5 किलोमीटर और आना-जाना दोनों मिलकर रास्ता 3  किलोमीटर लम्बा है। ट्रेल का रखरखाव स्थानीय वन विभाग करता है। इस ट्रैकिंग में मध्यम दर्जे की चढ़ाई है जो नौसिखिए या अनुभवी हाइकर्स  के लिए कोई चुनौती नहीं होनी चाहिए। एकतरफा ट्रैक एक घंटे से भी कम समय में तय किया जा सकती है। ट्रैक का अंतिम बिंदु एक सुंदर स्थानीय मंदिर है जहाँ जून-जुलाई के महीनों में एक खास दिन विशाल मेले और समारोह मनाया जाता है। उस दौरान यह ट्रैक  मार्ग न सिर्फ एक नेचर ट्रेल बल्कि तीर्थयात्रा ट्रैक भी बन जाता है। ट्रैक पूरे साल के दौरान कभी भी किया जा सकता है लेकिन जनवरी से मार्च और सितम्बर से नवंबर सबसे बढ़िया महीने हैं।

title: Beautiful river walk in Edingen-Neckarhausen (Heidelberg)
short_description: This river walk takes us along the beautiful Neckar and offers us a magnificent panoramic view.
long_description:
We start our tour at the swimming pool. We walk past the ferry that goes in the direction of Ladenburg. Then we walk towards Heidelberg, almost always along the Neckar. Here we have a beautiful view of the Bergstrasse at the Odenwald.
We have the opportunity to linger on one of the benches and watch the boats.
As the tour progresses, we can stop off at the "Fährhaus am Krottenneckar". Here we have a beautiful panorama.

title: Talsperrenweg
short_description: On the Talsperrenweg, we hike from Hagen in Westphalia through the Ennepe-Ruhr valley, make a short excursion into the Oberbergisches Land region, roam through the Siegerland region and finally reach the historic old town of Biedenkopf, located in the Lahn-Dill-Bergland region. Along the way, you will pass a total of eight dams as well as other exciting sights and scenic highlights in a constant up and down cycle.
long_description:
Stage 1: Hagen - Ennepetalsperre (20 km)
After crossing Hagen's Stadtgarten and Stadtwald, we hike past the Hasper dam, over the Scharpenberg and then down into the Ennepe valley to the Ennepetalsperre dam.
Stage 2: Ennepetalsperre - Wasserfuhr (19 km)
We continue our way in a southerly direction and walk across fields, meadows and through forests until we reach the Nayetal dam as well as the Schevelingen dam towards the end of the day.
Stage 3: Wasserfuhr - Aggertalsperre (25 km)
Shortly after Wasserfuhr we hike over the dam wall of the Kerspetalsperre, take a look at the stately villas in Rönsahl and a little later look down from the dam wall of the Lingesetalsperre. Past the Brucher dam and through Dannenberg, we now climb the Unnenberg, with its tower of the same name, which offers a great view. The Agger reservoir at Hackenberg is the last water reservoir and the destination of today's stage.
Stage 4: Aggertalsperre - Biggesee (19 km)
We turn east and hike over the Knollen, Beulberg and Wahlert to the small stream valley of the Herpel. Then we head uphill again and along a high trail to Dumnicke. Between Eickhagen and Rhode (OT of Olpe) we cross the Biggesee.
Stage 5: Biggesee - Krombach (16 km)
Today we walk around Olpe and enter the forest of the same name behind Altenkleusheim, which leads us to Krombach. Lovers of the famous Krombacher Pils will be pleased to have the opportunity to visit the brewery.
Stage 6: Krombach - Hilchenbach (14 km)
With the exception of the village of Müsen, today's stage takes us exclusively through the beautiful forest of the Siegerland region, passing the Breitenbach dam along the way.
Stage 7: Hilchenbach - Forsthaus Hohenroth (16 km)
Today we can expect some challenging climbs in the Rothaargebirge, the Ginsburg ruins on the Schlossberg, several idyllic ponds and the Netphe stream valley. At the Hohenroth forester's lodge we then reached the stage's finishing point.
Stage 8: Forsthaus Hohenroth - Fischelbach (20 km)
Today we will hardly encounter any traces of human settlement, but walk continuously through a vast forest area over the Grauhein, the Lahnkopf, the Jagd-Berg and along the Fischelbach to the village of the same name. In the process, we will also hike past the sources of the Eder and Lahn rivers.
Stage 9: Fischelbach - Biedenkopf (17 km)
The last stage is again very scenic and leads through Kleingladenbach and Breidenbach in the Perf valley to the old town of Biedenkopf on the Lahn, which is well worth seeing. A visit to the castle is a worthy conclusion to this eventful tour.

title: Sentier des 3 châteaux
short_description:
Partez à la découverte d’un circuit unique reliant Boussan, Aurignac et Montoulieu-Saint-Bernard. Cette boucle mêle nature préservée, avec une faune et une flore riches, et vestiges médiévaux comme remparts et châteaux. 
Translate to English
long_description:
Au départ de Boussan, ce circuit vous invite à un voyage à travers la nature préservée et l’histoire médiévale de la Haute-Garonne.
Dès les premiers pas, vous serez plongé dans un cadre bucolique où la faune locale, des chevreuils aux milans royaux, partage l’espace avec une flore variée, des chênes séculaires aux tapis de fleurs sauvages. Le village dévoile ses vestiges médiévaux, témoins d’un riche passé, avec des ruines de remparts et des maisons en pierre.
En poursuivant vers Aurignac, berceau de la Préhistoire européenne, vous découvrirez un village où l’histoire s’écrit en couches successives. Son château médiéval, surplombant la vallée, offre une vue imprenable sur la chaîne des Pyrénées, majestueuse et omniprésente tout au long de votre chemin. Prenez le temps de flâner dans les ruelles où se mêlent charme d’antan et panorama époustouflant.
Le sentier vous mène ensuite à Montoulieu-Saint-Bernard, village pittoresque niché dans un écrin de verdure. Ici, l’histoire se raconte à travers son église et ses bâtisses anciennes, véritables témoins de l’époque médiévale. Vous y ressentirez une quiétude intemporelle.
Enfin, le chemin du retour vers Boussan vous gratifie de points de vue spectaculaires sur les Pyrénées, qui semblent veiller sur ces terres chargées d’histoire.

title: माने भन्ज्यांग से चित्रे गुम्बा का ट्रैक
short_description: यह एक सुन्दर हाईकिंग ट्रेल है जो दार्जिलिंग के माने भन्ज्यांग से शुरू होकर नेपाल के चित्रे गोम्पा (ब ौद्ध मठ) तक जाती है।
long_description:
यह लूप ट्रेल भारत से नेपाल तक जाती है और एक सुन्दर पहाड़ी नेचर ट्रेल है। ट्रेल करीब 6 किलोमीटर लम्बी है और 2 घंटे में तय की जा सकती है। मार्ग का शुरूआती हिस्सा घने जंगलों से भरी हुई नेचर ट्रेल है और अपने गंतव्य 'चित्रे गुम्बा' पहुँचने के बाद वापस लौटते समय डामर वाली पक्की सड़क में बदल जाती है।
ट्रेल का कठिनाई स्तर मध्यम है और इसमें चढ़ाई भी है। यह अच्छा रहेगा की हाइकर फिट और स्वस्थ हों। यदि पहाड़ी मार्ग पर चलने में दिक्कत हो तो यह दौरा पक्की सड़क पर किराये की जीप या मोटरबाइक से भी किया जा सकता है। यह अनछुई ट्रेल बेहद ही सुन्दर है और इसके बारे में अभी तक ज्यादा बाहरी लोगो को पता नहीं है।

title: Forgotten World Highway
short_description: The north of New Zealand still seems to be a white spot on the map, but that’s exactly what makes this destination so charming, The legendary Forgotten World Highway takes you on a trip to several stunning sights, such as the beautiful Egmont National Park, the breathtaking Tangarakau Gorge - and even to the smallest republic in the world.
long_description: On about 90 miles of length this scenic route makes you discover the tranquil hinterland of new Zealand’s northern island. It follows the former State Highway 43 from the city of Stratford to the city of Taumarunui. The road was constructed in the late 19th century, but it hasn’t lost none of its charm. Crossing vast areas of unspoiled nature, it offers spectacular views of the hinterland. The scenic road is still pretty untraveled and stops by several distinct locations, such as Whangamomona, one of the smallest republics in the world. The route extends from the city of Stratford to the vast Egmont National Park, with an ever-changing landscape spanning from mountain saddles and impressive gorges to spectacular tunnels. Along the way, you will see from afar the stunning peak of Mount Taranaki, the heart of Egmont National Park. But don’t miss to stop by the route’s hidden treasure: Tangarakau Gorge, a deep and narrow valley with steep sides formed by Tangarakau river.
