title: Across the Picturesque Bridge - another wonder of the world!
short_description: The picturesque bridge in Serebryany Bor floats on cables over the Moskva River and is the highest cable-stayed bridge in Europe and the only one of its kind in Moscow.
long_description:
The bridge was opened right on the eve of 2007. The author of the idea – folk artist Nikolai Ivanovich Shumakov. The bridge was repeatedly redrawn and modified by the hands of the master. The author claims that the idea existed among the architects of imperial Russia, but technically it has been implemented only in modern times. The bridge is unique in that it is located between two park areas and neither of them was harmed during its construction. The structure was built over the river without touching any of the protected park areas.
In the beginning of the project, the bridge was going to be built without the medians. But after taking a close look, the legendary Yuri Luzhkov jabbed his finger at the drawing of the bridge and said: "There should be a cafeteria here. Thus, the bridge scheme had to be redrawn. Thus a suspension dome on top of Zhivopisny Bridge was created. The name Zhivopisny came not from the fact that the bridge is picturesque, of course, but it was named Zhivopisny after Zhivopisnaya Street, located a few steps away from the bridge. How else could the bridge have been called?

title: Easy winter route in Jungholz
short_description: The panoramic winter hike offers the Jungholz guests a unique and romantic view and insight into the traditional idyll of Jungholz. The unique nature, but also the culture of the Austrian enclave will leave a lasting impression. Enjoyable hiking is guaranteed!
long_description:
A wonderful short and easy tour with a great view of the local mountain and the Allgaeu Alps. The starting point is the free and spacious parking lot in the center of the village right next to the church. In the course of the easy tour, various viewpoints and sights can be admired. For the small hunger and the warming refreshment with drinks there are various possibilities to visit a pub or restaurant. For example, the Schrofenhütte restaurant or the Vitalhotel Tirol provide you with delicious regional products.
The village of Jungholz is waiting for you to bring you unique moments!

title: Shatrunjay Mahatirtha Track
short_description: The Shatrunjaya Mahatirthas are a large group of Jain temples located on the Shatrunjaya Hills in the city of Palitana in the state of Gujarat. Palitana is also called the "City of Temples" because of its more than 800 small and big temples. Shatrunjaya Mahatirtha, built in the 11th century, is one of the most sacred places of the Shvetambara tradition of Jainism.
long_description: Shatrunjay Hill Track is a hill pilgrimage route located in Palitana town of Bhavnagar district. This mountain summit route is a loop trail made up mainly of stairs. One has to climb more than 3000 steps to reach the top of Shatrunjaya hill (which was also known as Pundarik Giri in ancient times). If we talk about the city of Palitana, then it is a very important pilgrimage site for the Jains, where there are more than 1000 beautiful Jain temples. Tourists mainly come here for Jain temples and Jain pilgrimage.

title: Autumn hiking in Val d'Arpette
short_description: From the Champex (La Breya) cable car, this easy hike takes you through the unspoilt landscapes of the Val d'Arpette, offering a gentle, panoramic descent.
long_description: This hike, accessible to all walkers, starts at the top of the Champex cable car. The trail takes you through the wild, unspoilt landscape of the Val d'Arpette, one of the region's most emblematic valleys. The gentle descent allows you to take full advantage of the calm and natural beauty of the area. Autumn is the ideal time to explore this trail, when the larch forests that line the path take on golden hues. The contrast between the snow-dusted peaks and the bright gold of the trees creates a striking panorama, transforming this hike into a true immersion in autumn colors. Perfect for an outing with family or friends, this trail offers a unique experience every season.

title: Laufstrecke durch das Wormser Wäldchen und am Rhein entlang zurück
short_description: Laufstrecke durch das Wormser Wäldchen entlang der Bürgerweide, vorbei am Tierpark und Baseballfeld, bis hin zur Sandbank und entlang des Rheinufers zurück zum Startpunkt.
long_description: Der zentral gelegene Startpunkt dieser 8,2 km lange Strecke liegt am Parkplatz des Sportplatzes "Jahnwiese" und lässt einen innerhalb von 2 Minuten der geschäftigen Innenstadt entkommen. Entlang des Stadtparks Bürgerweide (hier kann die Strecke beliebig verlängert werden), vorbei an Tierheim und Wormser Grillhütte, verläuft der Weg bis hinter zum Tierheim parallel zu einer wenig befahrenen Straße. Kurz nach der Brücke über den Eisbach, verläuft der Weg geradlinig und eben bis zum Wormser Schützenverein. Ab dem zugehörigen Parkplatz geht es Richtung Rheinufer zur Wormser Sandbank. An besonders heißen Tagen, kann man, an diesem fast genau auf der Hälfte der Strecke gelegene Punkt eine kleine Pause einlegen und seine Füße im Rhein abkühlen. Danach geht es am Rheinufer entlang zurück Richtung Worms, bis man im Floßhafen ankommt. Die Überquerung der B9 und ein kurzes Stück durch ein Wohngebiet bringt uns wieder zum Ausgangspunkt zurück.

title: Saboteurstien - In the footsteps of the saboteurs from Rjukan Fjellstue to Vemork
short_description: The saboteur path is the road the world-famous Norwegian resistance fighters used during World War II to get from Hardangervidda to Vemork to blow up the heavy water factory.
long_description: The tour starts from Rjukan Fjellstue and follows into Hjerdalen, further up Fjøsbudalen with a great view towards Gaustatoppen and eventually the Norwegian Industrial Workers Museum. The trip continues down to the place where the saboteurs crossed the gorge. After climbing up from the gorge, we follow the old railway route to the museum.

title: Explore the heritage houses in the Szeklerland (circuit)
short_description: This an ideal circuit when in Brașov and you've checked off everything the city and its surroundings have to offer, or if you're looking for new routes close to Brasov and this area is still unknown to you.
long_description:
The circuit includes 4 of the mansions of the Hungarian noble families who once owned vast domains in the current Szeklerland. After their return to their rightful owners, most of them were exemplary restored and reintroduced into the tourist circuit as accommodation spaces, events, or local museums.
Even if you don't spend the night, you can admire the so-called castles and the generous parks that surround them, sip a coffee in an elegant gazebo, or exercise your history knowledge in a captivating conversation with the owner, if you're lucky to meet them (the history of these places span several hundred years and is always fascinating with its romantic elements).
Two highlights along the way are the Damokos Gyula Mansion - Haszmann Pál Museum in Cernat and the Kálnoky Mansion in Micloșoara respectively. The former has a fascinating collection of stoves and stove grates (it's not something you see too often, right?), and the latter is a favorite of Britain's King Charles III. In fact, here you can even enroll on a visit to Charles' estate at Valea Zălanului.

title: पश्चिमी घाट में वायनाड की चेम्ब्रा चोटी तक ट्रैकिंग मार्ग। केरल, भारत
short_description: यह ट्रेल पर्किंग स्थल से शुरू होकर चाय के बागानों से गुजरती है। उसके बाद घने जंगल में प्रवेश करती है और फिर घास के हरे भरे मैदानों स े मिल कर अपने आखिरी चरण में पर्वत चोटी की च ढ़ाई में बदल जाती है।
long_description:
चेम्ब्रा चोटी केरल के कोझीकोड जिले में, मेप्पदी शहर के पास स्थित है। 6890 फीट ऊँची चेम्ब्रा, पश्चिमी घाट की सबसे ऊँची चोटियों में से एक है। चेम्ब्रा ट्रैक के आयोजन की जिम्मेदारी दक्षिण वायनाड वन विकास एजेंसी की है। यही कार्यालय ट्रैकिंग की अनुमति देती है और ट्रेल के आरंभ बिंदु भी है। यहा से दो किलोमीटर आगे एक पार्किंग स्थल हैं जहाँ तक कुछ लोग ड्राइव करना पसंद करते हैं और उसे अपना आरंभ बिंदु बना लेते है।
वन कार्यालय से करीब पन्द्रह मिनट चलने के बाद चेम्ब्रा ट्रेक का आधिकारिक साइनबोर्ड दिखता है। यहाँ से ट्रेल जंगल में घुस जाती है और फिर बाद में घास के मैदान से जुड़ती है।करीब डेढ़ किलोमीटर चलने के बाद यह ट्रेल दिल के आकार वाली हृदयसरसु झील तक पहुंच जाती है जो बहुत सुन्दर है और हमेशा ठन्डे पानी से भरी रहती है। यहां थोड़ी देर आराम और अल्पाहार करना चाहिए।
हृदयसरसु झील से चेम्ब्रा चोटी तक का रास्ता डेढ़ किलोमीटर है। इस पर चढ़ते समय कुछ चट्टानी भाग आते हैं जिन्हें सावधानी से पार करना चाहिए। चेम्ब्रा शिखर पर पहुँचने के बाद वहाँ की प्राकृतिक सुंदरता, ताज़ी हवा हरी-भरी घाटी और शांत वातावरण बहुत ख़ुशी देते हैं।

title: Suleler - Akyar Dam
short_description: We walk about 11 kilometres from Kızılcahamam Süleler Köyü towards Akyar Dam
long_description:
Ankara and its surroundings have many köys, göls and dams where you can have a holiday. These köys, göls and dams are not only beautiful görüntüntüs but also allow you to get to know Ankara in different ways.
The Akyar Dam in Ankara is also worth seeing in summer and winter. There are many routes to Akyar Dam from different neighbourhoods. In this route, we are travelling from Süleler Köyü towards Akyar Dam. Including the resting periods, the route takes us approximately 4 - 4 hours and keeps us fit. Starting from Köy için, we discover both köy life and köy çphase a little. Then we arrive at Akyar Dam on the road passing near Karaağa Kö Kö yü where we watch the scenery and take beautiful photographs.

title: Rüthi - Box Saddle - High Box
short_description: Challenging but easy mountain hike with beautiful views of the Rhine valley, neighbouring Austria and Lake Constance. At the summit, the impressive Alpine Garden awaits us with many rare Alpine plants.
long_description:
From the bus stop Dorf, we hike on a slightly ascending path to Oberdorf and Brunnenberg. At the signpost Moolen we turn right to the Tobelbach, where the mountain trail through the romantic, steep mountain valley begins. After an hour we reach the Brunnenberg alp and shortly afterwards the Inneralp and enjoy the view over the Rhine valley for the first time. The road is a little less steep and leads over the Ochsenmoos to Unterkamor and Oberkamor. If the view is good, you can see as far as Lake Constance. We hike over the Kastensattel and climb up to HohenKasten. The nearby mountain restaurant and the magnificent panoramic view over the Rhine valley, the Lake Constance region and over the Alpstein to Graubünden reward us for the ascent.
The adjacent Alpine Garden is not only interesting for botanists. Around 200 different alpine herbs and mountain flowers are said to be found here, depending on the season.

images.caption: Rüthi, starting point of this rewarding hike

title: Frümsen - Stauberen - Hoher Kasten - Frümsen
short_description: The trail is a part of the geological hiking trail Hoher Kasten - Saxerlücke
long_description:
Frümsen forms the political municipality of Sennwald together with Haag, Salez, Sax and Sennwald.
From the mountain station we hike along the ridge to Stauberenfirst and Stelli towards Hoher Kasten. The trail is part of the geological hiking trail Hoher Kasten - Saxerlücke created by Dr. Heierli. At Baritsch we start the last ascent over the Kastensattel to the famous Hoher Kasten mountain, where we enjoy the beautiful panoramic view: To the south lies Werdenberg and the Principality of Liechtenstein, to the west the Alpstein chain with Lake Stettis and Alpsigel, to the northwest the Lower Rhine Valley and Lake Constance, and to the east Zimbaspitze and Schesaplana.
The descent leads down to the Kastensattel and back to Baritsch, where the actual descent into the Rhine Valley begins. The mountain trail zigzags steeply through forest and alpine pastures down to Alp Rohr, which is open to visitors in the summer months. The mountain path leads to the tunnels and galleries built in the 1930s as emergency work. At the Britschli junction, the trail leads to Sennwald - Lögert and on the Rheintal Höhenweg back to the starting point.

title: Diepoldsau - Old Rhine - Diepoldsau
short_description: A circular walk suitable for families along the new Rhine and through the nature reserve of the Old Rhine, for practically every season.
long_description: We start the hike at the Hängebrke on the east side of the Rhine, which was inaugurated in 1985. Here, exceptionally, the border to Vorarlberg runs along the Old Rhine. We walk along the Rhine embankment in a southerly direction and enjoy the view of the hills and mountains of the Appenzellerland and the Vorarlberg. At the old, but well-maintained iron bridge, we leave the Rhine dam briefly, but return to it at the wayside cross. After half an hour through the agriculturally used plain, we reach the southernmost point of the hike. Here, in 1923, the Rhine was diverted from the old river loop into the now straightened river bed. We turn left and follow the old course of the river. Let's take our time to enjoy the nature reserve! The calm waters are mainly inhabited by carp. For ornithologists, the bird life is of great interest: nightingale, oriole, common tern or whinchat are worth mentioning. Water lilies, irises, orchid and common skipping weed delight the botanist. We follow the shore path to the eastern point and walk along the New Rhine in a southerly direction back to the starting point.

title: Grabser Voralp - Nideri - Grabser Voralp
short_description: Challenging mountain hike with unique views of Lake Walen.
long_description: From the car park and the Höhi post bus stop, the trail leads to the Voralp mountain inn and üvia the Risiwald and Wetterbrunnen alps to the remains of the walls of the former alp «Alti Hütte» buildings, which were destroyed by a dust avalanche. On the hiking trail we climb üover the Pizol alpine pastures to the Nideri Pass on the Walenstadt - Grabs municipal border. Bunkers from the Second World War can still be seen here. We enjoy the magnificent view of the Seez valley with Lake Walen and the Glarus mountains. The narrow mountain path leads along the steep flank to the top with only a slight incline. In front of us lies the Alptal Naus, steeply sloping down to the Voralpsee, parallel to it the Schlawitz, which we have walked through, separated by the mountain range with Höchst, Glatthalden and Föhrenchopf. To the right rise Sichelkamm, the Wissi Frauen and the imposing Gamsberg, the highest point in the municipality of Grabs. The steep descent on the zigzag path brings us to the Obersässbrunnen and the alpine pastures of Naus Obersäss. Still steeply descending, we walk via Naus Unters, Muttelberg to the alp Bachboden, then we hike on the road back to Voralp. Through some clearings in the forest we enjoy the view of the green waters of the Voralpsee.

title: Along the Großer Alpsee up to the Juget-Alpe and back again
short_description: From the Outdooractive HQ along the shore of the beautiful Großer Alpsee in the middle of the Nagelfluhkette Nature Park. From the lake it is a few metres uphill to the Juget-Alpe and back to the starting point via a forest path.
long_description:
If you want to get a good first impression of the atmosphere in beautiful Immenstadt i. Allgäu, this circular walk is just right for you.
The large Alpsee lake is a real highlight for many tourists, locals and water sports enthusiasts. In summer, you can cool off here or watch the windsurfers out on the lake. Those who prefer a more leisurely pace can enjoy the sunshine on a walk along the shore. With the glistening water at your feet and a view of the picturesque mountains, you can't go wrong here.

Refreshments are also provided on this tour. A panoramic path leads up to the Juget-Alpe, where you can fortify yourself, enjoy a good Lake Constance wine or simply relax before setting off on the return journey.

images.caption: Blick vom Aussichtspunkt zur Juget Alpe

title: Gams - Sommerigweid - Wildhaus
short_description: Easy, panoramic mountain hike from the Rhine Valley into Toggenburg. Somewhat steep but varied ascent to the Sommerigweid vantage point. Then an easy descent to Wildhaus.
long_description:
The name Gams is derived from the Old Roman Campesias, which means sheep pasture. The once powerful castle, the remains of which were only uncovered in 1964, may have been an early seat of the barons of Sax.

At the church of Gams, we hike up the road to the stream and through the lane to Haslen. Steep meadow paths take us past the mountain schoolhouse and Eichlitten to Hardegg. Through the Steinengasse to the road and on to Oberwis and Mettlen. The forest road leading through the Eggwald brings us to the large wooden cross on the Chüeweid. We continue through the forest to Neuenalp, followed by a short but steep climb to Sommerigweid, where a unique panoramic view awaits us: from the Rhine plain to Vorarlberg and the Principality of Liechtenstein, to the Werdenberg and Bündner Alps and Toggenburg. We hike slightly downhill through the flower-filled Bilchenmoos and along the road to the Schönenbodensee, which invites you to take a refreshing dip, before continuing to the spa town of Wildhaus. Hidden in the forest on the left is the Wildenburg ruin, which gave Wildhaus its name. Built by the Lords of Sax to secure the pass, it was sold to the Counts of Toggenburg in the 14th century and later to the Abbey of St. Gallen.

images.caption: Gams, starting point of the tour

title: A trip around Lake Jasna
short_description: An easy and short hiking route around the magical Jasna lake in northern Slovenia. A small lake, but with a gorgeous appearance and view, at the foot of the Alps.
long_description: An easy and circular hiking route that surrounds Lake Yasna, the lake is relatively small compared to Lakes Bled and Bohini, but the translucent turquoise hue of its waters makes it a great hiking spot for nature lovers as well as for those who want to enjoy a lot of nature and mountains within a short walking distance. On hot summer days you can also bathe in it.

title: St. Gallen - Ramschwag Ruin - Muolen
short_description: Sitterstrandweg - family hike along the Sitter, varied and walkable in every season.
long_description:
From Stocken we walk down Kräzernstrasse and before the bridge turn right onto the Sitterstrandweg, which is also known as part of the St.Galler Brückenweg as far as Schiltacker. In front of us is the former Sittertal quarry, which closed its doors in the 1980s. We cross the Sitter on the Billenberg footbridge and walk past the open air site, the municipal sewage plant and the waste incineration plant. The Ganggelibrogg, a bridge built in 1882, brings us back to the other bank of the Sitter, which we follow to Spisegg. Accompanied by the murmur of the Sitter, we hike along the right bank through the shady Sitter and Hätteren forest. After the Lässerhof and the Erlenholz we come to Leebrugg. Now the hike becomes more demanding. The path leads us to the covered wooden bridge Wannenbrugg, a masterpiece of 44 m length. We follow the Sitter downhill, hike past Tobel and climb up über Engensbüel and Eggen to the ruins of Ramschwag Castle, built in the 12th century, abandoned in the 15th century because of the danger of landslides. Continue in a northerly direction past Chollberg and the Finkenbach farms to Rorenmoos. Halfway before Muolen, the trail turns right to Muolen railway station.




.

title: St.Gallen Neudorf - Solitüde - St.Gallen Haggen
short_description: The hiking route runs along the chain of hills from the east to the west of the city. A rewarding hike, with beautiful views of and over the city.
long_description:
From Neudorf we walk along Martinsbruggstrasse for about 400 m and then turn right through the neighbourhood up into the Achslenwald and onto the Hueb to the Capuchin nunnery of Notkersegg, which was founded in 1381. The current complex dates back to 1666 and stands slightly below the original site. Buy some of the famous nuns' crowns in the monastery as you pass by!
North of the monastery begins the panorama path along the St.Galler Hochtal. It leads past the Drei Weiern to the Mühlegg with the Steinachschlucht gorge, up to the Falkenburg and along the edge of the Bernegg forest down to the Nest. At Nestweier you cross the Teufenerstrasse, then head up to the Solit viewpoint. Westwards we descend through the Menzlenwald forest, past the hamlet of Wilen, to St.Gallen Haggen.

images.caption: Beautiful view of and over the city of St.Gallen

title: Grabser Voralp - Margelchopf - Grabser Voralp
short_description: Challenging but rewarding mountain hike with fantastic views.
long_description: From the Kurhaus bus stop, we hike through the forest to the Chalchofenhütte and climb up the steep mountain path to the small Inggarnascht alpine hut, which is no longer used today. A fountain with fresh spring water invites you to refresh yourself. Between huge stone leaves, the mountain path leads us up to Schlösslichopf. Here we enjoy the unique panoramic view of the Grabs Alps Gamperfin, Naus and Schlawitz, the mountains Gamserrugg, Säntis, Schafberg up to the Kreuzberge with the Hoher Kasten. Vertically below us lies the Voralpsee. We hike on and after a short while reach the alpine huts of Alp Sisitzsäss. From here the path leads with a pleasant incline up to the Sisitz ridge. With a small, but approximate climb, we ascend Grabs' local mountain Margelchopf and are rewarded with a magnificent panoramic view. We return along the same path to Schlösslichopf, continue to the buildings of Alp Oberlänggli and on a narrow mountain path down to the small high alp Unterlänggli and «Zu den Bächen», a rich source of drinking water. The mountain trail leads through the beautiful beech forest down to Chalchofen and back to the Kurhaus.

title: Buchser Malbun - Margelchopf - Buchser Malbun
short_description: Moderately difficult mountain hike üover mostly well-maintained alpine paths. The ascent to the Margelchopf is secured by ropes. The descent from the Chapf to Bützen leads partly over trackless alpine meadows.
long_description: From the car park, we hike across the alpine pasture to the left of the ski lift, follow the alpine road for a short distance and branch off through the sparse high forest to the old alpine path. Via Hanenspil, where capercaillie and black grouse mate in early summer, we reach the Luna fountains - in front of us the Margelchopf with its massive eastern wall. Passing the dreamy alpine lakes, we reach the Sisitzgrat. More experienced hikers dare the short climb to the top of the Margelchopf and enjoy a magnificent panoramic view of the Rhine valley and the surrounding mountains. From the Sisitz ridge, the trail leads down to Alp Sisitzsäss, where the short ascent to Chapf begins. Imposing views of the wild rock formations of the north side of Margelchopf reward us. Partly pathless, the hike leads over the Upper Alps from Gamperney down to Bützen and past the Wisli Alp to Valspuus - Säss. Here we enjoy a relaxing rest before tackling the last section of the trail. After an hour's ascent through the Buchser Hochwald forest, we return to the starting point in Malbun via the Rheintal-Höhenweg. On this section of the trail, we are once again spoilt by the magnificent view of the St. Gallen Rhine Valley.

title: Schlei-Eider-Elbe Hike
short_description: The Schlei-Eider-Elbe hike leads through what is probably the most historic landscape in Schleswig-Holstein and through towns and villages worth seeing. On the first stage from Schleswig to Dörpstedt we see numerous historically interesting towns to the left and right of the path.

title: Vögelinsegg - Over the Harrows - St. Gallen
short_description: One of the most beautiful and rewarding walks in the vicinity of the city. Especially beautiful in autumn, when nature puts on its colourful dress....
long_description:
The historic Vögelinsegg is known to us from the history of the Appenzell freedom battles. The battle monument on the hilltop, a dairyman with a weapon in his hand, reminds us of the victory of the Appenzellers over the troops of the abbot of the monastery of St. Gallen and the towns of Lake Constance on 15 May 1403.
We enjoy the beautiful panoramic view as far as the Swabian Sea and Thurgau and hike up to the Birt. We follow the forest path over the top of the Horstwald forest to the dip at Ober Horst. On the left we see the Appenzellerland with the Alpstein, on the right the woods and farms of the city of St.Gallen. On the Waldegg there is a stately Appenzell inn that invites you to take a break. We continue our hike via Hüslersegg - Egg to Schäflisegg and Frölichsegg. The descent takes us to the Rüti farm and on meadow paths and through the forest we reach Liebegg. From there we continue along the main road to the Riethüsli district.

title: St. Gallen - Wittenbach - Winden
short_description: Half-day hike through a varied landscape with a small ascent to the Peter and Paul Zoo. The hike is particularly beautiful at blossom time and in autumn.
long_description:
From Heiligkreuz, our path leads to the Catholic pilgrimage church Heiligkreuz, built in 1771 by Sebastian Dürr. We ascend on the shady forest path to the Peter and Paul Game Park. This is the only climb of the hike, but we are rewarded with a magnificent view, with the Alpstein to the south and the Lake Constance area to the north. The Peter and Paul Game Park was founded in 1892 by animal lovers and young people.
After the short wildlife excursion, we leave the park and hike northwest down to the village of Wittenbach, past the railway station to Dottenwil Castle, which we can see from afar in an elevated position. The castle, which is over 450 years old, has had many owners. In 1997 it was acquired by the IG Schloss Dottenwil association with the aim of transforming the former old people's home into a cultural centre and making it accessible to the public. The integrated restaurant is open at weekends.
We continue our hike through the well-tended fruit orchards to the Ruggisberg Lady Chapel, built in 1683 to mark the victory over the Turks on the Kahlenberg. Continue to Chrüzegg, then turn right to Lümmenschwil and through the village to Häggenschwil-Winden railway station.

title: St. Gallen - Fünfländerblick - Rheineck
short_description: Varied hike from the city of Gallus to the Rhine, with far-reaching views of Lake Constance and the lakeside landscape.
long_description: We leave the Neudorf district on the Martinsbrugg road and hike via Oberschachen - Riet - Schaugenbädli to Martinsbrugg. After crossing the Goldach, we walk along meadow and forest paths to Eggmoos, which offers a view of the city of St.Gallen that is well worth seeing. In Borüti, we turn off to the viewpoint Höchi. The varied panoramic view rewards us for the ascent. We continue östlich to Spitzen and Würzwallen. Past a reconstructed section of the old imperial road, the hike takes us to Feldmoos and Acker to the Rossbüchel and to the Fünfländerblick. At the chapel, built in 1892, there is a prominent stone: from here we can see the five countries of Bavaria, Austria, Switzerland, Baden and Wurttemberg, which used to be separated. A short descent via Unterbilchen - Landegg to Wartensee gives us a magnificent view of Lake Constance. Through the Kreienwald forest to the Buechstiggass and on the crest of the Buechberg, past Greifenstein Castle, to the Steiniger Tisch with a unique view. Via a stone staircase we climb through the vineyard into the valley to Feldmoos and the historic town of Rheineck, whose eventful history dates back to the Roman times. Various buildings from the 17th and 18th centuries are worth seeing.

title: Durch das Bolgental
short_description: Gemütliche Wanderung mit Einkehrmöglichkeit durch die atemberaubend schöne Landschaft des Allgäus.
long_description:
Wir fahren mit der Hörnerbahn bis zu ihrer Bergstation, wo unsere Wanderung durch die Allgäuer Bergwiesen und -wälder beginnt. Sie führt uns durch das Bolgental an zwei bewirtschafteten Hütten und dem Sonderdorfer Kreuz vorbei zurück zum Startpunkt, der Talstation der Hörnerbahn. Immer wieder bieten sich atemberaubende Ausblicke aus verschiedenen Perspektiven. Fernab des alltäglichen Lärms kann man hier die Natur genießen und zur Ruhe kommen.
Da es die meiste Zeit bergab geht, ist die Wanderung auch mit Kindern gut gehbar und für Leute mit wenig Kondition geeignet.

images.caption: Auf dem Weg zur Talstation der Hörnerbahn Bolsterlang
Durch ein Waldstück auf dem Weg zur Talstation der Hörnerbahn Bolsterlang

title: Toggenburg High Trail (Section 5)
short_description: Day 5 - Hike on the 5th stage of the Toggenburg Hiking Trail
long_description: &Uml;ber the Habrütispitz, the trail leads along the ridge to the Schindelberg mountain inn. Freshly invigorated, we climb to the highest mountain in Zürich, the Schnebelhorn. After the descent to Hirzegg, we reach our destination Hulftegg via Roten and Älpli, where we can spend the night - or hike to Mühlrüti, where the post bus takes us.

title: Walenstadtberg - Betlis - Weesen
short_description: Challenging mountain hike for good, safe mountain walkers with the best footwear.
long_description:
The route leads along the seven Churfirsten peaks over scree slopes and alpine pastures.

From the Knoblisbüel post bus stop, we follow the road üvia Hochrugg to Schrina. Here it is worth making a detour to the Paxmal, a temple-like monument created in 1924-1949 by the brand engraver Karl Bickel. Continue on to Schwaldis. Behind us are Gamsberg and Sichelchamm, to the east Palfris with the Alviergruppe and the Falknis, then the Grauen Hörner, the Guschagruppe, Spitzmeilen and Sächsmoor.
We hike under the rugged rocks of the Schären to the Sälser Hütten and up to Alp Säls, from where the mountain trail takes us to Hag - Stäfeli to Laubegg. On the way, we are surprised again and again by deep views of Lake Walen glistening in the sunlight with the delta of Murg and the Murg valley. On the way we cross various gullies that have to be walked very carefully.
We descend steeply through the Stösswald, then we recover on the way to Rüesteli before we tackle the last steep section to Fulenbach and into the Serenwald. Here we meet the well-known hiking trail Weesen - Quinten, which we follow in the direction of Weesen. After the shady Seerenwald, we reach the tanned wooden houses of Seeren and cross the Seerenbach, which cascades down from dizzying heights. Über Vorderbetlis we reach Strahlegg, then we hike along the narrow Strässchen, partly hewn out of the rock, to Fly and the well-known spa town of Weesen.

title: Toggenburg High Trail (Section 4)
short_description: Day 4 - Hike on the 4th stage of the Toggenbruger Hiking Trail
long_description: The surroundings change from the mountains to the hilly terrain of central Toggenburg. From Tanzboden we head down the valley to Stotzweid, followed by an easy ascent to Alp Oberbauml;chen. Up to the Regelstein vantage point, we repeatedly pass through small interesting moors. Through the Cholwald we reach the village of Ricken on the pass road of the same name, where the hike can easily be interrupted. A steep path leads from Oberricken to the Hattenberg inn. Uphill we reach the Rotstein, then üvia the Tweralpsptiz to the well-known Chrüzgg, where we admire the view of Lake Zürich and the Glarus Alps as well as Toggenburg and the Alpstein.

title: Tielenhof castle walking route
short_description: This hiking trail is 18.5 kilometres and takes about 4.5 hours.
long_description: Just outside Tielen stands the Tielenhof castle. This medieval castle was built in the 14th century. A real moat surrounds the castle and there is even a drawbridge. Over the years, the castle has grown bigger and bigger and has been rebuilt many times.

title: Discovery walk Gerona
short_description: An itinerary that allows you to discover the main historical points of interest in Gerona, from the walk on the wall to the stairs of the cathedral and the Eiffel bridge over the Riu Onyar!

title: Nebelhorn com time Outdooractive
short_description: Climbing the Nebelhorn with the Outdooractive team at the summer party.

title: Trip to Kalkhöf-Alpe
short_description: A relatively short circular hiking trail (on its own) leading to the cabin from which there is a gorgeous and panoramic view of the surrounding towns and mountains as well as of the large Alfaza lake.
long_description:
A nice and circular hiking route that leads in a relatively short walk (about a half hour walk with a relatively moderate ascent) to a local alpine hut where you can enjoy local delicacies as well as a unique view of the wonderful area. The road leading to the cabin is paved and therefore suitable for walking with strollers, but the circular road goes through a wooded area and includes stairs, so those who want to reach the place with a stroller can simply walk the same way back and forth.
Those looking for a shorter route can go to the Kammeregg-Alpe cabin, which is about a 10-minute walk from the parking lot, but it is recommended to make the effort to reach the Klackhof cabin, as the view from it is much richer and wider.

title: Schänis - Oberbogmen - Rieden
short_description: This moderately difficult hike in the St. Gallen Pre-Alps offers a steep ascent to the summit of Ober Bogmen. It will delight hikers of all levels.
long_description:
Before you start the hike, there are several buildings worth seeing in Schänis: the collegiate church of St Sebastian, which houses wonderful treasures from ancient times, the Gallus Tower (the only round tower from roman times in Switzerland) or the old town hall built in 1784.
From the village square, walk in the direction of Ledi and enjoy the shade of the trees on the steep path. After passing the Ramisbach stream, the forest road leads to the Grütwald forest. It continues in the direction of Gleiterbach, which overlooks the wide plain of the Linth region. At the end of the hiking trail to the Ober Bogmen vantage point, you are rewarded with a magnificent panoramic view that stretches from the peaks of Glarus and central Switzerland to the villages of the Linth region. To the east rises the Speer and further south the Federispitz.
The beautiful hike over the mountain ridges then leads us to Rieden. On a tour of the village, we can admire the Magnus Church, a neo-baroque parish church built in 1912.

images.caption: Church of St. Sebastian in Schänis

title: Amden - Rietbach - Krummenau
short_description: Easy mountain hike «from chairlift to chairlift».
long_description:
From Amden to Niderschlagwald we use the chairlift or walk back in about an hour. From the mountain station we hike along an alpine path via Strichboden - Gäudig to Hinter Höhi. Here our view sweeps over a large high moor towards the Alpstein with the Säntis and the Wildhauser Schafberg, which is strikingly folded from this view. On a gravel road on the north side of the Mattstock massif through the avalanche-prone shrub forests to Alp Vordermatt. From here the path climbs more steeply to Ober Chäseren, where we enjoy the view of the Glarnerland. We climb to Stelli. For a detour to the Speer, Europe's highest Nagelfluh mountain, we need to allow about an hour.
We change from Gasterland to Toggenburg and descend to the Speermürli. At the «Leiterli», a small Nagelfluh rock face, we hold on to the safety rope and the iron steps fixed in the rock. This way the descent is no problem. We hike on üvia Alp Bütz and along the ridge to Wolzenalp. On the ridge path we have a view of the whole of Mittlere and Obere Toggenburg. It is only a few minutes to the Rietbach mountain station of the chairlift, which takes us down to Krummenau (information on timetables 071 994 15 15). On foot we have to reckon with about an hour.

title: Way of St. James Tyrol-Allgäu: From Tannheim via Bad Hindelang to Immenstadt
short_description: A section of the Way of St. James also passes through Bad Hindelang. The "Tyrol-Allgäu" stage from Stams in the Inn Valley to Oberstaufen in the Oberallgäu region, with its almost 134 kilometres, connects the Munich Way of St. James with the Tyrolean Way of St. James.
long_description: Coming from the Tannheim Valley, the Way of St. James stops in Bad Hindelang before continuing to Immenstadt in the Alpsee-Grünten region. The route is marked throughout, either by large yellow signs with the inscription "Jakobsweg" (Way of St. James) or with the stickers reminiscent of a sun complete with rays, the symbol of the rays converging on a point on the shell of the scallop shell.

images.caption: The Marienplatz, on the left the city hall and the Mariensäule in the center

title: St. Margrethen - Stony Table - Rheineck
short_description: Leisurely family hike to beautiful vantage points.
long_description:
We hike in a south-westerly direction to Schäflisberg, the first vantage point. Passing a glacier hill and a hay field, we reach Burghalden and, after a short climb through the vines, the ruins of Grimmenstein Castle. The castle, built in 1250 as a fiefdom, was partially destroyed during the Apppenzellerkriege, rebuilt and demolished by the Constans in 1416.
In a north-westerly direction we hike to the Wiberg, an old manor house, which today has been converted to resemble a castle, and descend to the renovated farmhouse Hof from the 15th century. We continue through the protective forest to the Töbelibach and onto the hill above the historic town of Rheineck, with panoramic views of the Rhine bend and the foothills of Lake Constance in Austria. Via the Sandbüchel and Kruft we hike to the wine-growing village of Thal. After a short ascent über die Dorfhalde we walk in a westerly direction to the Tobelmüli, über the Tobelmüliweg to Boden, to the Steinlibach and to the Buechstiggass. After crossing the Thalerstrasse, we hike along the ridge with a unique panoramic view, past the 16th century Geifenstein Castle, to the well-known vantage point Steiniger Tisch.
An easy descent in a northerly direction leads down to Buriet. At the Schiff inn, we cross the main road and the Steinlibach stream, walk in a northerly direction under the railway line and reach Rheineck railway station directly via the Langenhag commercial district.



.

title: Rapperswil - Schmerikon - Benken
short_description: Pronounced flatland hike with no difference in altitude on the famous Strandweg from Rapperswil to Schmerikon and along the Linthkanal.
long_description:
A hike through especially flat countryside, along the famous lakeside path from Rapperswil to Schmerikon and the Linth canal.

Rapperswil is dominated by the castle hill, on which stands the imposing landmark built in the 12th century. Information about the numerous tourist attractions may be found at the Tourist Information on the Fischmarktplatz.

We walk to the Technikum - the engineering school - and to the Heilighüsli, a late Gothic stone construction in the lake. We pass the children's zoo and the beach and reach Busskirch and the Stampf beach, where the Jona river flows into the Obersee, and then follow the railway to Wurmsbach. The Mariazell Cistercian nunnery was founded in 1259, and since 1843, a school for girls has been associated with it. The lakeside path takes us to Bollingen on the Obersee, known in earlier times for its sandstone quarry. The St.Pankratius parish church was erected in the year 1764. In Oberbollingen we pay a short visit to the well-known St.Meinrad's chapel, erected in 1628. Our hike takes us past the shipyard to Schmerikon, formerly the headquarters of shipping on the Linth and on Lake Zurich. At the railway station we take a look at the Bürgerhaus zum Hirzen, built in 1610. Leaving the village, we pass through the industrial quarter to the covered wooded bridge over the Aabach. We cross the Gross-Allmeind and use the «Schwarzen Steg» to get to the Grinau shipping center, first mentioned in 670. The tower dates from 1325. The path now goes along the Linth dam and up to the Hinter Benkner Riet. In front of us we see the Benkner-Büchel, to the left we have a magnificent view of the Regelstein - Tanzboden - Speer - Chüemettler - Federispitz hills. We cross the Linth-Hintergraben and then the broad flatland of the Benken Riets to Benken. In 741, the Babinchova (Benken) monastery, an offspring of the Reichenau island monastery in Lake Constance, was first mentioned. From 824 to 828 Meinrad, later the founder of the Einsiedeln monastery, was a pupil in the monastery school.

title: Rieden - Oberbächen - Ebnat-Kappel
short_description: Medium-difficulty, panoramic hike in the foothills of the Alps, mostly on meadow paths and natural roads.
long_description:
Pre-alpine hike of medium difficulty, mostly meadows and unpaved roads, with plenty of vantage points.

From the village plaza we take the steep trail up through Bergli and Chirnenberg to the Alp Wielesch, where there is a summer restaurant. Here we take time for the beautiful view over the Linth area, Lake Zurich and the alps of Canton Schwyz. It's a somewhat easier hike through Breitenau to the Alp Oberbächen with its lovely playground. The restaurant is open as long as the cows are on the alp. We marvel at the breathtaking view from the hilly Toggenburg to Lake Constance and the Alpstein. Our trail descends to Unterbächen and through Müslen - Eich to Ebnat-Kappel.

Ebnat-Kappel is a combined community made up of the towns of Ebnat and Kappel. Ebnat was called Ober-Wattwil until 1762. In contrast to Wattwil, inhabited chiefly by St. Gall Chlysten, Ober-Wattwil residents were mostly the courtiers of the Toggenburg count. It was the cotton industry that brought the necessary upswing.

title: Altstätten - Höch Hirschberg - Gais
short_description: Impressive hike from the lowlands over the foothills of the Alps into the alpine terrain of the Appenzellerland - with major climbs.
long_description:
We hike to the Oberrüti farm and to the Strick farm. Then we turn right towards Hölzlisberg. The trail leads steeply uphill through meadows and woods to Erlen-gschwend, where we cross the cantonal border. Through the shady forest on the ridge of the Hirschberg we reach the border point Brandegg. Before the Nisplismoos farm, we leave the forest and after 400 m reach the Hirschberg mountain inn. What a lavish view opens up on all sides!
After the rest, we head slightly downhill to Hackböl and via Zwislen to the village of Gais.

Gais - according to tradition, the name actually comes from the goat - was connected to St.Gallen by tram in 1889. In 1904, the line was extended to Appenzell and in 1911 to Altstätten in the Rhine valley. The enclosed village square with church and fountain are well known.

title: Rhine Cycle Route - from Lustenau to Basel
short_description: On this almost 250 km long long-distance cycle route, we follow the course of the Rhine from the Austrian-Swiss border almost to the French border in Basel.

title: Breakneck Ridge short trail
short_description: A shortened version of the Breakneck Ridge trail that is a little easier that the full trail while still offering some wonderful views of the Hudson RIver Valley and Lake Surprise.
long_description: About 50 miles north of New York City, the town of Cold Spring, NY overlooks the Hudson River and majestic surrounding valley. The area offers many activities Historical, cultural and outdoor attractions for visitors. Surrounded by water, forests and ancient mountains, Cold Spring serves as a base camp for hikers, kayakers and climbers. Wooded hiking trails cover Clarence Fahnestock State Park, one of 14,000 acres of preserve east of Cold Spring. The park also has a lake beach, picnic areas, and good spots for swimming, fishing, hunting and bird watching. Several boathouses on rent canoes and kayaks the Hudson River on time for individual paddles or group tours along the banks of the river. Marsh Constitution, south of Cold Spring, is a top place to start kayakers.  They are rewarded with a panoramic view of the Hudson at the top.

title: A trip to Buchenegger Wasserfälle
short_description: A short hiking route that includes challenging sections leading to Buchenegger Wasserfälle in the Upper Allegoi
long_description: A hiking trail through a forest leading to the observation of Buchenegger Wasserfälle descending into pools with a mesmerizing turquoise hue. In the summer you can go down from the observation bridge and bathe in the cool water. A great hiking route but with challenging sections for those looking for a short route but rich in nature.

title: Heerbrugg - St. Anton - Altstätten
short_description: Challenging day hike through forests and meadows, with mostly pleasant ascents into Appenzellerland.
long_description:
Heerbrugg is dominated by the castle, built in 1708 by Abbot Ulrich III of St. Gallen. Rebuilt after a fire in 1774. Owned by the Schmidheiny family since 1867.

On the hiking trail we climb up to the Hümpelerwald and reach üvia Bechtenrüti - Spitz - Mitlehn the hamlet of Steingocht. After a short rest, we continue uphill to Fegg, with a beautiful view of the Rhine valley and Appenzellerland, and on to the viewpoint of St. Anton. The panoramic view of the nearby Alpstein massif and the vast Lake Constance, which on a clear day reaches as far as the German Feldberg in the Black Forest, rewards the effort of the ascent.
The descent to Altstätten takes us through the Rundenwald forest to Buschel with the Hoch-Altstätten castle ruins. However, the last remains of the walls are covered in the ground and thus protected from final decay. We descend through the wild and romantic Mültobel. In the forest park we reach the bottom of the valley and our hiking destination. A stroll through the historic little town of Altstauml;tten should definitely be planned.

title: Haldensee Round
short_description: Beautifully situated hike around the Haldensee lake with many vantage points and a great panorama of the mountains! If you want to enjoy your peace and quiet, this is the right place! The path along the clear water invites you to dream!
long_description:
The short but scenic tour starts at the well-kept Hall car park. From there you get directly onto the circular trail around the Haldensee. In addition to pure nature, cows and green meadows, you walk along a well-kept gravel path that offers many incredible viewpoints. From the view of the mountains to the crystal-clear water of the Haldensee, the tourers are offered a beautiful spectacle of nature. The difficulty level of the tour is very low, as there are only very short and easy uphill and downhill sections. You can either enjoy yourself at the Tauschers Alm or find shelter on the outdoor terrace of the Hotel Via Salina, which is comfortably located on the lake promenade. During the tour you will be able to recognise and admire other beautiful spots. It is also possible to cool off directly in the lake at several places. In addition, there is an official open-air swimming pool, which offers relaxation and cooling for a small fee.
Have fun on your leisurely hike!

title: Winter hike through the Isar meadows near Grünwald
short_description: Intact riverine floodplains alternate with the artificial construction of a weir.
long_description: The Isar above Grünwald shows its original side. We walk through the undergrowth on narrow paths. We experience an intact floodplain landscape with many small tributaries. We cross these on a few bridges. At the Baierbrunner weir we can see a modern river regulation. Some gravel bars offer interesting views of Grünwald Castle and the Isar itself. Further upstream we reach the Georgenstein. Here you will find particularly treacherous rapids in the river, which the rivers found very difficult to cope with. Therefore, a dam was built between the bank and the rock to steer the course of the river into more suitable channels. This is also where the main road from Augsburg to Salzburg crossed the Isar.

images.caption: Winter hike in the Munich region: Winter hike through the Isar meadows near Grünwald

title: Altstätten - Crystal Cave - Rüthi
short_description: Family-friendly, easy day tour to the natural phenomena Kristallhöhle and Hirschensprung.
long_description:
The eventful history of Altstadt begins in 853. The Marktgasse with 18th century houses is worth seeing. We walk through the outer quarter of Erlen to the medieval forest chapel with glass paintings by Ferdinand Gehr. Through the vineyards on the southern slope of the forest hill, which produce the famous forest wine, we reach Chrans and Fuchsnest. Continue to Strick and through woods and meadows to the village of Eichberg with the famous Hoch-Chapf vineyard. Via the beautiful timber-framed bridge we reach the Eichberg adventure zoo (admission by prior arrangement only).
In the hamlet of Süsswinkel überqueren we cross the Aubach and hike über Hard - Dürrenbach - Waldhütte - Fuchsplatz - Chessiloch to the crystal cave Kobelwald, first mentioned in 1682, which presents itself very impressively. A guided tour lasts about 30 minutes. No special equipment is required. Please note opening times.
We continue on the forest path downhill to the hamlet of Grubach to Kobelwald. We hike through the forest via Steig - Stieg - Rehag to Hirschensprung. For a long time, this striking rock cut formed the language border between Alemannic and Romansh. Numerous place names of Romansh origin, such as Plonen or Lienz, still bear witness to this. The destination of our hike, Rüthi, is soon reached. Two major fires in 1887 and 1890 decimated the village by more than 300 people.

title: Mount Belukha
short_description: The White Pearl of Altai – Mount Belukha – Altai's highest peak (4509m). Belukha – is an eternally white princess from head to toe and the mother of Altai's most full-flowing river – the Katun.
long_description:
The white jewel of Altai – Mount Belukha – Altai's highest peak (4509m). Belukha – is the eternally white Russian-Kazakh princess from head to toe and the mother of Altai's most full-flowing river – the Katun.
  The white crown of Altai – Belukha is not for everyone, but those who conquered it can consider themselves to have been to Altai and most likely even to Kazakhstan. The border between Russia and Kazakhstan just runs along the top of Belukha, but the ascent begins from the Russian side. Kazakhstanis catch up, make your way to Belukha and we will meet you at the highest summit of the region.
 .
Belukha is divided into western (4435m) and eastern (4509m) peaks. After climbing more than 110km of serpentine route, reaching its summit, a sacred place of the locals, one can also divide life before and after the ascent. And this so deep insight into one's personal life is helped by a 12-day hiking tour of one of the highest and most unspectacular mountains in Russia.

title: Walking from the Hohen-Schwangau Castle parking lot to the Marin Bridge overlooking Neuschwanstein Castle
short_description: An organized walking path leading to the Marienbrücke from which a unique and wonderful view of the famous Neuschwanstein Castle
long_description:
This itinerary starts from the large parking lot at the foot of Hohen-Schwangau Castle in Busan (P4). The route is not particularly long, but it partly includes walking uphill with a reasonable gradient (cumulative ascent of about 165 meters). The highlight is of course the spectacular view from the bridge of Neuschwanstein Castle and the gorge in the valley - definitely worth the reasonable effort as it is actually the most spectacular accessible view of the castle.
The walk is on an orderly and paved path and is therefore suitable in principle for walking with prams, but you have to take into account pushing uphill.
Since it is a one-way route, the distance as well as the walking time shown on this page are for one direction only, the walking time on the way back is slightly shorter than the way there since it is downhill.

title: Spaziergang auf den Hochholder
short_description: Walk up the "local mountain" of Akams near Immenstadt.
long_description: This easy hike starts in the tranquil village of Akams and leads through green meadows to a small peak called "Hochholder". From there you have a great view of the Allgäu Alps. This short tour is particularly suitable for families with children.

title: Brecon Beacons Horseshoe - Showcase Route
short_description: This is a fairly strenuous hiking route that takes you past gushing waterfalls, along stunning ridgelines, and up to the highest points in the park: the Brecon Beacons.
long_description: This route is a true showcase of the Brecon Beacons most beautiful parts. It meanders along some of the prettiest and least-visited waterfalls in the whole park — the Blaen y Glyn waterfalls — before shooting you directly up onto the towering Bwlch y Ddwyallt ridge. From here, the route follows the ridgeline, up and over the peaks of Fan y Big, Cribyn, Pen y Fan and Corn Du, before bringing you back down the opposite end alongside the shores of the now-empty Upper Neuadd Reservoir.

title: Toggenburg High Trail (Section 2)
short_description: Day 2 - Hike on the 2nd stage of the Toggenburg Hiking Trail
long_description:
The next morning the view widens to the west. On the ridge of the Glattchamm, the well-marked mountain trail branches off to the area of the Tritt, which demands our full attention. A steep descent then brings us to the rock faces of the First. Past the Flügenspitz, our path leads to the Vorder Höhi. In Schwisolen we branch off and reach Alp Hüttlisboden and the Furgglen alpine restaurant at the foot of the Gulmen. On a gravel road we go through a nature reserve - a high moor full of dwarf birds and interesting flora - to Hinter Höhi. Slightly downhill, the road takes us to the north side of the Mattstock, before a last steep ascent to the alp Oberchäseren, from where you can enjoy a dreamlike view of the Glarus Alps.



.

title: From Horto to Corcovado and Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon
short_description: Hiking through Tijuca Forest, passing by Horto waterfalls and climbing to Cristo Redentor on Corcovado hill, ending at Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon.
long_description: The route starts on the right side of the Jardim Botânico. At the beginning, we get up through the sidewalk where the houses of the city are disappearing giving way to a dense tropical forest. Just ahead, it will find the beginning of the trail to the waterfalls. Following the trail, it arrives at the first waterfall and continuing on the side trail we can find the second and highest waterfall. Following the signs of the park that towards to Corcovado Hill, you have a trail up on a natural path until you reach an asphalted street. Continuing straight ahead and with several beautiful views of the city, you get to the train station that takes up to the monument of Cristo Redentor. There starts the down trail to Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon through the another natural path inside the forest. At the end of the trail, you reach the Jardim Botânico street and crossing the street just ahead, you reach Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon, where it is worth drinking a delicious coconut water.

title: Toggenburg High Trail (Section 3)
short_description: Day 3 - Hike on the 3rd stage of the Toggenburg Hiking Trail
long_description: In the morning, it is worth climbing up to the Speer, the highest Nagelfluh peak in Europe at 1950 m.ü.m.. The actual Toggenburger Höhenweg bypasses the well-known peak östlich. After the descent über's Leiterli we reach Alp Bütz and the Elisalp plateau, another nature reserve. At the same altitude, we hike along the Wannenberg to the Schorhüttenberg and to the stage destination Tanzboden.

title: Bohusleden - Section 13 - Svarteborg to Lunden
short_description: The thirteenth stage of the Bohusleden takes you along an old country road from Svarteborg to Lunden.
long_description: This trail is very easy to walk. We walk about eleven kilometres along an old country road and through a large bog area, the Bredmossen;

title: Swabian-Allgäu Hiking Trail
short_description: The Schwäbisch-Allgäuer Wanderweg (SAW) has been leading since 1978 from the old Römerstadt Augsburg through a highly varied landscape to the Oberallgäu to Sonthofen at the edge of the high mountains.
long_description:
Forest and meadow sections alternate with river valleys and magnificent views. The trail varies from flat to steep, but is always easy to hike and also suitable for families. In addition to the natural beauty, this long-distance hiking trail offers cultural, historical and architectural attractions. Churches, chapels, monasteries and wayside crosses provide space for spirituality and refresh the spirit and mind. The trail partly follows old and new pilgrims' paths (e.g. the St. James and Crescentia paths). Worthwhile detours lead to the Oberschönfeld Folklore Museum and to Mindelheim and Kaufbeuren.
The 165 km long trail can be easily hiked in seven days. It is marked throughout with the blue St. Andrew's cross (blue cross on white background). The equipment, such as profiled shoes, a change of clothes or rain gear, should be appropriate for a multi-day tour. The trail reveals its special beauty especially in spring and autumn. On the newly erected standard signposts, a location number is attached at important points, which is a good help for the GPS device, but also for emergencies.

title: Brașov - Poiana Brașov via Kermen & Crucuru Mare Peak
short_description: This is one of the longer hiking routes that link Brașov to Poiana Brașov, or to Postăvaru peak and the same name cabin. It offers some nice landscapes, but also some challenging parts.
long_description:
The route starts pleasantly, at the edge of Kermen Hill. Climbing through the beech forest is an opportunity to dive deep into leafy carpets, admire a few towering trees, and watch the sun playing through the branches.
The hike initially advances in a slight ascent until the forest suddenly clears, unveiling the only belvedere area on the route. Then, the leafy path turns into a path marked by tree roots; this is where the beeches begin to thin out to be replaced with fir trees. The ascent gets increasingly steeper, before reaching the point called "La Amvon" - a rocky cliff resembling a pulpit.
At one point, the route meets the marked path that comes from the left, from Crucuru Mic. Although you're just a quarter of the way through, the general impression might be that you've been walking for a long time. At least from now on, there are no more steep sections.
The forest is already predominantly coniferous, the air becomes a bit colder. After about 1 km, you meet the "Blue Road", which comes from Răcădău and also goes up to Postăvaru.
The route continues at ease through the forest. You might meet other hikers or mountain bikers. Sometimes, animal tracks become visible on the path. Crucuru Mare  Peak - a possible landmark - is barely noticeable, only marked by a post. In winter or at the beginning of spring, this is the point where the snow gets more serious. The last 3 km to Postăvaru Cabin gradually make the transition from the quiet and relative wildness of the hiking route to the noise and congestion specific to the slopes of Poiana Brașov,

title: Zauberhafte Schneeschuhtour im Lechtal bis zum Hahntennjoch
short_description:
Diese atemberaubend schöne Tour nimmt euch im Winter auf eine Reise ins Schneeparadies mit. Schnallt eure Schneeschuhe unter die Füße und lasst euch verzaubern von der wundervollen Szenerie der Lechtaler Berge.
Translate to English
long_description:
Auf dieser zauberhaften Schneeschuhtour werden eure Schneeträume wahr. Ihr erlebt alles, was man von einer Wintertour erwartet: glitzernden Schnee, gepuderte Tannen, weiß-glasierte Bergriesen so weit das Auge reicht. Mit den Schneeschuhen unter den Füßen und einem Paar Wanderstöcken kommt ihr sicher am Hahntennjoch an. Die ganze Strecke ist von Anfang bis Ende in ihrer magischen Winterszenerie nicht zu übertreffen. Wer im Lechtal das volle Winterglück erleben will, der darf diese Tour nicht missen.
Translate to English

title: Westmill, Aspenden and Cherry Green loop
short_description: A circular route on mainly quiet road through various small villages.

title: Beycik - Cirali
short_description: Located on the Lycian Way, the famous road of Antalya, the starting point of this route is Beycik and extends to the coast of Antalya.
long_description:
The route is located on the Lycian Way, which is definitely on the list of nature and yürüyüş enthusiasts.
This route, which is quite long, can be considered as a difficult route and requires a lot of attention and care like every Lycian Way stage. Starting from Beycik, this route connects to Irali via a road that covers various track difficulties and levels. The route, which leaves you in the nature, first stops at Ulupınar. At the same time, the route requires actions such as crossing the main road in the Ulupınar bölge and crossing the stream after leaving Ulupınar behind. At the end of this route, which also includes viewing hills and camping areas, you have the opportunity to take a breather on the coast of Çiralı.
Depending on your condition and the breaks you will take, you can also spread this route over more than one day and develop a more relaxed and enjoyable route plan.

title: From Jungholz to the Wertacher Hörnle
short_description: Promising hiking tour to a worthwhile summit in the Oberallgaeu.
long_description: Our hike takes us from Jungholz in Tirol to the 1695 m high Wertacher Hörnle in the Allgaeu Alps. Here we hike mostly on narrow meadow paths and groomed hiking trails with easy to medium ascent to the summit. On the way we enjoy the beautiful views to the Upper and Eastern Allgaeu alps.

images.caption: Verweilen am Gipfel des Wertacher Hörnle
Der Ausblick vom Wertacher Hörnle in die umliegende Bergwelt
Auf dem Gipfel des Wertacher Hörnle

title: Kongevegen from Hå Old Vicarage to Varhaug Old Churchyard
short_description: Follow the King’s Road along the beautiful Jæren coastline
long_description:
Many say the trip along Kongevegen, “the King’s Road”, is the jewel in the crown of the Jæren coastline. The journey is a walk through Jæren’s history along a route traveled for hundreds of years. Along the way, visit some of the area’s most well-known landmarks and enjoy close contact with the landscape which is unique in Norway.
In the past all traffic followed Kongevegen along the coast. In recent times the main roads have been moved away from the water to protect the nature. From Varhaug Old Churchyard to Hå Old Vicarage, a stretch of 8.5 kilometers, you can take in wonderful scenery while visiting Obrestad Lighthouse, Obrestad Harbor, and Grødaland Museum.
The trail can be hiked in either direction, in smaller parts, or out-and-back. The churchyard is the northern end of the hike to Kvassheim (8.8 kilometers).

title: Canions Trail in the Chapada dos Veadeiros
short_description: The Cânions Trail explores the other beautiful landscapes formed by the Rio Preto and is one of the most beautiful trails of the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park.
long_description: This trail runs through the interior of the Park, through its beautiful vegetation and presents adventurers with impressive waterfalls and c&acircions. The trail starts at the Tourist Service Centre, near the entrance to the Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park, in Alto Paraíacute;so de Goiás, but precisely on the outskirts of the village of São Jorge. The trail is well signposted with red arrows and it is not necessary to hire a guide. The number of visitors on the trail is restricted, so start early and avoid holidays and weekends. Remember to bring cash, as access to all of PARNA's trails costs R$ 18 per person.

title: Walking route Bulskampveld estate
short_description: This route is 10 kilometres and takes about 2.5 hours.
long_description: The Bulskampveld is a 230-hectare nature reserve consisting of heathland, deciduous forests, fens and sand flats. It is a beautiful area where you can unwind. There is also a beautiful castle with a herb garden on this territory. There are more than 400 species of herbs in the herb garden.

title: Årsnesstølen
short_description: Visit an idyllic hideaway lake
long_description:
Årsnesstølen is a hidden treasure that is often forgotten in the eagerness to reach the more famous sights along Gaularfjellet. The small wooden farm houses with grass roofs are situated next to the calm Skardvatnet Lake. Through thousands of years the glaciers have shaped and grinded the steep, black mountain sides that surround the lake and created a green oasis. During the summer the fields surrounding the lake are dotted with white “myrull”, a cotton-like flower.
The trail is easy-going, but uphill. The area around Årsnesstølen and Skardvatnet Lake is a perfect place to pitch your tent for the night.
The lake is a great spot to set up camp for a night.
Near Sande on the the Sunnfjord side of Gaularfjellet, Villa Åmot offers a unique cultural experience. In Jølster and Førde you will find both self-catering apartments and hotels. 
Hov Hyttegrend offers cabins and facilities for tents, as well as shuttle services to Fossestien every morning in the high season.
Flatheim Farm is a traditional B&B. They offer comfortable beds and facilities for camping, as well as guided trips and a summer café with local refreshments.
In Balestrand you can find a choice of hotels, B&Bs and self-catering apartments. Historical Kviknes Hotel was the favourite of famous painters in the 1800s.

title: Hiking up the Siplingerkopf in winter (1,746 m)
short_description: A short and easy hike for those wanting to stretch their legs a little during the winter months.
long_description:
Snow conditions on the day will dictate whether you'll want to put on pair of trail spikes, snowshoes, or just your boots. 
The trail is evidently very popular with ski-tourers and so the snow was quite compacted and hard when I visited, but I'd imagine the going to be very slow if you attempted this after fresh/heavy snowfall. Check snow conditions using the Outdooractive Avalanche Report.

title: Niederwald - Egga - Fiesch
short_description: A leisurely hike through meadows and forests from Obergoms to Unnergoms.
long_description: The trail leads from Niederwald on a beautifully situated hiking path past the St. Anna Chapel to Fiesch. From here it is not far to Fiesch.

title: Westmill and Roman Road
short_description: A circular walk on, mostly, quite roads.  If you are looking for an easy countyside walk and a bit of history, this is for you...
long_description: This walk passes Button Snap which is a 17th-century cottage, that has been associated with the writer Charles Lamb.

title: Bohusleden - Section 15 - Vaktarekullen to Holmen
short_description: The fifteenth stage of the Bohusleden trail leads from Vaktarekullen through a beautiful lake landscape to Holmen.
long_description: We start our hike on Vaktarekullen in the middle of the Kynnefjäll nature reserve. The easy trail leads past several water bodies, such as Lake Stora Holmevatten, to Holmen, a small settlement by Lake Stora Kornsjön.

title: FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path (Tour 3)
short_description: A tour in Brandenburg specially adapted to the needs of cyclists and inline skaters. Good asphalt conditions and no cars make this tour perfect for families and beginners. This section of the trail network is the perfect introduction to the world of long-distance cycle paths and inline skating routes.
long_description: The FlaemingSkate cycle and skate path (Tour 3) is one of the sporting attractions in the region. You can join the route at various places, the circular route is well signposted throughout. There are some interesting sights along the way, such as the Zinna Monastery, great nature and, of course, the beautiful town of Jüterbog, which is our starting and finishing point. At just under twelve kilometres, this stage is only a small part of the FlaemingSkate cycle and skate route, which at just under 100 kilometres is the longest continuous route of its kind in Europe.

title: Along Lake Lugano to Monte Brè
short_description: The hike first leads along Lake Lugano to the fishing village of Gandria. From there, a not too steep forest trail leads up to the village of Brè Paese and the summit of Monte Brè.
long_description: The first section of the hike offers one postcard motif after another: Views of the lake, old stone houses, rocking fishing boats and a colourful array of flowers. During the climb to Monte Brè, the chestnut forest takes away from the view, but is pleasantly cool in summer. A detour to the village of Brè Paese is worthwhile if only for the fresh fountain water in the village square. At the summit of Monte Brè, a breathtaking view of the surrounding lake and mountain world awaits us.

title: Classic circuit up to Piatra Dragoslavelor, Leaota Mountains
short_description: The climb to Piatra Dragoslavelor, starting from Dragoslavele, Argeș county, is one of the few classic routes in the Leaota Mountains. Plus: it boasts rich scenery and accessible paths for almost anyone who wants a mountain hike.
long_description:
For those who do not dare to climb to the highest peaks in Leaota, this is one of the recommended routes. And for mountaineers, this can be a warm-up or training route.
Although you don't reach impressive heights, the route can still impress with beautiful panoramas and a few more challenging sections, especially a steep gravel segment. In winter, crossing the gravel might be easier, because you can draw out steps.
In autumn, this route rewards you with a display of every possible autumn colors you can think of, as it runs mostly through deciduous forests.

title: Crossing Petrópolis - Teresópolis: Day 3
short_description: The crossing between the two mountain cities of Petrópolis and Teresópolis in Rio de Janeiro is one of the most famous in Brazil and is also considered one of the most beautiful;
long_description:
Included in the National Park of Serra dos Órgãos - PARNASO - the recommended duration of the Traverse é of 3 days, so that you can take greater advantage of its stunning landscapes. There is a total distance of 30 kilometres between the two sites, reaching an altitude of 2,275 metres.
The third day of the Traverse consists only of the descent from Pedra do Sino to the Teresópolis headquarters of the Park. There are approximately 11 kilometres of descent with beautiful views of the city of Teresópolis and the Parque Estadual dos Tresós Picos. There is also the possibility of joining 2 more trails at the end of the course, towards the Park headquarters: the trails 360° and Mozart Cat&atildeo. There are about 2 kilometers more of walking and 2 beautiful viewpoints to contemplate the beautiful Serra dos Órgãos and the city of Teresópolis.

title: Explore ”Poiana cu schit”, a hidden gem near Iași
short_description: The walk to ”Poiana cu schit” (The Clearing with Ruins), this hidden place in the Boroșești forest, close to Iași, is rarely recommended to anyone. In part because, although marked, the route seems rather wild and deserted.
long_description:
The route starts from behind the Bârnova train station, advancing the Bârnova Sanatorium Church, then towards the former Bârnova Cottage. The route goes only through the forest, on an easy-to-discern path, but not one very popular with hikers or trekkers.
Closer to the clearing, you'll also see a board with the local Forestry Department logo.
Of course, the clearing is the focal point of the walk. On a nice day, this is a good place to relax and find peace of mind. The 30 sculptures resulting from the sculpting camps organized here in the 80s are spread throughout the clearing. For a better orientation, check out the weathered panel with the location of the sculptures. At one edge of the clearing are the ruins that give the name of the place; they are what's left of a 14th-century church.
The clearing is also classified as a botanical reserve, for the many species of rare plants identified here. However, none of them are signposted in any way, so the hiker has to make do with his own knowledge or maybe even an app that identifies the plants.

images.caption: A group of sculptures in the clearing

title: Tour through the Jozani Forest
short_description: The tour takes us through the Jozani National Park and the mangrove forests of Zanzibar, where we also see the different species of monkeys that live in Zanzibar, some of them only in the Jozani National Park.
long_description:
Our tour through Jozani Forest, the last remaining forest area in Zanzibar, starts at the main building of the national park. We first walk along a path through the forest where we can see different species of trees, such as mahogany. The national park is also home to many different animals, such as crabs, birds and mongooses, but also cobras and green mambas, which only roam around after sunset. Most likely to be seen, however, is the red stumpy monkey, or "colobus monkey", which lives only on Zanzibar;
After the walk we return to the main road. From here, other narrow paths lead into the forest. On these trails it is very likely to encounter all three species of monkeys that live in Jozani Forest. 
On the opposite side of the road, we walk back to the main road.
On the opposite side of the main road is the path to the mangrove forests. Here we walk on a wooden footbridge across the marshland. Due to the tides, salt water is constantly being flushed into this area, but the mangroves are not susceptible to it. They store the salt in their leaves to extract nutrients from it. Furthermore, the mangroves prevent erosion of the coastal area through their roots and provide shelter for reptiles and amphibians.

title: Ramot Menashe Trail
short_description: A circular hiking trail of medium length in the area of the Ramot Menashe region. The route is rich in nature and Mediterranean landscapes.
long_description: The Ramot Menashe Trail is a hiking trail about 80 kilometers long, and as its name suggests, it passes through the territory of the Ramot Menashe region. The route is characterized by wooded Mediterranean landscapes and it passes near several springs.

title: Springs Trail
short_description: A short linear hiking trail in the Jerusalem mountains between Harbat Sa'adim and Ein Khandak passing by several springs, which makes it fun and interesting. This is a short-medium route depending on the ability of the travelers.
long_description: The Spring Route (or: the Spring Trail) is a walking route about 3-8 kilometers long characterized by the typical landscapes that characterize the Jerusalem mountains. Even the shortest route contains a large number of springs. You can walk part or all of the route. The recommended walking sections are Harbat Sa'adim - Ein Tamar - Ein Khandak (Sapphire Stone) - The Steph

title: Morro do Chapéu Trail
short_description: Uphill trek to the mountain that is the largest mountain in the Chapada das Mesas, the Morro do Chapéu, where we have a privileged view of the entire National Park and neighbouring towns.
long_description:
The way to the top of the Chapéu hill begins on a sandy road that during the rains can find itself very difficult to traffic. After finding a sign indicating the path of the trail, begins the ascent that has a certain difficulty by the slope of the terrain, besides having loose stones and that should be cause for attention to hikers. Also pay attention to snakes and buzzards that can be found on the path. During the rainy season the trail is almost always closed for safety reasons, especially if there is a possibility of lightning. Therefore, the ideal é travel in the dry period, from May to September.
After arriving at the top, which has the format of a plateau, é possible to make other walks to é some viewpoints that exist where é possible sight the city of Carolina and the River Tocantins, and & é other hills that are part of the impressive Chapada das Mesas. Really é a breathtaking view and an adventure not to be missed.
