title: GR 10: Pyrenees Trail
short_description: The legendary long-distance hiking trail G10, which connects the Atlantic with the Mediterranean along the Pyrenean ridge, makes the hearts of passionate long-distance hikers beat faster. You ll hike through one of the most beautiful mountains in the world.
long_description: The route from Hendaye to Banyuls-sur-Mer is one of the most famous long-distance hiking trails in France. On its way from the rugged Atlantic coast to the Mediterranean, you will pass tranquil villages, idyllic valleys, imposing ridges, magnificent mountain lakes and deep gorges. You will pass some of the highest peaks in the Pyrenees, experience overwhelming panoramas and landscapes, but also often very steep and long ascents and descents A good part of the route is in the Néouvielle nature reserve. If you are looking for peace and variety, you will find it here. An experienced hiker will need one and a half to two months for the grandiose trekking route.

images.caption: Tutte le forme e i colori che si possono incontrare sui Pirenei

title: In four days over the Nagelfluhkette
short_description: We have been dreaming of hiking from Immenstadt to Hittisau, always along the ridge of the Nagelfluh chain, since last autumn. Now we have made this dream come true and experienced a really great hiking adventure: we hiked over a total of 14 peaks, and in between, of course, down again and again, through all the associated saddles. But always at respectable heights, between 1,451m (Mittagberg) and 1,833m (Hochgrat).
long_description:
To really enjoy this strenuous tour through the Naturpark Nagelfluhkette, we stayed overnight three times along the way: In the Kemptener Naturfreundehaus (Alphöhe), in the Staufner Haus (Hochgrat mountain station), and also in the Berggasthof Hochhäderich (directly below the summit!).And one more time then finally in the Pension Bals, in Hittisau.
This way we bought enough time on the way to be able to take pictures in peace and quiet and to get enough pictures for this report. Because the aim of our tour was of course once again to be able to present our hiking adventure in as detailed a daily report as possible and with as many photos as usual.
You can therefore find all the details about the individual hiking days in the respective daily reports.

title: दयारा बुग्याल ट्रैक
short_description: दयारा बुग्याल उत्तराखंड राज्य के उत्तरकाशी जिले में स्थित एक हिमालयी अल्पा इन चरागाह है जो एक सदी से भी ज्यादा से एक लोकप्रिय हाइकिंग और क ैम्पिंग गंतव्य रहा है।
long_description:
बुग्याल हिमालयी राज्य उत्तराखंड की खास भौगोलिक पहचान हैं। स्थानीय भाषा में बुग्याल का मतलब ऐसे अल्पाइन हिमालयन घास के मैदानों से है जो की बसंत ऋतू में मवेशियों के चरागाह के तौर पर काम करते हैं।
आमतौर पर बुग्याल साल के सभी महीनों में बेहद सुन्दर दिखते हैं। गर्मियों में हरीभरी घास और ठंडी हवाएं इनको पिकनिक के लिए बेहतरीन जगह बनाती है। बरसात में बुग्यालों की घास की चटाई और भी ज्यादा घनी और हरी हो जाती है। सर्दियों में जब बुग्याल सफ़ेद बर्फ से भर जाते हैं तो जादुई दुनिया जैसे दीखने लगते हैं। बसंत के मौसम में पिघलती हुई बर्फ के बीच में बुग्याल हज़ारों रंग बिरंगे फूलों से ढक जाते हैं।
दयारा बुग्याल भी एक ऐसा ही बेहद सुन्दर बुग्याल है। यह हाइकर्स और ट्रैकर्स के बीच में बेहद लोकप्रिय है। दयारा बुग्याल का ट्रैक बसंत और सर्दियों दोनों में ही किया जा सकता है। यह उत्तराखंड के उन चुनिंदा ट्रैक में से एक है जो सर्दियों में ज्यादा लोकप्रिय रहता है। सर्दियों में बर्फ से भरा बुग्याल इतना बड़ा हो है कि इलाके का आदि-अंत नहीं दिखता है। जहाँ तक नज़र जाती है वहाँ तक सिर्फ बर्फ ही दिखती है।
दयारा बुग्याल ट्रैक का आरंभ बिंदु रैथल गाँव हैं जो की समुद्र तल से करीब 12000 फ़ीट की ऊंचाई पर है और उत्तरकाशी शहर से करीब 40 किलोमीटर दूर है। रैथल गाँव से ट्रैक करीब 7 किलोमीटर लंबा है। ट्रेल पूरी तरह से बुरांश और देवदार के पेड़ों से ढकी हुई है। यहाँ पर ध्यान देने वाली बात है की क्योंकि दयारा बुगयाल इतना बड़ा है इसलिए उसके अलग अलग हिस्से तक पहुंचने के लिए कई ट्रेल हैं। दयारा बुग्याल से हिमालयी पर्वत-चोटी बन्दरपूँछ एकदम सामने दिखती है जो अपने आप में एक अनोखा अनुभव है। हाइकर्स बरनाला शिविर स्थल या नायता शिविर स्थल में तम्बू लगा कर रात गुज़ार सकते हैं। दोनों ही शिविर स्थल सुन्दर और साफ़ हैं। रास्ते में कई तरह की हिमालयी चिड़ियों की आवाजें सुनना और कई किस्म के पेड़-पौधे को देखना भी दयारा बुग्याल ट्रैक का एक और अतिरिक्त फायदा है।

title: Mirante do Caeté Trail (Prainha)
short_description: Light trail, safe and with an incredible view of the carioca coast. Meet the beautiful Prainha Park and discover one of the most beautiful beaches of the west zone.
long_description:
The trail to the Mirante do Caeté é an ideal walk for families and for those who want to get to know a different place in the city of Rio. The viewpoint offers a beautiful panorama of the carioca coast, with Macumba beach, Pedra do Pontal, Reserva, Recreio dos Bandeirantes, Barra da Tijuca and Pedra da Gávea.
The trail was closed for two years, but in March 2021 the Caeté viewpoint was restored and the trail reopened. Avoid weekends and holidays, as the place is usually quite crowded. Read the rules of conduct carefully and help maintain the site by not throwing rubbish on the trail and respecting nature!
After your walk, take the opportunity to sunbathe and swim in the waters of the beautiful Prainha.

title: Through the mountainous Jordan
short_description: A linear hiking route of medium length that runs along the side of the Jordan River and other points of interest
long_description: A varied and interesting itinerary in the southern part of the Jordan River, north of the Sea of Galilee. Along the way, flowing water, wild nature, diverse vegetation, animals, historical points of interest and more await you. Parts of the trip can also be done with the car.

title: Schwyz Panorama Trail
short_description: Varied and well-developed walking trail.
long_description: On this uniquely varied panoramic mountain trail, you will find various feeder transport facilities, many mountain restaurants and alpine huts, four mountain chapels, shelters and beautiful resting places with various fireplaces.

title: From Löffingen down the Gauchach Gorge to Döggingen
short_description: The route hike to Döggingen is a beautiful, easy tour and well suited as a family hike.
long_description: From Löffingen, we follow the path marked with a green dot and walk past the church (1) towards the children's playground. Here we turn left to the mini-golf course (2), walk right up to the festival hall. We leave the village via Haslachstraße and Talstraße. Turn left at the junction, right at the town sign and onto the Wilhelm-Engler-Weg (3). Follow this path for 3 km. After the Hartwäldle, we leave the path and continue left on a grassy path. At a field cross (4) we reach the asphalt path again. We walk along the Linden-, Gauchach- and Grünbergstraße through Unadingen towards the Gauchachschlucht. Outside the village, we follow the Burgweg to the Stehleskreuz (5). Here we turn left towards Gauchachschlucht (6), cross the valley and follow the path up to Döggingen. Just before the village, we turn diagonally left and follow the signs to the railway station. The train brings us back every hour.

images.caption: At the wayside cross we have a good view to the east of Döggingen and the Gauchach gorge.
A view into the Gauchach Gorge.
We start in the centre of Löffingen.
The Guggenmühle is a prominent point on our tour.

title: Scenic one-day hike in Bucegi Mountains: Bucșa & Strungile Mici
short_description: A super scenic hike on the western side of the Bucegi Mountains with wide and captivating panoramas over the Grohotiș Abrupt. It can also be extended to two days, with an overnight stay at the Strunga Refuge, to get the full experience.
long_description:
Ascents in the Bucegi Mountains that start from the Rucăr - Bran corridor bring you quite quickly - just over an hour of strenuous ascent - face to face with the imposing mountain walls.
The route to Bucșa Peak starts steeply through the forest; it takes you through a desolated area, with traces of both logging and ravages caused by various storms. After a few tens of minutes through this landscape, you come out into the alpine plateau. A short climb of a few gentler peaks brings you to Bucșa Peak - the first objective of the route.
Looking backward, you have a full view of Piatra Craiului Mountian; on the left, you can clearly see the Grohotiș Abrupt, the Strunga Pass, and the path that we will follow on the way back.
Wandering between Bucșa and Strunga, through the alpine plateau, all you have to do is enjoy the spectacular view, especially if the weather allows it.
The paths get more crowded near the Strunga refuge, due to the easy access from Padina - a popular destination especially among Bucharest residents.
On the way back, you follow the path just below the Grohotiș Abrupt - a forbidden route in winter. Avoiding many obstacles (boulders) at first, you pass over two sheepfolds, and finally, descend into the forest. The last segment, just after leaving behind the former Bângăleasa cabin, is steep and very rugged.

images.caption: Starting the ascent on Piciorul Bucsa
A tipical picture in the Romanian Carpathians, close to Bucsa Peak
Strunga refuge, panorama towards Padina Chalet

title: Snowshoe: High Fricken from Garmisch-Partenkirchen
short_description: This snowshoe tour to the Hohe Fricken (1940 m) gives us a long ascent, but at the summit we are rewarded for our efforts by a magnificent view. On the descent we pass the Esterbergalm, where we can take a break.
long_description: At 1940 m, the Hohe Fricken is somewhat higher than the neighbouring Wank. You need to be in good shape for the ascent. The ascent is very steep in places, so a solid ascent technique is a prerequisite. The descents are all quite steep and, depending on the choice of route, have a westerly, southerly or easterly exposure. This and the steepness of the slopes require stable conditions for our tour! There is also the danger of snow cornices on the summit ridge. Orientation is initially very easy, but from the saddle between the Hoher Fricken and the Wank it can become a challenge in poor visibility and if there are no tracks. The Esterbergalm is a cosy place to stop for a bite to eat on the descent.

images.caption: Daxkapelle on the ascent to the Esterbergalm.

title: Möggers border hike near Scheidegg
short_description: On this tour, we experience the heights above Lake Constance with magnificent distant views between Scheidegg and Pfänder. We start in Germany and also reach Austria during the round.
long_description:
We start in Oberstein and walk left into the forest at the end of the village. There we first turn right and then straight ahead to the Ulrichs Chapel (1). We cross the border to Austria unawares - you should therefore take your passport with you.
After the 1000-year-old Ulrichs Chapel, we continue uphill in the forest and finally downhill again to Möggers (2). There we enjoy a rest in the typical Vorarlberg village. Now we keep to the left and hike uphill across meadows. Through the forest, past the Trögerhöhe (3) and along the foot of the Hochberg, we continue via Schüssellehen (4) finally to the right on the Riedweg to Ried (5). From here you come uphill to Möggers and on the already known path back to Oberstein.

images.caption: The Allgäu brown cattle await us along our route.
There are many magnificent views along our tour. They range from the Pfänder in the west to the Nagelfluhkette in the east.
Many forest sections make the route a pleasant experience even in summer.

title: With Romans and Knights from Erlingshofen to Titting
short_description: In the footsteps of knights and Romans, we hike from Erlingshofen to Titting and back.
long_description:
On this hike, the historical sights are worth highlighting. Our path first leads us to the Brunneck castle ruins. It was built at the end of the 14th century by the Lords of Heideck and sold to the Hochstift Eichstätt in 1413. During the Peasants' War, the "Veste Prunnekke" was occupied and plundered, then served as a residence for some time before falling into disrepair after 1691.
In the further course of the hike, we move from the Middle Ages to Roman times by following the Limes for a short distance. Along this section we can not only look at the foundations of Roman watchtowers, but also visit a reconstructed border tower. It is the only reconstructed Roman watchtower in Bavaria and was built in 1992. A memorial stone near the tower marks the further course of the historical Roman border system.
In Titting, the former moated castle awaits us. It already existed in the 13th century, has an irregular octagonal ground plan with two towers and today houses a brewery specialising in wheat beer. In the Breustüberl we can taste the result.

images.caption: Titting in the direction of Mantlach.

title: On the Shebenik into the heart of the National Park
short_description: Lonely high forests, icy mountain lakes and, to crown it all, one of the most panoramic ridge tours in the Balkans - this demanding hike leads to the eponym of the Shebenik-Jablanica National Park. As a crisp day tour or a comfortable two-day tour with tent, you are on your way here in a beautiful mountain world that is still considered a secret tip even by Albania connoisseurs.
long_description: From the mountain village of Dragostunjë, this hike leads up to the high valley of the Shebenik massive on gravel paths and little-used trails, with ice-cold glacial lakes and a summit ridge that offers almost unbelievable views in all directions. Lynx and brown bears can only be seen with extreme luck, but proud eagles often soar through the skies here. The trail is only marked in the upper part, but finding your way is no problem, at least in good weather (see trail description). Apart from a few shepherds, there are usually no other hikers, even in high season - a secret that is well worth discovering, and panoramic views that compensate for the tough climb.

title: Georoute PN8 - Añisclo Canyon
short_description: A hike to understand the formation process of the Pyrenees
long_description:
A route that crosses the upper part of the Añisclo valley, a place that is not very popular because it requires a long excursion, but which has great geological interest. A high mountain route that allows us to observe many details about the deformation of the rocks during the formation of the Pyrenees.
In its final part, wonderful views of the Pinetanous valley allow us to understand the landscape of 65,000 years ago, at the time of the glacial maximum.
The upper part of the Añisclo valley allows us to deduce the complex tectonic structure of the Mont-Perdu massif, since glacial erosive action has carved out a deep canyon that leaves a succession of overlaps exposed. To access the upper part of the valley, it is necessary to start from San Úrbez (and take the PN 7 route) or to follow a steep ascent from Pineta and take the descent route (the opposite of what is described). On the other hand, the route allows us to get to know some of the karstic features of the massif (such as the resurgence of the Fuen Blanca), to make observations on the rocks (sometimes studded with small fossils) and to deduce the glacial origin of the valley, always in the middle of an extraordinary landscape, up to the Añisclo valley, which offers an exceptional view of the Pineta and Añisclo valleys.

title: Amrum Island Circuit
short_description: On an extended circular walk around Amrum, we familiarise ourselves with the small villages and wide dune fields on the North Sea island.
long_description: Our hike takes us once around the island of Amrum. The starting point is Wittdün, the place on the island most clearly marked by tourism. Founded in 1890 as a seaside resort, Wittdün has meanwhile developed into Amrum's most important ferry port. From here you can walk to the striking Amrum lighthouse near Süddorf, the oldest village on the island. The lighthouse can also be visited during the summer months. On the edge of the Amrum dunes nature reserve, we continue through the impressive island landscape. We are always accompanied by the calls and cries of thousands of sea birds that breed here on Amrum. Passing the village of Norddorf, we finally reach the Amrum Odde, the northern tip of the island. In the large bird sanctuary, wading birds and other animals can be observed very well. However, we are only allowed to visit the area with a guided tour and otherwise have to walk around it near the coast. The hike takes us along the east coast to Nebel, now Amrum's largest village. Here we can visit the St. Clemens Church, the Öömrang Hüs, the windmill and the homeless cemetery. Continuing south, we come back to Wittdün, where there are many inns and restaurants - an ideal place to stop after the hike.

images.caption: The hike leads through a wide dune landscape.

title: From Großdalzig to Pegau
short_description: This medium-difficulty tour lets us experience a typical industrial landscape of the Saxon Burgenland.
long_description: We start our tour at the railway station in Großdalzig, from where we follow the country road southwards and reach Großdalzig via a footpath. From the village square we pass the church and the fiedhof and after a few minutes we reach Tellschütz. Now we leave the road to Pegau and go left on the village road to the south and further east through the fields. We now follow the field paths to Wiederau, we pass two ponds on the right and continue to the village square. In Wiederauf we should not miss the baroque church and the castle in the same style. We finally walk on the road "Am Schloss" out of the village again and back into the field paths. First to the south in the direction of the transmission mast and then along the flood protection dam of the White Elster to Weiderroda we walk further along the millrace to Pegau. On Ernst-Reinsdorf-Straße we reach Mühlengraben and from here via Frankenplatz and Martin-Luther-Platz onto Leipziger Straße. We cross the Mühlgraben into the Leipziger Vorstadt. From here we take the same route back to our starting point.

title: Route planned on June 13, 2008
short_description: This hike takes us along hilly paths in the scenic surroundings of Untersteinbach. Along the tour we are repeatedly offered wonderful views of the Hohenlohe countryside.
long_description:
Our hike begins at the outdoor pool car park in Untersteinbach. First we cross the Ohrnbrücke, pass the open-air swimming pool, the mini-golf and camping site as well as the sports centre and follow hiking trail 11 to the left to the new sports ground and then straight on in the direction of Bühl. At the main road we turn right onto hiking trail 10. A few hundred metres after the water treading pool we come to a fork in the road. Here we deviate from our actual tour and make a detour to the Kalksklinge.
From there we go back along the familiar path, then continue to the left. We soon rejoin trail 11, which leads us uphill to the edge of the forest. Here you have a wonderful view over the Steinbach valley. Now head downhill and then turn left onto a gravel path. We hike for a long time through the forest, always keeping to the right, until we reach the edge of the forest and the vineyards. From here we can see the village of Renzen. The hiking sign „red dot“ shows us the way to the right until we reach the main road of Renzen. Follow this to the right, then cross the Ohrn and then the Landesstrasse.
This takes us to Altrenzen, where we keep to the left and continue to the wine village of Heuholz. The old wine press appears in front of us, where wine was pressed in earlier times. Here we keep half-right and get onto hiking trail 12, which we follow up to the „Umsetzer“. From there we have a wonderful view over the beautiful Hohenlohe countryside. In good weather, you can even see as far as the Katzenbuckel in the Odenwald.
We continue üalong the „Rot-Kreuz-Weg“ and hiking trail 12 until, following the „Rot-Kreuz-Weg“, we turn off into a gorge. We come across the sign „HW8“ (main hiking trail 8), which shows us the way to the Strohberg and the Herbenberg. Here we leave the „HW8“ and walk straight on through the village of Herbenberg to Simonsberg (naturist area). At the end of the path, we turn sharply to the right, walk downhill and come across a footpath. Walk down this path to the village of Untersteinbach. When we reach the end of the footpath, we turn right and come to the main road. Continue straight ahead until you reach Fleinersmühlenweg. After another 500 m, we are back at our starting point, the outdoor pool car park.

title: From Ehingen to the Urdonautal - Natour 2
short_description: On our hike we encounter a Fasnets figure and Stone Age finds. A view into the valley of the Urdonau rounds off this tour.
long_description: The idiosyncratic dwelling of an Ehingen original, the "Mühlener Dom", a Stone Age site and the cosy resting place "Gesundheitsbrünnle" are just a few of the waypoints worth seeing on our hike into the primeval valley of the Danube.

title: Erlbach circular walk near Markneukirchen
short_description: On this tour, little hikers can look forward to a nature trail and an open-air museum.
long_description: The nature trail, which starts in Erlbach, is particularly suitable for suitable for families. The tour is 13 km long and leads to the open-air museum in Eubabrunn with a view into the Schwarzbach valley. Via the The starting point is reached again via the Galgenberg/Schlosspenzelplatz.

title: Adventure trail around the Engelstock
short_description: This trail offers all visitors, families and schools, groups and associations a unique opportunity to walk leisurely along a beautiful circular path and at the same time learn something about nature and the area in a pleasant way.
long_description:
On the adventure trail you can hike and walk, linger and experience.
The adventure trail is not a dry educational trail, but it engages the senses with play and experience. At six thematic stations you will learn new and surprising things. The stations consist of various components: Information boards, small boxes with changing content on current events and game elements such as a turntable, puzzle, hand pipe, search game and riddle. Not to forget the resting places and fireplaces that are available in the immediate vicinity of the stations for cosy picnics.

title: Fichtelberg
short_description: The pleasant walking tour takes us to the Fichtelberg and the Illschwanger Höhe.
long_description: On this pleasant round, we walk up the Fichtelberg and the Illschwanger Höhe and enjoy magnificent views of the surrounding countryside. On the village square in Illschwang we can also admire the listed ensemble of the "old forge" (town hall) and the church. (town hall) and the church.

images.caption: The starting point of our Nordic walking tour is the picturesque village of Illschwang.

title: From Schönau am Königssee to Funtensee - the cold pole of Germany
short_description: This tour takes us over the Königssee into the Berchtesgaden National Park to the Funtensee - the coldest place in Germany. We walk from St. Bartholomä along the Königssee for a while, before we go through the Schrainbachtal and the Saugasse into the high altitudes of the national park. Once we have passed the Saugasse, it is only a few metres uphill to the Kärlinger Haus, which lies charmingly above the Funtensee.
long_description: This hike takes us into the heart of the Berchtesgaden National Park. The Berchtesgaden National Park is the only "Alpine" national park in Germany. It was founded in 1978 and covers an area of approximately 210 square kilometres. The national park not only aims to protect individual animal and plant species, but also to protect nature as a whole. Further goals of the protected area are the scientific observation and research of natural communities as well as the education and recreation of its visitors. It contains the Königssee, the largest body of water in the area at 521 ha. It has been able to retain its drinking water quality to this day. On its banks lies the small village of St. Bartholomew with its famous baroque church of the same name. The settlement first served the prince and canons of Berchtesgaden, later the Bavarian kings as a hunting lodge. The destination of the hike is the 1600 m high Funtensee, the "coldest" place in Germany. Here, at Christmas 2001, the lowest temperature ever measured in the Federal Republic of Germany was recorded at -45.9 °C. It remains unclear whether the forest-free environment is due to grazing or to the cold at this location.

images.caption: The famous baroque church of St. Bartholomä.
In a wonderful location above the Funtensee - the Kärlinger Haus.
In their splendour, the gentians that are still common here.
National Park Information Centre St. Bartholomä.
Again and again, insights into the wonderful diversity of alpine flowers open up at the edge of the path - here the alpine auricula.
The Watzmann - landmark and highest mountain in the Berchtesgaden Alps.
The Funtensee and the 2113 m high Ledererkopf rising behind it.
With a little patience, you can discover alpine marmots on the alpine mats.
The pyramid of the 2653 m high Schönfeldspitze - in the foreground St. Bartholomä.

title: Along the gazebo trail overseeing Băile Herculane resort
short_description: The route touching all the gazebos built above the Băile Herculane resort is an excellent opportunity for a short hike, as well as a very good reason to take a series of memorable pictures.
long_description:
The educational route called "In the footsteps of Empress Elisabeta" can be done in both directions - either starting from Hotel Roman, or from Izvorul 3 Diana. In the version shown here, the route follows Roman Hotel - Coronini Plateau - Zăvoi District but extends beyond the Diana spring.
The path climbs steeply westwards of Băile Herculane and has some beautiful sights: some gazebos - Ciorici, Red (Elisabeta), Yellow, Green -, the Munk spring, Coronini plateau in the Coronini-Bedina nature reserve, part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Information panels are placed next to each gazebo. The path that goes up from Diana spring to Foișorul Verde (Green Gazebo), then to Munk spring has been known since the beginning of the 19th century, being practiced by tourists who visited the resort in large numbers.

images.caption: Băile Herculane seen from Ciorici gazebo

title: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon)
short_description: The route to the highest mountain in Wales is a pleasure, especially on a clear day. The first half of the ascent is easy walking in beautiful countryside and the last few kilometres are a breath of fresh air over steep rocky slopes.
long_description:
Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon) is a must on a trip to Wales. It is also a great route to do with children: The way to the "Halfway House,” where an ice cream break is waiting, is quite easy. For small hikers, who find the whole route too long, there is the possibility to take the train approximately to the Halfway House and walk only the last (but also most difficult) part.
The first part of the ascent leads through green mountain meadows with many opportunities to rest on the way and enjoy the fantastic view of the mountains of Snowdonia National Park. The silence is only occasionally interrupted by the nostalgic whistling of the Snowdon Railway.
As you get closer to the summit, it gets colder and foggier. The landscape changes to steep cliffs next to the path. The number of tourists in trainers decreases rapidly.

images.caption: Panoramic view on the route to Mt Snowdon
Path to the summit of Mt Snowdon

title: A quick run up to the Säntisblick-Hütte from Lenzkirch, Black Forest
short_description: If you're looking for a short trail run in the Lenzkirch area, jogging up to the Säntisblick-Hütte viewpoint is a decent option. You could even hike it if running isn't your thing.
long_description:
Anyone requiring a quick burst of activity while in Lenzkirch can do worse than taking a run (or walk) up to the Säntisblick-Hütte (hut).
This uncomplicated route takes in some nice views over the town and its immediate environs and provides a good sense of the Black Forest's unique tranquility and amazing air.
It can equally be done in reverse. 
If you enjoy this, you might also like to check out my other route nearby: Trail running up Pflumberg from Lenzkirch, Black Forest

title: Hiking From Sad to the top of the 'White Mountain'
short_description: Enjoy some nice views of Amerat, Al Khuwair, Bawsher, Madinat Qaboos, and beyond on this prominent and well-known jebel in Oman's Capital Area.
long_description:
There are several ways to get to the top of the White Mountain, but this one was my favourite when I was living in the area and needed some exercise and a bit of quiet.
The addition of the road crossing to Amerat on the back of the mountain hasn't really impacted the views, which are still great.

title: Trilha da Pedra do Baú, Bauzinho e Ana Chata
short_description: The Pedra do Baú is part of a complex of rocky formations that also includes Bauzinho and Ana Chata, and an incredible trail with via ferrata and a stunning view.
long_description:
To the Pedra do Baú é it is mandatory to hire a guide, since the ascent requires safety equipment, such as helmet and rope. There are two entrances to the rock trails: the Bauzinho and the Chico Bento car parks. Starting at the Bauzinho car park, the trail is considered easy and self-guided.
From Bauzinho to the Pedra do Baú there is also a small trail that has an incredible view, but already á in a more difficult level. Much of the trail é made in a á area of Atlantic Forest in which the difficulty é only the relief of the region ão. When approaching Pedra do Baú, to overcome the large rocks along the way, the visitor ends up needing to use his hands a little. In the final part, one has to crouch inside a small cave, as well as a small stretch of via ferrata to reach the summit.

title: Around Saig
short_description: Wonderful views await us on this pleasant Nordic walking tour around Saig. With just under 6 km and around 140 metres of altitude difference, it is also well suited for beginners.
long_description: We start the tour at the tourist information in Saig. From here, we walk along the Vitenhofweg on the right, which we follow out of the village in the direction of Vitenhof. We walk across an open area from which we have a fantastic view of Saig, the Black Forest ahead and the Feldberg peak. Continue past the Vitenhof (1), straight ahead along the field path. We continue to follow the signpost with the green heart into the forest. After about 1 km in the forest, we keep to the left following the signpost and choose the slightly ascending forest path. Follow this for about 3 km, always following the signpost with the green heart, until you reach the upper edge of Saig (2). At the Hotel Alpenblick (3) we turn left and follow the road back to the tourist information office at the church. All in all, the tour with a length of just under 6 km and about 140 metres of altitude difference is easy to manage even for beginners. The route runs on easily accessible asphalt and forest paths that are well signposted.

images.caption: The tour around Saig offers views of the Black Forest heights.

title: Blue Round Brotterode
short_description: We walk near the winter sports resort of Brotterode with its long tradition of Nordic skiing and the ski jump on the Großer Inselsberg.
long_description: We walk from the car park into the forest. At the edge of the forest, a display board (1) marks the starting point of our loop. The double board contains interesting information about Nordic Walking and cross-country skiing as well as the route of our tour. From the board, we follow the blue signs with a white arrow to the right uphill. Soon we pass a nice rest area (2), which is slightly elevated to the left of the path. After the second crossing, a display board informs us about heart rate measurement (3). We continue along the well-signposted route. At the edge of the forest, a bench (4) with a wonderful view invites us to take a break. We continue through the beautiful mixed forest. Finally, we can take a rest at the refuge on the right.

images.caption: The second display board gives information on heart rate measurement and strengthening.
From the bench at the edge of the forest we enjoy a beautiful view.

title: Toroiaga Peak, Maramureș Mountains
short_description: A less popular hiking route in Maramureș, respectively in the Mramureș Mountains, nevertheless extremely pleasant and full of surprises one, in terms of trail accessibility and scenery.
long_description:
Along the way, you pass the former Măcârlău mining colony, near the Borșa resort (hence the name of the town - Băile Borșa). Of this, the industrial road that led to the mining galleries, some constructions, the entrance tunnels to the galleries, and a huge tailings dump remain.
Once you get past this desolate landscape, you enter the real trail, through the forest. Although the climb seems never-ending, it is worth all the effort.
From the top of Toroiaga, on a clear day, you can see the ridge of the Rodna Mountains and panoramas that go far, toward the border with Ukraine.

The path in the alpine plateau

title: Wümme Cycle Route
short_description: This cycle path in the Bremen catchment area runs for almost 260 km, always close to the river Wurm. Over roads with little traffic and through impressive moorland, you cycle partly in Lower Saxony and partly in Bremen through the foothills of the Lüneburger Heide.
long_description: On this trail we cycle on mostly flat, asphalted terrain along a well-signposted, low-traffic route. The tour can be divided up and is also suitable for day trips. In the nature reserve of the Lüneburger Heide, through which the cycle route runs, there are many places of interest and places to stop for refreshments. Here the paths are a little more demanding and no longer asphalted throughout;

images.caption: Moorland landscape in the Lüneburg Heath

title: Rimpers-Jossatal Tour - Schlitz
short_description:
Our tour is an easy hike through fields, woods and meadows on easily accessible paths.

Note: GPS-guided hiking!
long_description:
We start from the Pension Stürz in the direction of the cemetery, then turn right to the forest, after a short ascent the path leads back to the edge of the forest. Here you will find a bench with a wonderful view of the forest-fringed village of Willofs between Eisenberg and Steinberg. Now we walk through high mixed forest on the way to the Rimperser meadows. In these meadows stood a village until the year 800, which was completely destroyed by a war. The people who remained are said to have settled in the present-day village of Willofs. Even today, the largest part of the meadows is still owned by Willofs farmers. We hike through the valley, (where deer and
muffle herds can often be observed) until we reach the beech forest, turn left onto the old Udenhausen-Grebenau trade route past the old Mordeiche oak. At the crossroads, take a sharp left downhill through young spruce forests, past fish ponds to the Jossatal valley. Now walk to the right along the edge of the forest past the trout ponds and turn left across the Jossa to the Forellenhof, a pleasant restaurant with a café. After about 200 m on the main road towards Wernges, turn left into the Jossa valley, past the memorial sign of the former Rainsmühle (view of the Jossa valley), through the spruce-pine forest along the Jossa until you see the first meadows of Willofs. The old dry pit stood here until 1965. Now the trail goes up Jossa to Willofs.

title: Curonian Loop - bicycle tour around the Curonian Lagoon
short_description: This 3-day bike tour takes us to the three large waters of Lithuania: the Memel, the Baltic Sea and the Curonian Lagoon as well as through a historical landscape.
long_description:
This bicycle tour is a journey through time through the historical cities of East Prussia to the traditional regions of Lithuania Minor. The tour starts in Klaipeda. Then it goes over the Curonian Spit to Nida. There you will take a ferry across the Curonian Lagoon to the island of Rusné in the Memel-Nemunas Delta.
In spring and autumn millions of migratory birds gather in the region and it is said that there are more seabirds than people.
The picturesque cycleroute lead over sand dunes passing small fishing villages and old towns and to a deserted airfield. Along the route there are many opportunities to stop for a break.
You can plan a good three to four days for the route. You can stay overnight in hotels, pensions or camping sites.

title: From Rothaus near Schluchsee to the Mettmastausee lake
short_description: The gorge-like Mettmatal in the Upper Black Forest promises a beautiful hike along the torrent. From Rothaus, the source of the Schlücht, a valley path leads down to the Mettmamündung.
long_description: Our starting point is the car park at the local museum „Hüsli“ in Rothaus – known from the TV series „Die Schwarzwaldklinik“. From here, after crossing the connecting road, we walk through the western part of Brünlisbach. We orientate ourselves by the signposts of the Mittelweg (red rhombus). Leaving the village behind you, follow the markings down to the ski and toboggan runs/Mondhof of the Brünlisbach district (1). Follow a narrow meadow path along the edge of the forest and after a short stretch downhill you reach the Mettma. We cross it and immediately meet the Mettmatalstrasse and follow it through the forest to the Schaffhauser Säge (2). The paved path leads mainly through coniferous forest. We continue to hike down the valley to the right side of the Mettma. The last stretch to the Säge leads past green meadows. The name of the Schaffhauser Säge is a reminder that Pope Urban II gave the village of Grafenhausen to the monastery of Allerheiligen near Schaffhausen in 1095 – here the forests are under German sovereignty, but they are still looked after by Swiss monks. Immediately at the south side, the Mittelweg changes to a narrow, asphalted road for about 1 km due to the narrowness of the valley, but little traffic is to be expected here. The road takes us directly to the Lanzenfurt forest car park, which is located directly in a sharp left-hand bend. The car park has a small rest area with benches where you can take a break. From here we turn left on the beautifully laid out valley path in the direction of Klausenmühle. We cross the stream and hike comfortably downhill with barely noticeable feeling. The babbling of the torrent is our constant companion. After leaving the Klausenmühle on the right, we continue along the Kehrhalde and pass the Heidenmühle (3), an old sawmill. At this point the valley is crossed by a road. There is also a car park for hikers here. We continue along the valley path, always following the signs, and only a little later reach the Mettmaholzhütte. The beautifully situated hut with barbecue area and fresh spring water from the Heinrich Geisert fountain (4) invites you to take a break. The Mittelweg continues gently downhill towards the reservoir. If you observe the course of the stream, you can quickly see that the stream bed is becoming increasingly wider. With every kilometre we cover, we come closer to the artificially dammed Mettmastausee. A short time later we reach the dam wall (5) of the Mettmastausee. Here the water of the Wildbach is diverted and fed underground to the Witznau Schwarzastausee. We take the opportunity to walk around the reservoir and return on the familiar path to our starting point in Rothaus. However, it is also a charming alternative to continue hiking to the Mettmabrücke (approx. 5 km) and from there take the bus back to Rothaus: We walk along the valley path between the Mettma and the foot of the Erlenberg down to the Lochmühle. We immediately meet the connecting road between Berau and Riedern. After crossing the road, we continue through the forest and, without noticing it, pass the ruins of Mandach Castle. The castle lies on the slope to our left and is unfortunately not visible from the path. We walk further down the valley, still hearing the babbling of the Mettma to our right, and a short time later we reach the bus stop at the Mettmabr bridge. The bridge is located near the gorge below the Schwedenfelsen. There is a bus stop directly at the bridge.

title: Ankara Karagöl Nature Park Hiking Route
short_description: If you are looking for places to do nature walks in Ankara, you can try this route in the natural park phase
long_description:
Ccedil;ubuk Karagöl Nature Park, located 68 km away from Ankara city centre, is an important point for those who want to travel in Ankara and its surroundings. This area, where the natural beauty is felt more than enough and which also contains a volcanic göl, attracts attention in terms of tourism and recreation. 
This 13 km round-trip route, which you can complete in 4 hours, is only one of the beautiful routes you can do in this region. The route starts from Karagöl and ends in Karagöl again after the circular line completed on the trail. During your walk you can discover the natural beauties, flora and fauna of the region. 
Öz "z especially in the summer or autumn, when the leaves are falling, it's a route where you can capture beautiful photographs.

title: Israel National Trail
short_description: The extremely varied long-distance hiking trail Israel National Trail (INT) connects the towns of Dan in the north and Eilat in the south of Israel. It winds through impressive landscapes and makes the hearts of long-distance hikers beat faster. From rolling green hills and stretches of beach, to inhabited and agricultural regions, to impassable gorges and sand and stone deserts, there are diverse sections of trail to be found here.
long_description:
The Israel National Trail is one of the most beautiful long-distance hiking trails in the world, according to National Geographic. Over more than 1000 km, the Shivil Israel, as the trail is called by Israelis, winds through the Holy Land. The trail changes character several times: it offers unique and impressive landscapes as well as diverse nature - from rich vegetation in northern Israel and a Mediterranean coastal landscape around Tel Aviv to the suburbs of Jerusalem and the two imposing desert landscapes of the Judean Desert and the Negev. 
In the north, the trail is characterised by sometimes large ascents and descents, in the centre the trail runs through flat regions and along the Mediterranean Sea - with the exception of the rocky ascent to Jerusalem - and in the south of the country, often rocky and impassable paths lead through wadis and gorges as well as into the mountains around Eilat. Mostly the route runs mostly on easy to moderately difficult paths. However, there are also numerous climbing sections where you have to use your hands, such as in the Carmel Mountains or the Negev Desert.
The Israel National Trail avoids the big cities, with the exception of the coastal promenade, but towns are frequently crossed or touched upon, so that the supply of water and food is assured on large parts of the trail - except in the desert region. In the desert, on the other hand, there are extremely few opportunities to get water. Depending on the route planning, there are ten to thirteen night camps without water supply on the way through the Negev Desert. Here it is advisable to create secret food depots with water in advance or to bury them or to have them created or delivered by a so-called "cacher" or "service provider" 
Supply.  
The long-distance trail is not an easy undertaking. Those who want to hike the INT should be physically extremely well trained and well prepared. It is advisable to plan around six to eight weeks for a complete hike. The trail leads exclusively over Israeli territory and through all regions of the country except the West Bank, Gaza and the Golan Heights - safety first here too.

title: International Art Trail Hoher Fläming - Southern Route
short_description: Varied art trail with 17 art stations on the theme of "Settlement of the Fläming by people from Flanders" by six German and six Flemish artists from Belgium and the Netherlands.
long_description: The southern route of the International Art Trail runs between Wiesenburg and Bad Belzig without much altitude gain. Along the way, cow udders graze peacefully in the meadow, a pack of wolves has returned to the Fläming and the Resting Bridge turns everything upside down. The art hiking trail invites you not only to hike, but also to wonder Some works of art are monumental, others delicate and poetic. The southern route of the International Art Trail encompasses a broad spectrum of modern art and leads past a total of 17 works of art that can be discovered in beautiful forests and small villages, on flower-filled meadows or sometimes in the middle of a village pond. 12 of these works of art were erected along the trail in 2010 as part of a German-Belgian-Dutch competition Along the way, there are many beautiful views over the hilly landscape, with majestic castles and palaces towering above.

title: Horse Bowl Lake Track
short_description: This is a nature trail that leads to the very beautiful Ghoda Katora lake in Rajgir district of Bihar state.
long_description:
Ghoda Katora Lake Trek is a beautiful nature trail located in the city of Rajgir in the state of Bihar. It is believed that horses loved to drink the water of this lake and hence the name Ghoda-Katora which means horse pot.
The trail leading to the lake is currently about 7 kilometers long and is surrounded by lush green grass on both sides. There are also dense trees and flowering plants on both sides of the trail. The trail is almost flat from its starting point right up to the lake, but the path becomes gently sloping as it approaches the lake.
The difficulty level of this track is 'Easy'. It is suitable for all types of hikers whether experienced or new. The trail is well maintained and has wooden benches to rest along the entire path. Keep in mind that bicyclists, hikers, and horse-drawn carriages all use this same trail, so you need to be careful while hiking.
The end point of this nature trail is the beautiful Ghoda Katora lake which is surrounded by lush green mountains on three sides. There is a huge statue of Lord Buddha meditating in the center of the lake which gives a grand look to this lake. Boating is also possible in the lake and other facilities like restaurants, toilets, parking are also present in the area.

images.caption: Rajgir's Ghoda Katora Lake is a beautiful tourist destination. Bihar, India

title: Entdecke das spirituelle Erbe von Puno: Wanderung auf der Route Pachamama-Pachatata zur Isla Amantani
short_description: Entdecke die zauberhaften Pfade der Isla Amantani: Eine morgendliche Wanderung voller Schönheit, Kultur und Gastfreundschaft der Einheimischen
long_description:
Erkunde die faszinierenden Wege der Isla Amantani: Eine morgendliche Wanderung durch malerische Pfade, geschaffen von den Einheimischen der Insel. Starte den Rundgang von Pachamama, einem der Hauptdörfer der Insel. Folge den gut gepflasterten Wegen, die dich durch sanfte Hügel, terrassierte Felder und kleine Gemeinden führen.
Genieße den atemberaubenden Blick auf den Titicacasee und die umliegenden Berge während du dich zum Dorf Pachatata bewegst. Dort kannst du eine Pause einlegen und das kulturelle Erbe der Insel erkunden. Erfahre mehr über die lokale Landwirtschaft, Traditionen und Rituale.
Nach einer kurzen Erholungspause setze deinen Weg fort und kehre nach Pachamama zurück. Tauche ein in die warme Atmosphäre der Gemeinschaft, während du durch die engen Gassen wanderst und die Gastfreundschaft der Einheimischen erlebst.
Es wird empfohlen, eine Nacht in diesem charmanten Dorf zu verbringen, da es viele Familien gibt, die Unterkunft mit köstlichen Mahlzeiten anbieten. Genieße das lokale Essen, lerne die Traditionen kennen und erlebe die einzigartige Kultur der Isla Amantani.

title: Böhmweg
short_description:
The Böhmweg is one of the oldest connections between the Danube and the Vltava. It was probably already in Celtic times that well-trodden footpaths led across the North Forest. When the path was paved with granite slabs in the 18th century, it could be used by covered wagons. Because of the dangers posed by highwaymen, thieves and wolves, merchants, missionaries, pilgrims, kings and emperors, artists, warriors and travelling people travelled in columns back and forth along the path. At the beginning of the 19th century, the Böhmweg lost its importance as a traffic route due to the construction of the Ruselstrasse, but revived as a hiking trail.
Today it leads the hiker in the footsteps of the old traders and travellers from the Danube valley over the mountains of the Bavarian Forest to Böhmen. Because of its relatively short daily stages and the mainly comfortable, wide paths, the Böhmweg is well suited for families and leisurely hikers. There is always plenty of time to visit the numerous villages and places of interest along the way.
long_description:
1st stage: Deggendorf – Bischofsmais (17 km, approx. 4 hours)
You can take the city bus from the bus station or the splendid town square in Deggendorf to Maxhofen, Zwieslerbruck in the direction of Tattenberg. From here, the varied hike leads up into the Bavarian Forest. The ascent to the Josephsbuche (480 metres of altitude) is rewarded by wonderful views, the idyllic landscape and the beautiful church in Greising (1691/92). The trail then descends through extensive forests and hedgerows to Bischofsmais to the pilgrimage site of St. Hermann.

2nd stage: Bischofsmais – Wei;enstein (7 km, approx. 2 hours)
The trail continues in a more leisurely fashion: From Bischofsmais, the trail first descends to Schlossauer Ohe. Then there is an ascent (180 metres) to the majestic Wei&szligstein castle ruins on the quartz rocks of the Pfahl. From the castle tower you have a wonderful panoramic view over the mountains. There is also plenty of time to visit the museum in the "Fressendes Haus" and to take a walk in the Glittering Forest.

3rd stage: Weißenstein – Zwiesel (12 km, approx. 3 hours)
Today's route from Weißenstein üvia Poschetsried and Schweinhütt to the glass town of Zwiesel takes you effortlessly through open cultivated landscapes. If you prefer narrow footpaths, you can also hike along the river trail through the idyllic Regental valley from Regen to Zwiesel. In Zwiesel you can visit the forest museum, the Catholic parish church (with magnificent neo-Gothic stained glass windows) or one of the glassworks (and the world's largest glass pyramid).

4th stage: Zwiesel – Bayerisch Eisenstein (16 km, approx. 5 hours)
Without major differences in altitude, today's route takes you through the extensive mountain forests of the Bavarian Forest National Park and Šumava. From the glass park in Theresienthal you first reach Ludwigsthal (information centre „Haus der Wildnis“ with outdoor enclosure) with the neo-Romantic Art Nouveau church and finally the forest enclave Zwieslerwaldhaus. There the hike continues through the extensive border forests to Bayerisch Eisenstadt, where the border railway station can be visited today as a border-crossing information centre.
Text: Tourism Association Oberbyern e.V.

title: From Memmingen to Bad Grönenbach
short_description: Despite extensive forest passages, we experience a very varied hike. Towards the end, we walk through the picturesque landscape around Bad Grönenbach.
long_description: First we explore a part of the old town of Memmingen. Through a very long avenue with many old Bäumen we reach the Stadtwald. At its other end we can climb a lookout tower, but the wide view is severely restricted by the Bäume. We cross the Woringen forest. If we dare to climb one of the high seats, we can enjoy a wonderful view of the surrounding landscape. Shortly before Zell we have to use a very overgrown section of path. Here we must not be tempted to choose another path. After a while, we cross a small tarred road behind the small village. Behind it, the path crosses meadows up to Ziegelstadel. Unfortunately, there is no signpost at the bottom, so we can easily miss the turn-off. If we have walked too far, we can turn left into the forest at the next sharp right-hand bend. After a few metres a small path leads up to the Pfaffenhalderundweg. Follow this to the north until you can end this alternative at a turning loop. This path can also be very helpful if the meadows are impassable due to grazing in summer. From Bad Grönenbach we follow the cycle path along the Kreisstrasse to the railway station.

title: Route of the Vienna City Marathon (VCM) 2024
short_description: The Vienna City Marathon will take place for the 41st time on April 21, 2024 and once again more than 40,000 runners from all over the world will be at the start in the various competitions to tackle one of the most beautiful marathon courses in the world.
long_description: The highlights of the marathon route are the section through the Vienna Prater, a monument to the sport of athletics and once the scene of Eliud Kipchoge's record-breaking marathon run. The route then leads along the Danube Canal and for the first time on the Ringstrasse towards Schönbrunn Palace, from where it heads back to the city center via Mariahilferstrasse and into the Prater for another loop. Then it's time for the grand finale on the Ring. The route leads past the magnificent buildings of Vienna before the finish line awaits after 42 kilometers between the Burgtheater and City Hall. A marathon route like a poem, but one that can only be run smoothly on the day of the marathon.

title: Short walking route Maasduinen
short_description: This walk is 10 kilometres and takes about 2.5 hours.
long_description: On this walk, you will discover the beautiful Maasduinen nature reserve. This area consists of beautiful land dunes formed during the last ice age. You walk through beautiful forests and along the heathland. You also walk a long stretch next to the Reindersmeer.

images.caption: The fens of the Maasduinen nature reserve

title: A trip to the cliffs at Yasmond Reserve on Regan Island
short_description: A light and flat hiking route (it is also possible to make it circular) leading through a forest to the impressive cliffs of the Jasmund Reserve
long_description:
This hiking route is nice, easy, flat and shady and actually leads to several viewpoints (some of which still require a relatively short climb) on the massive limestone cliffs of the Jasmond Nature Reserve in northeastern Germany. Through the many paths in the park, it is possible to turn the walk on the route into a circular one and even go down to the foot of the cliffs (a challenging path that naturally also includes an ascent of several meters on the way back).
For those who cannot do the route on foot, there are shuttles that leave from the park's official parking lot towards the visitor center, from where the walk to the cliffs is significantly shorter, but as mentioned above, the route is easy to walk. You can also check the possibility of doing one direction with the shuttle and one direction on foot.
Due to the fact that most of the route is flat and wide, it is accessible to strollers as well as wheelchairs, it must be taken into account that the road is not paved and that there may be slight slopes along the way and that some of the observation points are easily accessible only on foot.

title: Views of the North Chuya Range
short_description: The North-Chuisky Range is a rocky massif in Altai. Its length is more than 120 km and width averages 25 km. Its highest peaks are Masheev (4173), Aktru (4044), Kurkurek (3982).
long_description: Russia is known for its roads in many counties as not the most passable. But there is one such road – the Chuisky Tract in the Altai Mountains, ranked by National Geographic as one of the five most beautiful roads in the world. This road – Chuisky path leads travelers to Chuisky ridges, moreover, this is the road where the actor and Altai citizen Mikhail Yevdokimov passed away. The Northern Chuisky Ridge can already be seen from some of the viewing platforms around this road. All you have to do is to drive down to a convenient spot and take a brisk walk to the viewpoints shown on the map. The viewpoints offer views of the North Chuisky Range with its permanently white caps.

images.caption: Северо-Чуйский хребет и его местный проводник

title: Pfaffenwinkel Milk Trail
short_description: We learn everything about milk on this tour around the Schönegger Käsealm. At the end we can let off steam at the playground and watch rabbits, sheep, chickens and goats.
long_description: On this informative tour, you can learn everything about milk. The trail runs mainly on asphalt and is therefore suitable for prams and pushchairs. In between, a playground and a water pump provide variety. The highlight is the Schönegger Käsealm. There you can fortify yourself with delicious cheese sandwiches or cakes and let off steam in the playground. There is also a small animal enclosure, a herb garden and some play tractors!

images.caption: Signposting of the Pfaffenwinkel Milk Trail

title: Tageswanderung durch den Huayllay Steinwald in Pasco
short_description: Erkunde die beeindruckenden Felsformationen: Ein Tag im Huayllay Steinwald mit flexibler Routenwahl und Übernachtungsmöglichkeiten für ein unvergessliches Naturerlebnis.
long_description:
Entdecke die faszinierende Welt der Felsformationen im Huayllay Steinwald bei einem eintägigen Rundgang. Die Route bietet verschiedene Möglichkeiten, darunter der kurze Rundgang 1 und der längere Rundgang 2. Der kurze Rundgang enthüllt zahlreiche felsige Formationen, die Tier- oder Ortsnamen ähneln. Der längere Rundgang ermöglicht eine umfassende Erkundung des Reservats. Ich persönlich kombinierte beide Routen und erkundete auch abgelegenere Orte fernab der ausgetretenen Pfade.
Diese eintägige Wanderung bietet eine beeindruckende Erfahrung der natürlichen Schönheit. Es besteht die Möglichkeit, in Unterkünften im Herzen des Steinwaldes zu übernachten oder an ausgewiesenen Campingplätzen zu zelten. Bitte informiere dich an der Kasse über die genauen Modalitäten. Darüber hinaus befinden sich in der Nähe des Gebiets Thermalquellen, die zum Entspannen einladen.
Um dorthin zu gelangen, kannst du ein Sammeltaxi von der Stadt Huayllay nehmen. Erlebe die einzigartigen Felsformationen und tauche ein in die zauberhafte Atmosphäre des Huayllay Steinwaldes.

title: Route through the Belsky Forest
short_description: Run trough Belsky forest, 6km long trail for a good condition
long_description: The route is suitable for running and relaxing walks through the Belsky Forest near the center of Ostrava. The relax route is clearly outdated and suitable for every occasion. Most of the route is reinforced, it is not necessary to have special equipment. Forest is a well-visited place, if you want to be alone so better are early mornings or the evenings.

title: The Puy de Sancy from the ridges
short_description: This hike takes you to the heights of Mont-Dore between the Chastreix Nature Reserve and the Chaudefour Valley Nature Reserve, towards the summit of Puy de Sancy!
long_description:
In the heart of the Auvergne volcanoes, this route is one of the must-do hikes in the region!
Starting in Le Mont-Dore, you begin by going deep into the forest overlooking the village. This is where your ascent begins, a good warm-up! You then reach the top of the Capucin funicular. The route alternates between paths and some tarmac sections. After the Capucin salon, you continue on the GR30. The Puy de Cliergue, the Rochers de l'Hor, the Tour Carrée... the route follows the path of the crests of the Massif du Sancy with the Mont-Dore valley on the left and the Chasteix-Sancy nature reserve on the right. The panoramic views are omnipresent and the sound of cowbells can be heard below.
.
Once at the top of the Sancy station, you will have a few more steps to go to the summit (orientation table). Then turn left to take the other side of the Puy de Sancy and thus reach the village by another route.

title: Visiting Cemetery Bay, Muscat, Oman
short_description: A short but interesting hike to the old Christian graveyard next to Muscat with the added options of swimming, snorkeling, and fishing :)
long_description:
For those looking to do something a bit different, a trip to Sheikh Jaber Cove Cemetery - or 'Cemetery Bay', as it is also known - is worth considering and not nearly as macabre as it might sound. 
The graves are actually split between two coves (The eastern cove and the main beach).  Information is quite scant, but from what little I know, the graveyard dates back to the 18th Century and most of the graves belong to Commonwealth soldiers who fought in the First World War - though I don't know how they ended up in Muscat. 
The walk itself is pretty rugged and does require a degree of sure-footedness and even a little light scrambling, but it's relatively short and a novel way to spend a morning or afternoon, though you should check the tides beforehand. The reef in the main bay is also pretty good for snorkeling, plus fishing from the rocks is also an option. 
Sadly, the beaches and surrounding waters are not nearly as clean as they used to be, but the walk still manages to capture something of old Muscat's interesting past. 
If you like this route, you might also enjoy this other one nearby:
The Riyam-Muttrah Hill Walk, the C38, Muscat, Oman

title: A cable car ride and from there a trip to Sebeensee in Ehrwald
short_description: A magical panoramic walk from the top station of the Ehrwald cable car leading to Seebensee
long_description:
A magical hiking route with panoramic views towards the Alps and Mount Tsogeshfitz. After getting off the cable car (of course you can go up on foot as well) you pass an animal, small waterfalls and flowing water when the route ends at the magnificent Zevan Lake.
The walk to Lake Zevan is not particularly difficult, but still includes a number of climbs, but nevertheless, thanks to the variety of stopping and refreshment options on the way, it is definitely suitable for those in basic fitness. Further down the road there is a road that has been adapted for walking with baby strollers, but it must be taken into account that it includes climbs and it is not paved.
For walkers, it is recommended to continue from here and also reach the upper lake (Darchan Lake), click here to view the full route summary .

title: Hiking circuit: La Palme loop
short_description: An immersion in the past of La Palme
long_description:
<Dive into history by discovering the vestiges that made La Palme nationally renowned. From old salt pans to wash house and clock tower, this route offers an immersion in of Palme.<There are no particular difficulties on the route. You will find alternating covered and shaded sections with water if you have a dog.

You will cross protected natural areas.

title: Climbing Neuschwanstein Castle through the forest (the shortest way)
short_description: The shortest walking route leading to Neuschwanstein Castle through a wooded area
long_description:
There are two main roads that lead to the impressive castle from the parking lots at its foot, the walking route that appears on this page will lead you in the fastest way to Neuschwanstein Castle via a path that goes through a forest. The advantages for those who choose to walk this route are a saving of about 10 minutes, a lot of shade along the way (great on hot days), as well as usually less traffic and an incremental ascent that is 5 meters less than the one on the paved road. However, it should be taken into account that since it is a natural road and therefore it is not accessible to strollers, among other things.
Click here to view the second route which is slightly longer but paved.

title: Milford Road
short_description: This stunning route takes you to New Zealand’s most original spots and offers an impressive scenery for nature lovers and appassionate drivers alike. Among the places worth seeing is the fjord Milford Sound, New Zealand’s most important touristic site.
long_description: In the southwest of New Zealand you will find what is possibly the island’s most picturesque scenic route. It’s natural beauty galore on more than 120 km from the small town of Te Anau to the breathtaking fjord Milford Sound. Alongside the highway there are crystal-clear lakes such as the scenic Mirror Lakes or the beautiful lake Fergus. Besides, you’ll even get to see a few of the island’s mountains: At Homer Tunnel, for instance, you can discover Homer Saddle, a spectacular peak towards the end of the route.

title: 611 PAZIN - BERAM - PAZIN
short_description: A panoramic circular tour takes us across the Pazinski Grotto and picturesque landscapes to the Pazinski Waterfall, which can offer us  cooling down almost at the end of the tour.
long_description: The route to Beram and back starts in the immediate vicinity of the 13th century Pazin parish church of St. Nicholas, more precisely in front of the office of the Central Istria Tourist Board. From there, the path leads straight through the old town to the largest and best-preserved fortress in Istria, the Pazin Castle, which dates back to the 10th century. The castle is rightly called the symbol of the town of Pazin, because it is precisely to it that the town owes its well-known appearance. The path continues to the Vršić Bridge, which stretches across the Pazin Grotto, over this unique hydrogeological phenomenon, which served the French writer Jules Verne as inspiration for his world-famous novel "Matthias Sandorf". Then continue along the former "Pazinka" factory, which was the backbone of the Pazin economy in the second half of the 20th century. After bypassing the factory premises, begin the ascent to Gortan Hill, from where there are magnificent views of the entire area.Once you have passed Gortan Hill, turn off the gravel road onto the marked mountain path and descend through the meadows and forests to the road near the village of Beram. Do not be tempted by the picturesque scenery of this small village and do not turn left, but continue your hike on the path you are on and turn right. Pretty soon you will pass a secluded little church of St. Mary ("sv. Marija na škrilinah"), which has been welcoming walkers and hikers since the 15th century. Follow its invitation and take a look inside the church, where the "Dance of Death" is hidden, a widely known fresco by the master Vincetius de Castua.Continue your walk by climbing up the gravel road to the hillside, and then descend along the forest paths, into the Pazinčica valley, to the Pazinski krov ("Pazin Roof") waterfall, known to the local inhabitants, which shines in all its glory during the spring months and when the water levels are higher. After refreshment at the rushing stream, you climb back up to the old town via a dirt road and reach your destination via the streets of the town.

title: Hike in to Grizzly Lake camp site
short_description: Very beautiful hike to the campsite at Grizzly Lake. Carrying all the gear in might make it feel longer than it is, but the breathtaking views are so worth it.
long_description: This hike takes you up from the parking area on the Dempster Highway to the campsite on Grizzly Lake. You can hike in and spend a few days at Grizzly Lake or continue on to Divide Lake and Talus Lake. Each of these Lakes have campsites as well, and it makes for an excellent multi-day trip. When we were here at the beginning of July, there was still too much snow and these trails and campsites were not open yet.

title: Hondoq Ir-Rummien Hiking Trail
short_description: Scenic circular walk on the south side of the island of Gozo
long_description: Our hike takes us through several villages on the Maltese island of Gozo, where we marvel at two magnificent parish churches, among other things. From the forecourt of the parish church of Ghajnsielem, as well as along the entire route, we enjoy the panoramic views of the neighbouring islands. At the harbour of Mgarr we experience a veritable hustle and bustle of large ferry boats, small boats bringing holidaymakers and locals to the small island of Comino, and traditional fishing boats – like the Maltese Luzzu – in bright colours. We enjoy the atmosphere at the harbour and end our tour with a meal in one of the many restaurants.

title: Ascent to Neuschwanstein Castle on the paved road
short_description: The "classic" walking route leading to Neuschwanstein Castle, which runs over a well-paved asphalt road

title: Markgräfler Wiiwegli
short_description: This scenic hiking trail meanders leisurely through the gentle hills of the foothills of the Black Forest. We experience the fertile landscapes of the Markgräflerland on the Wiiwegli (High German: Weinwegchen) and let our eyes wander far into the Rhine Valley, the Vosges and the elevations of the Black Forest.
long_description:
Stage 1: Weil am Rhein - Blansingen (21 km)
We start our hike at the border triangle of Germany, France and Switzerland and head north from Weil am Rhein via Ötlingen, with an Inca café, to Binzen. The ridge of hills then leads us to the vineyards around Fischingen and above the Rhine, past the Schafberg, to Blansingen. The stage's finishing point lies a little to the east of the marked path and has several pretty frescoes to offer in St. Peter's Church.
Stage 2: Blansingen - Müllheim (19 km)
On today's stage, idyllic winegrowing villages await us again, first and foremost Schliengen, where we can take a look at the moated castle. We continue our way along the two famous Markgräfler wine-growing areas "Schliengener Sonnenstück" as well as "Auggener Schäf" via Auggen to Müllheim.
Stage 3: Müllheim - Staufen (19 km)
On a short circular tour through Müllheim, we discover the Markgräfler Museum, the Mill Museum, the historic wine cellar and the Amtshaus - and find the markings of the Wiiwegli again at the open-air swimming pool. Now the path climbs towards the Steinberg and we hike halfway up the mountain through the Eichwald forest over the Ehebach stream. Through the fertile landscape of the Markgräflerland, we continue past Britzingen and through Muggardt to Sulzberg, with the early Romanesque church of St. Cyriak. Now the Kastellberg and Fohrenberg await us until we reach Staufen im Breisgau through Grunern on the Eschbach.
Stage 4: Staufen - Freiburg/St.Georgen (25 km)
After visiting the castle ruins of Staufen, we walk along the edge of the forest and then enter the valley of the Möhlin, which flows through Ehrenstetten. On the vineyards on the Batzenberg above Pfaffenweiler, the Wiiwegli once again lives up to its name. Shortly after Ebringen, the trail alternates between vineyards and forest to Freiburg-St. Georgen. Here the official signposting stops, but we should not miss a detour to the city centre with its famous cathedral. The futuristically winding Schlossberg tower offers a fantastic panoramic view of the entire city.

title: Hiking trail Ta' Gurdan
short_description: About 10 km long, panoramic circular hike in the northwest of the island of Gozo, Malta's neighbouring island.
long_description: Our circular walk begins and ends at the village square of Gharb, at the foot of the church. With its baroque architecture, the church already leaves a special impression on us. On the way we discover interesting valleys and gorges, while we walk along the coast in a wind-formed landscape of limestone, which seems almost moonlike. In addition, we find many of the island's widespread fossils along the way. The fossilised remains of early creatures prove that the Maltese Islands are made up of sedimentary rock that formed under the sea over 20 million years ago. With a bit of luck, we can even enjoy a view of Italian Sicily, given the right visibility.

images.caption: Auf dem Weg zu den Klippen

title: संगमचट्टी-डोडीताल ट्रैक
short_description: उत्तराखंड के उत्तरकाशी जिले में 9926 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स् थित डोडीताल साफ़ मीठे पानी की अल्पाइन झील है । उसका ट्रैक संगमचट्टी गाँव से शुरू होता है और हा इकर्स के बीच बहुत लोकप्रिय है।
long_description:
डोडी ताल उत्तराखंड की सबसे खूबसूरत झीलों में से एक है। डोडीताल झील साफ़ मीठे पानी अल्पाइन झील है जिसमे हिमालयन गोल्डन ट्राउट मछलियाँ भी मिलती हैं।
डोडीताल ट्रैक सौ साल से भी ज्यादा पुराना ट्रैक है। ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी (1903) के समय से ही लोकप्रिय यह ट्रैक संगमचट्टी गाँव से शुरू होता है, जहाँ तक उत्तरकाशी जिले से टैक्सी या बस द्वारा पहुँचा जा सकता है। ट्रैक की एकतरफा लम्बाई करीब 16 किलोमीटर है।
ट्रैक का पहले दिन का पड़ाव बेबरा गाँव (7.8 किमी) या अगोडा गाँव (8.4 किमी ) है जो दोनों ही संगमचट्टी से करीब 8 किलोमीटर दूर है। अगले दिन अगोडा गाँव से बाकी बचा हुआ 8 किलोमीटर का रास्ता तय करने पर डोडीताल आ जाता है।
डोडीताल की ट्रेल घने खूबसूरत जंगलों के होकर गुजरने वाली एक हलकी लगातार चढ़ाई वाली ट्रेल है जो फिट हाइकर्स के लिए कोई परेशानी पेश नहीं करती है।
डोडीताल से अस्सी गँगा नाम की नदी है। डोडीताल में रुकने के लिए बढ़िया शिविर स्थल और एक सरकारी फारेस्ट रेस्ट है। झील साफ़ और ठंडी है और इसके किनारे गणपति जी का मंदिर भी है। यह ट्रैक बसंत और सर्दियों की बर्फ के मौसम दोनों में ही करना अच्छा है।

images.caption: संगमचट्टी-डोडीताल ट्रेल पर एक हाइकर, उत्तरकाशी जिला, उत्तराखंड, भारत।
डोडीताल झील के किनारे घास चरता हुआ एक जंगली घोड़ा, उत्तरकाशी जिला, उत्तराँचल, भारत।
डोडीताल झील के पास बना हुआ सरकारी वन विश्राम गृह (फॉरेस्ट रेस्ट हाउस), उत्तराखंड, भारत।
डोडीताल झील के किनारे पर भगवान श्री गणेश का मंदिर, उत्तराखंड, भारत।
डोडीताल झील की शिविर स्थल के प्रवेश से पहले सीढ़ियों पर लगा हुआ नोटिस बोर्ड, उत्तराँचल, भारत।
बसंत के मौसम में उत्तरकाशी जिले की डोडीताल झील का पैनोरैमिक दृश्य, उत्तरांचल, भारत।
सर्दियों के दौरान उत्तरकाशी जिले की डोडीताल झील का पैनोरैमिक दृश्य, उत्तरांचल, भारत।

title: कावनई किला ट्रैक
short_description: महाराष्ट्र के नाशिक जिले में बसे हुए शांत कावनई गांव का यह ट्रैक सह्याद्री पर्वतमाला के कम देखे हुए प हाड़ी ट्रैक में से एक है। करीब 3 घंटे ट्रैकिंग करके किले तक पहु ँचा जा सकता है।
long_description:
कावनई गाँव में स्थित यह प्राचीन किला अब अवशेष मात्र रह गया है। ज्यादातर ट्रैकर वाकी जंक्शन को आरम्भ बिंदु के तौर पर इस्तेमाल करते हैं लेकिन रेलगाड़ी से आने वाले लोगों के लिए घोटी रेलवे स्टेशन से लंबा ट्रैक भी संभव है। यह ट्रैक डामर की सड़क, चट्टानी भूमि, जंगल और गाँव के बीच से गुजरता है। किले पर चढ़ने के लिए लोहे की सीढ़ियां बनीं है। 2500 फीट पर स्थित किले से सूर्योदय और मुकणे जलाशय का सुन्दर दृश्य दिखता है।आसपास देखने के लिए कई मंदिर भी हैं।
एक ध्यान देने वाली बात यह है कि जब तक आप ट्रेल (मार्ग) पर नहीं होते हैं तब तक आप यह नहीं जान पाएंगे की यहाँ पर किले के लिए एक पगडंडी है। ऐसा जानबूझकर दुश्मन के सैनिकों और जासूसों को गुमराह करने के लिए किया गया था।

title: Jogging Tour Weilburg Valley in Wiesbaden
short_description: Ideal jogging tour after a strenuous day at work. The tour starts at the Rheineck Hotel in the Wiesbaden district of Dotzheim and runs along the Aunelstrasse for about 1 km through the town before entering the Weilburg Valley and running gently uphill through the forest. After about 3.5 km you reach the turning point and from there you walk back on the other side of the Aunel stream. Another small climb, a hairpin bend and then you head back towards the hotel.

title: Trekking to Kutralam (Courtallam) Five Falls
short_description: Courtallam also called Kutralam is a small but very beautiful town located on the banks of the Chittar River in the Tenkasi district of Tamil Nadu. It is also known as the "Spa of South India" because of its medicinal springs and waterfalls.
long_description:
कोर्टल्लम तमिलनाडु के तेनकासी जिले का एक छोटा लेकिन शांत और सुन्दर शहर है। यह अपनी अनेक छोटी-बड़ी झीलों, रिसॉर्ट्स,और स्पा के लिए प्रसिद्ध है, जिसकी वजह से कोर्टल्लम को 'दक्षिण के स्पा टाउन' भी कहते हैं। कोर्टल्लम का ख़ास पर्यटन आकर्षण हालांकि इसके झरने ही हैं जैसे की (1) कोर्टल्लम मेन फॉल्स जिसे पेरारुवी भी कहा जाता है, (2) कोर्टल्लम फाइव फॉल्स जिसे आइंथारुवी भी कहा जाता है, (3) हनीकोंब फॉल्स जिसे थेनारुवी भी कहा जाता है और (4) शेनबागा फॉल्स।
 कोर्टल्लम फाइव फॉल्स ट्रैक 4 किलोमीटर लम्बा है।यह कोर्टल्लम बस स्टेशन से शुरू होता है और फाइव फॉल्स झरने पर जाकर ख़त्म होता है। यह मुख्य रूप से एक शहरी ट्रेल है जो की फाइव फॉल्स मेन रोड भी कहलाती है। यह ट्रैक सभी के लिए आसान और उपयुक्त है। झरने के पास एक झील और बोटिंग क्लब भी है। फाइव फॉल्स से आसपास और उससे पहले कई रेस्टोरेंट भी है। यह ट्रैक परिवार संग छुट्टियां और पिकनिक मनाने के लिए बहुत अच्छा है।
