title: Circular hike Thierstein
short_description: We hike along field and forest paths past numerous bodies of water to finally walk along the once important Magdeburg-Regensburg trade route.
long_description:
On this hike we pass many historical sites that bear witness to the settlement and industrial history of the region:
The rocky peak of the Lärchenbühl is, like the Thierstein castle hill, an extinct volcanic vent. Its basalt columns were probably removed to build the castle in Thierstein. Since Thierstein Castle was already so dilapidated at the end of the 16th century that repairs seemed too costly, the margravial government in Bayreuth decided to build a new official building. In 1602, the official building still called "Schlößlein" was built (today privately owned).
In Leupoldshammer or Neuenhammer, there had been a stately armoury in the Margrave's time (around 1800). Today, the power station is located at this site, which was put into operation in 1935. In Blumenthal, water power was used early on. In the mid-18th century there was an iron cutting mill here which was later converted into a saw and grist mill. At the end of the 19th century, the porcelain factory owner Hutschenreuther bought Blumenthal, built a villa and had numerous ponds constructed for fish farming. A holiday farm was created in the buildings of the estate for employees and jubilarians seeking recreation.
Hafendeck, one of the oldest mills in the region (end of the 15th century, also known as the Thierstein mill), once belonged to the Thierstein clay industry (quartz mill). When there were no more potters, it was converted into a grinding mill. Pfannenstiel was once the home of pitch scrapers, tar burners, pitch and grease boilers. A large, flat stone in the forest, popularly called the Devil's Table, is the base plate of a lubricating furnace. Here, grease was extracted from pine wood and tree pitch, which was needed by the hammer mills and carters. During the heyday of iron smelting in the Eger valley, ore and charcoal transports from the Arzberg ore mine and from the Reich and coal forests also rolled along the important trade route that led from Magdeburg to Regensburg. That is why the much-travelled road used to be called "Eysenstras".

images.caption: The starting point of our circular walk is the market square in Thierstein.
Picturesque ensemble - castle and church in Thierstein.

title: On the Adriabike cycle path to Venice and Chioggia
short_description: The cycle tour covers a total of 417 km from the Slovenian Adriatic coast via Trento, Grado and Venice to the seaport of Chioggia in Veneto. The scenic route is made up of a total of three paths: the Emerald Path, the Path of Merchants and Cows and the Path of the Serenissima.
long_description: Starting from Portorož in Istria, the emerald green path (the so-called „Via verde smeraldo“) leads to the harbour city of Trieste in Italy. It crosses the impressive mountain landscape of the Julian Alps and offers panoramic views of the mountain massif right from the start of the tour. The route then leaves Monfalcone near the Timavo and Isonzo rivers. There you can admire the Mediterranean flora and numerous bird populations in the Foce dell’Isonzo nature reserve. The rest of the route leads to the town of Grado, which is located on the so-called Isola del Sole (Isola of the Sun). The Grado lagoon, a bird paradise with lush vegetation, is located in front of it. The route continues via the neighbouring municipality of Aquilea to Torviscosa and via the Marano lagoon directly to Lignano Sabbiadoro. Now we are already on the Serenissima road, which leads straight to Venice.

images.caption: Mit dem Mountainbike in Lignano Sabbiadoro

title: Circular hike in the Sonnenwald forest around Zenting
short_description: This circular trail takes us on comfortable paths through the Sonnenwald region - with ever-changing views of the Dreiburgenland.
long_description: From Zenting, we walk past the building yard in the direction of the sewage treatment plant. We cross the Zentinger Bach stream and follow the forest path. Behind the edge of the forest, we turn left and pass a pond. Our path crosses the stream again and we follow the meadow path straight ahead through the forest to Manzenreuth. A small concrete road leads through the idyllic hamlet to Burgsdorf, with a beautiful view of the Brotjacklriegel. We turn right onto the state road and immediately turn left onto the path to the "Bründlkapelle". At the next junction, turn right to the hill with a view of the Ebenreuther Badesee lake. Behind the farm in Gessenreuth, we turn left and hike to Winden. We reach Fradlberg via scenic field paths and hike back down to Zenting.

title: Wanderung an den Algarvenstränden von Albufeira
short_description:
Vom Parkplatz des Teaumstrandes Praia de Sao Rafael startet unsere Wanderung die an ca. 10 Buchten die zum Teil zu Fuss erreichbar vorbeifuehrt. Folgt man dem direkten Weg, dauert die Tour mit Rueckweg nur 1 Stunde, aber wenn man zu den Aussichtspunkten oder den Buchten abzweigt, kann man gut einen halben Tag dort verbringen. Absolut traumhaft!

title: Odenwald-Vosges (German section)
short_description: The Odenwald-Vosges hiking trail connects the two European long-distance hiking trails E1 and E2. The German section through the Odenwald low mountain range is managed by the Odenwaldklub e.V..
long_description:
We start in the very north of the Odenwald in Darmstadt and immediately experience the low mountain range from its mountainous side. Via Bensheim, Heppenheim and Weinheim, we can expect gruelling climbs and steep descents into idyllic river valleys. We are rewarded with fantastic views over the Odenwald. Behind Heidelberg, where the Neckar flows into the Rhine and the famous castle towers over the city, we hike steeply downhill once more and then reach calmer climes. Past Leimen, Nußloch and Wiesloch it is only a slight up and down and we have enough time to admire the sights along the way. The route to the next stops at Mingolsheim, Ubstadt and Bruchsal also offers us tourist attractions such as Bruchsal Castle, small villages and historic half-timbered houses in addition to the nature experience. The last section of the tour via Weingarten, Durlach and Karlsruhe is just as charming and gives us a good impression of the urban-rural contrast in the region.
The approx. 190 km of the long-distance hiking trail can be divided into the following stages, for example:
Stage 1: Darmstadt - Frankenstein - Elmshausen
Stage 2: Elmshausen - Gronau - Heppenheim
Stage 3: Heppenheim - Juhöhe - Weinheim
Stage 4: Weinheim - Oberflockenbach
Stage 5: Oberflockenbach - Wilhelmsfeld - Heidelberg
Stage 6: Heidelberg - Königstuhl - Leimen - Wiesloch
Stage 7: Wiesloch - Bad Schönborn - Ubstadt
Stage 8: Ubstadt - Bruchsal - Weingarten - Karlsruhe
Stage 9: Karlsruhe - D axlanden - Neuburgweier

title: Taganai National Park - Upper Taganai Trail
short_description: Taganai is the most popular natural area in the Southern Urals. The park is loved by tourists because of its rocky, unique and bizarrely shaped areas.
long_description:
The Taganai National Park is located in the vicinity of the Ural town of Zlatoust, 150 km from Chelyabinsk.
The length of the hike along the Upper Taganai Trail to Kruglitsa Mountain and back is 28 km. Depending on possibilities and interest the trekking can be broken up into several sections and days. There are many scenic spots to visit on the trail. These include Chernaya Skala Mountain, Dvuglava Sopka, Mit'ki Rocks and Reverberation Ridge. Kruglica Mountain is the highest mountain in the park (1178m) - the trail ends here. The trail goes straight through the Valley of Fairy Tales, a fantastically beautiful place with rocky ledges and low trees winding around them.
In the middle of the trail you will find the Rattlesnake Key Refuge, where you can organise your holiday.

title: The wine road through the wine cellars of Bistrita
short_description: Although less promoted or sought after, the Bistrița County wine trail takes you through a dreamy natural setting, where the traveller has the opportunity to experience the balanced taste of Transylvanian wines and to rediscover pieces of the area's medieval history;
long_description:
The Bistrițene Podgories (Batoș and Lechința) do not occupy a large area and are separated from those located in the Târnavelor Plateau. That is why they deserve a special place on the map of wine trails. This proposal for a circular route around the wine cellars of Bistrita satisfies the tastes of quality wine lovers. Not only will you find several tasting options, but you also have plenty of sights to stop at.
The wineries in Bistrita county are mostly small, family-owned, with limited production. The wines preserve the Transylvanian tradition, being in a considerable proportion white, dry wines. For the more discerning, there are even organic wines.
The journey can be broken up at various stops to enjoy local dishes or the hospitality of the people of Bistriț. Two wineries along the route also offer accommodation. Don't miss Herghelia Beclean for a great equestrian ride or to find out more about the possibilities of trails in the area.

title: Via Alpina C3a: Sargans - Weisstannen
short_description: The Via Alpina crosses 14 of the most beautiful Alpine passes. Across six Swiss cantons and the Principality of Liechtenstein with diverse culture, geology and topography. Wide roads end in airy ridge paths. One of the world's most diverse flora and fauna line the way.
long_description:
The Via Alpina crosses 14 of the most beautiful Alpine passes. Across six Swiss cantons and the Principality of Liechtenstein, the hiker experiences a diverse culture, geology and topography. Quiet oases of relaxation alternate with prosperous tourist resorts.
Broad roads end in dizzyingly airy ridge paths. There is no better way to get to know the Swiss Alpine culture in all its facets. The ultramodern alp with pipelines and its showroom is just as much on the way as the alpine hut, where pigs, goats and cows watch the farmers cooking in the copper kitchen over the open fire. One of the most diverse animal and plant worlds in the world surrounds the path. Displacements, shifts, subsidences and rock erosions bear witness to interestingly structured geology. Breathtaking panoramas alternate with small curiosities along the way and the gastronomy has a variety of delicacies in store. ©schweizmobil.ch

Stage 3: Weisstannen - Elm:
The wide, steep and remote Weisstannental enchants visitors with impressive nature, peace and idyll. About halfway through the stage, shortly before the beautiful hamlet of Vermol, it is worth taking a detour to the nearby Chapfensee lake. Along hilly paths on the western flank of the valley, you penetrate deeper and deeper into the long valley until you reach the village of Weisstannen. Alpine culture is still alive here; booted goats graze, the alpine dairymen still cultivate the tradition of the call to prayer and the waterwheel chugs by the old, restored saw. Text in part ©schweizmobil.ch

title: Via Alpina C2: Vaduz - Sargans
short_description: The Via Alpina crosses 14 of the most beautiful Alpine passes. Across six Swiss cantons and the Principality of Liechtenstein with diverse culture, geology and topography. Wide roads end in airy ridge paths. One of the world's most diverse flora and fauna line the way.
long_description:
The Via Alpina crosses 14 of the most beautiful Alpine passes. Across six Swiss cantons and the Principality of Liechtenstein, the hiker experiences a diverse culture, geology and topography. Quiet oases of relaxation alternate with prosperous tourist resorts.
Broad roads end in dizzyingly airy ridge paths. There is no better way to get to know the Swiss Alpine culture in all its facets. The ultramodern alp with pipelines and its showroom is just as much on the way as the alpine hut, where pigs, goats and cows watch the farmers cooking in the copper kitchen over the open fire. One of the most diverse animal and plant worlds in the world surrounds the path. Displacements, shifts, subsidences and rock erosions bear witness to interestingly structured geology. Breathtaking panoramas alternate with small curiosities along the way and the gastronomy has a variety of delicacies in store. ©schweizmobil.ch

Trip 2: Vaduz - Sargans
On Gaflei, 1490 m above sea level, the hiker has a magnificent view of the Rhine Valley. From Gaflei, the hiking trail leads via a woody descent to Vaduz, capital of the Principality of Liechtenstein. Vaduz has much to offer: Art, culture, architecture, events and a varied gastronomy. The lively main town with its car-free pedestrian zone invites you to linger in the cosy street cafés and offers a variety of cultural attractions. Special sights include Vaduz Castle, the landmark for all the royal moments to be discovered in Vaduz, the Liechtenstein Museum of Art, the Court Winery of the Prince, the Citytrain, the government quarter, the Liechtenstein National Museum and the "Red House". The route continues over the Rhine at Sevelen. With a view over the wide Rhine valley, the trail leads through forests and meadows at the foot of the Gonzen. The destination of the stage is the historic town of Sargans with its castle, visible from afar, perched on a rocky outcrop.
Text in part © schweizmobil.ch

title: बरनाला बुग्याल (बरनाला झील) ट्रैक
short_description: बरनाला बुग्याल एक छोटा सा अल्पाइन चरागाह है जो की दयारा बुग्याल ट्रैक म ार्ग पर ड़ता है। नाग देवता मंदिर और बरनाला ताल इस छोटे लेकिन बेहद सुन्दर बुग्याल की पहचान हैं।
long_description:
हिमालयी राज्य उत्तराखंड अपने ग्लेशियर, पर्वत चोटियों और हाई एल्टीट्यूड अल्पाइन चरागाहों (जिन्हें स्थानीय भाषा में बुग्याल कहा जाता है) के लिए हाइकर्स और ट्रैकर्स के बीच बहुत लोकप्रिय है। जहाँ पर्वतारोहण, और ग्लैसिअल हाइकिंग के लिए बेहद अनुभवी होना जरूरी है वहीँ बुग्यालों की ट्रैकिंग के लिए कुछ भी खास अनुभव नहीं चाहिए। यहीं कारण है की उत्तराखंड के बुग्याल सभी किस्म के हाइकर्स को अपनी ओर आकर्षित करते हैं। इन बुग्यालों की सुंदरता बेमिसाल है - चाहे यह सर्दियों में बर्फ से भरे हों या बसंत में फूलों से ढके हों।
बरनाला बुग्याल भी उत्तराखंड के उत्तरकाशी ज़िले में बसा हुआ ऐसा ही एक सुन्दर बुग्याल है। असल में इसकी ज्यादा चर्चा नहीं होती है क्योंकि इस से सिर्फ कुछ ही दूर बेहद प्रसिद्ध दयारा बुग्याल है जो लोकप्रियता में आसपास के सभी गंतव्यों को पीछे छोड़ देता है।
बरनाला बुग्याल का ट्रैक रैथल गाँव या फिर बरसु गाँव से शुरू किया जा सकता है। ट्रैक बसंत और सर्दियों दोनों में ही किया जा सकता है। रैथल गाँव समुद्र तल से करीब 12000 फ़ीट की ऊंचाई पर है और उत्तरकाशी शहर से करीब 40 किलोमीटर दूर है। बरसु गाँव भी रैथल गाँव के पास है। बुग्याल की ट्रेल मार्ग पूरी तरह से बुराँश और देवदार के जंगलों से ढकी हुई है। गर्मियों के दौरान ट्रेल में कई तरह की हिमालयी चिड़ियों और अनोखे पेड़-पौधे को देखने का मौका भी मिलता है। ट्रेल ज्यादा कठिनाई वाली नहीं है और कोई भी फिट इंसान बुग्याल तक का सफर आसानी से पूरा कर सकता है।
बरनाला बुग्याल में शिविर स्थल लगाने की अनुमति है। शिविर स्थल सुन्दर और साफ़ हैं। बुग्याल में साफ़ मीठे पानी की एक झील भी है और नाग देवता का एक मंदिर भी है।

images.caption: बरनाला बुग्याल से बर्फीली हिमालय पर्वत चोटियों को देखता हुआ एक अकेला तंबू, उत्तराखंड, भारत।
बरनाला झील के किनारे नाग देवता मंदिर का निर्माण कार्य, उत्तराखंड, भारत।
गर्मियों में बरनाला बुग्याल का दृश्य, उत्तरांचल, भारत।
मंदिर, और झील, और हिमालयी चोटियाँ, और बर्फ से ढका बरनाला बुग्याल उत्तराखंड, भारत।

title: Ås til Åsleden - Ekeröd to Timan
short_description: The ninth stage of the s til Åsledens goes from Ekeröd to Timan.
long_description: On the Linder train, our path runs mainly along small gravel paths. At the beginning we pass a few houses, then the area becomes increasingly uninhabited. Idyllic pastures alternate with small wooded areas and bogs. Most of the paths were created to facilitate peat extraction and transport, which was the livelihood of many people in the region;

title: Riedholzer Kugel circular woodland hike
short_description: A beautiful trip from the iberg ski lift car park in Riedholz village, up the Riedholzer Kugel Mountain and through the surrounding woodlands, heading back down the iberg.
long_description: This magnificent, medium length, circular woodland/mountain hike begins at the easily accessible car park situated at the foot of the iberg, in Riedholz village. There it is possible to park your car free of charge, and head down to the base of the Riedholzer Kugel Mountain. You will ascend up to the peak of this well maintained and wonderfully equipped mountain climb, passing two small childrens play areas and rest stops, one located at the highest point. If the weather permits, it is from here you will discover a stunning view of the mountain range. On reaching the peak you will make the gradual woodland descent east, towards Hohenegg. Another rest stop can be found at the top of the iberg slope, here you can enjoy another fantastic view of your surroundings, as you head down you will eventually phase out of the woodlands and down the iberg summit, always following a clearly marked path, towards the car park where this adventure began.

title: Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail
short_description: Varied hiking trail that runs for just under 95 km from Kirn on the southern edge of the Soonwald-Nahe Nature Park to Bingen on the Rhine.
long_description: The Rhine-Nahe Wine Trail takes us in four days from Kirn on the southern edge of the Soonwald-Nahe Nature Park through the varied landscapes of Hunsrück and Naheland to Bingen on the Rhine. We hike through a region characterised by wine along the Nahe. Striking rock formations, castles and palaces, forests and meadows as well as vineyards line the way. The charming wine villages of the Naheland and the numerous wine taverns and winegrowers' farms along the way invite you to take a leisurely break with a hearty snack and a glass of Nahe wine.

title: Parry Kauri Park Loop Track
short_description: Short boardwalk loop track through magnificient bush with some mature kauri trees.
long_description: From the car park at the Warkworth District's Museum you can already see two of the largest kauri trees in the region. With a girth of more than 7 meters and an estimated age of over 800 years, the McKinney kauri tree is thought to be the largest kauri tree on New Zealand's east coast. A wooden viewing platform protects the sensitive roots of the trees from visitors. The magnificent loop trail can be walked in different directions and the sections can be combined from 10 minutes to approximately 30 minutes walking. Especially children will have fun exploring the winding track through dense bush, passing many kauri trees. There is a bird feeding station at a viewing platform in the bush and with a little bit of luck, Kereru can be spotted. Before or after walking the track, the museum may be visited. Inquire about current opening times on the museum's website. The loop track and the visit of the museum are highly recommended as a short stopover activity.

title: From Schöntal Monastery through the Schelmenklinge
short_description: This hike takes us to the ruins of the Storchenturm (Stork Tower), from where we have a magnificent view over the Jagst valley. The trail then winds its way through the "Schelmenklinge".
long_description: Our hike begins in the courtyard of Schöntal Monastery. Passing the gate tower on the right, we cross the Jagst bridge. There we cross the car park and then turn left onto the steep grassy path marked by a red cross. We climb up to the edge of the forest, turn left and come across a forest path running across our path. Here we change to a footpath and then to a forest path, via which we reach the ruins of the Stork Tower. The view from there is impressive. You can see the monastery and far into the Jagst valley. Follow the unpaved forest path into the stork forest. A short time later, a paved forest path turns off to the right and is again marked with a red cross. Follow this straight ahead along the eastern edge of the steep "Schelmenklinge". Then the path leads us into the fields and on to Rossach past the children's playground and cemetery. A driveway branches off to the left and brings us to circular trail no. 7, which comes from Jagsthausen. We follow it in a southerly direction to the left onto the district road and to the edge of the forest. At the emergency call pillar, we walk left onto a forest path. The trail descends in serpentines into the "Schelmenklinge". Before we reach the edge of the forest, a steep path branches off to the left and takes us up the forest slope. From the top we have a magnificent view of the Berlichingen church. The unpaved path passes above the Storchenturm (stork tower) and at the edge of the forest we rejoin the grass path marked by a red cross, which takes us down the steep slope back to our starting point, Schöntal Monastery.

title: To Engeratsgundsee and Giebelhaus
short_description: This technically easy hike takes us from the Edmund Probst Haus past the Großer Daumen to the Giebelhaus. Along the way we pass idyllic mountain lakes such as the Engeratsgundsee and enjoy views of the Allgäu mountains.
long_description: From the Edmund-Probst-Haus near the mountain station Höfatsblick of the Nebelhorn cable car, this easy tour takes us to the Großer Daumen. At 2280 m, its summit is the highest point of the Daumengruppe, a subgroup of the Allgäu Alps. On the way there, we pass through barren alpine terrain. Picturesque small mountain lakes attract our gaze. After enjoying the view of the Großer Daumen, we follow a steep path down to the Engeratsgundsee. From there we descend via the Gündleshütte to the Engeratsgundhof farm, where we take a rest. We then follow a wide forest road to the Giebelhaus, where we take the hiking bus back to Bad Hindelang. This hike is especially recommended when the alpine roses are in bloom.

title: खाजागुड़ा झील ट्रैक
short_description: खाजगुडा झील तेलंगाना राज्य के हैदराबाद शहर के पास मौजूद एक शहरी झील है ज ो अर्बन हाईकिंग के लिए बढ़िया है।
long_description:
खाजागुड़ा एक अर्बन लेक यानी की शहरी झील है जो की रंगा रेड्डी जिले के खाजागुड़ा इलाके में स्थित है। यह झील हैदराबाद शहर से करीब 15 किलोमीटर दूर है। इस तक हैदराबाद से आना ज्यादा आसान है क्योंकि खाजागुड़ा एक प्रमुख रिहायसी और औद्योगिक इलाका है और हैदराबाद से इसके लिये अच्छी कनेक्टिविटी है।
अगर इस ट्रेल की बात करें तो यह एक पक्की सड़क और नेचर ट्रेल का मिश्रण हैं। शुरुआत लैंको हिल्स के गोलचक्कर से होती है और पक्की सड़क के कुछ देर बाद नेचर ट्रेल शुरू हो जाती है। रास्ता हलकी चढ़ाई वाला है लेकिन कठिन नहीं है। नए और अनुभवी सभी हाइकर्स के लिए यह उपयुक्त है। पास में ही खाजागुड़ा हिल्स भी हैं जहाँ पर भी हाईकिंग और बोल्डरिंग (पर्वतारोहण) होता है। शहरी जीवन से बोर होने पर वीकेंड पर यह ट्रैक किया जा सकता है।

title: Mocăniței Half Marathon - Cross-Country route
short_description: This route represents the route of the cross-country race of the trail running competition Mocănița Half Marathon - an initiative whose aim is to raise funds for the restoration of the Teaca - Lechința Mocănița (also called Mocănița Transilvaniei) to the tourist circuit.
long_description:
Riders can try all or part of the route as training.
The first part of the trail is the most spectacular - a level curving path through orchards and along the edge of deciduous forests, with superb views over the old villages of Bistrita. This part also coincides with the Via Transilvanica hiking trail.
Once you leave the marked trail, at the highest point, you descend through the forest, on a forest road that in wet weather is very rutted, to the TeTa fruit farm.
After crossing the access road to the farm, the trail cuts across the pasture land that separates the farm from Teleki Castle in Posmuș, roughly parallel to the main road. On the last hundred metres, you return to the path you started on.

title: Bergheidenweg
short_description: Southern flair between juniper heath and pine groves. Wonderful paths lead us through mixed forest, along the Nette and the Selbach. We enjoy wonderful views of the Eifel. Those who want to really enjoy the juniper heaths can use the connection to the Wacholderweg.
long_description:
Highlights:
Mountain and juniper heath, Nettetal, Selbachtal gorge valley, Raßberg, Heidbüchel nature reserve and Dr. Heinrich Menke Park.
The trail starts at the car park of the winter sports facility not far from Arft and leads through open heathland to the Heidbüchel nature reserve. Primeval pines line the path through the typical sand and heath vegetation. Once you reach the summit of the Heidbüchel, a unique view rewards the ascent. On the descent through the forest, a path branches off to the neighbouring "Wacholderweg" dream trail. At the edge of the forest, the trail turns left towards Nettetal. Behind the small village of Netterhöfe, the Nette is crossed and then the dream trail follows the small river into the valley. You cross the water once more over a wooden bridge. In the following Selbach valley, high forest surrounds the hiker, impressive cliffs give the valley a gorge-like character. Along the babbling brook, the trail climbs through the forest and later on dirt roads to a refuge from where you can enjoy a breathtaking panorama. Continue slightly uphill across the open field. After crossing the L10, the trail continues to Dr. Heinrich Menke Park. After crossing the L10 again, past the Konrad Adenauer Monument, the route continues around the Raßberg. Soon you will reach the starting point of the dream path.

images.caption: Along our route there are always nice places to rest.
Hiking is not only the miller's delight.

The cool water of the stream refreshes the battered feet of hikers.

long_description: यह दौरा खूबसूरत हिलस्टेशन 'मुन्नार' का एक नया और लोकप्रिय हाइकिंग ट्रैक है। आउट एंड बैक किस्म की यह ट्रेल करीब 3 किलोमीटर लम्बी है और आना जाना मिलाकर 6 किलोमीटर की कुल दूरी तय की जाती है। यह ट्रेल चर्च ऑफ़ साउथ इंडिया से शुरू की जा सकती है और अट्टुकड़ झरने के बिल्कुल पास बने एक सीमेंट-पुल पर जा कर ख़त्म होती है। रास्ते का ज्यादातर हिस्सा एक नेचर ट्रेल है और कुछ हिस्सा कभी कभी डामर की सड़क से गुजरता है। ट्रेल का कठिनाई स्तर 'आसान' है और यह नए या अनुभवी सभी हाइकर्स के लिए ठीक है। ट्रेल में हलकी चढ़ाई है जो किस्म की दिक्कत नहीं देती है। ट्रेल हरियाली और चाय बागानों से होकर गुजरती है और बहुत आनंददायक है।

short_description:
This small loop allows you to go around the dunes of Carnac and Kermario by the paths authorized to the public free of charge and in all seasons.

title: Path of Love in Bad Oberdorf
short_description: This short jog takes us through Bad Oberdorf along the romantic path of love and further along the Vaterlandsweg back to the starting point.
long_description: Romantic benches, great views and shady paths await us during this jog. First, the path leads along the tarred road through Bad Oberdorf past typical Allgäu houses. Right from the start, the path climbs steadily uphill to the Prinz-Luitpold-Haus, which is known for its sulphur springs. On the shady "Path of Love" many resting benches with engraved poems on the theme of love invite you to rest and reflect. The covered pavilion with a view of the Ostrachtal mountains is a nice place to stretch. After crossing a small bridge below the Schleierfall, great views of the Ostrachtal valley await us along the Vaterlandsweg. The last stage takes us along the Ostrach over a shady path back to the starting point.

title: Illuminated wood path Toepen
short_description: With its short but crisp ascent to the Petersgrad, the Leuchtholzweg offers a magnificent view over the Saale valley.
long_description: We start in Töpen and walk along the Töpener Bach stream through a beautiful meadow landscape. We walk through the valley of the Tannbach to its confluence with the Saale and from there follow the latter in a southerly direction. Then we have a steep ascent over wooded slopes to the Petersgrad, which, however, gives us wonderful views of the Saale valley. Via Isaar, where we can refresh ourselves in the village inn, we return through open countryside to Töpen.

images.caption: On hiker-friendly paths we follow the Töpener Bach, the Tannbach and the Saale.

title: Disc Golf: Around the Ofterschwanger Horn
short_description: Get out into nature for the adventure of disc golf.
long_description: Never heard of it? Don't do anything! Disc golf is a guarantee for action and good humour. Like golf, there is a lane and a discard area. However, the Frizbee disc must land in a basket at the end of each lane rather than in a hole. It is only a short walk from the mountain station of the World Cup Express to the Frizbee course Ofterschwang. There are 14 holes to play on the spacious, natural terrain. Disc golf promises not only a lot of fun, but also an active adventure in front of a breathtaking mountain backdrop.

title: From Tröstau to the Rösla meadows near Marktredwitz
short_description: This hike is a day tour. It leads us along the romantic Rösla valley and through the high moor area "Zeitelmoos".
long_description:
Tröstau, then called Drosen, was first mentioned in 1314. The village lies on a high plateau on the south-western edge of the Fichtelgebirge. A building worth seeing in Tröstau is the former, approx. 700-year-old Hammerherrenschloss (hammer lord's castle) in the district of Leupoldsdorf.
The hike through the Rösla meadows and through the high moor "Zeitelmoos" is designed as a day tour. It is therefore advisable to take enough food and drink with you.

title: Stoffelbergrundweg near Waltenhofen
short_description: Leisurely tour with great panoramic views around the Stoffelberg.
long_description: The Stoffelbergrundweg leads us mostly on gravel paths through the cattle pastures, meadows and forests around the Stoffelberg. The tour, which climbs slightly at first and then descends again on the way back to the starting point, impresses with the magnificent panoramic views we can enjoy on the southern half of the circular trail. The tour can also be combined with the Stoffelbergweg.

title: Monastery Village Tour in the Southern Black Forest
short_description: After a short climb, you have fantastic views along the high trail that connects St. Märgen and St. Peter.
long_description: Follow a farm track uphill towards Rankmühle and at the edge of the forest turn left towards Kapfenkapelle (2 km). Follow the yellow rhombus along the edge of the forest. Here, numerous benches invite you to enjoy the view of the Black Forest heights. We pass a water treading place, the Birkenwegeck (1) and the Ibenbachquelle (2). Our path continues to the Kapfen Chapel (3), to the "Red Cross" and along the edge of the forest to the Vosges Chapel (4). Here we go straight on into the forest and then across the meadows of the Hochrütti. At the Vordere Willmer Höhe (5), we finally leave the forest and turn left. We can already see the two towers of the baroque church of St. Peter. The signposts to St. Peter (yellow rhombus) show us the way down. Past a café, under the country road, we reach the baroque church of St. Peter (6). Cross the monastery courtyard to the exit and turn left at the through road to the bus stop at Zähringer Eck. From there, buses run about every half hour back to St. Märgen.

title: Nebelhorn - Hindelanger via ferrata - Giebelhaus
short_description: The Hindelang via ferrata is the longest and most demanding via ferrata in the Allgäu. It runs along the rugged grade between Nebelhorn and Grosse Daumen. Via the Gündlesalpe, the Käseralpe and the Engeratsgundalpe we descend to the Giebelhaus. A fantastic panoramic tour with views of the Allgäu Alps.
long_description: The Hindelanger via ferrata, which runs for 5 km on the highly exposed grade between Nebelhorn and Gro;em Daumen, is secured with almost 1 km of wire rope and about 100 m of ladders. Three emergency exits in a southerly direction via the Koblat make it possible to get out early if your condition decreases or the weather deteriorates, whereby the difficulty of the via ferrata increases after the emergency exits. At the end of the tour, a wonderful descent awaits us via the large slopes of the Gündlesalpe, the Käseralpe and the Engeratsgundalpe (managed) to the Giebelhaus (also managed).

title: Rajgarh Fort Track, Maharashtra, India
short_description: Rajgarh is a hill fort located in the Pune district of the state of Maharashtra, which was the capital of the Maratha Empire for 26 years under the rule of Shivaji Raje. It is also called the king of all the forts of Maharashtra.
long_description:
Rajgarh Fort is located about 60 km from Pune and about 15 km from Nasrapur village. The fort is built on a height of 1376 meters above sea level in the Sahyadri mountain range. Today, palaces, ponds and tunnels are found in the remaining remains of the fort. The fort was built on Murumba Devi Dongar (Mountain of Goddess Murumba). Rajgarh was the capital of the vast and powerful Maratha Empire for 26 years before Shivaji shifted the capital to Raigarh. During its lifetime, this fort was occupied many times by the Mughals, Marathas and the British.
The fort is currently maintained by the state government and is a popular trekking site among the Indian hiking community. There are three trail routes leading up to the fort and avid hikers prefer to climb all three routes to the fort. Though the trek up to the fort is not difficult but in the last stage one has to climb 2000 steps from the entrance to reach the top of the fort. There is a small shop on top of the fort where home style traditional Marathi food is available.
After the monsoon, when the entire Western Ghats are covered with greenery, then trekking to this fort becomes even more enjoyable.

title: Climbing route Schützensteig on the Kleiner Jenner
short_description: Climbing tour via the newly built Schützensteig on the Kleiner Jenner
long_description: The Schützensteig is an easy via ferrata (A/B) on the Kleiner Jenner in Berchtesgadener Land. Opened in 2015, it is ideal for recreational athletes and families with children. The route is about 330 m long and secured throughout with ropes and stirrups. The highlight is without question the "Flying Fox" suspension bridge that leads to the entrance.

short_description: This half-day walk will take you through some exceptional and varied landscapes.You will pass by the Cap de la Chèvre, the southern cape of the Crozon peninsula, which is part of the Parc naturel régional d'Armorique. You will essentially be walking along the "sentier de grande randonnée 34" (GR 34).
long_description: At the far end of the Cape, you can enjoy a 180° view of the bay of Douarnenez and Cap Sizun on one side and the islands of Ouessant and Molène on the other.

title: Snowshoe:Feichteck in Chiemgau
short_description: This moderately difficult snowshoe tour to the Feichteck (1514 m) is offered to us in early winter and in less than ideal conditions, but it is by no means boring. The summit offers us a fantastic view of the foothills of the Alps.
long_description: This snowshoe tour on the Feichteck is suitable both for beginners and as a introductory tour at the beginning of the season. The Feichteck is nevertheless not a boring mountain. It offers us a dreamlike, wintry fairytale forest and gently sloping alpine meadows. From the summit we can enjoy a fantastic view of the foothills of the Alps. The Spitzstein seems to be within reach. The orientation of the slopes is mainly west, south and southeast. In extreme weather conditions there is only a danger of avalanches on the slopes above the Schneibereralm. The slopes to the north and east of the summit are game reserves and you are asked to avoid these areas consistently.

title: Snowshoe tour: Teufelstättkopf from Unterammergau
short_description: This snowshoe tour to the Teufelstättkopf (1758 m) is relatively snow-sure. The August-Schuster Haus is a cosy place to stop for refreshments along the way.
long_description: This snowshoe tour to the Teufelstättkopf (1758 m) is relatively snow-sure. The path up to the August-Schuster-Haus (also called Pürschlinghaus) is shared with tobogganers under certain circumstances, but their goal is the August-Schuster-Haus. We want to reach the summit, however, and to get there we climb another 200 metres. A short, wire-rope-secured stretch leads to the summit over a rock step, so sure-footedness is required here. The majority of this technically quite easy tour leads through forest, which promises us good views of snow until well into spring. We move on mostly gently to moderately steep slopes in an east to north orientation. Orientation is easy, as we follow a road throughout the first part of the tour.

title: Stylus and tablet maker Ludwigsstadt
short_description: The hike leads past former Griffel slate quarries and delights with magnificent views of Lauenstein Castle and the Thuringian-Franconian Slate Mountains.
long_description: The hike leads past former slate quarries and delights with magnificent views of Lauenstein Castle and the Thuringian-Franconian slate mountains. with magnificent views of Lauenstein Castle and the Thuringian-Franconian Slate Mountains. We make a detour to the former village of Ebersdorf with its historic dance hall and the Magdalenenkirche church. There are interesting exhibits to see in Lauenstein Castle, which was the home of the table-makers in the 19th century. At the end of the tour we take a look at the profaned Marienkapelle, a remarkable round building from the 15th century, which is now the seat of the Hermann-Söllner Foundation. A visit to the slate museum with its focus on the production of slate boards is a successful conclusion of the tour.

images.caption: In Lauenstein Castle we can admire interesting exhibits of the table-makers.

long_description: The Jezreel Trail crosses the Jezreel Valley for 61 kilometers, due to the length of the trail it is customary to walk it in several sections. The hikers on the trail pass birds-eye views, archaeological sites, heritage sites, national parks and nature reserves.

title: Hiking along the Aibga Ridge
short_description: Hiking or trekking along the whole length of the Aibga Range. The route will take you through the three ski resorts of Krasnaya Polyana and will reveal the landscapes of the Achishkho, Pseashkho, Aishkho and even the Black Sea.
long_description:
The Aibga Range – is one of the mountain ranges of the resort paradise of Krasnaya Polyana. Aibga borders with Abkhazia and consists of 4 peaks: Aibga I (2391 m), Aibga II (2450 m), Aibga III (2462 m) and Black Pyramid Peak, which are waiting for hikers and lucky ones to catch and then share their unforgettable adventures. The highest peak of the massif – it is Stone Pillar Mountain (2509 m), it is also the extreme summit of the massif and the aim of our route.
The route will take us along the ridge of the massif in areas no longer covered by forest, so panoramic views of the neighbouring mountains and snowy peaks are guaranteed. Luck lies only in the weather conditions. Lucky with the weather, lucky with the hike. At worst, the time will not be wasted. In the best case the panoramic views will also include parts of the warm Black Sea.
 .
By the way, meaning of Aibga comes from Abkhazian tribe «aibga» which inhabited the massif and this tribe was so called by Kabardians. And, yes, in Abkhazia there is a surname Ayba, which has a direct relation to the ancient tribe. So good luck to those who suddenly encounter someone of this ancient tribe in the mountains of Krasnaya Polyana.

title: Across Ilaló to the hot springs of La Merced
short_description: Lovely hike with stunning views from El Tingo over meadows and through forests to one of Quito's city hills and on to La Merced, village of volcanic hot springs.
long_description: Ilaló is a comparatively small volcano on the south-eastern outskirts of Quito. The panoramic plateaus and a large cross on one of the pre-summits make it a popular but rarely overcrowded excursion destination for Quiteños. The route described here leads from El Tingo on a pilgrims' path to the cross and from there on to the highest point of the massif. On pleasantly shady paths, the trail descends through the sparse eucalyptus forest to La Merced, where volcanic springs with lukewarm water invite you to splash around. The varied hike leads past small farm fields, sunny highland meadows and dreamy forests and repeatedly reveals impressive views of the volcanic giants Cotopaxi, Cayambe, Cotacachi and the Ilinizas. A worthwhile undertaking in the immediate vicinity of the capital.

title: Snowshoe tour to the Reutter Wanne near Jungholz
short_description: This easy snowshoe tour to the Reutter Wanne (1542 m) is particularly worthwhile especially when there is fresh powder snow. It is also ideal for beginners. suitable.

However, it offers relatively avalanche-safe touring fun and is particularly worthwhile especially worthwhile when there is fresh powder snow. The view from the summit of the the foothills of the Alps. The slopes of the ascent and slopes of the ascent and descent route are west to south-west facing and only flat to moderately steep. Orientation is easy for the most part. With the Restaurant Reutter Wanne is located directly on the trail.

title: Gadebusch and the town forest
short_description: This easy hike shows us one of the oldest settlements in the region. The town forest is largely left in its natural state. Walking through the town, we see historic brick buildings.
long_description: Directly above our starting point we walk to the Renaissance castle. From here we have a first view of the castle lake and the city forest behind it. Information boards tell us about the town and its history. The castle hill we are standing in front of today was laid out by the Slavs in the 8th century. The castle was rebuilt to its present form at the end of the 16th century. We walk down the sandy path, cross the wooden bridge over the castle lake (1) and turn right directly behind it. After a short stretch through the mixed forest, we come to the Century Stone (2), which was erected in 1925 to mark the 700th anniversary of the town. We pass the monument on the left and hike in a loop through the forest to the Burgsee. From a picnic and playground (3) we have a beautiful view of the historic town centre. The further path along the Burgsee leads us to the railway station, which is located in the middle of the town forest. After crossing the tracks, we turn right and walk up the slope to the forest stage (4), which is used for events in summer. We continue walking through the forest until we reach the end of Gadebusch. Here we turn left into the residential area. Behind the sports field we cross the tracks again. After a detour to the Burgsee lake, we reach the main street of Gadebusch, into which we turn left. The historic buildings with their shops invite you to take a stroll. We come to the town church (5), the first hall church between the Elbe and Oder rivers. It was built in the 13th century. Behind the church we walk along old brick houses and arrive at the market square with the town hall (6). The brick building dates from around 1340. On the opposite side of the market square we enter Amtsstraße and return to Schlossplatz.

title: The Sulzfluh via ferrata in the Rätikon
short_description: The Sulzfluh via ferrata was opened in 2005 and leads through the south flank of the Sulzfluh (2817 m) in the Rätikon. The Sulzfluh is the border peak between Vorarlberg and Graubünden.
long_description:
The Sulzfluh via ferrata, which was opened in 2005 on the mountain of the same name in the Rätikon, offers the best rock quality and a sunny ascent. The Carschina hut is a place to stop for refreshments close to the trail. The Carschina hut is at 2236 m and is open from mid-June to mid-October. The access and descent routes to the via ferrata are well signposted. Orientation is no problem at all. The via ferrata itself is well secured and has some very exposed passages with good views. Steep ascents demand good arm strength. There are even two bridges. Ambitious via ferrata climbers are guaranteed to have a lot of fun on this via ferrata. The Sulzfluh via ferrata is closed in winter. Parts of the rope and the access ladder are dismantled and are always reinstalled at the beginning of the season. As the weather in the Prättigau can change quickly, the current weather forecast
should be checked

always be checked before the tour. The wall through which the path leads is exposed from the south to the south-east.

title: In the valley near Illschwang
short_description: The Nordic walking route "Im Tal" leads through varied terrain from Illschwang to Dietersberg.
long_description: We walk through varied terrain over the Fichtelberg and the village of Gehrsricht to Dietersberg, do a lap through the valley of the Ammerbach and return to Illschwang through the Hirtangerholz and the so-called "Loch".

images.caption: The pleasant forest paths around Illschwang are great for walking.

title: Schöne Rundwanderung in Burgberg
short_description:
Ein leicht begehbarer Wanderweg über Wiesen und Wälder mit Aussicht auf das Illertal - vorbei an der Ruine Burgberg und an der Alpe Weiherle.
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Route startet direkt in Burgberg und schon nach kurzer Zeit ist auf der rechten Seite die Ruine Burgberg erreichbar. Weiter bergauf führt der Weg über Wiesen und durch Wälder nach oben und bietet schließlich eine tolle Aussicht auf das Illertal. Gemütlich führt der Weg dann langsam wieder bergab, vorbei an der Alpe Weiherle. Zueletzt bietet die Kapelle Steinbichel eine tolle Aussicht auf den Ort und die Berge dahinter. Die Route führt schließlich durch den Ort zurück zum Ausgangspunkt. Der Rundweg dauert ca. 1:35h und ist leicht begehbar.
Translate to English

title: From Neuschönau to the animal enclosure
short_description: Wolves, wild cats - these are some of the animals we can observe on our hike through the open spaces of the Bavarian Forest National Park. True to the motto "Let nature be nature", the wild and romantic forest landscape is influenced as little as possible by human hand.
long_description: We start our hike through the animal enclosure at the meeting point at car park P1, near the Globus. The hike through the open area brings us close to around 30 of the original inhabitants of the Bavarian Forest National Park: bison, wolf or brown bear have been extinct in the region for over 100 years. Early morning and late afternoon are usually good for observing the animals. Due to the extensive landscape enclosures, it is also advisable to bring binoculars. At the end of the hike, we should definitely climb up to the Hans Eisenmann House. This is where the approximately 1 km long circular trail to the plant enclosure begins.

images.caption: An approximately 1 km long circular path in the open-air plant area begins at the Hans Eisenmann House.
The large animal enclosures blend unobtrusively into the hilly landscape.
Guided tours of the animal enclosure start at the P1 car park near the kiosk.

title: Railway stalking near Wildpoldsried
short_description: We enjoy a leisurely hike on easy paths in the picturesque Allgäu landscape. Most of the time the trail runs next to, or within sight of, the railway line.
long_description: Behind Wildpoldsried, the winding ascent of the Bavarian Allgäu Railway begins up to Günzach station, which at 801 m is the highest double-track station in Germany. We follow the railway line in a northerly direction, mostly close to the tracks, or within sight of them, until we reach a subway at Moosmühle. From a nearby hill there is a wonderful view of the railway line. Via Eufnach and Sellthüren we reach a subway south of Immenthal, which is the turning point of our hike. On the other side, we now walk southwards on easy paths to Oberegg. We walk back to the starting point along the already familiar route.

title: Winter hike around the Obersee in Näfels
short_description: A leisurely circular trail around the beautiful Obersee in Glarnerland, first along the shore and then through the snow-covered forest. A hidden insider tip that not everyone knows about.
long_description:
The leisurely walk around the Obersee starts at the parking lot, which can be reached via a steep mountain road by car from Näfels or by bus in summer.The path along the lake offers a magnificent panorama of various mountains, including the imposing Brünnelistock. Whether you trudge along the shore through the white snow or walk through the enchanted and snow-covered forest, you can enjoy a wonderful "winter wonderland".
If the lake is properly frozen, you can also walk across the lake, although the path around the lake is always possible.

images.caption: Winter hike in the canton of Glarus: Winter hike around the Obersee in Näfels

title: Hiking trail 6 - From Mitwitz to Bächlein
short_description: This relaxing hike takes us past idyllically situated bodies of water to the hamlet of Bächlein, where you can stop for refreshments.
long_description: We hike through forests and meadows on quiet paths from Mitwitz to the hamlet of Bächlein, where we can take a leisurely break at the Waldhotel. The numerous bodies of water we pass are idyllically embedded in the beautiful nature. Many of them are used for fish farming. In summer, blueberries grow on the sandy soils between the pine stands, so we should not set off without a basket.

title: From the Füssener Jöchl via the Friedberger Steig to the Rote Flüh above the Tannheim Valley
short_description: The Friedberg via ferrata is an extremely scenic undertaking high above the Tannheim Valley. The tour can be rewardingly extended with a traverse of the Rote Flüh.
long_description: The Friedberger Steig above the Tannheimer Tal with a subsequent traverse of the Rote Flüh (2108 m) is certainly one of the most scenic undertakings in the Tannheimer Tal. The climb itself is not too difficult (maximum B) and therefore also suitable for children with good physical condition. However, surefootedness and a head for heights are required. If you use the cable car to Füssener Jöchl, the metres of ascent are kept within limits. The location of the Tannheimer Hütte or the Gimpelhaus is ideal for stopping off after the most difficult part of the undertaking with an excellent view. The exposition of the trail is mainly south to east facing. Orientation is easy. The route is well secured, but very slippery when wet. Inexperienced via ferrata climbers and children should definitely take the appropriate via ferrata equipment with them. If you choose the variant described here with the descent via the Gimpelhaus, either park a car in Nesselwängle and drive back to Grän or keep the bus times in mind to get back to the starting point after the tour.

title: From the beach of Le Palus to the headland of the Bec de Vir
short_description: For a unique view of the highest cliffs in Brittany by the customs path.
long_description:
The beach of Le Palus in Plouha is a beach well known to families. Surrounded by cliffs, it offers a perfect setting to rest and contemplate. The famous customs path (GR34) passes through this beach. This hike along the cliffs takes part of this trail. It will take you to the tip of the Bec de Vir, from where you can enjoy the view of the Palus and part of the highest cliffs in Brittany.
From the Pointe du Bec de Vir, you can enjoy a panoramic view from the bay of Saint-Brieuc and the Penthièvre coast in the east to Bréhat in the north, beyond the Pointe de Minard en Plouézec.
An orientation table will complete your "geographical panorama".

images.caption: The cliffs from the beach of Palus
View of the Palus from the Bec de Vir point

title: Along the Ryck from Greifswald to Wieck
short_description: We get to know the surroundings of Greifswald on this hike: Highlights are the fishing village of Wieck with its drawbridge and the Eldena monastery ruins.
long_description: We start our walk at one of Greifswald's outstanding sights, St. Nikolai's Cathedral. Then we keep to the right and walk to the market (1). At the end of the market, we walk through Knopfstraße to the harbour on the river Ryck. Now we just stay to the right of the river and walk along the Old Harbour (2) towards the east. On the opposite bank we soon see the young marina. Finally, we leave the former harbour area behind us and a quiet footpath and cycle path leads us along the banks of the Ryck to Wieck. In Wieck our path ends and we walk along the road "An der Mühle" until we reach the Gasthaus Fischer Hütte. Behind it on the right, the "Studentensteig" branches off, leading us to the well-known Eldena monastery ruins (3), which the painter Caspar David Friedrich set in scene in several paintings against different backdrops. After visiting the monastery ruins, we walk parallel to the road in an easterly direction until after 200 m the Boddenweg branches off to the left. It leads us to the shore of the Bodden and we pass the large car park to the drawbridge (4), which was built on the Dutch model. Here we cross the river and walk on the opposite side along the bulwark to the lighthouse. Benches invite you to linger at the last house, the Utkiek restaurant (5). On a clear day, the tower at the restaurant offers a wide view over Wieck and the Greifswald Bodden. It is also worth taking a short walk through the picturesque village. Via Dorfstraße, Kirchstraße, Rosenstraße and again Dorfstraße we reach well-preserved fishermen's and captain's houses (6) with their typical thatched roofs. Then we return to the drawbridge. On the southern side of the Ryk is the bus stop for the bus to Greifswald.

images.caption: We look out over the harbour and old warehouses on the banks of the Ryck in Greifswald.
The imposing ruins of the Cistercian monastery of Hilda still impress today.
At the market near the town hall, we look back through Lappstraße to St. Nikolai's Cathedral.
The thatched houses of Wieck are worth a walk through the village.

title: Baepi Peak Trail
short_description: Short trail, but of moderate difficulty due to its high elevation, that goes to the most famous peak of Ilhabela.
long_description: The trail of Pico do Baepi is approximately 3 km long, ending at the 1,048 m of altitude of its summit. The trail is well consolidated, does not require the accompaniment of guides, besides being excellently articulated, as there are no bifurcations. On the way, it is possible to admire various species of fauna and flora of the region, as well as the pleasure of being all the time in the midst of the exuberance of the Atlantic Forest. <The trail is well signposted, with pink ribbons tied to the trees and some wooden plaques that, besides indicating altitudes distance covered be covered, in linear metres, contain information of an educational environmental nature names trees. From summit there a privileged panoramic view, where it possible see Serra do Mar, Alcatrazes Archipelago several other peaks, as wonderful view San Sebastian Channel.

title: Short shore excursion through the Fischbach Valley
short_description: From Fischbach on Lake Constance, this nice hike takes us away from the lake through the Lake Constance hinterland.
long_description: We hike through fields, meadows and small villages in the Fischbacher Senke. Our tour begins in Fischbach with its old village centre, where we cross the Brunnisach over a stone bridge and pass old half-timbered farmhouses and the church of St. Vitus. Outside Fischbach, a short section of our trail runs along the Brunnisach, which runs in wide loops through the valley. We pass the old oak mill and can have our well-deserved dinner on the way at the Gasthof Gehrenbergblick in Kluftern. We continue through orchards and past the Höge and Ziegelacker farms. Over bridges, meadows and paths, the path finally leads us back to Fischbach.

title: Skiathos, Kastros Beach (Route no. 6)
short_description:
Incredible route perfect for a day trip. Passing by beautiful churches and historic houses, always with a view of the sea in the background. Halfway along the way is the incredible Kastro beach where pausing, enjoying the crystal clear water and a drink at the small bar is almost a must.
It's a great place for a day trip.
Of the most beautiful hikes I've ever done, you couldn't ask for more for a one-day hike.
It's the most beautiful hike I've ever done, you couldn't ask for more for a one-day hike.
long_description:
Circular route number 6 starts at the Evangelist Monastery "Theotokou",
The route starts at the Evangelist Monastery "Theotokou".
Passing through incredible scenery, beautiful ancient churches, the lost and natural beach of Kastro as well as the fascinating views all along the route, make this one of the best routes to experience in the area.
For the route you should plan a full day to have enough time to enjoy Kastro beach and to visit all the small churches along the way.
It is a recommended hike.
This route is recommended all year round and has a medium level of difficulty. There are no very difficult or climbing areas, but it is so long that it does not allow shortcuts or a quicker return to the start. However, it does pass through some streets where you can still ask passing cars to take you back or call a taxi.

title: Hiking over artificial mountains through the Saar coal forest
short_description: Until now, the Saarland was known more for mining than for unspoilt nature. This has changed in the meantime, as this hike through the Saar coal forest shows us. Here, nature is once again allowed to develop naturally.
long_description:
This hike is not for the untrained: functional hiking clothing, good shoes and good physical condition are the prerequisites for this tour. From the starting point, the Heinrichshaus Saarbahn stop, we walk in the direction of Forsthaus Neuhaus. On the way, we pass the Kleiner Fuji, an approximately 30-metre-high heap cone. Once you have completed the steep climb, you will be rewarded at the top with a magnificent panoramic view of the Saar coal forest. We walk through the Steinbachtal/Netzbachtal forest reserve to the Steinbachtal biotope and the Gouvys pond. Named after Pierre Gouvy, a French industrialist, the pond is now used for recreation. We reach the Neuhaus forester's lodge, which was once built as the "Jagdschlo&szlig Philippsborn". In recent years, its barn has been converted into a centre for forest culture with a wide range of ecological and artistic activities.
Our route continues to the Netzbachweiher pond, where we can stop off at the "Zum Seeblick" inn. If you want, you can make a detour to the Lydia slag heap with its "sky mirrors". In the 1950s, two conical slagheaps began to be built, which were later combined to form a table mountain. On the plateau, from which you have a great view of the Saar coal forest and the Sulzbach and Fischbach valleys, there are now three "sky mirrors" filled with rainwater. But beware: the tour is extended by about 5 km.
Then we follow the course of the Fischbach and come to the Grühlingstra&szlig slagheap. Here the "literary ascent" takes us to a plateau with a summit cross.
After we have reached the top of the slag heap, we walk uphill.
After passing the Steinbach pond, we return towards the starting point.

title: Crossing on foot from Brasov to Rasnov
short_description: An easy and relaxing walk for those who are curious if or how to reach Râșnov on foot, starting from Brașov; at the same time, a greener alternative to using a car or train, albeit a little longer. Probably a more interesting way to run this route is with an MTB.
long_description:
For the first half, the hike passes through beautiful, apparently deserted forests; then it turns into a hotspot for picnics, sunbathing, and barbecues, especially for locals. In the last half, you'll get to walk mostly on asphalt.
Children may enjoy the route, at least in part, though it might become boring after a while.
The first few kilometers, through Valea Sticlăriei, are enjoyable at any time of year: the forest unveils its trees with captivating shapes and a web of roots, lush foliage, and paths that are not very crowded. Following the exit to Poiana Brașov, to Stâna Turistică, respectively, you can stop for lunch or refreshments.
You then follow a dusty macadam road that takes you to Poiana Aviatorilor. On both sides of the road, you'll see families picnicking, as well as tourists boasting their ATV driving skills, especially during weekends.
After Poiana Aviatorilor, a wilder path follows. Though it shows few signs of ever being trodden, it safely takes you to the more touristy Poiana Cristian. From here, you'll start a steep, short descent through a rustling forest. After reaching the DN1E road and another 4-5 kilometers on asphalt, you enter Rasnov, close to Dino Park.

images.caption: Macadam road close to Poiana Aviatorilor

title: Walking tour Ellhofen "with bite" (Tobel, Balzer Berg and back)
short_description: Versatile (walking) loop from Ellhofen through the Ellhofer Tobel, up to the Balzer Berg and back to the village of Ellhofen.
long_description: From Ellhofen we walk a short distance along the edge of the ravine, then descend to the Tobelmühle and follow the Tobelbach stream. After about one kilometre, we leave the Tobel to the left towards Balzer Berg - and follow the rest of the route. At the end of the crossing, we keep left and walk back down along the flank. Finally, we descend again into the Tobel (the lowest point is the small bridge over the Tobelbach, where there was an open-air swimming pool until the 1940s) and from here up again and back to the village.

title: Skåneleden - Österlenleden - Stage 2
short_description: The second stage of the Österlenleden runs from Nybrostrand to Löderups Strandbad.
long_description:
The tranquil little town of Nybrostrand lies a few kilometres east of Ystad on the Swedish coast and consists mainly of holiday homes. In the summer season Nybrostrand is a popular seaside resort, but outside the season you will meet few people here. If you are well wrapped up, you will get to know the rough side of the Baltic Sea in the winter months, with high waves and cutting winds.
The highlight of this tour is clearly the huge stone rocks "Ales Stenar" west of Kåseberga, which are considered the "Stonehenge of Sweden". The almost 60 rocks were probably collected and erected there in Viking times. We also pass the meditation place Backåkra shortly before Löderup's lido.

title: 10k Jogging Runde Richtung Bachtelweiher (Kempten)
short_description:
Schöne 10km Jogging Runde die in Kempten startet, entlang der Iller führt und dich anschließend Richtung Landschaftspark Engelhalde, Bachtelweiher und Fischhalterwiesen lotst (perfekt für den Sommer)
Translate to English
long_description:
Diese 10 km Jogging-Runde in Kempten startet im Herzen der Stadt und führt dich zunächst entlang der Iller zum Illerwehr. Hier überquerst du mit herrlichem Ausblick den Fluss. Auf der anderen Flussseite lässt du schon bald das Stadtleben hinter dir und tauchst in die Natur ein. Der Weg führt dich durch den Landschaftspark Engelhalde, wo dich weite Grünflächen und frische Luft erwarten. Weiter geht es Richtung Bachtelweiher, einem idyllischen See, der sich perfekt zum kurzen durchschnaufen oder auch einer frischen Abkühlung und Genießen der Umgebung eignet. Die Strecke bietet eine angenehme Mischung aus urbanen Abschnitten und ruhigen Naturpfaden. Dabei sind leichte Anstiege und abwechslungsreiche Wege eine willkommene Herausforderung für erfahrene Läufer, aber auch für entspannte Jogger geeignet. Der Rückweg führt dich wieder Richtung Kempten, wo du die Runde wieder auf der anderen Seite der iller beendest. Diese Route ist ideal, um dem Alltag zu entfliehen und gleichzeitig fit zu bleiben, während du die Schönheit der Allgäuer Natur erlebst.
Translate to English

title: उनाकोटी पहाड़ी ट्रैक
short_description: त्रिपुरा राज्य के कैलाशहर के घने जंपुई जंगलों वाला यह पहाड़ी ट्रैक, चट् टानों में उकेरी गयी भगवान शिव और अन्य देवताओं की विशाल मूर्तियों के बीच से होकर उनाकोटी पहाड़ के शीर्ष तक जाता है।
long_description:
उनाकोटी को अक्सर भारत का माचू-पिच्चू भी कहा जाता है।
इस छोटे लेकिन आकर्षक ट्रैक की खासियत लगभग 11वी -13वी शताब्दियों के दौरान चट्टानों पर बनाई गयी विशाल मूर्तियां हैं। यह दक्षिण एशिया के सबसे आश्चर्यजनक विरासत स्थलों में से एक है और कंबोडिया के अंगकोर-वाट मंदिर की मूर्तियों की याद दिलाता है।
यह ट्रैक 2 किलोमीटर से भी छोटा है और मुख्यत प्राकृतिक ट्रेल के साथ साथ सीढ़ियों से बना है। पूरी ट्रेल में थोड़ी-थोड़ी दूरी पर अनोखी मूर्तियां उकेरी गयी हैं। ट्रेल का कठिनाई स्तर 'आसान' है। नए हों या अनुभवी, किसी भी हाइकर को इसे पूरा करने में कोई कठिनाई नहीं आनी चाहिए।
हर साल अप्रैल के महीने में उनाकोटी में अशोक अष्टमी का प्रसिद्ध एक बड़ा मेला लगता है। इस उत्सव में हजारों तीर्थयात्री आते हैं। ऐसा ही एक और छोटा त्योहार जनवरी में भी आयोजित होता है।उनाकोटी पहाड़ियां के बारे में बीते कुछ सालों से सोशल मीडिया, इंटरनेट लेखों, व्लॉगस और वीडियोज के माध्यम से बहुत जाग्रति आयी है। पिछले कुछ वर्षों से यहाँ आने वाले पर्यटकों की संख्या में निरंतर बढ़ावा हो रहा है और यह त्रिपुरा के सबसे लोकप्रिय पर्यटन स्थलों में से एक बनने की राह पर बढ़ रहा है।

title: The Sheepfolds' Trail in Șureanu Mountains
short_description: Potecu' Stânelor - loosely translated as the Sheepfolds' Trail - is the perfect hike for anyone looking for THE detail that usually recommends Romania as an "authentic" tourist destination. It brings together hiking as a form of discovering the area and a traditional element - sheep breeding and the making of dairy products.
long_description:
There are 6 sheepfolds („stână”, in Romanian) along the route:
Stâna Luncile Prigoanei
Stâna Prisaca
Stana La Aurelia
Stâna Aușel
Stâna Puru I "Plai"
Stâna Puru II "Izvor"
  Depending on the time of year and availability at each sheepfold, you can stop and maybe take part in some specific activities (milking, making dairy products, etc.). Or enjoy a hot, traditional meal (polenta with cheese, basically).
There are also a few cabins on the way, since the route passes over the Șureanu ski slope, so a touristy area. The maximum altitude is a little over 2000 meters, close to the Aușel Peak.

images.caption: Classic mountain signs plus the signs specific of this trail
Typical landscape along the way and specific signs

title: Running circuit: park of the Domaine de Marly
short_description: The ideal nature horsehair to stretch your legs
long_description:
<Built by J. H. Mansart, the estate was used as a summer residence for Louis XIV. The castle destroyed in early 19th century, but park is still available to visitors.
A few miles from Paris and a stone's throw from Versailles is the ideal place to go for a jog "in town" while enjoying the countryside. If you go there in the morning, you may be lucky enough to see some animals.

The Domaine national de Marly is open to the public every day from 8am to 5.30pm from November 1st to March 31st (low season) and from 7.30am to 7.30pm from April 1st to October 31st (high season).

title: Rund um Reutte
short_description:
Aussichts- und abwechslungsreiche Wanderung rund um den Reutter Talkessels.

Durch die Wiesen wandern wir zurück zum Ausgangspunkt.

title: Skåneleden - Österlenleden - Stage 1
short_description: The first stage of the Österlenleden leads from Ystadt along the coast to Nybrostrand.
long_description:
Even before we start our hike, it is worth visiting the town of Ystad. There are narrow streets, picturesque half-timbered houses and a beautiful church to visit. Ystad is also well known to crime fiction fans, as it was the home of the famous detective Kurt Wallander, who plays the main role in Henning Mankell's novels of the same name.
Along the coast we then hike the first stage to Nybrostrand. Our path takes us on flat terrain past bathing beaches and fishing bays and through a beautiful pine grove planted at the beginning of the 20th century.

title: Au fil du Doubs: Die Schweizer Flussroute
short_description:
Auf der einen Seite Frankreich, auf der andern die Schweiz, und mittendurch fliesst ein Fluss: der Doubs. Sein wildromantisches, langes Tal ist kaum bewohnt und wird als Naturpark noch mehr zum Paradies für Fischer und Wanderer. Ein besonders ursprüngliches Stück Schweiz eröffnet der Uferweg zwischen Soubey und St-Ursanne. Er führt in vier Stunden, vorbei an Fischbeizli und Badeplätzen, durch eine fast unberührte Flusslandschaft.
Translate to English
long_description:
Zwischen Soubey und Saint-Ursanne liegen 15 Kilometer meditatives Wandervergnügen und einer der schönsten «Wasserwege» der Schweiz. Im Hotel du Cerf in Soubey, dem Ausgangspunkt der leichten, aber langen Wanderung, gibt es nur ein Thema: Fische. Damit ist nicht nur die Speisekarte gemeint, das Restaurant ist das «Basislager» der Angelfreunde.
Danach gehts dem Fluss entlang weiter nach Tariche. Sollte man hier auf der falschen Flussseite sein, wenn man den Doubs schon bei La Charbonnière überquert hat, ist das auch kein Problem: Einfach ein wenig gestikulieren und rufen, und schon rückt der Wirt mit seinem Boot aus und setzt die Gäste fürs Mittagessen über. Spezialität des Hauses? Natürlich Forelle.
Die Flusslandschaft nahe an der Grenze zu Frankreich überrascht auch mit ihrer reichhaltigen Flora und Fauna und verzaubert mit ihrer Ruhe. Das historische Zentrum des mittelalterlichen Städtchens St-Ursanne schliesslich hat sich über die Jahrhunderte nur wenig verändert und vermittelt mit seinen Bürgerhäusern aus dem 14. bis 16. Jahrhundert Geschichte. Bekannteste Sehenswürdigkeit ist das Kloster mit Kreuzgang und romanisch-gotischer Stiftskirche, deren Ursprünge auf das 12. Jahrhundert zurückgehen.
Translate to English

title: From Furth im Wald to the Dieberg
short_description: We hike through the historic old town of Furth im Wald via an underwater observation station to the observation tower on the Dieberg.
long_description: From the car park, we turn left into Freudensprungstraße and turn right into Bahnhofstraße. We leave this to the right into Postgartenweg. When this ends, we follow Lorenz-Zierl-Straße to the left and its course to the right, past the baroque parish church of the Assumption of Mary (built 1725-1727). Soon after, we turn left into Burgstraße and now walk through the core of the historic old town of Furth im Wald. We pass the old town hall on the right, whose historic walls date back to the 16th century and were probably the seat of civic self-government as early as 1332. On the left is the historic market square, the scene of the famous "Drachenstich", the oldest folk play in Germany. We continue straight ahead and pass the tourist information office uphill. On the right we see the town tower, built in 1866 to replace the keep of the medieval Pflegerschloss, which had been destroyed by a devastating town fire three years earlier. Directly adjacent to the town tower is the Furth im Wald Landestorm Museum, where you can also find the First German Dragon Museum. The monster used for the "Drachenstich" is stored in this house outside the play season. We continue straight ahead across the Schlossplatz and follow a pedestrian path at its end. This leads into Rosenstraße, which we follow to the left. Then we follow the signs "Wanderweg F1" in the direction of Dieberg to the right and get downhill onto a footpath. This leads into a road, which we follow to the right and shortly afterwards turn left in the direction of the open-air swimming pool. At the next fork in the road, we choose the right-hand option and continue straight ahead. We cross a bridge and pass the Chamb. Directly after the bridge, the open-air swimming pool on the right invites us to refresh ourselves in the warm months. The path leads into a road, which we follow briefly to the left and then leave at the first turn to the left. We walk past the Einberg campsite. Shortly afterwards, we find a very original rest area on the left side of the path with wooden seating and stone tables as well as a water pump. Directly opposite is the entrance to the wild garden. This beautifully arranged area offers a lot of interesting information about nature and is very vividly designed. The highlight of the garden is an underwater observation station at a pond. Here we can observe the fish living in the pond through large panes of glass, just like in a zoo aquarium. These include pike, roach, zander and perch. Shortly after the wildlife garden, we cross the Chamb on a very beautiful wooden bridge. Now we follow a path straight ahead that leads along the bank of a stream. Behind a crossing, it continues as a path and joins a road, which we follow to the right. We pass the level crossing and walk uphill towards the edge of the forest. There, at the school bus stop, we continue to the left and shortly afterwards follow the signs to the right into the forest. Soon the hiking trail "F1" branches off to the left in the direction of Dieberg onto the Herbert-Hartl-Steig. This leads us to the Dieberg hut of the Further mountain rescue service, in front of which a nice rest area invites us to take a break. We continue along the hiking trail "F1" in the direction of the Bayernwarte. This beautiful wooden lookout tower offers a magnificent view. It was built in 1974/75 by the Further mountain rescue service and is 20 m high. From the Bavarian Observatory we follow the hiking trail "F1" in the direction of Furth im Wald. It leads us beautifully through the forest down into the valley. We pass the Hackl Chapel and cross a railway tunnel. In the valley we come across the new "Drachensee". The reservoir, which serves as a flood retention basin for the Chamb, will be flooded from 2008. We walk back along the river and meet up with the outward route.

title: Through the Saalegau near Euerdorf
short_description: On this tour, we hike through the beautiful river meadows of the Saalegau, which were created by the impressive loop of the Franconian Saale near Aura and Euerdorf.
long_description: Our circular hike starts directly at the Franconian Saale, where there is also an information board with the circular hiking trails of the region. The tour leads us to the old town hall of Aura. Directly next to the building, a cross path leads us up to the parish church of Sankt Laurentius (1), the former monastery church of the Aura monastery. We follow the circular hiking trail with the "2" on this section. There is a wayside shrine behind the cemetery. Walk past it and continue up the hill on the meadow behind it. We walk along the edge of the valley and through orchards with a wonderful view of the valley of the Franconian Saale with the Trimburg ruins in the southwest. The slopes along which we are now walking were once vineyards. At a pasture fence, our path turns up to the left and we reach a forest path. We walk along it a few metres to the left, then turn right and already see the "Ruine Aura" inn in front of us, adjoined by the walls of the same name. Here we can take a rest and also have a closer look at the remains of the monastery building that was never completed. At the ruins we find a signpost pointing east towards Euerdorf, marked "RA1". We now follow it and walk past a cattle pasture to the edge of the forest. We cross a forest road there and now walk on a wider path through the Hainbuch. On a level stretch, our hike now leads through copper beeches and we leave the field of vision of the Saalegau for a few kilometres. At Männerholz, we cross a forest road and continue straight ahead through the forest, past a small statue of a saint, until we meet a forest road that slopes down. On it, we go downhill for a few metres to a crossroads. Here we turn right and hike out of the forest on a paved gravel path. At the beginning of the meadow, there is a wooden table and benches (2) on the right, where you can stop and take a break. The trail continues across orchard meadows to Euerdorf, which we can already see ahead of us in the valley. We reach the village via the Alte Kissinger Straße and walk down to the Fränkische Saale and cross it at the old Saale bridge. On the river bank (3) there are benches for resting and an information board for hikers. Opposite, we can stop at the Wolz inn and fortify ourselves for the return march to Aura. In front of the gatehouse, turn left into Ringstraße and walk up to the Willibrords Chapel (4) at the cemetery. Via Bahnhofstraße we finally reach the centre of the village. At the fountain on the market square, we walk up Hammelburger Straße, which brings us in front of the parish church of Sankt Johannes (5) in Euerkirchen. We turn right in front of the church into a small alley, walk along a path to the ring road and cross it. Now we reach the Franconian Saale again. We leave the town on the left side of the river. Our path now leads us across the floodplain back towards Aura. We hike through the very quiet and scenic river landscape and once again enjoy the magnificent view (6) of the Aura monastery church and the old vineyards. Via the Wässerungsweg (watering path) we reach the main road in Aura and cross the bridge over the Fränkische Saale to reach the car park again and the destination of this beautiful circular walk. We can now stop off at the "Zur alten Brauerei" inn, directly at the car park in Aura.

title: From the lake to the castle - Meinhard
short_description: A loop from Lake Werratal to Wolfsbrunnen Castle, a forest cemetery and a secluded vantage point.
long_description:
We start at the camping park. At first, the route is easy and flat along the lake until you reach the main road. Crossing the road is sometimes difficult, but unfortunately unavoidable.
On field paths and then upwards through the forest we reach the castle. Here you can take a short tour of the park.
Further up through the forest we reach a cemetery where the von Keudells are buried, a family that resided here.
After this little idyll, we walk back along the path for a short distance and then up along a path through the forest and then continue along gravel and asphalt paths to a path that is hardly used and to beautifully and solitarily situated meadows.
On the way back we walk through Schwebda past old half-timbered houses and the estate.
At point 08 we can decide whether to go back the same way or still walk around the lake on asphalt to the starting point.

title: Walking route Loonse and Drunense dunes
short_description: This walking route is 10 kilometres and takes about 2.5 hours.
long_description: You walk across the beautiful Loonse and Drunense dunes. This nature reserve is located in the south of the Netherlands. During the route, you first walk through a beautiful forest. The forest is rooted in loose sand. After that, you walk a bit on the sandy plains with large areas of heathland.

short_description: Short hike with a beautiful view of Nemmersdorf and the Kronach valley.
long_description: The hike takes us through the beautiful landscape to the south of Nemmersdorf. We enjoy wonderful views of Nemmersdorf and the Kronach valley. We have to climb a steeper ascent, otherwise the short hike is effortless.

Découvrez le Pas de la Balme, un des rares points de passage de la barrière Est du Vercors permettant de rejoindre le plateau dit des "Quatre-Montagnes"et qui fût un haut lieu de la Résistance du maquis du Vercors !
