title: From Bad Kissingen to the Klauswald
short_description: We experience a long, varied day tour that takes us along the Franconian Saale and through the Klauswald forest.
long_description: From the car park "In der Au" we walk to the Schweizer Haus and cross the bridge of the same name over the Fränkische Saale. At the promenade path we turn left and walk upstream out of Bad Kissingen. On this stretch we also encounter our trail marking for the first time, a black "K" on a golden sceptre, the Karolingerweg. We walk around the Heinz-Kalk-Klinik and come across the graduation building (1), where salt used to be extracted and which is now used as a spa. On the opposite side of the river, the Auwiesen meadows stretch out and we soon see the Bismarck Museum, which is located in the Upper Saline and is worth a detour. Passing the bottling plant of the Theresienquelle, we reach the village of Hausen with its former monastery and immediately cross the Nüdlinger Bach stream at a small bridge and a little later also the Saale. Now we walk along the left bank and reach Kleinbrach. In the village, we turn right into Tränkgasse and walk under the main road. We soon find ourselves back in the Saale valley and walk along a small path through the floodplain meadows. The path describes a bend and leads us across the Saale again at a weir house. On the opposite bank of the river is the Luitpold-Sprudel (2). Healing water has been flowing here since 1912 and we can fill our water bottle with it. We finally walk to the road and under it. Then we keep to the right and at a crossroads to the left. We walk close to the Franconian Saale again and can now already make out the castle in Aschach in front of us through the treetops. At the edge of Großenbrach, we turn left onto a cycle path that takes us to the bridge in Aschach. We hike into the village and have now earned a first rest in the garden of the castle (3). In the centre of the village, we then turn right into Von-Henneberg-Straße, which takes us in the direction of the sports field. We now leave the Karolingerweg and follow the black double triangle that points us to the Premicher Straße. We walk up the hill and past the turnoff to the sports field. After about 500 m we find a signpost to Frauenroth and turn left here. We now walk along orchard meadows and can look back over the valley of the Franconian Saale, which we have walked through. At a crossroads, we enter the forest and walk over the Bauersberg to Frauenroth. We reach the monastery walls at the edge of the village and turn left in front of them. A famous minnesinger is buried in the monastery church (4). In the centre of the village, we turn into the Schmalzmühlweg, which takes us up the hill over a small stream. We cross a crossroads with a crucifix and reach another crossroads with a bench. Here we turn left and have to change to a path on the left at the next bend. This brings us to the Schmalzmühle and we also cross the Aschach here. Continue along the road for a while, which we cross after 300 m and reach Stralsbach via a forest road. In the inn "Zum Weißen Rössl" we can now take a longer break and fortify ourselves. We then walk through the village and turn left into the Silberdiestelweg. This leads up to the Hermannsruhe forester's lodge (5). We hike over the crossroads and are now in the Klauswald. Now we follow the yellow triangle on a white background, which takes us down to a wooden cross. Here we turn left and reach the Klaushof with game enclosure, where we can also stop for a bite to eat. Behind the inn, our path now leads along the road to the Kaskadental valley (6). We follow the man-made course of the river until we reach a small covered rest house. Here we turn right and hike down the hill until we reach the Schweizer Haus again. Soon we have reached the destination of our day trip on the left again.

title: Nature trail around Buhui Lake
short_description: Locally known as the "Buhui Lake Circuit", this nature trail route is a pleasant walk around the lake suitable for anyone. Chose to stroll around the lake solo, with your family, with children, with your dog, at any time of the year. Stop from time to time to read the panels and learn bits and pieces about the ecosystem around you.
long_description:
The panels mention details about the tree species in the Semenic - Caraș Gorges Natural Park, with an emphasis on the whereabouts, as well as on the formation of the lake. Precious info is offered on the evolution of the amphibian species or the geological aspects here.
The route is perfectly suitable for trail running or mountain biking.
Don't miss the two viewpoints on the route.

title: A day out at the Kolomna Kremlin
short_description: The Kolomna Kremlin has survived the centuries and survives to this day. In the town of Kolomna by the Moskva River stands a majestic Kremlin, little known to modern times.
long_description:
The Kremlin was laid out as early as the 13th century in wooden furnishings. In earlier centuries, strange invasions came constantly, and in one such event the Kremlin was set on fire by the Crimean khans. The history of Kolomna did not stop there and in the 15th century already Vasiliy the Third, father of Vasiliy the Great, issued a decree on the laying of a new and mighty Kremlin in Kolomna. Red brick in the walls of the Kremlin perpetuated the old town of Kolomna.
Today on the territory of the Kolomna Kremlin it is real to spend free time, enjoy the sky within its walls, go on excursions – a great cultural success and to feel yourself a part of the world by the Moscow River in the Kremlin structures – this is a guarantee of intentional health and generosity for many years to come.

short_description: Beautiful hiking tour from Fischen along the Iller, through Oberstdorf to the Freibergsee.

title: Ås til Åsleden - Timan to Rebbetuaröd
short_description: The tenth stage of the s til Åsledens goes from Timan to Rebbetuaröd.
long_description: This stage also takes you over the Linder hills. The impressive moorland areas of Viss Mosse and Fjällmossen and the extensive forests around them have long been used as hiding places by migratory birds, but today we only see black grouse, which we can watch from a birdwatching tower on Fjällmossen. At 21 km, this is the longest stage of the tour, but it can be shortened if you wish.

title: Creglingen Cultural Landscape Trail
short_description: The short hike offers us not only wonderful nature but also a lot of information about the cultural landscape in this part of the Tauber valley.
long_description: Our starting point is at the end of Klingener Straße, on the outskirts of Creglingen. In the extension of this road, a path leads between two houses into the meadow landscape with individual, scattered trees and rows of trees. On this path we walk along a slope that is home to many protected orchid species and rare insects. An intact cultural landscape has also been preserved here, about which we can learn from 15 information boards along the way. They explain, for example, why steep slope farming was necessary for survival in the past, or how the wealth of the builder can be read from the typical dry stone walls that delimit the fields here. On our way we meet a herd of dwarf zebu cattle, a breed that also eats dry grass. In a wooded area we come to a crossroads where we turn right and soon meet a wider path. We follow it for a bit, but then turn right again into the meadow landscape and return to our starting point on the outskirts of Creglingen. After the tour, it is worth taking a detour into Creglingen's town centre. In addition to numerous places to stop for refreshments, such as the "Grüner Baum" restaurant, there are also many historical buildings and museums here, such as the Lindlein Museum in the old defence and watchtower, or the Jewish Museum.

title: The Friesenried Forest Bird Trail near Kaufbeuren
short_description: A hike into the realm of birds.
long_description:
The forest bird nature trail near Friesenried teaches us about nature in a special way: At 20 stations, hikers are introduced to a total of 30 native bird species. The interested walker learns that the long-eared owl does not build its own nests and that the stock dove is not stupid despite its name. All nature discoverers are invited to take part in the bird quiz. The quiz sheets are available at the beginning of the nature trail or as a PDF file on the internet at http://www.vgem-eggenthal.de.
The trail is suitable for prams and wheelchairs. The paths are paved and have only slight inclines. There are benches along the way for a rest.

images.caption: We can learn in detail about the world of birds on the walk.

title: From Bürchau through the small Wiesental
short_description: Bürchau is located in the far southwest of Germany in a widening of the Kleine Wiesental. Well-marked hiking trails lead you through the entire Kleine Wiesental.
long_description: We start at the Sonnhalde mountain inn, located at the Hollbach biotope nature reserve at the foot of the 1415 m high Belchen. From here we walk uphill along the asphalted road to Obere Sonnhalde (1). Here we follow the signposting of the blue rhombus downhill in the direction of Bürchau to the right into the forest to the Silberberg shelter (2). Via the clog forest (3), the trail leads uphill to the pointer. Following the middle path downhill, we reach the beautiful viewpoint Silbereck (4) with a view of the Belchen. After a short stretch in the forest, we reach the Hau car park (5) between meadows and pastures with a view into the valley. From here, a small footpath leads us down to the village of Neuenweg (6). In the centre of the village, walk along the road towards Bürchau and turn left at the first opportunity. We walk uphill along a forest path until we reach the clog forest again. From here we walk back to the Silberberg refuge as for the outward route and reach the car park via the Obere Sonnhalde.

images.caption: We pass many attractive Black Forest farms during our tour.
Impressive views of the surroundings arise during our tour.
Village structures in the Black Forest village of Bürchau.

title: Pedra Furada Trail
short_description: Trail that leads to one of the main attractions of Jericoacoara, the Holed Stone, going by the Hill of Serrote and returning by the beautiful coastline with several caves and natural pools.
long_description:
Leaving from Jericoacoara Beach, start the route along the street Forró and cross the centre of Jericoacoara Village until é the beginning of the path to é the Pedra Furada that passes through the Serrote Hill. No doubt this is the shortest way, but you will have to face the climb up the Serrote, which is the highest point of the National Park of Jericoacoara, approximately 100 m high, and where there is a lighthouse that makes the scenery even more beautiful from the top.The advantage of taking the Serrote is that regardless of the sea, you can get there.
After visiting Pedra Furada, go back through Malhada Beach, where there are several rocks, caves and natural pools, which you can stop and enjoy. The ideal thing é plan this route in advance to check the time of the high sea that makes it impossible to return by the coast, being obligatory to return by the Serrote again.

title: Pozanti - Belemedik
short_description: Pozantı - Belemedik route is one of the alternative routes for those looking for a route in Adana
long_description:
There are many beauties you can discover in Adana. There are also different routes for travellers.
Pozantı - Belemedik bölge is a popular bölge for those looking for a nature route in Adana. The paths and roads where you can walk between the sloping structure of the bölge and where you can be accompanied by the Çakıt Water are ideal for those who want to realise the activity of walking. While travelling in this region, you can adventure on tracks that will challenge yourself, or you can do calm and short hikes. Important historical and cultural values of the region accompany you during your journey.
This route, which is parallel to Akıt Water, is one of the alternative routes you can try in this region. The route starting from Pozantı extends to Belemedik. On the route, there are areas where you can take a break on the shore of Çakıt Water. 
You can capture Belemedik landscapes that turn into different colours in different seasons.

title: Hechenberger panoramic tour from Dietramszell
short_description: This long hike takes us through the fields around Hechenberg - we also reach the Kirchsee lake with its leisure facilities.
long_description: We start our panoramic walk at the car park above the monastery in Dietramszell. We walk downhill and past the Dietramszell monastery (1). Behind the monastery we keep to the right and follow the signposted road to Obermühlthal. For 2 km we walk along the Zellerbach - a wonderful idyllic landscape awaits us. After passing through Obermühltal, we turn right towards Niederreuth. Behind the small footbridge over the Zellerbach we enter the forest and later into open terrain. Finally we see Walleiten. However, we do not enter the village, but continue straight on to Hechenberg. Here we have the opportunity to take a shortcut: if you don't want to make the detour to Hechenberg, you can hike directly to Helfertsried from here and then rejoin the Hechenberger Aussichtsrunde. Our actual route to Hechenberg runs in a constant up and down. In Hechenberg (2) the restaurants around the village square offer us the opportunity to take a break. After strengthening ourselves, we make a U-turn, keep to the right and hike along a small side road to Helfertsried. Here we go uphill to the right. We stay on the road until we reach the state road 2368 after a descent. We cross it and walk straight ahead into the forest. Now we follow the large signs. We stay on the forest path until we reach a wooden sign pointing us left to Kirchsee and right to Bad Tölz. We keep to the right and at the next opportunity turn left, again towards Bad Tölz. Soon we leave the forest and in front of us is the Kogl farm, which we cross. Behind the farm we go downhill until we turn left onto the hiking trail S5 to Kirchsee. Now the path runs directly along the shore of the Kirchsee (3). Enjoy the wonderful view, including the church of Sachsenkam. There are numerous park benches on the shore and nothing stands in the way of a short rest. Finally, the path along the riverbank changes to Kirchseestrae. To the left and right of the path, many a beautiful house is hidden in the forest. At the eastern end of the Kirchsees there is a kiosk (4), a car park and public toilets. From the kiosk we also reach the bathing beach. We now walk on to Stubenbach, where we keep to the left. Behind the village, a forest track begins. A wooden sign signals that we are back on the hiking trail towards Dietramszell. We stay on the path until we come to Wampen Moos. Soon we find another signpost to Dietramszell. We go right, at the next opportunity left uphill and at the next crossroads straight on. We leave the black cross and the green cross on the right and go downhill on the left. Again we follow the signs (wooden arrow on the tree) in the direction of Dietramszell. At the unsigned T-junction we turn left. We hike downhill to the right again and then see the small chapel "Maria Elend" (5) between the Bäumen. The interior of the small chapel, which is open to visitors, is also worth seeing. Behind the chapel, somewhat hidden, are park benches where we can rest. We now walk past the parish hall and back to the monastery. If you feel like it, you can visit the monastery shop. Finally, we can fortify ourselves in the monastery tavern to end the day.

images.caption: A view of the Kirchsee lake with Reutberg Monastery.

title: From Beilngries to Wodansburg Castle with the divining rod
short_description: With dowsing rod in hand, we hike to the Wodansburg vantage point above the Main-Danube Canal and learn all kinds of interesting facts about earth radiation.
long_description: With divining rod in hand, we hike to the vantage point of the Wodansburg above the Main-Danube canal and learn all kinds of interesting about earth radiation. This is the name given to phenomena that are said to have various effects on health. Information boards along the route explain the principle of earth radiation. If you wish, you can buy a wish card at the tourist information office in tourist information office in Beilngries and try out their talent themselves. try out your talent yourself.

title: Along the Düssel into the Neander Valley
short_description: Along the Düssel we experience historic town centres and fascinating river meadows, explore the Neander Valley and reach the Neanderthal Museum at the end.
long_description:
This tour runs from Wülfrath-Aprath to Alt-Hochdahl and always takes us along the Düssel. This tributary of the Rhine gives its name to the state capital Düsseldorf and the village of Düssel. We cross it on our hike and can visit the well-preserved historic centre of the village. Downstream we continue via Tillmannsdorf and Hahnenfurth to Schöller. There we see the keep and remains of the castle wall of the former Schöller manor from the 12th century. A special feature is the square ground plan of the fortified tower.
After visiting the half-timbered houses and the old church tower in Gruiten, we walk on to the Neandertal nature reserve, which presents historical background information on information boards. We now often cross the river and pass ponds until we reach the Winkelsmühle. Passing the Ice Age game reserve, we finally reach the much-visited Neanderthal Museum. There we embark on a journey through four million years of human history with a focus on the Neanderthal man, who was discovered nearby in the middle of the 19th century. The museum works with many interactive elements and is thus an exciting experience at the end of the hike.

title: Going-to-the-Sun Road
short_description: A stunning scenery with rocky mountaintops makes for an interesting ride: Going-to-the-Sun Road in the midst of Glacier National Park takes you along winding roads into Montana’s stunning hinterland
long_description:
Going-to-the-Sun Road is located in the Rocky Mountains and named after the eponymous mountain in Glacier National Park, Montana. There are several legends surrounding its early days. One of them has it that the author James Willard Schultz gave the mountain this name to express its stunning beauty and grace. Nowadays, this scenic route is known as National Historic Place, National Historic Landmark and Historic Civil Engineering Landmark. It has been immortalized in blockbusters such as “The Shining“or „Forrest Gump“ where it reflects the unique scenery in all its beauty and greatness. And it’s even as impressive in real life as it is in the movies, actually.
Nonetheless, you shouldn’t underrate this road: Due to its numerous hairpin turns you should only go there if you’re an experienced driver. That’s why the route is closed in winter time which usually comes across with lots of snow.

images.caption: Distant views of Glacier National Park
On tour with a classic Red Jammer
Logan Pass seen from Bearhat Mountain

title: From the leisure centre in Meinhard to three vantage points - Meinhard Eschwege
short_description: A day hike in beautiful surroundings to the viewpoints Silberklippe and Meinhardsköpfchen. This tour can also be done very well by bike.
long_description:
Start at the leisure centre near Meinhard-Grebendorf.
At first, it is a leisurely walk through the field to a hill. From there you have a wonderful view of Eschwege, the Leuchtberge and the surrounding hills. Shortly afterwards you reach the Diebsgraben, an already impressive depression for our landscape.
On a little-used path, you go up to Neuerode, beautifully situated on the slopes of the Meinhard.
Through Neuerode you reach another very beautiful vantage point, which allows another very beautiful view of the Werratal.
Now the trail continues upwards. Soon you are at the top and have also reached the Silberklippe. This is a good place to take a break.
If you stand at the very front, you can see from left to right: the wind turbines at Struth/Effelder, if you look closely, you can see the "Cathedral of Effelder" on the right of the wheels, Hülfensberg, Plesse, Heldrasteinturm, Schlierbach, Leuchtberge, Ringgau.
If you want, you can take the rightmost path in a north-easterly direction for about another 200 m to Kellablick. Another very impressive view of the village of Kella, which you could not have until 1989.
Take the path back a little way and then follow a beautiful path through the forest to the "Meinhardsköpfchen".
Steeply downhill to the forest car park, once again through Neuerode with beautiful views down to the "Teich in den Rüsten".
Through the road we walk downhill to the Schambach and there along the forest always with a view of beautiful valley meadows.
Through sparse forest we return to the starting point.

title: Nature trail in the Silver Forest (Pădurea de Argint)
short_description: A walk suitable for all ages on a nature trail in the Silver Forest is more than welcome when you tour around the monasteries in Neamț County.
long_description:
To foreign tourists, this might be just another forest, but for Romanians, it's a symbolic place, mentioned in a famous poem written by Mihai Eminescu. The nature trail aims to highlight the importance of the deciduous trees that impressed Eminescu so much.
The information boards are limited to just mentioning various types of trees. However, guessing the trees can be a fun game for children to discover and distinguish the types of leaves, fruits, or bark.
Plenty of resting benches add to the route, even large tables for a picnic, an opportunity to spend some more time under the enchanting breeze of the deciduous trees.
The whole circuit takes 30 minutes tops.

images.caption: Benches and tables on the route

title: The Ruoms gorges - Gorges de l'Ardèche
short_description:
Truly beautiful and easy walk, despite a rather steep downhill section to reach the river.
The divine sandy beach, swimming in the transparent waters of the Ardèche, the magnificent views of the Ruoms dunes and the Cirque de Gens will be the objectives of your hike.

title: De la Chevalerie au château de Champchevrier
short_description:
Les chemins pédestres de Cléré-les-Pins offrent une expérience riche en nature, histoire et patrimoine. 
Translate to English
long_description:
Nichés dans un cadre boisé, ces sentiers vous mèneront au Château de Champchevrier, prisé par Louis XIII. Une randonnée idéale pour les amateurs de paysages et d’histoire. À découvrir de juin à septembre !
Translate to English

title: A hike around the Eibsee
short_description: A circular and easy hike that surrounds the magical Eibsee lake, near the Zug-Spitz mountain. The route passes islands, small lakes and rapids that connect to the lake.
long_description: An easy hiking route rich in views around the Iveza lake, characterized most of the year by transparent waters with a mesmerizing turquoise hue. During the winter the lake freezes and during the summer you can bathe in its waters and rent pedal boats. Along the route you can observe small islands located in the heart of the lake and enjoy small waterfalls that spill into it, as well as small ponds.

title: Hiking through Wadi Nakhur, Jebel Shams
short_description: Wander in the shadows of massive cliffs and embrace the silent vastness of your surroundings on this wadi trip in Oman's al Hajar mountains.
long_description:
Also referred to as Wadi Ghul and unofficially as Oman's 'Grand Canyon', a trip to Wadi Nakhur means getting a valley-floor perspective of the vista anyone who's been up to the viewing points on Jebel Shams will have seen.
The route down Nakhur isn't always drivable, as winter storms and flash floods frequently destroy the track that leads to the little village at the far end. If this is the case, then walking is always a pleasant alternative and one- I feel- that lets you appreciate your surroundings all the more. I have also ridden up here on a donkey.  
The thing that makes Nakhur so spectacular is the massive vertical-to-overhanging cliffs that rise up hundreds of metres straight from wadi bed and while this is not uncommon in Oman, it's the sheer scale of what you see up here that really sets Nakhur apart.

title: Jogging route from Trebiano Magra to Lerici
short_description: This jogging circuit leads from Trebiano Magra to Lerici through partly wooded countryside and past isolated houses.
long_description: The route leads along a small asphalt road that is closed to traffic for a short distance. In parts, the path leads through shady woods. The view back to Trebiano Magra and then out to the harbour and the sea in Lerici is magnificent. Small boats are anchored in the harbour.

title: Birkenhain Street
short_description: Several cycling tours on the Birkenhain road
long_description: In the Middle Ages, the Birkenhainer Stra&szlig was a military and trade route that connected Franconia on the Rhine with Franconia in the East. Prehistoric finds and old fortifications suggest that the history of the route goes back to the Stone and Iron Ages. The route also played an important role in the Middle Ages, which is impressively demonstrated by the stone witnesses along the way.

images.caption: Our path runs past fruit trees and fields.
View of the Neuwirtshaus small fort

title: Around Lake Blaibach
short_description: Magnificent views over the Blaibacher See and the Höllensteinsee await us on this hike.
long_description: From the church we walk to the Black Rain. After crossing both bridges, we turn left to the campsite, which also offers us a chance to stop for a bite to eat. We orientate ourselves by the red and white marker "B5" and follow the river to the dam wall of the Blaibachsee. Now we follow the path along the lake to a silted-up lake area with reeds. Via a staircase we reach the dam of the Höllensteinsee. From the Seeblick inn, we enjoy the view over both lakes during a detour. The path now leads to a picnic area with a Kneipp basin. The varied hike offers us views of the Blaibachsee again and again, including at the rest area near Ahrain. We continue to follow the signs to Blaibach. Behind the campsite we walk back to the church.

images.caption: A picnic area with a view of Lake Blaibach.
The railway bridge over the rain.
The view back to the dam wall of the Blaibachsee.
The view of the Höllensteinsee power station.

title: Randonnée par le sommet du Moucherotte (Vercors)
short_description:
Ce circuit de randonnée permet de rejoindre "Le Moucherotte", un sommet emblématique du Vercors offrant une vue sur Grenoble, les vallées l'Isère et du Drac et au loin le Mont Blanc !
Translate to English
long_description:
Au départ de Les Pucelles, l'itinéraire emprunte un joli sentier en lacets qui serpente en forêt jusqu'à Sous la Dent Gérard. On poursuit jusqu'au Roc Bataillon, les Forges avant d'arriver au sommet du Moucherotte. 
Profitez du panorama exceptionnel avant de redescedre vers le vallon des Forges et le Bois de Poussebou !
Translate to English

title: From Sulzfeld via the Annabild to the Jews' Hill
short_description: This small but beautiful hike from Suzfeld to Kleinbardorf shines with cultural highlights and also offers wonderful distant views.
long_description: From the village square in Sulzfeld, we hike via Raiffeisenstraße up into the forest and soon reach Annabild (1) via a field path. We turn left here and have a beautiful distant view of the two Gleichberge mountains to the north-east. Through dense forest we now reach the Judenhügel with a Jewish cemetery (2). We walk through it and at its end we come across the remains of a prehistoric rampart. The trail then descends steeply to Kleinbardorf, where it is worth making a detour to the moated castle (3). We leave the village via the Celtic ring and hike back to Sulzfeld. We walk down past a meadow and reach the Bärental country inn (4), where we can stop for a bite to eat. Via the sports field we finally return to the village square and the destination of this tour.

images.caption: The Annabild is a chapel that was built in 1745.
The moated castle in Kleinbardorf was built in 1589/90 and is now privately owned.
In the Tahara Hall in the Jewish cemetery, the ritual ablutions were performed on the deceased.
The parish church in Kleinbardorf is dedicated to St. Ägidius and was built in 1709.

title: To the High Mountain near Syke
short_description: This hike takes us to the vantage point on the Hohe Berg. From there we have a magnificent panoramic view as far as the Hanseatic city of Bremen and over the glacial valley of the Weser.
long_description: We start our hike at the school centre on Gesseler Straße in Syke and first cross under the railway tracks, follow the road Am Ristedter Weg to the right. After a while, we reach the edge of the forest and walk along it to the left before turning right into the forest at the second junction. Here we come across the district road Am Spreeken and turn left onto it. Before the road bends to the left and becomes Leerßer Straße, we keep to the right for a short while and then turn left to walk straight along the road Am Hohen Berg to the viewpoint on the hill. The Hohe Berg lies on the northern edge of the Syker Geest and from its crest we have a wonderful view of the Hanseatic city of Bremen and the glacial valley of the Weser. We continue our hike on Casparistraße and come to Leerßen. Here we briefly follow Leerßer Straße to the right and then leave it to the left on the street Am Heidbergbad. We reach a small wood and turn left at the end of our path. After a few metres we turn right and soon meet the road Am Ristedter Weg on the left. Now we walk back to the school centre the same way we came.

title: Bohusleden - Section 18 - Vassbotten to Håvedalen
short_description: The eighteenth stage of Bohusleden leads from Vassbotten to Håvedalen.
long_description: At just under 20 kilometres, this stage is one of the longest on the tour. The trail leads across a characteristic landscape of hills, which was formed when different layers of rock met. In addition, we partly walk along the Swedish-Norwegian border, where there are still a few marker stones.

images.caption: View over the Swedish lake landscape

title: Höglandsleden (Kråkshult-Ingatorp) - Sweden
short_description: The Höglandsleden trails are just as suitable for families as they are for adventurous outdoor enthusiasts. However, the weather conditions play a decisive role in whether all sections of the trail can be walked without "wet feet".
long_description:
Höglandsleden is a circular hiking trail that runs about 454 km through the Småland highlands. Here you can experience the typical Swedish forest landscape, which we all know from Astrid Lindgren's films and stories, on easy and sometimes more challenging trails. Depending on your preference, the individual sections of the trail can be walked as hikes, day tours or multi-day tours, as you can always take a rest in cosy little villages or towns in between.
As Höglandsleden is a circular trail, but we only walked part of it, we had to find a suitable means of transport or take a taxi back to Kråkshult. In Sweden, many places and villages are very remote and therefore have no connection to public transport. The smartest way is to walk towards each other in groups, as the route can also be walked from Ingatorp to Kråkshult.

title: Türle
short_description: The "Türle" and the Engeratsgundsee are the highlights of this varied hike above the Hintersteiner Valley. Surefootedness is required from the Türle to the Gündles-Alpe.

images.caption: Our hike starts on sunny meadows in the Hintersteiner valley.
The door is already in sight.
The first part of the climb takes us through a forest.

title: Via ferrata Graustock
short_description: The via ferrata to the Graustock (2661 m) allows direct ascent of the mountain over an exposed ridge with breathtaking deep views of its north face and Engelberg.
long_description: The via ferrata on the Graustock (2661 m) offers us a mix of mountain path and the overcoming of the partly steep and exposed rocky upturns. Breathtaking views into the 700 m high north face of the Graustock and into the Engelberg valley await us. From the summit we enjoy a magnificent panorama over the peaks Titlis, Spannort, Rigi, Mittelland and Pilatus and the Bernese peaks "Wetterhörner, Schreckhorn and Finsteraarhorn". In early summer, large snow cornices can still protrude over the ridge, also snow bridges over the karst areas can collapse when stepped on. So caution is advised in these places! Orientation is easy in good visibility, but in poor visibility the descent can be a challenge. The ridge is exposed on the southeast side. Pay special attention to the weather forecast, as the entire tour is very exposed and offers no exit possibility.

title: Winter hike on the Urschlauer Achen river
short_description: This easy winter walk in Ruhpolding takes us idyllically along the Urschlauer Achen.
long_description:
The Urschlauer Achen is a tributary of the Weiße Traun and flows through the municipality of Ruhpolding. On this winter hike we follow the course of the river in parts and let the beautiful snow-covered landscape take effect on us. The circular route also scores with a beautiful view of the mountains. The first section of the tour goes along the Sagenweg and there are several places to stop for refreshments along the way.
This beautiful walk can be done at any time of the year.

title: Langenbach Walking Tour near Zwickgabel
short_description: First you follow the flat, meandering path along the beautiful Langenbach stream, eventually you head into the heights of the Black Forest and have a few climbs ahead of you.
long_description: We start our tour at the car park in the centre of Zwickgabel. After a short warm-up phase, we keep to the left and walk over the narrow bridge at Gasthof Mohren to the other bank of the stream. We follow the signs with the yellow rhombus to Mittellangenbach at a distance of 3.5 km and walk on a flat gravel path along the meandering Langenbach in wide loops and pass the colourful Weiherhütte. In Mittellangenbach we cross a bridge and follow the yellow rhombus, partly steeply ascending, through the forest back to Zwickgabel. This takes us to Leimiß, a small settlement. We now follow the path steeply downhill and walk to the cemetery. Via the narrow access road, we reach our starting point again, walking along the main road on the right.

images.caption: This is the view we have on the way back.
A view of the Langenbach Valley.
The Langenbach accompanies us on our tour.

title: Over the hills from Immenstadt to Martinszell
short_description: We experience a varied hike through small farming villages, across well-tended meadows, through quiet forests and past churches and chapels. We explore an old castle and walk along a small moor area. Looking back, the Allgäu Alps remain a constant companion.
long_description: The hilly landscape north of Immenstadt extends northwards to just before Kempten and is broken by the Niedersonthofener See lake. In the northwest, the more powerful mountain ranges of Hauchenberg and Sonneck-Grat border the hill country. To the east lies the Illertal valley. We pay attention to this, but not until the second part of the tour from Werdenstein. The castle of Werdenstein was the ancestral seat of the Lords of Werdenstein from around 1239. The chapel was consecrated in 1469. In the middle of the 17th century, the castle was sold to the Counts Köigsegg-Rothenfels. Since then, the building fabric has fallen into disrepair. It was not until 1988 that renovation work began, which enabled the entrance gate to be preserved in its present form. The world's largest horseshoe ever forged can also be found on the gate. It was forged in the castle courtyard on the night of the new millennium as a lucky charm, as can be read on a small plaque. A model of the former castle can be found in the photos for this tour. Afterwards we visit the Werdensteiner Moos, which is one of the largest raised bogs in the Upper Allgäu with an area of approx. 85 ha. After intensive peat cutting until the middle of the last century, numerous renaturation measures have been taken in recent years to protect the flora and fauna. This is how the moor was able to acquire the status of a European FFH protected area.

title: CMP Trail Short 18 km
short_description: Short route of the CMP Trail held in October in Bassano del Grappa
long_description: This run is ideal for everyone who wants to approach trail running without particular difficulties.

title: Spridlington to Normanby-by-Spital
short_description: A pleasant off road route from the village of Spridlington to Normanby-by-Spital and The Bottle & Glass Pub.
long_description: Plotted as a linear route but we stopped and the The Bottle & Glass Pub for lunch and it is easy to remember the way back - even after a couple of pints!

images.caption: The Bottle & Glass Pub at Normanby-by-Spital
hike in Central England and the Midlands: Spridlington to Normanby-by-Spital

title: Ås til Åsleden - Rebbetuaröd to Agusa
short_description: The eleventh stage of the s til Åsledens leads from Rebbetuaröd to Agusa.
long_description: On the shortest section of the long-distance trail we hike mostly through wooded areas. In this seclusion lies a former facility of the Swedish Air Traffic Control Service. It is completely underground and consists of a 200 m long tunnel and a 400 square metre, three-storey building. At our stopover in Agusa, we can visit the Agusastugan, a half-timbered courtyard that has not been altered since 1945.

title: From Bad Hindelang via the Hirschalpe to the Spieser
short_description: This easy snowshoe tour takes us to a wonderful panoramic peak above Oberjoch and Bad Hindelang.
long_description: This snowshoe tour on the Spieser (1649 m) offers us lots of sun and a fantastic panorama from the summit. We move on predominantly south-facing slopes with a moderate gradient. Orientation up to the large wooden cross near the Hirschalpe is completely unproblematic, as we are on the service road. From the Hirschalpe onwards, it can be a little more difficult to find the way to the summit of the Spieser if visibility is poor and there are no tracks. The Hirschalpe is usually open from Christmas onwards and offers us a cosy place to stop for a break.

images.caption: Ausblick vom Hirschberg auf die Tannheimer Berge und die Zugspitze im Winter

title: Origins of the Ruhr area - Eckenhagen
short_description: On this tour we experience the origins of industry in the Ruhr region.
long_description: On this tour we experience the origins of industry in the Ruhr region. Although coal was mined as early as the 13th century, it was not yet mining. With the beginning of the 19th century, economic coal mining was also promoted along the Ruhr, which gave industrialisation in the Ruhr region a proper boost. The Ruhr was developed as a supplier of coal and steel, and the burgeoning industry subsequently drove the founding of many railway companies. railway companies.

images.caption: The Ruhr region also has its green sides.

title: From Schöneck through the forests of the Vogtland region
short_description: On this extensive tour we hike through the dense forests of the Vogtland.
long_description:
Schöneck is located in the nature park Erzgebirge/Vogtland, at an altitude of between 700 and 800 m above sea level. and is surrounded by vast forests. With its breathtaking view of the Elster and Fichtelgebirge mountains, the town has been a hiking parc paradise, winter sports resort and summer retreat for over a hundred years. summer resort.
Around Schöneck there are many idyllically located idyllically situated ponds and small lakes. Most of them used to serve as water reservoirs for timber rafting. Today Today, hikers and day trippers enjoy the beauty of nature on their shores.
This extensive hike through the forests of the Vogtland near Schöneck is designed as a day tour. Therefore, we should wear good shoes and provide sufficient food and drink.

images.caption: The landscape in the headwaters of the Rote Mulde near Schöneck.

title: Around the Staffelsee
short_description: A varied hike through forests, meadows and moors and past pretty houses.
long_description: Where Pfaffenwinkel and Fünf-Seen-Land meet, on the edge of the Zugspitz region, lies the Staffelsee, which was formed during an ice age. It can be reached in less than an hour from Munich and is one of the local recreation areas for Munich residents. The hike has only a few small ascents and therefore offers relaxed hiking with a mountain panorama. The impressions of nature that we can gain around the lake are very diverse: forests, moors, villages and again and again the lake itself with its islands. The circular trail is marked with the number 1 throughout.

images.caption: View across the moor to the Staffelsee.
View over the Staffelsee with mountain panorama.

title: Snowshoe: Hörndlwand from Seehaus in Chiemgau
short_description: Along with the Kampenwand, the Hörndlwand (1684 m) is one of the most spectacular rock massifs in the Chiemgau. On the ascent and descent we enjoy the combination of rock and snow here, which reminds us very much of the Dolomites.

title: Kust till Kustleden - from Klinten to Verum
short_description: The eighth stage of the Kust till Kustledens leads from the Klinten campsite through the village of Osby through an extensive moorland to the Verum campsite.
long_description: In the idyllic moorland of Gullarps Mosse we get a good insight into the local flora. We also pass some striking depressions in the ground, where fuel peat or tar was extracted. Also striking are the large rocks at the edge of the path, which once served as boundary markers.

title: Hike from Oberjoch to Hirsch-Alpe
short_description: This is an eventful and panoramic hike for everyone from Oberjoch to Hirschalpe and through Hirschbachtobel down to Bad Hindelang.
long_description: As the name suggests, Oberjoch (1136 m), the well-known and highest winter sports and health resort in Germany, is located in a Joch landscape: to the right and left, imposing pre-Alpine peaks rise up to the sky. From the centre of the village, after a short hike along the easy Ornach Panorama Trail, we reach the alpine pastures high above the Ostrachtal valley, where our view widens considerably. Especially the Jochschrofen (1625 m) offers impressive views and panoramas. To the Hirschalpe, where we find a nice place to stop for a break with a view of the nature reserve „Allgäuer Hochalpen“, we descend again a little way. Then we take the path through the Hirschbachtobel (caution is advised here in wet weather) down to Bad Hindelang. From there we can take the bus back to our starting point.

title: From Gröbenzell via Blutenburg Castle to Nymphenburg Palace
short_description: We experience the landscape on the western outskirts of Munich and walk from there through charming green strips past Blutenburg Palace to Nymphenburg Palace.
long_description:
Gröbenzell was only founded as a separate municipality in 1952 from districts of Munich, Puchheim, Olching and Geiselbullach. Behind the last houses, the area of the city of Munich begins. The Böhmer ponds, already visible in the distance, are to be developed into a landscape-compatible recreation area. At the moment, the former quarry ponds are private land. Swimming is prohibited there. Many scenic stretches in green strips and along railway lines alternate with typical residential areas. Near Langwied station we can overlook the Pasing depot from hills next to the line. Near Blutenburg Castle we come across a memorial to the death march of prisoners from Dachau concentration camp. Blutenburg Castle was first mentioned in a document in 1432, but construction on the grounds began years earlier. The castle is based on a moated castle from the 13th century. The Blutenburg is said to have been destroyed during the Thirty Years' War, but there is no evidence of this. In the second half of the 17th century, interest in the castle waned and activities shifted to Nyphenburg Castle. At this time, the middle house was built first. Already at the end of the 18th century, the castle park was opened to the public. Today you can meet a lot of joggers there in the morning. Opening hours vary depending on the season, but they can be found on the homepage of the castle
. Next to the palace is the City of Munich Botanical Garden. On the way, two playgrounds invite children to take a break. The two S-Bahn stations we pass on the way mean that the tour can also be conveniently shortened.

images.caption: Memorial to the death march of the prisoners of Dachau concentration camp.
Green strip between Langwied and Blutenburg.
On the railway line between Lochhausen and Langwied.

title: Hohenloher Landheg Tour
short_description: We set out on a historical and varied bike tour around the former country seat of Schwäbisch Hall. There are many places of interest along the way.
long_description:
This historic cycle tour takes you around the former landed town of Schwäbisch Hall. In 1150 Schwäbisch Hall was granted town charter and at the end of the 13th century it was granted imperial freedom until 1802. In the 14th and 15th centuries Schwäbisch Hall acquired an extensive territory, which was surrounded by a 120 km long 'Landheg' and had to be defended again and again.
Worth seeing: Romantic old town of Schwäbisch Hall with Hällisch-Fränkisches Museum, Kunsthalle Würth, Freilandmuseum Wackershofen, Michelfeld-Gnadental Monastery Church, Römermuseum Mainhardt, Church of St. Martin in Michelbach an der Bilz.Martin in Michelbach an der Bilz, Romanesque Kleincomburg and former Benedictine monastery Großcomburg in Schwäbisch Hall-Steinbach.

images.caption: We cycle through the beautiful Hohenlohe countryside.

title: Circular walk in the forests of Schönau
short_description: A pleasant and easy circular hiking route starting from the town of Schönau in the southwest of the Black Forest and passing several points of interest
long_description:
A circular hiking route that offers a great view of the wooded valley surrounding the town of Schönau, as well as a visit to the ruins of an old citadel and a walk beside the tiny lake. Itinerary is recommended for those who want to enjoy a short walk in nature.
The route is not suitable for walking with strollers, but since it does not include difficult climbs, even young children can climb it on foot.

title: Walk from Cocksdorp to De Koog
short_description: This route gives you a good impression of what Texel has to offer.
long_description: This route takes you from Cocksdorp to de Koog via the Lighthouse. During this walk you will walk through the beautiful nature reserves of Texel. You finish the route in de Koog. A nice town to have a drink after the route.

title: Easy walk through Borsec - mineral waters, caves and former quarry
short_description: A relaxing hike of several hours that gives you the opportunity to see a large part of Borsec and reach some of the most interesting sights around.
long_description:
The walk is a combination of several marked tourist trails, the first of which is the so-called "Owl Fortress" trail.
The steps take you, at the beginning, through the centre of the resort, past abandoned villas with beautiful architecture, a sign of the prosperity the place once enjoyed. The green area is beautifully landscaped, as are the mineral springs.
A first stop, after almost an hour, is Poiana Zânelor, a place where you can rest and relax. Also here you can see a traditional, renovated and accessible bathhouse. Continuing on through coniferous forests, you will reach, by road, the ancient spring (mofette), then the Pierre Curie spring, and finally the Owl Fortress. Here you have a panoramic view of the surrounding valley.
The trail returns to the same path for a stretch, to drop off în right of the skunk and follow the yellow cross marker to the Ice Cave. After about 10 minutes spent in the small cave, continue towards the former travertine quarry, now abandoned. From here, after about 15 minutes you reach the Bear Cave - a small cave that is slightly less accessible.

title: Bridalveil Fall
short_description: A short and relatively easy hiking route leading to the closest accessible viewpoint to the impressive Bridelville Falls in Yosemite Park
long_description: A one-way hiking trail leading to a frontal view of the Bridelville waterfall. This is actually the closest arranged observation point to the waterfall. The Bridelville waterfall is considered one of the largest and most prominent waterfalls in Yosemite Park when its height is about 188 meters and it is full of water all year round. The route is short but includes an ascent of about 90 meters.

title: Over the Geißhorn to the Vilsalpsee
short_description: This demanding but rewarding tour with a great mountain panorama leads the experienced hiker from Hinterstein over the Geißhorn to the Vilsalpsee in the Tannheimer Tal. Surefootedness and good physical condition are required.
long_description: From the village of Hinterstein, which is surrounded by the Allgäu High Alps nature reserve, we first hike to the beautifully situated Willers-Alpe (1456 m), which is located on a kettle-like alpine pasture below the Ponten. Then we continue up to the summit of the Geißhorn (2247 m), which is famous for its extensive panoramic view. From there we descend to another nature reserve at the Vilsalpsee, which is located on the Austrian side in the Tannheimer Tal (Tyrol). On this stretch tour we experience a high alpine environment that every experienced hiker will enjoy. For a day tour, the Geißhorn including the descent to the Vilsalpsee is an ambitious undertaking that requires some experience in mountain hiking. Above all, we should always keep a close eye on the time so that we don't miss the last bus that leaves from the Vilsalpsee at the end (approx. 5 p.m. in the high season).

title: Through the Spree meadows near Spremberg
short_description: We enjoy a small but nice circular walk through the Spree Valley south of Spremberg.
long_description: We enjoy a small but nice circular walk through the Spree Valley south of Spremberg. The old town of Spremberg lies between two Spree arms on an island surrounded by an attractive floodplain landscape. If you wish, you can visit the Lower Lusatian Heath Museum in Spremberg or enjoy a leisurely stop at the market square.

title: From Sehlen on Rügen to Karnitz Hunting Lodge
short_description: Our circular walk in the southwest of the island of Rügen passes an ostrich farm and runs around Kniepower Lake to Karnitz hunting lodge.
long_description: Our circular walk starts at the sports field in Sehlen. We walk straight ahead on the road "Am Sportplatz" towards the end of the village. At the end of Swine, we turn right to the end of the road and then turn left along a path between fields. We follow this field path straight on to Swine to the ostrich farm (1). Now we walk past the ostrich farm through a forest, pass a wood on the right before turning left again through a forest towards Karnitz. At the entrance to Karnitz, we turn right onto the cycle path towards Kniepow. We walk straight ahead through the forest past Katharinenteich pond, see Kniepower See through the trees on our left and continue straight ahead to Kniepow. In Kniepow we go left along the main road and left again. We finally follow the road to the right until we reach the information board and turn left, following the signs "Wanderweg See". Our hike now leads us through the Kniepower See nature reserve, past the Slavic fortress wall (2). We walk on a path along the shore of the lake until we reach a rest area (3) with a wooden footbridge. Turn right at the rest area and left at the information boards. At the crossroads we walk right back to Karnitz. In Karnitz, we walk right through the village along the main road to Karnitz hunting lodge (4). At the hunting lodge, we walk right along the main road, then left in the direction of the golf course and straight on past the golf course (5). At the crossroads, we finally walk left on the Ostsee Küsten-Radweg (Baltic Sea Coastal Cycle Path) in the direction of Putbus and follow the path straight ahead to a crossroads. We go left uphill, walk through a forest and through Tangnitz until we reach the main road. We turn right and follow the main road to the Dankeskirche (6) in Sehlen before returning to the starting point.

images.caption: The "Kniepower See" rampart is a Slavic lowland rampart with a section wall 280m long and 5-12m high.
The very stately-looking Karnitz manor house was built in 1834/35.
Along the Kniepower Lake, numerous swamp forests have settled.
The ostrich farm in Swine is not only home to ostrich birds, goats and guinea pigs, but also to the only albino kangaroo in Europe.
The Kniepower Lake nature reserve has a rich dragonfly and amphibian fauna and a diverse bird life.
A staircase leads up to the castle rampart, which is about 1000 years old.
There are numerous magnificent views of Kniepower Lake from the lakeside path.
A small meadow by the lake with a rest area invites you to linger.
The rest area on the "Kniepower See" castle rampart provides a fantastic view of the Kniepower See.
Karnitz Hunting Lodge was built in 1834/35 under Count Guido von Usedom.
The Dankeskirche in Sehlen is surrounded by the village's cemetery.

title: A trip around the "Blue Pot" spring (Blautopf)
short_description: A short and easy hiking route that surrounds the sparkling and wonderful spring known as "The Blue Pot" which is a short drive from the city of Ulm in southern Germany
long_description:
A circular hiking route that starts from the town of Blaubeuren and surrounds a gorgeous spring with a gorgeous transparent bluish-turquoise shade. Along the entire length of the spring, a small waterfall flows into another pool that flows into a small stream. A wonderful and fun itinerary for those traveling in the area.
The track itself has a negligible slope and is therefore suitable for walking at any age and physical fitness.
Due to the nature of the route, it is possible but not particularly convenient for a trip with a stroller, so it is recommended to lock it at the beginning of the route and pick it up at the end.

title: Hike from Annaberg-Buchholz to the Chocolate Rock
short_description: This beautiful hike in the heart of the Ore Mountains takes us to the "Chocolate Rock".
long_description:
This beautiful hike in the heart of the Ore Mountains takes us to the "Schokoladenfelsen" (Chocolate Rock), whose curious name first appeared as such in 1872 in a first appeared as such in a hiking book in 1872. According to tradition, the children from Wiesa used to carry the luggage of the spa guests up the and often received a piece of chocolate as a reward. Hence the name of the rock.
A bus takes us back to Annaberg-Buchholz from the thermal spa of Wiesenbad.

images.caption: We hike through Frauenholz to the chocolate rock.

title: Into the valley to Emmendingen
short_description: On this tour you will hike across the open plateau near Helgenreute - with a fantastic view of the Black Forest range.
long_description: We start in Helgenreute, a district of Freiamt. There are different spellings for this district: Helgenrütte, Hölgenrütte and Helgenreute. The name "Reute" or "Rütte" refers to a cleared area. It is thanks to this clearing that we have the open plateau here, which affords us fantastic views as far as the Black Forest range. From the house with the number 3, we hike out on the side road to the district road. There we take the footpath and cycle path to the right in a southerly direction and past the bus stop to the next junction. Here we follow the bicycle signpost in the direction of Mußbach. At the hiking signpost Mußbach-Siedlung, we leave the district road and follow the yellow rhombus to the right in the direction of Landeck and past individual farmsteads until we reach the forest. There we continue our hike on the middle path along the yellow rhombus. At the edge of the forest, we continue with a wonderful view to the signpost at the Stabhalterhof farm (1). Here we follow the yellow rhombus in the direction of Landeck, cross a small road and continue on the meadow path along the edge of the forest to a farm on a small road. Follow this to the right in the direction of the country road. At the signpost "Schirmer", we turn left onto a narrow path before reaching the road. We walk over small tree trunks through a "primeval forest-like" forest until we leave it after about 1.5 km. We are surprised by a great view, which we can enjoy comfortably on the bench standing here. We follow the paved farm road on the opposite side straight ahead until we reach the "Stilzer Fritz" restaurant (2). Here we stay on the little road until shortly before reaching the next farmstead. Before reaching the barn, turn right onto the meadow path and walk past fields and a raised hide into the forest. Here we come to a forest path, which we follow to the left until we reach an even wider forest path after about 500 m. Follow this to the right downhill. Follow this down to the right along the blue rhombus. At the next forest road junction, we continue walking to the right in the direction of Emmendingen. We follow the blue rhombus until we reach a tiny shelter, where we continue our hike to the right along the hay path. Continue to the rest area at the "Gebrannte Eiche" (3). Here we walk out of the forest to the right and follow the private path below the meadow to the settlement of Wöpplinsberg (4) at the junction to the chapel. If you wish, you can make a small detour and walk across the meadow to the chapel. Our actual path leads on the road through the settlement and at the crossroads below the farms further down the hill to the left. About 100 m after this junction, we leave the road and follow the trail markings with the red dot to the left across the meadow into the forest. At the next crossroads, walk uphill along the wide forest path towards Emmendingen, follow the red dot through the forest and leave the wide path at an old oak tree. Here we turn right onto a narrow path and continue to a shelter at the cemetery (5). We hike on the forest path to the right for about 100 m and then turn left again onto a path. Follow the blue rhombus around the cemetery (turn left at the turning point). We continue to follow the path marking with the blue rhombus along a narrow path to the church at the Stadtpark (6) in Emmendingen. Over the Elisabeth bridge and past picturesque houses, we now walk straight ahead. Through the pedestrian zone we continue straight ahead to the station. In front of the station building we follow the road to the left. At the next crossroads, we turn right to the bus stop where bus line 211 takes us back to Helgenreute almost every hour (please check the exact times beforehand).

images.caption: A half-timbered house in the old town of Emmendingen.
If there is no snow, this is a good place to rest.
We see mighty Black Forest farms on our tour.

title: The landscapes around Wegscheid
short_description: This varied hike takes us to a former brown bear area and to the largest bathing lake in the region. If you like, you can also climb up the Eidenberg Lusen.
long_description: From the Haus des Gastes we walk downhill and turn right onto the main road behind the hospital. At the police station, we go down the narrow tarred path on the right and turn into the road called "Waldweg". We reach a path on the left that leads us directly into the forest. Here the Heindlmühle inn is already advertised. After a short hike, we emerge from the forest and see the inn ahead of us. We pass a ski lift (1) and follow the sign to the right to the Seeweg. We hike close to the Austrian border. At a bridge we turn left onto a narrow tarred path. Behind the stone mill is a barn with many old agricultural tools and machines attached to its façade - almost a museum! We continue up the slope and into the forest. After passing through the villages of Fronau and Monigottsöd, we cross a field path and come to the Osterbach, which marks the border to Austria. This is where the landscape conservation area of the "Eidenberger Lusen" begins. We first hike at the foot of the mountain into the forest. This part is called "Bärenloch". On an information board at a resting place we read the reason: Brown bears were still native to this forest area in the century before last. The forest was declared a protected area when plans were made to build a large hydroelectric power station here. We follow the stream on the forest path to a shelter (2) with a picnic area. After a break, we continue along the stream. We pass an information board that tells us about the old sawmill on the Osterbach. Farmers in the region used the water's gradient to process wood. In the spring of 1944, huge masses of snow destroyed the mill. At the edge of the forest there are works of art made of old agricultural implements. We first walk to the village of Eidenberg before deciding whether to venture the detour to the Lusen summit. The climb to the summit would extend our hike by two hours. Finally, we hike out of Eidenberg and follow the river Ranna. Before reaching the outskirts of Maierhof, we go uphill for a bit, then a sign points us down to the Rannasee (4). It is the largest bathing lake in the Bavarian Forest. On the shore of the lake, the restaurant "Zur Wasserrutsche" with a large playground invites us to linger. The southern shore is already in Austria. We then carefully cross the main road and enter the forest. Behind the Stierbach stream, after a bend, we reach the old dam of the rack railway (5). The not too dense trees let us look far into the mixed forest on both sides. We pass the Stiermühle on the left and continue hiking until we reach the entrance to Niederwegscheid. There we turn left and follow the signs at the edge of the forest. We can rest at a resting place under trees. The path leads to a farm. There we turn right and walk the last stretch to Wegscheid along a narrow tarred road. We hike into the village and decide to visit the parish church (6). The former neo-Gothic church on this site was demolished in 1967 and a modern church built in its place. The tranquil interior is worth a look. The square ground plan is surmounted by a roof whose four pointed gables form a uniform cross. The light penetrates through the stained glass windows on the gable walls and bathes the room in warm colours. After the visit, we walk back to the starting point via the main street of Wegscheid with its restaurants.

images.caption: Art made from old agricultural implements.
A typical farmhouse in this region.
We walk along the edge of the forest to Wegscheidt.
This path is the old dam of the rack railway.

title: Heath hike into the Tiefental valley near Hermannsburg
short_description: We will follow historical traces in the Südheide Nature Park, which is why a visit to the Ludwig-Harms-Haus in Hermannsburg is recommended beforehand.
long_description:
It is advisable to start the hike with a visit to the Ludwig Harms House opposite the tourist information office. Here a permanent exhibition provides information about the history and present-day work of the Hermannsburg Mission. We start the walk at the tourist information in Harmsstra&szlig 3a. From there we turn left into Harmsstra&szlig and follow the street into Missionsstra&szlig. At the end of the Christian-Schule grounds on the right and the Missionsseminars on the left we turn right into Sägenförth and after 25 m turn left into Sunderstra&szlig. At the end, turn right into Alte Celler Heerstra&szlig. After a few hundred metres, cross the Hermannsburg-Unterl;ß (K17) connecting road and continue straight ahead until you reach the turn-off to the Hiester farm. Here we stay on the main path and continue straight ahead for about 200 m, then turn left onto the path, which we follow for about 1.9 km until we reach the Tiefental car park on the heath. (After approx. 450 m, the path leads up a small incline at a fork on the right through the forest). At the Tiefental car park, turn left onto the main hiking trail, which leads between the two heaths. Opposite the car park there is a memorial stone to the earlier missionary festivals in Tiefental, and at the shelter in the car park there is a plaque with information about them. (Here we have the option of shortening the circular trail by 4 km by following the 6A marker sharply to the left past the car park. However, we then miss one of the most beautiful heath areas of the Lüneburger Heide). We follow the main circular trail through the
heath and turn right into the path after approx. 400 m before the edge of the forest. After approx. 500 m we reach the actual Tiefental. (Note: The name "Tiefental" is usually missing on the hiking maps, the field name is
"Hermannsburger Gehege") After another 400 m through the heath, we turn left and walk along the edge of the forest until after one kilometre we cross the Oldendorf-Lutterloh path at a refuge. We continue along the
heath until after 500 m we follow a small path through a depression and after a few metres and a short climb we reach another heath. We are now in the area of Misselhorner Heide and follow the narrow path
straight ahead through the heathland. The next two kilometres offer us a beautiful view in places. Finally, the path joins a main path, which we can follow to the Misselhorner Heide car park, or what
is highly recommended is to cross it and walk along the smaller heath on the left side of the path to the car park. At the car park, the path leads onto the main road Hermannsburg-Unterlüß (K17). Here you have to turn left and follow the cycle path for about one kilometre until you reach the riding arena in Misselhorn next to the Misselhorner Hof inn. Here you can turn left, follow the bridle path and continue parallel to the road next to the riding arena. After about 600 m, we cross the Alte Celler Heerstra&szlig and walk along the path between woods and meadows until we reach the nursing home for the elderly on Schlüpker Weg. Turn right onto this path and follow it first through the forest and then through a housing estate until you reach Lotharstra&szlig. At the pedestrian crossing we can cross the street and continue to the left until after about 500 m, past the La Taverna restaurant, we turn back into Harmsstra&szlig at the Ludwig-Harms-Haus and arrive at the starting point of our walk.

title: Spectacular hike in Vrancea Mountains: Golul Cozei rock
short_description: Well sign-posted, although not many come here, surprisingly picturesque, challenging, and predictably wild with many wildlife traces left behind, this route is one of the mountain gems in Vrancea county.
