title: Winter hike along the Tegelberg to the Rohrkopf and Drehhütte huts
short_description: From the Drehhütte / Outward Bound car park, we hike up to the Rohrkopfhütte, which invites you to stop for refreshments when skiing is in progress. The tour then leads us past the Drehhütte and back down into the valley.
long_description:
From the Drehhütte / Outward Bound car park, we first head upwards on the forest road. Behind a bend, we disregard a first small turn-off and turn right at the next one in the direction of Rohrkopfhütte. Through the dense wintry forest we climb up a steep mountain slope. To our right, a view opens up through the trees towards the valley station of the Tegelberg cable car. We continue along the path for a while and finally come to the place where a landslide occurred a few years ago, when a large part of the north-western flank slid down into the valley. An information board tells us exactly what happened. From here we can see the two royal castles of Neuschwanstein and Hohenschwangau in the distance.
  Now we continued our ascent in the direction of the Rohrkopfhütte and reached it a little later. It is located directly on the downhill slope of the Tegelberg and invites you to a cosy stop.
  We leave the hut behind us and set off on the descent to the Drehhütte, which starts to the left of the ski slope. (The path can be closed in winter for weather reasons, please follow the signs!) We quickly reach the hut (currently not managed) via two hairpin bends and can take a break. Where the hut stands today, there were once two huts where whetstone makers lived. They worked the dark grey stones in the nearby quarry. Later, the huts were used by alpine herdsmen, before finally the currently unmanaged Drehhütte was built.
  Our way back leads us along the forest road back to the starting point.
  Alpine dangers! Hike at your own risk!

title: The Emeindras loop - Le Sappey en Chartreuse
short_description: A very pleasant loop through forest and meadows, perfect for enjoying the magnificent alpine pastures under the benevolence of Chamechaude.
long_description:
From the parking lot, follow the GR®9 (red and white markers) to the hamlet of Jallière. After returning to the road for a short while, continue on a good path to the meadows of Montjalat (1150 m). The path enters the forest and, after about 100 m, leaves the GR at Pied de Velouse to go right (signposted Emeindras). You join a wider path below, which leads to the ruins of the habert (sheepfold) at Emeindras de Dessous, a former refuge destroyed by an avalanche.
The path curves wide to the right across the meadow before reaching Emeindras de Dessus, where the janitor of the cows who spend the summer here makes his home. The ridge above offers magnificent views of the Alps, from Taillefer to Mont Blanc, via the Belledonne chain and the Chartreuse peaks (Dent de Crolles, Chamechaude, Grand Som...). For the descent, at the first sharp right-hand bend below Emeindras de Dessus, take the steep forest track on the left. Cross the torrent and keep left at the crossroads.
At the hamlet of Les Combes, rejoin the road for 200 m, then return to the parking lot by turning right at the crossroads at La Croix du Rocher.

images.caption: hiking in the Chartreuse Massif: Boucle des Emeindras - Le Sappey en Chartreuse

title: The Episcopal City - Eichstätt
short_description: We walk through the medieval bishop's town with its many monasteries and churches.
long_description:
With its many monasteries and the Willibaldburg overlooking everything, Eichstätt is an impressive little town where you can still feel the breath of the Middle Ages.
A visit to Willibaldsburg Castle is highly recommended. The castle was built around 1353 and was the representative castle and residence of the Eichstätt bishops until the 18th century. Today, the castle houses the Jura Museum of Natural History. It has numerous fossil pieces, including the famous Eichstätt Archaeopteryx.

title: "All's die Baach nab" - circular walk along the Elzbach river
long_description:
Author
Tabea Götze 
Update: March 17, 2020

title: The path of the winemakers' huts
short_description: At the foot of the Pic de Brau, an enchanting stroll through the vineyards and huts of winemakers who watch over this place steeped in history.
long_description:
A few years ago, vinemakers together with volunteers decided to rebuild the huts that former winemakers used to shelter from the sun. They still work regularly to this task, building in the rules of the art of stone huts that you can admire throughout this course.
Every year, in summer, the association "Entre Magrie et Cournanel" celebrates these famous huts , sometimes considered as "modest stone cathedrals" at the event "Cabanes en fête". Visitors go from hut to hut to meet winemakers who tell their stories and share the best of their region (wine, honey, fruit ...)
Whatever the season, this course enchants. The peak of Brau watches over this quiet valley where since time immemorial, the man cultivates the vine.

images.caption: Cancian hut, starting point of the path of the huts
Terminals inform you about your route

title: Hiking Mount Timpanogos (2 Summits)
short_description: Challenging hike with a breathtaking view from the top of Timpanogos and South Timpanogos close to Orem and Provo, Utah.
long_description:
Mount Timpanogos is with it's peak at 3.582m (11.751,97 feet) the second-highest summit of the Wasatch Mountains and a well-known hiking destination in Utah. The summit of Mt Timpanogos can be reached through two different trails. One is the Timpanokee Trail and the other one is the one from Aspen Grove which is steeper, but more scenic and passes several waterfalls. This trail is described here. 
Waterfalls, wildflowers and wildlife can often be seen along the trail. If you are lucky there might even be some mountain goats around. You will also pass a scenic mountain lake, the Emerald Lake. Depending on the month you are hiking, there is a snowfield on the top of the mountain which varies in size. During the summer season temperature will stay warm, but be aware of the altitude and that it might get chilly the higher you get and depending on the month you are hiking.  
In case you want to hike more after reaching the top of Mt Timp, you can hike a little longer to South Timp, the second summit. Along the Saddle of Mt Timp you will have a great view into the valley and over the mountains in the distance.

title: Ås til Åsleden - Agusa to Brösarp
short_description: The last stage of the Ås til Åsledens runs from Agusa to Brösarp.
long_description: At the end of our tour on the Ås til Åsleden we walk from the Linderödsåsen hill train down to the village of Brösarp. In an old common, where the local farmers used to graze their pigs, we pass huge oaks and juniper bushes. Not much has changed here in the last centuries, as the area has remained largely cut off from civilisation.

title: World Heritage hike through the Lavaux vineyards
short_description: Wonderful panoramic hike through the central part of the Lavaux UNESCO World Heritage Site with its wine terraces. This tour demands that you taste a glass of wine somewhere!
long_description:
This is an easy circular hike through the wine terraces of the Lavaux UNESCO World Heritage Site. Throughout the hike, you have a marvellous panoramic view of Lake Geneva and the surrounding mountains in France and Switzerland. In fine weather, the view stretches across the entire lake and as far as the Rhone Valley in Valais. On the opposite side of the lake we can see Evian and Hochsavoien.
The outward route runs along winegrowers' roads, on which many hikers and cyclists are travelling, but otherwise only winegrowers with their vehicles. It is very exciting to watch the winegrowers at work. As early as the 12th century, Cistercian monks built walls here to cultivate terraced vineyards. The way back leads continuously downhill on a pavement along a road, but always on the lake side of the road with wonderful views. The entire route is also suitable for pushchairs.

images.caption: Hike in the Lake Geneva region: World Heritage hike through the Lavaux vineyards

title: Causeway Coastal Route
short_description: This scenic road stretches from the busy metropolis of Belfast to the charming city of Londonderry. With its beautiful coastline, gentle hills and lovely fishing villages, Causeway Coastal Route is indeed a feast for the eye.
long_description: Causeway Coastal Route is a scenic route of about 135 miles alongside the impressive coastline of Northern Ireland, following the historical Giant's Causeway, a stunning formation of about 40,000 basalt stone columns left by volcanic eruptions about 60 million years ago. It’s the country’s only natural monument and UNESCO world cultural heritage site. Alongside the route you can also find further points of interests: From the bustling metropolis of Belfast to the tranquil coastal city of Larne past the delightful Glenariff Forest Park, there is a huge variety of interesting sights waiting for you to discover them. If you feel like experiencing the country‘s history vividly you should stop by Dunseverick Castle, a former fortress on the beautiful coastline. Nature lovers can enjoy the spectacular views onto the sandy shores the headland of Torr Head. If you still can’t get enough of Northern Irland’s most impressive scenic route, you should stop by at the Giant's Causeway Visitor Centre as well.

title: Great Supramonte Traverse (GTS)
short_description: 4-day trek in the beautiful and wild territory of Supramonte, Sardinia
long_description:
This trek traverses the limestone massif of Supramonte, a very rugged and wild area in east-central Sardinia. You pass through dense forests, sinkholes, caves and cliffs, plus you often encounter grazing animals, rural buildings, ancient settlements dating back to Nuragic times, natural monuments (e.g., the Su Sercone sinkhole) and some spectacular viewpoints.
There are no accommodations along the route, but you can bivouac in one of the so-called "cuiles," old shepherds' huts now restored and made available to hikers (but not managed).

title: Walk on the coastal path of Portbail
short_description: This is a very easy walk that allows you to get some fresh air and recharge your batteries by the sea in the Cotentin region. This walk follows part of the GR223, the coastal path of the Manche.

title: Aboda Klint circular route
short_description: The circular trail in the Aboda Klint nature reserve in Småland takes us once around Lake Kleven.
long_description: The Aboda Klint nature reserve is ideal for a quiet break from everyday life. Several hiking trails lead through the beautiful nature. The area is equipped with barbecue areas, fireplaces, toilets and a restaurant (not open all year!) and is accessible all year round. In addition to hiking, you can also go mountain biking or bring your fishing rod. Aboda Klint is a combination of deciduous woodland and primeval forest, as well as agricultural land. The tour around Lake Kleven also takes you to the Aboda Klint viewpoint, which offers a great view down to the lake and over the surrounding forests. At the end of the tour, you can also take a refreshing dip in Lake Kleven and enjoy a piece of cake with a view at the café (when open) on the cliff.

images.caption: Picknick am See Kleven im Wandergebiet Aboda Klint

title: Trail to the Cabeça do Índio in Trindade
short_description: Beautiful trail located in the village of Trindade, in Paraty, which goes to é à curious rocky form called Cabeçãa do Í ndio. This natural monument é the divisor of the states of SP and RJ.
long_description:
This region is located in the lower part of the Serra da Bocaina National Park and, although the official site of the Park states that there is no trail to Cabeça do Índio, it is possible to reach this place and contemplate the beautiful scenery around by a relatively easy but unsigned trail. 
The trail passes through beautiful attractions of the village of Trindade that are à worth visiting, such as Praia do Meio, Praia da Caixa D'Aço and the Natural Pools of  Caixa D'Aço. At all times, you will be surrounded by a rich vegetation, typical of the Atlantic Forest, and have the mountains of the Serra do Mar in the background. <The PARNA of Serra da Bocaina does not charge an entrance fee nor requires authorization to visit these attractions and there is no time control for entry or exit visitors.

title: Tadiandamol Peak Trek
short_description: Tadiandamol peak is the highest peak in the Coorg district of Karnataka. Located in the Western Ghats (Sahyadri range), this 1748 meter high peak comes under the Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary area.
long_description:
Tadiandamol is the highest peak in Kodagu district and the fifth highest peak in Karnataka. This trail route starts from the Nalknad Palace which has been recognized as an important historical landmark during the National Trigonometric Survey.
The Tadiandamol peak is situated at an altitude of about 1740 feet and is home to a wide variety of flora and fauna. The Tadiandamol track has waterfalls and dense shola forests and plantations of a variety of spices such as black pepper, coffee, cardamom, betel leaves and betel nuts. This 5-hour trek is moderately challenging. The climate is generally cool, the trail is unpaved and some parts can be slippery in the monsoon.
Tadiandamol Trek is one of the most popular trekking routes in Coorg (also known as Kodagu). It also attracts a lot of trekkers who come to Madikeri or Coorg hill station to spend leisure time. In recent times international trekkers have also started coming here.

title: To Sergiev Posad for 1 day
short_description: Sergiev Posad – a city not just in the Moscow region, but a city – the dream of any and every decent person.
long_description:
Sergiev Posad is located in the north-eastern part of the Moscow region, 52 km from Moscow. The main attraction of Sergiev Posad – is, of course, Holy Trinity Laura of Sergiev Posad. The Lavra is an impulse not only of Posad itself, but of the entire Russian state and its people, a relic with a priceless sacred memory, and a simple ray of unextinguished, unextinguished, current and future manifold open light.
Sergiev Posad was founded over the centuries and with the labours of many illustrious and nameless associates of history. It was not until March 22, 1782 that Catherine II signed a decree establishing from the villages and slobodas near the Trinity-Sergius Lavra the Sergiev Posad. Now Lavra is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and from the very capital of Russia - Moscow - there is a passable path to the capital of Russian Orthodoxy - Sergiev Lavra, which was named as «road to Lavra&nbsp.

title: Posses Waterfall Trail
short_description: Hike to the beautiful Posses waterfall in the mountainous region of the Serra da Bocaina National Park, in São José do Barreiro, SP.
long_description:
<This walk coincides with the initial stretch of famous Gold Trail (or Mambucaba Trail) and begins at gateway to Serra da Bocaina National Park.
Posses waterfall is about 8 km from the entrance of the park and has a fall of about 40m. You will also pass by important historical landmarks, ruins present on the trail that were part of an old farm responsible for planting and extracting pine, cedar and eucalyptus.
If you wish, before arriving at the Posses waterfall you can also visit the famous Santo Izidro waterfall. It is one of the highlights of the park and its fall is an impressive 70 meters high, forming a beautiful pool perfect for bathing. The waterfall is located only 1.5 km from the entrance and the trail is well signposted.

title: गवर्नर हिल ट्रेल
short_description: पश्चिमी घाट में स्थित सापुतारा गुजरात के डांग जिले का एक प्रसिद्ध हिल स्टेशन ह ै। हरियाली से भरपूर, टेबल टॉप पॉइंट से लेक व्यू पॉ इंट तक की ट्रेल यहाँ हाइकिंग का बढ़िया अवसर देती है।&nbsp ;
long_description:
सापुतारा का मतलब है 'नागों का वास' और यह एक घना जंगली क्षेत्र है। सापुतारा को कई लोग गुजरात का अकेला हिल स्टेशन भी मानते हैं। कभी यहाँ के सागौन और बांस के जंगलों पर अंग्रेजों की नज़र थी जिसके लिए उन्होंने यहाँ के वर्ली, खुम्बी, भील और डांगी जनजातियों से दोस्ती करी थी।
सापुतारा के डांग जंगलों में नागों की बहुत सारी प्रजातियां पाई जाती हैं। इलाके के नागेश्वर महादेव मंदिर में नाग पंचमी के दिन श्रद्धालुओं की भारी भीड़ जुटती है। यहां के लोगों की मानें तो मर्यादा पुरुषोत्तम भगवान राम अपने वनवास के दौरान लंबे समय तक यहां रुके थे।
टेबल टॉप पॉइंट (जिसे टाउन व्यू पॉइंट और गवर्नर हिल भी कहते हैं) से लेक व्यू पॉइंट तक एक बहुत प्रसिद्ध ट्रेल मार्ग भी है। इस ट्रेल का नाम गवर्नर हिल ट्रेल है। जहाँ इस ट्रेल के शुरूआती बिंदु (टाउन व्यू पॉइंट) से पूरा शहर दिखता है वहीँ इसके अंतिम बिंदु (लेक व्यू पॉइंट) से विशाल और शांत सापुतारा झील दिखती है।

title: auf dem Sendero el Café zum Salto El Limón
short_description:
schöne, abwechslungsreiche Tour zum Wasserfall von El Limón
Translate to English
long_description:
Die Tour startet am Parkplatz „Parada Maria y Miguel“. Von dort aus folgen wir einem kleinen Pfad, der auf die Dorfstraße zuläuft, der wir anschließend folgen. Bald erreichen wir ein kleines Häuschen, wo man den Eintritt für den Wasserfall zahlen muss (ca. 0,80€). Ab hier beginnt der schöne Teil der Wanderung: wir folgen einem kleinen Waldweg, bis wir einen Fluss erreichen, den wir überqueren müssen. Anschließend laufen wir am Ufer entlang (flussaufwärts) und überqueren den Fluss noch zweimal. Ab jetzt folgen wir dem Pfad aufwärts durch den Wald. Nach kurzer Zeit erreichen wir den höchsten Punkt und haben einen wunderschönen Ausblick! Der Weg verläuft ab hier nun abwärts und wir erreichen bald ein kleines Café. Von hier aus kann man den Wasserfall schon sehen. Hinter der Terrasse geht der Pfad hinunter zum Wasserfall. Bevor wir den Salto El Limón erreicht, passieren wir einen kleineren Wasserfall und müssen hier erneut den Fluss überqueren. Danach folgen wir den Treppen hinauf zum Salto El Limón.

title: Nature trail to Tinovul Poiana Stampei  (Poiana Stampei marsh)
short_description: The educational route in the Tinovul Mare marshland at Poiana Stampei aims to inform tourists about the importance of this type of habitat.
long_description:
The route is about 1.8 km long and shows only a very small part of what the Tinovul Mare marshland means. Actually, the protected marshland area stretches over more than 681 hectares. Access to the area is possible only on the wooden bridge plus the path that is part of the route.
The information panels include details about what a grove is, the flora and fauna of the habitat, and their importance.

title: From Acquacalda to the Alpi del Lucomagno
short_description: On the south side of the Lukmanier Pass we hike through the largest alpine pasture area in Ticino with colourful flower meadows, enchanting park landscapes and lively alpine farming.
long_description: The Valle Santa Maria, situated on the south side of the Lukmanier Pass, is fascinating not only because of its magnificent mountain landscape, but also because of some superlatives. During the circular hike on the "Sentiero naturalistico Lucomagno Nr. 7" we can discover the largest alpine area in Ticino, the largest alpine pine forest on the alpine side and one of the largest springs in the canton. Of the numerous alps we pass, four are still in operation today.

title: Crane points

title: Pays de Collines hiking trail

long_description: During this walking route, you will discover the Parc Naturel Du Pays Des Collines. This area consists of many hills and pale valleys. During your route, you will also walk past Chatêau Vanhabost. You cannot visit this castle, but from the trail it is a beautiful sight. The castle is built symmetrically and has 4 beautiful corner towers. In 1940, the Belgian capitulation to the Germans was signed in this castle.

title: Hochfelln Mountain Run - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: The international Hochfelln mountain run is an "oldie" that is well attended every year.
long_description: The Ski-Club Bergen e.V. regularly organises Germany's oldest mountain run. Athletes, top cross-country skiers, the most successful international mountain sports specialists and well-known athletes from other sports umbrella organisations can compete against each other. But also well-trained non-licensed popular runners (hobby, recreational and amateur athletes) like to take part in the performance comparison and see who has the longer breath. The German classic is held on the 2000 World Cup course (8.9 km, 1,074 metres altitude difference).

title: Taking the kids to the Retezat Mountain: Scorota gorges and sheepfold
short_description: Climbing from the national road 66A towards the Scorota sheepfold is one of the most picturesque and accessible ways to get to know the wonders of the Retezat Mountains (for novices) or to revisit them, for experienced mountaineers. In addition, the route offers not only wonderful landscapes but also two karst formations: a cave and some gorges.
long_description:
The gradient of this route is comparable to climbing Mount Tâmpa from Brașov, a tourist experience familiar to many. So don't hesitate to take the children with you, especially if they are somewhat familiar with mountain hikes.
Along the way, you can stop at the Scorota cave, very close to the national road, then pass through the Scorota gorges. The intriguing narrowness of these gorges makes you stop at every step for pictures. 
An incredible coniferous forest takes you to the alpine plateau - to the glacier valley, actually. The roots of the fir trees ramifying in every direction and the moss-covered ground make you think of fantasy worlds.
At the sheepfold, you can find some food, possibly shelter. Of course, if you have a tent, you can spend the night near the huts.
From here, there's relatively easy access to the Buta mountain hut and further on, to the Piule peak. At least up to the sheepfold, you can hike the route in winter as well.

title: Vimmerby - The primeval forest in Norra Kvill National Park
short_description: Exploring the small Norra Kvill National Park in the hilly landscape of northern Småland
long_description: Norra Kvill National Park lies somewhat hidden near Vimmerby. The mysterious atmosphere of the original nature can still be felt today. Nature management and forestry have kept a low profile in the national park area for 150 years, so nature has hardly changed since then. In the area, which has been designated as a national park since 1927, a small primeval forest is increasingly forming: thick trees, large boulders from the last ice age, over 200 species of moss and two beautiful lakes offer a special kind of recreation area. The short route is particularly suitable for families with children, because in the unspoilt natural landscape you can discover many a peculiarity and maybe you will even discover some shy animals or fairies and goblins – in this enchanted nature it would be quite possible.

long_description: The spectacular and unforgiving Al Hajar mountain range in Oman offers some truly jaw-dropping scenery and no more is this so than from its highest peak. A military installation has sadly removed any chance of visiting the actual summit, but the experience and views from the south summit are just as rewarding.

The snow-covered Traunauen are a highlight of this tour.

The East Frisian island of Juist on the tidal flats of the North Sea is only 17 km long and in many places only 500 m wide. Motor vehicles are almost exclusively prohibited on the island, so hiking and cycling here can be a particularly relaxing experience.
From Juist, the island's main town, we walk to the small airfield in the east. Our path takes us through dunes and across the long, wide sandy beach on the north side of the island.

title: Hike to the Col de Balme via the Lachat reservoir
short_description: The hike to Combe de Balme via the Lachat reservoir is an exciting adventure for mountain lovers.
long_description:
The route begins near the reservoir, offering panoramic views of the turquoise waters of the dam and the surrounding peaks. Along the way, hikers pass through verdant alpine meadows and shady paths, perfect for a peaceful walk.
The trail, which is accessible to hikers of all abilities, allows you to admire the wealth of local flora and fauna. On arrival, the Combe de Balme reveals a spectacular and serene landscape.
This hike combines relaxation and wonder in the heart of the Alps.

title: Kernberglauf - Salomon Trailrunning Cup
short_description: Shortly before the running season comes to an end, the Jena University Sports Association (Universitätssportverein Jena e.V.) organises the Jena Kernberg Run. The programme includes distances of five kilometres (for everyone), 15 kilometres and 27 kilometres.
long_description: The first Jena Kernberg Run was held in 1975. Whereas in the early days just 20 local residents met to run the race, the number of participants continued to rise over the decades. With the new millennium, there are regularly over 1000 enthusiastic runners every year.

title: Hike to the summit of Chamechaude
short_description: Chamechaude, at 2082 m, is the highest point in the Chartreuse massif. It's a popular spot for climbing enthusiasts, offering breathtaking panoramic views over the whole massif, as well as Belledonne and Mont Blanc on a clear day.
long_description:
From the Col de Porte parking lot, head for the cross-country fireplace and follow the sign for "Cabane de Bachasson". The path first follows the meadow, then quickly enters the forest until you reach the hut.
From here, continue left towards La Folatière to the summit. Whether ascending or descending, stay on the S-shaped path to limit erosion. The descent is on the same path.
For the return journey, and to avoid making a round trip on the same route, extend the hike by returning to the Bachasson hut, then continue towards Pré Boiteux as far as Habert de Chamechaude.
Then descend towards Le Sappey en Chartreuse. At Montjalat, join Le Churut, then Le Réservoir. Follow the GR®9, and at Appanon, turn right to climb up to Col de Porte.

title: Panoramic round hike on Magura Codlei
short_description: A circular hiking route with numerous panoramic views over the mountains close to the Brașov Depression.
long_description:
This route is just one of the circuit options on the small Măgura Codlei mountain. The circuit reaches some important points such as Pietrele Albe, Stâncile Călărețului, Cetatea neagră, Poiana lui Sulică.
On at least two sections, the route involves rocky areas. The one in the Pietrele Albe area, on the first part, is exposed, so it is not a recommended route in winter.
The route leads largely through deciduous forest. Up to Pietrele Albe, the climb is steep and continuous. But the view from the viewpoint is worth the effort. Surprisingly, not much can be seen from the top due to the vegetation. Even in the cold season, the top is "buried" under the branches of trees. But there are several clearings along the way, an opportunity for beautiful views: at Pietrele Albe, a little below the peak on the route to the fortress, or from Poiana lui Sulică.

title: Through the Sodenberg Goose near Hammelburg
short_description: This hike takes us through the Saale valley, over hilly fields and meadows, through forests, up volcanic mountains and to a former basalt plant.
long_description:
We cross the Saale to the south at the Roßmühle campsite. Opposite the leisure market, we turn left into a stream valley. At the right edge of the valley, a meadow path leads us uphill and through a short section of forest. We reach the road "An der Klappermühle" which leads up to the village of Weickersgrüben. On the left side of the road are two old, lovingly renovated buildings. The house with blue shutters and an old water wheel is the so-called "Klappermühle".
We continue along the road to the centre of the village and turn sharp left at a lime tree into Blumenstraße. In front of a large wooden house, a path leads us uphill at an acute angle to the right. We finally turn right towards the forest, which we reach at a rest area under large deciduous trees with many tables and benches. We enjoy the view over the fields and the hilly landscape, then we continue hiking uphill through the beech forest and reach a platform.
We turn left onto the gravel path and follow it until it would lead out of the forest after a left turn. However, we go downhill to the right on a forest path that runs along the edge of the field. We come across a gravel path with trail markings "2" and "3" and turn right. The path first leads through mixed forest, then under a canopy of hazel bushes and fruit trees between fields.
At a fork in the path, we keep to the right, then shortly afterwards turn right into Weickersgrübener Weg. At a fountain in the hamlet of Ochsenthal we enjoy the refreshing water and then turn right to the Sodenberg inn. At the deer enclosure with an information board on deer, the road turns into a path. At the next crossroads we go straight on, following hiking trail "4". A forest path leads quite steeply uphill and then in an arc to a clearing. We follow the lower, longitudinal edge of the field until we reach a cross path. Now we hike right uphill to a gate, where a path leads us to the left to the summit of the Sodenberg, one of the southernmost Rhön volcanoes. We are rewarded for the climb with a wonderful panoramic view.
Back at the gate, we follow the wide gravel path straight ahead. This runs in a right-hand bend to the Gasthof Sodenberg. A board informs us about the Sodenberger Gans nature reserve. We like to stop at the historic inn with its beautiful beer garden before following the road for a while. At the next junction we go right uphill towards the forest, then keep left at the edge of the forest. The path leads into the mixed forest. Only at the third fork do we turn right. We pass a signpost to the chapel and soon reach a platform.
From here we have the option of turning left onto a path that leads us along a steep edge with a view of the Saale valley to the former pit of the basalt works. The view into the 70 m deep quarry is very impressive. In an adjoining refuge, we read about the history of the mine, which was worked between 1904 and 1958, and learn about the flora and fauna of the region.
Then we continue hiking until a field appears on our left. We keep to the left downhill at the edge of the forest and, keeping to the left, we come back to the forest path we already know. This time we go steeply downhill and straight back to Ochsenthal. We cross the village with its many half-timbered houses and floral decorations and continue towards Morlesau. At the transformer house, turn left onto a path with grass strips. The path leads westwards above the Franconian Saale with a view of Morlesau. Soon we approach the natural bank of the river on a footpath across meadows. Finally, we reach the Roßmühle campsite again.

title: Winding thermal ribbons in the river-carved wastelands
short_description: Soaking in the warm water after a long roll is always a turn off. This thermal loop crosses the Great Plain and connects 32 thermal spas
long_description:
We cycle from the junction of the Tisza and the Maros rivers to the foothills of the Mátra Forest, crossing numerous thermal baths along the way. From the Lower Tisza we cycle to the Körösök and from there to the Kiskunság National Park. We cross the Tiszazug region several times by ferry, and also pass through Kecskemét and Szolnok. We will finish the tour at Gyöngyös, passing through the Tápióság and Jászság. The lowland, cut by rivers, hides numerous marshes, sandbanks and dead branches.A rich fauna is hidden in the vast grassland, many of which are protected species.
Each section begins and ends at a thermal bath, so you can get ideas if you fancy a dip in the joint-conditioning waters after a long summer's roll. 
With the Alföld in the fortunate position of having plenty of spas, you can create a variety of other hiking variations to explore the thermal waters and the wonderful Hungarian landscape individually.

short_description: We walk from Vacha along the Werra to Philippsthal. On the way back we get to know the beautiful historic old town of Vacha.

In Philippsthal we reach the road and turn left towards the sports grounds. The path leads through the beautiful castle park to the Werra bridge, which we cross to the left. We turn left onto a footpath and cycle path. When the crash barrier opens on the left side of the road, we walk to the left onto a field path where a bench with a beautiful view invites us to take a break. Back in Vacha, we turn right onto the church square and walk back to the starting point via the market square with the historic town hall, Weingasse and Widemarkterstraße.

title: From Altenberg Cathedral to the Dhünn Dam
short_description: This tour takes us from the "Bergisches Dom" through lots of forest to the impressive Dhünntalsperre.
long_description: In the course of this hike we will pass a beautiful barbecue and rest area and the second largest drinking water reservoir in Germany - the Dhünn reservoir. Altenberg Cathedral, which is often called the "Bergische Dom", is the starting point of our tour. The former monastery church of the Cistercian monastery of Altenberg Abbey, founded in 1133, was built from 1255 and is a magnificent example of Rhenish Gothic architecture. The of the three-nave basilica did not end until 150 years later, with the with the magnificent west window, the largest church window in the Gothic style north of the Alps.

But also for holidaymakers who want to reach a summit with a great view, but don't want to take up a whole day, this tour is just right.

title: Freudenthalweg
short_description: We hike from Hamburg-Harburg through the middle of the Lüneburger Heide über Walsrode to Verden on the Aller. The villages, historical sights and the natural habitat of the heath promise a unique hiking experience.
long_description:
Stage 1: Hamburg-Harburg - Holm/Seppensen (26 km)
We start our hike in the south of Hamburg and pass the outdoor pond. Now the Schulteichgraben leads us into a large wooded area. The route continues via Westerhof, Klecken, Kleckerwald, Itzenbüttel and Osterberg to Holm-Seppensen.
Stage 2: Holm/Seppensen - Wilsede (22 km)
Today we hike through a beautiful forest to Handeloh, where we can explore the planetary nature trail. Shortly afterwards, we enter Inzmühlen, the gateway to the Lüneburger Heide nature reserve, which is an exceptional nature experience, not only during the high season from August to September.
Stage 3: Wilsede - Schneverdingen (18 km)
From Wilsede the route leads through a varied heathland landscape: we pass the Wilseder Berg, woods, ponds, burial ponds and, of course, the open heathland. The stage destination Schneverdingen is only a few metres from the course of the Freudenthal Trail. Here we can visit the heath garden and the Pietzmoor moor.
Stage 4: Schneverdingen - Soltau (20 km)
We follow the idyllic course of the Böhme in a southerly direction all day and hike via Heber, Surbostel and Ahlften to Soltau. In the evening, if you want to, you can soothe your body and soul in the Soltau thermal baths.
Stage 5: Soltau - Bad Fallingbostel (23 km)
Fields, woods and meadows alternate constantly in the hilly landscape of today's stage. Except for the village of Dorfmark, we only pass a few houses and farms and enjoy the solitude of nature to the full.
Stage 6: Bad Fallingbostel - Sieverdingen (21 km)
From the state-recognised Kneipp spa of Fallingbostel, we once again follow the Böhme and take a long curve to Walsrode. The Heide Museum in a typical Heide hall, the Walsrode Monastery and the former town hall are definitely worth a longer stay in the town. The many new impressions pleasantly shorten the way back to Sieverdingen.
Stage 7: Sieverdingen - Verden (Aller) (22 km)
The Freudenthalweg also offers us pure hiking pleasure today: the Lohheide, the Salingsloher Forst, the Lindhoop and finally the Tütheide accompany us to Verden on the Aller. Standing in Verden Cathedral, St. John's Church or the Verden Historical Museum, we can reflect on the journey. For those who want more action, the Magic Park Verden is the place to go, because the amusement park for children offers everything to do with fairytales and magic.

title: From Röthenbach via Lindenberg to Hergatz
short_description: This tour takes us to Lindenberg and then on to Niederstaufen via the Kinberg mountain. There we dive into the valley of the Laiblach and follow the Laiblach hiking trail upstream to Hergatz.
long_description:
The railway station of Röthenbach is located in the Oberhäuser district 2 km away from the centre of the village. In the past, the railway lines to Weiler and Scheidegg branched off here. Since 1993, there has been no more branching train traffic and the tracks have been converted into cycle paths. A large part of our route to Lindenberg runs along this route.
In Lindenberg we pass through the newly designed town park. This includes a stream with a pond and an interesting children's playground with a trampoline.
From Kinberg we have a beautiful view over the hills to the Nagelfluh chain, which stretches from Immenstadt to Hittisau. It is also an important part of the Nagelfluhkette Nature Park.
The Laiblachtal hiking trail, which we hike between Niederstaufen and Hergatz, is a very lovely affair. The path leads past a waterfall, over small bridges, past pretty farms and through varied meadows and forests. However, we should not be confused by the time indications on the signposts, as for a long time only the same time is written on them.

short_description: Surnamed "The Venice of Brie", Cr&eacute-la-Chapelle (Seine-et-Marne) is crossed by three arms of the Grand-Morin river which form canals in the interior of the town, hence its small resemblance to Venice.
long_description: As you walk through its streets, you will see that the town has kept the traces of its past, when the tanners used the water of the Grand-Morin to make leather. A place that attracted many painters in the 19th century, including Corot, Toulouse-Lautrec, Dunoyer-de-Ségonzac, Van Gogh and André Planson. The promise of a charming and bucolic stroll.

title: Baiului Mountains trail, between Sinaia and Bușteni
short_description: This is a classic hike in the Baiului Mountains, easily accessible by train from Bucharest or from Brasov. It starts at Sinaia train station and ends in Bușteni.
long_description:
For a start, you take the wide forest road that climbs sometimes steeply through the forest. It leads close to an abandoned sheepfold and then exits to the Baiului Mountain's main ridge. Though it might seem neverending, the forest road eventually takes you to a clearing with beautiful views over the road ahead.
The ridge has gentle and seemingly endless hills and broken paths due to the ATVs that often venture on these mountains. Cyclists also come here often for on-day MTB  routes. The main path is relatively easy to recognize on each hill. The panoramas open up on a clear day towards several mountains: Bucegi, Piatra Mare, Ciucaș, Grohotiș.
The difficulty of the route rather stands in its length than in the required effort. Stops can be made anywhere on the route.
We descended on Mount Zamora, although if there is time, one can continue to the Sorica slope and descend to Azuga, for a complete crossing of the Baiului Mountains. We came across a sheepfold on the way down, where you could buy cheese. The last part seemed very long, on a forest road that ended close to the Cantacuzino Castle in Busteni.

title: Climbing the Linkerskopf (2,459 m) in Allgäu
short_description: Breathe in the fresh air and leave the crowds behind on this fun hike up a grassy and somewhat lonely mountain in the stunning setting of the Allgäu Alps. Staggering views are guaranteed.
long_description:
Despite its prominence as you travel up the Rappental (valley) from Faistenoy - and from other locations - the Linkerskopf comes across as a fairly overlooked and unloved peak in comparison to its neighbours.  
Having bypassed it myself on so many occasions, I'm glad to be able to say I finally took the time to go up to the top - and I very much enjoyed the trip. 
What starts as a wander up benign grassy flanks eventually gives way to a steeper and rockier upper section that requires some light scrambling (UIAA I) before you reach the ridge of the summit and the two small crucifixes that mark a successful ascent. From the top, you can enjoy a largely uninterrupted view all the back down to Oberstdorf and beyond, as well as the spectacular ridgelines to the west and east.  Looking south you will see the nearby Rappensee, the outline of Germany's southernmost peak (the Biberkopf), and beyond that, the Lechtal Alps.
The first section of the route follows the extremely well-trodden path from Faistenoy to Enzianhütte via Einödsbach, which I tried to get through as quickly as possible. Maps do not provide an officially marked trail up the Linkerskopf itself, but I discovered on my way up that there are in fact traces of a trail, though these completely disappear in places. I tracked my hike, so the route I'm providing is a pretty faithful recreation of what I consider to be the optimal approach. 
In all, I'd say this was a very satisfying trip and a fun way to spend my Sunday morning. I hope you enjoy it too.

title: La Soufrière
short_description: The trail is embellished with informative panels that guide visitors through the exploration of the Soufrière volcano, nicknamed the "Old Lady", following the story of Andézinn and Patiss, a young girl and her grandfather.
long_description: This hike to the summit of La Soufrière is a must for nature and adventure lovers. Starting in Bains Jaunes, this demanding route passes through dense tropical forest before climbing to an altitude of 1,467 meters. The trail, dotted with fumaroles and volcanic landscapes, offers spectacular views of the island and the ocean. At the summit, hikers are rewarded with breathtaking views and the unique sensation of being on an active volcano.

title: Vom Strandbad Hauser zur Juget-Alpe
short_description:
Vom Parkplatz Strandbad Hauser entlang des Ufers am wunderschönen Großen Alpsee inmitten des Naturparks Nagelfluhkette. Vom See geht es ein paar wenige sportliche Höhenmeter noch oben bis zur Juget-Alpe und über einen Waldweg wieder zurück zum Ausgangspunkt.
Translate to English
long_description:
Wer einen guten ersten Einblick davon bekommen möchte, wie die Atmosphäre im schönen Immenstadt i. Allgäu wirkt, für den ist dieser Rundwanderweg genau richtig.
Der Große Alpsee ist für viele Touristen, Einheimische und Wassersportler ein echtes Highlight. Im Sommer kann man sich hier abkühlen oder den Windsurfern draußen auf dem See zuschauen. Wer es gemütlich mag, der genießt die Sonne bei einem Spaziergang entlang des Ufers. Mit dem glitzernden Wasser zu den Füßen und dem Blick in Richtung der malerischen Berge, kann einem hier nichts mehr fehlen. 
Für Verpflegung zwischendurch ist auf dieser Tour ebenfalls gesorgt.  Ein aussichtsreicher Weg führt nach oben zur Juget-Alpe. Hier kann man sich stärken, einen guten Bodensee-Wein genießen oder einfach die Seele baumeln lassen, bevor man den Rückweg antritt.

title: In search of the Virgin Mary waterfall
short_description: The Virgin Mary Waterfall is a lesser known or sought after tourist attraction in Domogled-Valea Cerna National Park, although access is fairly easy. The hike may seem long, but the scenery rewards you in full.
long_description:
The waterfall takes its name from the symbolic protection provided by the Catholic statue of St. Mary, located in a niche in the rock next to the water.
The path is clear, marked, with no difficult portions. You walk only on the dirt road, through several shady passages, past several panoramic points with the tail of Lake Prisaca. For those who still have the energy once they reach the waterfall, if they continue a little further, they reach a clearing, from where another even more generous view of the lake opens up. Here you can also take a lunch break.
The walk to the waterfall can be an alternative hike for those who are reluctant to climb to the Vânturătoarea waterfall - a more strenuous but more demanding route.

title: Crossing Nagelfluhkette from Hochgrat to Bühl
short_description: The crossing of the Nagelfluhkette is considered a very demanding mountain tour.
long_description: The crossing of the Nagelfluhkette can be described as a truly extensive mountain tour. Above all, however, it is one of the most beautiful ridge and crest hikes of the entire German Alpine rim. It is also a spectacular mountain tour with a wealth of views, which requires both surefootedness and fitness. Refreshments are available at the Hochgrat mountain station at the mountain restaurant and on leaving the summit in the direction of Bühl at the Alpe Gund and the Sennalpe Mittelberg. The Nagelfluhkette Nature Park is a cross-border nature park in the Nagelfluhkette in the Allgäu Alps, between the German region of Allgäu and the state of Vorarlberg. The nature park is the first cross-border nature park between Germany and Austria

short_description:
Immerse yourself in history and awe-inspiring landscapes with the Grande Traversée du Mercantour (GR® GTM).

From Entraunes in the upper Var to Menton on the Mediterranean coast, cross the emblematic valleys of the Tinée, Vésubie, Roya and Bévéra, for breathtaking panoramas between the Alps and the sparkling sea.
The Grande Traversée du Mercantour (GTM) invites you to combine sporting challenge and wonder. This exceptional itinerary, demanding but rewarding, unveils spectacular panoramas where Alpine peaks meet the azure reflections of the Mediterranean.

title: Grohotis Peak from Bratocea Pass
short_description: Having a landscape similar to that of the Baiului Mountains, Mount Grohotiș offers relaxing mountain hikes. The hike to Grohotiș Peak might seem endless, but nevertheless rewarding.
long_description:
Mount Grohotiș is not very popular among hikers. Instead, off-road enthusiasts come here often, taking advantage of the unforested and gentle peaks, which also allow extraordinary panoramas.
Grohotiș Peak (1768m), the highest of these peaks, could very easily be confused with a hilltop. To get here, you follow the marked path. It takes you first through a forest, continues on a forest road visibly marked by ATV wheels. In the end, you reach the alpine meadow. The path, still visible on the dry vegetation, goes by several peaks until actually reaching the main peak.
The walk in the alpine meadow might seem very long. Many hikers mistake the Bobul Mare peak for Grohotiș Peak, and stop there. But the latter is marked with a concrete pillar.
On the horizon, on clear days, you can see the entire ridge of the Bucegi Mountains, the Baiului Mountain, and parts of Ciucaș Mountain.

images.caption: A path is visible in the dry vegetation

title: On top of Tisaru Peak, above Tișița Gorges, Vrancea Mountains
short_description: A scarcely known hiking idea, very unpopular as such, dedicated to those who want to admire Țișița Gorges from a different angle. From above, more specifically.
long_description:
If it weren't for hiking enthusiasts, willing to roam through the wilderness of Vrancea Mountains, nobody would have known about this route. In Lepșa, you won't find any markings. In Lepșa, tourism is all about the Tisița Gorges and Putna Waterfall, both easy to access and tick off your list.
But this route offers you not only the pleasure of exploring a nature that just seems from a different universe compared to what happens below, in the gorges. Up here, you find silence, stillness, and wildness, regardless of the season. Down there, there's a lot of hustle and bustle, especially in the warm season. Here, you can also enjoy the delight of discovering really little-traveled places, namely little-known panoramas over the gorges, but also towards most of the prominent peaks in the Vrancea Mountains (Goru, Pietrosul Vrancei).
At the top, you will spot a torn flag, a sign that some have tried to somehow leave a mark here. But reaching this peak is not about the sign at the top, it's about the sense of grandeur you can enjoy standing up here, no higher than 1268 meters, and yet so far above everyone and everything.
The hike also covers a tiny segment of the gorges, not representative of all that they actually have to offer.

The flag on the Tisaru Mic peak
Forest galore in some of the wildest areas in Romania
Wild nature and the hiker trying to conquer it

The first stage of Via Aurelia leads from Rome, the heart of the former Roman Empire, to Northern Italy and beyond the French frontier to Southern France. Alongside the route you can discover the picturesque national park of Cinque Terre with its five breathtaking small towns Riomaggiore, Manarola, Corniglia, Vernazza and Monterosso al Mare.
From the fortress of Castello Doria at Vernazza you can enjoy stunning views of the sunny coastline. To those who are interested in culture, we recommend to stop by at the historic cemetery “Necropoli Monterozzi Tarquinia“.

title: Lakes Trail
short_description: The Lake Trail, which is just over 2 km long, has five incredible lakes in an area that contrasts with the brown tones of the cerrado, creating an enchanting scenery.
long_description:
The Trail of Lakes begins at a fork just after the entrance to the Juquery State Park. Continuing the journey, you arrive at the streets before the lakes, actually an old stables dating from the time of the Juquery Hospital Complex. Then you climb a ladder made of tyres, which leads to a belvedere with a beautiful panoramic view of the five lakes in the surroundings. From here, just follow the omnipresent trail of red earth, to the east, and you arrive at an extensive plateau that leads to the main path.
The Juquery State Park was created in June 1993 with the purpose of preserving the áMananciais areas of the Cantareira System. A long time ago, the site used to house the Juquery Psychiatric Hospital, designed by Ramos Azevedo and founded by Franco da Rocha in 1895. The place still maintains the structure of its former building, being possible to see it in many points of the trails.

title: जुडा का तालाब ट्रैक
short_description: जुड का तालाब उत्तराँचल राज्य के उत्तरकाशी ज़िले के संकरी गाँव के पास म ौजूद एक अल्पाइन झील है। केदारकंठा शिखर ट् रेल की इस पौराणिक झील के साथ महाभारत की कई कहानिया ं जुड़ी हैं।
long_description:
जुडा का ताल उत्तरकाशी जिले के गोविंद वन्यजीव अभयारण्य में 10000 फीट की ऊंचाई पर स्थित एक हाई अल्टीट्यूड झील है। जुडा तालाब का ट्रैक अनुभवी और नौसिखिया दोनों किस्म के हाइकर्स को बहुत पसंद आता है। इसकी ट्रेल देवदार, ओक, बाँझ, और बुरांश के जंगलों से होकर गुजरती है और ठंडी नीली झील पर आकर कर ख़त्म होती है।      
संकरी गांव इस ट्रैक का बेस कैंप है और जुडा का ताल वहां से करीब 4 किलोमीटर दूर है। संकरी गाँव से शुरू होने वाली केदारकंठा ट्रेल पर करीब 2.5 किलोमीटर जाने पर जुडा का तालाब के लिए एक ट्रेल कटती है जो बहुत बाद में आगे जाकर फिर से केदारकंठा ट्रेल से मिल जाती है। 
झील के किनारे रहने के लिए एक पर्वतीय कुटिया/आश्रय स्थल भी बनाया गया है जहाँ हाइकर्स आराम से रात गुज़ार सकते हैं। आसपास अपना खुद का तम्बू भी लगा कर रुका जा सकता है। 
जुडा का तालाब ट्रैक की सबसे अच्छी बात यह है की यह हाईकर्स को अगले बड़े केदारकंठा ट्रैक के लिए शारीरिक और मानसिक रूप से तैयार कर देता है। इसके अलावा परिवार और बच्चे जिनके लिये शायद कठिन केदारकंठा ट्रैक करना लगभग असंभव सा है, उनको भी जुडा तालाब ट्रैक करके वैसा ही लैंडस्केप और अनुभव मिल जाता है।
वैसे तो यह बारहमासी ट्रेल मार्ग है लेकिन फिर भी जुडा का तालाब की ट्रैकिंग का सबसे अच्छा समय वसंत और जाड़ों का मौसम है। जहाँ वसंत में मौसम में हाइकर्स को हरियाली, फूल, तितलियाँ, चिड़ियाँ, और साफ़ हिमालयी हवा मिलती है, वहीँ दूसरी ओर जाड़ों में सफ़ेद बर्फ की चादर से भरा हुआ लैंडस्केप और जमी हुई ठंडी झील एक जादुई दुनिया का जैसा नज़ारा पेश करती हैं।

title: Kust till Kustleden - from Verum to Hårsjö
short_description: The ninth stage of the Kust till Kustledens leads from Verum campsite through wide forests and light woodland to Hårsjö campsite.
long_description: Our stage today runs along the Vieån River and some lakes that are great for swimming, fishing or canoeing. Around Lake Vittsjö we find the traces of medieval iron mining and even today there are lumps of ore at the bottom of the lake. In Vittsjö we have the opportunity to learn about the early history of the region. The Swedish-Danish border once ran through here and the rich iron deposits were protected by fortifications

title: Kristdala - The small farms around Krokshult
short_description: Large circular tour around the abandoned, typical Swedish farms of Krokshult with their high fences
long_description: On the hike we learn a lot about the former small-scale agriculture in Småland. The infertile soil, which was covered with stones, did not allow for large-scale agriculture. As a result, many small farms were formed, which mainly cultivated for their own needs. Our route takes us past some of these small historic farms and we marvel at the high fences that were traditionally built to protect against moose. One of the farms is now protected as a Krokshult nature reserve: With its beautiful wooden houses, well-kept gardens and typical Swedish appearance, this small village is a real eye-catcher. The hike runs through the forest and partly on gravel paths. On the way we can fully enjoy the peace and quiet and the rural country life.

title: The wine road through the vineyards of Vaslui and Iasi
short_description: The wine road through the vineyards of Huși-Iași is, basically, a journey in search of the authentic scent and taste of two types of Romanian wine: Busuioaca de Bohotin and Grasa de Cotnari.
long_description:
This route is the north-eastern alternative to the wine route through Panciu and Odobești vineyards. The salty winery halls dotted along the vineyard hills of Vaslui and Iași are less compact than those in Vrancea, and the existing infrastructure requires a little more organisation.
As expected, Cotnari wines are one of the main highlights of this tour. The most important winery here, Cotnari, is making efforts to develop this tourist segment by diversifying its visit/tasting packages. This is why wine tourism in the area could have the city of Iasi as its central point or as a stopover.
The Vaslui-Iași wine route does not excel in natural landscapes, but the richness of cultural activities is not lacking. Thus, besides tasting the best Moldovan wines - including one of the most popular local varieties, Busuioaca de Bohotin - you can include in your trip visits to various mansion-museums or spending several days in Iasi.

title: A pilgrimage to the Shoani temple
short_description: The Shoani temple is an artful temple in a stunning high mountain location on the way to Dombai or the outskirts of Karachay-Cherkessia.
long_description: One of the oldest temples of present-day Russia in Karachay-Cherkessia – the Shoani Church. It has been whispering incessant prayer for over a thousand years. The temple was built in the 10th century and it is still active. It dates back to the former Alan Republic thanks to Byzantium. Byzantine craftsmen built the temple in the densely populated and economically important at that time way. The pilgrims of the temple still honour and observe the old traditions, which have not been lost to this day. They carry lambs from the village to the summit to observe the ritual there. In central Russia, the temple became known only in the 19th century, when Potemkin paid a visit. Undoubtedly such a temple will forever be a value and treasure, both of the region and of the whole country.

title: The "phosphatières du Cloup d'Aural"
short_description: Jump into the history of earth and life
long_description:
The unit of time in geology is one million years. Difficult to imagine what this represents, often we compare the history of the Earth to a year: if it had been formed on January 1st at 00:00 am, man would have appeared on December 31st around 7:00 pm.
For this hike, the times have been transposed into a distance, respecting the proportion 2 meters for 1 million years. On this scale, one must imagine that the 9km of the circuit represents the 4.5 billion years of the Earth!
A visit guide, in the form of cards to be slipped into the 37 terminals on the circuit, is available at the site's reception desk and allows you to locate the main stages in the history of the Earth and Life step by step.
For families, ask for the children's guide.

title: A Peak of Love for us!
short_description: Love Peak — a mountain for lovers and lovers of easy conquests of beautiful peaks. The mountain is situated on the Tunkinsky mountain range at an altitude of 2124 metres, in Buryatia.
long_description:
The name - Peak of Love - comes from legend, the essence of which is that if lovers climb the peak together, their love will be stronger and more inseparable. This is why the mountain is a success with both believers in the legend and doubters alike. In any case, queues of fans of this eternal and not only bookish word «love» flock to Arshan – the village where the trail to Love Peak begins.
To be sure of the credibility of the legend, it is worth visiting the village of Arshan itself, where, according to the residents, «grace» descends to take the peak of Love entirely and without residue.

title: Hiking day to the foothills of the Ptysh mountains, Dombiy-Ulgen, Ine Peak - Ptysh Waterfall
short_description: A one-day trek to the Ptysh glacier introduces us to many of Dombai's protected areas at the same time. The hike follows the Dombai-Ulgen Gorge, passing Ine Peak and waterfalls to the foot of Ptysh.
long_description: The Ptysh Glacier - on the border between Russia and Abkhazia - is enormous, with an average altitude of over 3,500. The trail leading to it is not the most popular, but it is rarely less scenic than the popular ones. White rhododendrons grow in the Ptyszka Gorge, a very rare plant species. The glacier itself is shrinking from year to year, thawing and therefore diminishing. The reason: global warming, not the influx of active hikers! On the way to the glacier one can see Ine, a chic, pointed peak reminiscent of the great and naughty Matterhorn. In addition to the mountains, the trail takes us to Ptusz Waterfall, aka Maiden's Spits;

title: Crossing the Lençois Maranhenses
short_description: With some of the most beautiful landscapes in all of Brazil, the Travessia dos Lençóis Maranhenses can be divided into three sections that make it an unforgettable experience for everyone.
long_description:
The Travessia dos Lençóis Maranhenses long-distance trail begins at Canto de Atins, a little north of Ponta do Mangue. After two or three hours of walking, small and small lakes begin to be noticed, and the dunes gain a good few meters of slope. Arriving in Baixa Grande, where some families live.
The second stretch has 11 km and goes to Queimadas. On this day the scenery of dunes and lagoons é surreal and há several stops for bathing. The restinga vegetation becomes more abundant on the way that one hour leads to a riverside clearing, the village of Queimada dos Britos.
The último day of the stretch é the most physically challenging, but the effort é rewarded by the sunrise from the top of the dunes. Some of the most beautiful landscapes are seen during this route. The next two hours follow the dunes  and with the sun higher on this final stretch, the tip é refresh yourself passing by the last lagoons, before reaching Santo Amaro.

title: From the centre of the world across Cerro Casitagua
short_description: Moderate hike with stunning views to a mild 3000er on the outskirts of Quito.
long_description: From Quito's northern suburbs, Casitagua presents itself as a rolling hill with a peculiar head of trees. While it might not look as impressive as some of the other mountains surrounding the Ecuadorian capital, the hike across this long-stretched hill offers spectacular views over the city, the Western Cordillera, and all the way to the snow-capped peaks of Cayambe and Cotopaxi. Starting precisely on the ecuator, the route leads through beautiful vegetation, a cooling forest, and to an observation tower on three and a half thousand meters. Unfortunately, parts of the trail have been heavily eroded by motorbikers and rains, which makes this route more challenging than it would have to be. Still a worthwile undertaking and a perfect first acclimatization tour before attempting higher peaks in the Sierra.

title: From Kempten to the Forest Chapel
short_description: We enjoy a scenic and very varied tour near Kempten. Unfortunately, the proximity of the A7 motorway cannot be denied in some sections, but this does not detract from the nature experience.
long_description:
The Bachtelweiher is a pond in the east of Kempten that was created in the 13th century. For a long time it was used for fish farming and the operation of the Bachtelmühle. Today there is a restaurant with a beer garden and a miniature golf course. There is a playground for the little ones. You can swim in the pond to your heart's content.
On our tour we follow the course of the A7 federal motorway to Süden for a while. In 2010, the last section was opened in the Allgäu.
The motorway runs from the German border at Ellund to the Austrian border at Füssen. Drivers cross the border through a tunnel. Near the village of Durach, the valley of the Durach is crossed on a 290 m long bridge. We can marvel at the imposing dimensions of this bridge from below on the way.
The Neuenburg castle on the slopes of the Durach valley was built at the beginning of the 14th century. The last owner of the building was the Kempten baron Friedrich von Laubenberg. Today, the castle's dimensions can only be guessed at, as only a few remains have been preserved after it was used as a building material donor.
There are numerous play and adventure stations for children along the Durach, such as a climbing spider's web, or a long slide at the motorway bridge.
The forest chapel, built in 1937 by Michael Suppmeier, stands between the Waldschänke and the station of the Sulzbrunn iodine baths in the foothills of the Kempt forest. Many signposts show the hiker the right way there.

title: Evening tour at sunset from the Riedberg Pass to the Riedberger Horn
short_description: The Riedberger Horn - whether in winter or summer - is perfect for an evening tour at sunset.
long_description:
The route starts in the large parking lot near the Grasgehren mountain hut. The summit of the Riedberger Horn and the Besler can be seen from the start. The start of the hiking trail is at the end of the parking lot just behind the Grasgehren mountain hut. The trail leads across lush autumn meadows past a small stream and into a small wooded area
The somewhat steeper serpentines provide repeated views of the breathtaking Allgäu Alps. From the ridge at the latest, you are rewarded with an incredible view of the Allgäu Alps - from the Hochvogel to the Großer Widderstein.
Now all you have to do is follow the ridge to the top of the Riedberger Horn to immerse yourself in the wonderful panoramic view with sunset in the Lake Constance region.

title: Panoramic tour around Bernau
short_description: This pleasantly hikable route impresses with its views over the valley around Bernau and the open landscape, but also with occasional dips into the gently undulating hilly landscape.
long_description: From the Ankenbühl hikers' car park, we take the narrow path to the left of the overview board and walk uphill across a pasture. We already have a beautiful view of the valley. After we have crossed the pasture, we go above the country school home (1) into a forest and continue hiking uphill. At the first bench, we follow the trail marking (yellow rhombus) further uphill until the gravelled path meets a wider driveway. We walk downhill on this in a south-westerly direction until we meet a road that leads us uphill again. We enjoy the unobstructed view as far as Bernau-Dorf and always follow the yellow rhombus. Finally, we leave our path, descend on a left turnoff to Bernau-Dorf (2), which we reach after about 3 km. We cross the asphalt road that crosses it. There you can take a 3 km detour via the Hans-Thoma-Weg to the Milchberg, with a brilliant view of the eastern high valley. Bernau is best known for the painter Hans Thoma, who was born in 1839 as a farmer's son in the Oberlehen district. It is also possible to make an excursion to the Herzogenhorn, the second highest mountain in the Black Forest, but this makes the tour a more than strenuous day's undertaking with an additional 4h. Our actual route follows the yellow rhombus to the left at the first junction in Bernau-Dorf in the direction of Bernau-Innerlehen, then the Dorfstraße. We ignore an uphill turn-off to the left marked with a yellow rhombus and continue along Nettenbachweg and Schulweg to the through road. A detour to the Innerlehen district is worthwhile because of the wood-processing handicraft businesses that are present everywhere there (you can see them in the Resenhof, Innerlehen district, next to the tourist information office). The Hans Thoma Museum in Innerlehen's town hall shows many original paintings by Hans Thoma; in the church next door we can see two altarpieces by him. The Resenhof, built in 1789, houses a farm museum that is well worth seeing. The museum documents how hard the farmers had to work to earn their living back then. Life in the Bernau high valley has always been shaped by wood processing (the "Schnefeln") - the changes in this craft are impressively documented. At the eastern end of the village, we cross the through road on our hike, continue towards the tennis courts and turn left onto a gravel path directly after a small stream before a bend. We follow this Albweg (3) (blue rhombus), which is lined with wooden sculptures at the beginning, for the next 5 km. We always keep in the direction of St. Blasien or Weierle and enjoy this idyllic section of trail, which is flanked by a steep section of forest on the right. Soon we cross the stream and reach a playground (4) with a barbecue area - an ideal place for a rest. Our route leads along a narrow path, initially through forest, to later open up views of the entire Bernau high valley. After these last two kilometres, we reach Weierle (5). From the through road, our path branches off to the left, following the sign towards Ankenbühl. The tour can be shortened by using the bus connection between Bernau-Weierle and Bernau-Dorf (please check the exact times beforehand, limited service at weekends).

title: Himmelschrofen Crossing
short_description: This wonderful mountain tour offers fantastic views of the Tettach and Stillach valleys. The mostly moderately difficult trail urgently requires surefootedness and a head for heights, as it partly runs directly on the ridge Some places can really be described as "airy". When descending to the Ostwandsteig, good orientation is necessary, especially in fog.
long_description: The Himmelschrofen is more of a ridge than just a summit, as it is formed by several elevations of different heights. From the Oberstdorf Golf Club we follow the normal trail steeply up to the summit cross. Afterwards, we make the pathless descent to the Ostwandsteig. From the basin of the front Rindersgundalpe, we reach the Trettach valley again via the old cattle drive trail. From here, it is a relatively long hike back to the starting point.

images.caption: Steep ascent below the terrain level

title: Jogging Route
short_description: Follow me on my personal favourite running route through Kempten! Once through the town and around the nearby Bachtelweiher pond and back along the Iller river. Very suitable for a walk or a short run.
long_description:
The small jogging route starts in the Kempten city park. Here you can first warm up and stretch before you start running.
The 10 km jogging loop takes between 1h - 1h 30min.

title: Dachstein: the suspension bridge, observation stairs to nowhere and the observation deck walking on the sky
short_description: A short but particularly spectacular hiking route starting with the descent from the Dachstein-Gletscherbahn in Styria, Austria
long_description:
A one-way hiking trail on a mountain that rises to a height of 3,000 meters above sea level! This is a particularly attractive experience that includes walking on a suspension bridge leading to the famous observation deck known as " Stairs to Nowhere ".
In this route, with the help of a short walk from the cable car that requires minimal physical effort, you will be able to reach a huge and spectacular suspension bridge from which a stunning and unique view of the enormous Dachstein glacier can be seen. Towards the end of the bridge, you can go down with the help of a few stairs and reach the transparent observation deck known as the stairs to nowhere. Also, it is recommended after getting off the cable car / on the way back, to go to the other side of the station and from there reach another observation deck on the valley known as the "SKY WALK" or in Hebrew translation: walking on the sky. On days with good visibility, you can look out over Slovenia and the Czech Republic from the balcony !

images.caption: The suspension bridge leading to the Stairs to Nowhere lookout
The view of the stairs to nowhere

title: Saint Marcellin
short_description: From the lair of the Paillasses to the mansions carved out of the rock: a walk through the eroded rock formations of the Cirque de Saint Marcellin.
long_description:
In the very heart of the Saint-Marcellin cirque, explore the Paillasses spring and explore the magnificent troglodyte village of Saint-Marcellin, all the while admiring a breathtaking view of the Gorges du Tarn.
Listen out for the sounds and movements of the mouflons that inhabit the steep cliffs of the Gorges du Tarn ledge.

title: The Black Water Trail
short_description: Trail along the shores of the Preta Água Preta Lake with beautiful scenery that provides an incredible experience within the exuberance of the Amazon forest within the Utinga Park.
long_description:
Practically the entire route of the trail takes place along the shores of the Lago Água Preta, which causes the path to flood in some stretches. In others, this proximity offers an incredible view of the lake. The trail draws attention by its beauty and also by the close contact with the exuberance of the forest, which has several typical trees of the Amazon region, ciphers, preserved land and a great diversity of fauna and flora.
The end of the trail é at the natural nursery of the Utinga State Park, which is next to the Visitor Centre. There is also the possibility of a boat trip on the lake, but the trip is short and restricted to the number of places available on the boat. However, it is worth it to see everything you would expect from a biome like the Amazon: flooded forests, aquatic plants, small forest trails and, if you are lucky, spot wildlife.

title: Winter Hiking
short_description: Kleiner Alpsee - Hub - Großer Alpsee - See - Konstanzer Ach - AlpSeeHaus - Naturpark Nagelfluhkette - Bühl a.Alpsee - Großer Alpsee Rundwanderweg - St. Stephan - Loretokapelle
long_description: After reaching the starting point by any means of transportation, just start the tour being in a great mood as you are going to experience the beauty of nature. Initially you will walk through some beautiful grasslands where there are benches to sit. After that you will cross the railway track. Just after walking a few minutes, you will see the lake of "Grosser Alpsee". Here you can rent a small boat or eat some delicious food. From now we are going towards the "Vorder See". You can play the game "Memory" on the way (See pictures). Here you can have a bath or have some fun with your kids. There is a Sportsclub nearby too where one can play Tennis. After this you will walk through a small tunnel and then reach the main road. After crossing the main road the hiking on the mountains starts. There are proper hiking ways for some distance but not all the way. One might feel, hopefully this road will bring us to an end too. Some small water falls can be seen too. From some points one can see the city. It is breathtaking. After about an hour of hiking, the way back will begin. It can be quite tricky at some point. All in all enjoy the trip :)

title: From Jungholz to the Stubental Alpe
short_description: asy hike to the Jungholzer Stubental Alpe. Enjoyment of nature and a unique view of the mountain landscape are included into this little hiking trip.
long_description:
A wonderful short and easy tour with a great view to the surrounding mountain landscape. The starting point is the free and spacious parking lot in the center of Jungholz. We start directly from the Jungholz church in the direction of the Langenschwand district. We are continuously on tarred paths and experience the idyll and landscape of the smallest Austrian enclave. During the route through forests and the unique nature, beautiful views can be enjoyed. After about an hour we arrive at the Alpe Stubental. There we can relax with a great view, good food and a cozy drink with "Karl" (the hut owner). On Fridays we enjoy the culture of the Austrians and Allgaeu with music and a great atmosphere.
  Whoever walks this tour will not forget it!

title: The Three Spouts
short_description: A mythical hike in the Sao Paulo forest, the 3 beaks are a must for experienced hikers.
long_description:
It will allow a magnificent view of the Couspeau massif to the east, the Drôme valley to the north, with a particular rocky hole in the La Laveuse rock; rocky le Trou de la pelle  in the rock of La Laveuse and finally a look plunging over the syncline to its western end Rochecolombe.
To find out more about this destination, visit their website

title: Picturesque trekking through a few Maramures traditional villages
short_description: A small part of the staged tourist route called `Drumul Maramureșului` that takes you through some of the most picturesque and popular localities on the Marei and Cosău valleys, while also offering the possibility of slight detours to admire some wonders of nature.
long_description:
This is sometimes called the Green Road, aiming at promoting sustainable tourism in Maramureș. Trekking this road, you can spend time in the small local communities you pass through, but you also have the chance to admire most attractions in the region: traditional villages, wooden churches and wooden gates, dreamlike natural landscapes culminating in the wide alpine meadows and rocky peaks of the Gutâi Mountains, with the possibility to hike to the highest point: the Crest of the Cock (Creasta cocosului).
Breb or Mara are tourist destinations popular among Romanians, but this route takes to paths with little traffic, known mainly to cyclists or locals. Even in the villages, you walk past the main road, so you have every chance to avoid large groups, noise, and traffic. Except when you need to get supplies from dowtown.

title: Le Tour des Monts d'Aubrac - GR® de Pays
short_description:
Explorez le vaste plateau de l'Aubrac en empruntant l'itinéraire du GR de Pays® du Tour des Monts d'Aubrac, et découvrez un territoire marqué par les forces naturelles, avec des paysages authentiques sculptés par la vie de ses habitants."
Translate to English
long_description:
Parcourez à pied sur 8 jours, des montagnes aux villages, l'immensité ondoyante des collines, burons, lacs, forêts, et troupeaux de vaches d'Aubrac. Explorez depuis les sentiers ancestraux un paysage de contraste, où les horizons s'étirent sous l'influence des vents et bravent les caprices du climat.
Translate to English

title: Track 6 Bretagne - Carhaix to St-Méen-le-Grand
short_description: Explore Argoat from the edge of the Monts d'Arrée on a bike tour along the Voie 6 Bretagne.
long_description:
This route, built mainly on a former railroad line, takes you past charming villages with every pedal stroke.
Surrounded by wooded mountains, Lac de Guerlédan stretches for 12 km, offering an invigorating recreational break before reaching Louison Bobet's birthplace.

title: Juget Alpe
short_description: Short tour from the Schlettermoos parking lot via Köpfle to Jugetalpe
long_description:
This beautiful, fairly easy circular tour is ideal for a family outing and for anyone who appreciates beautiful views and doesn't want to exert themselves too much. The footpath alternates between shady sections at the beginning and sunny passages with far-reaching views.
The two alps on the route are perfect for a leisurely stop - and you will be rewarded with magnificent views of the Großer Alpsee and the Allgäu Alps along the way.
