title: Circular hike in the Ein Gedi Nature Reserve at the Dead Sea
short_description: Varied hike in the Ein Gedi nature reserve between the mountains of the Judean Desert in the west and the Dead Sea in the east
long_description: This extremely popular hike takes us through the Wadi David in the Ein Gedi Nature Reserve. Two streams run through the oasis, fed by rainfall in the mountains. As a result, there are numerous plants and animals in the nature reserve, some of which are rare. On the way there are wonderful views of the Dead Sea. An absolute highlight of the tour is the waterfall in Wadi David, under which there is a cool, natural pool that invites you to take a refreshing dip. A few entry aids take you into the small pool, which is filled with cool spring water.

images.caption: Camels grazing in the date grove
Excavation site near the date grove

title: Easy trip to Josefsthaler Wasserfälle
short_description: An easy, short and family-friendly hiking trail leading to the Josefsthaler Falls in southern Germany near the Austrian border
long_description: A linear and easy route that is a great travel destination for families with young children as well as for adults who want to experience a lot of nature within a short walking distance and with minimal effort. Along the way, flowing water, picnic lawns, wading spots and of course two large waterfalls rising to a total height of 8-12 meters await you. Hikers will be able to continue walking on a route beyond the route marked on the map and complete the circular route.

title: From Iacobdeal Lake to Priopcea Peak, Măcin National Park
short_description: A hike that partially covers the Troemsis route in the Măcinu Mountains National Park. Try it to reach the main tourist attractions in the region: Iacobdeal Lake and Priopcea Peak.
long_description:
The hike starts from Iacobdeal Lake, crosses the Bulgarian Peony Reserve, reaches the Chervant - Priopcea pass, and climbs steeply to the top of Priopcea for a well-deserved panorama.
For the most part of the route, the landscape is typical for Dobrogea: arid hills, lots of boulders of various shapes and sizes, shrubs, and clusters of trees. If you're lucky enough, you'll see turtles.
Marked with a yellow stripe, the route starts from the ruins of the Troemsis fortress, heads to the lake, and crosses the entire Priopcea ridge, while also touching the peak of the same name. Finally, it descends into Cerna.
On this segment, if not entirely, the route is suitable for children.

title: Hiking circuit: the Fautais coastline
short_description: La Faute-sur-Mer is a sandy peninsula in constant morphological evolution. Bordered on one side by the Lay river and on the other by the Ocacutean river for more than 10 km, its width does not exceed 2 km. From year to year, the peninsula grows and the sand piles up in the middle of the river.
long_description:
On your way:
The national natural reserve of the casse de la belle Henriette.
Created in 2011, this reserve extends over 337 ha, between La Tranche-sur-Mer and La Faute-sur-Mer.
It is accessible to visitors within the limits and respect of the improved and marked paths.
The Lay estuary
Between the points of Arçay and Aiguillon, the Lay estuary opens up where the movements of the tide have been regulated by the construction of the Braud and Moricq dams. Between land and sea, fresh and salt water, the Lay estuary constitutes an environment of exceptional biological productivity.

title: Comfortable tour around the Salzach-Lakes in Liefering
short_description: A relaxing and educational walk through the local recreation and landscape conservation area Salzachsee-Saalachspitz, a wonderful break from everyday life at any time of year.
long_description:
Not far from Salzburg's historic city center lies the Salzachsee-Saalachspitz recreation and landscape conservation area. It covers an area of 184.4 hectares and is located on a gravel plain from the Upper Cretaceous period. There are a total of 10 lakes and ponds in the area, not all of which are freely accessible.
Both flora and fauna in this area are remarkable: With a little luck, walkers will encounter hedgehogs, squirrels and different species of ducks and geese, and there are also various species of trees such as sycamore and English oak and a variety of shrubs to discover. It is also worth taking a look at the water: pike, zander and chub feel at home in the waters. The trail also passes a protected deadwood area and thus offers not only recreation in the fresh air but also instructive insights into the animal and plant world.
If you fancy a bit of a change of pace along the way, you can jump into the bathing lake, take a break at the nearby mini-golf course or stop off at Charly's Auwirt after your walk.

images.caption: Wanderung in Salzburg: Gemütliche Salzachsee-Runde in Liefering

title: On the Vânturiș peak: an ideal route for children
short_description: Would you like to take the kids on a mountain bike ride higher up, but don't know where to start? The Bucegi Mountains are among the most permissive. And the Vânturiș peak is a recommended climb to do in any season.
long_description:
Vârful Vânturiș rises up near the Dichiu hut and dominates part of the Transbucegi trail. From the road level, it looks like a partly wooded, partly pine-covered mound.
There are several reasons why this trail is recommended even for younger children, who are getting used to walking on rough and sloping terrain:
very gentle ascent on foot and on foot
approach to the hut or other attractions in Bucegi (so the walk can be combined with other activities)
easy access from the national road
spacious landscapes with lots of flowers in spring;
possibility to capture the cloud ceiling in autumn; superb views in all seasons - so a great variety of details for children to learn from
except for the winter climb, the route does not require special equipment
The hike to the valley begins as a dirt road, in the same direction as the hike to St. Moritz. About 100-200 metres after starting off, look to the right for a narrow, dry valley with boulders that you have to climb almost like a ladder. Follow the valley for a while, then aim for the ridge on the left side of the valley. As there is no clear path, you can walk through the blueberry bushes. In spring, the slopes are full of bramble; in summer - rhododendron.
It is possible to see a red dot on some stones, a sign that this is the right path. The plateau of the valley is quite wide, but fixed to the valley there is a metal plate erased.

images.caption: Vânturiș Peak, from the Vânturiș Waterfalls

title: View of Montreal
short_description: A one-way urban walking route that passes through the urban nature of the city of Montreal and leads to the highest and most impressive observation point of the city
long_description:
A relatively short hiking trail (relatively moderate in elevation) that leaves the city center, passes through the wooded area of the city and reaches a view point overlooking the Mont-Royal mountain, this view point is the most successful on the city center of Montreal.
Due to the fact that the route is linear, i.e. one-way, the walking time as well as the distance shown on this page are for one direction only, but at any point on the route you can retrace the steps to the beginning of the route. Please note that there are many roads leading from the city to the observation point, for example you can go down another way and then reach another part of the city.

images.caption: Look for the giant man on one of the buildings!
A stunning view of the city's skyscrapers
A panoramic image of the city of Montreal

title: From Jungholz to the Pfeifferberg
short_description: Medium-difficulty hiking tour through Jungholz with fabulous views and great sights in the Tyrolean and Allgäu Alps.
long_description:
Jungholz is Austria's smallest enclave with around 300 inhabitants. It lies in the middle of untouched nature and is known as an insider tip and starting point for unique outdoor tours.
  This is a moderately difficult hiking tour up the Pfeifferberg (1457 metres) with a guarantee of wonderful views of the Allgäu and Tyrolean mountains in the most peaceful atmosphere. There are numerous places to stop for refreshments and sights to see along the way.

title: The V42 "Saint-Malo/Arzal.  Saint-Malo - Rennes"
short_description: The V42 "Saint-Malo/Arzal", also known as the "Liaison Manche Océan", is an itinerary of national importance that links the English Channel to the Atlantic Ocean, following former railroad lines and the towpaths of the Rance, the Canal d'Ille-et-Rance and the Vilaine. The route passes through charming villages, towns of art and history such as Dinard, Dinan and Rennes, and exceptional sites such as the Eleven Locks and the Boël Mill, offering magnificent scenery along the way.
long_description:
As one of the department's major routes, the V42 crosses it from north to south and intersects with other itineraries, particularly for cyclists, offering the chance to venture off the main paths. Numerous services are available in the vicinity of the Voie Verte, including information, accommodation for walkers, restaurants, tourist sites and bike rentals.
The route is divided into two sections, "Saint-Malo/Rennes" and "Rennes/Redon", and here we focus on the "Saint-Malo/Rennes" section. With a total distance of 108 kilometers, it is recommended that you cycle it over 2 to 3 days. For a 2-day tour, a stage is suggested in the Hédé/Tinténiac area (45 km), while for a 3-day tour, stages are proposed in Montreuil-sur-Ille (33 km) and Dinan (46 km).

title: Hiking Adventure from Ofterschwang to the Ofterschwanger Horn
short_description: Scenic hike from the World Cup village of Ofterschwang to the northernmost peak of the Hörnerdörfer, the Ofterschwanger Horn.
long_description: The Ofterschwanger Horn is a 1406 m high peak of the Hörner group and a popular destination in summer and winter. The mountain is optimally accessible by the World Cup Express (4-seater chairlift). It is not for nothing that the Ofterschwanger Horn is known as a panoramic mountain - from the top we enjoy wonderful views of the Allgäu main ridge, the Illertal valley around Sonthofen and the Oster and Gunzesrieder valleys.

title: Machabee Viewpoint, Black River National Park, Mauritius
short_description: Hike to Machabee Viewpoint in Black River National Park, Mauritius
long_description:
The tour leads via the Colophane Trail to Machabee Viewpoint. On the way, we have an impressive view over the Black River National Park, the "Black River Peak", with 835m the highest mountain of Mauritius, and towards the north to the mountain range near Port Louis with the two mountains "Le Pouce" (820m) and "Pieter Both" (820m).
At Machabee Viewpoint we look through a gorge to the small village of Tamarin, the associated Tamarin Mountain (560m) and directly behind it the open sea.

title: Malmveien - A walk through history.
short_description: The route follows the DNT's marked path from Røros to Langen Gjestegård at the gateway to Femundsmarka. The route is just under 50 km long and has overnight accommodation at Marenvollen and Fjølburøsta.
long_description:
The oldest traces of people along the Malmveien are many thousands of years old. The landscape in parts of the area is characterised by pine forests and elongated oaks (esker). These landforms were formed at the end of the last ice age, about 10 000 years ago. Along waterways and wetlands such as Feragen, Langtjønna and Femunden there are many traces of human activity. On the dry, self-drained gravel marshes along the reed beds there were fine settlements and good fishing opportunities.
From Røros at 667 moh. the route goes through easy mountain terrain with the highest point at 900 moh., and along pine-clad sand and gravel marshes.

title: From the Bovilla Reservoir to Gamtit
short_description: The Bovilla reservoir above Tirana is becoming increasingly popular not only among sport climbers - the surprisingly wild valley between gentle hills on one side and imposing rock faces on the other promises an impressive nature experience just a few kilometres outside the capital. The best view is from Gamtit, but the way up is a bit tedious.
long_description: The trail up Gamtit mostly follows old shepherds' paths - and therein lies the problem: numerous paths get lost in the undergrowth of the dense vegetation, making finding your way a real challenge. Also, especially in summer, the branches of the bushes overgrow the path, which makes progress very frustrating at times. On the last few metres to the ridge, however, the vegetation opens up and the views on the way to the summit compensate for the drudgery.

images.caption: Gamtit (in the background) is certainly one of the most striking mountains in the Tirana area. The ascent is from the reservoir on the back side.
It is hard to believe that this wild and romantic landscape is less than 20 kilometres outside the capital.
One of the rare views in the lower part of the trail: morning mist over the Bovilla reservoir
The dense vegetation makes progress in the lower part sometimes very arduous.
The largest inhabitant of the Dajti National Park is also one of the shyest: you always get to see the brown bears' footprints.
The view from the summit compensates for the struggle through the undergrowth on the ascent.

title: Pedra Bonita Trail
short_description: The Pedra Bonita trail is one of the most famous in Rio de Janeiro. Located in the Tijuca National Park, it offers the most spectacular views of the city.
long_description: The Pedra Bonita trail is one of the most famous trails in Rio de Janeiro, because besides offering the most fantastic view of the city, it is also a short, relatively easy and free trail. The trail is located in section C of the Tijuca National Park, which is home to one of the largest urban forests in the world. Enjoy a new perspective of places already known as the beach of S o Conrado, the Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas and the Christ the Redeemer; the Pedra da Gávea, the Two Brothers Hill and the beaches and lagoons of Barra da Tijuca.

title: मावफलांग सेक्रेड ग्रोव (पवित्र वन) का साइकिल दौरा
short_description: शिलांग से 25  किलोमीटर दूर मावफलांग गांव की खासी पहाड़ियों में स्थित सेक्रेड ग्रोव्स 192 एकड ़ में फैला हुआ एक संरक्षित जंगल है जो सदियों पुरानी खासी म ान्यताओं के अनुसार एक पवित्र वन है।
long_description:
शिलांग के कैथेड्रल ऑफ़ मैरी चर्च से मावफलांग सेक्रेड ग्रोव्स तक का 25 किलोमीटर साइकिल दौरा बहुत ही रोमांचक है। यह दौरा मुख्यतः शिलांग की अंदरूनी शहरी सड़कों और फिर बाद में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 106 से होता हुआ मावफलांग गाँव तक जाता है। 
मावफलांग सेक्रेड ग्रोव्स (पवित्र वन) में केवल एक नियम है - "इस जंगल से कोई कुछ नहीं ले सकता, अन्यथा देवता गुस्सा हो जाते हैं"। जंगल के कुछ पेड़ 1000 साल से अधिक पुराने हैं। ऐसी मान्यता है कि यहाँ पाए जाने वाले कुछ पौधों में तपेदिक और कैंसर को ठीक करने की क्षमता हैं। मावफलांग सेक्रेड ग्रोव्स के अंदर पुराने राज्याभिषेक और बलिदान स्थल भी हैं जहाँ खासी जनजाति के मुखियाओं का राज्याभिषेक हुआ करता था और देवताओं को जानवरों की बलि दी जाती थी। ऐसे स्थान मोनोलिथ (चट्टान स्तम्भों) द्वारा चिह्नित है। अब हर साल इन पवित्र जंगलों में आदिवासी विरासत और संस्कृति दिखने वाला वाला तीन दिवसीय मोनोलिथ उत्सव आयोजित होता है। 
हालांकि यह साइकिल टूर ज्यादा मुश्किल नहीं है, लेकिन बाइकर्स को पहले आठ किलोमीटर तक हलकी चढ़ाई मिलेगी। उसके बाद का बाकी 16 किलोमीटर रास्ता समतल और आसान है। यह ध्यान देने वाली बात है की मावफलांग गाँव में या सेक्रेड ग्रोव्स में तम्बू/टेंट लगाने की कोई जगह नहीं है इसलिए अगर रुकने की योजना है तो पहले से ही एक होमस्टे बुक करना ठीक रहेगा।
